programs.program: Masterstudium Computermusik und Klangkunst (MA Computer Music and Sound Art)
programs.university: Kunstuniversität Graz (KUG) — Institute of Electronic Music and Acoustics (IEM)
programs.institutionType: Public university of music and performing arts (art university)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics + Sonic Arts + Immersive/Spatial Audio (computer music)
programs.language: German is the programme language; the admission interview is held in German OR English
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS
programs.whatYouStudy: Four intertwined strands: computer music composition; performance and interpretation of electronic works; conception and development of new electronic instruments; and music informatics. Plus history, theory and aesthetics of computer music, and (master level) methods of artistic-scientific research. IEM is one of Europe's leading centres for Ambisonics/spatial audio research and runs its own well-known open-source plug-in suite and multichannel performance spaces; graduates are prepared for music, art, media and the creative industries.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree; you upload the bachelor diploma and transcript with certified German/English translations. The study dean formally assesses equivalence of the prior degree ("der Studiendekan die Gleichwertigkeit des Vorstudiums prüfen kann"). The curriculum names a BA in Computermusik or in Komposition und Musiktheorie (or an equivalent degree from a recognised post-secondary institution) as the reference qualification, and the admission colloquium can prescribe up to 20 ECTS of bachelor elective catch-up courses where skills are missing.
programs.portfolioSpec: Two meaningful examples of your own artistic work ("zwei aussagekräftige Beispiele deiner künstlerischen Arbeit"), approx. 5 minutes each, as audio or video documents. Multichannel material must be reduced to stereo. Total upload not more than approx. 150 MB, uploaded before the registration deadline. Works may be compositions with electroacoustic means, sound installations, documentation of performances/interpretations of computer-music works, development of computer-music instruments, or music-informatics applications.
programs.auditionSpec: No live/on-site audition. The exam is a colloquium/interview held via Zoom in German or English, discussing the submitted works, your motivation, interests and intended area of specialisation. No instrument required.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 March (annual)
programs.deadline: Registration 1 March – 1 May; the KUG page currently shows the Zoom interview taking place in June 2027, i.e. the cycle for a September 2027 start. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (exact interview day was not published on the page read).
programs.tuitionIntl: €726.72 per semester Studienbeitrag for third-country nationals (Tunisian citizens are third-country nationals), plus €26.20 ÖH student-union fee per semester (2026 rates).
programs.scholarship: None found specific to this programme. KUG operates a tuition-fee waiver for third-country nationals from a defined list of Eastern/South-Eastern European countries — Tunisia is NOT on that list. KUG itself states that financing a degree purely from internal scholarships is barely feasible.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (low public fee only; no stipend found)
programs.stipend: UNVERIFIED — no stipend attached to admission
programs.facilities: IEM: multichannel/Ambisonics production and performance spaces, electronic-instrument development labs, strong music-informatics research profile; internationally recognised for spatial-audio tooling. Specific room inventory not listed on the pages read (UNVERIFIED in detail).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — leaning No without preparation. The public page only says a bachelor's degree plus equivalence assessment by the study dean; the curriculum names computer music / composition-and-music-theory bachelors as the reference. A software-engineering BSc would be judged on the portfolio plus possible catch-up of up to 20 ECTS of bachelor courses. Realistic only if the two 5-minute works are genuinely strong electronic/computer-music pieces.
programs.fitNotes: The single best European home for serious electronic/computer music and spatial audio, and the admission burden is unusually light: two 5-minute works and a Zoom interview in English — no live instrument audition, no German test for the exam itself. Main obstacle: the degree is taught in German, and the aesthetic centre of gravity is experimental/art computer music, not club-oriented DJ/producer craft.

programs.program: Master Programme Postdigital Lutherie
programs.university: Kunstuniversität Linz (University of Art and Design Linz) in cooperation with Anton Bruckner Privatuniversität
programs.institutionType: Public art university (jointly with a private music university)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics + Sound Design (postdigital musical-instrument design and performance)
programs.language: English — taught entirely in English; "German skills are not required to join the programme"
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years); ECTS UNVERIFIED (not stated on the pages read, normally 120)
programs.whatYouStudy: Postdigital musical instruments at the intersection of design & technology, composition & performance, and art/media theory. Students reconnect acoustic, electronic and digital approaches to instrument design in tangible sonic artefacts — building controllers, interfaces and instruments and then composing/performing with them. Hosted by the Media Institute's Tangible Interaction Design lab (tamlab), with the composition/computer-music department of Anton Bruckner Privatuniversität as partner; courses are cross-creditable with the ABPU MA Komposition.
programs.entryRequirements: "A valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree" is required — no field restriction is stated. Applicants who did not graduate in Austria may have to supply additional entrance requirements/legalisations of documents. No German-language requirement.
programs.portfolioSpec: "A portfolio of your works" uploaded during online registration, plus materials to bring/present for the interview. The page does not fix a number of works, a duration or a file format (UNVERIFIED at that level of detail) — contact Univ.-Prof. Dr. Martin Kaltenbrunner (martin.kaltenbrunner@kunstuni-linz.at), who handles the registration procedure.
programs.auditionSpec: Entrance examination in the form of an interview around the submitted portfolio. Whether it is on-site in Linz or remote is not stated on the page (UNVERIFIED) — the 2026/27 entrance exams were scheduled for a single day, 29 June 2026, which implies attendance.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027 cycle
programs.deadline: For the 2026/27 intake: applications open until 19 June 2026, entrance exams 29 June 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Note this is a June deadline, i.e. much later than the usual Oct–Feb window.
programs.tuitionIntl: Free of charge for EU citizens; non-EU citizens currently pay €726.72 per semester (plus the standard ÖH fee). Students can apply to university fee-reduction funds.
programs.scholarship: University fee-reduction funds are mentioned on the admission page; no named external scholarship found (amounts and eligibility UNVERIFIED).
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (very low fee; fee-reduction funds may apply)
programs.facilities: tamlab (Tangible Interaction Design laboratory) inside the Media Institute; access to Anton Bruckner Privatuniversität's electronic-music production and presentation spaces; Linz's Ars Electronica ecosystem sits next door and Kunstuni Linz programmes routinely present work there.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes (best-in-slice on this point). The admission page states only: "To study at Postdigital Lutherie you need a valid bachelor (or equivalent) degree to qualify for the admission to this master programme" — no music degree, no conservatory training and no German is demanded, and the subject matter (building instruments, code, interfaces) directly rewards a software-engineering background.
programs.fitNotes: The most realistically enterable, genuinely hands-on, English-taught, near-free option in Austria for someone with a CS/SE bachelor and no conservatory record — he would be building his own instruments and performing with them. Obstacle: it is instrument-design/performance research, not a DJ/producer or mixing-and-mastering course; he must also confirm the 2027 dates because the cycle closes in June, not February.

programs.program: Masterstudium Tonmeister_in (specialisations: Musikproduktion Klassik / Musikproduktion Popularmusik / Filmton)
programs.university: mdw – Universität für Musik und darstellende Kunst Wien (University of Music and Performing Arts Vienna), Institut für Kompositionsstudien, Ton- und Musikproduktion
programs.institutionType: Public university of music and performing arts
programs.focus: Recording/Engineering + Music Production + Film Sound (Tonmeister)
programs.language: German — proof of German at level B2 is a condition of admission (Goethe-Zertifikat B2, ÖSD B2, or the mdw German test)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters; ECTS UNVERIFIED on the pages read (curriculum PDF not parsed)
programs.whatYouStudy: Managing complex audio productions end to end — artistic-technical planning, creative realisation, completion — with a large elective share so you sharpen an individual artistic profile within one of three specialisations: classical music production, popular-music production, or film sound. Sound reinforcement and sound design can be taken as additional emphases regardless of specialisation. A master project is central.
programs.entryRequirements: Passed admission examination; a completed subject-relevant bachelor's or diploma degree; proof of German at B2; and proof of unimpaired hearing. The admission info sheet is explicit: you must upload "Nachweis über ein abgeschlossenes Studium (Bachelor o. Diplom) in einem facheinschlägigen Studium Tonmeister_in" — i.e. a Tonmeister-type degree. Also required: a current specialist medical certificate with audiogram (not older than two months) confirming physiologically unimpaired hearing across 125–8,000 Hz.
programs.portfolioSpec: Very heavy and fully specified. (a) Motivation video, max 3 minutes, answering a fixed question list for your specialisation. (b) Instrument/voice video: for Popularmusik, 2 jazz/popular works with improvisation or ad libs (an own composition is allowed; for piano, one piece may be improvisation using keyboards/synths/DAWs such as Ableton Live with clearly audible playing craft and own sound design); band or play-alongs permitted; total video duration max 15 minutes. (c) Piano video if piano is not your main instrument. (d) PORTFOLIO — Popularmusik: SIX popular-music productions in different styles, produced, recorded and mixed substantially by you, at least three with vocals and at least two involving recording of acoustic instruments, all delivered as stereo audio (5.1/Dolby Atmos versions optional), each at least 2:30 and max 30 minutes in total, plus written documentation of 7,000–12,000 characters (approach, microphone choices, session photos, DAW screenshots, challenges, critical reflection). Klassik: three music-recording projects, two pure stereo audio productions with different ensembles plus one free project (audio or video, stereo/5.1/Dolby Atmos, with a stereo version supplied), total 20–40 minutes, plus the same 7,000–12,000-character documentation. Filmton: three film-sound projects (production sound, sound design, mixing), two with more complex sound design or mixing and one at least in 5.1, plus documentation. Formats: one work per file, .wav (5.1 as labelled single wavs), ADM BWF for Atmos, .mp4/.mov video, max Full HD, max 8 GB per file, documentation as PDF.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-part commission exam. Part 1 is the submitted video/audio package. If the commission invites you, Part 2 is an ON-SITE oral exam at the mdw in Vienna: a practical studio task (e.g. editing, mixing or sound design), questions on music theory and music literature, ear-training tasks, analysis of a listening or film example, questions on acoustics and audio/studio technology, and a technical discussion of your portfolio.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 April 2026 (registration for the admission exam) — PRIOR CYCLE
programs.deadline: Registration 1 April – 26 May 2026; all files uploaded to the mdwBox by 2 June 2026 23:59 CEST; exam date 25 June 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for a September 2027 start.
programs.tuitionIntl: €726.72 per semester for third-country nationals plus €26.20 ÖH fee (total €752.92 per semester).
programs.scholarship: None found for this candidate profile on the pages read.
programs.facilities: mdw's Tonmeister institute in the Anton-von-Webern-Platz campus, with recording, mixing and film-sound studios used for the on-site practical exam and for the three production specialisations (classical, popular, film sound); detailed room/console inventory not published on the pages read (UNVERIFIED).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No. The admission information sheet requires proof of "ein abgeschlossenes Studium (Bachelor o. Diplom) in einem facheinschlägigen Studium Tonmeister_in", and the MA page requires "ein facheinschlägiges Bachelorstudium" with the mdw BA Tonmeister_in named as the intended route. A software-engineering BSc does not satisfy this, and German B2 plus an audiogram are hard gates.
programs.fitNotes: Objectively one of the best Tonmeister/music-production masters in Europe and exactly the craft he wants — but it is closed to him on paper: it needs a Tonmeister bachelor, German B2, a certified audiogram, six finished pop productions with documented multitrack acoustic recording, an instrument audition and an on-site studio exam. Treat it as a 3–5-year goal reachable only via a Tonmeister/audio bachelor first, not as a 2027 application.

programs.program: Masterstudium Komposition (individual emphasis in Medienkomposition / Computermusik)
programs.university: Anton Bruckner Privatuniversität (ABPU), Institut für Komposition, Dirigieren und Computermusik
programs.institutionType: Private university of music, drama and dance (state-accredited)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics + Electroacoustic Composition with practical media-music production emphasis
programs.language: German. A 2019-era official source states German B1 is required for the Komposition master — UNVERIFIED for the current cycle; confirm with studium@bruckneruni.at
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters; ECTS UNVERIFIED (ABPU masters are normally 120)
programs.whatYouStudy: The MA Komposition drops the bachelor's three-way split, so you set your own emphasis — Jazz, instrumental composition, or Medienkomposition/Computermusik. The media-composition/computer-music emphasis teaches artistic approaches, well-grounded sound-technical skills and theoretical reflection, explicitly framing composition as a way to explore a technologically saturated world rather than training service suppliers for the media industry. Students may also take Postdigital Lutherie courses (the joint MA with Kunstuni Linz) as electives.
programs.entryRequirements: A successfully completed bachelor programme or equivalent education, plus a passed entrance examination. Field-of-degree wording for the Komposition master is not published on the pages read (UNVERIFIED).
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED at the level of number/length of works. The general music-admission page describes a two-round structure whose first round is a VIDEO SUBMISSION; the per-subject portfolio requirements for Komposition are not published on the pages that loaded. Request the Komposition/Dirigieren admission sheet from studium@bruckneruni.at.
programs.auditionSpec: Two rounds for artistic masters (KMA): round 1 video submission, round 2 an AUDITION ON SITE in Linz. An older official page gives the Komposition registration window as 1 March – 15 May with the practical part of the entrance exam on 12 June. PRIOR CYCLE / older source - confirm.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 March (per an older official page) — confirm
programs.deadline: Registration 1 March – 15 May, practical exam 12 June, per an older official ABPU page. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Note ABPU was moving between two application platforms in 2026.
programs.tuitionIntl: €450 per semester for EU/EEA citizens and €900 per semester for third-country nationals (master level), per ABPU's tuition-fee information; plus a €100 late-enrolment fee if applicable.
programs.scholarship: None found on the pages read.
programs.facilities: The Institute for Composition, Conducting and Computer Music states it provides "excellently equipped spaces for the production and presentation of electronic music", including a Computer Music Studio; it co-runs the tamlab-based Postdigital Lutherie master with Kunstuni Linz. Console/room detail UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — probably No without a strong compositional portfolio. Only the generic rule is published ("a master programme requires a successfully completed bachelor programme or equivalent education") and admission runs through an artistic entrance exam with an on-site audition. Nothing on the pages read addresses non-music bachelors.
programs.fitNotes: A credible, small, well-equipped electronic/media-composition department where he could specialise freely, and the same institute co-owns Postdigital Lutherie — so ABPU is worth contacting as the German-track alternative to the English-track Lutherie route. Obstacles: German, an on-site audition in Linz, and portfolio requirements that are not published, so early direct contact is essential.

programs.program: MultiMediaArt (Master), specialisation AUDIO
programs.university: Fachhochschule Salzburg (Salzburg University of Applied Sciences)
programs.degree: Master of Arts in Arts and Design (MA)
programs.institutionType: University of applied sciences (public-funded Fachhochschule)
programs.focus: Music Production + Sound Design + Film/Game Sound + Immersive Audio
programs.language: English (whole programme); proof of English at CEFR B2 is an entry requirement
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time
programs.whatYouStudy: You pick ONE of four departments — Audio, Film, Communication Design or Producing — and build advanced skills in conceiving, designing, implementing and managing cross-media projects (feature films, documentaries, games, VR, interactive installations). The Audio department covers music production & recording, composition, sound synthesis & sound design, mix & mastering, interactive audio, soundtracks & audio post-production, and sound & performance, with cross-department collaboration on film soundtracks, game audio and multimedia installations. Head of Audio: DI (FH) Martin Löcker.
programs.entryRequirements: A relevant university degree (bachelor or diploma) from a domestic or foreign higher-education institution; English B2; AND documented minimum ECTS in three core subject areas: 35 ECTS in "creative-artistic design practice" (graphic/media design, film, TV, audio, music, game design…), 10 ECTS in "basic sciences" (media theory, media informatics, media technology, aesthetics…), and 5 ECTS in "economics and working methods in the field of media" (project management, media economics, marketing, media law…). Proof is a completed form plus transcripts. Non-Austrian documents may need notarisation/legalisation.
programs.portfolioSpec: For Audio (as for Film and Communication Design) a PORTFOLIO is mandatory, uploaded in the application portal under "Upload application project" as a ZIP file containing a PDF: "Present at least three of your best creative works from the last few years. Describe in your portfolio the role you played in the projects shown." All third-party material and any soundtrack used must be credited — undeclared external material or copied ideas means exclusion from the admission procedure. Also required: CV in English, choice-of-department form, proof-of-academic-level form with transcripts, passport copy, English B2 proof, bachelor certificate (may be submitted by 31 October).
programs.auditionSpec: No performance audition. A ~15-minute interview with the department head and lecturers about your motivation, previous projects, professional experience and any master-project ideas; you may show further creative work (audio snippets, streaming links, screenshots). "Personal interview or, if travel to Salzburg is not possible, via video conference via MS Teams" — remote is explicitly allowed.
programs.applicationOpens: 30 October 2025 for the 2026/27 winter-semester intake — PRIOR CYCLE
programs.deadline: General applications 30 October 2025 – 1 July 2026; FINAL deadline 1 April 2026 for applicants who hold neither EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship nor an entrance qualification/degree from those countries — this earlier non-EU deadline is the one that binds a Tunisian applicant. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (expect roughly Oct 2026 opening, ~1 April 2027 non-EU cut-off).
programs.tuitionIntl: €363.36 per semester tuition + €26.20 ÖH fee (published for the programme). Applicants without EU/EEA/Swiss citizenship or degree must additionally pay a TUITION FEE DEPOSIT, which is credited against the first semester's tuition and ÖH fee or refunded if you do not enrol; the deposit amount is set in a separate guideline (amount UNVERIFIED).
programs.scholarship: None found on the pages read.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (very low fee for a fully English-taught master; no stipend found)
programs.facilities: Professional recording studio for music recording, a Dolby Atmos studio for immersive sound, and a large collection of synthesizers and hardware; departmental online portfolio of student/alumni work (portfolio.fh-salzburg.ac.at/departments/audio).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — the degree field is flexible but the ECTS gate is the real obstacle. "Media Technology and Media Informatics" (internet technologies, digital media, media technology and design) is explicitly on the published list of relevant disciplines, so a software-engineering BSc can count as a "relevant" degree. However he must document 35 ECTS of creative-artistic design practice (audio/music/media design courses), which a pure SE curriculum will usually not contain. The published exemption from full ECTS proof applies only to the Producing department, not Audio.
programs.fitNotes: The strongest English-taught, low-fee, studio-equipped music-production/sound-design master in Austria, and the admission is humane: three works in a PDF plus a 15-minute interview that can be done over Teams. The obstacle is arithmetic, not artistic — the 35 ECTS creative-practice requirement. He should email study@fh-salzburg.ac.at with his transcript now and, if short, spend 2026/27 collecting creditable audio/media coursework or consider the Producing department as a fallback.

programs.program: Digital Media Production (Master), Master Class "3D Audio & Sound Design"
programs.university: Fachhochschule St. Pölten / USTP – University of Applied Sciences St. Pölten
programs.degree: Master (MA/Dipl.-Ing. designation UNVERIFIED — the official programme page was unreachable during research)
programs.institutionType: University of applied sciences
programs.focus: Immersive/Spatial Audio + Sound Design + Film/Game Sound
programs.language: Programme primarily GERMAN; the 3D Audio & Sound Design master class is stated to be offered alternately in English or German. UNVERIFIED against the official page (fhstp.ac.at / ustp.at returned HTTP 503 repeatedly during this research).
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time — reported consistently by Austrian study portals but UNVERIFIED against the official page
programs.whatYouStudy: One of three master classes (Animation & Visual Effects, 3D Audio & Sound Design, Film & TV). The audio track combines sound-related production with acoustic information design: semester 1 covers audio system design (acoustics, sound-reinforcement technology), film sound design and television audio, plus master-class project work, programming and loudspeaker focus; semester 3 is master-class project work with an emphasis on 3D and spatial audio, alongside electronics, signal processing and digital real-time systems. Students work with Ambisonics, MPEG-H and Dolby Atmos, vector-based panning systems and sound installations. Positioned between traditional digital audio production and industry-oriented R&D. (Semester detail from the department-run master-class site, which states it is not an official USTP page.)
programs.entryRequirements: A relevant bachelor from a university of applied sciences or an equivalent degree from a recognised Austrian or foreign post-secondary institution, with at least 180 ECTS and at least six semesters — reported by Austrian study portals, UNVERIFIED against the official page. Admission runs through the standard Austrian FH admission procedure.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED. No portfolio specification could be confirmed because the official admission pages (fhstp.ac.at/de/studium/bewerbungsinfo) were unreachable throughout this research. Do not assume there is none — Austrian FH media masters normally require work samples plus an admission interview.
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED — an FH-style admission procedure (documents plus interview/test) is expected rather than a musical audition; confirm directly.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — not obtainable from the official site during this research. Austrian FHs typically run applications from autumn to spring with earlier cut-offs for third-country applicants.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED. Austrian FH degree programmes are typically €363.36 per semester plus the ÖH fee, but the FH St. Pölten fee page could not be read; a €4,385/semester figure found in search results belongs to a DIFFERENT postgraduate continuing-education programme (Film, TV & Media) and must not be applied here.
programs.scholarship: UNVERIFIED
programs.facilities: Four audio studios for practical exercises and software training, plus 24 up-to-date iMac workstations with high-quality audio interfaces and industry software; an Audio Lab used for sound installations, vector-based panning systems and production of Ambisonics, MPEG-H and Dolby Atmos; an active AES Student Section linking teaching and research with professional practice; student projects have been presented at Ars Electronica.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Likely Yes in principle — this is an applied-sciences media/technology master, not a conservatory, and no music degree is indicated anywhere. But the exact wording could not be verified. UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: On paper an excellent technical fit for a software engineer who wants immersive-audio and sound-design craft (Atmos, Ambisonics, MPEG-H, real-time systems, programming) at a low public fee. Two real obstacles: the programme is primarily German-language, and every admission fact here needs re-verification — the institution's own site was down throughout this research, so treat this entry as a lead to confirm, not as verified.

programs.program: Master of Arts in Music — Media Music (Scoring for Film, Music Production, Music for TV Ads, Music for Video Games, Sound Design)
programs.university: JAM MUSIC LAB Private University for Jazz and Popular Music Vienna
programs.institutionType: Private university specialising in jazz, popular and media music
programs.focus: Music Production + Film/Game Sound + Sound Design (media music)
programs.language: English (German version of the programme also offered)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS
programs.whatYouStudy: Applied media-music production plus research into the relationships between music, communication, media and society. Covers scoring for film, music production, music for TV advertising, music for video games and sound design, across pop, rock, electronic music, orchestral, production music and cinematic styles. The core is a self-directed, research-oriented artistic project supervised across artistic practice, musicology and artistic research; the university advertises 70+ artistic/practical major options including songwriting and band performance & recording.
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree in MUSIC is stated as the prerequisite qualification, plus a passed entrance examination. Language requirements are handled on a separate page (level UNVERIFIED).
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED at the level of number/length of works for master entry. The application pages route applicants to programme-specific "Application Information" documents that did not render. Note that for Media Music, remote applicants may submit relevant materials INSTEAD of performance videos — a meaningful concession for a producer rather than an instrumentalist. Confirm with office@jammusiclab.com.

programs.applicationOpens: Rolling / by arrangement

programs.fitNotes: Content-wise this is the closest Austrian match to "producer for screen and games", it is taught in English, and online auditions remove the travel barrier — but it demands a music bachelor and costs about €4,560 per semester with no verified funding. Include only as a labelled self-pay fallback, and only after asking whether a strong production portfolio can substitute for the music-degree requirement.

programs.program: Masterstudium Elektrotechnik-Toningenieur (Electrical Engineering and Audio Engineering) — inter-university
programs.university: Kunstuniversität Graz (KUG) jointly with Technische Universität Graz
programs.degree: Diplom-Ingenieur/in (DI / Dipl.-Ing.), i.e. a second-cycle engineering master
programs.institutionType: Public art university + public technical university (joint degree)
programs.focus: Sound Engineering / Recording Arts (audio engineering with musical training)
programs.language: German — C1 required; alternatively applicants at A2 may take a supplementary German exam before starting
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS
programs.whatYouStudy: The programme deliberately fuses technology and music, science and art: scientific and music-theoretical foundations leading into specialisations in audio engineering, music practice and electro-informatics. You register at either KUG or TU Graz as home university and take courses at both — the KUG side supplies the musical and studio training (and the IEM environment), the TU side the electrical-engineering and signal-processing depth.
programs.entryRequirements: A relevant bachelor's degree from a university or a university of applied sciences. Graduates of the KUG/TU Graz BSc Elektrotechnik-Toningenieur are admitted unconditionally. Graduates of OTHER bachelor programmes are invited to an admission colloquium and may be required to complete up to 30 ECTS of courses and exams from the bachelor programme, depending on prior education, to reach full equivalence. All external applicants must pass the admission examination. German C1 (or A2 plus a supplementary German exam).
programs.portfolioSpec: None — there is no artistic portfolio. Submission is academic: diploma, transcript of records and official translations via KUGonline.
programs.auditionSpec: An admission examination with three musical-aptitude components: a Seashore hearing test (~40 minutes), a musical ear test including dictation (~20 minutes), and a music-theory assessment (~15 minutes). The KUG page states the admission examination is conducted ONLINE for WS 2027/28 — a significant advantage for an overseas applicant.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (registration via KUGonline)
programs.deadline: Application deadline 3 June, with the admission test in June 2027 for WS 2027/28 per the KUG page (exact test day not published). This appears to be the 2027 cycle already — confirm the exact day before relying on it.
programs.tuitionIntl: €726.72 per semester for third-country nationals plus €26.20 ÖH fee.
programs.scholarship: None found for this profile. KUG's fee waiver for third-country nationals covers a defined list of Eastern/South-Eastern European countries only; Tunisia is not on it.
programs.facilities: Shared KUG/TU Graz infrastructure including the IEM (Institute of Electronic Music and Acoustics) with its multichannel/Ambisonics facilities, plus TU Graz electrical-engineering and signal-processing labs. Detailed studio inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, explicitly and by design — this is the one Austrian entry where a technical bachelor is the expected route: "Graduates of other bachelor's degree programmes are invited to the admission colloquium" and "may be required to complete coursework and exams from the bachelor program amounting to up to 30 ECTS depending on their prior education". A software-engineering BSc is a plausible base, subject to the top-up.
programs.fitNotes: The most credible path in Austria for a software engineer to become a properly trained audio engineer, with no artistic portfolio required and an ONLINE admission exam for WS 2027/28. Two real obstacles: German at C1 (or an extra German exam) and the musical-aptitude tests — Seashore hearing test, ear-training dictation and music theory — which need ~12 months of deliberate ear-training preparation. Also note this is engineering-led, not DJ/producer-led.

programs.program: Master of Arts in Composition and Theory — Major SOUND DESIGN
programs.university: Zürcher Hochschule der Künste (ZHdK / Zurich University of the Arts), Department of Music
programs.degree: Master of Arts ZHdK in Composition and Theory, Major Sound Design
programs.institutionType: Public university of the arts (one of Europe's largest)
programs.focus: Sound Design + Film/Game Sound + Immersive Audio (linear and interactive media)
programs.language: German OR English; non-native speakers must prove sufficient competence in the language of instruction
programs.durationEcts: Duration and ECTS UNVERIFIED — the ZHdK programme pages that loaded did not state them (Swiss MA Music programmes are normally 4 semesters / 120 ECTS)
programs.whatYouStudy: Creative work with sound and the interaction of image and sound in linear AND interactive media. You build technical and artistic-creative skills in sound generation and manipulation and in linear/interactive sound dramaturgy, with programming knowledge from basic to advanced depending on whether you take the linear or the interactive specialisation. Delivery is mentorships and individual sessions, class-based technical/aesthetic/craft teaching, and a majority of self-directed project work. Interdisciplinary links to interaction, game and product design as well as film and music. Degree components: a performative (or installative) master project, a research-led written thesis, a colloquium, and a portfolio of work from the programme. Career fields named: film and podcast sound design, theatre audio, video-game sound, interactive media and product sound, and applied research via ICST.
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification from a recognised and accredited university. Exception clause: "In Ausnahmefällen kann die ZHdK Personen ohne Bachelorabschluss oder gleichwertigen Abschluss einer anerkannten und akkreditierten Hochschule zulassen" — in exceptional cases ZHdK may admit people without a bachelor's degree.
programs.portfolioSpec: 3–4 of your own works totalling approx. 10 minutes: scores/texts/images as PDF, audio as MP3, video as MP4; all files compressed into a single ZIP not exceeding 1.95 GB, filenames containing your name without special characters. Plus a commentary on each work (concept, significance, creation process) in ONE PDF of max two A4 pages, and a motivation letter of max two A4 pages in German or English covering your education, musical training, musical activities, knowledge of music software and interests. ADDITIONAL requirement for applicants WITHOUT a BA in Music: a video of an artistic-musical performance, max 15 minutes, max 1.95 GB, .mov or .mp4, from a fixed camera perspective without cuts, hands and face visible, from your own recordings.
programs.auditionSpec: On-site aptitude assessment on 13–14 April 2026 (prior cycle) in three parts: a PRACTICAL sound-design task (90 minutes preparation, 20 minutes presentation); an ORAL part — analysis of a media/scene example (60 minutes preparation, 10 minutes presentation) plus a 10-minute portfolio discussion; and a 30-minute music-theory exam (memory exercise; reproducing rhythms and melodies).
programs.applicationOpens: 6 January 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE
programs.deadline: Online application 6 January – 2 March 2026; aptitude assessment 13–14 April 2026. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for a September 2027 start (expect roughly early Jan – early Mar 2027).

Application fees: CHF 100 registration and a further CHF 200 examination fee if invited to the second stage.

Crucially, the art scholarships are open to "students from a limited number of countries only" and the country list for 2027–28 will only be published in August 2026 — TUNISIA'S ELIGIBILITY FOR THE ART CATEGORY IS UNVERIFIED (Tunisia is eligible for the broader research-scholar categories per secondary sources). Contact sgs@sbfi.admin.ch.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial confirmed (moderate fee); potentially Full if the Swiss Excellence ART scholarship is open to Tunisia — UNVERIFIED
programs.stipend: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarship: up to CHF 2,450 per month (maximum figure published by SBFI). Whether tuition or housing is included is not stated on the SBFI page — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Toni-Areal campus; access to the Immersive Arts Space (IAS) and the Institute for Computer Music and Sound Technology (ICST); electives in electroacoustic composition, theory and sound design.

There is also a 30-minute music-theory exam in the on-site assessment.
programs.fitNotes: Europe's most prestigious dedicated sound-design master, English is an accepted language of instruction, the fee is modest by Swiss standards, and the door for non-music graduates is written into the regulations. programs.acceptsNonMusic: No as published — HEMU requires a bachelor's degree in Music from a Swiss university or an equivalent qualification for master entry, plus French B2 and an in-person artistic performance at the admission test.

Lowest-priority entry in this slice for a would-be DJ/producer.

programs.program: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound Design for Media Arts
programs.university: IADT Dún Laoghaire (coordinator) with Universidade Lusófona Lisbon + LMTA Vilnius
programs.degree: Joint Master's Degree in Sound (Irish NFQ Level 9), code DL935
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters. ECTS total UNVERIFIED (not stated on the pages read; Erasmus Mundus joint masters of this length are normally 120 ECTS)
programs.institutionType: Public art/design/technology institute (IADT) in a FilmEU consortium with a public university and a state music academy
programs.focus: Sound Design; Music Production; Immersive Audio; Film Sound; Electronic Music
programs.language: English
programs.whatYouStudy: Sem 1 IADT Dublin: Acoustics & Psychoacoustics, Audio and Music Production, Synthesis and Sampling, Interactive Systems, Sound Psychology. Sem 2 Lusófona Lisbon: Film Sound Theory, Sound Ecosystems, Sound/Music Interface, post-production tools. Sem 3 LMTA Vilnius: Sound and Environment, Sound Design and Immersion, Sound Concepts, thesis preparation. Sem 4: thesis/creative project with personalised mentorship. Genuinely hands-on: synthesis, sampling, audio and music production, audio post-production and immersive audio are named modules.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree (min EQF Level 6) in sound, music, film, media studies OR computational science. English: IELTS 6.0 with no component below 6.0, or TOEFL iBT 79, or Duolingo 110, or Cambridge B2, or LanguageCert ESOL — test within 2 years; alternatively evidence of a full qualification (min EQF Level 4) taught in English over at least one academic year. Motivation letter max 1000 characters. Academic references.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly. IADT lists "computational science" among the accepted bachelor fields, and the ReSound application page states: "Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience in areas such as sound, music, film, or media studies." This is the single most CS-friendly entry wording found in this slice.
programs.portfolioSpec: No more than 3 examples of your sound or media-related work, 10–15 minutes of material in total, submitted as a SINGLE hyperlink (portfolio website or one compiled audio/video file). A short reflective paragraph on each piece explicitly stating your role. Motivation letter max 1000 characters answering (1) what you hope to gain and (2) why a career in sound matters to you personally and societally — the page instructs: "Make this personal, and do not use AI / Large Language Models."
programs.auditionSpec: No live audition. Top-scoring applicants are invited to an ONLINE INTERVIEW; others are informed of non-selection as soon as possible.
programs.deadline: 27 January 2026 (extended from 20 January 2026) — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The ReSound application page currently states "Applications for ReSound 2026 have now closed" and publishes no 2027 dates. Expect the 2027-entry call around Oct 2026 – Jan 2027.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for 2027 entry — no date published as of July 2026. Prior cycle opened in autumn and closed late January.
programs.scholarship: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship — open to non-EU/Partner Country nationals including Tunisians, awarded "on the basis of excellence". A maximum of 24 places per intake, with a scholarship available only to a percentage of those places.
programs.stipend: Scholarship holders pay NO participation costs/tuition and receive €1,400 per month for 22 months from September, intended to cover travel, visa, installation and subsistence.
programs.tuitionIntl: €15,000 total for the 4 semesters (€7,500 before semester 1, €7,500 before semester 3) for non-scholarship holders — same figure for EU and non-EU
programs.facilities: IADT National Film School campus studios; Lusófona (Lisbon) film-sound and post-production facilities; LMTA Vilnius state music academy studios. Specific console/room inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Best single target in this slice for him: fully funded, English-taught, explicitly accepts a computational-science bachelor, portfolio is only 10–15 minutes of self-made work, and the curriculum includes music production, synthesis and sampling. Main obstacle: only a fraction of 24 places carry the scholarship and selection is on excellence, so his portfolio must be strong; also the 3-country mobility means three visa/residence processes.

programs.deadline: 2027-entry applications are shown as closed on the course page (register interest only) — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for the following intake

programs.fitNotes: The strongest craft training in the UK for sound-for-picture and a genuine industry pipeline — but it is film/TV sound, not club music, and the January start (not September) plus £27,600 × 2 years with essentially no non-EU funding makes it a self-pay proposition. Realistic only as an aspirational/self-pay fallback, or after he has a real sound-design reel.

programs.program: Sound Design (MSc)

IELTS Academic total 6.5 with at least 6.0 in each component; test no more than two years old at programme start. Portfolio mandatory.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — borderline. The listed "relevant subjects" do NOT include computer science or software engineering, though "acoustics" and "media arts" are listed. A software-engineering BSc would need a strong sound-design portfolio to carry the application; contact admissions before applying.

Music compositions may be included, but because the focus is sound design it is "desirable for portfolio examples to reflect a commitment to work in this area, e.g. by including examples of creative work using experimental sound processing." Submit as a single PDF up to 4MB, or upload larger files elsewhere and paste the link into a Word document — password-protected links are NOT accepted.
programs.auditionSpec: None stated — portfolio-based selection, no live audition or on-site test mentioned
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates. 2026-entry rounds were: Round 1 apply by Monday 15 December 2025 (decision by 19 March 2026); Round 2 apply by Monday 4 May 2026 (decision by 30 June 2026), with applications possibly remaining open after Round 2 if places remain. programs.fitNotes: A genuinely practice-based sound design MSc at a world-top-50 university, with a portfolio spec (three pieces, flexible media) he could realistically build in a year. Main obstacle: the 2:1 requirement in a listed "relevant subject" — his software-engineering BSc is not on that list, so an unusually convincing experimental-sound portfolio is the whole ballgame.

Son and Cinéma concours carry an eliminatory-mark system. PHASE 3 (oral, ON-SITE, half a day per candidate): 'Oral d'écoute et d'analyse' 30 min (a short sound piece is played; listening, analysis, imagination assessed); 'Oral de techniques du son' 30 min (technical discussion, 'des questions pratiques, impliquant la manipulation de matériel, peuvent également être posées'); 'Oral de culture générale et de motivation' 30 min. 16 admitted per Master per year.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — no music degree, no conservatoire diploma and no audition on an instrument. The published condition is only 'deux années d'études supérieures dans une même formation ... reconnue par l'État et égales à 120 crédits ECTS'. The Master Son référentiel is explicitly technical/scientific ('Notions générales d'informatique', 'Notions de matériel informatique', electricity-electronics, maths/physics) plus 'Culture cinématographique / Culture musicale / Culture radiophonique' and, under Motivation, 'Parcours antérieur — Expérience et pratique personnelles — Stages dans les domaines du son'. A software-engineering BSc is a genuine advantage on Phase 2.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 2026 cycle pre-registration opened 1 Dec 2025 at 15:00. Expect early Dec 2026 for the Sept 2027 intake; the Livret de concours is published each late November.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 cycle: pre-registration closed 14 Jan 2026 15:00; fee paid by 21 Jan 2026 15:00; Phase 1 dossier due 20 Feb 2026 15:00; Phase 1 results 24 Mar 2026; Son written test 10 Apr 2026; Son orals 8-12 Jun 2026; final admission list mid-July 2026.
programs.tuitionIntl: €300 annual registration in 2025-2026 + CVEC ~€105. 'La scolarité est gratuite pour les 150 étudiant·e·s, hors frais d'inscription annuels (300€ en 2025-2026).' No differentiated non-EU fee published. Concours entry fee €120 (€60 for CROUS scholarship holders).
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition effectively free; no stipend attached)
programs.scholarship: CROUS bourse sur critères sociaux if eligible; France Excellence Eiffel is possible in principle but must be nominated by the institution — UNVERIFIED whether ENS Louis-Lumière nominates. No programme-specific scholarship found.
programs.stipend: No stipend. Living costs in the Paris region are the candidate's own. UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Based at La Cité du Cinéma, Saint-Denis (Luc Besson's studio complex) since 2012. Avid and Merging Technologies audio post systems; Wwise/Unity; three specialised pathways with studio, live-sound and immersive/spatial facilities. Founded 1926 under Louis Lumière and Léon Gaumont. Applied-research projects; only 150 students total across the three Masters. Teaching staff publish concours preparation material (autopscience.com, informatique-audio-electronique.over.blog).
programs.fitNotes: The single best public-sector fit in France for this profile: near-zero tuition, an entrance exam whose written half (maths, physics, electricity, electronics, computing notions) plays directly to a software-engineering degree, and no music-degree prerequisite. The obstacles are the 3-min original sound creation for Phase 1 (he must build a real recording/editing/mixing practice in 2026), the compulsory on-site written and oral rounds in Île-de-France (three separate trips), the DELF B2 certificate, and the age cap of 27. Career emphasis is film/live/arts sonores rather than club-oriented DJ/producer work — he would get world-class craft, not electronic-dance-music career coaching.

programs.program: Diplôme de La Fémis — Département SON (via the Concours international, reserved for non-EEA nationals)
programs.university: La Fémis — École nationale supérieure des métiers de l'image et du son
programs.degree: Diplôme de La Fémis conférant le grade de Master (RNCP niveau 7)
programs.durationEcts: 4 years full-time ('cursus principal'). ECTS UNVERIFIED.
programs.focus: Film Sound (production sound, editing, mixing, sound design for cinema)
programs.institutionType: Public national film school (Ministère de la Culture / CNC)
programs.language: French only — 'La maîtrise de la langue française est obligatoire. Les épreuves se déroulent en français, de même que les enseignements dispensés à l'École.'
programs.whatYouStudy: Full four-year cinema cursus in the Son department alongside the six other departments (réalisation, scénario, image, montage, décor, production), built around collective film productions. Detailed module list not published on the pages read — UNVERIFIED. The concours syllabus signals the content: cinema culture, professions and equipment, 'esthétique sonore et culture musicale', and applied science (acoustic units, periodic phenomena, Fourier, microphones/amplifiers/loudspeakers, impedance, hearing and loudness, Fechner's law, Fletcher diagram, DC/AC and Ohm's law).
programs.entryRequirements: Concours international is open only to nationals of countries outside the EEA, Andorra, Monaco and Switzerland — a Tunisian national must use this route (dual nationals of those states must take the concours général). 'Les candidats doivent être âgés de moins de 27 ans au 1er janvier' of the concours year; must hold the equivalent of a baccalauréat AND have validated at least two successive years of higher education (by equivalence), with certified translations of diplomas. A 'professionnel' route exists: under 30, baccalauréat, and at least two years of professional activity in ANY sector. French: for non-nationals of francophone states, a certificate from a French-government-approved body attesting CEFR B1 minimum, or a copy of a higher-education diploma obtained in a francophone cursus. Maximum three attempts at any Fémis concours.
programs.portfolioSpec: First round, all submitted by 12 Feb 2026 12:00 via the candidate space (anonymised — no name anywhere, including in audio/video files or credits): (1) 'dossier personnel d'enquête' max 20 pages on an imposed theme — written part max 10 pages (font ≥10, numbered) + visual part max 10 pages, optionally illustrated by a video document max 5 min AND/OR a sound document max 5 min (links on page 1 via an anonymous account); (2) 'note de synthèse' summarising the dossier, max 1 A4 page; (3) 'lettre de présentation et motivation' explaining the path taken and why cinema, why La Fémis and why the chosen department, max 1 A4 page; (4) 'un portfolio de projets personnels : 3 projets au maximum, sur 8 pages au maximum, au format PDF' — accepted: photos, drawings, screenplay, comics, video (viewing link in the PDF), 'son (via un lien d'écoute indiqué sur le PDF)'; total running time of moving image or sound limited to 3 minutes.
programs.auditionSpec: First round also includes, remotely by videoconference: a film-analysis test (25 Feb 2026, 3 hours, extract screened 3 times, candidate records a 5-8 minute spoken analysis; coefficient 1) and the DEPARTMENTAL SON tests (24-26 Feb 2026, coefficient 2): (a) written paper 1h30 on cinema culture, sound aesthetics, musical culture and the science list above — 'C'est uniquement la « compréhension », le « principe » des notions énumérées ci-dessus, qui sont pris en compte'; (b) oral 30 min in which 'les jurés pourront revenir sur l'épreuve écrite, et interrogeront le ou la candidat·e sur son parcours et ses motivations'. Max 14 candidates declared admissible across all seven departments. SECOND ROUND: one public oral interview in PARIS, max 30 min, coefficient 4, between 15 and 26 June 2026, covering culture, tastes, experience and projects, the earlier tests and the submitted portfolio/letters. Max 7 admitted in total, jury balancing across departments.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES for the diploma requirement — only 'l'équivalent d'un baccalauréat' plus two successive years of higher education in any field is required, and the alternative 'professionnel' route accepts two years of work experience 'quel que soit le secteur d'activité'. No music or audio qualification is demanded. BUT the son written paper tests cinema culture, sound aesthetics AND musical culture, so the gap is cultural, not formal.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 2026 cycle online registration opened Tuesday 9 December 2025 at 12:00.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 cycle: registration closed 9 Jan 2026 12:00; documents due 12 Feb 2026 12:00; departmental tests 24-26 Feb 2026; film analysis 25 Feb 2026; admissibility list 2 Apr 2026; oral 15-26 Jun 2026; admitted list 26 Jun 2026.
programs.tuitionIntl: Concours international registration fee €142 (card only). Tuition for non-EU admitted candidates: '32000 euros au total pour les quatre ans de scolarité', paid as '8000 euros (à renouveler chaque année)' by bank transfer. Before 24 April a sworn declaration of ability to pay the €8,000 is required as a financial guarantee; admitted candidates must provide, before early July, an attestation of full coverage for the whole four years — 'qui pourra notamment être délivrée par l'Ambassade de France pour les bénéficiaires d'une bourse'. CVEC ~€105. Living costs excluded.
programs.fundingLevel: None from the school for non-EU candidates — this is a self-pay route unless a third party funds it. 'Les candidats peuvent assumer cette charge financière ou elle peut être assurée pour leur compte par un tiers (ambassade, famille, entreprise privée…).'
programs.scholarship: No Fémis scholarship for international-concours students found. The modalités explicitly point to an Ambassade de France attestation for scholarship holders, i.e. a French Embassy / Campus France Tunisie bourse would be the realistic vehicle. Bourses et aides sociales are mentioned for students in difficulty. Otherwise: None found.
programs.stipend: None. €32,000 total tuition plus four years of Paris living costs must be covered by the candidate or a sponsor.
programs.facilities: France's flagship national film school; the Son department works inside full-scale collective film productions with the réalisation, image, montage and production departments. Alumni and staff lists not read — UNVERIFIED. Note: 'L'enseignement à La Fémis est à plein temps et requiert l'assiduité des étudiants. Un travail en parallèle est donc possible mais seulement les week-ends ou soirées.'
programs.fitNotes: Prestige route into French film sound, and the international concours is designed for exactly his nationality profile — but it is a four-year, French-language, cinema-centred commitment costing €32,000 in tuition alone, with roughly 7 admitted per year across all departments. It does not serve a DJ/producer goal: there is no music-production, mixing-for-records or electronic-music track. Realistically a stretch/self-pay fallback, not a primary target, unless the French Embassy in Tunis funds him.

programs.program: Formation supérieure Musique Son Image — mention SON (FSMSI mention Son), 2e cycle / intégration post-licence
programs.university: Conservatoire national supérieur de musique et de danse de Paris (CNSMDP)
programs.degree: Diplôme de 2e cycle supérieur de Musicien-ingénieur du Son valant grade de Master
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (Cycle 2 only; the full FSMSI path is 4 years / 240 ECTS including Cycle 1)
programs.focus: Music Production + Recording/Engineering + Immersive/Spatial Audio + Sound Design (option) + live sound
programs.institutionType: Public conservatoire national supérieur (Ministère de la Culture), member of Université PSL
programs.language: French (interviews are held in French); an 'Anglais : métiers de l'audiovisuel' module is compulsory
programs.whatYouStudy: Two individualised years with a chosen professional specialisation among PRODUCTION MUSICALE, SPECTACLE VIVANT or CRÉATION, under personal tutors. Compulsory modules with ECTS: Technologie audio (12), Projets de production / 'Book' (24), Projet de recherche (22), Prise de son classique (9), Prise de son jazz et musiques actuelles (9), Mixage musiques actuelles (9), Mixage musique acoustique (9), Travaux pratiques FSMSI, Communication et gestion de projet (4), Stage FSMSI (20), plus law/regulation and live-performance safety modules. Optional 5-ECTS modules include Design sonore, Mastering, 'Réalisation et mixage en musiques actuelles', 'Vidéo 360, Audio 3D, nouveaux médias', 'Réalisation en informatique musicale : développement, création, répertoire', Direction artistique, Sonorisation, Son à l'image, Arrangement (chanson ou jazz), Création/composition/production pour la musique à l'image. Compulsory two-month placement with the Conservatoire's audiovisual department; research themes include Audio 3D, spatialisation for live performance, augmented reality, 360 video. Optional joint Licence Musique et Musicologie with Sorbonne Université.
programs.entryRequirements: 'No age limit for this competition.' Prerequisites as published for the 2026-2027 entry: 'BAC+3 diploma (European bachelor's degree or bachelor's degree from a scientific, technical or audiovisual training course) or international equivalent' AND 'D.E.M level from a Conservatoire for music. Applicants must have a very good knowledge of music theory, a sound musical culture, a knowledge of composition (harmony and/or counterpoint) and musical analysis.' French: candidates admitted to the 2nd cycle who are not nationals of francophone countries must present CEFR B1 before 30 June preceding first enrolment and B2 before 10 December following first enrolment.
programs.portfolioSpec: Eligibility stage: 'Review of each candidate's project portfolio, CV and covering letter. Candidates will be required to submit 3 personal musical, sound or audiovisual projects demonstrating a degree of originality or creativity, or simply showing a certain level of technical mastery. The projects are free and may take any form: score, recorded music, model, sound recording, sound fiction, soundtrack for images, film music, sound design, video creation, audiovisual music clip, short film, video sequence of filmed music, etc.' Each project must carry an explanatory note on artistic aims, choices, constraints, locations and tools used plus an assessment of the result, stating what the candidate personally implemented — 'This note must be concise and may not under no circumstances exceed 3 pages.' Projects uploaded to the registration platform by midnight on 24 May 2026.
programs.auditionSpec: Jury pre-selection of applications 4 May 2026; eligibility selection 1 June 2026. Admission tests, all on site: oral test in musical training (16 June 2026); oral test in sciences (17 June 2026); critical listening test on recordings OR comparative analysis test on films/videos/film-repertoire extracts (17 June 2026); interviews in French with the jury on the submitted personal projects and professional experience (18-19 June 2026). Roughly 8 places per year at FSMS level (per Onisep) — UNVERIFIED against the school's own page.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PARTLY — CHECK. The bachelor requirement explicitly welcomes a non-music degree: 'European bachelor's degree or bachelor's degree from a scientific, technical or audiovisual training course'. A software-engineering BSc satisfies this literally. HOWEVER the same prerequisite block demands 'D.E.M level from a Conservatoire for music' and 'a very good knowledge of music theory, a sound musical culture, a knowledge of composition (harmony and/or counterpoint) and musical analysis', and there is an oral test in musical training. Without conservatoire-level musicianship this is the hard blocker, not the degree.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: registration for the 2026-2027 entry opened 12 January 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026-2027 entry: application to be completed online by 13 April 2026; projects uploaded by midnight 24 May 2026; pre-selection 4 May 2026; eligibility 1 June 2026; tests 16-19 June 2026.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — no fee figure on the pages read. CNSMDP is a public Ministry of Culture establishment with low annual droits de scolarité (order of a few hundred euros) but this was not confirmed on an official page. CVEC applies.
programs.fundingLevel: UNVERIFIED (likely low-fee public; no stipend found)
programs.scholarship: The Conservatoire has a 'Bourses et aides' section (seen in site navigation) but its content was not read — UNVERIFIED. None found specifically for non-EU candidates.
programs.facilities: 'L'enjeu de cette formation, originale et sans équivalent en France' — trains 'musicien·nes-réalisateur·trices'. Access to the Conservatoire's centre audiovisuel and to the whole musical life of the institution (orchestras, ensembles, jazz and musiques actuelles departments) as recording material. Research partnerships on Audio 3D, spatialisation for live performance, augmented reality and 360 video. Sorbonne Université partnership for a joint musicology licence. Department renamed from 'métiers du son' to 'Musique Son Image'.
programs.fitNotes: Curriculum-wise this is the closest thing in France to a genuine music-production and mixing master: prise de son classique/jazz/musiques actuelles, mixage musiques actuelles, mastering, design sonore, Audio 3D, plus a production 'Book'. It is also nearly free and has NO age limit. The realistic obstacle is severe: DEM-level music theory, harmony/counterpoint, musical analysis and an oral musical-training test. Without several years of formal music training he will not clear the admission tests, however strong his engineering background. Worth a long-shot application only if he spends 2026 doing serious formation musicale.

programs.program: Master Composition électroacoustique (diplôme de 2e cycle supérieur, Métiers de la création musicale)
programs.university: Conservatoire national supérieur de musique et de danse de Lyon (CNSMD Lyon)
programs.degree: Diplôme de deuxième cycle supérieur des Métiers de la création musicale — Composition électroacoustique, 'valant grade de master' (grade conferred by arrêtés of 22 July 2021 and 16 June 2023, for the 'métiers de la création musicale' mention up to 2026-2027)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters full-time / 120 ECTS ('Le 2e cycle de deux ans, incompressible')
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics / Electroacoustic Composition (practice-based, studio-centred)
programs.institutionType: Public conservatoire national supérieur (Ministère de la Culture)
programs.language: French (Espace Transversal de Création; UE3 includes a modern language) — UNVERIFIED whether English-taught options exist
programs.whatYouStudy: 'La pratique de l'électroacoustique est envisagée comme discipline principale.' The name is deliberately open 'afin de pouvoir accueillir toutes les formes de projets, d'usages et de visées dans le domaine des musiques électroniques, qu'elles soient accompagnées ou non d'images, de vidéo, de mise en scène ou de lumières.' Studies are defined 'en termes de pratique quotidienne (aux contacts du studio et de ses machines)'; there is 'pas de parcours étudiant·e « type » ou prédéfini ; les projets compositionnels individuels sont le support même des études'. Structure: UE1 discipline principale; UE2 associated knowledge + one complementary discipline linked to the master research project; UE3 transversal (language, professional-insertion placements, research methodology, master's mémoire); UE4 disciplines d'ouverture from over a hundred options. Annual participation in the Empreintes creation festival; collaborations with ENSBAL and ENSATT, Mannheim and symphonic orchestra formats, an improvisation collective; principal teacher François Roux, plus Michele Tadini in the electroacoustic class.
programs.entryRequirements: External candidates: 'Peuvent se présenter au concours d'entrée en 2e cycle du CNSMD de Lyon, les étudiants titulaires d'un DNSPM ou d'un diplôme valant grade de Licence (Bachelor) DANS LA DISCIPLINE CONCERNÉE, délivré par un établissement d'enseignement supérieur français ou étranger.' 'L'admissibilité se fait sur dossier.' Age: 'Le candidat devra être âgé de 16 à 30 ans.' No candidate may sit the entrance concours in the same discipline more than three times (a fourth attempt is granted to anyone who has been admissible at least once). Studies are full-time with compulsory attendance.
programs.portfolioSpec: Admissibility is on dossier, submitted entirely online via the CNSMD 'Cadence' platform, with a required 'Fiche projet de recherche — Master' form, a 'Déclaration sur l'honneur 2e cycle' and a 'Parenté et authenticité des œuvres' declaration; video recommendations are published as a separate document. Exact number, length and format of the works to submit for composition électroacoustique: NOT published outside the yearly 'programme des épreuves', which 'sont publiés le jour de l'ouverture des inscriptions' — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: Concours d'entrée in two stages: admissibility on dossier, then on-site admission tests whose programme is released only when registration opens. Exact test format for électroacoustique UNVERIFIED. Annales for the 2025 concours are downloadable from the school site.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO / very unlikely — the wording is restrictive: a licence-grade degree is required 'dans la discipline concernée'. A BSc in software engineering is not a degree in electroacoustic composition, so a Tunisian CS graduate would almost certainly be ruled inadmissible on dossier. He would first need a DNSPM, a licence in music, or a DEM-level electroacoustic qualification. CHECK directly with the concours office before investing.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 'Le calendrier des concours ... est publié chaque année en NOVEMBRE sur le site du CNSMD Lyon' — so the 2027 calendar should appear around November 2026. The 2026 calendar is currently online.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date — only the 2026 concours calendar is published; no 2027 dates. Registration and document upload are both done on the Cadence platform and no late request is accepted.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — no fee figure on the pages read (public Ministry of Culture conservatoire; expect low annual droits plus CVEC, but not confirmed).
programs.scholarship: None found. The school has an international-partnership network (90+ institutions) and Erasmus+ mobility, but no named scholarship for a Tunisian degree-seeking student was found on the pages read.
programs.facilities: Dedicated electroacoustic studio practice ('aux contacts du studio et de ses machines'); Espace Transversal de Création; 11 diplomas accessible from the discipline including an international master (CoPeCo); Empreintes festival and What'Sup festival; cross-disciplinary work with dance, staging and the ENSATT theatre school and ENSBAL art school; possibility to add the Diplôme d'État or Certificat d'aptitude in composition; onward routes to a Doctorat Recherche et Pratique and an Artist Diploma CreationS.
programs.fitNotes: Artistically this is one of the most attractive electronic-music masters in France — individual composition projects, daily studio practice, an explicitly open definition of 'musiques électroniques', and cheap public tuition. The blocking clause is the admission rule requiring a licence-grade degree 'dans la discipline concernée' plus the age cap of 30. For a CS graduate with no conservatoire background this is realistically closed for 2027; a plausible two-step plan would be a French university master in electroacoustic/musical computing first (e.g. Saint-Étienne or Gustave Eiffel), then this.

programs.program: Parcours Conception son (Diplôme Arts et Techniques du Théâtre)
programs.university: École Nationale Supérieure des Arts et Techniques du Théâtre (ENSATT)
programs.degree: Diplôme Arts et Techniques du Théâtre conférant le grade de Master
programs.durationEcts: 3 years full-time, of which one is a preparatory year ('Formation initiale en trois années dont une année préparatoire'), entered at Bac+2 / 120 ECTS. ECTS total UNVERIFIED.
programs.focus: Sound Design for live performance / theatre + Live Electronics + Sound Engineering (régie, ingénierie, création)
programs.institutionType: Public grande école (Ministère de la Culture)
programs.language: French — non-nationals of officially francophone states must supply a DALF C1 (or equivalent TCF/DALF). Tunisia is NOT on the school's exemption list, so a C1 certificate is required.
programs.whatYouStudy: Three years covering physical acoustics, sound technologies and practices, and the aesthetics of artistic projects, training students for 'régie, ingénierie ou création' roles as 'l'interlocuteur privilégié' providing both technical and artistic guidance on a production. A master-level mémoire is written (the prerequisites explicitly ask for 'qualités rédactionnelles (en vue de la rédaction d'un mémoire de niveau Master)'). Cross-disciplinary work with the other nine ENSATT parcours (jeu, mise en scène, scénographie, conception lumière, direction technique, écriture dramatique…) and with CNSMD Lyon. NOTE: the programme page states it is 'en cours de mise à jour' — detailed module list UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: Minimum age 18 at 1 September of the entry year, no dérogation. All candidates must hold the baccalauréat (or an equivalence) AND 'justifier d'au moins 2 années d'études supérieures et être détenteurs de 120 crédits ECTS ... délivrés dans le cadre d'une formation reconnue par l'État'. Foreign nationals (except nationals of the listed francophone states — Tunisia is not listed) must provide their most recent diploma translated into French by a sworn translator, plus DALF C1 or an equivalent. Desired knowledge: 'Mathématiques, Physique : niveau minimum requis BAC + 1 scientifique' (published syllabus: integral calculus, linear ODEs, complex numbers and De Moivre, log/exp/power functions, Taylor expansions, derivatives, binary arithmetic and 'notion de programmation algorithmique'; electricity and electromagnetism, mechanics, damped/forced oscillators, resonance, Q factor, travelling and standing waves, interference); writing ability; broad general, literary, contemporary-art and theatre culture; ability to work collectively; any professional experience (placements, personal projects) is desired. Three recommended books: Daniel Deshays 'Pour une écriture du son'; Larrue & Mervant-Roux 'Le son du théâtre XIXe-XXIe siècle'; Yann Paranthoën 'Propos d'un tailleur de sons'.
programs.portfolioSpec: Admissibilité 1 = 'Dossier de recherche : projet de réalisation sonore sur un thème donné'. The 2026 brief: 'Vous réaliserez, à partir de sons que vous aurez enregistrés vous-même, une courte séquence sans musique ni parole ni texte dont le sujet sera (au choix) : le portrait sonore d'un espace naturel que vous avez visité (mer, forêt, lac, montagne...) OU le portrait sonore d'une promenade nocturne que vous avez effectuée' — the sequence must remain comprehensible to the listener. Deliverables: (1) a sound document not exceeding 3 minutes in WAV or AIFF ('format compressé refusé'), where 'la réalisation sera structurée par la prise de son, le montage et le mixage effectués avec les moyens dont dispose le/la candidat(e), MÊME RUDIMENTAIRES'; (2) a PDF text justifying the reflection, conception and realisation, not exceeding 6 typed A4 pages. Both uploaded via francetransfert.numerique.gouv.fr to concours@ensatt.fr, files named CONCOURS_NAME_INITIAL_REGISTRATIONNUMBER.
programs.auditionSpec: Admissibilité 2 (on site at ENSATT, Lyon): a written physics paper (2h00, coefficient 1) and a written paper analysing texts and/or audiovisual documents (1h30, coefficient 1). Admission: an interview with the jury on the CV, motivations and the earlier tests (about 20 minutes). Maximum 6 places ('Nombre de places maximum : 6'). A candidature-review commission first decides who is authorised to compete at all.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — no music or audio diploma is required, and the desired knowledge is explicitly scientific ('Mathématiques, Physique : niveau minimum requis BAC + 1 scientifique', including 'notion de programmation algorithmique'). A software-engineering BSc over-satisfies the 120-ECTS and maths/physics prerequisites. The real filters are the self-recorded 3-minute sound portrait, the theatre/contemporary-art culture expected, and the DALF C1.
programs.applicationOpens: 2027 CYCLE PUBLISHED: online registration 5 January 2027 to 27 February 2027 (registration fee €95). (For comparison, 2026 cycle: 6 Jan 2026 12:00 to 3 Feb 2026 12:00, fee €75.)

Confirm on ensatt.fr/concours as the fiche concours 2027 is released.
