programs.fundingLevel: Partial (very low public fees; no stipend)
programs.scholarship: None found on the pages read. ENSATT is a public Ministry of Culture school; bourse sur critères sociaux may apply if eligible — UNVERIFIED for a non-EU candidate.
programs.stipend: No stipend found. Lyon living costs at own expense.
programs.facilities: France's national theatre arts-and-techniques school; ten parcours trained together on shared productions, so the sound designer works with directors, scenographers, lighting designers and actors on real stagings. Collaboration links with CNSMD Lyon. Detailed studio/equipment inventory UNVERIFIED (page under revision).
programs.fitNotes: The most actionable target in this slice right now: the 2027 concours calendar is already published, fees are €605/year, entry needs only 120 ECTS plus Bac+1-level maths/physics — which his degree covers outright — and the portfolio brief is explicitly forgiving about equipment ('même rudimentaires'). Two real obstacles: DALF C1 must be obtained (he is fluent, so achievable, but it must be certified and booked early), and only 6 places exist. The mismatch is content: this is theatre and live-performance sound design, not club music production — he would emerge a superb sound designer/live-sound engineer, with electronic-music production as a side benefit rather than the core.

programs.program: DNSEP Design mention Design sonore (years 4 and 5)
programs.university: École supérieure d'art et de design TALM — site du Mans (ESAD TALM-Le Mans), with IRCAM, ENSCI-Les Ateliers and Le Mans Université / LAUM
programs.degree: DNSEP (Diplôme National Supérieur d'Expression Plastique) conférant le grade de master
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (années 4 and 5, semesters 7-10). ECTS total UNVERIFIED (French DNSEP = 120 ECTS at 2nd cycle).
programs.focus: Sound Design (industrial, object, environmental, multimodal) + Sonic Arts + some Immersive/Spatial Audio
programs.institutionType: Public art and design school (école supérieure d'art), in partnership with a research institute (IRCAM), a design school (ENSCI) and a university acoustics lab (LAUM/CNRS)
programs.language: French (a compulsory 'Anglais, le langage comme matière, matériau et matériel' module in UE3)
programs.whatYouStudy: Semesters 7 and 9 modules: 'Création sonore appliquée', 'Workshop applicatif', 'Production, diffusion et perception du son, appliquées au design sonore', 'Informatique sonore et technique son', 'Workshop arduino', 'Méthodologie créative en design sonore', 'Atelier Radio', 'Éléments scientifiques', 'Concepts de design et cognition auditive appliqués au design sonore', 'Histoire et théorie du sonore', 'Ateliers de recherche et création (ARC)', 'Anthropocène : usage et mésusage du monde', histoire des arts, pratique professionnelle, pré-mémoire then mémoire. Semester 8 is international exchange or a company placement. Semester 10 = mémoire and plastic-work defence before a jury of professionals. The year opens with a two-week 'workshop applicatif' answering a real brief from an industrial or institutional partner, in mixed teams with ENSCI design students — past clients: Décathlon, SETRAM/Le Mans Métropole tram sonification, Groupe PSA (gestural and sound interfaces), SNCF Direction Innovation, Maison de la Radio / Radio France, RATP, GHT Psychiatrie Sainte-Anne. Students also run '24 heures' of radio on the school station Radio-on and produce work for Le Mans Sonore, the city's international sound biennial.
programs.entryRequirements: 'Ce DNSEP s'adresse à tout type de créat.eurs.rices sonores, designers, musicien.ne.s, composit.eurs.rices, artistes, dont la pratique sonore et musicale peut s'adapter aux champs d'application très divers du design sonore.' Accepted profiles: 'Le.la candidat.e peut être diplômé.e d'une filière artistique ou d'électroacoustique des universités (ou être inscrit.e en licence au moment du concours - titre RNCP niveau II -) ; d'une école d'art ou de design équivalent au niveau licence (DNA ou équivalents étrangers) ; d'une école d'enseignement musical spécialisé équivalent au niveau licence (DNSPM ou équivalents étrangers), d'un DEM de composition ou électroacoustique d'un établissement musical spécialisé agréé par l'État, à condition de posséder en plus une licence scientifique ou en sciences humaines.' Selection criteria: 'La motivation, l'ouverture d'esprit, la faculté d'adaptation à des contextes spécifiques, le potentiel à travailler en équipe'. About ten places ('accessible à une dizaine de jeunes diplômé.e.s').
programs.portfolioSpec: Two-stage commission. 'La phase de pré-sélection se déroule sans la présence du.de la candidat.e et comporte une seule épreuve : l'évaluation du dossier personnel de candidature par la commission d'admissibilité — composée du directeur de TALM-Le Mans et d'au moins trois intervenant.e.s de la mention Design sonore — avec un examen approfondi des éléments fournis'. The jury reads 'votre portfolio envoyé pour la présélection'. The exact number of works, durations and file formats are NOT specified in the official presentation document — UNVERIFIED; request the current concours notice from contact-lemans@talm.fr.
programs.auditionSpec: 'La phase d'admission' — admissible candidates present a personal dossier before a jury which has already read the portfolio; 'les membres de la commission évaluent la motivation du.de la candidat.e, son goût pour la création, sa curiosité intellectuelle, sa capacité à être en prise avec les enjeux contemporains, ainsi que sa capacité à développer une réflexion et une pratique personnelle.' On-site interview at Le Mans. Dates for the 2027 entry UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — probably not on its own. The published list of accepted diplomas is art, design, university electroacoustic/artistic filières, DNSPM or a DEM in composition/electroacoustics. A scientific licence appears only as an ADDITIONAL condition attached to the DEM route ('à condition de posséder en plus une licence scientifique ou en sciences humaines'), not as a standalone qualification. A software-engineering BSc with no artistic or electroacoustic credential is therefore not clearly eligible; the school does, however, open the programme to 'tout type de créateurs sonores ... dont la pratique sonore et musicale peut s'adapter'. Ask the school in writing before applying.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — no 2027 concours calendar found on the pages read.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no published date for the 2027 entry. (The public art-school concours cycle in France typically runs January-May.) Contact contact-lemans@talm.fr / 02 72 16 48 78.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — no figure on the documents read. Public écoles supérieures d'art typically charge several hundred euros per year plus CVEC, but the differentiated non-EU regime for écoles d'art was not confirmed.
programs.scholarship: None found in the official presentation document.
programs.facilities: 'Studio son, équipé d'une écoute en 5.1'; multitrack digital recorders, an ambisonic microphone, an octophonic diffusion system, assorted microphones, audio interfaces, amplifiers and loudspeakers; MIDI controllers and a radio studio; plus full art-school workshops (volume, photography, video, engraving and print, painting, casting, mechatronics). Partners: IRCAM (Labo STMS and Perception & Design Sonores team — Nicolas Misdariis, Patrick Susini), ENSCI-Les Ateliers Paris (Roland Cahen, sound studio), Le Mans Université's LAUM (CNRS). Teaching team: Olivier Houix (IRCAM researcher, coordinator), Rodolphe Alexis, Fabien Bourdier, Ludovic Germain (ENSCI graduate, founder of the LAPS sound-design agency). Host of Le Mans Sonore biennial.
programs.fitNotes: Exceptional industry exposure — real briefs from SNCF, RATP, PSA, Radio France — and the IRCAM/ENSCI/LAUM triangle is unique in Europe. But the discipline is FUNCTIONAL sound design (product, transport, museum, UX signage), not music production, and the admissions list is built around art/design/electroacoustic diplomas. For a CS graduate aiming at DJ/producer work this is both a fit mismatch and an eligibility risk; it would suit him far better if he first built an art/sound portfolio and if the school confirms in writing that a scientific licence plus a strong sound portfolio is admissible.

programs.program: Master Acoustique et musicologie — parcours Ingénierie et conception sonore
programs.university: Aix-Marseille Université (AMU), Faculté des Sciences / UFR ALLSH
programs.city: Marseille (campus Saint-Charles), with some sessions in Aix-en-Provence
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (30 per semester)
programs.focus: Sound Design + Immersive/Spatial Audio + Recording/Engineering, with a strong acoustics and signal-processing spine
programs.institutionType: Public university
programs.language: French (C1 minimum for non-French speakers); English B2 minimum required
programs.whatYouStudy: Semester 1 is a common core with the musicology side, then specialisation into Ingénierie et conception sonore from semester 2. Modules: physical acoustics and signal processing; perception and cognition; computer programming and software development; sound and music listening practices; collective projects and field schools; compulsory 5-month internship in semester 4.
programs.entryRequirements: Selection on dossier via monmaster.gouv.fr. 'Licences conseillées: Physique, sciences et technologies, mathématiques, informatique, mécanique, MPCI (Mathématiques, physique, chimie, informatique), sciences pour l'ingénieur.' Language: French C1 minimum for non-French speakers, English B2 minimum. Capacity UNVERIFIED.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio requirement published on the programme page — selection is on academic dossier (transcripts, motivation) through monmaster.gouv.fr. UNVERIFIED whether a personal project or sound works may be attached; check the mention's 'critères d'examen des candidatures' on monmaster when the 2027 campaign opens.
programs.auditionSpec: None published — no live audition, no on-site test mentioned. Selection appears to be dossier-only. UNVERIFIED whether an interview is used.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, explicitly and unusually favourably. The recommended bachelor list names 'informatique' and 'sciences pour l'ingénieur' directly, and the syllabus assumes programming ability. This is one of the few French sound masters where a software-engineering BSc is the INTENDED entry profile rather than an exception.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: national monmaster.gouv.fr campaign for M1 typically opens late February. The programme page's indicative timeline shows applications March-April, review April-June, admission June-July (2023 cycle shown).
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date — the page shows only an old indicative March-April window. The 2027 deadline will be set by the national monmaster.gouv.fr calendar (published each winter).
programs.tuitionIntl: Standard national master fee applies to exempted students (~€250-260/yr) but non-EU 'droits différenciés' of about €3,950/yr for a master in 2026-2027 may apply unless AMU grants an exemption. AMU's own exemption policy was NOT read — UNVERIFIED. Plus CVEC (~€105).
programs.fundingLevel: Partial to full depending on the differentiated-fee exemption (which is a university-level decision, capped nationally at 30% of affected students in 2026-2027 and 25% in 2027-2028).
programs.scholarship: None programme-specific found. Realistic vehicles: France Excellence Eiffel (€1,181/month at master level, age limit 25 for master, nominated BY the institution — the 2026 call closed 8 January 2026, so the 2027 call will likely close early January 2027); Campus France Tunisie / French Embassy bourses; AMU international scholarships UNVERIFIED.
programs.stipend: No programme stipend. Eiffel, if awarded via the university, pays €1,181/month plus air ticket and social cover.
programs.facilities: AMU acoustics and musicology environment, Saint-Charles campus in central Marseille; field schools and collective projects; 5-month industry internship. Studio/console inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The best 'front door' in France for exactly his degree: the programme asks for a physics/maths/informatique licence, is dossier-only (no live audition, no music theory test), costs public-university money, and is in a major city. The caveat is orientation — the mention is 'Acoustique et musicologie', so expect a heavier scientific and perceptual load (signal processing, cognition, acoustics) than hands-on beat-making; production craft will come from the projects and the internship rather than from a mixing studio curriculum. Strong first-choice candidate, but he should pair it with a portfolio of his own tracks to argue the creative side, and check the differentiated-fee exemption early.

programs.program: Master Cinéma et Audiovisuel — parcours Ingénierie du son à l'image (département SATIS)
programs.university: Aix-Marseille Université — Faculté des Sciences, département SATIS
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (M1 + M2); entry requires 180 ECTS for M1, 240 ECTS for M2. Programme ECTS UNVERIFIED (French master = 120 ECTS).
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound + Recording/Engineering (son à l'image, multichannel mixing, live capture)
programs.institutionType: Public university film school (described as France's fourth public higher film school)
programs.language: French — C1 level required for international students
programs.whatYouStudy: Production-driven curriculum on professional equipment in professional configurations. M1: 5 fiction shorts shot on Super 16mm, 5 documentaries, multicamera capture work. M2: 2 fiction shorts (15 min, HD, multichannel mix), 1 cine-concert, 1 documentary (26 min, HD). Plus a placement of 6 months or more. SATIS teaches five specialities side by side — image, sound, music, editing, production/directing — so sound students work inside real crews.
programs.entryRequirements: M1 entry: 'Licence, 180 ECTS et 4 semaines de stage dans le secteur'. Candidates 'doivent avoir un projet professionnel (appuyé par une première expérience professionnelle d'au moins un mois dans le domaine de l'audiovisuel : convention de stage et rapport d'activité) et une forte motivation'. M2 entry: M1 Cinéma/Audiovisuel, 240 ECTS, 8 weeks of prior sector experience. French C1 for international students.
programs.portfolioSpec: No creative portfolio of finished works is specified. Instead the decisive documents are the professional project statement plus PROOF of at least one month of audiovisual-sector experience (internship agreement + activity report) and 4 weeks of sector internship. UNVERIFIED whether personal sound works may be attached.
programs.auditionSpec: 'Le recrutement se fait sur dossier, QCM et entretien' — application file, a multiple-choice test and an interview. No instrumental audition. Test content and location UNVERIFIED (likely on site in Aubagne).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES on the diploma (any 'Licence, 180 ECTS' is the stated requirement — no music or audiovisual degree named), BUT there is a hard non-academic condition a fresh CS graduate will fail today: four weeks of sector internship plus at least one month of documented professional experience in audiovisual, with an internship agreement and activity report. He would need to arrange an audio/audiovisual internship in 2026 to be eligible at all.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Pre-registration deadline is stated as 'early April'; contact sciences-satis-scol@univ-amu.fr. Platform for M1 is expected to be monmaster.gouv.fr — UNVERIFIED for this parcours.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 'pre-registration deadline is early April' with no year specified on the page read. Confirm the 2027 date with the SATIS scolarité (Florence Tildach, sciences-satis-scol@univ-amu.fr, 04 12 23 10 48, 9 boulevard Lakanal, 13400 Aubagne).
programs.tuitionIntl: Public university fees; non-EU 'droits différenciés' of ~€3,950/yr for master in 2026-2027 may apply unless exempted (AMU policy UNVERIFIED). Plus CVEC.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial to full depending on differentiated-fee exemption; no stipend.
programs.scholarship: None programme-specific found. Same external routes as any French public master: France Excellence Eiffel (institution-nominated, €1,181/month, master age limit 25), Campus France Tunisie / Embassy bourses.
programs.facilities: Purpose-built public film school in Aubagne (near Marseille); Super 16mm film shooting, multichannel/HD post, cine-concert production, multicamera live capture; five co-located specialities create genuine crew experience. Console/studio inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Excellent hands-on volume — around a dozen real productions across two years — and a licence in any field is formally acceptable. Two frictions: the mandatory documented audiovisual work experience before applying (a 2026 to-do, not a 2027 one), and the film-and-television orientation, which trains a boom operator/re-recording mixer rather than a music producer. Good backup if he can land an audio internship in Tunisia or France during 2026; weak fit for the DJ goal.

programs.program: Master Cinéma et audiovisuel — parcours Son (ENSAV)
programs.university: Université Toulouse - Jean Jaurès / École Nationale Supérieure d'AudioVisuel (ENSAV, formerly ESAV)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (M1 + M2). ECTS for the programme UNVERIFIED; M1 entry requires 180 ECTS, M2 entry 240 ECTS.
programs.focus: Film Sound + Sound Design + Recording (practice-based, very production-heavy)
programs.institutionType: Public university film school (école interne of Université Toulouse - Jean Jaurès)
programs.language: French
programs.whatYouStudy: Roughly 15 compulsory exercises over the two years — sound pieces, documentaries and fiction works, each with defined pedagogical constraints — plus a personal film at the end of M1 and of M2 with no restriction on genre or duration, each accompanied by a methodological dissertation. Taught content covers acoustic principles, analogue and digital audio technology, sound recording, mixing and distribution/diffusion techniques.
programs.entryRequirements: 'Licence Création Audiovisuelle ou d'une formation bac+3 équivalente dans les domaines des arts, des arts du spectacle, de l'architecture, du design, des arts plastiques, DE L'INFORMATIQUE ou des beaux-arts.' M1 candidates need Bac+3 / 180 ECTS; M2 entrants 240 ECTS. Admission is at the end of L3 plus selection on dossier; 'à l'issue de l'examen du dossier, un entretien peut être programmé avec le candidat'. Dossiers are emailed to ensav@univ-tlse2.fr (the Production parcours uses monmaster; the son route is handled by ENSAV directly).
programs.portfolioSpec: The dossier de candidature is a downloadable ENSAV form ('Dossier-M1-2026-2027.pdf'). For the Production parcours the dossier requires a one-page mémoire project; the equivalent requirement for the SON parcours (personal sound works, number, length, format) is NOT specified on the pages read — UNVERIFIED. Request the son-specific dossier from ensav@univ-tlse2.fr.
programs.auditionSpec: Selection on dossier, with a possible interview after the file review ('un entretien peut être programmé'). No live audition or written concours found. UNVERIFIED whether the interview is remote or on site.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, and this is the clearest positive wording found anywhere in this slice: the accepted bachelor list explicitly includes 'DE L'INFORMATIQUE'. A Bac+3 in computer science is a named, accepted entry qualification. No music degree, no audition, no music-theory test.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: the ENSAV M1 dossier for 2026-2027 was posted in March 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026-2027 cycle: dossiers due 10 May 2026 (M2 REX: 31 August 2026); the M1 Production route on Mon Master closed 16 March 2026. Confirm the 2027-2028 son deadline with ensav@univ-tlse2.fr.
programs.tuitionIntl: Public university fees; non-EU 'droits différenciés' of ~€3,950/yr for master in 2026-2027 may apply unless exempted (Toulouse Jean Jaurès policy UNVERIFIED). Plus CVEC. Not stated on the programme page — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial to full depending on differentiated-fee exemption; no stipend.
programs.scholarship: None programme-specific found. External: France Excellence Eiffel (institution-nominated, master age cap 25, €1,181/month + air ticket + social cover; the 2026 call closed 8 Jan 2026), Campus France Tunisie.
programs.facilities: ENSAV is one of France's four public film schools; the sound parcours is built on a heavy schedule of collective and personal productions with multi-format delivery. Equipment inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Very strong practical fit and the most explicitly CS-friendly admissions wording in France for a film-sound master — no audition, dossier plus possible interview, and 'informatique' named as an accepted licence. Downsides: it is cinema sound rather than music production, the son dossier contents are not public so he must write to ENSAV, and it is French-language throughout (not an obstacle for him). Realistic primary or secondary target, and probably his highest-probability admission among the public film schools.

programs.program: Master Ingénierie de l'image, ingénierie du son — parcours Image et Son (ISB)
programs.university: Université de Bretagne Occidentale (UBO), Faculté des Sciences et Techniques — Image & Son Brest
programs.degree: Master (mention Ingénierie de l'image, ingénierie du son)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, semesters 7-10, approximately 60 ECTS per year (total 120). Stated as 'approximately 60 credits per year'.
programs.focus: Recording/Engineering + Immersive/Spatial Audio + Music Production (studio) + film/AV post-production
programs.institutionType: Public university (science faculty), engineering-oriented sound and image school
programs.language: French
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound modules: 'Electroacoustique & Acoustique des salles'; 'Traitement du signal audionumérique'; studio practice in recording, mixing and mastering; 'Son spatialisé' (stereo, object-based and binaural formats); music informatics; classical sound recording. Image and post-production courses run alongside across both years. Graduates go into audiovisual and cinema (lighting, editing, sound, post-production) and into music careers — recording studios and live events.
programs.entryRequirements: M1: an L3 in the SPI mention with the 'Image & Son' specialisation 'ou équivalent', assessed after examination of the dossier and an interview. The programme notes that students normally follow the full L3 to M1 to M2 path rather than joining at M1. M2: continuation of the M1 Image et Son 'or equivalent master', again on dossier plus interview. Capacity: 'La limitation à 18 étudiants par promotion'. Total school enrolment about 50 students; the school reports 100% professional insertion 18 months after the M2.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio of works specified — selection is 'examen du dossier de candidature et entretien'. Whether personal sound work can be attached is UNVERIFIED; the school's own admissions page does not list the dossier contents.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. An interview ('entretien') follows the dossier review for both M1 and M2. Format and location UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — leaning yes but not proven. The requirement is an L3 in Sciences pour l'Ingénieur with the Image & Son specialisation 'or equivalent'. A software-engineering BSc is scientifically adjacent, and the master's own spine is signal processing and electroacoustics, but the page also warns that entry at M1 is unusual because most students come up through the in-house L3. The school does not publish any wording accepting non-specialised science degrees. He must email the ISB to test eligibility before applying.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: M1 applications for 2026-2027 opened 17 February 2026 on monmaster; L3 and M2 applications opened 27 April 2026 on eCandidat.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026-2027: M1 window 17 February - 16 March 2026 (monmaster.gouv.fr); L3 and M2 window 27 April - 31 May 2026 (eCandidat UBO). The 2027 M1 window will follow the national monmaster calendar.
programs.tuitionIntl: Public university fees. UBO publishes a 'Droits d'inscription différenciés' notice — content not read, so the non-EU rate and exemption policy are UNVERIFIED. National differentiated master rate for 2026-2027 is about €3,950/yr where applied. Plus CVEC.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial to full depending on the differentiated-fee exemption; no stipend.
programs.scholarship: None programme-specific found. External: France Excellence Eiffel (institution-nominated), Campus France Tunisie / Embassy bourses.
programs.facilities: Studio practice for recording, mixing and mastering; spatial audio work across stereo, object-based and binaural formats; music-informatics teaching; cohort capped at 18 so studio access is high per student. Reported 100% employment 18 months post-M2. Console/room inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Technically the closest French public master to a 'sound engineer' training with real music-studio content (recording, mixing, mastering, spatialisation) and a very small cohort. Two frictions: the programme is designed as a continuation of its own L3, so a direct M1 entry from a Tunisian CS degree needs a case-by-case ruling, and Brest is remote from any electronic-music scene. Worth an early eligibility email; if they accept him, the curriculum-to-goal alignment is among the best in the slice.

programs.program: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master DIGICREA — Digital Creativity, Art & Science, SOUND-MUSIC specialization
programs.university: Consortium: Université Jean Monnet Saint-Étienne (coordinator, France) + Universidade Católica Portuguesa Porto (Portugal) + University of Silesia Katowice/Cieszyn (Poland)
programs.degree: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master — multiple degrees awarded by Université Jean Monnet, Universidade Católica Portuguesa and University of Silesia
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters across three countries, ending with an internship. ECTS total UNVERIFIED (EMJM standard = 120).
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Music Production + Sound Design + digital creation (there is a dedicated SOUND-MUSIC specialization path, distinct from the IMAGE path)
programs.language: English — 'The entire program is taught in English.'
programs.institutionType: Public university consortium (Erasmus Mundus Joint Master, EU-funded)
programs.whatYouStudy: Training in audiovisual new media, emerging technologies in the film industry, music, graphic design, artificial intelligence, virtual reality and their applications. Two specialization paths: SOUND-MUSIC and IMAGE; all candidates apply to one only. The Selection Board 'assesses the candidate's predispositions for professions related to the production of audio-visual and musical forms, including the production of Extended Reality films'. Mobility: Saint-Étienne, then Porto, then Katowice, then an internship with public and private sector partners. The programme shares courses with the Université Jean Monnet Master CCNT (Création Contemporaine et Nouvelles Technologies, RIM/Arts numériques), so the Saint-Étienne semester connects to the RIM music-computing environment. Detailed module list UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: 'A Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS is the minimum requirement to enrol' — no field restriction stated. Candidates with at least 150 ECTS at application may be considered with a sworn statement that 180 ECTS will be obtained before the start. Documents: EUROPASS CV in English; proof of nationality; certified copies (with certified English translations) of higher-education and high-school diplomas and full transcripts; at least two letters of recommendation in English on letterhead, signed and stamped, with referee contacts; a 'Science qualification and experience in New Technology' form in which candidates 'describe their level in mathematics, digital signal processing, and computer science ... their skills and level in JavaScript, Python or C, HTML, real-time graphics programming, geometry, trigonometric functions, and algebra courses'; English certificate at minimum B2, C1 recommended (IELTS 6, TOEFL iBT ≥90, TOEFL ITP 550, TOEIC ≥650, or a degree taught 100% in English with a university letter). Applications via the UJM eCandidat portal — explicitly NOT via Études en France.
programs.portfolioSpec: 'Artistic or Professional Portfolio: Document presenting artistic productions related to the DIGICREA curriculum and specialization path chosen by the applicant. All projects included in the portfolio must not be more than 5 years old. Submit EXACTLY 3 TO 5 specific works or project (video/audio/images) including metadata (title, short description, public link, and their role): minimum 3 works - maximum 5 works. Please number works presented in the portfolio from 1 to 5.' For Sound-Music applicants 'it can be a composition project (orchestral or electronic), sound design project, sound concept project, music piece cycle, demo, etc.' The PDF is capped at 5 MB, so online links are used for the media. Also required in place of a cover letter: a VIDEO PRESENTATION of maximum 2 minutes covering, in order, current situation, motivation for applying, understanding of the programme, why the candidate can succeed, and ideas for applied research and professional development — link supplied in a PDF 'Motivation letter' item, accessible to anyone with the link until mid-April.
programs.auditionSpec: Stage II: shortlisted applicants only, an ONLINE 15-minute interview (2026 cycle: forecast 24-30 March 2026) assessing 'the candidate's personality characteristics, way of thinking, personal life experience, and character attributes'. Candidates may additionally be asked to attend a videoconference to verify English level. No on-site test, no live audition, no travel needed to apply.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — the strongest case in this slice. The only academic requirement is 'A Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS', with no field restriction, and the application actively rewards a software background: a compulsory form asks the candidate to rate their level in mathematics, digital signal processing and computer science, and specifically in JavaScript, Python or C, HTML, real-time graphics programming, geometry, trigonometry and algebra. A software-engineering graduate with a music portfolio is close to the ideal applicant profile.
programs.applicationOpens: 2027 CYCLE: 'The call for applications for the next DIGICREA cohort 2027-2029 is expected to open in November 2026. Further information regarding this procedure will be available in the autumn. Please note that some requirements will differ from those of the 2026 selection process.'
programs.deadline: 2027 intake not yet fixed. PRIOR CYCLE reference: the 2026-2028 call opened 14 November 2025 and closed 16 February 2026, with Stage II interviews forecast 24-30 March 2026 — expect a comparable mid-February 2027 deadline. Confirm from November 2026.
programs.tuitionIntl: ZERO. 'Students (scholarship holders and non-scholarship holders) are not charged any tuition fees.' Self-funded students must submit a Guarantee of full financial support with a budget simulation, and document their income for the visa.
programs.fundingLevel: Full (for scholarship holders) — the best funding on offer in this slice
programs.scholarship: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master (EMJM) scholarship: 'a grant of 1,400 euros per month, for a total duration of 24 months. The maximum amount per student is therefore 1,400 euros x 24 months = 33,600 euros', awarded for full-time enrolment over the whole course, covering travel, visa, installation and subsistence, paid into the student's own bank account. A limited number per cohort. 'The application for the scholarship is included within the application for the program itself.' Non-scholarship holders can add Erasmus+ KA131/KA171 mobility funds. Special-needs support available for students with long-term impairments.
programs.stipend: €1,400 per month for 24 months (€33,600 total) plus zero tuition, for scholarship holders. This is the only fully funded option identified in the French slice.
programs.facilities: Three-country mobility with a design and digital-creation environment at each site; at Saint-Étienne it shares teaching with the CCNT/RIM programme, which provides a music studio, video studio, multimedia prototyping studio, sensors, interfaces and sound capture/diffusion equipment. Professionals involved in the shared Saint-Étienne teaching include a sound designer at Ubisoft, a developer at Ableton (Berlin) and Cycling'74 (USA), the sound engineer running the FIL venue studios, and researchers from INRIA and GRAME Lyon.
programs.fitNotes: This is the standout recommendation for him: no tuition, €1,400/month for two years, taught in English (so IELTS/TOEFL rather than DALF), a bachelor in ANY field accepted, a Sound-Music specialization, an application that explicitly credits his programming skills, and a fully remote selection process (online 15-min interview only). The 2027-2029 call is expected to open November 2026 — exactly his window. Two things to do now: build a portfolio of 3-5 numbered works (a composition or sound-design project, a demo, a music cycle) with public links and metadata, and book an English test at B2 minimum, C1 preferred. Caveat: the programme is broad digital creativity — AI, XR, graphic design — rather than a dedicated club-music production course, and it is competitive.

programs.program: Master Arts — parcours Création Contemporaine et Nouvelles Technologies (CCNT), option Réalisateur·rice en Informatique Musicale (RIM)

RIM option: 'la connaissance et la maîtrise des technologies électroniques et numériques' preparing for the Réalisateur en Informatique Musicale profession, at the interface between software developers, music-computing researchers, composers and any company integrating sound. Teaching is shared between the Arts plastiques and Musicologie departments and is delivered in part by international professionals. Max/MSP appears in the module descriptions. Dedicated equipment and production spaces are provided for both years: 'Un parc matériel spécifique (ordinateurs, capteurs, interfaces, outils de prise de vue, de prise de son et de diffusion, etc.), ainsi que des lieux de production dédiés (studio musical, studio de prise de vue, studio de maquettage de dispositifs multimédia...)'. The programme's own RIM page (M2 route) states: entry for 'Master I en musique, en arts numériques, ou équivalents', or any Master 1 with a demonstrated strong level in music or digital-arts practice; professionals may enter via VAE. Candidates are expected to have 'une culture scientifique et une expérience en informatique musicale et/ou en programmation dans le champ des arts numériques'. Cohort: maximum 20 students. Note the ambiguity: the university presents CCNT as a two-year M1+M2 master, while the older RIM site describes an M2-only professional route — confirm which entry point applies for 2027.
programs.portfolioSpec: For the M2 RIM route: a dossier obtained from the secretariat or downloaded from the university site, submitted via eCandidat, plus an 'audio commentary' exercise for RIM candidates (an analysis of a work, for RAN candidates an artwork analysis) 'demonstrating artistic/musical competence'. For M1 entry via monmaster the required documents are UNVERIFIED — check the mention's 'critères d'examen des candidatures' when the 2027 campaign opens.
programs.auditionSpec: An interview with a jury of professionals assessing motivation and career project, plus the audio-commentary exercise described above. No instrumental audition. 2018-cycle indicative dates were: application deadline 31 May, admission exams 8 June, start September — PRIOR CYCLE, not current.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PARTLY YES — the profile expected is explicitly scientific: 'une culture scientifique et une expérience en informatique musicale et/ou en programmation dans le champ des arts numériques', and the programme accepts 'des étudiants issus d'autres formations ayant validé un Master 1 et pouvant justifier d'un bon niveau en pratique musicale et/ou artistique numérique'. So a computer-science background is welcome in substance. The obstacle is level, not field: the RIM route as documented starts at M2 and therefore assumes an M1 already completed, plus demonstrable music-computing or digital-arts practice. Confirm whether direct M1 entry from a Bac+3 is open for 2027.

programs.tuitionIntl: Favourable: UJM applies an AUTOMATIC PARTIAL EXEMPTION from differentiated fees to non-EU students enrolling in a national master's diploma, bringing the fee down to the standard national rate (the page cites €255 as the reduced rate for a previously enrolled cohort). The €3,950 figure on that page is quoted for an engineering diploma, not the master. Plus CVEC (~€105). Confirm the 2027-2028 rate.

External routes: France Excellence Eiffel (institution-nominated, €1,181/month at master level, age limit 25 for master; 2026 call closed 8 January 2026), Campus France Tunisie.
programs.stipend: None from this programme. UNVERIFIED whether UJM nominates for Eiffel.
programs.facilities: Dedicated music studio, video studio and multimedia prototyping studio; computers, sensors, interfaces, capture and diffusion tools available across both years. Professional teaching staff include Pierre Colomies (sound designer, Ubisoft Montpellier), Emmanuel Jourdan (RIM/developer, Ableton Berlin and Cycling'74), Christophe Lebreton (RIM, LISILOG), Stéphane Letz (GRAME Lyon), Romain Michon (INRIA), Jérémy Lhuillier (sound engineer, head of studios at Le FIL Saint-Étienne), Michele Tadini (electroacoustic class, CNSMD Lyon), Michel Pascal (CNRR Nice). Regional partners include GRAME and AADN Lyon. Also opens onto doctoral study.
programs.fitNotes: Content-wise one of the best matches for a programmer who wants to make electronic music: Max/MSP, music computing, sound design for games and live performance, an Ableton engineer on staff, a real music studio, and Ubisoft/GRAME/INRIA connections — at near-zero fees thanks to UJM's automatic exemption. Two cautions: the documented RIM route starts at M2, so he must confirm whether he can enter M1 directly with a Bac+3, and the shared DIGICREA courses mean strong English is useful. Practical strategy: apply here AND to DIGICREA at the same university, since a DIGICREA place brings the €33,600 scholarship.

programs.auditionSpec: None published — dossier-based selection. No audition or on-site test found. UNVERIFIED whether an interview is used.

programs.university: HKU University of the Arts Utrecht (Utrechts Conservatorium / HKU Music and Technology)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS
programs.language: English and Dutch (Master of Music is offered in English; HKU states the pathway is taught in 'English and Dutch')
programs.institutionType: University of the arts (hogeschool / university of applied sciences, art school)
programs.focus: Music Production; Sound Design; Electronic Music/Live Electronics (Music Technology strand); Film/Game Sound (Sound Design strand works in film, theatre, games)
programs.whatYouStudy: Individually negotiated study programme, re-planned each semester with the study coach. Four strands: Music Production ('musical, contextual and productional aspects that play a role in the production of music. From live performance to recorded music'); Sound Design (multidisciplinary work areas 'such as film, theatre, and games'); Music Technology ('development and meaningful application of technology within a creative or musical field'); Composition. Weekly 75-minute one-to-one lessons with a principal teacher, group classes, module choices, a practical internship project, artistic research, midterm presentations each January, and a final performance/presentation capstone. Facilities named by HKU: music studios, Blackbox workspace, libraries and multimedia libraries.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in a relevant field, or active as a professional at a comparable level, or comparable training abroad. English: IELTS Academic 6.0, TOEFL iBT 80, or Cambridge C1 Advanced / B2 First 169 (HKU general enrolment requirements page explicitly lists Master of Music, Music Design pathway). Bachelor diploma + transcript upload; document deadline 1 June before the start year.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check – conditionally yes. HKU wording: 'completed a bachelor's degree in a relevant field or are active as a professional at a comparable level. Or if you have followed a similar training abroad.' And explicitly: the 'academy can make an exception for candidates without a Bachelor of Music, but only in case of exceptional talent and a steady track record.' A BSc Software Engineering is arguably 'relevant' to the Music Technology strand, but the portfolio would have to carry the whole case.
programs.portfolioSpec: Portfolio of your work + motivation letter + preliminary MMus study plan + CV. HKU sets no fixed number of works, length or file format; the committee assesses whether you have 'successfully created a musical work' and whether you can 'explain and tell about the creative judgements and decisions' behind it. Number of works / duration / format: UNVERIFIED (not published).
programs.auditionSpec: Online interview with the admissions committee, discussing the admission documents and your motivation. No on-site practical exam is published for the Music Design pathway (the general Master of Music page lists practical exams 30 March – 10 April for the conservatoire; whether Music Design candidates sit these on-site is UNVERIFIED).
programs.applicationOpens: 1 October 2026 for the 2027-2028 academic year (HKU states: 'You can apply for the year 2027-2028 as of 1 October')
programs.deadline: Published for the TARGET intake: document upload rounds 24 November, 12 January, 16 February and 13 April; 'Non-EU/EEA candidates are advised to apply before 1 April.' General HKU document deadline 1 June before the start year.
programs.tuitionIntl: Statutory fee 2026-2027 verified at €2,694 (EEA / first Dutch degree only). Institutional fee for non-EEA master students: UNVERIFIED – HKU publishes it only via a fee calculator and a PDF that could not be read. Aggregators quote c. €10,500/yr; treat as unconfirmed.
programs.scholarship: NL Scholarship (formerly Holland Scholarship) – HKU is a participating institution
programs.stipend: NL Scholarship: €5,000 one-off, paid in the first year of study. Does not cover full non-EEA tuition. No full-ride scheme found at HKU.
programs.facilities: HKU music studios, Blackbox workspace, multimedia libraries. HKU Music and Technology is one of the longest-running music-technology departments in the Netherlands and runs multidisciplinary projects with animation, modern dance, theatre, film, games and visual art. Specific console / Atmos / immersive room inventory: UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Probably the single best structural fit in this slice: it is the only NL master that offers Music Production AND Sound Design as named strands, the assessment is documents + an online interview (no on-site audition, no instrument exam), and the 2027-2028 application window is already published. Main obstacle: he has no musical work yet — the portfolio plus the 'exceptional talent and steady track record' clause is the whole hurdle, so he needs roughly 12 months of serious releases/production before 1 April 2027. Secondary obstacle: funding is thin (€5,000 NL Scholarship against an unconfirmed but likely ~€10k non-EEA fee).

programs.program: Master of Music in Sonology
programs.university: Royal Conservatoire The Hague – Institute of Sonology
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (ECTS figure UNVERIFIED on the programme page; 2 years is stated)
programs.language: English
programs.institutionType: Conservatoire (Royal Conservatoire, part of University of the Arts The Hague)
programs.focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based); Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Electroacoustic composition; Immersive/Spatial Audio (Wave Field Synthesis)
programs.whatYouStudy: Electroacoustic music, computer music and sound art, with the premise that you compose the sound itself rather than composing with existing sounds — grounded in physical principles, perception or compositional concepts. Named studio/course areas: Composition and History of Electronic Music, Live Electronic Music, Algorithmic Composition, Field Recording & Sound Installations, Sound and Space, Wave Field Synthesis, Music Theory. Core of the degree is a self-directed two-year research project ending in a thesis situating the work in an artistic context; the institute warns 'in addition to your artistic activities, you will be writing extensively.' Master students may also take units from the One-Year Course.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's diploma relevant to the professional field of Sonology. Two-page study plan (mandatory): brief project description (practical, theoretical or both); a four-semester timeline including possible One-Year Course participation; a detailed project description with central research question, context and presentation format; an overview of the subjects for the final-examination thesis. English: non-EU applicants must prove proficiency by 1 September of the start year — IELTS min. 6.0, TOEFL min. 80, TOEIC, or Cambridge FCE/CAE/CPE, scores valid through that date.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES – explicitly. The bachelor may be in 'related subjects such as artificial intelligence, computer science or electronic engineering, musicology, music perception, film studies, or as a performing musician.' A BSc Software Engineering is a named-adjacent qualifying background.
programs.portfolioSpec: 'A portfolio with previous compositions, sound installations, recordings of live performances or research results in the form of computer programs, articles, theses, etc.' Note the last clause: code, articles and theses count as portfolio items. Number of works, durations and file formats: UNVERIFIED (deliberately not fixed).
programs.auditionSpec: None – 'There is no live admission exam.' No interview requirement is published (UNVERIFIED whether one is held informally).
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027-2028 cycle; applications go through Studielink plus the Royal Conservatoire's own portal, historically opening in the autumn
programs.deadline: 26 February 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (this was the deadline for September 2026 entry; expect late February 2027 for September 2027)
programs.tuitionIntl: €11,488 per year, institutional fee for non-EEA master students, academic year 2026-2027 (verified on koncon.nl). Statutory EEA fee €2,694. (A reduced €8,250 rate exists but applies only to the DNOA and NMO master programmes, not Sonology.)
programs.scholarship: Royal Conservatoire Excellence Scholarships – 'awarded to Master's candidates who perform best in the entrance exams (both EEA and non-EEA students are eligible)'
programs.stipend: UNVERIFIED – the English scholarship page gives no amount, no tuition-waiver statement and no deadline; detail exists only on a Dutch-language page. Must be confirmed directly with koncon.nl.
programs.facilities: The Institute of Sonology (founded 1960s, one of the two or three most historically important electronic music institutes in Europe alongside IRCAM and WDR). Wave Field Synthesis system for spatial audio, electronic music studios, field-recording and sound-installation infrastructure. Alumni pathway into composition, sound design, programming, teaching and PhD research.
programs.fitNotes: The most CS-friendly admission in the whole slice: a computer-science bachelor is named as acceptable, code and written research count as portfolio, and there is NO live audition — so his software background is an asset rather than a gap. The honest caveat is direction: Sonology is electroacoustic/sonic-arts research with heavy writing, not club music. It will make him a formidable sound designer and technologist but will not train him as a DJ or commercial producer. Also the most expensive option here at €11,488/yr with no verified full funding.

programs.program: Master in Immersive Audio (Focus Master within Master of Music)
programs.university: Conservatorium van Amsterdam (Amsterdam University of the Arts / AHK)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years full-time / 120 ECTS
programs.language: English
programs.institutionType: Conservatoire
programs.focus: Immersive / Spatial Audio; Recording/Engineering; Music Production
programs.whatYouStudy: Year 1: six-week modules introducing immersive production across genres, plus year-long courses in acoustics, mixing, production, management and research. Year 2: choose one specialisation track — 'Composing for Immersive Audio' or 'Production for Immersive Audio' — leading to a capstone project. Industry-standard DAW work (Pro Tools, Ableton) is assumed from day one rather than taught from scratch.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree (BA) in Music or a closely related field; alternatively a degree in sound engineering or music technology (Abbey Road Institute, SAE or equivalent) may be considered. Mandatory: 'Significant experience in audio engineering at a professional level is required.' Proficiency in Pro Tools (or main DAW), Ableton or other industry-standard DAWs required. Demonstrated interest in immersive audio and its applications.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check – partly. The page accepts 'a bachelor's degree (BA) in Music or a closely related field' and separately names sound-engineering/music-technology qualifications from SAE or Abbey Road Institute. A software-engineering BSc is not named, and the hard blocker is the separate requirement of 'significant experience in audio engineering at a professional level', which he does not have.
programs.portfolioSpec: Motivation letter, max 500 words; detailed CV; 'at least three high-quality stereo recordings demonstrating diverse musical styles'; optionally a research proposal for potential immersive audio projects. (Stereo, not immersive, mixes are what is asked for.)
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage. Stage 1: portfolio review. Stage 2: a 10-minute interview plus a 10-minute practical Pro Tools mixing test, with the admission decision given immediately afterwards. This is an on-site practical test of DAW competence.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027-2028 cycle
programs.deadline: 1 March 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (deadline expires 23:59 on the date stated; expect c. 1 March 2027 for September 2027)
programs.tuitionIntl: €8,250 for 2026-2027 — AHK institutional fee for non-EEA students on Master Music (was €7,375 in 2025-2026). Indexed annually, so expect slightly more for 2027-2028.
programs.scholarship: AHK Talent Grant; AHK Changemaker Scholarship; Profiling Fund. NL Scholarship (participation by AHK: UNVERIFIED).
programs.stipend: UNVERIFIED – the AHK tuition-fee page names Talent Grant, Changemaker Scholarship and Profiling Fund but publishes no amounts or coverage on that page.
programs.facilities: Conservatorium van Amsterdam's building on the Oosterdokseiland is one of the best-equipped conservatoire facilities in Europe; the Immersive Audio master is built around immersive/Atmos-capable production rooms. Exact console and immersive-room inventory: UNVERIFIED. Deep links into the Dutch recording and post-production industry.
programs.fitNotes: Best-in-slice for high-end studio craft and the growth area of spatial audio, and the €8,250 non-EEA fee is the cheapest of the Dutch conservatoires here. But it is the wrong door for him right now: 'significant experience in audio engineering at a professional level is required' plus an on-site 10-minute Pro Tools mixing test makes this a mid-career engineer's programme. Realistic path is to treat it as a 2029+ target after a diploma (SAE/Abbey Road are explicitly accepted) or two years of paid studio work.

programs.program: Master's Programme in Live Electronics (Focus Master within Master of Music)
programs.university: Conservatorium van Amsterdam (Amsterdam University of the Arts / AHK)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years full-time / 120 ECTS
programs.language: English
programs.institutionType: Conservatoire
programs.focus: Live Electronics / Performance; Electronic Music; Sound Design (spatialisation, audiovisual)
programs.whatYouStudy: Project-based coaching plus theory. Named content: using the acoustic instrument as an electronic controller through feature extraction and DSP; Max and Ableton Live training; sound spatialisation and audiovisual techniques; synthesizer programming and DAWs; electroacoustic techniques including 'waveform synthesis, granular synthesis, vocoders and Fourier analysis/resynthesis'; improvisation, composition and notation for electronic performance; new controllers (MIDI, motion-based devices, OSC); multidisciplinary and theatrical applications; professional practice and research skills.
programs.entryRequirements: 'The Live Electronics programme is intended for performers with an instrumental bachelor's degree or equivalent.' Candidates with bachelor's degrees in other musical fields may be admitted if they demonstrate proficiency in music theory and adequate performance ability. Own equipment mandatory: a recent MacBook Pro, Max and Ableton Live, a professional audio/MIDI interface, and appropriate microphones and cabling for live performance.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO (as published) – the programme is framed for holders of 'an instrumental bachelor's degree or equivalent', with the only stated flexibility being other MUSICAL bachelor degrees, and even then only 'if they demonstrate proficiency in music theory and adequate performance abilities'. The department does say it is open to 'laptopists' / software-based musicians 'as long as they can show proficiency in music theory and performance practice' — that is the only realistic opening for him, and it demands demonstrable music theory.
programs.portfolioSpec: 'Links to (an) audio and/or video recording(s) of a performance of live electronic music' plus a motivation letter. No fixed number of items or durations is published.
programs.auditionSpec: Selected applicants give a live electronic performance of no more than 10 minutes, followed by an interview of about 10 minutes. A genuine live performance audition.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027-2028 cycle
programs.deadline: 1 March 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (expect c. 1 March 2027 for September 2027)
programs.tuitionIntl: €8,250 for 2026-2027 — AHK institutional non-EEA fee, Master Music
programs.scholarship: AHK Talent Grant; AHK Changemaker Scholarship; Profiling Fund
programs.stipend: UNVERIFIED – amounts and coverage not published on the AHK fees page.
programs.facilities: CvA electronic music and live-electronics studios; Max/Ableton-based teaching infrastructure; strong Amsterdam new-music and multidisciplinary performance network. Specific room/equipment inventory: UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Directly relevant to a live-performing electronic artist, and cheap by Dutch standards. The barrier is the hardest kind for him: a 10-minute live electronic performance audition plus demonstrable music theory, on a programme written for conservatoire-trained instrumentalists. Only viable if he spends the next 12–18 months building a genuine live set (Ableton/Max, controllers) and shoring up theory — his coding background would be a real asset in the Max/DSP side once inside.

The Creative Producer main subject develops the producer as 'designer and/or manager of the technological elements of performances' — Codarts explicitly describes the role as fluid (producers also perform as instrumentalists, singers write songs, bass players produce, keyboard players manage technology). The published hard skill requirement is 'reasonable command of a harmonic instrument (piano/guitar)', which is a real filter for a self-taught DJ/producer.

programs.program: Master of Music – Pop / Creator Performer
programs.university: Fontys Academy of Music and Performing Arts (Fontys Hogeschool voor de Kunsten)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years full-time / 120 ECTS (ECTS UNVERIFIED on the page; 2 years full-time stated)

programs.institutionType: University of applied sciences / academy of music
programs.focus: Music Production (via Pop and Creator Performer profiles) — practical production emphasis UNVERIFIED, the framing is performer/creator rather than studio production

The distinctive mechanism is a personal budget: students receive funds to buy in teaching and can 'engage teachers globally, even outside Fontys', which in practice lets a producer assemble mentors that Fontys does not employ. Individual lessons, ensemble coaching, research guidance, and electives tailored to personal goals. Campus Zwijsenplein houses 17 art programmes and is pitched as experimental and collaborative.

programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check – not resolved. Fontys states applicants need 'a certain level of musical knowledge' and 'a relevant bachelor's degree' but does not address non-music bachelors either way. UNVERIFIED whether a BSc Software Engineering is treated as relevant; must be asked directly.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not published as a numbered portfolio. The assessed written submissions are the Personal Development Plan plus the A4 (500–1,000 word) research proposal. Audio/video portfolio requirement: UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: Entrance assessment / entrance exam with an exam commission that evaluates the Personal Development Plan as part of the application procedure. Live audition format for Pop / Creator Performer: UNVERIFIED.

programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED – Fontys directs applicants to a tuition-fee calculator; no non-EU amount published on the programme page. Living costs given as €900–1,100/month.

programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED. The genuinely unusual asset is the personal study budget, which can be spent on external teachers worldwide — useful for someone whose ideal mentors are working producers rather than academics.

The personal budget is a real advantage for a self-taught producer who wants to buy mentoring from industry names. Weakest evidence base in the NL set — non-music entry, portfolio spec, fee and current deadlines all need direct confirmation before he invests effort.

programs.program: Master of Music – Music Production (Master muziekproductie)
programs.university: KASK & Conservatorium, School of Arts Gent (HOGENT and Howest)
programs.degree: Master of Music (2nd cycle, Master in de muziek)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (on top of a 3-year bachelor; 3+2 path)
programs.language: Fully English-language master track alongside the Dutch one — 'There are no differences in curricula, competencies, learning outcomes or organization between the English-language programmes and their Dutch-language counterparts', and 'every academic year, dozens of foreign students start in the English master's'
programs.institutionType: Conservatory / school of arts within a university of applied sciences (HOGENT/Howest)
programs.focus: Music Production (primary); Recording/Engineering; songwriting and composition for production
programs.whatYouStudy: Year 1 (60 ECTS) is built around 'Producing & artistiek onderzoek master I' (31 credits), plus master seminars, professional skills and elective specialisations. Year 2 (60 ECTS) culminates in the 'Masterproef Producing' (33 credits) which integrates your own productions, commissions from external artists, and live performances. The department's stated philosophy is 'creativity, musicality (both performance and songwriting/composition) and technique', and it works in professionally equipped studios with extensive equipment collections. Explicit industry bridge via external mentors, internships and 'Arts in Practice' coursework. Programme founded in 1999 and described by the school as a unique combination in Flanders.
programs.entryRequirements: Degree route as published: 'a bachelor in performing music (for the master in classical music or jazz/pop), or a bachelor in composing music (for the master in music production, composition or music theory)'. Language: 'You can study all our master's programs in Dutch or English. There are no formal level requirements for English in the master programs, but the Vantage B2 level is strongly recommended' — i.e. NO IELTS/TOEFL required, a significant advantage given he has not tested yet.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check – bridging likely. Published wording: holders of 'an academic bachelor's degree in another artistic discipline may have to take a preparatory program before they are admitted to the master's programs.' Software engineering is not an artistic discipline, so a preparatory/bridging year is the probable route rather than direct entry. Worth noting the school confirms 'Scholarships can be awarded to students in a bridging program, preparation program and master program' — funding is not lost by going through a bridge.
programs.portfolioSpec: Digital portfolio only at application: 'You must upload links to an online portfolio or upload a PDF portfolio. We do not accept portfolios in physical format (usb, dvd, paper...).' No physical portfolio is required at interview stage for music production (unlike some other options). Plus a motivation statement of max 1 page. The department describes the music-production portfolio as four songs or compositions, each composed (individually or in collaboration) and/or recorded, mixed, produced, and/or performed as a musician and/or arranged by the candidate — but that 'four works' figure could not be confirmed on the master admission page itself, so treat the exact number as UNVERIFIED and confirm with paul.lamont@hogent.be.
programs.auditionSpec: Orientation test (oriënteringsproef), held several times per academic year. 'Based on your portfolio and master proposal, the orientation committee will decide whether or not to invite you for an intake interview or audition.' So stage 1 is dossier-only; an on-site interview/audition follows only if shortlisted.
programs.applicationOpens: Registration via webreg.hogent.be; opens ahead of each orientation-test session
programs.deadline: Orientation test session for music production: 24 August 2026 (with the equivalent 2025 session having a dossier deadline of 21 June for an August test) — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for September 2027 entry; expect sessions spread across the 2026-27 academic year plus a late-August 2027 session
programs.tuitionIntl: Non-EEA increased tuition 2026-2027: fixed administrative amount €916.20 + €131.40 per credit, i.e. €8,800.20 for a standard 60-credit year (verified on the KASK financial page). Some non-EEA students belong to an exempted category.
programs.scholarship: (1) KASK & Conservatorium's own non-EEA scholarship system for drama, visual arts, audiovisual arts and music: 'Annual scholarships will be awarded that equal the amount of the increased tuition for non EEA-students', and 'Scholarships can be awarded to students in a bridging program, preparation program and master program'. (2) Government of Flanders Master Mind Scholarship.
programs.fundingLevel: Full (potentially) — the KASK non-EEA scholarship is explicitly sized to the increased tuition, and Master Mind adds a living grant
programs.stipend: KASK non-EEA scholarship: equals the increased non-EEA tuition amount (i.e. effectively a tuition waiver of up to c. €8,800/yr) — number of awards and selection criteria UNVERIFIED, contact paul.lamont@hogent.be. Master Mind Scholarship: €10,225 grant per academic year PLUS a tuition-fee waiver (host institution may charge only the lowest local rate, €136.50 for 2026-2027); 2 academic years for a 120-ECTS master; cannot be combined with Erasmus+/Erasmus Mundus, BAEF or Fulbright; max 20 applications per institution. The 2026-2027 Master Mind call is closed — the 2027-2028 call should open around winter 2026/27: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.facilities: Professionally equipped studios with extensive equipment collections; the music-production department has run since 1999 and is presented as unique in Flanders for combining technique, musicality and creativity. External mentors and internships connect students to the working music industry. Specific console/Atmos inventory: UNVERIFIED. Alumni work as songwriters, performers, producers and composers.
programs.fitNotes: The strongest overall bet in this slice for a candidate in his exact position, for three reasons no other programme matches: (1) it is literally a Master in Music Production with a producing-focused capstone; (2) NO formal English test is required (B2 merely recommended), which removes his missing IELTS from the critical path; (3) the school runs a scholarship explicitly sized to wipe out the €8,800 non-EEA fee, and it is available to bridging/preparatory students too, on top of Master Mind's €10,225 + waiver. The obstacle is honest and structural: the master expects a bachelor in composing music, so he should plan for a preparatory/bridging year and treat September 2027 as entry into the bridge rather than the master.
