programs.auditionSpec: Round 2 is IN PERSON at RMC in Copenhagen, 25 minutes total: a 10-minute presentation of DIFFERENT material (live, recording or hybrid; up to 5 musicians including a sound engineer permitted), a 5-minute contextual presentation of methods and artistic traditions/influences, and a 10-minute interview. Scored on a 100-point scale; minimum 40 points to pass.
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 10,000 per study year for the Master programme (students from outside EU/EEA). Free for Danish, EU/EEA and Swiss citizens. 2025/26 figures.
programs.scholarship: None found on RMC's own tuition page. Listed fee EXEMPTIONS: participation in Erasmus Mundus, Fulbright or DIS programmes, bilateral agreements, permanent Danish residency (or qualification for it), Ukrainian temporary-residence holders, and certain Afghanistan-related cases. Third-party sources mention Danish Government Scholarships for highly qualified non-EU/EEA students - UNVERIFIED on RMC pages.
programs.fundingLevel: None verified (self-pay at EUR 10,000/yr unless an exemption route applies)
programs.applicationOpens: 16 December (opened 16 Dec 2025 for the Aug 2026 intake) - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect mid-December 2026 for a Sept 2027 start
programs.deadline: 3 February 2026 at 12:00 CET - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Prior-cycle rhythm: round-1 results 5 March, on-site round 2 on 7-10 April, programme start 17 August.
programs.fitNotes: On CRAFT this is the single best-aligned programme in the Nordics for a computer-based producer: RMC explicitly admits people who "work exclusively on computers" and no instrument is required. The obstacle is the degree gate - it wants a music bachelor, and the one-third "composed for and performed by others" rule plus a no-co-writes rule will be hard to satisfy from a self-taught DJ/producer portfolio. Also budget for a trip to Copenhagen: round 2 is on-site, not online.

programs.program: Master of Music (cand. musicae), Music Performance
programs.university: Rhythmic Music Conservatory (Rytmisk Musikkonservatorium, RMC)
programs.institutionType: Conservatory (state conservatoire under the Danish Ministry of Culture)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS, full-time with compulsory attendance
programs.language: Primarily Danish; entrance examination can be conducted in English if you do not speak Danish. Full-degree English delivery: UNVERIFIED
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics / Performance (artist-producer path; all genres including electronic)
programs.whatYouStudy: Artist-led two-year performance master built around your own artistic practice, an industry-facing external module and a concluding master's project presented publicly. The page states "All genres and styles are welcome" and "All genres and musical expressions are welcome", and electronic elements and samples are explicitly permitted in submissions. RMC's technology labs (electronic music, multimedia) and recording studios are available.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in music, or expected completion by 1 July of the entry year. You must appear "as a singer or instrumentalist and be artistically responsible for the music", though other roles supporting your artistic vision may be accepted on individual assessment. Application fee DKK 600.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK - No as published; a music bachelor is required, with discretionary recognition of "other artistically based Bachelor's degrees" only. A software-engineering BSc would be an exception case requiring direct negotiation with RMC.
programs.portfolioSpec: Round 1: 2-3 music examples ON VIDEO (mp4), total duration 10 minutes, showing "a live situation - with or without an audience". Videos must be "one-takes from a fixed camera ... without post-production". Supporting material: sheet music / graphic notation / text as PDF, plus supplementary descriptions of max 500 characters per example.
programs.auditionSpec: Round 2 IN PERSON at RMC, 25 minutes total: a 10-minute concert with minimum one and maximum four other people, a 5-minute presentation of your methods, and a 10-minute interview. Prior cycle held 7-10 April.
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 10,000 per study year for non-EU/EEA students (Master level). Free for EU/EEA/Swiss.
programs.scholarship: None found on RMC pages; same exemption list as other RMC programmes (Erasmus Mundus, Fulbright, DIS, bilateral agreements, Danish permanent residency).
programs.applicationOpens: 16 December (16 Dec 2025 for the Aug 2026 intake) - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date
programs.deadline: 3 February 2026 at 12:00 CET - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date
programs.fitNotes: Genuinely open to electronic/DJ-style live practice, and the live-performance framing suits someone who wants to perform, not just produce. But the fixed-camera, no-post-production one-take video requirement is brutal for a studio producer, and the requirement to be artistically responsible AS a performer is a stricter bar than RMC's Music Creation route. If he applies to RMC, Music Creation is the better door; keep this as the second choice on the same application cycle.

programs.program: Master of Music (MMus) in Tonmeister / Sound Engineer (Tonemester)
programs.university: The Royal Danish Academy of Music (Det Kongelige Danske Musikkonservatorium, DKDM / RDAM)
programs.institutionType: Conservatory (state conservatoire)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years. 120 ECTS is the standard for a Danish MMus but is not restated on the programme page - treat the ECTS figure as UNVERIFIED.
programs.language: English. RDAM states its programmes are taught in English; Danish proficiency is required only for Music Teaching, Aural Training and Music Theory programmes.
programs.focus: Recording / Engineering + Music Production (both rhythmic/pop-rock-jazz and classical)
programs.whatYouStudy: Principal study is music production and recording techniques, organised in close collaboration with the Danish Broadcasting Corporation (DR). Alongside: aural studies, basic piano, music theory and music history. Semester projects, set productions, studio recordings, CD recordings, film sound design and PA work for performances. Students can specialise by genre, sector, producer role or sound-technician role. "Well-equipped studios and plenty of mobile equipment." Study trips, masterclasses, company visits and listening tests.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor as Tonemester from DKDM, or Bachelor as Tonemester or equivalent from a Danish music conservatory, or Bachelor as Tonemester or equivalent from a higher education institution abroad at a level corresponding to DKDM. External applicants must sit an entrance examination in addition to holding the musical bachelor exam. RDAM's general prerequisites page states a "Bachelor's degree in music ... or equivalent from a higher education institution abroad at a level equivalent to RDAM".
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO. The published requirement is a Tonmeister bachelor or an equivalent conservatory-level music degree. A BSc Software Engineering does not meet this and no discretionary clause is offered on the pages read. This is the best-fitting curriculum in the whole slice and the hardest gate - he would need a music/audio bachelor or a documented equivalent first.
programs.portfolioSpec: Two musical production examples, EACH at least 7 minutes: one from the rhythmic genres (pop/rock/jazz) and one from classical music. Non-EU/EEA applicants must ADDITIONALLY submit a production plan documenting the creative process - timeline, equipment/software used, roles of participants and the recording context. (The certified audiogram, max 1 year old, is a Bachelor-level requirement, not master.)
programs.auditionSpec: Principal-study audition of approximately 30 minutes including assessment, built around a roughly 20-minute discussion of the submitted works plus theoretical and practical questions on your "technical and musical standpoint". EU/EEA applicants audition IN PERSON; non-EU/EEA applicants audition ONLINE, with a possible additional interview covering piano, ear training/solfege and theory. Graded on the Danish 7-point scale; decision based on documentation of previous education plus evaluation of the submitted productions.
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 11,100 per academic year for the Tonmeister/Sound Engineer MASTER (non-EU/EEA), paid in two instalments: 1 June (new students) and 1 September. Free for EU/EEA. For comparison the master fee table runs EUR 11,000-14,900 across specialisations.
programs.scholarship: None found on RDAM pages. Exemptions may exist under Danish national law and must be documented by the applicant (contact admission@dkdm.dk).
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (portal opening date not published on the pages read)
programs.deadline: 1 December for both EU/EEA and non-EU/EEA applicants at Master level - PRIOR CYCLE date pattern, confirm the 2027-intake date. RDAM aims to answer non-EU/EEA Bachelor and Master applicants about six weeks after the deadline.
programs.fitNotes: Content-wise this is the classic Nordic recording/production master - DR collaboration, real studios, both rhythmic and classical production, and non-EU applicants audition online so no travel cost. The deal-breaker is entry: it presumes a Tonmeister bachelor. Also note the portfolio demands a CLASSICAL production of 7+ minutes, which a DJ/electronic producer will not have. Realistic only after a bridging audio-engineering bachelor.

programs.program: MSc in Medialogy - specialisation in Sound and Music Computing
programs.university: Aalborg University (AAU)
programs.institutionType: Public university
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (4 semesters)
programs.language: English
programs.focus: Immersive / Spatial Audio and Sound Design (engineering-side sound and music computing)
programs.whatYouStudy: A creative interdisciplinary programme combining engineering, design, music performance, psycho-acoustics, signal processing and computer science. Content covered across the SMC track: sound processing, music perception and cognition, New Interfaces for Musical Expression; a Sonic Interaction project semester with courses in Embodied Interaction, Sound and Music Signal Analysis, and Physical Models for Sound Synthesis. First-semester electives include Sound and Music Perception and Cognition; after semester 1 you choose whether to continue in Medialogy or specialise in Sound and Music Computing. AAU's problem-based learning means every semester is built around a group project. Industry destinations named by AAU: Bang & Olufsen, T-Rex Engineering, IO Interactive, Carl Martin, Dicentia. NOTE: the standalone MSc in Engineering "Sound and Music Computing" was CLOSED FOR ADMISSION FROM 2024 and replaced by this specialisation inside Medialogy.
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree in a qualifying area - the published list includes BSc Medialogy, Datalogi (computer science), Software and various engineering-related fields; "Applicants with other backgrounds will receive individual evaluation by the Study Board of Media Technology." Documented English proficiency required. Non-EU applicants must also submit final documentation by 15 June.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES - this is the one programme in the slice built for his exact background. Qualifying bachelors explicitly include "BSc Medialogy, Datalogi, Software, and various engineering-related fields", and "Applicants with other backgrounds will receive individual evaluation by the Study Board of Media Technology." No music degree, no music theory and no audition are demanded.
programs.portfolioSpec: None published. Admission is on academic transcripts plus English proficiency documentation - no portfolio of works is requested on the pages read.
programs.auditionSpec: None - no audition, no on-site test.
programs.tuitionIntl: DKK 57,850 per SEMESTER (approx. EUR 7,745) for engineering/technical programmes, i.e. roughly EUR 15,490 per year. Payment due 1 August for the autumn semester. Full refund before study start, 75% within the first month, none thereafter (visa delays excepted).
programs.scholarship: AAU awards approximately 15 scholarships per year consisting of a full TUITION WAIVER plus a monthly stipend of DKK 11,225 (approx. EUR 1,503). All non-EU applicants are automatically considered - no separate application.
programs.fundingLevel: Full (competitive - approx. 15 awards per year university-wide); otherwise self-pay
programs.stipend: Full tuition waiver + DKK 11,225 per month (approx. EUR 1,503) for scholarship holders
programs.applicationOpens: Portal opens mid-December; up to 3 prioritised programme choices allowed
programs.deadline: 15 January, 23:59 CET for non-EU/EEA fee-paying applicants (September intake), decisions 10 April. EU/EEA deadline is 1 March. PRIOR CYCLE pattern - for a Sept 2027 start expect 15 January 2027; confirm when the portal opens in December 2026.
programs.fitNotes: The realistic fully-funded Nordic option for him: his BSc Software Engineering is directly qualifying, there is no audition or portfolio, and the ~15 AAU scholarships give a genuine tuition-waiver-plus-stipend path with automatic consideration. The honest caveat is that this is sound and music COMPUTING - signal processing, synthesis models, sonic interaction, C++/Python-style project work - not DJing, mixing records or A&R. It builds him into an audio developer or technical sound designer. Best used as the funded safety net alongside one or two craft-focused applications.

programs.program: Master's Programme in Performance - Music Production (Masterprogram i musik: musiker, musikproduktion)
programs.university: Royal College of Music in Stockholm (Kungl. Musikhogskolan, KMH)
programs.institutionType: Conservatory / public university college of music
programs.degree: Master of Fine Arts in Music (konstnarlig master)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (hogskolepoang), full-time
programs.language: SWEDISH. The programme page states Swedish is the primary teaching language and the entrance examination is conducted in Swedish; the entrance-test page repeats: "Please note that test is in Swedish as Swedish is the main language for the Master's programme."
programs.focus: Music Production (including music for TV, film, games and interactive media)
programs.whatYouStudy: "Advanced sound and music production focusing on production planning, composition, arranging and orchestration, recording, mixing and mastering." Course spine: Musikproduktion 1 & 2 (theory plus practical work, with seminars in design and communication theory, musical leadership, business insight, entrepreneurship, and music law/copyright) and Eget konstnarligt projekt 1 & 2 (self-directed production projects). Artistic-research preparation courses shared with other master's students. Final year includes a 30-credit thesis project: an extensive music production carried out with research methodology. KMH studios; programme contact is Studio Director Peter Schyborger.
programs.entryRequirements: General eligibility for advanced-level (second-cycle) studies; a completed first-cycle degree of at least 180 ECTS, specifically a Bachelor of Fine Arts in Music or a Bachelor in Music Production (180 credits) or equivalent; and a pass in the entrance examination. Application via antagning.se / universityadmissions.se, code KMH-85000.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO, effectively. Published wording requires a "Bachelor of Fine Arts in Music or Bachelor in Music Production (180 credits), or equivalent", and the entrance test is held in Swedish. Two independent blockers for a Tunisian software-engineering graduate.
programs.portfolioSpec: Test 1 - Portfolio and presentation (digital): "The portfolio must contain four digital files with music productions of your own." For each production you must document composer, text author and arranger names; the recording and mixing techniques used; the performers; and your work process and tools. Plus a "comprehensive description of yourself: who you are, musical background, areas of musical interests (approx. 500 words)", a CV, and a "description of what you would like to develop during your master studies (approx. 500 words)". Graded 0-25 points, 10 required to pass.
programs.auditionSpec: Test 2 - conversation, ONLINE via Zoom, approximately 30 minutes, with the jury, based on your portfolio material. Conducted in SWEDISH. Assessed 0-25, 10 or above passes. No travel to Stockholm required for the test itself.
programs.tuitionIntl: SEK 264,000 per academic year for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens, billed regularly through the studies. Application fee SEK 900 paid via universityadmissions.se. EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay neither.
programs.scholarship: "KMH offers a limited number of scholarships that cover the entire tuition fee cost to talented master level students." Number of awards, application process and eligibility conditions are NOT published - UNVERIFIED. Fee-paying master's students also receive FAS+ student insurance.
programs.fundingLevel: Full possible but limited and competitive (tuition-only); otherwise self-pay at SEK 264,000/yr
programs.stipend: Tuition-fee coverage only; no living stipend published
programs.applicationOpens: 1 December (opened 1 Dec 2025 for the Aug 2026 intake) - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date
programs.deadline: 15 January 2026 (final application and priority ranking on antagning.se; code KMH-85000), entrance exams 7-15 March 2026, programme start 31 August 2026 - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect 1 Dec 2026 to 15 Jan 2027 for a Sept 2027 start
programs.fitNotes: Curriculum is close to ideal - production planning, arranging, recording, mixing, mastering, plus a full-scale production as the thesis, and tuition can in principle be fully waived by a KMH scholarship. But the programme is taught in Swedish AND the audition conversation is in Swedish, which rules it out for him unless he spends a year on Swedish. Worth keeping on a longer 2028/2029 horizon only if he decides to learn Swedish; otherwise deprioritise despite the excellent content.

programs.program: Master's Programme in Composition - Electroacoustic Music (Masterprogram i komposition, elektroakustisk musik)
programs.university: Royal College of Music in Stockholm (Kungl. Musikhogskolan, KMH)
programs.institutionType: Conservatory / public university college of music
programs.degree: Master of Fine Arts in Music (konstnarlig master)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (hogskolepoang), full-time
programs.language: Programme pages are in Swedish and the entrance test material shows no English alternative; entry requires English 6 / English level 2. Language of instruction NOT explicitly stated - UNVERIFIED, assume Swedish-dominant.
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics / Sonic Arts (electroacoustic concert music, interactive sound art, live electronics, experimental electronica)
programs.whatYouStudy: Composition studies at KMH focus on "knowledge, experimental investigations and artistic deepening". The electroacoustic specialisation covers electroacoustic concert music, interactive sound art, live electronics and experimental electronica. Students get access to well-equipped studios and concert halls to present newly composed music, often together with students from other specialisations or in collaboration with professional musical life. Roughly 4 students admitted per year for autumn entry.
programs.entryRequirements: General eligibility for advanced-level studies; an artistic bachelor's degree in music (180 ECTS); English 6 or English level 2; and a passing score on the mandatory entrance audition. Application code KMH-29000.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO as published - "an artistic bachelor's degree in music (180 ECTS)" is required. No discretionary clause found on the pages read.
programs.portfolioSpec: Prov 1 (work sample): THREE different compositions, maximum 30 minutes total, all composed within the last three years - "Arbetsprovets ska bestaa av tre olika kompositioner som ger en tydlig bild av din konstnarlig praktik". Accepted formats: scores as PDF, audio as AIFF/WAV/MP3, digital representations, video as MPEG-4 for audiovisual works, and single-page PDF documentation for sound installations. Accompanying single PDF must contain: project description (max 300 words), bullet-point CV (max 300 words), artist statement (max 200 words), motivation for applying (max 200 words) and individual work descriptions (max 50 words each). Work sample due 26 January in the prior cycle.
programs.auditionSpec: Prov 2, conducted ONLINE/at distance: a composition test of 4-8 hours based on materials provided to you, plus a jury interview of approximately 15 minutes. Prior cycle held 7-15 March. No English-language alternative for the test is mentioned.
programs.tuitionIntl: SEK 264,000 per academic year for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens; SEK 900 application fee. Free for EU/EEA/Swiss.
programs.scholarship: "KMH offers a limited number of scholarships that cover the entire tuition fee cost to talented master level students." Details UNVERIFIED.
programs.fundingLevel: Full possible but limited and competitive (tuition-only); otherwise self-pay
programs.stipend: Tuition-fee coverage only; no living stipend published
programs.applicationOpens: 1 December (1 Dec 2025 for the Aug 2026 intake) - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date
programs.deadline: 15 January 2026 on antagning.se (code KMH-29000); work sample by 26 January 2026; on-site/online auditions 7-15 March 2026 - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date
programs.fitNotes: Strong for someone who wants live electronics and experimental electronica with world-class studios, and the online 4-8 hour composition test avoids travel. But it is an art-music composition track, not a route to club/dance production, it demands three finished compositions from the last three years, it requires an artistic music bachelor, and the working language is Swedish. Poor match for his stated DJ/producer goal - list it only as an ambition-stretch option.

programs.program: Experimental Composition and Creation - Master of Fine Arts in Music with Specialisation in Composition (K2KMP)
programs.university: University of Gothenburg - Academy of Music and Drama (Hogskolan for scen och musik)
programs.institutionType: Public university / academy of music and drama
programs.degree: Master of Fine Arts in Music (MFA), specialisation Composition
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS
programs.language: Instruction primarily in ENGLISH
programs.focus: Sonic Arts / Electronic Music (practice-based composition and creation)
programs.whatYouStudy: The programme spans "instrumental and vocal music, sound art, performance and sound installation, electronic and free improvised music". Students pursue an individual explorative project while engaging with visiting experts and collaborating ensembles. Small cohort: only 8-10 students admitted. GU also states that composition students share studios and courses in electronic music and sound art with the music and sound production programme in the professional studio environment at Brewhouse (Gothenburg's music-industry hub) - this statement appears on GU's music overview page rather than the programme page.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in Fine Arts or equivalent; demonstrated musical knowledge and skills assessed via admission tests; English proficiency at English 6 / B level or an equivalent international test score.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK - unlikely. Requirement is a "Bachelor's degree in Fine Arts or equivalent" plus admission tests. A BSc Software Engineering is not a fine-arts degree, so admission would hinge entirely on the "or equivalent" assessment and on test performance. Treat as a long shot.
programs.portfolioSpec: Applicants must submit "a description of your idea" - an explorative project proposal - with the application, which together with the admission tests forms the basis for selection. The exact media, number of works, durations and file formats are NOT published on the programme page - UNVERIFIED. Request the provbeskrivning from the Academy.
programs.auditionSpec: Admission tests are referenced but their format (on-site vs remote, content, duration) is NOT published on the page read - UNVERIFIED.
programs.tuitionIntl: Full education cost SEK 566,000 for the whole programme, with a first instalment of SEK 141,500. EU/EEA citizens and holders of a Swedish residence permit pay no fees.
programs.scholarship: None found on the programme page - UNVERIFIED
programs.fundingLevel: UNVERIFIED (no programme-level funding found; self-pay SEK 566,000 total)
programs.applicationOpens: 1 December (opened 1 Dec 2025 for the Aug 2026 start)
programs.deadline: CRITICAL SCHEDULING ISSUE: the programme "accepts new students every two years". The 1 Dec 2025 - 15 Jan 2026 window was for the August 2026 - June 2028 cohort, and GU's application page states the next opening is DECEMBER 2027 for an AUTUMN 2028 start. There is therefore NO September 2027 intake. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm with the Academy, but plan around autumn 2028.
programs.fitNotes: English-taught, tiny cohort, real electronic-music and sound-art studio access at Brewhouse - attractive on paper and one of very few English-taught Swedish options in this field. Two hard problems: the biennial intake means it cannot serve a September 2027 start (next is autumn 2028), and it wants a fine-arts bachelor. Note it as a 2028 target and ask the Academy in autumn 2026 whether the "or equivalent" clause could cover an engineering degree plus a strong portfolio.

programs.program: Master's Programme in Music (Konstnarligt masterprogram i musik) - Composition: Music for Film and Media (Komposition - Musik for film och media)
programs.university: Malmo Academy of Music (Musikhogskolan i Malmo), Lund University
programs.institutionType: Public university / academy of music (Faculty of Fine and Performing Arts, Lund University)
programs.degree: Master of Fine Arts in Music (konstnarlig master)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years. 120 ECTS is the standard for a Swedish konstnarligt masterprogram but is not restated on the admission page - treat as UNVERIFIED.
programs.language: UNVERIFIED - the admission pages are in Swedish and the final interview is held on site at the Academy; confirm whether the programme can be followed in English.
programs.focus: Film / Game Sound and applied composition (scoring for film and media)
programs.whatYouStudy: Composition and production of music for film and media: writing, orchestrating and MIXING original scores to picture. The admission process itself indicates the working method - composing a theme and scoring an assigned film clip, delivering lead sheet, audio and video. Malmo's composition studio is described by third-party programme listings as "the programme's platform for students' creative work in electroacoustic music, live electronics, and experimental studio production" - AGGREGATOR-SOURCED, not confirmed on a Lund page, so treat as UNVERIFIED. A separate general Composition specialisation and a Composition Diploma also exist at Malmo.
programs.entryRequirements: "Grundlaggande behorighet for hogskolestudier" (basic Swedish higher-education entrance qualification) plus a bachelor's degree in music or equivalent completed by programme start. English/Swedish language requirements: UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO as published - "a bachelor's degree in music or equivalent" by programme start. No clause addressing non-music degrees was found.
programs.portfolioSpec: 3-4 portfolio pieces representing your creative work. At least ONE must be a QuickTime video (.mov) containing an original film score that you composed AND mixed. At least ONE must be sheet music in PDF; MP3 recordings must accompany any scores. Plus a one-page written statement of your study goals, and a CV documenting credentials and previous studies. Portfolio submission deadline was 21 January in the prior cycle (application deadline 15 January).
programs.auditionSpec: Three-part process. Part 1: jury evaluation of the submitted works; those who pass advance. Part 2 - distance/take-home exam (due 23 February in the prior cycle): compose an independent theme, then write music to an assigned film clip incorporating that theme, submitting a lead sheet PDF, an MP3, a .mov video and a written rationale. Part 3 - INTERVIEW ON SITE at the Academy in week 10, discussing the submitted work, the exam tasks, your creative background and your expectations of the studies.
programs.deadline: 15 January 2026 (application), portfolio 21 January 2026, distance exam 23 February 2026, on-site interview week 10 of 2026 - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (Swedish national cycle normally opens mid-October to 1 December)
programs.tuitionIntl: Swedish non-EU/EEA tuition applies (Lund University fee-paying rules), but the amount for this specific programme is UNVERIFIED - request it from the Academy.
programs.scholarship: None found - UNVERIFIED
programs.fitNotes: The most transparently specified admission process in the Swedish slice, and the take-home scoring exam is exactly the kind of test a self-taught producer could actually smash - compose a theme, score a clip, mix it. But it is film/media scoring rather than club music, it demands a music bachelor and notated sheet music, and the final interview is on site in Malmo. Realistic only if he can produce notated scores; otherwise the sheet-music requirement alone disqualifies him.

programs.program: Creative Music Technology - Master's programme (MMUST)
programs.university: Norwegian University of Science and Technology (NTNU)
programs.institutionType: Public university
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS, of which the thesis alone is 60 ECTS
programs.language: English (instruction conducted entirely in English)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Music technology and creative audio production
programs.whatYouStudy: A practice-heavy degree: half the programme (60 ECTS) is the thesis itself, an artistic/creative project, with the remaining time in supporting courses. Focus on developing expertise in audio technology and its creative possibilities and on a "deeper aesthetic understanding of new musical expression made possible by technology", worked interdisciplinarily. An intensive introduction to AUDIO PROGRAMMING (Csound) is offered to those without prior experience - directly leverageable by a software engineer. Detailed course list beyond this: UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: "A bachelor's degree with a music technology specialization (at least 80 ECTS) or equivalent", with a grade point average of at least C. English proficiency required for all international students - IELTS, TOEFL or Pearson, and the test "should not be older than two years at time of the application deadline". Documents: passport, transcripts, diplomas, CV, motivation letter (max 1 page); non-EU/EEA applicants must also provide funding documentation.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK - no on paper, but a real individual-assessment door exists. Published: "Admission requires an applicant to have completed a bachelor's degree with a music technology specialization (at least 80 ECTS) or equivalent. If you have a different background but think you are qualified, you will be able to apply and get an individual assessment of your previous qualifications." Only one external degree (Music Production from Kristiania University College) automatically qualifies; everything else, including his BSc, goes to individual assessment. Worth a direct pre-application enquiry with a portfolio attached.
programs.portfolioSpec: NONE published on the admission page - required documents are passport, transcripts, diplomas, CV and a max 1-page motivation letter. Whether an artistic portfolio is requested during individual assessment: UNVERIFIED. Ask the programme coordinator.
programs.auditionSpec: None published - no audition or on-site test listed.
programs.tuitionIntl: NOK 198,800 per academic year (2025/2026) for students from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland. Students admitted before autumn 2023 are exempt.
programs.scholarship: "NTNU does not offer scholarships covering tuition costs." None found.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (Norwegian non-EU cycle typically opens in October)
programs.deadline: 1 December for non-EU/non-EEA applicants; 1 March for EU/EEA/Swiss; 15 April for Nordic citizens. PRIOR CYCLE pattern - for a September 2027 start expect 1 December 2026; confirm.
programs.fitNotes: Very appealing structurally: English-taught, 60-ECTS creative thesis so he would spend a full year making work, no audition, no portfolio in the published requirements, and a Csound audio-programming on-ramp that rewards a software engineer. Two real problems: the 80-ECTS music-technology prerequisite means he must win an individual assessment, and NOK 198,800/yr with an explicit no-scholarship statement makes it the most expensive unfunded option in the slice. Note also that NTNU's separate Music, Communication and Technology (MCT) master no longer resolves on ntnu.edu (both its programme and admission pages return 404) - treat MCT as discontinued/UNVERIFIED.

programs.program: Master of Music in Composition - specialisation Creative Music Technology
programs.university: Norwegian Academy of Music (Norges musikkhogskole, NMH)
programs.institutionType: Conservatory / state academy of music
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS, full-time, autumn start
programs.language: Norwegian / English
programs.focus: Electroacoustic Composition / Live Electronics / Sonic Arts with a strong technology component
programs.whatYouStudy: The Composition master has four focus areas - acoustic composition, interdisciplinary composition, creative music technology and jazz composition. The Creative Music Technology specialisation is "aimed at composition students who wish to work with an expanded range of materials and approaches within an electroacoustic and music technology-oriented context" and "extends to include areas such as instrument design, electroacoustic composition, sound installation, video, electrical engineering, experimental performance practice, and creative programming". Delivery is seminar-based full-time study combining teacher-led instruction, academic supervision and independent study; attendance generally optional except where a course specifies otherwise. The core is a master project: an original artistic project with subprojects, developed from the first semester. One or two semesters abroad at partner institutions are possible without extending the degree. Staff include Anders Tveit (Assistant Professor, Music Technology) alongside composition professors Eivind Buene and Jon Henrik Hellstenius.
programs.entryRequirements: Per the 2025 study plan: a Bachelor of Music with a minimum of 80 ECTS credits in Composition (jazz-composition applicants may substitute equivalent credits in jazz/improvised-music performance subjects or 80 credits in musicology). Entrance evaluation emphasises "original compositions" demonstrating a "high degree of artistic achievement". International applicants must additionally meet the GSU-list minimum academic qualifications (hkdir.no) and NMH's language requirements.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO. The study plan requires "a Bachelor of Music with minimum 80 ECTS credits in Composition". A BSc Software Engineering does not qualify and no discretionary clause was found on the pages read.
programs.portfolioSpec: Original compositions are submitted for jury evaluation, with assessment weighted on "original compositions" showing high artistic achievement - but the exact number of works, durations, formats and accompanying documents are NOT published on the pages read. UNVERIFIED - request the audition requirements from opptak@nmh.no.
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED - the admission pages read do not state whether a live audition/interview is required or whether recorded submissions suffice for overseas applicants. Confirm with opptak@nmh.no.
programs.tuitionIntl: NOK 220,000 per academic year for students from outside the EU/EEA/Switzerland (performance studies at NMH). Must be paid IN FULL by 1 June before the academic year starts - instalments are not permitted, and missing the deadline means automatic loss of study rights. Exempt: exchange students from NMH partner universities, and students who began before autumn 2023.
programs.scholarship: "NMH does not provide financial aid to cover tuition costs." None found.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 November
programs.deadline: 15 December for undergraduate and graduate programmes (applications open 1 November). PRIOR CYCLE pattern - for a September 2027 start expect 15 December 2026; confirm.
programs.fitNotes: Excellent facilities and a genuinely technology-forward composition environment (instrument design, sound installation, creative programming) in Norway's leading music academy. For this candidate it is effectively closed: the 80-ECTS-in-composition prerequisite is the strictest gate in the slice, tuition is NOK 220,000/yr payable in one lump by 1 June with zero scholarships, and the portfolio spec is not even published. Note also that NMH's former "Master of Music in Performance Technology and Electroacoustic Composition" no longer appears among current graduate programmes - it has been absorbed into this Composition master.

programs.program: Master's Programme in Popular Music - specialisation Electronic Music
programs.university: University of Agder (UiA)
programs.institutionType: Public university
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS, full-time
programs.language: English (taught in English at the Kristiansand campus)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics / Music Production
programs.whatYouStudy: The programme emphasises balancing "practice, composition, programming and production" with theoretical grounding in popular musicology. The Electronic Music specialisation focuses on "music technology and sound design in the studio, or use of Live Electronics in a concert context" and on "performance and its relationship to music technology and sound design". Course structure (2023 plan, indicative): MF-404 Aesthetics (5 ECTS), MF-405 Audience Development and Marketing (5 ECTS), MF-406 Arts Entrepreneurship (5 ECTS), MUR402-405 Individual Performance and Interpretation I-IV (15 ECTS each), music-business courses, musicological theory, and a 30-ECTS master's thesis. Sibling specialisations: Performing Music, World Music, Songwriting, and Music Business and Management. UiA also runs a Bachelor in Electronic Music, so the department has an established electronic-music teaching base.
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree or equivalent of at least three years (180 credits) with at least 20 credits at level 2 in the specialisation unit; for the Electronic Music/performance specialisations, at least 80 credits in performing music / electronic music, a music-technology degree, or another approved programme; minimum grade average of C across the bachelor. Performance specialisations also require "a very high level on the principle instrument" plus documented music theory/analysis coursework equivalent to UiA's own bachelor. Programme coordinator: Per Elias Drablos (per.e.drablos@uia.no).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO as published - the entry route requires "at least 80 credits in performing/electronic music, music technology degree, or other approved programs" plus a C average, plus documented music theory/analysis. A pure software-engineering BSc would need an exceptional individual assessment; nothing on the pages read promises one.
programs.portfolioSpec: Applicants submit a PROJECT PROPOSAL with the application, which feeds the evaluation. The exact audio/video portfolio specification (number of works, durations, formats) is NOT published on the pages read - UNVERIFIED. Request it from the programme coordinator.
programs.auditionSpec: Entrance exam has two equally weighted parts: AUDITION worth 50% of the score with a minimum of 10 out of 20 required to pass, and INTERVIEW worth 50% (also scored 10-20), held only after the audition is passed. Whether the audition may be submitted as a recording or held online for overseas applicants: UNVERIFIED - confirm before booking travel.
programs.tuitionIntl: NOK 135,000 per academic year (60 ECTS) for 2026/2027 - Category B, which explicitly covers the Master in Popular Music and the Master in Popular Music - Music Business and Management. Payment deadline 1 September for active students. The cheapest Norwegian option in this slice.
programs.scholarship: "The University of Agder does not offer any scholarships for 2026/2027." None found; no fee waivers mentioned.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 November
programs.deadline: Non-EU/EEA international applicants: 1 November - 15 December, with an extended deadline of 15 April 2026 noted for the 2026 intake - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect 1 Nov - 15 Dec 2026 for a Sept 2027 start
programs.fitNotes: Of all the Nordic craft-focused options this is the closest fit to "I want to make electronic music and perform it": English-taught, an explicit Electronic Music specialisation covering studio sound design and live electronics, entrepreneurship and audience-development modules that map onto a DJ career, and at NOK 135,000/yr it is roughly a third the cost of NTNU or NMH. The obstacles are the 80-credits-in-music prerequisite, an audition worth 50% of the score whose remote-submission status is unpublished, and a flat no-scholarship policy. Highest-value action in this slice: email Per Elias Drablos in autumn 2026 with a portfolio and ask directly whether an engineering BSc plus documented electronic-music practice can satisfy the 80-credit rule.

programs.program: Master's Programme in Music Technology - study profiles: Recording Arts / Film and Game Music Producer / Creative Electronic Music Practices
programs.university: Sibelius Academy, University of the Arts Helsinki (Uniarts Helsinki)
programs.institutionType: Conservatory / national university of the arts
programs.durationEcts: 2.5 years / 120 ECTS, plus up to 60 ECTS of complementary studies if required
programs.language: Finnish, Swedish and English - and "English having a very pronounced status within the Music Technology programme"
programs.focus: Recording / Engineering + Film & Game Sound + Electronic Music Production (choose one of three profiles)
programs.whatYouStudy: You select ONE of three study profiles at application: Recording Arts; Film and Game Music Producer; or Creative Electronic Music Practices. Studies are built individually around a Final Project - applicants must submit both a FINAL PROJECT PLAN and a STUDY PLAN of up to 150 ECTS as part of the application, so the curriculum is negotiated to your artistic goal. The Music Technology department also shares teaching with Aalto's Media Lab (Aalto students may take Sibelius Academy Music Technology courses, and vice versa). Detailed course lists: UNVERIFIED - the admissions guide is the source and is reissued each cycle.
programs.entryRequirements: Eligibility routes: a lower university degree in music; OR "a lower university degree in another field and, additionally, higher education studies in music"; OR an applicable foreign degree that provides eligibility for corresponding higher-education studies in the awarding country. Holders of "a higher education degree in the field of technology or media" may apply if they possess sufficient music coursework. Sufficient proficiency in Finnish, Swedish or English is required. Non-EU applicants pay a EUR 100 application fee.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: THE CLOSEST TO A YES IN THIS SLICE, with one condition. Published wording: eligibility via "a lower university degree in another field and, additionally, higher education studies in music", and applicants holding "a higher education degree in the field of technology or media" may apply if they have sufficient music coursework. A BSc Software Engineering is therefore explicitly contemplated as a base degree - but he must first acquire DOCUMENTED higher-education music studies (e.g. open-university music courses, a music-technology certificate) to bolt onto it. That is a concrete, achievable action item before the 2027 call opens.
programs.portfolioSpec: ADVANCE ASSIGNMENTS = 40% of the total evaluation. (1) Portfolio and presentation: MAXIMUM 10 MINUTES TOTAL, with a 3-minute presentation recommended; include UP TO 3 WORKS, at least one of which must be audio or audiovisual; formats MP3 for audio or MP4 with H.264/AAC codecs for video. (2) Project description form as PDF detailing each portfolio work. (3) Motivation letter, maximum 2 A4 pages. (4) CV covering education, training, artistic work and experience. (5) Final project plan, maximum 2 A4 pages. (6) Study plan of maximum 150 ECTS.
programs.auditionSpec: ENTRANCE EXAMINATION = 60% of the total evaluation, held REMOTELY (prior cycle: 31 March - 1 April). Two components: an INSTRUMENT/VOICE AUDITION of 7-10 minutes worth 40% of the exam, demonstrating technical proficiency and musical sensitivity; and an INTERVIEW of up to 25 minutes worth 60% of the exam, covering your portfolio, your performance, your background and the feasibility of your project. Note the instrument/voice audition is a real hurdle for a non-instrumentalist - clarify with siba.admissions@uniarts.fi how it is applied to Music Technology applicants.
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 28,000 per academic year for non-EU/EEA/Swiss students in English-taught programmes starting August 2026 or later. "The amount of the fee will stay the same for the statutory duration of your degree studies." Plus a EUR 100 application fee. The single most expensive option in this slice.
programs.scholarship: Explicitly none from the university: "The university does not grant any scholarships to cover the tuition fee for students starting in August 2026 or later", and "Uniarts Helsinki does not grant scholarships for living expenses." ONE published workaround: Finnish- and Swedish-taught programmes are exempt from fees, and "students may apply to change their language of study to Finnish or Swedish", eliminating the fee going forward - relevant here because Music Technology's languages of tuition include Finnish and Swedish. Whether the national Finland Scholarship (EUR 5,000 relocation grant, first year of master's studies) applies at Uniarts: UNVERIFIED.
programs.fundingLevel: None from the institution (unless the Finnish/Swedish language-of-study route is available and workable)
programs.applicationOpens: 7 January in the prior cycle. CRITICAL AND FAVOURABLE: the programme page states the NEXT application period for this programme is in 2027 and that the admissions guide will be updated in OCTOBER-NOVEMBER 2026 - so the September 2027 intake is the live target and the guide lands right when he should be preparing.
programs.deadline: 21 January 2026 at 15:00 EET (supporting documents by 28 January 2026, 15:00 EET); entrance exams 31 March - 1 April 2026 remotely; results 10 April 2026; study-place confirmation by 9 July 2026 - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date from the admissions guide published Oct-Nov 2026
programs.fitNotes: The single best CONTENT match in the Nordics for his ambitions - a Creative Electronic Music Practices profile at a top-tier conservatory, remote entrance exams so no travel cost, and an eligibility clause that explicitly contemplates a technology bachelor. Two serious obstacles: EUR 28,000/yr with a written no-scholarship policy makes it self-pay-only unless the Finnish/Swedish language-of-study exemption can be used, and there is a 7-10 minute instrument/voice audition worth 40% of the entrance exam. Action items before the Oct-Nov 2026 guide drops: acquire documented higher-education music studies, and email siba.admissions@uniarts.fi about both the instrument audition and the Finnish/Swedish fee-exemption route.

programs.program: Master's Programme in New Media - major Sound in New Media
programs.university: Aalto University, School of Arts, Design and Architecture (Aalto Media Lab)
programs.institutionType: Public university (art, design and technology)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS, full-time
programs.language: English (thesis may be written in English, Finnish or Swedish)
programs.focus: Sound Design / Sonic Arts / Immersive Audio and music technology
programs.whatYouStudy: The programme combines the art, design and media-driven aspects of sound, "covering a wide range of disciplines from concept design to live performance and from storytelling to programming". It explores "emerging digital technology and its aural impact in society" through project-oriented, hands-on learning. Study areas: sound design, sonic interaction, music technology, audio-visual production and interactive art. Students build a PERSONALISED study plan and may take courses from Sibelius Academy's Music Technology department. Graduates work in "sound and music computing, sound art, sonic interaction design" and related creative industries, or continue to doctoral study. Programme contact: antti.ikonen@aalto.fi.
programs.entryRequirements: A "relevant Bachelor's degree"; portfolio; motivation letter of maximum 4,000 characters explaining interest and objectives; CV covering background, experience, exhibitions and achievements; and an English proficiency test (IELTS/TOEFL/PTE). No GRE/GMAT/GPA threshold. Admissions run ONCE a year.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES in practice - the only stated degree requirement is a "relevant Bachelor's degree" with NO music-degree and NO music-theory requirement, and this is a design/technology programme run by Aalto Media Lab whose remit explicitly spans programming and concept design. Selection is portfolio- and motivation-driven, so a software-engineering BSc plus a strong sound/music portfolio is a legitimate route. The exact list of fields Aalto counts as "relevant": UNVERIFIED - confirm with the programme.
programs.portfolioSpec: An online presentation of your artistic/design work, submitted as a PDF of maximum 1.0 GB, which is then discussed during the interview. Plus a motivation letter of maximum 4,000 characters and a CV including experience, exhibitions and achievements. NO fixed number of works, durations or audio formats are published - UNVERIFIED, so treat the portfolio as free-form and curate it hard.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-phase selection, NO live on-site audition. Phase I evaluates motivation and background. Phase II comprises portfolio review, assignments (written or AUDIO-BASED), and a 30-minute interview.
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 20,000 per academic year for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens. EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay nothing.
programs.scholarship: Aalto University Scholarship: covers EITHER 50% OR 100% of the tuition fee for the standard duration of the degree (two years full-time for a master's). Merit-based, granted primarily on academic excellence; non-EU/EEA applicants to two-year master's programmes are considered as part of the admission process.
programs.fundingLevel: Full or partial (competitive tuition waiver of 50% or 100%)
programs.stipend: Tuition waiver only (50% or 100%); no living-cost stipend published
programs.applicationOpens: 1 December (opened 1 Dec 2025 for the 2026 intake)
programs.deadline: 2 January 2026 (application period 1 December 2025 - 2 January 2026) - PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect approximately 1 December 2026 - early January 2027 for a September 2027 start. Note the window is SHORT (about one month) and falls over the holidays.
programs.fitNotes: Probably the best RISK-ADJUSTED choice in the whole Nordic slice for him. No music degree required, no instrument audition, no on-site test, portfolio-driven selection that rewards self-taught work, English-taught, and a 50-100% tuition scholarship assessed automatically at admission - so a genuinely fundable path. The honest trade-off: it is sound design, sonic interaction and sound art for media and installation, not club-music production or mixing records; the DJ/producer ambition would be served indirectly, though he can cross-register into Sibelius Academy Music Technology courses to close the gap. Treat as the primary Nordic application, with the Aalto and Sibelius Academy applications prepared together since they share a portfolio.

programs.program: Music Composition MA / M.Mus
programs.university: Iceland University of the Arts (Listahaskoli Islands, LHI)
programs.institutionType: Art school / self-owned university of the arts
programs.durationEcts: UNVERIFIED - not published on the pages read (LHI MA programmes are typically 2 years / 120 ECTS)

programs.focus: Electroacoustic composition / Sonic arts (art-music oriented, with electro-acoustics as an elective strand)
programs.whatYouStudy: The programme allows a student to "develop his/her artistic and theoretical activity in a stimulating creative and critical environment, with access to the staff's wide professional experience", with emphasis on exploring and developing a personal compositional approach. Elective modules span musicology, music theory, ELECTRO-ACOUSTICS, instrumentation/orchestration and interdisciplinary studies. Students' compositions are performed by professional contemporary-music performers and ensembles - Caput New Music Ensemble has been ensemble in residence since 2015, with collaborations including Ensemble Adapter, Siggi String Quartet, Hljomeyki and Spilmenn Rikinis (this ensemble detail is AGGREGATOR-SOURCED, not confirmed on an lhi.is page). A second music MA, New Audiences and Innovative Practice (NAIP) M.Mus, is described as "suitable for musicians with diverse backgrounds" using "innovative and interdisciplinary approaches to creating and communicating music" - potentially a softer entry route worth investigating.

programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED - no portfolio specification published on the pages read. Request it from the Department of Music.
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED - no audition or on-site test details published on the pages read.

On content it is an art-music composition MA with electro-acoustics as an elective, so it serves a DJ/producer ambition only weakly; the NAIP M.Mus, described as suitable for musicians with diverse backgrounds, may be the better fit and the more open door. Email lhi@lhi.is early.

programs.program: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound
programs.university: Consortium: IADT Dún Laoghaire (IE) · Universidade Lusófona (PT) · Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre / LMTA (LT)
programs.focus: Sound Design · Film/Game Sound · Immersive Audio · Music Production · Electronic Music
programs.degree: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts (joint degree)
programs.institutionType: Consortium: art-and-technology institute (IADT), private university film school (Lusófona), state conservatory/academy (LMTA)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters. Total ECTS not stated on the pages read — UNVERIFIED (EMJM standard is 120)
programs.language: English (all instruction)
programs.whatYouStudy: Semester 1 Dublin: Acoustics & Psychoacoustics, Audio and Music Production, Synthesis and Sampling, Interactive Systems, Sound Psychology. Semester 2 Lisbon: Film Sound Theory, Interdisciplinary Project Incubation, Sound Ecosystems, Sound/Music Interface, Film Audio Post-production. Semester 3 Vilnius: Sound and the Environment, Film Sound practice, Sound Concepts, Sound Design and Immersion, Thesis Preparation. Semester 4: thesis project placement. Practice-led and industry-informed; covers stage/performance art, film, VR, natural and urban soundscapes.
programs.facilities: Dolby Atmos studios, Foley stages and immersive media labs across the consortium; links to AES, MPSE and CILECT. LMTA is Lithuania's national performing-arts university (QS Performing Arts top-50). Specific room lists per campus UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in sound, music, film, media studies, computational science or related disciplines. English (non-native): IELTS 6.0 with no component below 6.0, TOEFL iBT 79, Duolingo 110, Cambridge B2, or LanguageCert ESOL; alternatively a full EQF Level 4+ qualification of at least one academic year taught through English.
programs.portfolioSpec: "No more than 3 examples" of your sound or media-related work, each with a short reflective paragraph. Submit as a single hyperlink to a portfolio website OR one compiled audio/video file. The review team states it can realistically engage with 10–15 minutes of material per application.
programs.auditionSpec: None stated — no live audition or on-site test found on the application page. Selection is on written application + portfolio. (Any interview stage UNVERIFIED.)
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly. The published eligibility list names "computational science" as an accepted bachelor field, and adds that applicants "with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience in areas such as sound, music, film, or media studies." This is the single best-worded acceptance of a software-engineering background found in the whole Baltic/Polish slice.
programs.tuitionIntl: €15,000 total for the 2-year programme if self-funded (€7,500 before semester 1, €7,500 before semester 3). Fee is identical for all students regardless of origin. Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders pay no tuition.
programs.scholarship: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Scholarship — open to non-EU/Partner Country nationals including Tunisians; awarded on excellence. Max 24 places on the programme per year, with "a significant percentage" receiving the scholarship.
programs.stipend: €1,400 per month, which covers tuition and contributes toward travel, visa and living allowance (as stated on the ReSound application page).
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE — opened 20 October 2025 for the 2026 intake. Expect roughly October 2026 for a September 2027 start; confirm on resound-ma.eu.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The 2026 intake deadline was extended to 27 January 2026; the site now reads "Applications for ReSound 2026 have now closed." A 2027 call had not been published as of July 2026.
programs.fitNotes: The strongest single match in this slice and probably one of the best in Europe for him: English-taught, explicitly welcomes computational-science bachelors, portfolio is small (3 pieces, 10–15 min) and can be DJ/producer work, no live audition, and the Erasmus Mundus scholarship is genuinely fully funded with a €1,400/month stipend. Main obstacle: extremely competitive (24 places worldwide) and the emphasis is sound design/film/immersive rather than club music production — his portfolio needs at least some designed/narrative sound, not only dance tracks.

programs.program: Composition and Music Technology (MA) — Electroacoustic Composition specialisation
programs.university: Estonian Academy of Music and Theatre (EAMT / EMTA)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics · Electroacoustic Composition (practical production emphasis) · Sonic Arts
programs.institutionType: Public national academy of music and theatre (conservatory)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years. ECTS not stated on the pages read — UNVERIFIED (Estonian MA standard is 120 EAP/ECTS)
programs.language: English (tuition fees apply to all international students "whose language of tuition is English"); Estonian-taught study is free
programs.whatYouStudy: One curriculum with four tracks — classical composition, electroacoustic composition, audiovisual composition, recording arts. The electroacoustic/audiovisual studies "combine musical, artistic and technical creativity" in the Academy's sound and multimedia studios. Students are not tied to one professor and move between several mentors. Strongly interdisciplinary: drawing, photography, video, light and performance are treated as "an extension of sonic art." Annual COMMUTE Festival each spring puts student work in front of international professionals.
programs.facilities: Dedicated sound and multimedia studios inside a 13,500 m² purpose-built building in central Tallinn. Guest teachers have included Arvo Pärt, Erkki-Sven Tüür, Kaija Saariaho, Chaya Czernowin and Thomas Adès. Collaborations with Estonian Public Broadcasting and the Estonian National Symphony Orchestra (mainly via the Recording Arts track).
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree (level not further specified on the admission page). Documented English proficiency required; language skills are also assessed in the interview. A listening test on knowledge of different music eras forms part of the entrance examination for all composition-curriculum applicants. Application fee €75.
programs.portfolioSpec: Portfolio of original works, plus: "electroacoustic compositions in a recording or live performance (a total of approximately 15 minutes)." Scores welcome but not required for this track. All specialisations are graded 0–10 on artistic originality, development of the work, technical refinement, fulfilment of requirements and cultural understanding.
programs.auditionSpec: Entrance examination = portfolio presentation + a listening test on music history/eras + an oral colloquium in which the board assesses knowledge of the specialisation and related cultural issues. Format (on-site vs remote) UNVERIFIED for this curriculum; EAMT does run Zoom interviews "under special circumstances" for the related Sound Engineering intake.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — the admission page does not address non-music bachelors at all. There is no stated requirement for a music degree, but the listening test on music eras and the composition-focused portfolio effectively demand musical fluency. Contact katrin.puur@eamt.ee before applying.
programs.tuitionIntl: Non-EU: €7,700/year for English-taught master's, academic year 2026/2027 (€7,500 in 2025/2026). EU/Ukrainian: €1,750/year full-time.
programs.scholarship: "A limited number of scholarships are available for international students. Auditions for the scholarships usually take place at the end of September." No named scholarship for Tunisian nationals found — value and eligibility UNVERIFIED.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE — DreamApply opened 1 February 2026 for English-taught programmes (2026/27 entry). Expect ~February 2027 for September 2027.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Admission period for 2026/27 ran 1 February – 3 July 2026 via DreamApply.
programs.fitNotes: English-taught, in a lively Northern European electronic-music scene, with a moderate €7,700/year non-EU fee and real studio access. Main obstacle: it is a composition curriculum — the portfolio wants ~15 minutes of electroacoustic work and there is a music-history listening test, which is exactly what a self-taught DJ/producer with no conservatory training will find hardest. Worth attempting only if he spends 2026 building a genuinely compositional (not just club-track) portfolio.

programs.program: Composition and Music Technology (MA) — Recording Arts specialisation
programs.university: Estonian Academy of Music and Theatre (EAMT / EMTA)
programs.focus: Recording / Engineering · Music Production
programs.institutionType: Public national academy of music and theatre (conservatory)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years. ECTS not stated on the pages read — UNVERIFIED (Estonian MA standard 120)
programs.language: English
programs.whatYouStudy: The only place in Estonia to study classical-music recording. Practical studio and location recording, working with the main national actors in the field — collaboration with Estonian Public Broadcasting and the Estonian National Symphony Orchestra is built into the track. Sits inside the wider Composition and Music Technology curriculum, so electroacoustic/audiovisual modules and the COMMUTE Festival are accessible alongside. Note: EAMT's Sound Engineering and Music Production curriculum (studio recording, live recording, songwriting, DAW work in Ableton / Logic / Pro Tools) exists at BACHELOR level only — this MA is the master-level continuation.
programs.facilities: Academy sound and multimedia studios; Estonian Public Broadcasting and Estonian National Symphony Orchestra partnerships for live/classical recording sessions.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree; documented English proficiency; listening test on music eras is part of the entrance exam for composition-curriculum applicants. Application fee €75.
programs.portfolioSpec: Present 10 minutes of recorded music with a detailed explanation of it. The portfolio "must include acoustic and overdub recordings." Submit in addition a list of your sound-engineering works.
programs.auditionSpec: Colloquium covering professional competence and cultural knowledge, plus presentation and defence of the submitted recordings. Graded 0–10. On-site vs remote format UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — not addressed on the page. The portfolio demand (acoustic + overdub recordings, a list of prior sound-engineering credits) is the real gate, not the degree title. A software-engineering BSc is not itself excluded, but he would need demonstrable recording credits.
programs.scholarship: Limited number of international scholarships, auditions usually end of September. No Tunisia-specific scheme found — UNVERIFIED.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE — 1 February 2026 for 2026/27; expect ~February 2027.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (1 February – 3 July 2026 for 2026/27).
programs.fitNotes: The most craft-oriented English-taught option in Estonia — genuine console and location-recording work with a national broadcaster and symphony orchestra. programs.program: CoPeCo — Contemporary Performance and Composition (MA)

programs.program: Reżyseria dźwięku (Sound Engineering / Sound Direction), studia II stopnia — specialisations: reżyseria muzyczna, reżyseria dźwięku w filmie i telewizji, reżyseria dźwięku w multimediach

programs.whatYouStudy: Three master-level specialisations: (1) Reżyseria muzyczna — recording of classical and popular music, live and studio sessions; (2) Sound engineering for film and television — building the sound layer of a film and audio post-production; (3) Sound engineering in multimedia — interactive sound design, particularly for VIDEO GAMES and audiovisual forms. Students may extend the programme with additional multimedia subjects.
programs.facilities: Faculty operates multiple recording studios with professional audio equipment for student projects. Founded 1954 — one of the first sound-direction training centres in the world and the only one of its kind in Poland. Specific console/Atmos detail UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: First-cycle diploma (bachelor's minimum), secondary-school certificate, pass marks in the knowledge-and-skills tests and completion of the qualification procedure. For the sound-engineering field the secondary certificate is expected to include mathematics at basic level, with mathematics or physics at extended level recommended. Application fee 150 PLN via IRK (irk.chopin.edu.pl).
programs.portfolioSpec: No conventional creative portfolio is specified for entry — selection is by examination (see audition field). Where audio-video recordings are submitted, UMFC requires the candidate to be shown "in full without close-ups, without image movement, and without editing within a single piece," with clear audio and proper lighting.
programs.auditionSpec: ON-SITE and two-stage. Stage 1: written/practical test in ear training with elements of harmony, acoustics, knowledge of music-recording production and sound in film. Stage 2: qualification interview. Scoring — ear-training test up to 25 points, interview score ×2, maximum 75 points. In addition, ALL sound-engineering candidates must pass a free AUDIOMETRIC HEARING TEST at the Department of Musical Acoustics and Multimedia (room 413), ~40 minutes, offered 22 May – 14 June 2026 for the 2026/27 cycle.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — the published requirement is only "a diploma from first-cycle studies," with no subject restriction, and the matura expectations point at maths/physics rather than music. In principle a software-engineering BSc is admissible. The real filter is the ear-training and harmony test, which assumes solfège-level musicianship.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED for reżyseria dźwięku. General rule in Poland: Polish-taught programmes at public universities are free for students who qualify (including Polish Card / permanent residence / certain scholarship holders); all English-taught programmes at UMFC are paid. The 2025/26 fee schedule is in "Cennik opłat za usługi edukacyjne 2025-2026" (Zarządzenie Rektora nr 12/2025).
programs.scholarship: Polish government / NAWA schemes. IMPORTANT: the Banach NAWA scholarship (for which Tunisia IS eligible, Group 3) restricts Group-3 nationals to second-cycle studies in ENGINEERING AND TECHNICAL SCIENCES, AGRICULTURAL SCIENCES or NATURAL SCIENCES — humanities and arts are open only to nationals of a separate list of Eastern-European/Central-Asian countries. Reżyseria dźwięku as an arts field would therefore NOT be Banach-eligible for a Tunisian.
