programs.facilities: Institute of Acoustics, Faculty of Physics and Astronomy — the Institute also runs Poland's Reżyseria dźwięku bachelor, so studio and measurement facilities exist. Detail UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: A first- or second-cycle degree in EXACT SCIENCES, TECHNICAL OR NATURAL SCIENCE FIELDS. Selection: GPA from prior studies (max 5 points) + a qualification interview on signal analysis, psychoacoustics and physical acoustics (max 5 points). Non-EU: Polish B2 certificate, legalisation, sworn translation and equivalency recognition of foreign documents. Recruitment fee 100 PLN. Limit: 15 places.
programs.portfolioSpec: None — no portfolio required. Admission is GPA + technical interview.
programs.auditionSpec: Qualification interview on signal analysis, psychoacoustics and physical acoustics. For the 2026/27 cycle the exam was held 17 September 2026 with results on 18 September. On-site vs remote UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly. Entry requires a degree "in exact sciences, technical or natural science fields," which is precisely what a BSc in Software Engineering is. No music background required or expected.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — recruitment fee 100 PLN is stated; tuition for non-EU self-funded students is not published on the page read.
programs.scholarship: Potentially Banach NAWA — Tunisia is eligible (Group 3), and Acoustics sits within natural/technical sciences, which IS an eligible Banach field for Group-3 nationals. Field classification should be confirmed with NAWA. Banach also funds a preparatory Polish-language year for Polish-track students, which would address the B2 Polish requirement.
programs.fundingLevel: Full (if Banach NAWA is won) / otherwise UNVERIFIED
programs.stipend: Banach NAWA: PLN 2,500/month + tuition exemption + PLN 2,500 travel allowance + funded preparatory Polish course.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 June 2026 for the 2026/2027 cycle (registration closed 11 September 2026). Expect a comparable June 2027 window — PRIOR CYCLE, confirm.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026/27: registration 1 June – 11 September 2026, exam 17 September 2026, results 18 September 2026.
programs.fitNotes: Second of the two Polish routes where his engineering degree is explicitly accepted, with no portfolio and a technical interview he could actually prepare for, plus a plausible Banach NAWA funding path. Main obstacle: B2 Polish is mandatory for non-EU applicants and only 15 places exist — and the training is scientific acoustics with a sound/multimedia slant, not music production.

programs.program: Zvuková tvorba (Sound Design) — navazující magisterský studijní program (N0211A310015)
programs.university: Akademie múzických umění v Praze — FAMU (Film and TV School)
programs.institutionType: Public film school / academy of performing arts (FAMU is one of the oldest and most famous film schools in the world)
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive Audio
programs.language: Czech (the master's Sound Design track is NOT offered in English; FAMU's English-taught MFAs are Directing, Cinematography, Montage, Photography only)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (104 credits across 42 compulsory courses + 8 elective + 8 required-elective)
programs.whatYouStudy: Film sound as the organising premise, taught as theory + studio practice: film sound mixing theory and spatial/multichannel formats, sound design and sound composition technique, sound dramaturgy, interactive audio for game design, multichannel post-production processing, and 'post-cinematic' uses of the audio component. Students run the sound on FAMU student films end-to-end (pre-production, production, post-production) and graduate as sound supervisors / sound designers / re-recording mixers. Roughly 7 students admitted per year — extremely small, high-contact cohort.
programs.entryRequirements: Completed bachelor's degree (any institution). The department states candidates from other schools/fields may apply, but must demonstrate theory + practice at the level of the programme's own BA graduates. Czech-language study means a Czech certificate at B2/C1 (CCE) is in practice required to enrol and to keep tuition-free status. Full-time attendance only — no distance form. IELTS/TOEFL is irrelevant here; Czech is the gate.
programs.portfolioSpec: Round 1 (documents only, candidate not present): (1) a LIST of all own sound works made during bachelor's study — audiovisual/multimedia works, music recordings, radio and theatre sound design — each with title, genre, director, production company, duration, year; (2) TWO audiovisual works on which the applicant made a substantial sound contribution, each with a detailed written explication; (3) the applicant's own theoretical work or an essay in the field; (4) a written project/statement for the master's study at FAMU (intended specialisation, expected outcomes, elective courses wanted at FAMU or other universities, interest in international internships). All works must be the applicant's own authorship, confirmed by a signed declaration. Works are uploaded by the separate works deadline (1 Sept in the 2026/27 cycle), not with the application form.
programs.auditionSpec: Round 2 is an IN-PERSON oral examination in Prague: interview testing technical and artistic knowledge of the field, musical competence, and readiness for master's-level work, plus defence of the submitted works and the study project.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — formally yes, practically hard. The department page states candidates from other schools and fields may apply with any bachelor's degree, but adds they should show theoretical and practical knowledge equivalent to graduates of the programme's own bachelor track. There is no wording excluding a software-engineering BSc, but the portfolio (two finished audiovisual works with sound by the applicant) is the real filter.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026/27 cycle (from the official specific-conditions PDF): applications 1 June – 13 August 2026; works/portfolio upload by 1 September 2026; Round 1 on 14 September 2026; Round 2 on 17 September 2026. NOTE the unusual summer cycle — for a September 2027 start expect an analogous June–August 2027 window, i.e. much later than most European deadlines.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 1 June (2026 cycle opened 1 June 2026 via prihlaska.amu.cz). Application fee 990 CZK.
programs.tuitionIntl: 0 CZK for study in Czech at a Czech public university — nationality is irrelevant under Czech law; only study in a foreign language is charged. (For comparison, FAMU's English-taught MFA programmes cost CZK 550,000 per year in 2026/27 — but none of those is Sound Design.)
programs.scholarship: No dedicated scholarship found for Tunisians. Czech Government Scholarships (Developing Countries) do NOT cover Tunisia — the 2026/27 eligible list was Bosnia & Herzegovina, Georgia, Ukraine, Belarus (democratic forces), Guatemala and Jordan. AMU offers internal accommodation, social and merit scholarships (eligibility for non-EU students UNVERIFIED).
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free if studying in Czech; living costs self-funded)
programs.stipend: Tuition waiver by law (Czech-taught). No stipend identified. UNVERIFIED whether AMU internal scholarships reach non-EU first-year master's students.
programs.facilities: FAMU's Department of Sound (Katedra zvukové tvorby, Smetanovo nábřeží 2, Prague 1) runs mixing and post-production rooms integrated with the school's film production pipeline; the department describes 'a combination of technologies allowing students to finish films in first-class quality' and active collaboration with the Czech film industry for placements and contacts. Audio-recording teaching is partly delivered by HAMU's Sound Studio. Exact Dolby Atmos certification of FAMU rooms: UNVERIFIED. FAMU alumni include Miloš Forman, Věra Chytilová, Jiří Menzel, Emir Kusturica, Agnieszka Holland.
programs.fitNotes: The most prestigious name on this slice and genuinely hands-on, but it is a FILM sound school, not a music-production school — nothing here trains him as a DJ or a club/electronic producer. Two obstacles compound: Czech at B2/C1 for the free route, and a portfolio of two finished audiovisual works with his own sound design, which he does not have. Realistic only as a 2028+ target after building a film/game sound reel; the June–August application window at least gives him a full extra year of preparation.

programs.program: Zvuková tvorba a hudební režie — specializace Zvuková tvorba (Sound Design / recording engineering), navazující magisterské studium
programs.university: Akademie múzických umění v Praze — HAMU (Music and Dance Faculty)
programs.institutionType: Public conservatory / academy of music (music faculty of AMU)
programs.focus: Recording/Engineering; Music Production; Electronic Music/Live Electronics; Immersive Audio
programs.language: Czech
programs.durationEcts: 2 years; ECTS total UNVERIFIED (standard Czech follow-up master = 120 ECTS)
programs.whatYouStudy: Artistic-technical sound work at the highest level of autonomous sound creation: classical-music and jazz recording technique, realisation of electroacoustic music, sound and music post-production, live sound reinforcement, concert recording, online streaming, and sound-to-picture. Taught content covers microphone technique, signal processing, spatial/dynamic/timbral transformation of sound, analogue and digital console practice, and research methodology in musical and psychological acoustics. Graduates work as recording engineers in professional music studios, radio sound engineers, and in-house engineers for cultural institutions.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree. Applicants must submit a CURRENT AUDIOGRAM with an ENT specialist's statement — a hearing test is a formal admission condition. Czech-language study; Czech at B2/C1 needed in practice.
programs.portfolioSpec: 'Presentation of audio recordings' by the candidate, presented and defended in Round 2. The department does NOT publish a number of works, a maximum duration or a file format on its admissions page — UNVERIFIED beyond 'presentation of own recordings'; contact katedra zvukové tvorby a hudební režie for the exact spec.
programs.auditionSpec: Yes — two IN-PERSON rounds in Prague. Round 1: electronic/aural test (analysis of a sound signal, stereo imaging, melodic and rhythmic patterns, detection of sound faults) plus a written knowledge test in physiological, spatial and musical acoustics, musical electronics and sound engineering; minimum 20 of 25 points to progress. Round 2: practical mix of speech + music + noise on an ANALOGUE console (~2 min); mix of abstract electronic music on a DIGITAL console (max ~2 min); a basic instrumental proficiency test (piano preferred); presentation of own recordings; interview on professional vision.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, conditionally — quoted from the programme page: students coming from other bachelor's programmes may enrol 'if they meet minimum technical and artistic requirements for the Sound Creation specialisation', and will progressively make up missing bachelor-level knowledge through elective courses. The hard filter is not the diploma but the Round-1 hearing/acoustics test and the piano/instrument test.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — the department page points to its 'Magisterské studium' section for current dates and does not publish them inline. Confirm directly for the 2027/28 cycle.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED. Application fee 990 CZK, paid by card via prihlaska.amu.cz.
programs.tuitionIntl: 0 CZK for Czech-taught study at a Czech public university, any nationality.
programs.scholarship: None found specific to Tunisians (Czech Government Scholarships exclude Tunisia). AMU internal accommodation/social/merit scholarships exist; eligibility for non-EU students UNVERIFIED.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free in Czech; living costs self-funded)
programs.facilities: HAMU's own Zvukové studio (Sound Studio) at Malostranské náměstí 258/13, Prague 1 — analogue and digital mixing consoles, recording studio used for classical/jazz sessions, and the facility that also delivers audio-recording teaching to FAMU. Department also runs bachelor, master and doctoral levels plus faculty-wide electives.
programs.fitNotes: This is the closest thing in Prague to a Tonmeister/recording-engineering master, and its electroacoustic and post-production strands touch electronic music. But the entrance exam is brutal for a self-taught producer: an acoustics knowledge test, an ear/fault-detection test with a 20/25 pass bar, a live analogue-console mix, and a piano test — plus a medical audiogram. Czech is required. Not realistic for September 2027 without a year of Czech plus serious classical-recording and keyboard preparation.

programs.program: Zvuková tvorba a hudební režie — specializace Hudební režie (Music Direction / classical record production), navazující magisterské studium

programs.language: Czech

programs.whatYouStudy: Training as a classical music producer/record producer: leading complex orchestral and chamber recording sessions, detailed score analysis and instrumental knowledge, session planning and direction, post-production (editing, mixing) in professional DAWs, live concert recording with streaming integration, audiovisual projects, and communication/team leadership with artists and the recording crew.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree plus very high musical literacy — score reading, orchestration knowledge, aural dictation and piano are all examined. Czech-language study.
programs.portfolioSpec: Presentation of own sound recordings in Round 2. Exact number/duration/format not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: Yes — IN-PERSON, two rounds. Round 1: written practical + theoretical test, ear-training dictation and listening comprehension, score analysis and orchestration assessment, and a piano proficiency examination. Round 2: presentation of sound recordings and an interview on artistic vision and professional orientation.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No in practice. The page states no formal bar on the prior degree, but Round 1 examines score analysis, orchestration, aural dictation and piano — a software-engineering BSc holder without conservatory training cannot pass. Treat as effectively closed.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — check the department's Magisterské studium page for the 2027/28 cycle.

programs.tuitionIntl: 0 CZK (Czech-taught, public university).

programs.fitNotes: Listed for completeness as the region's classical record-production master. It is a genuine craft degree, but it is aimed at conservatory-trained musicians and is the wrong instrument entirely for a DJ/electronic-producer ambition. Recommend skipping.

programs.program: Zvukový design a multimediální technologie (Sound Design and Multimedia Technologies) — navazující magisterské studium
programs.university: Masarykova univerzita (Masaryk University), Faculty of Arts — Department of Musicology, jointly delivered with FEKT VUT Brno

programs.focus: Sound Design; Music Production; Recording/Engineering; Immersive Audio
programs.language: Czech
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS; full-time (prezenční) or part-time (kombinovaná)
programs.whatYouStudy: Four strands over four semesters: (1) technical foundations — mathematics, physics, acoustics, studio technology; (2) production foundations — sound design proper; (3) sound production and programming — recording-studio work, audio software, autonomous sound production in the digital environment, live music production sound; (4) theory, history and contemporary practice of sound creation. Practical skills training runs through all four semesters and a MANDATORY external internship is part of the degree. Taught by leading practitioners alongside MUNI musicologists and BUT engineers.
programs.entryRequirements: Any bachelor's degree. Quoted from the official page: 'Program je určen absolventům bakalářského studia – bez omezení' (the programme is intended for bachelor's graduates — without restriction). Czech-language study, so Czech at B2/C1 is the practical requirement.
programs.portfolioSpec: No conventional portfolio of finished works is demanded. Instead the second exam component is a CREATIVE PROJECT PROPOSAL of maximum 2 pages, setting out motivation and the intended creative/research direction. (Own works can be referenced in support but are not a stated fixed requirement.)
programs.auditionSpec: Oral entrance examination in two parts: (a) professional and artistic competence — technical, production and theoretical knowledge; (b) discussion of the max-2-page creative project. Scoring: pass mark 50 of 100; the professional exam is worth 40 points and the creative project 60 points. On-site oral exam in Brno.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. 'Program je určen absolventům bakalářského studia – bez omezení' ('for bachelor graduates — without restriction'). This is the only programme found in the whole Czech/Slovak/Hungarian slice that states openness to any bachelor field in writing, which makes a software-engineering BSc formally unproblematic.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 cycle: applications 1 January – 30 April 2026, with the entrance exam after. For a September 2027 start expect 1 January – 30 April 2027.

programs.scholarship: None found earmarked for Tunisians; Czech Government Scholarships do not cover Tunisia. MUNI runs internal merit and social scholarships — eligibility for non-EU master's students UNVERIFIED.
programs.stipend: Tuition waiver only; no stipend identified. UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Recording-studio work and live-sound practice built into the curriculum; technical teaching and laboratories supplied by FEKT VUT Brno (anechoic chamber, audio labs); compulsory external internship places students in Czech industry. Detailed equipment list UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The single best structural fit in Czechia for a software-engineering graduate: it explicitly accepts any bachelor, its entrance test is a knowledge interview plus a two-page project rather than a portfolio of finished films, its engineering half rewards a technical background, and its production half (studio recording, live sound, digital production) is close to what he actually wants. The one real obstacle is Czech at B2/C1 — which would need a year of intensive Czech before applying in January 2027. Worth building the whole Czech plan around.

programs.program: Audio inženýrství (Audio Engineering) — navazující magisterský program, specializace Zvuková produkce a nahrávání (Sound Production and Recording)

Treat as a secondary enquiry made in the same email.

programs.program: Strihová a zvuková skladba — študijný plán Zvuková skladba (Sound Composition / Sound Design), magisterské štúdium
programs.university: Vysoká škola múzických umení v Bratislave (VŠMU / Academy of Performing Arts), Film and Television Faculty (FTF) — Ateliér zvukovej skladby
programs.institutionType: Public film and television faculty of a national academy of performing arts
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive Audio; Recording/Engineering
programs.language: Slovak
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (4 semesters) / 120 ECTS, full-time (denná forma)
programs.whatYouStudy: Named courses on the official page: Mixing and Mastering; Sound Creation – Audiovisual Production; Film Sound Theory; Music Recording Theory and Practice; Sound Design Theory – Musical Dramaturgy; Music Direction; Sound Synthesis. Theory and practice are oriented to SURROUND formats, and the master level explicitly targets film sound in Dolby Surround 7.1 and Dolby Atmos, plus film music. The stated aim is independent creative thinking in sound composition for audiovisual work of any genre — training 'sound masters' who use sound expressive means to realise a dramaturgical intent.
programs.entryRequirements: Completed bachelor's degree before enrolment. Slovak-language instruction. Electronic application via ePrihláška; application fee €40.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED at the level of exact specification — the atelier page states requirements and exam procedures are published per programme page, and the programme page gives dates and fee but not the portfolio spec. Expect submitted sound works with explications; request the 'požiadavky na prijímacie skúšky' from the study coordinator Jana Mihoková (jana.mihokova@vsmu.sk, +421 2 2100 6511 ext. 511).
programs.auditionSpec: On-site entrance examination in Bratislava on a single published date (23 June 2026 in the prior cycle). Format UNVERIFIED. Note that the Music and Dance Faculty of the same university runs a two-round process with an online interview for international applicants — whether FTF offers any remote option is UNVERIFIED and worth asking.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — no statement found on the programme page about the required field of the prior bachelor. Ask the coordinator directly; the atelier trains sound engineers and sound designers rather than musicians, so the question is genuinely open.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 cycle for Zvuková skladba Mgr. art.: application deadline 8 April 2026; entrance exam 23 June 2026. For September 2027 entry expect roughly April 2027 with a June 2027 exam.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Via ePrihláška; opening date UNVERIFIED, fee €40.
programs.tuitionIntl: €0 for full-time study in Slovak within the standard length of study — VŠMU states foreign applicants have the same conditions as Slovak applicants and tuition is free for the standard duration. A €1,650 fee applies only for exceeding the standard length or for parallel study. (By contrast the Music and Dance Faculty's English-language track is €5,000/year — that is a different faculty and not this programme.)
programs.scholarship: Slovak Government / National Scholarship Programme (SAIA) — 'Scholarships for talented students from abroad', open to full-time master's study at a Slovak public HEI, all nationalities worldwide. Reported at up to €1,025 per month, up to €10,000 total over two academic years, with roughly 45 master's places globally. Tuition is not automatically covered but Slovak-taught full-time study is already free.
programs.fundingLevel: Full (potentially) — tuition-free by default plus a monthly stipend if the SAIA scholarship is won; otherwise Partial (tuition-free only).
programs.stipend: Up to €1,025/month for up to 2 academic years (~€10,000 total) under the Slovak scholarship for talented foreign students. Amounts as reported — confirm on studyinslovakia.saia.sk and scholarships.portalvs.sk. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: the 2026/27 round closed 31 July 2026, so expect a ~July 2027 deadline for 2027/28.
programs.facilities: Founded 1999. Described on the official page as one of Slovakia's most modern audio complexes and holding DOLBY ATMOS MUSIC STUDIO certification: five sound mixing suites, a cinema hall, professional microphones and field-recording equipment, working from stereo through multichannel for cinema and streaming. A development project upgrades one mixing suite to Dolby Atmos 12.1 and the cinema to Dolby Atmos 39.2, positioning the atelier as a teaching centre for 3D spatial audio. Head: Mgr. art. Tobiáš Potočný, ArtD.; staff include prof. Peter Mojžiš, doc. Dušan Kozák, doc. Marek Piaček.
programs.fitNotes: Best combination in this slice of world-class facilities (Dolby Atmos Music certified, five mixing suites), zero tuition for everyone, and a real chance of a €1,025/month government stipend — the only plausibly FULLY FUNDED route across Czechia, Slovakia and Hungary for this profile. The blocker is Slovak-language instruction, which is a serious commitment with no Arabic/French bridge, plus an unpublished portfolio spec and an on-site June exam. Also note it is film/TV sound and immersive audio, not DJ/club production.

programs.program: Zeneszerző MA (Music Composition MA) — Elektronikus zenei médiaművészet (Electronic Music Media Art / EZMM) specialisation
programs.university: Liszt Ferenc Zeneművészeti Egyetem (Liszt Academy of Music), Composition Department
programs.institutionType: Public conservatory / national academy of music
programs.focus: Electroacoustic Composition; Electronic Music/Live Electronics; Sonic Arts
programs.language: Hungarian, with English tuition available — but conditionally. Quoted rule: for non-instrumental majors, 'tuition is only offered in English if there are a minimum of 3 international students admitted in a given year to the same major.' This is the key risk for an English-track applicant.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (4 semesters); ECTS UNVERIFIED (Hungarian MA standard 120)
programs.whatYouStudy: Composition at master level with the option to deepen electronic-music work; the EZMM strand continues the Academy's electronic music media art line (launched 2011) covering the history and compositional technique of electroacoustic and computer music, sound analysis, synthesis and transformation, MIDI/OSC, interactive and algorithmic music. Composition-related special courses are chosen freely according to the student's interests. Applicants who did NOT take electronic-music courses in their prior studies must complete a 2-semester 'Foundations of Electronic Music Composition' course during the first MA year.
programs.entryRequirements: BA diploma. All applicants must submit a PRELIMINARY CREDIT RECOGNITION REQUEST to establish whether their BA diploma can be accepted for the MA, unless the BA was taken at the Liszt Academy — the request form plus the BA transcript/diploma supplement and English course descriptions go in with the application. Certificates need an official certified attested Hungarian translation. Applications route through felvi.hu (Hungarian central admissions) or through the Stipendium Hungaricum portal.
programs.portfolioSpec: Uploaded portfolio evaluated first: sheet music of THREE of the applicant's own compositions, with recordings if possible. For the EZMM specialisation the presented works must total NO MORE THAN 25–30 MINUTES and comprise (a) one recorded tape/fixed-media piece and (b) one work for instrument + electronics, OR an interactive live performance, OR an audiovisual work. Style exercises additionally required: one fugue in the style of J. S. Bach (EZMM candidates may realise the Bach-style task electroacoustically), one classical sonata or rondo movement, and one 20th-century etude in the style of a named composer. EZMM candidates also sit an electronic-music fundamentals test.
programs.auditionSpec: YES — mandatory in-person. 'All applicants are required to appear before the Entrance Examination Committee in person.' Components: a practical examination (live audition) in the chosen specialisation; a written theoretical examination; written and oral form analysis based on Schoenberg's 'Fundamentals of Musical Composition' including analysis of classical/romantic and 20th–21st century works; an on-site orchestration/scoring task; score reading (sight-reading classical/romantic and contemporary scores); and a career-orientation interview.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No, in practice. Nothing formally bars a non-music BA, but the mandatory preliminary credit-recognition check on the BA diploma, plus a Bach fugue, a classical sonata/rondo movement, score sight-reading and an orchestration task, make a software-engineering BSc holder without conservatory theory effectively unadmittable. Quote from the Academy: applicants 'must submit a preliminary credit recognition request to determine whether the applicant's BA diploma can be accepted to apply for the MA programme'.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Two routes: (a) Stipendium Hungaricum — the 2027/28 call is reported to open November 2026 with a 15 January 2027 deadline (confirm on stipendiumhungaricum.hu when the call is published); (b) self-funded/Hungarian route via felvi.hu, mid-February deadline in the ordinary Hungarian cycle — exact 2027 date UNVERIFIED.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Stipendium Hungaricum 2027/28 reported to open November 2026.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED for self-funded non-EU applicants — the Liszt Academy publishes fees per programme; not confirmed on pages read. Fully covered if admitted through Stipendium Hungaricum.
programs.scholarship: STIPENDIUM HUNGARICUM — Tunisia is an eligible partner country (one of fifteen eligible Arab states). The Liszt Academy is a Stipendium Hungaricum host institution and 'MA Music Composition' appears in the Stipendium Hungaricum course catalogue as an English-taught option. Also relevant: Hungarian Diaspora Scholarship (not applicable here).
programs.stipend: Stipendium Hungaricum covers full tuition, a monthly stipend, a housing/accommodation contribution and medical insurance. Exact 2027/28 monthly amounts UNVERIFIED — read the official Call for Applications when published (the 2026/27 BA/MA call PDF is on stipendiumhungaricum.hu).
programs.facilities: Composition Department of Hungary's national music academy; the EZMM line (electronic music media art, running since 2011) teaches sound analysis, synthesis, transformation, MIDI/OSC, interactive and algorithmic music with associated computer-music studio provision. Exact studio inventory UNVERIFIED. Institutional prestige is very high.
programs.fitNotes: This is the only fully-funded English-possible master in the whole slice that touches electronic music — Stipendium Hungaricum would pay tuition, stipend and housing, and Tunisia is eligible. But the admission is a classical composition examination: Bach fugue, sonata form, orchestration, score reading, in person in Budapest, on top of a diploma credit-recognition check. Without conservatory theory this is not a realistic September 2027 target. Keep it on the list only if he is willing to spend 2026–27 on harmony, counterpoint and score reading.

programs.program: Hangművészet mesterszak (Sound Art MA)
programs.university: Pécsi Tudományegyetem (University of Pécs), Faculty of Music and Visual Arts — Electronic Music and Media Department / Design and Media Arts Institute
programs.institutionType: Public university, arts faculty
programs.focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based); Electronic Music/Live Electronics; Immersive/Spatial Audio
programs.language: Hungarian (no English option found — UNVERIFIED whether one can be arranged)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters, full-time (nappali). Credit structure published: 14 credits theory/history/culture, 12 credits creative and research work in sound art and electroacoustic/computer music, 48 credits studio and creative projects in the chosen sound-art specialisation, 10 credits electives, 6 credits professional practice, plus thesis and diploma work.
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound art as a primary medium — installation, multimedia performance, sound experiments and interdisciplinary forms, sitting at the intersection of music, visual art and media art. The programme continues the topics of the faculty's Electronic Music Media Art BA and is the clearest practice-based sonic-arts master in Hungary. The bulk of the credits (48 of ~120) sit in studio and creative project work, so it is genuinely hands-on rather than theoretical.
programs.entryRequirements: A BA or higher university qualification, held by applicants who possess 'complex computer-based artistic (especially musical) knowledge' and whose interests point at the creative and research areas of sound art. Programme established 2020, accreditation materials prepared 2022.
programs.portfolioSpec: Practical entrance examination consisting of a PORTFOLIO presentation together with a WORK PLAN (a proposal for what the applicant intends to make during the MA). Number of works, duration and file format are NOT published — UNVERIFIED; request the exact spec from the Design and Media Arts Institute (+36 72 501-500 ext. 28240).
programs.auditionSpec: On-site: an oral discussion of the portfolio plus a PRACTICAL MULTIMEDIA TASK completed at the university during the entrance examination.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — favourable wording. The requirement is a BA 'or higher university qualification' plus 'complex computer-based artistic (especially musical) knowledge', not a music degree. A computer-science graduate with a demonstrable computer-music practice arguably meets that description better than most; a strong portfolio would carry the application. Confirm with the institute.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Applications run through felvi.hu on the Hungarian central cycle (mid-February deadline in the ordinary round); exact 2027 date UNVERIFIED. If applying via Stipendium Hungaricum, the 2027/28 call is reported to open November 2026 with a 15 January 2027 deadline.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (felvi.hu central cycle).
programs.tuitionIntl: 1,000,000 HUF per SEMESTER for the self-funded track (≈€2,500/semester at 2026 rates), as published on the faculty page. State-funded (állami ösztöndíjas) places exist but are for Hungarian/EU-eligible students; a non-EU applicant would need Stipendium Hungaricum. Whether this specific programme is in the Stipendium Hungaricum catalogue: UNVERIFIED — check the SH programme finder.
programs.scholarship: Stipendium Hungaricum (Tunisia is an eligible country) IF this programme appears in the SH catalogue — UNVERIFIED for Hangművészet specifically. Otherwise none found.
programs.fundingLevel: UNVERIFIED — potentially Full via Stipendium Hungaricum, otherwise self-pay at 1,000,000 HUF/semester.
programs.stipend: If via Stipendium Hungaricum: full tuition, monthly stipend, housing contribution, medical insurance. Amounts UNVERIFIED for 2027/28.
programs.facilities: Electronic Music and Media Department at the Zsolnay Quarter campus (Zsolnay Vilmos u. 16, Pécs), running media-art studios and computer-music teaching; 48 of the programme's credits are studio/project work. Specific equipment inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: On paper the friendliest Hungarian entry route for a computer-science graduate — admission is a portfolio plus a work plan plus an on-site practical task, with no fugue and no score reading, and the wording actively values computer-based musical knowledge. Two cautions: it is taught in Hungarian, and the faculty's own admissions page currently flags the programme 'Jelenleg nem indul' (not launching at present) while the programme description page says it is running — this contradiction must be resolved by phone before he invests anything. Sound art and installation rather than dancefloor production.

programs.program: Master of Music in Music Production, Technology, and Innovation (MPTI)
programs.university: Berklee College of Music – Valencia Campus
programs.institutionType: Private specialist music college (US institution, Spanish campus)
programs.focus: Music Production; Electronic Music; Sound Design; Immersive/Interactive Audio
programs.durationEcts: 1 year / 3 consecutive semesters (fall, spring, summer); 32–33 US credits required (up to 37–38 with optional internship). ECTS equivalence UNVERIFIED.
programs.language: English
programs.whatYouStudy: Core module: audio engineering, studio production, video production, interactive media, electronic music production, career preparation. Elective module (4+ credits) with tracks in mixing, DJing, sound design and multimedia installation. Final Project module = three seminars (Past/Present/Future) plus a 'culminating experience' proposal, development and public defence. Placement exams in Engineering and in Ableton set your course level. Tools taught: Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools, Adobe Premiere.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree required. English proficiency for non-native speakers: TOEFL iBT 100 (exams before 21 Jan 2026), IELTS Academic 7.5, Duolingo 130, or Cambridge CAE/C1 Business Higher. Exemption if bachelor was completed at an English-language university. Also required: statement of purpose (400–500 words), résumé, one letter of recommendation, official transcripts with third-party credential evaluation (SpanTran or ECE) for non-US institutions, $150 application fee.
programs.portfolioSpec: Three recorded musical projects — audio or video files of your own work — each with a short description of your role. Optional scores may be added. All materials organised into ONE PDF with embedded links.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition for MPTI (auditions apply only to the Contemporary Performance Production concentration). Interview only, for shortlisted applicants; all interviews scheduled in Central European Time.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes (conditionally). Entrance-requirements page states for Contemporary Performance/Music Production that a music bachelor is preferred but "Bachelor's degrees in other disciplines will be considered, provided the student demonstrates a high degree of musicianship." A software-engineering BSc is therefore admissible, but the portfolio must carry the case.
programs.tuitionIntl: USD 50,430 tuition + USD 1,600 comprehensive fee = USD 52,030 direct costs for 2026/27, plus a required software bundle of USD 200–850 and a USD 2,500 non-refundable deposit (credited to first payment). Highest-cost option in this slice.
programs.scholarship: Berklee Valencia allocates more than €125,000 in scholarships across all campus master's programmes for 2026–27. Named awards include the Berklee Outstanding Women Scholarship and Mentorship (up to 70% of tuition, explicitly tied to the MPTI programme) and the Berklee Global Partners Scholarship. No named Tunisia/North Africa award found.
programs.stipend: Tuition discount only; no stipend, no housing. Scholarship deadlines run 15 days after each application deadline (Nov 15 / Feb 1 / Mar 10).
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (Berklee advises starting "as early as possible"; the Early Action deadline is a fixed annual date, so the portal is typically open from late summer). For Sept 2027 entry expect opening around Aug–Sept 2026.
programs.deadline: Standing annual cycle published on the official deadlines page: Early Action 1 Nov (decisions 15 Dec), Regular Action 15 Jan (decisions 15 Mar), Extended Action 10 Mar (decisions 20 Apr). For a Sept 2027 start these map to 1 Nov 2026 / 15 Jan 2027 / 10 Mar 2027 — CONFIRM the 2027 dates when the site updates. Only one application per cycle is allowed; rejected applicants must wait a full year.
programs.facilities: State-of-the-art recording studios, technology labs, scoring stage and dedicated DJ labs on the Palau de les Arts campus in Valencia. Strong industry-placement network and internship option built into the degree.
programs.fitNotes: The single best pure fit in Spain for someone who wants to be a DJ/producer: DJing, electronic production and mixing are actual elective tracks, and no audition is required. Two obstacles: the price (≈USD 52k for one year, only partial scholarships) and the IELTS 7.5 requirement, which is one of the toughest English bars in this whole slice and would need serious preparation from a 'working English' baseline.

programs.program: Mestrado em Som e Imagem — especialização em Design de Som (Master in Sound and Image, Sound Design track)
programs.university: Universidade Católica Portuguesa – Escola das Artes, Porto
programs.institutionType: Private university (Catholic University of Portugal), art school faculty
programs.focus: Sound Design; Film/Game Sound; Music Production (electronic); Immersive Audio; Sonic Arts
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS, pós-laboral (evening) regime
programs.language: UNVERIFIED — Portuguese is the working language of the School of Arts; an English-language course page exists and international students are explicitly catered for. Confirm directly.
programs.whatYouStudy: Verified Sound Design study plan: Y1S1 — Project Production I: Outdoor and Studio (12 ECTS), Sound Production for Video Games (5), Electronic Production (5), Sonic Arts and Technologies (5), Research in Sound and Image (3). Y1S2 — Project II: Post-Production Sound Design (12), Film Soundtrack (5), Interdisciplinary Project (5), Interdisciplinary Seminar (3), Tangible Interfaces and Physical Computing (5). Y2 — Portfolio and Showreel (3) + Dissertation/Project/Internship (57). Shared cohort with Animation, New Media Art and VFX specialisations.
programs.entryRequirements: A licenciatura (bachelor) in cinema, audiovisual, photography, multimedia, visual arts, architecture, ENGINEERING or related fields; or a foreign Bologna-compliant first-cycle degree; or a qualification/professional CV recognised by the School of Arts Scientific Council as demonstrating capacity for master's study. Documents: degree certificate with grades/ECTS, ID copy, CV, artistic portfolio, (special-needs form if applicable).
programs.portfolioSpec: Artistic portfolio required, submitted as a link (URL) in the application. The published document list does not fix a number of works, duration or format — confirm the expected scope with candidaturas.porto@ucp.pt. No letter of motivation is listed.
programs.auditionSpec: No live audition. Interview required for external candidates (i.e. applicants who did not do their bachelor at UCP) — you would be interviewed.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly. "Engenharia" (engineering) is named in the list of eligible bachelor fields alongside cinema, multimedia and design. This is one of the very few pages in the slice that names engineering outright, which makes it unusually safe for a software-engineering BSc.
programs.tuitionIntl: €657/month × 10 months × 2 years = €13,140 total, plus €460 enrolment fee and €50 application fee (2026/27 figures). No separate higher international rate was published.
programs.fundingLevel: UNVERIFIED — no scholarship scheme for non-EU master's students was found on the pages read.
programs.scholarship: None found
programs.applicationOpens: Phase 1 opens 2 February (2026/27 cycle)
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Published 2026/27 rounds: Phase 1 2 Feb – 9 Apr (international applicants until 24 Apr), results 21 Apr; Phase 2 30 Apr – 11 Jun, results 23 Jun; Phase 3 1 Jul – 26 Aug, results 7 Sep. 45 places in total across all phases and specialisations. Expect the same shape for 2027/28.
programs.facilities: Motion Capture Laboratory, Surround Sound Mixing Studio, Interactive Art and Digital Fabrication Lab, Cinema/TV studio with chroma key. Research access through CITAR (Centre for Research in Science and Technology of the Arts) and the Digital Creativity Centre (CCD). Faculty mixes working professionals with academic supervisors.
programs.fitNotes: Strongest all-round Portugal option on paper: a genuine hands-on sound-design master that includes a whole unit called Electronic Production plus game audio and film soundtrack, in a city with a low cost of living, at ~€13k for two years. Obstacles: it is a private university with no visible funding for non-EU students, the evening timetable assumes you can support yourself, and the language of instruction needs confirming.

programs.program: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound Design for Media Arts
programs.university: Consortium: Universidade Lusófona (Lisbon) with IADT Dún Laoghaire (Dublin) and Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre (Vilnius)
programs.country: Portugal (joint programme with Ireland and Lithuania)
programs.degree: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts (EMJM), Level 9, 120 ECTS
programs.institutionType: Joint consortium: art/technology institute + private university + state music academy (FilmEU European University alliance)
programs.focus: Sound Design; Sonic Arts (practice-based); Film/Game Sound; Immersive Audio
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, with compulsory mobility across three countries
programs.language: English
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound design for media arts across the three partners: IADT Dublin (media arts and screen sound), Lusófona Lisbon (sound production and technologies — the Lisbon partner also runs the Produção e Tecnologias do Som master, sharing Pro Tools / Max-MSP / Arduino infrastructure), LMTA Vilnius (music and theatre technology). Semester 4 is a thesis/practice placement located according to your research needs. Detailed module list UNVERIFIED — request the current study plan from the consortium.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in sound, music, film, media studies, COMPUTATIONAL SCIENCE or related disciplines; applicants from other fields considered with relevant professional experience. English (certificate within 2 years): IELTS 6.0 with 6.0 in every component, TOEFL iBT 79, Duolingo 110, Cambridge B2, or LanguageCert ESOL — or evidence of a full EQF Level 4+ qualification of at least one academic year taught in English. Online interview for shortlisted candidates, focused on motivation and portfolio.
programs.portfolioSpec: Maximum THREE examples of previous sound or media work, 10–15 minutes of material in total (the selection team states it can realistically review 10–15 min per application), each accompanied by a short reflective paragraph explaining your role. Submit either as a single portfolio website link or as one compiled audio/video file. All documents in English.
programs.auditionSpec: None. Online interview only, for shortlisted applicants.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly and unusually favourably. The IADT entry-requirements text names "computational science" as an accepted bachelor field, and the consortium adds that applicants from other fields "may be considered if they demonstrate relevant prior experience in areas such as sound, music, film, or media studies." A software-engineering BSc is directly named-adjacent here.
programs.tuitionIntl: €15,000 total for the two years (€7,500 per year) for self-funded students — but scholarship holders pay nothing.
programs.scholarship: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship — open to non-EU nationals including Tunisians, awarded on merit. Maximum 24 places on the programme each year with "a significant percentage" receiving the scholarship.
programs.stipend: Full tuition waiver + €1,400/month living allowance + travel allowance of roughly €2,000–3,000 per year + health insurance + a €1,000 installation allowance (figures as published for the current call — reconfirm against the 2027 call, EMJM rates are set per call).
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The 2026 intake opened 20 October 2025. Expect the 2027-intake call to open around mid/late October 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The 2026 intake closed 27 January 2026 (extended from 20 January). Applications for 2026 are now closed. For September 2027 entry expect a deadline in the second half of January 2027 — this is the single most important date to watch in this whole slice.
programs.facilities: FilmEU European University alliance infrastructure across three schools; IADT is one of Ireland's principal screen-media schools, LMTA is Lithuania's national music and theatre academy, Lusófona runs the Lisbon sound labs (Pro Tools, Max/MSP, Arduino). Alumni/staff detail UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: By far the best funding-to-fit ratio available to a Tunisian applicant anywhere in this slice: fully funded, English-taught, portfolio-assessed rather than audition-assessed, and it explicitly welcomes a computational-science background. The obstacles are competition (max 24 places, worldwide) and the fact that it is media-arts sound design rather than club/DJ music production — it will make him a sound designer with production skills, not a dance-music producer per se.

programs.program: Mestrado em Computação Musical e Design de Som (Master in Musical Computing and Sound Design)
programs.university: Universidade de Coimbra — Departamento de Engenharia Informática (FCTUC)
programs.institutionType: Public university (informatics engineering department, interdisciplinary with music and design)
programs.focus: Sound Design; Music Production; Electronic Music; Film/Game Sound; Immersive/Interactive Audio
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (60 ECTS per year, full-time)
programs.language: Portuguese
programs.whatYouStudy: Verified study plan. Year 1 core (48 ECTS): Musical Perception and Cognition; Programming for Sound and Music; Seminar 1 — Sound, Art and Technology; 20th/21st-Century Compositional Theories and Practices; Computer-Assisted Composition and Sound Programming; Sound Design; Signal Processing for Sound and Music; Seminar 2 — Current Trends in Sound Design. Year 1 options: Audio for Audiovisual Media, Video Game Sound Design, Recording and Mixing, Sound Improvisation Laboratory. Year 2 core (12 ECTS): Artificial Intelligence in Music; New Interfaces for Musical Expression. Year 2 capstone (42 ECTS): dissertation OR internship. Stated career profiles include sound designer, music producer, audio engineer, music software programmer, composer, performer.
programs.entryRequirements: Holders of a licenciatura or legal equivalent in Informática (computer science), Música, Design e Multimédia "e licenciaturas afins" (related degrees), or a foreign first-cycle degree organised under Bologna principles. Portuguese-language capacity is effectively necessary given the language of instruction. €50 application fee.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — no portfolio specification was published on the course pages read. Selection criteria are set in the course-specific edital (opening notice); request it from the DEI or check the course page's "Editais" menu.
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED — none published; no audition is indicated for an engineering-department master.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — the strongest explicit statement in the slice. The admission rule opens the course to "titulares do grau de licenciado ou equivalente legal em: Informática, Música, Design e Multimédia e licenciaturas afins." Informática (computer science) is listed FIRST, ahead of music. A software-engineering BSc is squarely inside the target intake.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED for a standalone 2nd-cycle master. programs.program: Biennio Accademico di II livello in Music Production (Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Music Production)
programs.university: Saint Louis College of Music (AFAM institution authorised by MUR)
programs.institutionType: Private specialist music academy, ministerially authorised (AFAM) — degrees recognised by the Italian MUR
programs.durationEcts: 2 years; approx. 300 contact hours per year. CFA total UNVERIFIED (the standard is 120 CFA for an Italian biennio).
programs.language: Italian and English (the course page states "Lingua: Italiano e Inglese")
programs.focus: Music Production — the closest thing in this slice to a producer's degree
programs.whatYouStudy: Verified from the official page. Each student learns to run a music-production project through every phase, from the creative idea to arrangement with real and virtual instruments, recording, mixing and mastering. Named modules: LABORATORIO DI PRODUZIONE — developing original projects with a music-producer's approach to the whole production chain; TECNICHE DI RIPRESA E REGISTRAZIONE — each specialising student produces TWO TRACKS end-to-end, from pre-production and arrangement through rehearsals, recording and overdubbing, microphone choice and placement, editing, mixing and mastering; ORCHESTRAZIONE — professional virtual orchestration, arrangement, real and virtual instruments, sound construction within the production; ANALISI DELLA PRODUZIONE MUSICALE — evolution of the producer's role, the approaches of the most influential producers in history, and the compositional/structural/expressive techniques of the main contemporary popular-music languages, completed with sound design applied to the timbral character of a track; DIRITTO D'AUTORE, ROYALTIES E CONTRATTUALISTICA — copyright, royalties, licence, publishing, production and performance contracts. The bienni are explicitly "costruiti intorno alle inclinazioni artistiche di ciascuno studente", built around each student's own artistic direction, with original productions and third-party commissioned work running through the whole degree.
programs.entryRequirements: Stated requirement: "Diploma accademico triennale di primo livello già conseguito o da conseguirsi entro la sessione di Febbraio" (conditional enrolment possible). Attendance is compulsory at a minimum of 80% of classes; a part-time route exists for students who cannot attend everything. Erasmus+ mobility of up to 12 months within the biennio is available.
programs.portfolioSpec: VERIFIED and exact for the pre-selection stage: "Registra uno o più video contenenti 3 brani, eseguiti da te in gruppo (minimo trio) che siano rappresentativi della tua attività artistica" — record one or more videos containing THREE PIECES, performed by you in a group of at least a TRIO, representative of your artistic activity; files must be uploaded to YouTube or a similar web portal and the LINKS entered in the application form. IMPORTANT CAVEAT: this ensemble-video wording is the shared text used across Saint Louis's academic courses and is clearly written for performer tracks — for the Music Production biennio you should ask the Segreteria in writing what the equivalent production portfolio is (most likely produced/mixed tracks rather than a live trio video). Also mandatory: download and check the Piano di studi, which lists the competences tested in each individual prova.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage: (1) pre-selection on the submitted video links; (2) for those who pass, admission tests held ON SITE in Rome over TWO CONSECUTIVE DAYS, in the June and September sessions. Numero chiuso: maximum 20 students per academic year, drawn from Saint Louis's own first-level graduates plus external candidates selected by audition.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — this is the weak point. The published requirement names a "diploma accademico triennale di primo livello" (an Italian first-level academic diploma in music). The honest caveat: this is engineering, not craft — he would spend two years on signal processing, coding and acoustics, and would emerge as an audio engineer or audio-software developer, not a trained producer or DJ. Realistic strategy: treat it as the fundable anchor application and pair it with a craft-focused programme, or accept that Milan itself supplies the scene while the degree supplies the technical depth and the visa.
