The MFA Digital Arts is English-taught and practice-based, which are real advantages, but there is NO PUBLISHED EVIDENCE that it teaches sound, audio or music production at all — its published description centres on visual art and the moving image. Do not apply here on the strength of this entry; email the department first and ask specifically whether sound practice is supervised. Malta should otherwise be treated as a country with no sound-design or music-production master.

programs.program: MFA Sound Design for Film and Television
programs.university: National Film and Television School (NFTS)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years full-time (ECTS not published; UK MFA)
programs.institutionType: Film school (independent postgraduate national film school; CILECT/GEECT member)
programs.language: English
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Immersive Audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Craft-first, entirely project-based: dialogue editing, atmospheres, Foley, ADR, designed FX, post-production technology and creative storytelling with sound. Students progress from foundational workshops to graduation films across fiction, documentary, animation, games and TV, working alongside NFTS composers, editors, directors and producers on real productions. Facilities used daily: Pro Tools edit suites on Apple hardware with PSI LCR/5.1 monitoring and Avid S1 controllers; Dolby-certified dubbing theatres with Avid S6/S4 consoles and JBL monitoring; a Dolby Atmos theatre in the historic Anvil studio; a music recording studio used for live music and Foley.
programs.entryRequirements: No fixed qualification list. Degree holders preferred but not required if the portfolio is strong; an 'alternative qualification' or 'creative track record' is considered. International applicants must meet UK visa and English-language requirements (IELTS/equivalent — he has NOT yet taken a test, so this must be booked well ahead).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes. The course page states applicants' 'background may be in the arts or other media' and welcomes those seeking 'a further professional qualification or [who] wish to broaden your knowledge'. No music or film degree is required.
programs.portfolioSpec: Two items, both submitted as Vimeo links: (1) a custom sound-design exercise — you download a video file during the application and design sound to it; (2) one further piece — preferably a short film you worked on, or an audio-only piece — maximum 10 minutes.
programs.auditionSpec: Interview, then a FIVE-DAY on-site selection workshop at the Beaconsfield campus (£150 workshop fee). Physical attendance in the UK is required — budget for visa/travel.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The January 2027 intake cycle opened in 2026 and is now closed. For the JANUARY 2028 intake expect the portal to open roughly mid-2027.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Applications for January 2027 entry are closed (an aggregator listed 3 Sep 2026 for that cycle; not confirmed on the official page). NOTE: NFTS sound intakes start in JANUARY, not September — his realistic target is January 2028, not September 2027.
programs.tuitionIntl: £27,600 per year for International students (incl. EU without settled status) for 2027 entry — roughly £55,200 over two years. Home fee £15,950/yr. Plus £150 selection-workshop fee and a £500 non-refundable deposit. Production and facility costs are included in the fee.
programs.scholarship: None found that is specifically open to a Tunisian/non-EU applicant. NFTS states it awards more scholarships and bursaries to BRITISH students, relative to student-body size, than almost any other UK institution; international and EU students are directed to a general Funding Guide.
programs.fundingLevel: None (for a non-EU applicant, on verified information)
programs.facilities: Dolby Atmos theatre in the Anvil studio; Dolby-certified dubbing theatres with Avid S6 and S4 consoles; Pro Tools edit suites with PSI LCR/5.1 monitoring and Avid S1 controllers; dedicated music-recording and Foley stage. Deep UK film/TV industry links; widely rated one of the top film schools in the world.
programs.fitNotes: Best-in-class hands-on sound-design training in Europe and, crucially, the most background-agnostic of all the film schools — a software-engineering BSc is genuinely acceptable here. The obstacles are money (~£55k tuition alone, no verified non-EU scholarship), a five-day in-person selection workshop, and the January start (so September 2027 is not available — aim January 2028). Also note this is FILM sound, not club/DJ production: it will make him a superb sound designer, not directly a dance-music producer.

programs.program: Film Sound Design — Master's Programme in Film and Television (major in Film Sound Design)
programs.university: Aalto University, Department of Film (ELO Film School Helsinki)
programs.degree: MA (Master of Arts, Art and Design)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS
programs.institutionType: Public university (art & design school with the national film school, ELO; CILECT/GEECT member)
programs.language: English
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering
programs.whatYouStudy: 120 ECTS split as 30 ECTS joint departmental studies (film theory, history, research skills), 60 ECTS advanced sound-design studies and 30 ECTS thesis. Advanced studies cover effects recording, audio drama, music in narrative, sound recording on set and post-production sound design. Teaching is explicitly 'learning by doing', in small groups with peer learning, on ELO's own productions. Students may take electives at other Aalto schools or at the University of the Arts Helsinki (Sibelius Academy) — a route to electronic-music and studio courses alongside film sound. Close working relationships with Finland's leading film-sound companies and with Yle, the national broadcaster.
programs.entryRequirements: A relevant Bachelor's degree. Aalto explicitly adds: 'Applicants without a previous degree or with a degree from another field are taken into account.' English proficiency evidence required (IELTS/TOEFL or equivalent — not yet taken).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — the strongest explicit wording found anywhere in this slice: 'Applicants without a previous degree or with a degree from another field are taken into account.' A BSc in Software Engineering is squarely inside that sentence; selection then rests on the portfolio.
programs.portfolioSpec: Downloadable links to a MAXIMUM OF THREE samples of your work (Vimeo, YouTube or equivalent) with a COMBINED viewing time of 30 MINUTES OR LESS. Plus a motivation letter (max 4,000 characters) and a report on your technical and artistic process (max 2,000 characters), and academic transcripts.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-phase selection. Phase I is a document/portfolio review (no attendance). Phase II is an interview for shortlisted candidates, who may be given assignments to prepare about a week beforehand. No live musical audition.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The last published window opened 1 December 2025. Expect the 2027-intake window to open around early December 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Last published: 1 December 2025 – 2 January 2026 for autumn 2026 entry. For SEPTEMBER 2027 entry expect approximately 1 Dec 2026 – early Jan 2027.
programs.tuitionIntl: €20,000 per year for non-EU/EEA citizens (Tunisian nationality = fee-liable). EU/EEA/Swiss citizens pay nothing.
programs.scholarship: Aalto University Scholarship — tuition-fee waivers awarded to fee-paying students at the point of admission (no separate application). Aalto's own wording: 'a small number of scholarships in the form of tuition fee waivers'. Waivers are typically 50% or 100% of tuition; the exact split for this programme is UNVERIFIED.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition waiver possible; competitive and not guaranteed)
programs.stipend: No living stipend. The waiver covers tuition only. Helsinki living costs must be self-funded — UNVERIFIED amount required for the residence permit.
programs.facilities: ELO is the only university-level film school in Finland and this is the only university-level sound-design major in the country — one of only a handful in Europe. Industry ties to Finland's main film-sound houses and to Yle. Specific studio inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The single best realistic target in this slice for him: taught fully in English, explicitly open to applicants from another field, a portfolio requirement he can build in 12 months (three pieces, 30 minutes total), no live musical audition, and a real chance of a full tuition waiver. Main obstacle: the €20,000 fee if no waiver is granted, plus Helsinki living costs. Content is film sound rather than dance-music production, but the Sibelius Academy elective route partly bridges that.

programs.program: Diplôme de La Fémis — département SON (via the Concours International)
programs.university: La Fémis — École nationale supérieure des métiers de l'image et du son (PSL)
programs.degree: Diplôme de La Fémis — state-recognised master-level (niveau 7) title; the school is part of Université PSL
programs.durationEcts: 4 years full-time (the cursus général). ECTS UNVERIFIED.
programs.institutionType: Public national film school (grande école under the Ministry of Culture; CILECT/GEECT member)
programs.language: French (mandatory — 'La maîtrise de la langue française est obligatoire'; non-francophone applicants must supply a certificate of at least B1)
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Music for film
programs.whatYouStudy: The Son department trains complete film-sound authors: location recording, sound editing, sound design, music supervision and final mixing, all through the school's own productions in collaboration with the six other departments (Réalisation, Image, Montage, Scénario, Décor, Production). Detailed module list UNVERIFIED — the departmental page was not retrievable at time of writing.
programs.entryRequirements: Baccalauréat equivalent PLUS a minimum of two validated years of higher education (bac+2) — his BSc satisfies this comfortably. Age: under 27 on 1 January of the competition year, OR under 30 with at least two years of professional experience. The Concours International is reserved for nationals of countries outside the EU-27, Iceland, Liechtenstein, Norway, Andorra, Monaco and Switzerland — Tunisia qualifies. Dual nationals holding an EU passport must instead sit the concours général.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes. No music, sound or film degree is required anywhere in the eligibility rules — only bac+2 in any subject, the age limit and French fluency. This is one of the most open-on-paper routes in the whole slice; the filter is the concours itself, not the diploma.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not a conventional portfolio. Phase 1 requires a personal investigative/creative dossier ('travail d'enquête personnel') developed on ONE of three themes set by the school, submitted by a fixed date; plus departmental (Son-specific) exams and a film-analysis exam.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-phase competitive concours. Phase 1 (admissibilité): the themed personal dossier, departmental exams by VIDEOCONFERENCE, and a film-analysis exam by videoconference. Phase 2 (admission): an oral before a seven-member jury representing all teaching departments, held ON SITE at La Fémis in Paris over roughly two weeks in June.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Online registration for the last cycle opened 9 December 2025 at 12:00. Expect the equivalent to open around early December 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Last cycle: registration 9 Dec 2025 – 14 Jan 2026; themed dossier due 12 Feb 2026; departmental videoconference exams 24–26 Feb 2026; film-analysis exam 25 Feb 2026; admissibility results 2 Apr 2026; oral admission exams 15–26 Jun 2026 in Paris; final results 26 Jun 2026 at 18:00.
programs.tuitionIntl: €458 for the 2025-2026 academic year (set annually by ministerial decree), payable by 31 October. Plus a non-refundable concours registration fee of €142 (waived for scholarship holders). This is effectively free tuition.
programs.scholarship: CROUS social-criteria grants (échelon 0 = fee waiver, up to échelon 7 = €5,539/yr) — but eligibility for a Tunisian national is restricted: available to OFPRA refugee-card holders, or where a parent has resided in France for two years, or under Treaty-of-Rome provisions for EU workers. On the verified text, a Tunisian applying directly from Tunisia would NOT normally qualify. Fondation Vallet offers €5,200 grants, but only AFTER completing one year of study.
programs.fundingLevel: Full on tuition (fees are €458/yr) / None verified for living costs at entry
programs.stipend: No entry-level stipend verified for a non-EU student. CROUS grants (up to €5,539/yr) plus CAF housing aid (ALS/APL), VISALE rent guarantee up to €1,500 in Île-de-France, and €3.66 university meals exist but the CROUS eligibility conditions read as excluding a first-year Tunisian arrival. Fondation Vallet €5,200 becomes possible from year two.
programs.facilities: France's national film school; PSL member; among the most prestigious film schools in the world with deep French industry placement. Studio inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: On paper the best value in Europe — near-zero tuition, no music degree required, and his fluent French removes the usual language blocker that kills most continental options. Two real obstacles: the Concours International is ferociously selective (a handful of places across all seven departments) and the Son track is a FOUR-year commitment in film sound, which is a long detour from a DJ/producer career. Also, an on-site oral in Paris in June is mandatory.

programs.program: Filmton / Sounddesign (Diplomaufbaustudium)
programs.university: Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg
programs.degree: Diplom der Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg — a postgraduate (Aufbau) diploma at master level
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters of coursework + 1 diploma semester (5 semesters total). ECTS UNVERIFIED.
programs.institutionType: Film school (state-owned specialist film academy; CILECT/GEECT member)
programs.language: German, with English in some project seminars ('Deutsch/Englisch im PS'). German B2 minimum required; solid English also expected.
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Immersive Audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Part of the combined 'Filmmusik & Sounddesign' department. Covers the entire chain: production sound on set, sound post-production (effects, sound design, ADR/dubbing), and final mixing in DOLBY ATMOS. Students work on Filmakademie's very large slate of student productions alongside the film-music students, with strong crossover into the Animationsinstitut's animation and games work. Pro Tools is the working environment.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed diploma, bachelor's or master's degree in musicology, media studies OR A RELATED FIELD, PLUS proof of approximately six months of practical/professional experience in the industry (recording studio, broadcasting, theatre, event production). Recommended prior knowledge: studio technology basics, microphone technique, DAW proficiency, basic musical understanding.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check. The wording is 'musicology, media studies or a related field' — a software-engineering BSc is not named and would have to be argued as 'related' (audio software/DSP framing helps). The harder gate is the mandatory ~6 months of documented industry audio experience, which he does not yet have. Verdict: not eligible today; potentially eligible after a 6-month studio/post-house placement plus German to B2.
programs.portfolioSpec: 'Vorlage eigener Werke' — your own works, e.g. film scoring, radio plays, sound collages, music recordings or audio mixes. TOTAL DURATION NOT MORE THAN 20 MINUTES. Technical spec: container MP4, codec H.264, data rate 15 MB/s, maximum file size 1 GB, must play in VLC or QuickTime. You must clearly describe your individual contribution to each submitted work.
programs.auditionSpec: Multi-stage and demanding: formal screening → portfolio review by a faculty commission → ON-SITE examination with individual interviews → a 72-HOUR PRACTICAL EXAM → a final colloquium. Decisions typically within 8-10 days after the on-site stage.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The portal opens annually in the autumn preceding the 15 February deadline.
programs.deadline: 15 February (annual, recurring date published on the school's own pages). For a 2027 start this means 15 February 2027 — confirm on the official Bewerbung page once the cycle opens.
programs.tuitionIntl: €1,500 per semester for non-EU citizens (i.e. roughly €7,500 over five semesters). EU citizens taking it as a second degree pay €0–€650. This is unusually cheap for a school of this calibre.
programs.scholarship: None found on the pages read that is specifically open to a non-EU/Tunisian applicant. DAAD external funding would be the usual route — UNVERIFIED for this institution.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (very low fee rather than a scholarship)
programs.facilities: Dolby Atmos mixing; combined film music and sound-design department; Filmakademie is consistently ranked among the leading film schools in Europe and produces a very high volume of student films, animation and games work through the Animationsinstitut, giving sound students an unusual amount of real material to work on.
programs.fitNotes: Outstanding craft training at a near-token fee (€1,500/semester for non-EU), and the Dolby Atmos + games/animation crossover is genuinely valuable. But it is currently out of reach: German B2, a music/media-adjacent degree, and ~6 months of documented professional audio experience are all required, and the entrance process includes a 72-hour on-site practical exam. Treat as a 2028-2029 target after a gap year building studio experience and German.

programs.program: Sound Design for Audiovisual Media (M.F.A.)
programs.university: Filmuniversität Babelsberg KONRAD WOLF
programs.durationEcts: 120 LP (ECTS). The official page states 6 semesters; winter-term entry only. Confirm the semester count directly with the programme office.
programs.institutionType: Public film university (Germany's oldest film school; CILECT/GEECT member)
programs.language: German (instruction). Non-German applicants educated outside German-speaking institutions must prove German at DSH-1 level or equivalent; B1 certification is accepted provisionally at application if higher proof is not yet available.
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Immersive Audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Four core domains: audio engineering, sound mixing, acoustics and music. Students learn to mix sound for theatrical motion pictures and to run projects as SOUND SUPERVISOR; graduates' competences are stated as equivalent to a Diplom-Tonmeister. Delivered through interdisciplinary collaboration on artistic projects with the university's directing, cinematography and production students, plus collaborations and contacts with the German film industry (Studio Babelsberg is next door).
programs.entryRequirements: 'Proof of a completed Bachelor of Fine Arts (B.F.A.) degree in Sound, Tonmeister*in or a comparable subject-specific degree.' Plus German at DSH-1. An administrative application fee is charged (amount UNVERIFIED).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No. The requirement is explicitly a B.F.A. 'in Sound, Tonmeister*in or a comparable SUBJECT-SPECIFIC degree', and the entrance exam includes a piano audition and score-harmony analysis. A software-engineering BSc will not clear this bar.
programs.portfolioSpec: Three components, all mandatory: (1) a documentation of works and projects from the last three years revealing the applicant's individual artistic position, MAXIMUM 12 PAGES; (2) video material totalling MAXIMUM 15 MINUTES including AT LEAST THREE FILMS on which the applicant did the sound design (MPG/MPEG/MP4/MOV/WMV, max 3.5 GB); (3) at least one piece of MUSIC that the applicant personally recorded or mixed (WAV/MP3/MP4, max 5 GB).
programs.auditionSpec: Three-part on-site entrance examination. Part 1 MUSIC TEST: hearing/interval identification, score harmony analysis, a PIANO AUDITION, and evaluation of audio examples. Part 2 INTERVIEW: portfolio presentation plus questioning on acoustics and recording technology. Part 3 ARTISTIC/PRACTICAL EXAM: create a soundtrack for a short film using Pro Tools and present an analysis of its tonal dramaturgy.
programs.applicationOpens: 12 April (as published on the official application page)
programs.deadline: 12 April – 18 May 2027 as currently published on the official page, for winter-semester entry. This aligns with an autumn 2027 start — but confirm on the page when the cycle opens, as film-university dates occasionally shift.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition fee stated; a semester/administrative fee applies but the amount is UNVERIFIED on the pages read. German public film universities normally charge only a semester contribution.
programs.scholarship: None found on the programme pages. DAAD would be the external route — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fundingLevel: UNVERIFIED (tuition-free public institution, but no named scholarship confirmed)
programs.facilities: Germany's oldest and largest film university, adjacent to Studio Babelsberg; strong industry pipeline. Specific studio and Atmos inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Elite, essentially tuition-free, and the Tonmeister-level training is superb — but it is the single hardest gate in this slice for him. It demands a sound/Tonmeister B.F.A., German at DSH-1, three existing films with his sound design, a self-recorded/mixed music piece, AND a piano audition with harmony analysis. Realistically closed unless he first does a sound bachelor. Listed for completeness, not as a target.

programs.program: MA Composition and Theory — Major in Sound Design
programs.university: Zürcher Hochschule der Künste (Zurich University of the Arts, ZHdK)
programs.degree: MA (Master of Arts in Composition and Theory, major Sound Design)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years. ECTS UNVERIFIED (Swiss MA is normally 120 ECTS).
programs.institutionType: Public university of the arts (music department; the film department is a GEECT member and the sound-design major works directly on film and game projects)
programs.language: German OR English — 'The language of instruction is German or English.' Foreign-language applicants must prove competence in the relevant language (native fluency, transcript, recognised certificate, or a degree taught in that language).
programs.focus: Sound Design; Film/Game Sound; Immersive Audio; Electronic Music
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound treated as raw material for linear AND interactive multi-sensory media. Students work under industry professionals on real film, game and interaction projects, are connected to national and international studios and sound professionals, and use industry-standard software and hardware. This is the most game-audio and interaction-oriented of the German-speaking options.
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree or equivalent from an accredited institution is the standard route. ZHdK explicitly notes it 'may admit individuals without a bachelor's degree or equivalent qualification' in exceptional cases, on submission of a special dossier. Language proof in German or English.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — leaning yes on paper. No music or film degree is named as a prerequisite and ZHdK will even admit without a bachelor via special dossier. HOWEVER the aptitude test includes a 30-minute MUSICAL APTITUDE TEST (theory tasks and improvisation), which is where a self-taught producer with no formal training is most likely to be filtered out. Worth attempting with a year of music-theory prep.
programs.portfolioSpec: 3–4 creative works totalling approximately 10 MINUTES MAXIMUM. Formats: scores/texts as PDF, audio as MP3, video as MP4 — all compressed into a SINGLE ZIP file of max 1.95 GB. Plus a written commentary on each work, maximum 2 A4 pages in total. An optional file of links to personal portfolio sites may be added.
programs.auditionSpec: On-site aptitude test in three parts: (1) PRACTICAL EXAM — sound-design tasks, 90 minutes preparation then a 20-minute presentation; (2) ORAL EXAM — film/game analysis, 60 minutes preparation then a 10-minute discussion, plus presentation of your submitted works; (3) MUSICAL APTITUDE TEST — theory tasks and improvisation, 30 minutes.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Last published window opened 6 January 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Last published: applications 6 January – 2 March 2026; aptitude test 13–14 April 2026; programme start 14 September 2026. For a September 2027 start expect approximately January – early March 2027.

programs.scholarship: None found on the pages read for a non-Swiss/non-EU applicant. Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships are the usual external route for Tunisian nationals — UNVERIFIED for this programme.
programs.facilities: Industry-standard software and hardware; real film, game and interaction projects; connections to national and international sound studios. Specific room/console inventory UNVERIFIED. Zurich living costs are among the highest in Europe.
programs.fitNotes: The most attractive continental option after Aalto: it can be taken in ENGLISH, it takes game and interactive audio seriously (closest to electronic-music thinking of any film-school-adjacent sound master here), and the portfolio ask is small — 3-4 works, 10 minutes total. The obstacles are the 30-minute musical aptitude test with improvisation, an on-site two-day aptitude exam in Zurich, and unverified (but certainly high) Swiss living costs.

programs.program: Music (M.A.) — Sonic Arts concentration area (1st Education / thesis master)

programs.whatYouStudy: Composition/creation with technology in the Sonic Arts stream. The Sonic Arts Lab is 'the main teaching and research space for students and faculty in the Sonic Arts program' and 'houses a 8 channel sound diffusion system that can be configured for a range of purposes including high order ambisonics, spatial composition, loudspeaker orchestras, or multichannel sound installations', plus a workstation with advanced sound-processing software and a variety of microphones and field-recording equipment. MIAM also runs an Immersive Lab, a professional recording studio, a Percussion Lab, a Sound Gallery, concert/seminar halls and a music library. Concentration areas alongside Sonic Arts include Sound Engineering and Design, Composition, Theory, Musicology, Ethnomusicology, Performance and Music Business & Management. Detailed Sonic Arts module list UNVERIFIED.
programs.portfolioSpec: PRIOR CYCLE (İTÜ MIAM 2022–2023 Entrance Exam Handbook) — confirm the current handbook. Sonic Arts: 'Composition portfolio (Audio + Scores if available). Any other relevant material is also welcome.' Explicitly: 'Optional: Custom made software of projects that have developed as a sample of programming skills including MaxMSP, SuperCollider, Processing etc.' Portfolio is emailed (not uploaded): files under 25 MB attached, larger files as a Google Drive / WeTransfer / Dropbox link, subject line '[MIAM20xx] Your Name & Surname'. A separate MIAM Entrance Exam Contact Form (name, surname, preferred concentration area, phone, e-mail) must accompany it. Note: sending the portfolio is an extra step and does NOT replace official registration at www.sis.itu.edu.tr.
programs.auditionSpec: Yes — on-site. 'ITU MIAM Entrance Exam and the interviews will be held in-person.' Structure (2022 cycle): a written General Music Knowledge and Music Theory exam (12:30–14:30), then a field exam for the chosen concentration area — Sonic Arts is explicitly listed among the masters field exams (15:00–17:00) — then individual interviews spread over the following ~3 days. Requires travel to Istanbul.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree; application governed by 'Istanbul Technical University Graduate Level Regulations and Senate Principles'. Two letters of recommendation are required 'to verify their motivation and determination', plus a portfolio relevant to the application area. Online pre-registration via www.sis.itu.edu.tr. ALES/GRE and the exact English-proficiency score threshold follow İTÜ Graduate School rules — exact required scores UNVERIFIED (not stated on the MIAM pages read). IELTS/TOEFL will be needed — he has not yet taken one.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — leaning favourable for this concentration. Neither the MIAM admission page nor the entrance-exam handbook read states any requirement for a music bachelor; selection runs on portfolio + exams. The Sonic Arts portfolio explicitly invites 'Custom made software ... including MaxMSP, SuperCollider, Processing' as evidence of programming skills, which directly rewards a software-engineering background. The real obstacle is the compulsory written 'General Music Knowledge and Music Theory' exam, which is not waived for non-music applicants. Formal wording on non-music bachelors: UNVERIFIED — confirm with miam@itu.edu.tr.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE — confirm new date. 2022 cycle: portfolio submission 24 June; online registration via SIS 27 June; written exams 29 June; interviews 29–30 June and 1 July. For a September 2027 start expect an equivalent late-June 2027 window plus a separate spring-semester round (a 2024–2025 Bahar/spring guide also exists, published late January).
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE — typically announced on the MIAM news page in May (2024–2025 guide published 23 May 2024) for the autumn intake, and late January for the spring intake. 2027 dates not yet published.
programs.scholarship: Türkiye Bursları (YTB) — Arts Scholarship Programme. İTÜ is one of only three universities in that programme (with Ankara Music and Fine Arts University and Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli University), and the music/performing-arts fields listed for it explicitly include music technology at master's level. Open to citizens of all countries except Türkiye; master's applicants need a minimum 75% prior academic average and to be under 30.
programs.fundingLevel: Full (if Türkiye Bursları is awarded); otherwise low-cost public tuition
programs.stipend: Türkiye Bursları master's package: 6,500 TL monthly stipend, full tuition coverage, accommodation, health insurance, a one-year Turkish language course, and round-trip airfare at programme start and completion.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED. İTÜ's own pages confirm international students pay a tuition/contribution fee set annually by the Council of Higher Education and payable in two instalments to Vakıfbank, but the numeric table was not accessible. Third-party sites quote roughly USD 2,000–5,000/year for İTÜ graduate programmes — treat as unconfirmed.
programs.facilities: Recording Studio; Sonic Arts Lab (8-channel diffusion, high-order ambisonics, spatial composition, loudspeaker orchestras, multichannel installations); Immersive Lab; Percussion Lab; Sound Gallery; one large and two medium concert halls; large music library with printed and audiovisual materials. Staff: 2 professors, 9 associate professors, 16 instructors from several countries. Currently ~141 master's and ~73 PhD students. MIAM reports 500+ graduates, many accepted for doctorates at Stanford, Columbia, UC Berkeley and Johns Hopkins. Located on the İTÜ Maçka campus in Beşiktaş, central Istanbul.
programs.fitNotes: Strongest single fit in this slice: fully in English, in a major electronic-music city, with a fully-funded government scholarship route (Türkiye Bursları Arts) that explicitly covers İTÜ music technology at master's level. His coding background is an asset here rather than a liability. Main obstacle: the compulsory written music-theory and general-music-knowledge exam plus an in-person Istanbul entrance exam — he would need roughly a year of deliberate music-theory preparation, and he must sit IELTS/TOEFL.

programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES (apparently) — the published condition is simply 'студенти завършили бакалавърска степен' (students who have completed a bachelor's degree), with no subject-field restriction. This contrasts sharply with the sister programme Audiovisual Design at the same faculty, which explicitly restricts entry to bachelors in Music Education Pedagogy (field 1.3) or Music and Dance Arts (field 8.3). Worth confirming in writing with the director that a foreign engineering BSc is accepted.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. FNOI publishes a 'Прием в ОКС Магистър' announcement each year (2025–2026 edition published for that cycle); intake is from the winter semester, so applications typically fall in September. The 2027/28 call is not yet published.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — historically late summer (August–September) for the winter-semester intake.
programs.scholarship: None found specifically attached to this programme. Bulgaria operates state scholarship quotas for foreign nationals via the Ministry of Education and bilateral agreements, but no Tunisia-specific award was verified.
programs.fundingLevel: UNVERIFIED — the programme is explicitly fee-paying ('платено обучение')
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED. FNOI publishes a semester fee table (Такси Магистри семестриални 2025–2026) but the PDF could not be parsed; request the figure from the faculty.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED for this programme specifically. Programme director: Prof. Dr. Adrian Georgiev (aggeorgiev@uni-sofia.bg, +359 2 970 62 45).
programs.fitNotes: On paper the single most accessible entry route in the whole slice for him: any bachelor accepted, and the entrance 'portfolio' can be a remix he produces himself. The blockers are language (all instruction in Bulgarian — he would need a Bulgarian preparatory year or self-study) and the absence of any verified funding, since the programme is fee-paying by design.

programs.program: Тонрежисура (Sound Engineering / Tonmeister) — master's programme
programs.university: New Bulgarian University (Нов български университет, NBU) — Department of Music
programs.institutionType: Private accredited university
programs.degree: Master's; professional qualification awarded: 'магистър по тонрежисура'
programs.focus: Recording / Engineering; Electronic Music; Music Production; Film & Game Sound
programs.language: Bulgarian
programs.durationEcts: 2 semesters / 63 credits for holders of a music-and-dance-arts bachelor. For graduates of OTHER fields: an individualised curriculum of MINIMUM 3 semesters, the first of which is preparatory. Credit split published as: 4 lecture courses (12 cr), 2 practical courses (6 cr), 5 training courses in semester 1 (15 cr), 6 courses in semester 2 (30 cr).
programs.whatYouStudy: Published scope: тонрежисура (sound direction), звукови технологии (audio technologies), софтуерни решения в музикалното студио (software solutions in the music studio), електронен звук (electronic sound), звуков монтаж (audio editing), аудиодизайн на звук (sound design), синтез на звук (sound synthesis), мастеринг (mastering), звук в киното и телевизията (sound in film and television), and компютърно моделиране на звуковата картина (computer modelling of the sound picture). NBU describes the programme as practice-oriented with exchange opportunities at European institutions. Graduation is by master's thesis defence or state exam.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not a formal portfolio. The specialised music entrance exam requires an essay on the theme 'Защо искам да се обучавам в тази специалност' (Why I want to study in this specialty). Candidates 'may also present compositions or developed audio projects to the commission' — i.e. a portfolio is invited but optional. No number, length or format is prescribed.
programs.auditionSpec: Specialised exam (essay) plus an interview with the admissions commission; exam fee 40 BGN. The general aptitude test (ТОП, a 100-minute online exam, 40 BGN, retakeable with the highest score counting) is REQUIRED for most candidates but foreign citizens and applicants who already hold a higher-education degree are exempt — so he would be exempt on both counts. Whether the essay/interview can be sat remotely is UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree. Foreign citizens and holders of an existing higher-education degree are exempt from the ТОП aptitude test.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. The programme documents a formal pathway: applicants with a bachelor in music and dance arts complete the programme in 2 semesters, while 'graduates from other fields follow an individualised curriculum lasting a minimum of 3 semesters, with the first being preparatory'. This is the clearest published accommodation of a non-music bachelor found in this entire slice.
programs.deadline: PRIOR/CURRENT CYCLE - confirm new date. NBU runs three ranking rounds per year; 2026 rounds were: July I — register by 3 July, results 8 July; July II — register by 24 July, results 29 July; August — register by 14 August, results 18 August. Expect an equivalent July–August 2027 sequence for a September 2027 start.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for 2027 — ТОП test sessions in 2026 ran June–August, with registration rolling from spring.
programs.scholarship: None found for this programme. NBU offers internal reductions (25% family, 50% disability, 50% full orphan; 25% off the first semester for NBU's own bachelor graduates) — none of which apply to an external Tunisian applicant.
programs.tuitionIntl: Programme-specific figure UNVERIFIED. NBU's published master's fee bands: two-semester programmes 1,800–2,000 EUR per semester; three-semester programmes 1,600–1,800 EUR per semester. On the 3-semester non-music track that implies roughly 4,800–5,400 EUR total. Fees are guaranteed unchanged for the whole period of uninterrupted study.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — no studio inventory published on the pages read. Department head: Prof. Dr. Milena Shushulova (+359 2 8110 504). Programme director: Dr. Ana Lincheva (alincheva@nbu.bg, 02/8110 505).
programs.fitNotes: The best structural fit for his exact profile in the Balkans: NBU has already designed a route for people arriving from non-music degrees, with a preparatory first semester. Content (electronic sound, synthesis, mastering, studio software) maps directly onto DJ/producer ambitions. Two real blockers: instruction is entirely in Bulgarian, and it is a self-pay private university with no funding route identified.

programs.program: Arta Sunetului de Film (Film Sound Art) — master
programs.university: UNATC 'I.L. Caragiale' — National University of Theatre and Cinematography, Faculty of Film
programs.institutionType: Public film and theatre school (national arts university)
programs.focus: Film & Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive / multichannel audio
programs.language: Romanian. Film Sound is NOT among UNATC's English-taught masters (those are Art of Game Design, Audiovisual Archives: Preservation and Programming, Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts, and Visual Effects).
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 credits
programs.whatYouStudy: Year 1: Sound Design; Sound Capture and Editing; Foley Art; Research and Creative Cinematography Workshop; Internship and Practice. Year 2: Advanced Sound Design; Film Sound Production/Post-production; Multichannel Mixing; Research and Creative Cinematography Workshop; Internship and Practice; Dissertation. The department states master's students 'concentrate on aspects related to the process of recording and processing sound, both for film and for games or virtual reality', and students work on real productions — fiction, documentary and animation — collaborating across departments to build professional portfolios. 13 specialised instructors.
programs.portfolioSpec: Dossier must contain: a CV in EuroPass format; and a portfolio of 'lucrări artistice cu design sonor realizat de către candidat' (artistic works with sound design created by the candidate), which may include digital copies of films or relevant sound-design projects. In addition, the candidate must BRING TO THE ORAL EXAM the DAW PROJECT FILE for one portfolio work of their own choosing. No minimum/maximum number of works and no duration requirement is published.
programs.auditionSpec: On-site, single evaluation stage in two parts. Proba 1 (written): 'probă de cultură cinematografică' — a film-culture exam based on a set bibliography, plus technical knowledge of sound design. Proba 2 (oral): presentation and discussion of one self-selected portfolio work, with a live DAW project demonstration. Minimum passing grade 6.0/10.
programs.entryRequirements: Completion of 'o specializare cu 180 credite sau 240 credite'. Foreign applicants must demonstrate Romanian at B1 minimum or complete a preparatory year (exemptions only for those with Romanian-medium credentials or a B1+ certificate from an accredited Romanian institution). Registration exclusively via the 2BitsEDU online platform, with portfolios uploaded electronically to a secure candidate folder. Places: 3 state-funded (bugetate) + 3 tuition-based per the admissions page; the department page states 5 places — confirm the 2027 figure.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES. The published eligibility is simply having 'absolvit o specializare cu 180 credite sau 240 credite' — no field of study is specified. UNATC's parallel non-EU English-programme page also lists Computer Science among relevant prior fields for its film-faculty masters, reinforcing that engineering backgrounds are contemplated.
programs.deadline: CURRENT CYCLE (Sept 2026 entry), NOT 2027 — confirm the 2027 dates when published. 2026 cycle: registration 4 August – 9 September 2026; file verification 10–11 September 2026; exam period 15–20 September 2026. For a September 2027 start expect the same August–September 2027 pattern.
programs.applicationOpens: CURRENT CYCLE: 4 August 2026 (a separate May–July pre-registration window applies to the English-taught masters). 2027 window not yet published.
programs.scholarship: Romanian Government scholarships offered through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAE), open specifically to non-EU citizens — Tunisia qualifies. Covers almost all academic fields except Medicine, Dental Medicine and Pharmacy. Requires an average of at least 7/10 (or 'Good') from the last school graduated.
programs.fundingLevel: Full (if the Romanian Government / MAE scholarship is awarded); plus 3 domestic tuition-free 'buget' places at programme level
programs.stipend: Romanian Government MAE scholarship: no tuition or registration fees, a monthly stipend, university accommodation where space allows, and a FREE preparatory year of Romanian language for non-speakers — which conveniently solves the B1 Romanian entry condition.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED. UNATC publishes 'TAXE DE ȘCOLARIZARE 2026-2027' as a Senate-approved PDF but the figures were not retrievable; contact secretariat@unatc.ro or study@unatc.ro.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED in detail. Curriculum implies Foley stage and multichannel mixing facilities; students work on live fiction, documentary and animation productions alongside directing, cinematography and editing departments. 13 specialised teaching staff.
programs.fitNotes: The best fully-funded route in the slice for someone with no music degree: eligibility is purely credit-based, the government scholarship covers everything including a free Romanian language year, and the DAW-project oral exam rewards practical production skill over conservatory training. The catch is direction of travel — this is film/game sound and Foley, not club music production, so it serves the sound-design half of his ambition rather than the DJ half. He also needs a portfolio with sound design applied to picture, which he does not yet have.

programs.program: Muzička produkcija (Music Production) — master academic studies (MAS)
programs.university: Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad (Akademija umetnosti, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu)
programs.institutionType: Public art academy within a public university
programs.degree: Master academic studies; professional title 'Мастер музички продуцент' (Master music producer)
programs.focus: Music Production; Electronic Music; Film/Media music production
programs.language: Serbian
programs.durationEcts: 1 year / 60 ECTS (2023 accreditation)
programs.whatYouStudy: Core: Музичка продукција (Music Production, 2+2); Звук и музика на филму (Sound and Music in Film, 2+1); Савремене тенденције у музичкој продукцији 1 and 2 (Contemporary Trends in Music Production); Музика-догађај-публика (Music–Event–Audience); Мастер рад - истраживање (master thesis research) and Мастер рад (master thesis). Electives (choose 12 ECTS): Драматургија савременог филма; Методе у музичком образовању у дигиталном окружењу; Историја електроакустичке музике (History of Electroacoustic Music); Историја популарне музике (History of Popular Music); Продукција музике за нове медије (Production of Music for New Media); Музика у медијима (Music in Media).
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED for the master level — the annual Konkurs PDF listing entrance-exam content, quotas and fees could not be retrieved. The sister programme Snimanje i dizajn zvuka at the same academy is documented at 5 places. Request the current Konkurs text from the academy before applying.
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED — an entrance aptitude check is standard for Serbian art academies, but the specific content for this programme was not confirmed on a page actually read.
programs.entryRequirements: UNVERIFIED in detail. Serbian master academic studies of 60 ECTS normally require a completed 240-ECTS undergraduate degree. Confirm via the academy's Konkurs.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED — no published statement found either way. Given the curriculum's heavy production/media orientation (rather than performance), it is worth asking directly, but assume an artistic or music-related prior degree may be expected.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The academy publishes an annual 'Konkurs za upis na master, specijalističke i doktorske akademske studije'; the most recent retrievable full text was the 2022/23 edition. Serbian master admissions typically run in September–October.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
programs.scholarship: None found. Serbia offers budget-financed places but these overwhelmingly go to domestic candidates.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED for this academy. (For comparison, FDU Belgrade charges non-neighbouring foreigners double the domestic self-financing rate.)
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED. The academy has run a Sound Recording and Sound Design programme since 2003 within its Department of Audio-visual Media, and also runs a four-year undergraduate Music Production and Sound Design degree, so studio infrastructure exists.
programs.fitNotes: Curriculum-wise this is the closest match in the whole slice to what he actually wants — a one-year master literally called Music Production, with electives in electroacoustic music history, popular music history and music production for new media. The problems are informational and practical: entrance requirements, fees and portfolio spec are all unpublished online, teaching is in Serbian, and no funding route was found. Worth a direct e-mail enquiry rather than dismissal.

programs.program: Ses Teknolojileri / Ses Teknolojisi (Sound Technology) — yüksek lisans (thesis and non-thesis)
programs.university: Bahçeşehir University (BAU) — Graduate School (launched under the Graduate School of Natural and Applied Sciences)
programs.city: Istanbul (classes in the Galata campus studios)
programs.institutionType: Private (foundation) university
programs.degree: Yüksek lisans (master's) — both tezli (thesis) and tezsiz (non-thesis) variants exist
programs.focus: Music Production; Recording / Engineering; Film sound; Electronic Music
programs.language: Turkish
programs.durationEcts: Non-thesis variant (verified on BAU's ECTS information package): 90 ECTS over 3 semesters, 10 courses plus a project course. A thesis variant of roughly 2 years also exists — its exact credit load is UNVERIFIED (a third-party listing quotes 120 credits / 2 years).
programs.whatYouStudy: Stated objective: 'Recording, mixing, mastering and production for the music industry, sound technique (acoustic, sound signing, sound information access), sound design for media (sound recording and production for cinema and TV).' Compulsory courses include Studio Recording Techniques, Multi-channel Mixing, Mastering and Film Sound Production; electives include Electronic Music, Musical Acoustics and Live Sound Equipment. The programme has 'a flexible structure ... comprised of mostly elective courses and projects', letting students take electives from the engineering and communication faculties. Classes are held in the Galata campus studios in the evenings or at weekends. A jazz performance/composition module is also reported (UNVERIFIED source).
programs.portfolioSpec: None published. Admission documentation lists only a bachelor's diploma, language proof where the programme is foreign-language (not applicable here, as it is Turkish-medium), and 'diğer ölçütler' (other criteria) determined by the Institute Management Board and Senate. No portfolio, no audition is specified — confirm with the coordinator whether an interview or work sample is used in practice.
programs.auditionSpec: None published. Selection criteria beyond the diploma are set case-by-case by the Institute Board — UNVERIFIED whether an interview is held.
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree or equivalent diploma, plus criteria set by the Institute Management Board and Senate. Turkish nationals normally require ALES; the requirement for international applicants is UNVERIFIED. Programme coordinator: Prof. Dr. Yahya Burak Tamer (burak.tamer@bau.edu.tr).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: LIKELY YES. No field restriction is published — the entry condition is simply a bachelor's or equivalent diploma — and the programme is deliberately built to draw electives from engineering and communication faculties, implying a technical intake is expected. No explicit wording on non-music bachelors was found, so confirm.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The programme launch announcement gave an application close of 3 September (year not stated on the page). BAU runs multiple graduate intakes per year. 2027 dates unpublished.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
programs.scholarship: None found. Türkiye Bursları does NOT list BAU among its Arts Scholarship universities (only Ankara Music and Fine Arts University, Ankara Hacı Bayram Veli University and İTÜ), so the YTB arts route does not apply here.
programs.fundingLevel: None found — treat as SELF-PAY FALLBACK
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — BAU publishes a 2026–2027 graduate fee table but it is rendered dynamically and returned no rows; request the Ses Teknolojileri figure from the Graduate School.
programs.facilities: Galata campus studios (evening/weekend teaching). BAU also runs a separate Music Technology undergraduate stream and the BAU IDEA audio/sound-design academy. Detailed studio inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Content is exactly right — music-industry recording, mixing, mastering, electronic music, film sound — and evening/weekend scheduling in Istanbul would suit someone gigging as a DJ. The two hard limits are that it is taught in Turkish and that it is a private university with no funding path found, so it belongs on the self-pay fallback list unless he first does a Turkish language year.

programs.program: Diplomski studij Montaža — usmjerenje Oblikovanje zvuka (MA Editing — Sound Design specialization)
programs.university: Academy of Dramatic Art (Akademija dramske umjetnosti, ADU), University of Zagreb
programs.institutionType: Public film/theatre academy within a public university
programs.focus: Film & Game Sound; Sound Design; theatre, radio and performing-arts sound
programs.language: Croatian — 'Prijamni ispiti, kao i nastava na ADU održavaju se na hrvatskom jeziku'
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS
programs.whatYouStudy: Though formally a module of the Montaža (Editing) master, it is 'largely conceived as an independent program'. It aims to educate creative and professional practitioners who acquire sound knowledge and skills through artistic, theoretical and professional subjects, for film and television as well as for other performing, broadcast and stage arts. Courses dealing with film sound are tied to practical work, individual and team-based: sound-design students realise film, television, radio and stage works produced by ADU's other departments and collaborate with other University of Zagreb faculties. Teaching staff are working sound recordists, sound editors, music editors, re-recording mixers and sound designers. Graduates work across film, television, theatre, radio, performing arts, multimedia projects and video games.
programs.portfolioSpec: EXACT, from the official 2026/27 entrance-exam document. Stage (A) submission, all eliminatory: (1) životopis (CV); (2) motivacijsko pismo — motivation letter, up to 2 'kartice' of text (~3,600 characters); (3) an audiovisual work for which the candidate conceived the sound picture or participated in creating it; (4) a written analysis of that submitted audiovisual work explaining the sound-picture concept AND listing the origin of the noises, music, sound effects and computer programs used in sound post-production. Positive evaluation of BOTH the audiovisual work and the written analysis is a precondition for reaching stage (B). (An older ADU booklet additionally specified DVD-video format in at least 3 copies and three copies of the analysis — check the current submission format.)
programs.auditionSpec: Yes — on-site, three-part, out of 100 points, with a hard 80/100 pass threshold. (1) klauzurni rad (supervised in-house practical exam) up to 20 points; (2) izlaganje koncepta zvučne slike za zadani predložak — presentation of a sound-picture concept for a given template/brief, up to 30 points; (3) razgovor s povjerenstvom (interview) up to 50 points. The commission assesses knowledge of film history, film-music history and music history, and recognition of musical forms, styles and genres. Recommended reading includes Sonnenschein, 'Sound Design: The Expressive Power of Music, Voice and Sound Effects in Cinema', and Weis & Belton, 'Film Sound'.
programs.entryRequirements: For Montaža the published prerequisite is a 'trogodišnji sveučilišni ili stručni prijediplomski studij, 180 ECTS bodova' — a three-year university OR professional undergraduate degree of 180 ECTS. Croatian-language competence is expected in speech and writing; ADU requires no certificate but 'Povjerenstva Prijamnih ispita imaju pravo eliminirati kandidata ... ako ocjene da kandidat ne poznaje hrvatski jezik u mjeri koja je potrebna za uspješno studiranje'. Non-EU nationals compete in a separate foreign-nationals quota with its own priority list.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES on paper. The prerequisite is stated purely as a 180-ECTS undergraduate degree, university or professional, with no field named — so a BSc in Software Engineering meets the formal condition. The direct-admission ('izravni upis') shortcut is reserved for ADU's own Montaža undergraduates, so an external applicant simply takes the full entrance exam. The genuine filter is the exam's assumed knowledge of film and music history, not the bachelor subject.
programs.deadline: 2026/27 CYCLE (Sept 2026 entry), NOT 2027 — confirm 2027 dates. Montaža: application and submission of works 1–4 September 2026; list of candidates admitted to stage (B) published 11 September 2026; Oblikovanje zvuka entrance exam 14 September 2026 (ADU, Trg RH 5, room 016 09:00–11:00, room 104 11:00–17:00, then Trg RH 8). NOTE: for the Snimanje department ADU ran a SEPARATE EARLIER WINDOW FOR FOREIGN NATIONALS (23–25 June 2026, exam 1 July 2026) — check whether an equivalent early foreign-national window applies to Montaža in 2027.
programs.applicationOpens: 2026/27 cycle opened 1 September 2026 for Montaža. Foreign nationals should check for an earlier June window. 2027/28 dates not yet published.
programs.scholarship: None found for non-EU applicants. Croatian diaspora and national-minority candidates get co-financing on equal terms with Croatian citizens — not applicable here.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial for EU/Croatian students (first year of a first study at this level is fully exempt); UNVERIFIED for non-EU
programs.tuitionIntl: For Croatian and EU citizens full participation is €1,278.00 per year, with one ECTS valued at €21.30, and the first year of a student's first study at a given level is fully exempt. For non-EU citizens: participation is set 'prema odlukama nadređenih tijela (Ministarstvo znanosti i obrazovanja, Sveučilište u Zagrebu)' — the actual non-EU amount is UNVERIFIED. Payable in two instalments (start of winter and summer semesters).
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED in inventory terms, but the programme is built on live production: students do the sound for ADU's directing, cinematography and editing productions plus radio and stage work, across three ADU buildings (Trg Republike Hrvatske 5 and 8, Frankopanska 22). Quota for 2026/27: maximum 4 Croatian citizens + maximum 1 foreign student on the Oblikovanje zvuka module.
programs.fitNotes: Formally open to him — a 180-ECTS engineering degree satisfies the entry level — and the entrance exam is transparent and well documented, which is rare. But it is an extremely narrow gate (one foreign place), it is taught and examined entirely in Croatian, and the submission requires an audiovisual work whose sound he designed, which he does not yet have. Realistic only after a year of building a picture-based sound portfolio and learning Croatian.

programs.program: Master akademske studije Dramske i audiovizuelne umetnosti — modul Snimanje i dizajn zvuka (Sound Recording and Design)
programs.university: Faculty of Dramatic Arts (Fakultet dramskih umetnosti, FDU), University of Arts in Belgrade
programs.institutionType: Public film/drama faculty within the University of Arts
programs.focus: Recording / Engineering; Film & Game Sound; Sound Design; radio and theatre sound
programs.language: Serbian
programs.durationEcts: 1 academic year / 2 semesters. Entry requires a completed undergraduate degree of at least 240 ECTS, so the master is 60 ECTS (total ECTS figure not stated explicitly on the pages read).
programs.whatYouStudy: Core courses: 'Sound Recording and Design for FTV 7 and 8', in which 'students perfect their knowledge in the field of sound recording and post-production for the most complex film and television structures'; and 'Sound Recording and Design for Theater and Radio 7 and 8', covering 'highly esthetic forms of radio creativity such as musique concrète' and stage sound design. Additional artistic courses in classical and popular music recording, plus sound design in multimedia, and elective theoretical and artistic courses. The department has 9 full professors plus associate professors; 8 of its 11 teachers are graduates of the department itself.
programs.portfolioSpec: EXACT: 'portfolio — pregled do tri reprezentativna samostalna autorska rada u minimalnom ukupnom trajanju od 10 minuta' — a portfolio reviewing UP TO THREE representative independent authored works with a MINIMUM TOTAL DURATION OF 10 MINUTES, drawn from domains including film sound design, television/streaming audio, radio production, live event sound design, creative music production, or video game / interactive audio design. Submitted with detailed PDF documentation. Also required: a motivation letter of maximum two A4 pages, 1.5 line spacing, font size 12, in Latin or Cyrillic script; a professional biography; a certified copy of the undergraduate diploma with average grade; proof of the 8,000 RSD application fee; and a health certificate INCLUDING AN AUDIOGRAM not older than three months.
programs.auditionSpec: Yes — on-site entrance exam in three parts: presentation of the candidate's individual authored work in sound design; completion of a practical work during the exam itself; and an interview assessing artistic potential. Scoring out of 100: up to 30 points from prior undergraduate success (average grade × 3) plus up to 70 points for aptitude. Budget-financed admission requires ≥80 points; self-financed requires ≥60 points.
programs.entryRequirements: Completed undergraduate academic studies with at least 240 ECTS. Serbian-language instruction. Total intake across the 9 specializations of the Dramske i audiovizuelne umetnosti master is up to 92 students (57 budget-financed and 58 self-financed places faculty-wide).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: PROBABLY NOT — this is the key caution. The department page states: 'A precondition for enrolling M.A. Studies are previously completed undergraduate ARTISTIC academic studies.' Combined with the 240-ECTS floor, a three-year non-artistic BSc in Software Engineering appears to fail on two counts. Verify directly with the faculty before investing effort.
programs.deadline: 2026/27 CYCLE, NOT 2027 — confirm new date. Registration of candidates 7 and 8 October 2026, 09:00–14:00, at the Faculty Secretariat; entrance examinations 12–13 October 2026. Expect an equivalent early-October 2027 window for a 2027/28 start.
programs.applicationOpens: 2026/27 cycle: 7 October 2026. 2027/28 dates not yet published.
programs.scholarship: None found for foreign nationals. Budget-financed (tuition-free) places exist but require ≥80/100 and in practice go to domestic candidates.
programs.fundingLevel: None found for a non-EU foreign applicant (budget places are effectively domestic)
programs.tuitionIntl: 2026/27 self-financing rates for Snimanje i dizajn zvuka: 440,000 RSD for Serbian citizens; 550,000 RSD for foreign students from neighbouring countries; 660,000 RSD for other foreign students (roughly €5,600). Application fee 8,000 RSD.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — no studio inventory published on the pages read. Strong regional reputation as the main Serbian film-sound school; teaching staff are almost entirely its own alumni working in the industry.
programs.fitNotes: Technically excellent and genuinely craft-focused, and the portfolio spec is unusually generous in scope — 'creative music production' and 'video game / interactive audio design' are explicitly listed as acceptable domains, so his own tracks could count toward the 10-minute minimum. The blocker is eligibility: the stated precondition of completed undergraduate ARTISTIC studies plus a 240-ECTS floor likely rules out his 180-ECTS engineering BSc. Confirm before anything else; if refused, Novi Sad is the fallback.

However, there is an option for those who do not have a degree, taking into account real-world work experience in related fields, and non-degree professional development courses." No music degree is required — a BSc Software Engineering is more than sufficient on paper.
programs.portfolioSpec: Applicants should provide "examples of audio manipulation in some form. Ideally, these would be examples of sound design replacements you have done to video games or film clips." Acceptable alternatives explicitly listed: audio editing, mixing/mastering, field recording, foley, and practical sound design. No fixed number of works or duration is stated.
programs.auditionSpec: No live audition and no on-site test. An optional (but recommended) one-to-one consultation with a course advisor is offered before applying.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. At time of reading the page was "accepting applications for September 14th start" (2026 cohort). Applications for a Sept 2027 start would normally open in the preceding academic year — confirm from ~Oct 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Only a September 14 start date was published; no hard deadline stated (rolling admission model).
programs.whatYouStudy: Seven-part structure: (1) Foundations of Game Audio; (2) Game Audio Technologies; (3) Research and Critical Reflection; (4) Interactive Audio; (5) 3D Audio Environments; (6) an elective chosen from FMOD, Unreal & Blueprint, Musical Sound Design, Audio Post-Production or Career Development; (7) Final Major Project / Dissertation. Tooling taught: Wwise, FMOD, Unity and Unreal Engine — i.e. exactly the middleware+engine stack that a software engineer can absorb fastest.
programs.facilities: No physical studios — fully online delivery, students work in their own setup. The real asset is teaching staff: 15+ practising professionals contribute, drawn from Electronic Arts, Blizzard, Bandai, Nintendo, Capcom, Frontier Developments and Dambusters Studios.
programs.fitNotes: Strongest pure game-audio fit found for this exact profile: any-degree entry, a portfolio brief he can build in a few months (redesign the sound of game/film clips), and a curriculum built on Wwise/FMOD/Unity/Unreal where his programming background is a direct advantage. Main obstacle: zero funding and £13,500 self-pay, plus it is online — no relocation to Europe, no student visa, no European club/label network, which matters a lot if the real goal is DJing and producing.

programs.program: Master of Music — Music Design
programs.university: HKU University of the Arts Utrecht (Hogeschool voor de Kunsten Utrecht), Utrecht Conservatoire / School of Music and Technology
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS
programs.focus: Music Production + Sound Design + Electronic Music, with an explicit games and interactive-installation strand
programs.institutionType: Conservatory / art school (university of the arts)
programs.language: English and Dutch (both used — confirm the practical balance with the department)
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED. The page does not publish a non-EU figure and directs applicants to HKU's "Collegegeldwizard" fee calculator. Dutch art-school institutional (non-EEA) master fees are typically far above the statutory EEA rate — get a written quote before committing.
programs.scholarship: Holland Scholarship — named on the page as available to talented international candidates, awarded competitively and independently of when the application is submitted. This is a Dutch government/institution scheme open to non-EEA students.
programs.stipend: UNVERIFIED. The Holland Scholarship is normally a one-off first-year contribution (commonly around €5,000) rather than a full waiver or a monthly stipend — confirm the amount with HKU.
programs.entryRequirements: Normally a bachelor's degree in a related field. Application dossier: motivation letter (motivatiebrief), study plan (studieplan), CV and portfolio. English/Dutch language evidence requirement UNVERIFIED on the page read.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — possible but demanding. The FAQ states: "It is possible to apply without a bachelor of music... The academy can make an exception for candidates without a Bachelor of Music, but only in case of exceptional talent and a steady track record." So a software-engineering BSc is not a bar in principle, but he would be admitted on the strength of demonstrated musical output, not the degree. The "steady track record" phrase is the hard part for someone with no professional audio history yet.
programs.portfolioSpec: A portfolio is required alongside a motivation letter, study plan and CV. The programme explicitly de-emphasises tooling: what matters is the creative musical work achieved with whatever technology the candidate has access to, plus the ability to explain the technical choices behind it. No minimum number of works, duration or file format is published — build the strongest possible self-directed body of work and be ready to justify every production decision.
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED whether a live audition is held. Selection is dossier- and portfolio-driven; an interview/selection conversation is standard at Dutch conservatoires but was not stated on the page read.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 October 2026 — the page states the 2026-2027 intake is closed and that applications for 2027-2028 OPEN 1 OCTOBER. This directly matches his September 2027 target intake and is the single most actionable date found in this slice.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new dates. The published 2026-2027 selection rounds were 24 November, 12 January, 16 February and 13 April. Expect a comparable four-round structure for 2027-2028 once the 1 October 2026 opening goes live — the earliest round (late November 2026) is the one to aim for.
programs.whatYouStudy: A single master with four non-binding strands the student combines: Music Technology; Music Production (covering live, recorded, media, GAMES and interactive installations); Sound Design (film, theatre, GAMES); and Composition. Because the strands are non-binding he can weight the degree toward club/electronic production while taking the games and interactive-installation work — which is where his coding matters. Detailed module list UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED on the page read. HKU's School of Music and Technology also runs bachelor programmes in Audio Design, Sound Design, Music Design for Games and Interaction, Composition and Music Production, and Composition Electronic Music — so the master sits on top of an unusually deep, dedicated music-technology faculty and its studio infrastructure.
programs.fitNotes: The best fit in this slice for someone whose real ambition is producing and DJing rather than only game audio: it is a conservatory-level Master of Music that explicitly covers games AND music production AND electronic composition, in the Netherlands, with applications opening exactly on his timeline (1 Oct 2026). Two obstacles: entry without a music bachelor requires "exceptional talent and a steady track record", which he does not yet have on paper, so the next twelve months must produce real released work; and non-EEA tuition is unpublished and likely high, with the Holland Scholarship covering only part.

Two cautions: it is a self-directed practice-as-research MA, so it assumes you already have a practice and can write about it (an academic writing sample is required), and it will not teach mixing from zero. programs.facilities: The Music Production specialism is "powered by Metropolis Studios, one of the world's leading music studios" — the strongest single studio association in this slice. ACM also cites Brixton House as "the UK's most advanced music learning space", and industry ties to Kane FM, Roland and Laney. Dr Gary Bromham is listed as Senior Lecturer in Production at Guildford and Metropolis Studios. Alumni cited include Ed Sheeran and Newton Faulkner.
programs.whatYouStudy: Four level-7 modules: CIF-701 Professional Practice Frameworks (60cr, benchmark and upskill your applied technical and craft competencies against an external framework); CIF-703 Ideas Into Action (30cr, rapid prototyping and pitching); CIF-702 Creative Applied Research (60cr, across two terms — this is where you choose the MA or MSc pathway); CIF-704 Making Connections and Building a Community (30cr, stakeholder and network building). The Music Production specialism is explicitly NOT beginner training: "The course is not about relearning technical fundamentals... aimed at practitioners who already have a grounding in production."
programs.fitNotes: The Metropolis Studios link is genuinely valuable and the entry routes are flexible. But read the warning on the page carefully: this programme states it is for producers who ALREADY have a grounding and are consolidating toward senior roles — it is not where you learn to produce. Combined with £17,200 payable in full before the visa is issued and no verified scholarship for non-EU students, this is a self-pay option that only makes sense if his portfolio is already strong. Also note international students are restricted to the London campus.

programs.entryRequirements: "The candidate should have a bachelor's diploma relevant for the professional field of Sonology (composition of electronic and/or acoustic music ..., sound synthesis research, sound art, related subjects such as artificial intelligence, computer science or electronic engineering, musicology, music perception, film studies, or as a performing musician)." Studies are in English and "applicants are expected to be adequately fluent with the language".
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. Computer science and electronic engineering are named as relevant bachelor backgrounds. This is one of the very few sound masters in Europe that names a CS degree as acceptable, which makes it the single best structural fit for his BSc.
programs.portfolioSpec: "a portfolio with previous compositions, sound installations, recordings of live performances or research results in the form of computer programs, articles, theses, etc." No fixed number of works, no duration limit and no format specified. Plus a two-page study plan containing: a short project description; a four-semester timeline with related coursework; a detailed description with research question, context and intended presentation form; and the thesis subject.
programs.auditionSpec: None — "There is no live admission exam." Selection is on portfolio + study plan (with contact/interview at the institute's discretion).
programs.deadline: 26 February 2026 (2026 intake) — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for Sept 2027
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
programs.tuitionIntl: €11,488 per year institutional fee for non-EEA students, 2026/2027 (Royal Conservatoire tuition page). EEA statutory fee €2,694. Payment can be split into 8 instalments for a €24 admin fee.
programs.scholarship: None found on the conservatoire's tuition page for non-EEA master's applicants.
programs.facilities: Institute of Sonology — one of the oldest electronic-music studios in the world (founded Utrecht 1960, moved to The Hague 1986): analogue and digital studios, a large multichannel/spatialisation studio, historic voltage-controlled systems alongside current computer-music tooling. Exact current inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Best structural fit in this slice: a CS bachelor is explicitly welcome, there is no live audition, and the portfolio spec is deliberately open — code, installations and tracks all count. The catch is honesty about what it is: Sonology is experimental/artistic-research electronic music, not club-music production. It will make him a far better sound designer and electronic musician, not directly a better DJ. €11,488/yr and no scholarship is the other obstacle.

Year 2 at the Institute of Sonology in The Hague: an individual artistic research project in composition, live electronics, sound art or field recording. Genuinely bridges engineering and artistic practice.

programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — and it is arguably designed for exactly his background. TU Berlin's parent M.Sc. Audiokommunikation und -technologie admits holders of first degrees in natural sciences, engineering, humanities, social sciences, artistic-academic, business or law fields, and additionally requires ~10 credits of higher mathematics (analysis, linear algebra) and knowledge of a programming language — requirements a software-engineering BSc normally satisfies.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED on the joint programme page. Year-2 placement runs through the Institute of Sonology, whose master admission uses an open portfolio (compositions, installations, performance recordings, computer programs, articles) plus a two-page study plan — confirm whether the joint track requires the same.
programs.auditionSpec: No live audition stated. Selection is document- and portfolio-based (Sonology explicitly has "no live admission exam").

programs.fitNotes: On paper the strongest match in Europe for a software engineer who wants spatial audio: the maths and programming prerequisites are things he already has, and the facilities (832-channel WFS) are unmatched. Two real obstacles: German TestDaF TDN 4 is a serious extra year of language work, and the content is technical/artistic-research, not club production. Not a DJ master.

The only real barrier is £32.9k — which is exactly the gap Chevening is designed to close, and Chevening is a strong fit for a Tunisian applicant. Prepare IELTS 6.5 and a Chevening application in parallel.

Be honest about the trade-off: it is a private school charging ~€12.6k with almost no funding, and it is artistic research, not a beat-making bootcamp — he must arrive with a project he genuinely wants to investigate.
