programs.entryRequirements: "Music production, technology, and innovation applicants should possess a bachelor's degree in music while demonstrating technological proficiency, musical excellence in performance and/or composition, leadership, motivation, intellectual curiosity, and promise of great achievement in their area of study." $150 non-refundable application fee. English test requirement not stated on the entrance-requirements page (UNVERIFIED).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, conditionally — quoted: "Bachelor's degrees in other disciplines will be considered, provided the student demonstrates a high degree of musicianship." His BSc Software Engineering is admissible in principle; the burden falls entirely on demonstrated musicianship.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not published in detail on the entrance-requirements or auditions pages (UNVERIFIED) — a completed online graduate application "with supporting materials" is required. Confirm the exact prescreening material list with admissionsvalencia@berklee.edu; this is the one field worth an email.
programs.auditionSpec: INTERVIEW ONLY, no audition: "All other master's degree applicants selected to move on to this stage are required to do an interview only" (only Contemporary Performance – Production Concentration requires an audition as well). Interviews run mid-November to early December for Early Action and late January to early March for Regular Action.
programs.deadline: Early Action and Regular Action rounds exist (interviews mid-Nov–early Dec and late Jan–early Mar respectively) but the specific dates are on a separate page not read — UNVERIFIED / PRIOR CYCLE - confirm for Sept 2027 entry
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
programs.tuitionIntl: €50,430 tuition plus €1,600 comprehensive fee = €52,030 total for the 2026/2027 academic year, plus a required software bundle of €200-€850. This is the most expensive option in this list by a wide margin.
programs.scholarship: Berklee General Scholarship: all master's applicants are eligible, amount varies by merit (typical award size UNVERIFIED). Berklee Outstanding Women Scholarship and Mentorship covers up to 70% of tuition but is awarded to one woman, so not applicable to him.
programs.stipend: None — scholarships are tuition reductions only.
programs.facilities: Purpose-built campus in the Palau de les Arts, Valencia: state-of-the-art recording studios, Dolby Atmos mixing, multi-channel audio production, technology labs with Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools and Adobe Premiere. Berklee's global alumni and industry network is the real asset. Stated career outcomes include "artists, technologists, producers, DJs, electronic composers, educators, and software/hardware designers".
programs.fitNotes: Of everything in this slice, this is the closest thing in Europe to a master built to make you a working producer/DJ — DJing is a named elective, electronic production and performance is a core course, and it explicitly considers non-music bachelors. His CS background is an advantage for the Max/MSP and instrument-design work. The blocker is money: €52k for one year with only variable merit scholarships. Label it clearly as the self-pay fallback, not a funded route.

programs.program: Master's Programme Computer Music and Sound Art (Computermusik und Klangkunst)
programs.university: University of Music and Performing Arts Graz (Kunstuniversität Graz, KUG) — Institute of Electronic Music and Acoustics (IEM)
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS
programs.language: German or English (the entrance exam is conducted in either); German proficiency is separately required
programs.institutionType: Public university of music and performing arts
programs.focus: Electronic Music/Live Electronics; Immersive/Spatial Audio; Sonic Arts; Electroacoustic Composition
programs.whatYouStudy: Curriculum covers algorithms in acoustics and computer music, algorithmic composition, performance practice and sound diffusion (Klangregie), recording technique, sound reinforcement, computer music systems, electroacoustic composition, installation art, instrumental music with live electronics, real-time sound synthesis, art and new media, musical acoustics, room acoustics, sound design and studio equipment. Focus areas: computer-music composition, electronic-music performance, instrument development and music informatics. Winter-semester start only.
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree, with "equivalency of preliminary studies" confirmed by the Dean of Studies; external applicants submit official diploma certificates and transcripts. German proficiency required per separate documentation.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — the page does not state a position either way (UNVERIFIED), routing it through a case-by-case equivalency decision by the Dean of Studies. IEM's own research culture is heavily engineering- and software-based, so a software-engineering BSc is a plausible equivalency case, but it is not published as accepted.
programs.portfolioSpec: "two examples of your artistic work, each with a duration of approximately 5 minutes", uploaded as audio or video documentation before the deadline. This is one of the smallest and most precisely defined portfolio asks in this list.
programs.auditionSpec: No performance audition. The examination is an oral interview conducted via ZOOM in German or English, in which candidates explain their motivation and discuss the submitted works — so no travel to Graz required.
programs.deadline: "1st March until 1st Mai via KUGonline" (annual application window for a winter-semester start). For September/October 2027 entry expect 1 March – 1 May 2027 — confirm once published.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 March (annual window opening, per the published window) — confirm for 2027
programs.tuitionIntl: Not stated on the page (UNVERIFIED). Austrian public universities generally charge non-EU/EEA students a tuition fee (commonly around €726.72 per semester) plus the ÖH student-union fee — CONFIRM with KUG, do not rely on this figure.
programs.fundingLevel: UNVERIFIED (Austrian public tuition is low, so effectively low-fee rather than funded)
programs.scholarship: None found on the programme page
programs.facilities: IEM Graz is one of the world's leading centres for ambisonics and spatial audio — it develops and maintains the widely used IEM Plug-in Suite and operates ambisonic installations for recording and reproducing a full spatial sound field, plus the CUBE multichannel performance space. If he wants ambisonics expertise, this is a top-3 institution in Europe.
programs.fitNotes: Excellent value-for-content: an ambisonics powerhouse, a tiny 2×5-minute portfolio requirement, a Zoom-only interview and low Austrian public fees. Two frictions: German proficiency is required even though the exam can be in English, and the artistic register is computer music and sound art, not club music. Best European choice if his goal shifts toward spatial-audio craft; a poor choice if he only wants to DJ better.

programs.program: Master Sound Design (joint inter-university programme)

B2 language proficiency (CEFR).

Not named verbatim, so: Check.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not published in detail on the page (UNVERIFIED). What is stated: applicants "must pass an entrance examination" assessing qualifications relevant to programme success and future career prospects. Request the current portfolio specification from idk@fh-joanneum.at.
programs.auditionSpec: Entrance examination required; format (on-site vs remote) UNVERIFIED. No performance audition mentioned.
programs.deadline: The official page lists four 2027 application rounds with the day still to be filled in — "xx.02.2027, xx.03.2027, xx.04.2027, xx.05.2027". So four rounds between February and May 2027 are confirmed in principle for the Sept 2027 intake, but the exact dates are NOT YET PUBLISHED — check back from late 2026.

programs.tuitionIntl: Not stated on the page (UNVERIFIED). Austrian universities of applied sciences typically charge €363.36/semester plus ÖH fee for EU students, with a separate non-EU rate — CONFIRM with FH JOANNEUM.

programs.facilities: Shared FH JOANNEUM design studios and KUG/IEM facilities, which include the IEM ambisonics infrastructure and the CUBE. Specific inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Notable because it is the one programme in this slice whose 2027 application rounds are already published in outline, and because its accepted-bachelor list is engineering/design-led rather than music-led — so a software-engineering BSc has a real path here. But be clear about content: this is product/interface/sonification sound design, not music production and not DJing. Recommend only if his interest genuinely extends to sound design for objects, screens and interfaces.

programs.program: Digital Media Production (MA) — Master Class "3D Audio & Sound Design"

programs.entryRequirements: UNVERIFIED — the official FH St. Pölten / USTP programme pages returned HTTP 503 to every fetch attempt during this research, so entry requirements could not be read first-hand. The programme sits in the Department of Media and Digital Technologies rather than a music faculty, and its sibling master classes are animation and film, so a technical/media bachelor is the norm rather than a music degree. A software-engineering BSc is plausibly relevant, but no published wording was read. Contact the department directly.

Second, the third-country application window closes very early (the 2026/27 one is already shut), so if this interests him he must be chasing the 2027/28 deadline from autumn 2026. Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships are the standard funded route for non-EU applicants to Swiss institutions and do cover arts universities — UNVERIFIED whether this specific major is eligible; worth checking with the Swiss embassy in Tunis.

programs.program: Master of Music in Music Recording (Tonmeister) / Music Directing (Musikregie)

The Erich Thienhaus Institut is the German Tonmeister tradition's flagship institute and internationally known for classical recording and, in recent years, immersive/3D music recording — although no immersive content is stated on the programme page itself (UNVERIFIED).

programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — unambiguously. The page requires "a Bachelor's degree in Music Recording respectively diploma in Tonmeister". A software-engineering BSc is not admissible. Listed here for completeness because Detmold is the reference institution for German Tonmeister training and immersive music recording — but it is closed to him at master level.

programs.applicationOpens: 15 February (winter-semester window opening) — confirm for 2027
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition fee is charged at German public music academies; only a semester contribution (Semesterbeitrag) applies — amount not stated on the page, UNVERIFIED. A €50 application processing fee via muvac.
programs.fundingLevel: Full in the sense of tuition-free public study, but no stipend found
programs.scholarship: None found on the programme page. DAAD is the normal funded route for Tunisian applicants to German music academies — UNVERIFIED for this programme.
programs.facilities: Erich Thienhaus Institut operates "professionally equipped studios with all the necessary equipment"; the institute is one of the most respected classical-recording training centres in the world with a strong reputation in high-resolution and immersive music recording (the latter not confirmed on the page read).
programs.fitNotes: Include-and-rule-out entry. Detmold is the gold standard for European music-recording training and tuition is free, but the master is a closed loop: it requires a Tonmeister/music-recording bachelor, is taught in German, and requires an on-site 30-minute aptitude test with three of your own productions. He is not eligible in 2027 and should not spend effort here. Useful only as a long-term aspiration if he later completes an audio bachelor.

Campus facility inventory UNVERIFIED.

But be blunt: SMC is audio research and software engineering for sound, not music production, and it will not make him a better DJ. It is the right choice only if he wants to build audio tools or plug-ins alongside producing. Also note that UPF's own site blocked verification, so every figure here needs confirming before he relies on it.

programs.program: Master's Programme Computer Music and Sound Art
programs.university: University of Music and Performing Arts Graz (KUG) — Institute of Electronic Music and Acoustics (IEM), Institute 17

programs.focus: Electronic Music/Live Electronics · Immersive/Spatial Audio · Sonic Arts · Electroacoustic composition with strong practical/technical emphasis
programs.whatYouStudy: Four named focus areas: computer music composition; performance and interpretation of electronic works; development of new electronic instruments; music informatics. IEM is the Austrian centre for Ambisonics and spatial audio research (the CUBE multichannel hall and Ambisonics loudspeaker arrays are IEM's signature facilities — detailed studio/software inventory UNVERIFIED on the official programme page).

Practically, the two 5-minute works carry the weight, not the diploma subject.

programs.stipend: UNVERIFIED — no stipend or living-cost support identified on the programme page.

programs.fitNotes: One of the cheapest serious European routes into computer music: ~€1.45k/year all-in tuition and no on-site audition. The catch is that the entry gate is two finished ~5-minute artistic works plus a Dean-of-Studies equivalency ruling on a software-engineering BSc — so he needs roughly a year of deliberate portfolio-building before the March 2027 window. Aesthetically it is art-music / spatial-audio / instrument-building, not club or dance production; it would give him extraordinary sound-design and Max/DSP depth but will not by itself teach him to finish a release-ready track.

Best treated as the technical-depth option: it would make him a formidable sound designer and Max/SuperCollider builder rather than a chart producer.

programs.facilities: ESMUC is located in the L'Auditori building in Barcelona and is described as a European leader in Jazz and Modern Music, Sonology (music technology) and Early Music, with Sonology taught at bachelor level. Specific studio/console inventory for this master UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Excellent value and excellent logistics: about €5,667 TOTAL, taught in ENGLISH (so no new language to learn — the only English-taught low-cost option here), evening-only timetable that leaves daytime free for studio work or a job, three application rounds including one as late as September, and a syllabus with Live Coding plus Programming and Interactive Systems that rewards his coding background directly. Two real caveats: it is a MASTER PROPIO, not an official Spanish master, which limits later PhD access and may complicate recognition and some scholarship eligibility; and at 60 ECTS in 9 months it is half the depth of the 120-ECTS options. Best treated as a fast, affordable, English-language conversion route into electroacoustic practice rather than a full conservatoire training.

programs.program: Mestrado em Artes e Tecnologias do Som (MATS — Master's in Arts and Sound Technologies)
programs.university: Escola Superior de Música e Artes do Espetáculo (ESMAE), Politécnico do Porto (P.PORTO)
programs.durationEcts: UNVERIFIED on the pages read (Portuguese mestrado is normally 2 years / 120 ECTS; a study-plan PDF exists but was not readable).
programs.language: UNVERIFIED — likely Portuguese, possibly with English accommodation. Must be confirmed; this is decisive.
programs.institutionType: Public polytechnic higher school of music and performing arts
programs.focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based) · Sound technologies · Electroacoustic and audiovisual composition · Recording/Engineering
programs.whatYouStudy: MATS "aims to promote singular authorial work and knowledge/practical competence, working in diverse epistemological fields, between classical and new devices, between art and technologies." Designed "for an audience with knowledge in music technologies, musical creation and performance, visual arts, acoustics, as well as other interdisciplinary areas with sound as an investigative object of interest." Detailed module list is in a study-plan PDF that was not readable — UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: Targeted at candidates with knowledge in music technologies, musical creation and performance, visual arts, ACOUSTICS, "as well as other interdisciplinary areas with sound as an investigative object of interest." ESMAE's companion Composition master states the general principle for the school: candidates should be "graduates in Composition or graduates FROM OTHER AREAS WHO HAVE A RELEVANT PORTFOLIO AND CURRICULUM in the application area." Language requirement UNVERIFIED.
programs.portfolioSpec: Three items: a PORTFOLIO, a PROJECT/DISSERTATION PROPOSAL, and an updated curriculum vitae. "Candidates must submit a Portfolio and Project/Dissertation Proposal, as well as an updated curriculum, which will be discussed by the jury in an interview." Number of works, durations and formats are NOT published — UNVERIFIED, request from ESMAE.
programs.auditionSpec: An INTERVIEW with a jury discussing the submitted portfolio, project proposal and CV. In the 2026/27 cycle the tests/interviews were scheduled for 11 and 12 May 2026. Whether attendance is on-site in Porto or remote is UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES in substance — ESMAE's master admission framework accepts "graduates from other areas who have a relevant portfolio and curriculum in the application area", and MATS itself names acoustics and "other interdisciplinary areas with sound as an investigative object of interest" among its target audiences. Sound-focused work by a software engineer fits that description. Confirm in writing, since the MATS page does not state it as bluntly as the Composition page does.
programs.applicationOpens: 5 January (2026/27 cycle)
programs.deadline: 5 January – 11 April 2026, with tests/interviews on 11 and 12 May 2026 (via the Politécnico do Porto application portal, per the Edital / Concurso de Acesso aos Cursos de Mestrado 2026/27) — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect an equivalent January–April 2027 window. Note this is a long, generous application window.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED on the pages read. Portuguese public polytechnic master fees are among the lowest in Western Europe (commonly roughly €1,000–€3,000 per year for nationals and EU students), but Portugal operates a separate INTERNATIONAL STUDENT STATUTE with higher fees for non-EU applicants — the ESMAE figure must be confirmed from the edital.
programs.scholarship: None found on the pages read — UNVERIFIED. Portuguese DGES social-action scholarships and Camões Institute awards are potential routes but applicability to a Tunisian applicant at ESMAE is unverified.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — no studio or console inventory published on the pages read. ESMAE also runs a Licenciatura in Música – variante de Produção e Tecnologias da Música, indicating an established production/technology teaching infrastructure.
programs.fitNotes: Genuinely promising and under-the-radar: a public Portuguese master built around authorial sound work, admitting graduates from other areas on portfolio and CV, with a jury interview rather than a musical audition, in a country with low public tuition and a long January–April application window. But it is the LEAST verified entry here — language of instruction, ECTS, fees and portfolio specification are all unpublished on the pages read, and language is the make-or-break unknown. Action: request the edital and the study plan directly from ESMAE, and ask explicitly whether the programme can be followed in English. If it can, this jumps up the shortlist; if it is Portuguese-only, treat it like the Italian options — a language investment decision, though Portuguese is comparatively accessible from his fluent French.

programs.program: Cursus — Programme on Composition and Computer Music
programs.university: IRCAM (Institut de Recherche et Coordination Acoustique/Musique), Centre Pompidou
programs.degree: NOT A DEGREE — a one-year postgraduate professional training programme at master level, delivered under contract between IRCAM and the participant. It confers no MA/MMus. Partner conservatoires (HEAR, CNSMD Lyon, CNSMD Paris) allow their own master's students to spend a master year inside the Cursus, which is how it is credentialed.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year, 850 hours. For 2026-2027: 12 October 2026 to 30 September 2027, Monday to Friday 10:00–13:00 and 14:30–17:30, with two weeks off in December. No ECTS award — UNVERIFIED whether any credit transfer is possible for non-partner students.
programs.language: ENGLISH
programs.institutionType: National research institute (public, associated with Centre Pompidou) — not a university or conservatoire
programs.focus: Live Electronics · Electroacoustic/computer-music composition · Spatialisation · Max/MSP and IRCAM software mastery
programs.whatYouStudy: Training aimed at "in-depth technical independence and mastery" of IRCAM-developed software used in composition: MAX, OpenMusic, Modalys, ASAP, Partiel and SPAT (spatialisation). The 850 hours comprise theory and technique classes, hands-on workshops, composition sessions, lectures by guest artists and scientists, individual follow-up meetings, rehearsals, and a FINAL CONCERT. The programme is "open to all forms of artistic practice, integrating technology into a wide range of aesthetic approaches and forms." The 2026-2027 edition, under Associate Composer Eva Reiter, emphasises technology serving musical thought, artificial-intelligence integration, and musicology.
programs.entryRequirements: AGE LIMIT: open to composers under the age of 37 (for 2026-2027, born after 1 January 1987). No prior degree requirement is published — UNVERIFIED. Selection is by jury. On acceptance a contract is signed between IRCAM and the participant, with a €600 deposit due by 29 April 2026 for the 2026-27 edition.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — the call material read does not specify the number of works, scores or recordings required. Given that selection is by jury and the cohort is composers, assume a substantial portfolio of compositions plus a project proposal, and request the exact specification from IRCAM before the December deadline.
programs.auditionSpec: Jury selection on the submitted dossier; no live audition published. Details UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED / UNLIKELY IN PRACTICE. No degree requirement is published, and the programme is described as "open to all forms of artistic practice" with only an age ceiling — so there is no formal diploma barrier. However the call addresses itself to "composers", selection is by jury against an international field, and the partner routes are through conservatoire master's programmes in composition. A software-engineering graduate with no compositional track record would be a very long shot in year one, though his programming ability is exactly what the Max/OpenMusic/Modalys curriculum assumes.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (autumn)
programs.deadline: 3 December 2025 for the 2026-2027 edition — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Because the Cursus runs October to September, a September-2027 start corresponds to the 2027-2028 edition, whose deadline should fall around DECEMBER 2026. Watch the IRCAM and Ulysses Platform pages from autumn 2026.
programs.tuitionIntl: €2,000 participation fee, with a €600 deposit due by the stated date after acceptance. Note that this buys 850 contact hours, which is exceptional value per hour — but Paris living costs for a year are the dominant expense.
programs.scholarship: None mentioned in the call material read — UNVERIFIED. The Ulysses Platform (a European network that circulates the call) sometimes supports mobility; applicability UNVERIFIED.
programs.stipend: UNVERIFIED — no grant or living-cost support identified. €2,000 fee plus a year of Paris living costs, self-funded.
programs.facilities: IRCAM is the pre-eminent computer-music research institute in the world, and the origin of Max/MSP, OpenMusic, Modalys, SPAT and AudioSculpt. Access to IRCAM's studios and the final-concert production apparatus. Guest artists and scientists lecture on the programme.
programs.fitNotes: Include for completeness and as a MEDIUM-TERM AMBITION rather than a 2027 application. The upsides are real: taught in ENGLISH, only €2,000 for 850 hours, no formal degree requirement published, and a curriculum (Max, OpenMusic, SPAT, Modalys) that rewards a programmer more than almost any other option here. The problems are that it is NOT A DEGREE — which matters for a student visa, for recognition, and for the task's own master's-level scope — and that the jury selects from international composers with substantial portfolios. Realistic path: do a master's elsewhere first (Sonology, ZHdK, KMH), then apply to Cursus. If he does want to try for 2027-28, the deadline is around December 2026, so the portfolio decision is immediate.

programs.program: New Technologies Applied to Composing (Nouvelles technologies appliquées à la composition) — within the composition programme, 2nd cycle (master) level
programs.university: Conservatoire national supérieur de musique et de danse de Paris (CNSMDP)
programs.degree: 2nd-cycle diploma (master level) in composition, with the NTAC discipline embedded. Exact degree designation UNVERIFIED.
programs.durationEcts: "2 or 3 years" for the discipline, plus advanced-cycle years 4–5 for those continuing. ECTS UNVERIFIED.
programs.language: UNVERIFIED — CNSMDP teaches in French and normally requires French proficiency for degree programmes. Assume French is required until confirmed.
programs.institutionType: National conservatoire (grand établissement, France's flagship state conservatory)
programs.focus: Electroacoustic composition · mixed and interactive music · multichannel/spatial electroacoustic work
programs.whatYouStudy: A structured progression in electroacoustic composition: first-year students focus on theory and produce an electroacoustic study; year two involves producing mixed works or large-scale electroacoustic pieces; year three requires developing an individual project for mixed/interactive composition or a multichannel electroacoustic work. Advanced-cycle years 4–5 add seminars on concert production, the durability of works, and self-analysis, culminating in a composition prize. "This course is compulsory during the first 2 years of the 1st cycle of composition", and for 2nd-cycle students in the mixed-music orientation it is mandatory.
programs.entryRequirements: UNVERIFIED on the page read. CNSMDP admits by national competitive examination (CONCOURS D'ENTRÉE) and the discipline page publishes no age limits, prior-degree requirements, application deadlines or concours content. Note the structural point that matters most: NTAC is a DISCIPLINE INSIDE the composition programme, not a standalone master — so entry is through the composition concours, which presupposes substantial compositional training.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — no concours requirements, submission works or application deadlines are published on the discipline page. Must be obtained from CNSMDP's admissions (concours) documentation, which is normally published in the autumn preceding the examination.
programs.auditionSpec: Entry is by competitive examination (concours), which at CNSMDP is on-site in Paris. Content and format for the composition concours UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO, in effect. Nothing on the page addresses non-music applicants, and because NTAC is reached through the CNSMDP composition concours — one of the most competitive composition entries in Europe, presupposing years of compositional and theoretical training — a software-engineering graduate with no music degree and no conservatoire background is not a credible candidate for the September 2027 cycle. Recorded here for completeness of the mandated coverage, with an explicit negative verdict.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED / NOT PUBLISHED on the pages read. CNSMDP concours calendars are normally published in the autumn for a spring examination — check from autumn 2026.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED. CNSMDP is a French state establishment with low registration fees rather than tuition, but the exact figure for a non-EU student was not verified.
programs.scholarship: None found — UNVERIFIED. French routes (Campus France, Eiffel Excellence) exist but their applicability to CNSMDP composition entry is unverified.
programs.facilities: CNSMDP is France's flagship national conservatoire, with close institutional links to IRCAM — students in the CNSMDP composition master "may also benefit from support after their second year of the Master's programme" within the IRCAM Cursus, and students at HEAR and CNSMD Lyon can complete a master year inside the Cursus after jury selection. Studio inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: HONEST VERDICT: not a viable 2027 target for this candidate, and listed only because the brief required CNSMDP to be covered. NTAC is not a standalone master's programme — it is a discipline inside the CNSMDP composition curriculum, entered through the national composition concours, on-site in Paris, in French, against applicants with formal compositional training. He has none of those. The one genuinely useful takeaway is the IRCAM link: CNSMDP, CNSMD Lyon and HEAR composition master's students can spend a master year inside the IRCAM Cursus, which means a French conservatoire composition master is the institutional back door to IRCAM. That is a 5-to-8-year path, not a 2027 one. His French fluency is the only asset that applies here.

programs.program: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound Design for Media Arts (EMJM in Sound)
programs.university: Consortium: IADT Dún Laoghaire (IE, coordinator) + Universidade Lusófona (PT) + Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre / LMTA (LT) — FilmEU alliance
programs.city: Dublin (Sem 1) → Lisbon (Sem 2) → Vilnius (Sem 3) → thesis at a consortium school (Sem 4)
programs.degree: Joint MA in Sound (Irish NFQ Level 9), plus recognition at each partner
programs.focus: Sound Design · Music Production · Film/Game Sound · Immersive Audio · Sonic Arts
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters, 120 ECTS (ECTS figure stated by consortium; IADT page does not repeat it)
programs.language: English
programs.institutionType: Art/technology institute + private university + state conservatory (music & theatre academy) consortium
programs.whatYouStudy: Sem 1 (Dublin): Acoustics & Psychoacoustics; Audio and Music Production; Synthesis and Sampling; Interactive Systems; Sound Psychology. Sem 2 (Lisbon): Film Sound Theory; Interdisciplinary Project Incubation; Sound Ecosystems; Sound/Music Interface; Film Audio Post-production. Sem 3 (Vilnius): Sound and the Environment; Film Sound Integrative Methods; Sound Concepts; Sound Design and Immersion; Thesis Preparation. Sem 4: thesis/major sound project. Projects connect sound design to film, games, immersive media, performance and interactive installation.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in "sound, music, film, media studies, computational science or related disciplines". English: IELTS 6.0 overall with no band below 6.0, or equivalent TOEFL/Duolingo/Cambridge taken within 2 years. Also required: CV, two letters of recommendation (at least one academic), motivation letter (max 1,000 characters), thesis project description (500 characters), passport, headshot, transcripts.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — and this is the single best-matched EMJM for a software-engineering BSc. The IADT programme page explicitly names "computational science" among the accepted bachelor fields, and the consortium adds: "Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience in areas such as sound, music, film, or media." He must therefore evidence prior sound/music practice via the portfolio.
programs.portfolioSpec: "Please supply no more than 3 examples" of your sound or media-related work, each accompanied by a short reflective paragraph. Delivery: "You can supply a single hyperlink to a portfolio website or a compilation audio or video file. The team can realistically listen/watch 10-15 minutes of material per application." So: max 3 works, 10-15 minutes total.
programs.auditionSpec: No live audition and no on-site test. Highest-scoring applicants are invited to an ONLINE interview. Appeals only on procedural grounds.
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 15,000 total participation cost for the four semesters for non-scholarship students (EUR 7,500 before Sem 1 + EUR 7,500 before Sem 3). Same fee for EU and non-EU.
programs.scholarship: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship — open to all nationalities including Tunisian nationals (Partner Country candidates are explicitly eligible and historically favoured in EMJM budgets). "ReSound can award Erasmus Mundus Scholarships on the basis of excellence."
programs.stipend: Full waiver of the EUR 15,000 participation cost + EUR 1,400/month allowance for up to 24 months (= EUR 33,600), covering travel, visa, installation and subsistence.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 intake opened 20 October 2025. Expect the September 2027 call to open ~October 2026 via resound-ma.eu.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 intake deadline was 27 January 2026 (extended). Expect late January 2027 for the September 2027 intake.
programs.facilities: Dolby Atmos studios, immersive media labs and experimental sound environments across the three schools; LMTA Vilnius is a full state music academy; IADT is Ireland's leading film/media school; FilmEU alliance industry links. Max 24 places per cohort.
programs.fitNotes: The strongest single target in this slice: it is a genuine sound-design/production master, fully fundable, English-taught, explicitly open to computational-science bachelors, needs no live audition, and only 10-15 minutes of portfolio material. Main obstacle: he must build a credible 3-piece sound/music portfolio plus IELTS 6.0 (no band under 6.0) during 2026, and competition for 24 places is heavy.

programs.program: DIGICREA — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master "Digital Creativity, Art & Science" (Sound-Music specialisation)
programs.university: Consortium: Université Jean Monnet Saint-Étienne (FR, coordinator) + Universidade Católica Portuguesa – School of Arts, Porto (PT) + University of Silesia in Katowice (PL)
programs.degree: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master's degree (multiple/joint award), 2nd cycle
programs.focus: Music Production · Sound Design · Electronic Music · Immersive/XR Audio · Film/Game Sound
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS
programs.language: English (100%); language courses in French/Portuguese/Polish included in the fee)
programs.institutionType: Public university (FR) + private Catholic university school of arts (PT) + public university (PL)
programs.whatYouStudy: Two entry specialisations — Sound-Music, or Image-New Media — inside a shared curriculum at the intersection of art, technology and science: music and sound design, interactive arts, film production, video game development, extended reality (XR), artificial intelligence in the arts, audiovisual new media. Hands-on studio and lab work with industry collaborations and interdisciplinary team projects across the three campuses.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree of at least 180 ECTS (candidates holding 150 ECTS at application may be admitted with a sworn statement undertaking to complete 180 ECTS). English B2 minimum, C1 recommended — evidence accepted: IELTS 6, TOEFL iBT 90+, TOEIC 650+, a degree taught 100% in English, or in exceptional cases a teacher attestation/sworn statement. Two letters of recommendation.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — no bachelor field is mandated. The stated candidate profile is an "artist/creator in the Sound-Music or Image-New media field WITH scientific knowledge and skills in maths and computer science", and applicants must show "predispositions for professions related to the production of audio-visual and musical forms". A software-engineering BSc is an asset here rather than a handicap; the missing half is documented creative sound work.
programs.portfolioSpec: Compulsory. "Exactly 3 to 5 specific works or projects" (video/audio/images), each with metadata: title, short description, public link, and the applicant's role. All works must be no more than 5 years old. For the Sound-Music specialisation the accepted work types are compositions, sound design, music pieces and demos. Candidates whose portfolio does not match the guidelines are discarded.
programs.auditionSpec: No live audition, no on-site test. Shortlisted candidates sit an ONLINE 15-minute interview assessing personality, thinking patterns and character.
programs.tuitionIntl: ZERO. "Students (scholarship holders and non-scholarship holders) are not charged any tuition fees." (Ignore the EUR 17,000 non-EU figure that appears on the site's tuition page — that text belongs to the university's other EMJM, DYCLAM+; the DIGICREA financial-aid page states no tuition is charged.)
programs.scholarship: EMJM scholarship, open to all nationalities including Tunisian nationals; the only stated disqualifier is having already held an EMJM scholarship. Non-scholarship students can additionally tap Erasmus+ KA131/KA171 mobility funds during the course.
programs.stipend: EUR 1,400/month for 24 months = up to EUR 33,600, covering travel, visa, installation and subsistence; no tuition to waive since the programme is fee-free.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026-2028 cohort opened 14 November 2025. The programme itself states the next cohort (2027-2029) is expected to open around November 2026 — which is exactly his cycle.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026-2028 deadline was 16 February 2026, 23:00 French time, via the e-Candidat portal. Expect ~mid-February 2027.
programs.facilities: UCP Porto School of Arts (strong sound/music technology tradition), Silesia's Cieszyn arts campus, XR/AI labs at Saint-Étienne; launched its first cohort in 2025-2026, so it is a young programme with small cohorts. Named professors/alumni UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Arguably the best value in this slice: no tuition at all, a dedicated Sound-Music entry track, and an explicit expectation that candidates combine creative work with maths/CS skills — a rare direct match for a software-engineering graduate who produces music. Obstacles: the portfolio bar is strict (exactly 3-5 works, none older than 5 years, public links required) and the programme is brand-new so track record and industry placement are unproven.

programs.program: REPLAY — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master, The European Game Design Masters
programs.university: Consortium: Universidade Lusófona (PT, coordinator) + LUCA School of Arts (BE) + Aalto University (FI)
programs.city: Lisbon (Sem 1) → Genk, Belgium (Sem 2) → Helsinki/Espoo (Sem 3) → Sem 4 at a chosen partner
programs.degree: Joint Master's degree + separate MA/MSc from each of the three partners (four degrees in total, 120 ECTS)
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound (game audio within game design) · Interactive/Immersive production
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS
programs.language: English
programs.institutionType: Private university (PT) + art school (BE) + public research university/art & design school (FI)
programs.whatYouStudy: Year 1: Critical Play, Design Sprint, Experimental Play Lab, Play in Context — studio practice building experimental, culturally aware game experiences. Year 2: Game Jam, industry seminars with working professionals, and a 30 ECTS thesis project. Game audio/sound design is available as a craft role inside team projects rather than as a taught audio specialisation — CONFIRM the audio pathway with the consortium before applying.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's or Master's diploma at NFQ level 8 / EQF level 6 minimum. Documents: online form, ID/passport, headshot, diploma, Europass CV, motivation letter (max 3,000 characters), a "post-mortem" of up to two projects (max 2,000 characters each), portfolio, showreel, English proficiency proof, residence certificate.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, explicitly. Open to "students of all nationalities holding a Bachelor's degree in relevant fields for game design and production (software engineering, computer science, multimedia, graphic art, etc.)", and "Students from all over the world are welcome to apply to this program, including those with diplomas in various fields of study" provided they have relevant experience in game design and production. Software engineering is named as a directly relevant degree.
programs.portfolioSpec: PDF portfolio, "a maximum of 5 games or projects across up to 7 pages" using the consortium's template: page 1 bio + photo; one project per page with project name, your role, team size, 3-4 images and a clickable link; plus a final links page. PLUS a showreel of maximum 3 minutes = 30 seconds self-presentation + 1.5-2.5 minutes of project showcase.
programs.auditionSpec: No live audition or on-site test. "Applicants with the highest scores resulting from the application package will be called for an online Interview."
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 15,000 for four semesters for non-scholarship students; non-EU status does not change the fee.
programs.scholarship: EMJM scholarship awarded "on the basis of excellence"; the published criteria make no EU/non-EU distinction, so Tunisian nationals are eligible.
programs.stipend: Covers tuition/participation costs in full plus EUR 1,400/month allowance for up to 24 months.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The site states the 2026-2028 call is closed and "the next call opens in October" — i.e. ~October 2026 for the September 2027 intake.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Expect a January 2027 scholarship deadline in line with FilmEU consortium practice; not yet published.
programs.facilities: Aalto (Helsinki) is a top-tier media lab environment; LUCA Genk has a games/media campus; Lusófona runs Portugal's largest game-design school. Specific audio suites UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The easiest EMJM in this slice for him to be ADMITTED to — software engineering is a named target degree — and it is fully funded. But the craft taught is game design, not music production or DJing; he would be building games, not tracks, and game audio is a side role. Worth applying as a funded backup only if he genuinely wants interactive audio.

programs.program: DocNomadsPLUS — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree in Documentary Film Directing
programs.university: Consortium: Universidade Lusófona (PT) + Budapest Metropolitan University / SZFE lineage (HU) + LUCA School of Arts, Brussels (BE)
programs.degree: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Degree, 120 ECTS
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound and hands-on audiovisual production (documentary directing; sound recording and post are taught as craft, not as the specialisation)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS
programs.language: English (B2 minimum)
programs.institutionType: Film school / university film & arts faculties consortium
programs.whatYouStudy: Intensive practice-based documentary filmmaking: directing, producing, shooting and editing your own films in three countries, with location sound recording, sound editing and mixing taught as part of the production chain. Roughly 24 students per cohort. Not a sound-design curriculum — sound is one craft among directing, camera and editing.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree, primarily in Film Studies, Audiovisual Arts, or Media/Communication studies. English B2 CEFR, provable via IELTS 6.5, TOEFL iBT 79, Cambridge 170+, Duolingo 110, or an English-medium degree from an accepted country.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — conditionally yes. "Applicants with a Bachelor's degree in other fields may also be considered, provided they submit a convincing artistic portfolio." A software-engineering BSc is therefore admissible but the portfolio must carry the whole case.
programs.portfolioSpec: Three video assignments, all mandatory: (1) a ONE-MINUTE motivational video on what documentary means to you, why you apply and what you expect; (2) a THREE-MINUTE original documentary film on the set theme "Around Me, in the Here and Now" which "must be shot and edited by the applicant" with NO added music or effects allowed; (3) a link to one previous film, maximum 10 minutes, with English subtitles and production credits.
programs.auditionSpec: Mandatory ONLINE interview. In the last cycle: 16-20 March for scholarship candidates, 11-15 May for self-funded applicants. No on-site test.
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 15,000 total for four semesters, paid in three instalments (non-scholarship students).
programs.scholarship: Erasmus Mundus scholarship "available to eligible applicants regardless of nationality" — Tunisian nationals eligible. Two-year awards to a subset of selected European and non-European students.
programs.stipend: Tuition/participation costs covered plus approximately EUR 1,400/month for living, travel and visa costs.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Recurring pattern: applications open 20 October. Expect ~20 October 2026 for the September 2027 intake.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Two deadlines in the recurring pattern: 20 January for Erasmus Mundus scholarship candidates and 15 April for self-funded applicants only. Confirm the 2027 dates.
programs.facilities: Three established film schools with full production and post-production infrastructure; DocNomads is one of the longest-running film EMJMs (previous edition ran Lisbon-Budapest-Brussels). Named staff/alumni UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Fully funded and reachable with a non-film degree, but the wrong craft: he would spend two years directing documentaries, and the compulsory 3-minute film must contain no added music — the opposite of his skill set. Only a fit if he is willing to pivot to filmmaking. Listed because it is one of the few reliably funded creative-production EMJMs and the entry route for non-specialists is explicit.

programs.program: Kino Eyes (KEM) — The European Film Masters, Erasmus Mundus Joint MA — SOUND specialisation
programs.university: Consortium: Universidade Lusófona (PT) + Screen Academy Scotland / Edinburgh Napier University (UK) + Baltic Film, Media and Arts School, Tallinn University (EE) + IADT Dún Laoghaire (IE)
programs.city: Lisbon (Sem 1) → Dublin or Tallinn (Sem 2) → Tallinn summer school → graduation at a consortium school
programs.degree: Erasmus Mundus Joint MA in fiction filmmaking, four semesters (120 ECTS)
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound — a dedicated Sound specialisation inside a fiction-filmmaking master
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters (120 ECTS)
programs.language: English
programs.institutionType: Four film schools (art institute, university film academy, public university film school)
programs.whatYouStudy: Intensive fiction filmmaking. Students are recruited into one of six craft specialisations — directing, screenwriting, producing, cinematography, editing and SOUND — and work in cross-national crews on short fiction films across the partner schools. Only 4-5 students are enrolled per specialisation, so the sound cohort is tiny and the hands-on time is high: production sound, sound design and post-production mixing on real fiction shoots.
programs.entryRequirements: "KEM is open to European and non-European students with a BA degree related with film production." English proficiency required. Showreel and interview mandatory.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — conditionally yes: non-film degrees are accepted "for applicants with relevant professional experience in film". He has none, so this is the weakest link; he would need demonstrable film-sound or audio-post work before applying.
programs.portfolioSpec: Showreel of MAXIMUM 6 MINUTES. It must "show the film credits and if possible, with English subtitles" and must "reflect your area of specialization chosen for the Master course" — i.e. for the Sound track, work where his sound credit is visible. No separate written portfolio specified.
programs.auditionSpec: No live audition or on-site test. Selected candidates are called for a Zoom interview on a date set by the selection committee.
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 15,000 for four semesters, identical for EU and non-EU students.
programs.scholarship: None found for the current call — the admissions page states plainly: "No Scholarships will be available to be awarded." The programme's Erasmus Mundus scholarship funding period has ended; the consortium's EU-funded successor effort is ReSound. TREAT AS SELF-PAY FALLBACK unless a renewed EMJM grant is announced.
programs.stipend: None currently. UNVERIFIED whether a new EMJM grant will fund the 2027 intake.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Applications currently closed; no dates published on the admissions page. Historic pattern is an autumn opening.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Not published.
programs.facilities: Four working film schools; Screen Academy Scotland and BFM Tallinn both run professional sound-post facilities; strong festival pipeline for KEM graduation films. Specific consoles/Atmos rooms UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The only European joint master that lets you enter as a dedicated SOUND specialist on fiction film crews, with only 4-5 places per craft — excellent craft training. Two blockers for him: no scholarships in the current call (EUR 15,000 self-pay), and the non-film-degree route requires professional film experience he does not yet have. Watch for a renewed EMJM grant; otherwise prefer ReSound.

programs.program: Nordic Master: The Composing Musician (NoCoM) — Nordplus/Nordic Master joint programme
programs.university: Rhythmic Music Conservatory Copenhagen (DK) + Norwegian Academy of Music, Oslo (NO) + Academy of Music and Drama, University of Gothenburg (SE)
programs.city: Copenhagen / Oslo / Gothenburg (mobility across the three)
programs.degree: cand. musicae (Music Performance, NoCoM) / Master of Music (MMus)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics · Music Production (composition-performance for the popular/rhythmic music field)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS
programs.language: "Primarily Scandinavian, but English will also be used to the extent necessary" — a serious barrier for a non-Scandinavian speaker
programs.institutionType: Three state conservatories / academies of music (RMC Copenhagen is the Nordic centre of gravity for rhythmic, electronic and pop production)
programs.whatYouStudy: Composition/Performance 45 ECTS + Semester Projects 22.5 ECTS + Electives 22.5 ECTS + Master's Project 30 ECTS. You develop and perform your own composed/arranged music as an artist-composer. RMC's own environment is rhythmic/electronic music, but the joint curriculum does not list dedicated production, studio-engineering or DAW modules — CONFIRM with RMC how much studio production the electives allow.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree IN MUSIC from an accredited conservatory (or expected completion before the programme starts). The conservatory "may recognise other artistically based Bachelor's degrees in music as qualifying" on individual assessment.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No (effectively). The requirement is a conservatory music bachelor; the only flexibility offered is recognition of "other artistically based Bachelor's degrees IN MUSIC". A software-engineering BSc does not satisfy this. He would need a music bachelor or an exceptional documented artistic case.
programs.portfolioSpec: "3-4 music examples on video (mp4, total duration 15 min.)", optionally with sheet music / graphic notation / text (PDF), plus CV and degree documentation. The material must be composed and/or arranged by the applicant, must include improvisation, and the applicant must perform in it and be "artistically responsible for the music".
programs.auditionSpec: Video-based assessment of the 3-4 examples; shortlisted candidates are normally called to a live/online audition-interview at the conservatories — CONFIRM the 2027 format directly with RMC. UNVERIFIED whether on-site attendance is required.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED for non-EU/non-EEA applicants. Denmark, Norway and Sweden all charge non-EEA tuition at arts institutions since 2023 (Norway included); the RMC page does not state a non-EEA rate. Assume a fee and confirm in writing.
programs.scholarship: Nordplus study grants exist for the mobility legs (e.g. EUR 1,000 grants are cited for the sister Nordic Master in Folk Music), but Nordplus is a NORDIC mobility instrument — it funds movement between the partner schools, NOT a full scholarship for a Tunisian national, and it does not cover non-EEA tuition. No dedicated non-EU scholarship found for NoCoM.
programs.stipend: UNVERIFIED / effectively none for a non-EEA student beyond small mobility grants.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Opened 16 December 2025 for the 2026 intake. Expect ~mid-December 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Closed 3 February 2026 at 12:00 CET for the 2026 intake. Expect early February 2027.
programs.facilities: RMC Copenhagen is one of Europe's best-equipped rhythmic/electronic music conservatories; NMH Oslo and HSM Gothenburg both have strong studios. Specific consoles/Atmos rooms UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Included because it is the flagship Nordplus/Nordic Master in the popular-music field, but it is a poor fit for him: it demands a conservatory music bachelor, teaches primarily in Scandinavian, funds nothing meaningful for a non-EEA student, and assesses him as a performing composer-improviser. Realistic only after a music bachelor or years of documented artistic practice.

programs.program: DAAD Study Scholarship — Postgraduate Studies in the Field of MUSIC (artistic scholarship; funds a Master/Konzertexamen/Meisterklasse at a German state Musikhochschule)
programs.university: Any German state college of music (Staatliche Musikhochschule) — e.g. the electronic-music/music-production and Tonmeister masters in Berlin, Cologne, Detmold, Karlsruhe, Düsseldorf; the DAAD does not itself place you
programs.city: Applicant's choice of German city (scholarship follows the admission)
programs.degree: Master of Music / postgraduate artistic qualification (Konzertexamen, Meisterklasse), 2-4 semesters
programs.focus: Music Production · Electronic Music · Electroacoustic Composition · Recording/Engineering — provided the host programme is classified as ARTISTIC, not scientific
programs.durationEcts: 10-24 months of funding for a degree programme (2-4 semesters); 12 months (extendable) for non-degree advanced studies
programs.language: German or English depending on the host Musikhochschule; DAAD funds a 2/4/6-month preparatory German course, compulsory if teaching is in German
programs.institutionType: Funding scheme routed to state conservatories / colleges of music
programs.whatYouStudy: Whatever the German host programme delivers — the scheme is the money, not the curriculum. IMPORTANT LIMIT: "This programme only funds projects in the artistic field." Musicology, music education and scientific/technical projects belong to other DAAD lines. Sound engineering / music production is fundable ONLY where the host programme is artistically classified — verify the classification with the intended Musikhochschule before applying.
programs.entryRequirements: A first degree in music (the scheme targets graduates who have "exhausted all training opportunities" at home). Degree must be no more than 6 years old at the deadline. You must not have lived in Germany for more than 15 months at the deadline. Cannot fund a programme already started in Germany. Documents: tabular CV, 1-3 page letter of motivation, transcripts with grading explanation, degree certificate, language certificate (max 3 years old), German/English translations, a supervision confirmation from a lecturer at the German host institution, plus the Master's profile form and the letter of admission before the scholarship starts.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No, as written. The DAAD music line addresses applicants with "a first degree in music". A software-engineering BSc does not meet the stated profile — he would more plausibly use the parallel DAAD line for Fine Art/Design/Visual Communication/Film (listed separately below), or a general DAAD Master line if the German programme is academically rather than artistically classified.
programs.portfolioSpec: Artistic work samples uploaded to a DAAD media database within TWO WEEKS of receiving the access link. VIDEO files only (mp4, max 1080p). Exception: composition and AUDIO ENGINEERING applicants may submit audio (mp3, wav). MIDI realisations and technically manipulated files are NOT accepted. An overview form listing the recorded pieces is required.
programs.auditionSpec: No DAAD live audition — the media-database work samples are the audition. A dedicated DAAD committee of professors from German art, music and film colleges decides. Separately, the German Musikhochschule will almost certainly run its own ENTRANCE EXAM, usually on-site in Germany — that is the real audition and it is the host institution's requirement, not DAAD's.
programs.tuitionIntl: German public Musikhochschulen charge no tuition, only semester contributions (typically EUR 150-400/semester). Note explicitly: "the DAAD does not cover tuition fees."
programs.scholarship: Yes — Tunisian nationals are eligible. DAAD maintains a Regional Office in TUNIS (covering Tunisia, Algeria, Libya, Morocco) with pre-application consultation in Arabic and French, and Tunisia appears in the DAAD scholarship database as a supported country. Confirm the Tunisia entry for the specific music line each year, since country lists are refreshed annually.
programs.stipend: EUR 992/month (the music line; DAAD figures were EUR 934-992 across recent years) plus health/accident/liability insurance, a travel allowance on application, a one-off study allowance, German course funding, and possible rent and family supplements. Scholarship normally begins 1 October.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 June each year (portal opens).
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Deadlines are set annually and vary by line and country; the arts/music lines have historically closed in the autumn preceding the October start. For a 1 October 2027 start expect the portal open 1 June 2026-2027 window — CONFIRM the exact 2027 date on the DAAD portal and with DAAD Tunis.
programs.facilities: German state Musikhochschulen and Tonmeister institutes are among Europe's best-equipped (large-format consoles, Atmos/immersive rooms, electronic-music studios) and charge no tuition. Specific rooms depend on the chosen school — UNVERIFIED here.
programs.fitNotes: The scheme itself is excellent value (fee-free public conservatories + full living stipend) and DAAD Tunis gives him local support in French/Arabic. The blocker is eligibility: the music line expects a first degree IN MUSIC, and German Musikhochschulen run demanding on-site entrance exams. He should treat DAAD as the funding layer for a German target school and check whether that school's programme is artistically or academically classified, because that determines which DAAD line he uses.

programs.program: DAAD Study Scholarship — Postgraduate Studies in the Fields of FINE ART, DESIGN, VISUAL COMMUNICATION and FILM
programs.university: Any German art school, design school or film school (Kunsthochschule / Filmhochschule / HfG) — the applicant chooses and secures the admission
programs.degree: Master's or postgraduate degree in fine art, design, visual communication or film (also non-degree complementary studies)
programs.focus: Sound Design · Film/Game Sound · Sonic Arts — where delivered inside a German art/design/film school programme (e.g. sound for film, media art, sound-and-image design)
programs.durationEcts: 10-24 months of funding depending on programme length; 12 months for complementary studies
programs.language: German, English or both, depending on the host school; language certificates may not be older than three years
programs.institutionType: Funding scheme routed to art schools, design schools and film schools
programs.whatYouStudy: Determined by the host German school. This is the correct DAAD line for sound design taught within an art/design/film faculty (media art, sound-image design, film sound) rather than within a Musikhochschule. History of Art, Art Studies and Restoration are explicitly excluded from this line.
programs.entryRequirements: First degree in a relevant field; admission (or a professor's supervision confirmation) at a German art/film school. Degree not older than 6 years; not resident in Germany more than 15 months at the deadline. Language certificate for the language of instruction.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — more permissive than the music line. This line does not require a fine-art bachelor in the same rigid way the music line requires a music degree, and it is the natural DAAD route for someone entering sound design via an art/film school. But the decisive evidence is the work samples: "samples of your work" must meet the formal requirements published on DAAD's dedicated Fine Art information page. QUOTE the exact wording from that page before relying on it — UNVERIFIED here.
programs.portfolioSpec: Work samples are mandatory and formal requirements are set on DAAD's dedicated Fine Art/Design/Film scholarship information page (format, number and length not stated on the database entry) — UNVERIFIED, must be read directly.
programs.auditionSpec: No DAAD live audition; a DAAD committee of professors from German art, music and film colleges assesses the submitted work samples. The German host school will run its own admission/portfolio procedure, frequently on-site.
programs.tuitionIntl: German public art and film schools charge no tuition, only semester contributions. DAAD does not cover tuition fees where they exist (some film schools and private academies do charge).
programs.scholarship: Yes for Tunisian nationals in principle — DAAD supports Tunisia and runs the Tunis regional office. CAUTION: the country dropdown on this specific database entry did not visibly list Tunisia when checked, and the page warns "If your status and/or country is not included in the list, you cannot apply for this scholarship programme." VERIFY Tunisia's inclusion on THIS line directly with DAAD Tunis before building a plan around it.
programs.stipend: EUR 992/month plus insurance, travel allowance, one-off study allowance, German course support; start usually 1 October (or earlier with a pre-study German course).
programs.applicationOpens: 1 June each year.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. "Applications for this scholarship programme are possible between 1 June and the stated application deadline" — the exact date is published annually and was not stated on the page. CONFIRM for the 2027 start.
programs.facilities: German art and film schools (e.g. film academies with full sound-post pipelines, media-art sound studios) are tuition-free and well equipped; specific facilities depend on the chosen school — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Strategically the better of the two DAAD artistic lines for him, because it does not demand a music degree and covers film/media sound taught in art and film schools. Two things to nail down: (1) whether Tunisia is on this line's country list, and (2) the exact work-sample specification, which is the real gate. Pair it with a specific German school's sound programme identified in the Germany slice.

programs.program: Master Mind Scholarships (Government of Flanders) — funds any eligible Flemish master, including sound design and music masters
programs.university: Any participating Flemish institution — for sound: RITCS / Erasmushogeschool Brussel (Master in Audiovisual Arts – Sound Design), LUCA School of Arts (Master in Music; Master in Audiovisual Arts – Film), KASK & Conservatorium Ghent, University of Antwerp
programs.degree: Master of Arts (Audiovisual Arts – Sound Design) / Master of Music, 2nd cycle
programs.focus: Sound Design · Film/Game Sound · Recording/Engineering · Music Production
programs.durationEcts: Typically 1-2 years / 60-120 ECTS depending on the Flemish programme; the scholarship is awarded per academic year
programs.language: Mixed. RITCS Sound Design is taught largely in DUTCH — this is the main practical obstacle. Some LUCA and Antwerp masters run in English. VERIFY the language of the exact programme.
programs.institutionType: Universities of applied sciences / schools of arts (RITCS, LUCA, KASK) + public university (Antwerp)
programs.whatYouStudy: At RITCS, Sound Design "combines art, engineering and technology, and teaches students to create impactful soundtracks", inside a school organised by craft specialisation (animation, radio, directing, writing, production, cinematography, sound design, editing) from bachelor to master level. LUCA offers Master in Music and Master in Audiovisual Arts – Film. Detailed module lists UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: For the scholarship: previous degree obtained OUTSIDE Flanders; not already enrolled at a Flemish institution; GPA of 3.5/4.0 on the last obtained bachelor's or master's degree; good English with proof no older than 3 years at the time of processing; enrolment in an eligible master (preparatory, bridging and distance programmes are excluded). For the programme itself: RITCS/LUCA arts masters require an artistic admission assessment.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check. Master Mind imposes no field restriction — it funds "eligible Masters Degree Programmes offered at participating Flemish Institutions". Admissibility depends entirely on the art school's own entrance assessment. NOTE the hard scholarship filter: a 3.5/4.0 GPA equivalent from his SMU MedTech BSc.
programs.portfolioSpec: Set by the institution, not by the scheme. RITCS asks incoming students to "send your CV and a portfolio of your work"; exact counts, durations and formats for the Sound Design master are UNVERIFIED — request the artistic-admission brief from RITCS directly.
programs.auditionSpec: Institution-level artistic admission assessment. CRITICAL SCHEDULING RULE: "To be considered for the Master Mind Scholarship, you must participate in the first Master Assessment round (usually in March). Later applications cannot be considered." So the artistic assessment must be done in the FIRST round.
programs.tuitionIntl: Non-EEA tuition at Flemish arts schools is normally several thousand euros; LUCA does not publish a single figure, stating the fee depends on study contract, credits, scholarship status and nationality. Master Mind holders instead pay the lowest registration fee: EUR 140 for 2026-2027.
programs.scholarship: Master Mind Scholarships — approximately 30 awards per year for incoming international master's students. "International students from all countries except Russia can apply", so Tunisian nationals ARE eligible.
programs.stipend: Maximum EUR 10,225 per academic year plus reduction of tuition to EUR 140 for 2026-2027. Not a full-cost package for two years — budget the gap.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. "The call is mostly launched around the beginning of January", with the specific requirements updated during January/February. Expect January 2027 for a September 2027 start.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Tied to the institution's first Master Assessment round, usually MARCH, with processing in April. Confirm the 2027-2028 call dates with VLUHR/Study in Flanders and with the chosen school.
programs.facilities: RITCS is the audiovisual and performing-arts school of Brussels with a long-standing sound-design track; LUCA Genk/Leuven has music and media campuses; LUCA has previously hosted Master Mind holders in Master in Music: Classical Performance, Master in Audiovisual Arts – Film and Master in Visual Arts – Graphic Design.
programs.fitNotes: A realistic partial-funding route into a genuine craft sound-design school in a French-speaking city (Brussels), which suits his French fluency socially. Three obstacles: RITCS Sound Design is largely Dutch-taught, the scholarship demands a 3.5/4.0 GPA equivalent, and he must complete the artistic assessment in the FIRST (March) round or lose scholarship eligibility entirely.

programs.program: Stefan Banach Scholarship Programme (NAWA, Poland) — second-cycle studies scholarship
programs.university: Polish universities SUPERVISED BY THE MINISTER OF SCIENCE AND HIGHER EDUCATION (this is the critical restriction — see fit notes)
programs.city: Any eligible Polish city (Warsaw, Kraków, Wrocław, Gdańsk, Katowice…)
programs.focus: Music Production · Sound Design · Recording/Engineering — only insofar as such a programme exists at an eligible (Ministry-of-Science-supervised) Polish university, e.g. audio/acoustic engineering and multimedia faculties, NOT the Ministry-of-Culture music academies
programs.durationEcts: Master's programmes of 3 to 4 semesters, plus an optional preparatory language course year
programs.language: Polish or English
programs.institutionType: Public universities and technical universities (art and music academies are supervised by the Ministry of Culture and are therefore very likely OUTSIDE the scheme)
programs.whatYouStudy: Whatever the eligible Polish master delivers. Poland's celebrated sound-production tracks — Reżyseria Dźwięku (Sound Engineering/Direction) at the Chopin University of Music in Warsaw and the film-sound tracks at the Łódź Film School — sit under the Ministry of CULTURE, so they are probably NOT fundable through Banach. Technical-university audio/acoustics and multimedia masters are fundable but lean engineering rather than music production.
programs.entryRequirements: Citizenship of an eligible country; a first-cycle degree; enrolment in a full-time second-cycle programme at an eligible Polish university. Precise academic and language conditions are set in each annual call.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes at scheme level — the scholarship "covers all full-time second-cycle study programmes offered by Polish universities supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education, regardless of a specific scientific field". A software-engineering BSc is a natural fit for an eligible technical master. The constraint is not his degree; it is which institutions the scheme will pay for.
programs.portfolioSpec: None at scheme level. Any portfolio is set by the host Polish programme — UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: None at scheme level. Polish music academies (rezyseria dzwieku) run demanding on-site entrance exams including ear training and Polish-language components, but those institutions are probably outside Banach anyway.
programs.tuitionIntl: Scheme provides "exemption from tuition fees at public universities or for the preparatory course".
programs.scholarship: Stefan Banach NAWA Programme — TUNISIA IS EXPLICITLY ELIGIBLE. Tunisia is one of the 36 listed countries and sits in Group 3 alongside Angola, DR Congo, Egypt, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Palestine, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania, Yemen and Zambia. Note that some country groups are additionally allowed to apply for selected humanities/social-science masters, and Group 3 (Tunisia) is NOT among those groups — a further reason to expect arts programmes to be out of scope.
programs.stipend: Monthly stipend (amount not stated on the pages read — UNVERIFIED; historically in the region of PLN 1,700/month) plus tuition exemption. CONFIRM in the annual call.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED for the 2027/28 edition; NAWA publishes an annual call (recent editions have opened in spring).
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — not stated on the pages read. Recent Banach calls have closed around mid-May for an autumn start. CONFIRM on nawa.gov.pl.
programs.facilities: Poland has world-class sound-production training (Chopin University Warsaw rezyseria dzwieku; Łódź Film School), but those are the institutions most likely excluded from Banach. Eligible technical universities have good audio/acoustics labs — specifics UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Tunisia's explicit eligibility makes this look attractive, but there is a probable structural mismatch: the money follows Ministry-of-Science universities while Poland's best sound-production schools sit under the Ministry of Culture. ACTION: before investing effort, email NAWA to ask in writing whether the Chopin University of Music (Warsaw) and the Łódź Film School are eligible host institutions. If they are not, use Banach only for an engineering-flavoured audio master.

programs.program: Stipendium Hungaricum (Hungarian Government) — full master's scholarship
programs.university: Participating Hungarian institutions incl. Budapest Metropolitan University (METU), Liszt Ferenc Academy of Music, Hungarian University of Fine Arts, Budapest University of Technology and Economics
programs.focus: Music Production · Electronic Music · Sound Design — subject to which arts programmes are opened to Tunisian applicants in a given call
programs.durationEcts: Typically 2 years / 120 ECTS (programme-dependent)
programs.language: English (English-taught tracks) or Hungarian
programs.institutionType: Public universities, a private university (METU), state music academy, state fine-arts university
programs.whatYouStudy: Depends on the chosen Hungarian programme. Budapest Metropolitan University is the largest private university in Hungary with arts, media and communication programmes and "modern buildings with a sound studio, radio and television studio, smart boards, and a multimedia library" — the most plausible host for media/sound production. The Liszt Academy offers Stipendium Hungaricum places at BA, MA and postgraduate level but the search-visible MA offer is Piano Soloist, i.e. classical performance, NOT production.
programs.entryRequirements: Scheme level: a bachelor's degree, and citizenship of a country with a valid bilateral educational cooperation agreement with Hungary. Programme level: the institution's own academic and artistic requirements, plus a written and/or oral entrance examination for most Stipendium Hungaricum programmes.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — depends entirely on the host programme. A media/sound-production master at METU or a technical audio master would consider a software-engineering BSc; a Liszt Academy performance MA would not. No scheme-level restriction on the bachelor field.
programs.portfolioSpec: Set by the host programme, not the scheme — UNVERIFIED for any sound/music-production track. Arts programmes under Stipendium Hungaricum normally require a portfolio and/or entrance exam.
programs.auditionSpec: Most Stipendium Hungaricum arts programmes require an entrance examination, commonly held online for international applicants — UNVERIFIED for the specific programme; the Liszt Academy runs auditions.
programs.tuitionIntl: Fully covered by the scholarship (tuition-free for holders).
programs.scholarship: Stipendium Hungaricum — Tunisia participates: Hungary has hosted and publicly honoured Tunisian Stipendium Hungaricum students. IMPORTANT CAVEAT stated by the Liszt Academy itself: applicants must "check if music programmes are available for the citizens of your country in the framework of the scholarship programme" — the eligible FIELDS are set per country in each bilateral agreement, so music/arts may or may not be open to Tunisian applicants in a given call.
programs.stipend: Covers tuition, a monthly stipend, accommodation support and health insurance (the standard Stipendium Hungaricum package). Exact 2027 amounts UNVERIFIED.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Recent cycles have opened in November for the following September. Expect ~November 2026 for September 2027.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Recent cycles closed in mid-January. Expect ~mid-January 2027. CONFIRM on stipendiumhungaricum.hu.
programs.facilities: METU has sound, radio and television studios and a multimedia library; the Liszt Academy is a historic conservatory (classical focus). Hungary's University of Theatre and Film Arts (SZFE) sound track — participation in Stipendium Hungaricum UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Full funding including accommodation, and Tunisia is a participating country — genuinely worth checking. But two verifications decide it: (1) whether MUSIC/ARTS fields are open to Tunisian citizens in the 2027 call, and (2) whether any Hungarian institution actually offers an English-taught master in music production or sound design rather than classical performance. Do both checks before committing time.

programs.program: Türkiye Bursları — Art Scholarship Programme (full-time master's)

programs.degree: Master of Arts (e.g. ITU MIAM Music MA, Sonic Arts concentration)
programs.focus: Sonic Arts · Electronic Music / Live Electronics · Music Production

programs.language: English at ITU MIAM (MIAM is Türkiye's English-medium graduate music centre); Turkish at the Ankara institutions, with a one-year Turkish course provided by the scholarship
programs.institutionType: Public technical university research centre (ITU MIAM) + state fine-arts/music universities
programs.whatYouStudy: ITU MIAM's Music MA runs concentrations including Sonic Arts — electronic and electroacoustic composition, computer music, sound synthesis and studio practice — alongside ethnomusicology and performance tracks. CAUTION: a page checked stated "There is no quota available for international applicants to the Music Master's Program", and the MIAM programme page was unreachable (HTTP 503) at the time of research. Art Scholarship applicants are expected to hold international academic qualifications or language certificates (SAT, GRE, TOEFL, IELTS etc.). Programme level: ITU's own graduate admission requirements including ALES/GRE-type scores and an entrance evaluation — UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — UNVERIFIED. MIAM has historically admitted candidates from technical and scientific backgrounds into computer-music/sonic-arts work (it sits inside a technical university), which is encouraging for a software-engineering graduate, but no published wording was confirmed. Ask MIAM directly.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED. The Türkiye Bursları Art Scholarship track requires a talent/portfolio assessment but the exact specification for a Sonic Arts MA was not confirmed (MIAM page returned HTTP 503).
programs.auditionSpec: UNVERIFIED — the Art Scholarship route normally involves a talent examination or artistic evaluation; format (online vs on-site in Türkiye) not confirmed.
