programs.program: Sound Design for Audiovisual Media (M.F.A.)
programs.university: Filmuniversität Babelsberg KONRAD WOLF
programs.city: Potsdam-Babelsberg (Potsdam, Brandenburg; ~30 min from central Berlin)
programs.institutionType: Public film school (state film university, Land Brandenburg)
programs.durationEcts: 6 semesters / 120 LP (ECTS) — ANOMALY NOW RESOLVED: the official page states '6 Semester (120 LP)', and the university explains the workload as 30 credits in each of semesters 1–2 (full-time) and a reduced 15 credits in semesters 3–6 (part-time). So it is a 3-year programme with a part-time second half, not a compressed 120-ECTS degree. Plan for 3 years of residence, not 2.
programs.language: German. Applicants who did not obtain their university entrance qualification at a German-language institution and do not hold German citizenship must show German 'at least at the DSH-1 level or an equivalent language certificate'. The application page also indicates a minimum of B1 is accepted AT APPLICATION with higher levels required to complete the programme — this softening is worth confirming in writing, because DSH-1 remains the stated admission standard.
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Immersive Audio (cinema mixing)
programs.whatYouStudy: Confirmed at master level: audio engineering, sound mixing, acoustics/signal processing and music, applied to audiovisual work. Students plan and deliver cinema sound mixes and act as sound supervisors on the film university's own productions, developing an individual 'sound language' through interdisciplinary artistic projects. Pro Tools is the working DAW — the entrance exam itself is a Pro Tools scoring task on a short film. Entry is winter term only.
programs.entryRequirements: Quoted from the official application page: applicants must hold 'a completed Bachelor of Fine Arts (B.F.A.) degree in Sound, Tonmeister*in or a comparable subject-specific degree'. Foreign qualifications are evaluated via uni-assist. German at DSH-1 (see language note). An administrative fee is charged for the application. Medical certificate of normal hearing plus audiogram: NOT re-confirmed on the pages fetched in this pass — treat as unverified rather than certain.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO. The published wording is 'a completed Bachelor of Fine Arts (B.F.A.) degree in Sound, Tonmeister*in or a comparable subject-specific degree'. A BSc Software Engineering is not a 'comparable subject-specific degree' in sound, and the page offers no talent-based or portfolio-based alternative route. The programme page's own phrasing — 'Applicants should have successfully completed the Sound B.F.A. program or have comparable qualifications' — points to the same gate.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED on the official application page: (1) documentation of works and projects from the last three years revealing the applicant's individual artistic position, maximum 12 pages; (2) video material of 15 minutes total length containing AT LEAST THREE FILMS on which the applicant was responsible for sound (excerpts for longer projects; formats MPG, MPEG, MP4, MOV, WMV; max 3.5 GB); (3) at least ONE piece of music the applicant recorded or mixed themselves (WAV, MP3, MP4; max 5 GB).
programs.auditionSpec: YES — mandatory on-site three-part aptitude test, confirmed: Part 1 music test (interval/harmony hearing identification, piano audition, critical audio evaluation); Part 2 interview (presentation and discussion of submitted work plus acoustics/technology knowledge); Part 3 practical exam (scoring a short-film scene in Pro Tools).
programs.applicationOpens: 12 April 2027 (start of the application window for the winter-semester 2027/28 intake)
programs.deadline: 18 May 2027 — CONFIRMED CURRENT, not a prior cycle. The university's central 'Application Deadlines' page publishes '12.04. to 18.05.2027' as the cut-off period for the winter semester 2027/28 master intake, and lists 'Sound Design for Audiovisual Media (MA)' in that group. This is the correct window for a September/October 2027 start.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition fee — Brandenburg public institution, no fees for non-EU students. Semester contribution CONFIRMED at €397.80 per semester (of which €200.00 semester ticket, €17.00 equipment insurance, €4.50 production liability insurance); €422.80 if re-registering late. A separate administrative fee applies to the application itself (amount not published on the pages fetched).
programs.scholarship: No institutional scholarship found. External only: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies, and Deutschlandstipendium. NOTE: DAAD/Tunisia eligibility was NOT re-verified against DAAD in this verification pass — treat as plausible but unconfirmed.
programs.stipend: UNVERIFIED. The university itself pays nothing. DAAD graduate scholarship rates for 2027 not verified in this pass.
programs.facilities: PARTIALLY VERIFIED. Germany's oldest film school (founded 1954) on the historic Babelsberg Studios site in Potsdam; the curriculum's cinema-mix and sound-supervision deliverables confirm theatrical mixing stages and a full film-sound post chain. The specific claim of a 3–5% acceptance rate comes from a secondary source and remains UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Best-in-class for European film sound and the deadline is genuinely published for his cycle — but it is effectively closed to him. He would need a sound/Tonmeister bachelor he does not have, DSH-1 German, and a reel of at least three finished films he has personally mixed. It also trains cinema sound supervisors, not DJs or producers, so even a successful application would point him away from his stated goal. Do not spend application effort here.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed on official pages: programme exists at master level (M.F.A.), 6 semesters/120 LP with the part-time second half explaining the anomaly, winter-term-only entry, the exact prior-degree wording, DSH-1 German requirement, the full three-part work-sample spec, the three-part on-site aptitude test including the Pro Tools practical, the application window 12.04.–18.05.2027 for WS 2027/28 (a genuinely current date, corrected from 'verify — may be an earlier cycle'), no tuition, and the €397.80 semester contribution. NOT confirmed: the audiogram/hearing-certificate requirement (dropped to unverified), the application administrative fee amount, the reported 3–5% acceptance rate, and DAAD Tunisia eligibility. The sourceUrl was upgraded from the overview page to the application page, which is where the admission facts actually live.

programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time, consecutive master. Winter-semester start only.

Software engineering / computer science is NOT on that list. His only conceivable route in is to have the degree accepted as a 'Studiengang mit Medienbezug', which is a stretch for a pure SE degree. He MUST get a written ruling from the Popakademie admissions office before investing in an audition. Previously rated as a clean formal fit — that was too optimistic.

Live-Performance nachgewiesen werden können' — i.e. audio recordings, video/audiovisual material, notated material and possibly a live performance. A secondary source states FIVE titles are required for Producing/Composing (versus three plus a live video, max 200 MB, for the Performing and Educating tracks); that five-track figure is PLAUSIBLE BUT UNVERIFIED on the official page. Assume he needs a polished five-track producer portfolio and confirm the count.
programs.auditionSpec: YES — mandatory live on-site entrance examination. Confirmed components: a practical element (recording session for bass/keys/guitar applicants; a public live performance of up to three pieces totalling max 10 minutes), an ad-hoc examination, and an individual interview with the panel. A WRITTEN THEORY PAPER is also confirmed and is the real hurdle for him: a melodic-harmonic dictation from a song excerpt, questions on song form (identifying sections and bar counts), two questions on arrangement and music production (describing instrumentation and sound effects), PLUS an essay chosen from three topics on popular-music history, pop culture or music business. The entrance exam may be attempted a maximum of two times. Prior-cycle exam dates: 29–30 June 2026.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED. The online application portal opening date is not published; the operative fact is the fixed 30 April cut-off.
programs.deadline: 30 April, annually and fixed — 'Bewerbungsschluss zum Studienbeginn im Wintersemester ist der 30. April', upload complete by 23:59. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for the year: the 2026 cycle ran to 30 April 2026 with the entrance exam on 29–30 June 2026. For a September/October 2027 start he should plan on 30 April 2027 with an exam in late June 2027, and confirm once published.
programs.tuitionIntl: CONFIRMED: the Popakademie is a state Hochschule and charges no tuition for a consecutive master's — BUT under Baden-Württemberg's LHGebG, international students who are not nationals of an EU/EEA member state pay €1,500 PER SEMESTER (in force since winter semester 2017/18). As a Tunisian national he falls under this: approximately €6,000 over four semesters, plus the separate student-services semester contribution (amount not published on the pages fetched — UNVERIFIED).
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (no programme fee, but €1,500/semester non-EU levy; ~€6,000 total)
programs.scholarship: None found at the Popakademie itself. The institution's international page covers exchange and Erasmus+ only and says nothing about fee waivers or scholarships for non-EU degree students. External only: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies, Deutschlandstipendium. DAAD/Tunisia eligibility NOT re-verified in this pass.
programs.facilities: Professional recording studios, SMIX.LAB and a mediathek, confirmed in the programme description; taught by working industry practitioners. Located in Mannheim beside the Musikpark start-up cluster with dense German music-industry links. Individual studio/console specifications UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Still the closest thing in Germany to what he actually wants — real beat programming, electronic production, mixing and mastering, with techno and hip-hop explicitly in scope. But verification made the obstacles bigger, not smaller: (1) the accepted-degree list does not include software engineering or CS, so his eligibility is genuinely in doubt and needs a written ruling first; (2) only 20 places a year across all three tracks; (3) the written theory paper (melodic-harmonic dictation, form analysis, a German-language essay) is a conservatory-style hurdle for someone with no formal music training; (4) German B2 with no confirmation of the 'grace until end of semester' concession; (5) €1,500 per semester. Keep it as his primary German target, but the first action is an eligibility email to admissions, not portfolio work.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed on official Popakademie pages: the programme exists as a 4-semester / 120-ECTS consecutive M.A. with three specialisations including Producing/Composing Artist; 20 study places; winter-semester start; the 30 April upload deadline at 23:59; prior-cycle entrance exam 29–30 June 2026; the practical + ad-hoc + interview + written theory/essay exam structure with the two-attempt limit; the €1,500-per-semester non-EU levy under BW law; German required with DSH/Goethe certificates accepted; the formal 6-semester-degree condition; and the Producing/Composing evidence requirement in German verbatim. CORRECTED: acceptsNonMusic downgraded from a clean 'formal fit' to 'Check' because the Zulassung page publishes a restricted list of accepted degree fields that omits software engineering and CS. programs.program: Filmton / Sounddesign (Diplomaufbaustudium – postgraduate diploma)
programs.university: Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg
programs.institutionType: Public film school (state-owned GmbH; not a Hochschule in the ordinary sense)
programs.degree: Diplom der Filmakademie Baden-Württemberg. IMPORTANT CAVEAT NOW CONFIRMED: this is an institutional diploma, described by the academy as 'vergleichbar berufsbefähigenden Abschlüssen' of state art universities under Baden-Württemberg law — i.e. comparable to a professional qualifying degree. It is NOT an accredited M.A./M.F.A. and the pages do not state an EQF/ECTS master equivalence. If he needs a recognised master's degree (for a visa track, a later PhD, or recognition in Tunisia), verify this in writing first.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters plus 1 diploma semester for the final project = 5 semesters total. ECTS NOT published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.language: German, with English used in Projektstudium ('Deutsch/Englisch im PS'). The academy's general language standard is B2 German (Goethe-Institut, TestDaF level 4, or DSH level 2 accepted). Whether B2 is formally required for this specific Diplomaufbaustudium is not separately stated — assume yes.
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive Audio (Dolby Atmos); production sound
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED: production of the audio layers of film and television. Year 1 concentrates on original sound recording on set; year 2 on post-production. Content includes location recording, sound design, mixing in a DAW, cinema film mixing and Dolby Atmos, working with Foley artists, film-music recording and mixing, and dialogue editing. Optional specialisations in media design and sound for games. Entirely project-based — students work on the academy's own film productions.
programs.entryRequirements: General/subject-specific Hochschulreife (with a talent clause, the 'Begabtenpassus' under §10 of the exam regulations, for applicants without Abitur — an extended interview substitutes). For the Diplomaufbaustudiengänge specifically, an 'entsprechende Vorqualifikation, etwa mindestens ein Vordiplom oder Bachelor' is required, submitted as an officially certified copy. Applicants must bring working knowledge of studio audio technology, microphones and DAW operation. B2 German per the academy's general standard.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — most likely YES, but with one conflicting signal. The programme-overview table requires only 'entsprechende Vorqualifikation, etwa mindestens ein Vordiplom oder Bachelor' with NO subject restriction, and no music degree is anywhere demanded — a BSc Software Engineering satisfies that on its face. However, the general application page summarises Diplomaufbaustudium entry as requiring a 'completed degree in a related field', which introduces a relatedness test that is not defined for Filmton. A software-engineering degree is plausibly 'related' to audio technology, but he must get this confirmed in writing before applying. The decisive filter in practice is the Pro Tools practical exam, not the bachelor subject.
programs.portfolioSpec: PARTIAL. Own projects/work samples are uploaded via the online portal, and applicants must clearly identify their individual contribution to each. Published technical limits (example spec, varies by department): video up to 1 GB, MP4 container, H.264 codec, data rate 15 MB/s, typically 5–7 minutes maximum. The exact number and duration of AUDIO samples required for Filmton/Sounddesign is not published — UNVERIFIED. Also submit certified copies of the Hochschulreife and of any Vordiplom/Diplom/Bachelor/Master.
programs.auditionSpec: YES — pre-selection on the file, then an on-site Aufnahmeprüfung conducted IN PRO TOOLS. Confirmed: 'Die Aufnahmeprüfung für Filmton/Sounddesign wird mit dem Programm Pro Tools durchgeführt. Bewerber*innen sollten daher Grundkenntnisse in den Disziplinen Aufnahme, Sounddesign, Mischung und Bouncing mitbringen.' There is NO instrumental audition and no music-theory paper — the gate is a DAW competence test. This is by far the most learnable audition of the six programmes here.
programs.applicationOpens: The online portal opened 7 January in the current (2026) cycle. Expect a comparable early-January opening for the 2027 cycle — confirm.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 February, annually and without a year published on the programme page. The 2026 cycle ran with a portal opening on 7 January 2026 and the standard 15 February deadline (other departments had later dates: Motion Design 15 May 2026, Werbefilm Producing lateral entry 7 April 2026). For a 2027 start plan on 15 February 2027 and confirm when posted.
programs.tuitionIntl: CORRECTED AND MORE EXPENSIVE THAN RECORDED: the €1,500 is PER SEMESTER, not a one-off. The academy's fee schedule is €0/semester for a first degree, €650/semester for a second degree or Projektstudium, and €1,500/semester for non-EU citizens, plus a €131.50 semester contribution for everyone. As a Tunisian national over 5 semesters that is roughly €7,500 in fees plus ~€658 in contributions — about €8,150 total, before living costs. The Diplomaufbaustudiengänge are exempt from the second-degree fee, but NOT from the non-EU fee.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial at best — in practice closer to self-pay on fees (~€8,150 over 5 semesters) with no institutional funding found.
programs.scholarship: None found at the academy. External only: DAAD Study Scholarships (Film/Fine Art strand), Deutschlandstipendium. DAAD/Tunisia eligibility NOT re-verified in this pass. Note that DAAD art/film scholarships generally target accredited degree programmes, so the non-master status of this Diplom should be checked against DAAD's eligibility rules before counting on it.
programs.facilities: PARTIALLY VERIFIED via the curriculum: cinema film mixing and Dolby Atmos, Foley collaboration, film-music recording and mixing, on-set production-sound equipment, and DAW-based post-production suites are all taught, which confirms the corresponding facilities exist. Detailed room and console specifications UNVERIFIED. The academy is one of Europe's most production-active film schools with heavy German TV/film placement.
programs.fitNotes: The most realistically ENTERABLE film-sound route in Germany for someone without a music degree — the gate is a Pro Tools practical test he can genuinely train for, not a conservatory audition or a theory paper, and no music bachelor is demanded. But verification worsened two things: the fee is €1,500 PER SEMESTER (~€8,150 total, no funding found), and the award is an institutional Diplom rather than an accredited master's. And it makes film and game sound designers, not DJs or producers. Only worth an application if he decides he genuinely wants a screen-audio career alongside producing, and only after confirming both the degree recognition and whether his SE bachelor counts as 'related'.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed on official Filmakademie pages: the programme exists as a Diplomaufbaustudium in Filmton/Sounddesign awarding the Diplom der Filmakademie; 4 semesters + 1 diploma semester; German with English in Projektstudium; the curriculum including Dolby Atmos, Foley, dialogue editing and optional games-sound specialisation; the 15 February deadline (no year); the Pro Tools-based Aufnahmeprüfung with the required prior knowledge of recording, sound design, mixing and bouncing; the video work-sample technical spec (1 GB, MP4, H.264, 15 MB/s); the Hochschulreife requirement with the Begabtenpassus talent clause; B2 German as the academy standard; and the fee schedule. KEY CORRECTIONS: the non-EU fee is €1,500 PER SEMESTER plus €131.50 semester contribution (previously ambiguous), and the Diplom is officially described only as 'comparable to professional qualifying degrees' of state art universities rather than as an accredited master. NOT confirmed: ECTS, the audio work-sample count and duration, the 2027 portal opening date, whether a software-engineering BSc satisfies the 'related field' phrasing, and DAAD eligibility for a non-accredited Diplom.

programs.program: Zeitabhängige Medien / Sound – Vision (M.A.) — the Sound–Vision branch of Sound–Vision–Games
programs.university: HAW Hamburg – Hochschule für Angewandte Wissenschaften Hamburg, Dept. Medientechnik
programs.institutionType: University of applied sciences (public)
programs.durationEcts: 3 semesters. The official HAW page and the DAAD entry both state 3 semesters and neither prints the ECTS figure; German programme databases give 90 ECTS, which is consistent with 210 + 90 = 300 ECTS. Treat 90 ECTS as PARTIAL-verified.
programs.language: German. CONFIRMED verbatim: 'International applicants are required to demonstrate proficiency in the German language at level C1 in the Common European Framework of Reference for Languages.' English at B1 is additionally tested during the interview. C1 is the highest German bar of the six programmes here.
programs.focus: Sound Design; Immersive/media audio; Recording & audio technology; video/lighting and event technology (this is media technology, not music production)
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED as project-centred study at the intersection of science, technology and creative design, combining sound and moving image as the central means of expression in film, video and music production as well as event and performance technology. Modules span audio technology and sound design, video technology and image design, VFX, interactive design, lighting technology and design, and production/project management. The parallel Games branch covers concept art, 3D animation, level and game design and interactive programming with industry partners. Graduates go to audio/video/lighting manufacturers, production studios and theatres. Nationally distinctive in linking sound, moving image and games in one degree.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed Bachelor's or Diplom degree with a MINIMUM OF 210 ECTS in 'media technology, media systems, computer science, IT (applicants with a degree in applied IT or with a specialism in media are welcome), communication design, illustration or a related subject'; German C1; English B1 (tested at interview); and a passed aptitude assessment. A rating of 3.0 or better in part 2 of the aptitude assessment qualifies for admission.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly, and this is the single best formal fit of the six. The accepted-degree list names 'computer science, IT (applicants with a degree in applied IT or with a specialism in media are welcome)' by name. THE REAL GATE IS CREDITS, NOT SUBJECT: the minimum is 210 ECTS. A three-year 180-ECTS bachelor is short by a full semester; a four-year US-style BSc such as SMU MedTech's is likely to clear 210, but he must obtain a formal ECTS credit statement from SMU MedTech and, if short, ask HAW how the shortfall can be made up. No music background of any kind is required and there is no instrumental audition.
programs.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED to less specific than previously recorded. The official page states only: 'A sample of your work that provides a detailed and comprehensive demonstration of your interest in and your aptitude and potential for your chosen branch of the degree course.' The page does NOT publish a number range, and the previously recorded 'between 3 and 10 work samples' with the enumerated accepted media types (video, animation, light design, installation, soundscape, music production, performance, interactive work) could NOT be confirmed in this pass — treat the count and the media list as UNVERIFIED and request the current Arbeitsproben specification from the Fakultät DMI in writing.
programs.auditionSpec: NO live audition and no music-theory test. Two-stage Eignungsfeststellung, confirmed: 'Part 1: Submission of a sample of your work' — reviewed by the selection committee in early November — and 'Part 2: Interview, to which you will be invited if your performance in Part 1 merits it.' German C1 and English B1 are verified at the interview. A grade of 3.0 or better in part 2 qualifies for admission.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 October — registration for the aptitude test opens. CONFIRMED CURRENT: the DAAD database publishes the window as '01.10.2026 – 31.10.2026' for the aptitude test, i.e. the live window for the April 2027 intake opens in about ten weeks.
programs.deadline: TWO-STEP AND PARTLY CURRENT. Step 1, aptitude-test registration with work samples: 1–31 October, confirmed as 01.10.2026 – 31.10.2026 for the next intake (one secondary source says 'until 14 October' — resolve this discrepancy with the faculty before relying on the end of the month). Step 2, formal application for the study place: 1 December – 15 January. CRITICAL: entry is SUMMER SEMESTER ONLY, starting early April. There is no September/October intake at all. His options are April 2027 (register Oct 2026, apply Dec 2026–Jan 2027 — very tight, and impossible at C1 German from a standing start) or April 2028.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition fee for anyone, including non-EU students — DAAD confirms international students pay the same as domestic students with no additional tuition. Semester contribution: the official HAW page states €397 including the semester ticket and the Germany-wide Deutschlandticket rail pass; the DAAD entry states 'currently EUR 335.60'. Take €397 as the current figure from the university's own page and expect minor annual variation. This is the cheapest option of the six.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free; total institutional cost ~€397 per semester, ~€1,191 over three semesters)
programs.scholarship: No institutional scholarship found. External only: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines, Deutschlandstipendium. DAAD/Tunisia eligibility NOT re-verified in this pass. Note DAAD funding conventionally starts 1 October, which sits awkwardly with an April intake — check whether DAAD will fund a summer-semester start.
programs.facilities: PARTIALLY VERIFIED. Located on the Art and Media Campus Finkenau in Hamburg; the curriculum confirms audio, video and lighting laboratories and studios for sound design and interactive media. Specific equipment, studio counts and immersive-audio provision UNVERIFIED beyond the campus and module descriptions.
programs.fitNotes: Structurally the friendliest German public option for a software-engineering graduate — computer science and IT are named as welcome, there is no audition or theory paper, and the total institutional cost is about €397 a semester. But three real obstacles stack up against his stated plan: German C1 is the highest language bar on this list; the 210-ECTS minimum may formally exclude his degree and must be checked with a credit statement; and there is NO September intake, so September 2027 is impossible — realistically April 2028, with the October 2026 window arriving too soon. It is also media and event technology rather than club-music production, so even on success it would not directly serve a DJ/producer career.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed on the official HAW page and the DAAD programme database: the programme exists as an M.A., 3 semesters, summer-semester-only entry in early April, German C1 for international applicants with English B1 tested at interview, the accepted-degree list naming computer science and IT explicitly, the 210-ECTS minimum, the two-part aptitude assessment (work sample then interview), the 1–31 October aptitude-test registration window confirmed as 01.10.2026–31.10.2026 for the next intake, the 1 December–15 January formal application window, no tuition for international students, and the €397 semester contribution including the Deutschlandticket. CORRECTED: the '3 to 10 work samples' specification and the enumerated list of accepted media types are NOT on the official page and are now marked unverified. NOTED DISCREPANCIES: semester contribution €397 (HAW) vs €335.60 (DAAD); aptitude registration to 31 October (HAW/DAAD) vs 'until 14 October' (secondary source). ECTS total of 90 is database-sourced. The /en/master-sound-vision-games/ URL 404'd during this pass; the Sound–Vision page is the correct live source and has been kept.

programs.program: Integrative Komposition (M.Mus.) – specialisation Elektronische Komposition (taught at the ICEM)
programs.university: Folkwang Universität der Künste
programs.institutionType: Public art university (music, theatre, dance, design)
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED: '4 semesters full-time (part-time study is possible)' totalling '120 ECTS Credits'.
programs.language: German. CONFIRMED: applicants must 'verify proof of language level B1 with enrolment' (CEFR). B1 at enrolment — not at application — is the lowest language bar of the six programmes here and the single most achievable language requirement on this list.
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; electroacoustic composition; Sonic Arts (also pop composition as a combinable field)
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED: a project-oriented master built around the student's own artistic development project, with the study plan divided into composition/project work, seminars, tutorials and the thesis. Four combinable compositional fields — instrumental composition, ELECTRONIC composition, jazz composition, pop composition, and composition & visualisation — which students may weight differently and ideally combine. A major elective area from the whole Integrative Komposition offering lets students build the specific skills their project needs. Electronic composition is taught at the ICEM (Institut für Computermusik und Elektronische Medien). Admission is offered for both winter semester (start of October) and summer semester (start of April) — the October start aligns with his September 2027 target.
programs.entryRequirements: Quoted from the official page: 'Evidence of a first university degree which the Master study course is based on', plus evidence of 'artistic aptitude or outstanding artistic talent respectively by passing the aptitude test'. Foreign qualifications are checked against anabin. German B1 at enrolment. €50 application fee.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — the previous 'Yes, in practice' was too confident and has been downgraded. The requirement is a first university degree 'WHICH THE MASTER STUDY COURSE IS BASED ON' — that relatedness clause is doing real work and is not obviously satisfied by a BSc Software Engineering. The 'outstanding artistic talent' language is NOT a substitute for the degree: on the university's central aptitude-test page, artistic excellence substituting for a missing formal qualification (via an aptitude grade of at least 1.7) is described for UNDERGRADUATE programmes where applicants lack the university entrance qualification — not for master's admission. So there is no confirmed talent route around the degree requirement at master level. That said, no MUSIC degree is explicitly demanded and the aptitude test is a portfolio-plus-colloquium rather than an instrumental audition, so an electronic-composition portfolio may well carry a technical degree. He must obtain a written eligibility ruling from Folkwang before committing.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED: own compositions submitted as sheet music in PDF (especially for instrumental composition), and sound and video files in MP4 — files 'ideally smaller than 25 MB and no larger than 100 MB'. PLUS a concept / project plan for an artistic development project describing the intended artistic examination outcome (effectively a master-project proposal). No fixed number of works is published. The project concept is as important as the music and is where a non-music applicant can differentiate.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage Eignungsprüfung with a MANDATORY IN-PERSON second round. Stage 1: digital preliminary round in which the submitted compositions and the project proposal are assessed. Stage 2: in-person main round of approximately 30 minutes, consisting of a colloquium on the submitted works, artistic development and engagement with current artistic trends. Folkwang's central rules confirm that personal attendance is compulsory in nearly all programmes and that virtual participation is not permitted — so he must budget for travel to Essen. The test may be repeated an unlimited number of times and a pass remains valid for the following semester. No instrumental audition and no separate written theory paper are published for this programme. Prior-cycle exam dates: 11–15 May 2026 for the winter intake, 19–23 January 2026 for the summer intake.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED (no portal opening date published; the operative facts are the fixed 15 March / 15 November cut-offs).
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 15 March for the following winter semester, 15 November for the following summer semester — both published without a year. The 2026 cycle is confirmed as 15 March 2026 for a winter semester 2026/27 start, with the aptitude exam 11–15 May 2026. By the same pattern, a September/October 2027 start means applying by 15 March 2027 with an on-site aptitude test around May 2027 — confirm when the 2027 dates are posted. A few Folkwang programmes have later deadlines (31 May, 15 June), but Integrative Komposition is on the 15 March date.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition fee — 'No tuition fees are charged at Folkwang', NRW public art university, and no non-EU levy exists in NRW. Costs are the €50 application fee (confirmed) plus the semester social contribution to the Studierendenwerk including the NRW/Deutschland semester ticket — exact amount NOT published on the pages fetched, UNVERIFIED.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free; €50 application fee plus an unquantified semester contribution)
programs.scholarship: No institutional scholarship found. External only: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for Artists (Music strand) and Deutschlandstipendium. DAAD/Tunisia eligibility NOT re-verified in this pass.
programs.facilities: PARTIALLY VERIFIED. Electronic composition is taught within the ICEM (Institut für Computermusik und Elektronische Medien), which is confirmed as the institutional home of the electronic-composition field within Integrative Komposition. The specific claims of a live-electronic studio operating since 1971, a historic technical instrument collection, and regular PACT Zollverein collaborations were NOT re-verified in this pass — treat as UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: On paper the most open door of the six for someone with no music degree, and the cheapest realistic route to a real master's: tuition-free, German only at B1 and only at enrolment, a winter start that matches September/October 2027, a 15 March 2027 application, and an assessment that rests on a portfolio plus a project concept rather than an instrumental audition or a theory paper. Two honest caveats. First, eligibility is not confirmed: the degree must be one 'which the Master study course is based on', and the outstanding-talent clause does NOT substitute for a degree at master level, so he needs a written ruling from Folkwang. Second, this is art-music electronic composition — electroacoustic work, live electronics, installation, with pop composition available as a combinable field — not dance-floor production. He would have to frame his work as compositional practice, and the pop-composition field is the bridge worth asking about. Best combination of openness, cost and timing on this list, but rated B rather than A because his formal eligibility is unresolved and the artistic register is not his own.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed on official Folkwang pages: the M.Mus. Integrative Komposition exists with 4 semesters full-time (part-time possible) and 120 ECTS; the four combinable compositional fields including electronic composition; admission in both winter (October start) and summer (April start) semesters; German B1 verified at enrolment; the €50 application fee; no tuition fees at Folkwang; the 15 March (winter) and 15 November (summer) deadlines without a year, with the 2026 cycle confirmed as 15 March 2026 for WS 2026/27; the aptitude exam dates 11–15 May 2026 and 19–23 January 2026; the portfolio spec (PDF scores, MP4 audio and video, ideally under 25 MB and no larger than 100 MB) plus the required artistic-development project concept; and the two-round aptitude test with an approximately 30-minute in-person colloquium and compulsory personal attendance. KEY CORRECTION: acceptsNonMusic downgraded from 'Yes, in practice' to 'Check'. The 'outstanding artistic talent' route is not an alternative to holding a degree at master level — the central aptitude-test page describes talent (aptitude grade 1.7 or better) as substituting for a MISSING UNIVERSITY ENTRANCE QUALIFICATION in undergraduate programmes, and the master requirement remains 'a first university degree which the Master study course is based on', a relatedness test a software-engineering BSc may not pass. NOT confirmed: the semester social contribution amount, the portal opening date, the ICEM historical and PACT Zollverein claims, and DAAD Tunisia eligibility.

programs.program: Audio Communication and Sonology (double degree with the Institute of Sonology, Royal Conservatoire The Hague)
programs.university: Technische Universität Berlin – Fachgebiet Audiokommunikation (with Royal Conservatoire The Hague)
programs.institutionType: Public technical university + partner conservatory (University of the Arts The Hague)
programs.degree: Double degree, confirmed verbatim: "a Master of Science from the TU Berlin and a Master of Music in Sonology from the Royal Conservatoire"
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS. Confirmed split: year 1 = 60 ECTS (39 mandatory + 21 elective, taken from the Audio Communication and Technology M.Sc. in Berlin); year 2 = 60 ECTS (30 research project + 20 mandatory + 10 elective) at the Institute of Sonology. Start: winter semester (October).
programs.language: CORRECTED — this is the blocker. The double-degree page states German "at least on level TDN 4 / TestDaF" and English "at least on a level equivalent to the evaluation scales IELTS (6,0) or TOEFL (ibT level 83)". BUT the parent programme page (Audio Communication and Technology M.Sc.) states: "The main language of instruction in the Master's programme is German" and, for applicants with foreign qualifications, German at "C1 for admission" plus English at B2. Year 2 in The Hague is English: "The studies will be conducted in English and applicants are expected to be adequately fluent with the language." He has zero German.
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Immersive/Spatial Audio; Electroacoustic Composition; Sonic Arts — plus hard audio engineering
programs.whatYouStudy: Year 1 in Berlin: the mandatory 39 ECTS + 21 ECTS elective core of the Audio Communication and Technology M.Sc. — signal processing, electroacoustics, room and virtual acoustics, music informatics, spatial audio. Year 2 at the Institute of Sonology: a 30-ECTS research project plus 20 ECTS mandatory and 10 ECTS elective — electronic/electroacoustic composition, live electronics, sound synthesis research, algorithmic composition, sound art. Output is spatial-audio research and electroacoustic composition, not club-oriented production.
programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED and expanded from the parent programme page: "A first university degree in science, engineering, humanities, social science, arts, business or law", plus "knowledge of higher mathematics (analysis, linear algebra) at the level of the basic lectures of a science or engineering degree (at least 10 LP)" and knowledge of a programming language or computer algebra system. German C1 (foreign qualifications), English B2. Admission is listed as "Open admission" — NO numerus clausus (the original claim of an NC is WRONG). A research project proposal must be submitted. The Sonology side additionally requires a portfolio and a two-page study plan.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — strongly. TU Berlin side: "A first university degree in science, engineering, humanities, social science, arts, business or law" with higher mathematics (≥10 LP) and programming. Sonology side explicitly lists as relevant backgrounds "related subjects such as artificial intelligence, computer science or electronic engineering". A BSc Software Engineering is an asset on both sides.
programs.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED — the Sonology requirement is now confirmed and it IS a portfolio. TU Berlin side: a research project proposal must be submitted with the application; no music portfolio published. Royal Conservatoire / Sonology side: "Students for the Master of Music in Sonology are selected on the basis of a portfolio with previous compositions, sound installations, recordings of live performances or research results in the form of computer programs, articles, theses, etc." plus "a two-page study plan" covering the proposed project, a four-semester timeline, research methodology with central questions, and thesis subjects. No fixed number or duration of works is published.
programs.auditionSpec: No live audition anywhere in the chain. TU Berlin selection is document- and proposal-based. Royal Conservatoire states explicitly: "There is no live admission exam." programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — not published on either page.

Specific room/console inventory not published on either page — UNVERIFIED.

Three real problems: (1) the Berlin year is taught mainly in German and the parent programme demands C1 for foreign qualifications — he has none; (2) year 2 costs €11,488 as a non-EEA student, so it is not the near-free option it first appears; (3) it produces spatial-audio researchers and electroacoustic composers, not DJs. Also unresolved: the TDN 4 (double degree page) vs C1 (parent programme page) German discrepancy — this must be clarified in writing before he invests in German study.

programs.program: Professional Media Creation (M.A.)
programs.university: SAE Institute Germany — degree awarded by Folkwang Universität der Künste
programs.city: Bochum (mandatory weekend blocks); elective modules at SAE campuses including Berlin, Hamburg, Cologne, Munich, Frankfurt, Stuttgart, Leipzig, Hannover, Nürnberg
programs.institutionType: Private specialist audio/media academy in partnership with a public art university
programs.degree: M.A. (Master of Arts), state-recognised, awarded by Folkwang Universität der Künste
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED 2 years / 120 ECTS, of which 30 ECTS electives and 90 ECTS project/coursework. October intake.
programs.language: German. The page addresses a "deutschsprachig" (German-speaking) audience and the programme is delivered in German. No English track. He has no German — this is the decisive obstacle.
programs.focus: Music Production; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Sonic Arts — project-based and cross-media rather than music-specific
programs.whatYouStudy: Project-driven artistic master spanning music, film, video art, installation, sound art, photography and game art, built around a single self-defined artistic master project. Core modules cover artistic practice, project planning, narration, contract law, marketing and event management; electives cover audio, video, multimedia and lighting plus perceptual psychology, design, real-time systems and media history. Mandatory modules run as weekend blocks in Bochum, so part-time work alongside is feasible. Delivered with Folkwang's ICEM (Institute for Computer Music and Electronic Media).
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED: a "berufsqualifizierender Hochschulabschluss" (professionally qualifying higher-education degree) with a minimum of 180 ECTS, plus an assessment of artistic aptitude. No subject restriction is published.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes. The only degree condition published is a "Berufsqualifizierender Hochschulabschluss" with at least 180 ECTS — no subject restriction whatsoever, and no music degree is mentioned. His BSc Software Engineering qualifies formally; admission then turns on the artistic project concept and the colloquium.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED in substance but not in quantity: applicants submit "eine schriftlich verfasste Idee für ein künstlerisches Masterprojekt" (a written idea for an artistic master project). The commission at the colloquium then evaluates that proposal together with prior artistic work and creative vision. No number of works, duration, format or file specification is published — UNVERIFIED, must be requested from SAE Bochum admissions.
programs.auditionSpec: No performance audition. Selection is by colloquium with SAE and Folkwang representatives, assessing the written project concept and previous creative work. The colloquium is presumably on-site in Bochum and presumably conducted in German — confirm both.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — not published.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no application deadline is published on the official page. Intake is every October, so a September/October 2027 start means applying during roughly late 2026 to mid-2027. Must be confirmed with SAE Bochum admissions.
programs.tuitionIntl: Self-pay, CONFIRMED: €400 enrolment fee, then either 24 monthly instalments of €485 (€11,640) or 4 semester prepayments of €2,838 (€11,352). Total roughly €11,750–€12,040. The page mentions BAföG, education loans and income-contingent study financing as options — none of which a newly arrived Tunisian national can normally access.
programs.scholarship: None found for non-EU students. The degree is awarded by Folkwang Universität der Künste (a state art university), so DAAD Study Scholarships might in principle be argued — but the delivery is by a private provider and DAAD has not been confirmed to fund it. Do not rely on this without written confirmation from DAAD.
programs.facilities: SAE operates one of the largest audio-education networks worldwide and its German campuses are equipped audio/studio facilities; elective modules can also be taken with Folkwang and its ICEM computer-music institute. No console, control-room or immersive-room inventory is published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: On paper the most accessible formal qualification in this batch: a genuine state-university M.A., no audition, no subject restriction, only 180 ECTS needed — his degree clears the bar exactly. But three things sink it for him right now: it is taught entirely in German, it costs about €12,000 entirely out of pocket with no non-EU funding route confirmed, and the content is broad cross-media project work delivered in weekend blocks in Bochum rather than music-production drilling in a music city. Keep as a labelled self-pay fallback only if he first acquires German.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed on the official SAE page: M.A. awarded by Folkwang Universität der Künste, 2 years / 120 ECTS with a 30/90 ECTS split, Bochum location, German-language delivery, the 180-ECTS "berufsqualifizierender Hochschulabschluss" entry rule with no subject restriction, the written artistic master-project idea, the colloquium-based selection with no performance audition, and the exact fee structure (€400 + 24×€485 or 4×€2,838). NOT confirmed: any application deadline or opening date (none published), the precise portfolio specification (number/length/format of works), whether the colloquium is on-site and in German, and whether DAAD funding can be applied to a private-provider delivery of a Folkwang degree. Contact SAE Bochum admissions for the deadline and portfolio spec.

programs.program: Medienkunst/Mediengestaltung (Media Art and Design) – M.F.A.
programs.university: Bauhaus-Universität Weimar, Faculty of Art and Design
programs.institutionType: Public art and design university
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED: "two semesters for applicants with a previous Bachelor qualification of at least eight semesters and 240 ECTS points". Applicants holding 180–210 ECTS must take additional bridge semesters — so with his 180-ECTS BSc, realistically 3–4 semesters.
programs.language: AMBIGUOUS AND UNRESOLVED — treat as a red flag. The programme page describes an English-language curriculum (fully English only in Interface Design; "other chairs offer partial English-language course programmes") and states German A2 plus English C1 ("TOEFL min. 95 points or IELTS min. grade 7.0"). The Faculty of Art and Design's own application page, however, states that international applicants must demonstrate German at C1 level, accepting "DSH-2 or TestDaF TDN 4", with proof that the level will be reached by matriculation at the latest. These two official pages contradict each other and the difference is decisive for him.
programs.focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based); Electroacoustic Composition; Sound Design (experimental radio, acoustic ecologies)
programs.whatYouStudy: Project- and experimentation-driven MFA combining creative, analytical and critical work with organisation and technology. Six professorships shape the sound side: Electroacoustic Composition, Experimental Radio, Acoustic Ecologies, Media Environments, Interface Design and Media Events — an unusually dense cluster of sound chairs in one art faculty. Applicants must name a planned master topic in the motivation letter, and the degree is built around that self-defined project. Output is sound art, experimental radio and installation rather than commercial production.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED: "Either a Bachelor of Fine Arts degree in Media Art and Design from the Faculty of Art and Design or a first university degree recognized as professionally relevant by the responsible examination committee"; the standard period assumes 240 ECTS / 8 semesters; German A2 and English C1 per the programme page (but see the C1-German conflict above); a passed aptitude test; an artistic portfolio; a motivation letter of about one A4 page naming the desired focus and planned master topic; CV and prior certificates. Applications run "exclusively conducted digitally via the Bauhaus.CampusPortal" — NOT uni-assist.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — not guaranteed. The published wording is "a first university degree recognized as professionally relevant by the responsible examination committee", so relevance is judged case by case on the portfolio. A software-engineering BSc with a strong media-art portfolio is arguable but nothing on the page promises it, and the 240-ECTS expectation is a second, separate hurdle that would add bridge semesters.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED verbatim: "Artistic portfolio, i.e. a compilation of own artistic/creative works (formats: PDF (max. 20 MB); if applicable, links to hosted interactive or time-based works [Soundcloud, Vimeo, Github, private website, etc.])". No fixed number of works, no duration limits. Plus a motivation letter of about one A4 page stating the desired study focus and planned master topic, a CV and prior academic certificates.
programs.auditionSpec: No live audition. An aptitude test decided on the submitted portfolio and documents by the examination committee. CORRECTED: the official page states "A personal interview is usually not a compulsory part of the procedure" — so an interview is the exception, not the norm. Results are announced some weeks after the deadline.
programs.applicationOpens: 2 February — "Registrations for the aptitude tests are possible from – attention NEW – 2 February of the year" (recurring annual date; confirm for 2027).
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: the published recurring pattern is aptitude-test registration from 2 February, complete application with all documents uploaded by 31 March, successful applicants enrol online by 30 September, winter-semester start only. For a September/October 2027 start expect 2 February – 31 March 2027, but the 2027 dates are not yet published.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition fees. Confirmed wording: "No tuition fees, however enrolled students must pay a semester contribution fee." Thuringia charges no non-EU tuition. The contribution is not stated on the programme page; the university's Semesterbeitrag page indicates €338.20 for winter semester 2026/27, plus a one-off €20 Thoska card fee for new students (≈€358.20 in the first semester) — amount taken from the university fee page rather than the programme page, so treat as indicative.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships (the artists/designers strand for Fine Art, Design, Film, plus the all-disciplines strand); Deutschlandstipendium. Tunisia is a DAAD partner country. No programme-specific scholarship is published.
programs.stipend: DAAD Study Scholarships pay €992 per month for master's studies, for the standard period of study up to 24 months, normally starting 1 October, plus travel and insurance allowances. Deutschlandstipendium amount not confirmed for this university — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Bauhaus heritage institution; the Experimental Radio, Electroacoustic Composition and Acoustic Ecologies chairs run their own studio and broadcast infrastructure. No equipment inventory is published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The attractive parts are real: tuition-free, portfolio-only admission, no audition, no compulsory interview, and a genuine cluster of six sound professorships. But for him specifically it stacks up badly. He needs IELTS 7.0 (a full band above the IELTS 6.0 most programmes ask, and he has not sat the test); his 180-ECTS BSc falls short of the 240-ECTS assumption and would trigger bridge semesters; "professionally relevant" is a discretionary judgement his CS degree may not survive without a substantial media-art portfolio he does not yet have; and the two official pages disagree on whether he also needs German C1. On top of that the output is sound art and experimental radio, not production or DJing. Worth a written enquiry to the faculty about the German level and the ECTS gap before spending any effort.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed on the official programme page: M.F.A. title, "two semesters for applicants with a previous Bachelor qualification of at least eight semesters and 240 ECTS points" with bridge semesters for 180–210 ECTS, English-language curriculum with only Interface Design fully in English, German A2 and English C1 (TOEFL 95 / IELTS 7.0), the "BFA ... or a first university degree recognized as professionally relevant" entry rule, the exact portfolio wording and 20 MB PDF limit, the aptitude test, the 2 February / 31 March / 30 September dates, and "No tuition fees, however enrolled students must pay a semester contribution fee." Cross-checked the Faculty of Art and Design application page: Bauhaus.CampusPortal only (not uni-assist), and — CONFLICTING with the programme page — German C1 (DSH-2 or TestDaF TDN 4) for international applicants. CORRECTED from the original record: an interview is described as "usually not a compulsory part of the procedure", not a likely one. NOT confirmed on an official programme page: the semester contribution amount (€338.20 for WS 2026/27 comes from the university's Semesterbeitrag page), the Deutschlandstipendium amount, studio/equipment detail, and the 2027 cycle dates. The German-level contradiction is unresolved and material.

programs.program: Mediale Künste (Media Arts) – Diplom 2, postgraduate (MFA-equivalent), with Klangkunst / sound focus
programs.university: Kunsthochschule für Medien Köln (KHM)
programs.institutionType: Public art school (media arts academy)
programs.degree: Diplom 2 — postgraduate diploma. Official designation "Diploma 1 + 2 / Media and Fine Art"; KHM states it is "internationally comparable with a MFA (Master of Fine Art)".
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED 4 semesters for the Diplom 2 postgraduate course (Diplom 1 is the 9-semester undergraduate course). ECTS are not published anywhere on the application pages — UNVERIFIED. Winter-semester start only: "Courses always begin in the winter semester".
programs.language: German. CONFIRMED: "current german language certificate, at least A2" at application, and "good knowledge of the German language (Goethe-Institut level B2)" which must be "submitted at the latest when you enrol". Certificates from other providers are accepted "provided that the language tests correspond to the Common European Framework". So A2 to apply, B2 to enrol — a staged requirement, which is the gentlest German ramp in this batch.
programs.focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based); Sound Design; Electronic Music
programs.whatYouStudy: Free, project-based artistic study: students choose and combine their own artistic focal points, supervised across disciplines by professors and technical staff, with the individually developed artistic project at the centre of the degree. Klangkunst (sound art) is an available specialisation, delivered through the KHM's Klanglabor — project-oriented practice plus seminars, lectures, practical exercises and work presentations engaging current sound discourse. Note this is art-school sound practice, not mixdown-and-master training.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED for Diplom 2: a general higher-education entrance qualification plus a completed "higher-education degree in a relevant area of study. This could include courses in art/design as well as theatre, film and television theory, literature, art and cultural sciences as well as IT and engineering sciences". Alternative route: "general higher-education entrance qualification and at least two years of work experience in an artistic/design field". German A2 at application, Goethe B2 at enrolment. Work samples plus a project proposal must be submitted.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly. The accepted prior fields for Diplom 2 include "IT and engineering sciences" alongside art/design, theatre/film/TV theory, literature and cultural sciences. No music degree is required and none is mentioned. His BSc Software Engineering is directly in scope, which makes this the only programme in this batch where his background is named as qualifying and no ECTS shortfall is raised.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED: work samples of artistic/design work — the categories named are "videos/films, photographs, computer graphics/animation, drawings, texts, compositions, music videos". For Diplom 2 additionally "a project proposal is to be prepared"; the "project outline can be a text (usually two to three pages) or ... act around a sketch". No fixed number of works and no durations are specified — UNVERIFIED, worth confirming with the application office along with submission format.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition, no multi-stage examination, and no interview is mentioned on the application page. Selection is by commission: "artistic aptitude ... determined by a commission based on the submitted work samples". (Whether shortlisted applicants are in practice interviewed is UNVERIFIED.) Note the Diplom 1 undergraduate route does involve interpreting "a given theme in artistic and written work" — that task is not part of the Diplom 2 route.
programs.applicationOpens: mid-October — "application period is from mid October to January/February".
programs.deadline: Forward-looking and favourable: the page states "The application deadline for the winter semester 2026 is finished", and "Courses always begin in the winter semester", with the "application period ... from mid October to January/February". For a winter-semester-2027 start that means applying from roughly mid-October 2026 to January/February 2027 — exactly his target window. The precise 2027 closing date is not yet published: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition. Semester contribution only: the page gives "approximately 375 Euro per semester" in one place and "approx. 400 euros per semester" in the FAQ. It covers "semester ticket (valid throughout North Rhine-Westphalia on buses, trains and local trains), as well as contributions for the student union and insurance". Total cost of the degree in fees is therefore roughly €1,500–1,600 over four semesters.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free; ~€375–400 per semester, all-in, including an NRW-wide transport ticket)
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships (artists/designers strand for Fine Art, Design, Film, plus the all-disciplines strand); Deutschlandstipendium. Tunisia is a DAAD partner country. KHM's own scholarship/support schemes for enrolled students: UNVERIFIED — not published on the application page.
programs.stipend: DAAD Study Scholarships pay €992 per month for master's-level studies, for the standard period of study up to 24 months, normally beginning 1 October, plus travel and insurance allowances. KHM internal scholarships: UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Klanglabor (sound laboratory) and the exMedia sound area, plus full media-arts production infrastructure for film, video and computer graphics, in Cologne — Germany's media capital, home to WDR and a deep electronic-music history. Specific equipment inventory not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The best-fitting programme in this batch, and the only one that is not effectively blocked. It names "IT and engineering sciences" as a qualifying background, admission is decided on work samples plus a two-to-three-page project outline with no audition and no interview requirement, it costs about €375–400 per semester all in (transport ticket included), and its next application window — mid-October 2026 to January/February 2027 — lands exactly on his target. Two honest caveats: German B2 by enrolment, which means starting German now and sustaining it for a year; and the framing is art school, so he would be making sound art in the Klanglabor rather than learning club-ready mixdowns. Take it if he wants Cologne, a recognised credential, near-zero cost and creative freedom — not if he wants production drills.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed on the official KHM English application page: Diplom 2 is a 4-semester postgraduate course "internationally comparable with a MFA (Master of Fine Art)"; entry requires a higher-education degree in a relevant field explicitly including "IT and engineering sciences", with a two-years'-artistic-work-experience alternative; German A2 at application and Goethe-level B2 by enrolment; work samples in the named categories plus a two-to-three-page project outline or sketch; selection by commission on the work samples with no exam, audition or interview described; application period mid-October to January/February with winter-semester start only and the winter-2026 deadline already closed; fees of approximately €375 (main text) to €400 (FAQ) per semester covering the NRW semester ticket, student union and insurance. NOT confirmed: ECTS credit value (not published), the exact number/duration/format of required work samples, whether shortlisted applicants are interviewed in practice, KHM's own scholarship schemes, and the precise 2027 closing date. Sound-focus and Klanglabor details were not re-confirmed on this application page and should be checked against the exMedia/Klanglabor pages.

programs.program: Audiovisual Media Creation and Technology (M.Sc.), profile 3D Audio and Music Technology
programs.university: Hochschule der Medien Stuttgart (HdM)
programs.institutionType: Public university of applied sciences (media)
programs.degree: M.Sc. (Master of Science). Note the naming confusion: HdM's current programme pages give "Audiovisual Media Creation and Technology (M. Sc.)", while an older/parallel HdM page presents "Audiovisuelle Medien (M. Eng.)" with essentially the same admission rules — confirm with the programme office which title is awarded for a 2027 intake.
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED 3 semesters / 90 ECTS: 50 ECTS compulsory, 20 ECTS profile-specific and elective modules, and the master's thesis with research phase in semester 3. Winter-semester intake only ("Admission: Winter semester").
programs.language: German — CORRECTED and more severe than previously recorded. The programme page states "German (partly English)" and the German programme site lists the language as "Deutsch". HdM's admission page for the programme requires international applicants to provide "Nachweis über ihre sprachlichen Fähigkeiten in Deutsch" at C1 level, accepting specifically Telc C1, TestDaF 16 points, or Goethe-Zertifikat C1. This is a hard C1 requirement, not merely "proof of German".
programs.focus: Immersive/Spatial Audio; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Music Technology
programs.whatYouStudy: Three profiles: 3D Audio and Music Technology, Visual Media Creation, and Computer-Generated Imagery, each with mandatory core modules plus electives. The programme combines research, design and engineering, with students developing audiovisual concepts, prototypical media applications and scientific solutions for the media industry. The 3D Audio and Music Technology profile works on current audio-technology questions with a focus on 3D audio applied to sound design, radio drama (Hörspiel) and interactive audio installations, in modern studios. Engineering- and research-flavoured, not track production.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED and stricter than previously recorded: an internationally recognised first degree (Bachelor, Diplom, First State Exam or equivalent); the programme "builds on a bachelor's degree in media technology or design" and expects approximately 210 ECTS — with fewer credits "eine individuelle Prüfung hinsichtlich der Anerkennung von Kompetenzen" (individual competency review) is carried out, with up to 30 ECTS potentially credited. Applicants must evidence at least 15 ECTS in engineering fundamentals ("Mathematik, Informatik, Physik, Nachrichtentechnik, Elektronik") AND at least 15 ECTS in media-related applications ("visuelle Gestaltung, Bild-/Ton-/Textkonzeption, Sounddesign"). German C1. The NC "lay in recent years approximately in the range of 2.2" (German grading), varying annually.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — half yes, half no. No music degree is required and the FAQ lists many qualifying bachelors from engineering, film and design fields "oder andere ähnlich geartete Studiengänge/Hochschulen", so non-media backgrounds are not excluded outright. His BSc easily covers the 15 ECTS in engineering fundamentals (mathematics, informatics). The problem is the second, equally mandatory 15 ECTS in media-related applications — visual design, image/sound/text conception, sound design — which a software-engineering curriculum almost certainly does not contain, plus a 180-vs-210 ECTS shortfall triggering an individual competency review. Formally arguable, practically weak without documented media/sound coursework.
programs.portfolioSpec: No artistic portfolio is required — CONFIRMED. Optional supporting documents can improve the procedure grade by up to 0.5 grade points: a motivation letter of maximum 2 pages, evidence of two or more years of post-bachelor professional experience, letters of recommendation from universities or employers, and evidence of engagement in politics, culture, sport or social activities.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition, aptitude test or on-site examination is published. Admission is document- and grade-based (NC around 2.2 in recent years) via the HdM application portal.
programs.deadline: 15 July for the winter semester, per the official programme page ("15. Juli"); HdM's general master timetable describes a full-time master application window from mid-May to 15 July for an October start. Winter-semester intake only for this programme. For a September/October 2027 start that means 15 July 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date, since the 2027 window is not yet published, and non-EU applicants should confirm whether an earlier international deadline applies (HdM publishes a 1–31 May window, but that appears to be for exchange students, not degree applicants).
programs.applicationOpens: Approximately mid-May for the winter semester (per HdM's general master application timetable) — UNVERIFIED on the programme page itself.
programs.tuitionIntl: CONFIRMED: €1,500 per semester for international students who are not German, EU or EEA nationals enrolled in a bachelor's or consecutive master's programme — €4,500 over the 3 semesters. Plus mandatory semester contributions of €80.00 administration fee, €15.00 student body contribution and €96.50 Studierendenwerk Stuttgart contribution, i.e. roughly €1,691.50 per semester all in (about €5,075 total). Exemptions exist for a placement semester or leave of absence.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies for All Academic Disciplines; Deutschlandstipendium. Tunisia is a DAAD partner country. No programme-specific scholarship is published, and note DAAD Study Scholarships fund up to 24 months while this programme is only 3 semesters.
programs.stipend: DAAD Study Scholarships pay €992 per month for master's studies, up to the standard period of study, normally starting 1 October, plus travel and insurance allowances. Deutschlandstipendium amount at HdM: UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Modern audio studios used for the 3D-audio work, a television studio and full AV production infrastructure. No immersive-room, console or Atmos inventory is published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: On the surface this is the ideal technical route: no portfolio, no audition, no artistic gatekeeping, and a 3D-audio and music-technology profile where a CS degree is an advantage. In practice three things block him. German at C1 (Telc C1 / TestDaF 16 / Goethe C1) is mandatory and he has none. The admission rules demand 15 ECTS of documented media/design/sound coursework in addition to the engineering 15 ECTS, which his BSc almost certainly lacks, and his 180 ECTS falls short of the ~210 expected, triggering an individual review. programs.program: Master of Music – Elektronische Komposition (Electronic Composition)

programs.language: German. Applicants who did not graduate from a German-speaking institution must prove German 'min. level A2 according to the European Framework of Reference' — an unusually low bar, but teaching and the colloquium are in German.
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Electroacoustic and mixed instrumental-electronic composition (art-music, not commercial production)
programs.whatYouStudy: Independent compositional work and professionalisation: mixed instrumental/electronic composition, installations and internet works, self-organised concerts of student work. The electronic and instrumental composition classes cooperate closely, so students may join the other class's projects and take main-subject lessons there. All practical work happens in the Studio für Elektronische Musik. CONFIRMED on the official page. Note the aptitude exam explicitly tests knowledge of 'Literatur und Satztechniken der zeitgenössischen elektronischen und auch instrumentalen Musik' — i.e. contemporary art-music repertoire and compositional technique. No DJing, no club-music production, no mixing/mastering curriculum.
programs.entryRequirements: Official page: 'Successful completion of a four-year bachelor's degree in composition or equivalent. Admission to the electronic composition program is also possible with an undergraduate degree in instrumental composition.' The binding Eignungsprüfungsordnung annex (09.12.2025) is stricter and names the required bachelor as: 'Studiengang Elektronische Komposition oder Studiengang Instrumentale Komposition'. Plus German A2 minimum, application via muvac, €50 admission-procedure fee. The exam also requires proof of 'grundlegende Computerkenntnisse und Basiswissen in Musikelektronik' (basic computer skills and basic knowledge of music electronics).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No, other than as a rare exception — CONFIRMED in the binding regulations: 'Nur in Ausnahmefällen, bei außerordentlicher Begabung und Vorbildung kann ein Bachelorabschluss aus anderen Kunst- oder aus Informatikbereichen akzeptiert werden.' ('Only in exceptional cases, given extraordinary talent and prior education, can a bachelor's degree from other art or computer-science fields be accepted.') Computer science is named, but only as an exception route conditional on demonstrated extraordinary talent — not a normal pathway for a software-engineering graduate with no music training.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW EXACT (from the Eignungsprüfungsordnung annex, Anhang §5, 09.12.2025 — the programme page itself does not state it): 'Vorauswahl (digital) – Arbeitsproben: Erwartet werden Dokumentationen oder Produktionen von mindestens drei Kompositionen, welche ganz oder teilweise mit elektronischen Medien erstellt wurden, ggf. mit Partituren als PDF. Jede einzelne Arbeit muss mit Titel, Genre, Besetzung und Namen der Komponistin/des Komponisten versehen sein.' So: at least THREE compositions created wholly or partly with electronic media, documentation or production files, scores as PDF where applicable, each labelled with title, genre, instrumentation and composer name. No duration limit is published. Upload via muvac.
programs.auditionSpec: No instrumental audition. Es sind grundlegende Computerkenntnisse und Basiswissen in Musikelektronik nachzuweisen.' Note 'anspruchsvolle Fragen' (demanding questions) and that FURTHER works may be requested. The aptitude-test period for winter 2026/27 was 'expected end of May 2026 until 19 June 2026', i.e. an on-site examination window in Cologne; remote participation is not offered on the published pages.

Cologne's historic association with the WDR Studio for Electronic Music (Stockhausen) is context, not part of the school's facilities — treat as background, UNVERIFIED as a student resource.

programs.focus: Music Production; Recording / Engineering (two majors: classical acoustic, and jazz/pop)
programs.whatYouStudy: Two majors: Classical Acoustic Music Production, and Jazz and Pop Music Production. Three interwoven strands over four semesters: practical production work across genres and formats using the most recent production methods; instrumental/vocal tuition with ensemble performance; and technical methodology plus musical analysis including acoustics and ear training. Goal is artistically independent, methodically grounded professional production work. CONFIRMED on the official page — genuinely the most production-focused public master in this batch.
programs.entryRequirements: CRITICAL CORRECTION — the official Eignungsprüfungsanforderungen page states: 'Voraussetzung ist der Nachweis eines abgeschlossenen künstlerischen Bachelor- oder Diplomstudiums oder eines gleichwertig anerkannten künstlerischen Studiengangs mit Schwerpunktsetzung im Bereich Musikproduktion (z.B. Tonmeister, Soundengineering, Musikregie etc.). Im Sinne eines künstlerischen Abschlusses gilt auch ein Bachelorstudium im Studiengang Ton und Bild.' A completed ARTISTIC bachelor or diploma (or equivalent recognised artistic degree) WITH AN EMPHASIS IN MUSIC PRODUCTION is mandatory. Plus German B2 (Goethe), plus passing the concentration-specific Eignungsprüfung. Aptitude-test fee €50 for the first application, €10 for each additional application (confirmed).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No — this is a hard correction to the earlier 'Check'. The requirement is not merely 'a bachelor's degree': it must be an artistic bachelor/diploma with a music-production emphasis, and the examples given are Tonmeister, sound engineering, Musikregie, or RSH's own Ton und Bild bachelor. A BSc in Software Engineering is neither artistic nor production-focused in the sense meant, so he is formally ineligible, before the audition is even considered.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW EXACT (from the official Eignungsprüfungsanforderungen page). Jazz/Pop major pre-selection: a portfolio of FOUR TO SIX already-realised works (or excerpts) in different styles from the jazz/popular-music production field; one audio file/track package per work sample; TOTAL DURATION 15–20 MINUTES; accepted formats stereo, 5.1/7.1 or Atmos; stereo mixes as stereo .wav, multichannel as clearly labelled mono .wav files (5.1/7.1) or as an ADM file (Atmos); each work sample accompanied by a short description of how it was made. PLUS unedited videos of the applicant's own artistic performance on instrument/voice (jazz/pop) with improvisation or ad-libs, tempi and styles varying, own composition allowed, max 20 minutes total — with an important alternative for keyboard/jazz piano: 'die Einreichung von bis zu drei Stücken mit Improvisation mit Hilfe von elektronischen Instrumenten wie Keyboards, Synthesizern, DAWs (z.B. Ableton live) mit deutlich erkennbarem spielerisch-handwerklichem Anteil sowie erkennbar eigener Soundgestaltung' (up to three pieces with improvisation using keyboards, synths or DAWs such as Ableton Live, with clearly recognisable playing craft and own sound design). PLUS a motivation letter referencing the chosen major and a CV with certificates. (Classical major differs: 5–6 works, 30–45 minutes, plus three works from different stylistic periods on video.)
programs.auditionSpec: Yes — a substantial ON-SITE examination (Präsenzprüfung) in Düsseldorf, in four parts: (1) artistic presentation on instrument or voice with the same repertoire as the pre-selection, plus a prepared solo transcription (or a short a cappella piece for jazz/pop voice) AND sight-reading / sight-singing; six copies of the scores or lead sheets must be brought. (2) An UNPREPARED practical task in the chosen major, e.g. a mix or an edit, typically one to two hours. (3) Written examinations of both musical and technical hearing: musical ear (~40 min: dictations from piano and from recordings, intonation hearing, error detection, short aural analysis, instrumentation hearing) and technical ear (~40 min: listening examples including technical artefacts, level judgement, formant hearing). (4) A Fachgespräch with the selection panel, max 30 minutes. Fee €50.
