programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree or equivalent; German B2 (Goethe); aptitude assessment based on a portfolio, a motivation letter and a detailed project proposal for the chosen focus area. No numerus clausus. Aptitude-test fee €50 (first application; €10 per further application). Application via muvac; links open about one month before the deadline.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly, and this remains the clearest published welcome to a non-music graduate of any German programme in this batch. Official page: 'Musical practice is not bound to musical instruments; it encompasses many approaches to art and research. Accordingly, the master's program is open to students from all disciplinary backgrounds.' A software-engineering BSc qualifies on paper, and his coding ability is directly relevant to the algorithmic strand (the programme is co-led by Prof. Julian Rohrhuber, known for live-coding/SuperCollider work).
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW EXACT (from the official German Anforderungen page). Three documents, uploaded with the aptitude-test registration in the online portal: (1) 'ein Portfolio mit bereits realisierten Projekten' from the chosen focus area (Transmediale Formen or Epistemische Medien) — no number, duration or format limit is published; (2) a motivation letter expressing the applicant's interest in that specific focus area; (3) 'eine ausführliche Beschreibung eines Projektvorhabens mit detailliertem Zeitplan sowie konkreten Ideen zur Mitarbeit von Mitstudierenden in diesem Projekt' — a detailed project proposal WITH a detailed timetable AND concrete ideas for how fellow students would contribute to the project. That last element is unusual and easy to miss: the proposal must be designed as collaborative work.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition, no on-site test, and — importantly — the assessment is REMOTE: 'Das Projekt muss anschließend der Auswahlkommission in einer Online-Präsentation vorgestellt werden. Darauf folgt ein Online-Bewerbungsgespräch mit der Kommission. Die Präsentation und das Gespräch dauern zusammen maximal 60 Minuten.' An online presentation of the project to the selection panel followed by an online interview, together max 60 minutes. No travel to Germany is needed to apply.
programs.applicationOpens: About one month before the deadline: 'Die Bewerbungslinks werden in jedem Jahr etwa einen Monat vor dem jeweiligen Bewerbungsschluss freigeschaltet' — so roughly late September each year, via muvac.
programs.deadline: 31 October, published as a standing annual rule: 'Die Bewerbungsfrist ist stets der 31. Oktober' (and the central deadlines page confirms 'Der Bewerbungsschluss zum Sommersemester ist der 31. Oktober'). Aptitude tests are held for the SUMMER SEMESTER ONLY: 'Für den Masterstudiengang Klang und Realität gibt es Eignungsprüfungen ausschließlich zum Sommersemester.' Courses start at the beginning of April. CONSEQUENCE FOR HIM: a September 2027 start is impossible. The reachable options are apply by 31 October 2026 for an April 2027 start, or 31 October 2027 for April 2028.
programs.tuitionIntl: No tuition fees (NRW; no non-EU tuition). €50 aptitude-test fee (first application), €10 per further application, non-refundable. Semesterbeitrag payable; amount not readable on the RSH page (PDF-only) — UNVERIFIED.
programs.scholarship: DAAD Study Scholarships – Master Studies (artists/music or all-disciplines route); Tunisia is DAAD-eligible. RSH lists 'Stipendien' internally but no named scheme open to an incoming non-EU student was confirmed — UNVERIFIED.
programs.stipend: DAAD: €992/month plus insurance contributions, €460 annual study allowance, travel allowance. Note DAAD funding normally begins 1 October, which sits awkwardly with an April intake — check with DAAD before relying on it. No RSH institutional stipend confirmed — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Institut für Musik und Medien studios and collaborative project spaces; the IMM also runs a 'BASISLAGER' project space. No console, studio or immersive-room inventory is published for this programme — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: By far the easiest German conservatory door for him to open: open to all disciplinary backgrounds in the school's own words, no audition, no on-site test, assessment by a 60-minute online presentation and interview, and no tuition. His coding background is a genuine asset for the algorithmic strand. Three real caveats. First, German B2 is required — though the Kollegstudierender route lets him produce the certificate during year one, which is the softest German requirement of any RSH programme. Second, the intake is April only, so this cannot serve a September 2027 target; the nearest realistic entry is April 2027 (apply 31 October 2026 — that is roughly three months from now) or April 2028. Third and most important for his actual goal: this is artistic-research and transmedia practice, not production craft. He would graduate with a conceptual sound-art practice and a strong European network, not with mixing, mastering or dance-floor production chops. Best used as a funded, low-barrier route into a German art scene if he is genuinely drawn to experimental and algorithmic work — not as a producer's apprenticeship.
programs.verificationNotes: English programme page fetched (M.Mus., two years, two focus areas, 'open to students from all disciplinary backgrounds', B2, 31 October, April start all confirmed). The German Anforderungen page (rsh-duesseldorf.de/studienbewerbung/anforderungen/master/klang-und-realitaet) was scraped in full and produced two upgrades: the portfolio spec is now exact (portfolio of realised projects in the chosen focus area + focus-specific motivation letter + detailed project proposal with a detailed timetable and concrete ideas for fellow students' collaboration), and the assessment is confirmed as an ONLINE presentation plus ONLINE interview, max 60 minutes combined — no travel required. The central deadlines page confirmed 31 October as a standing rule and SUMMER-SEMESTER-ONLY entry, so the 'PRIOR CYCLE' label is not needed and the April-only constraint is now hard fact. Deutschkenntnisse page confirmed B2 Goethe plus the Kollegstudierender grace route; Eignungsprüfungsgebühr page confirmed €50/€10. NOT confirmed: 120 ECTS; Semesterbeitrag amount; facilities detail.

programs.program: Teilzeit-Master Audio Experience Design
programs.university: Staatliche Hochschule für Musik Trossingen
programs.city: Trossingen, Baden-Württemberg (small town, approx. 78647; nearest larger centre Tuttlingen)
programs.institutionType: Public conservatory / Musikhochschule
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters (Regelstudienzeit), part-time at 50% workload / 60 ECTS total (15 ECTS per semester) — CONFIRMED in the page's 'Facts' box. Max 10 on-site days per semester; supervision otherwise mainly remote.
programs.language: German — all programme material is German, and the school's binding Immatrikulationssatzung requires German B2 for foreign applicants. Crucial nuance, confirmed verbatim: for bachelor's and master's programmes generally (Gymnasiallehramt, Musikpädagogik and Musikwissenschaft excepted), the B2 certificate must be produced 'vor Ablauf der Rückmeldefrist für das dritte Fachsemester' — i.e. by the re-registration deadline for the THIRD semester, not at application. So he could be admitted and start without B2 and certify it during year one; re-registration into semester three is impossible without it.
programs.focus: Sound Design / Audio UX and design research; immersive and spatial sound. Explicitly NOT music production.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED on the official page: 'Development of audio experiences at the intersections of music, sound, language, technology, design, user experience and design research.' Semesters 1–2 centre on the applicant's own project, supported by design-research seminars, individual supervision (mostly remote) and up to four subject-specific workshops per semester with external experts, plus one smaller interdisciplinary project with students from the other part-time masters. From semester 3 the master's project takes over (it may but need not build on the first-year work). The page is unusually blunt about what this is not: 'This is not music production. Bei Audio Experience Design gestaltest du Klang als Erfahrung, nicht nur Tracks.' and, as a tagline, 'Stop producing. Start designing. Sound ist Material. Sound ist UX'. New programme, first intake October 2026, up to 10 students per year.
programs.entryRequirements: No specific bachelor subject is mandated. The page invites entrants from 'Architektur, Design, Musik, Medien, Informatik, Pädagogik oder Wissenschaft' and lists 'Einstieg aus vielen Bereichen und Disziplinen möglich' as a selling point. Submit: a motivation letter with a chronological account of prior musical and/or design background plus any publications or competition results; certificates (Zeugnisse); the Zulassungsantrag; proof of the transfer (fee payment); further documents per the Zulassungsantrag; and the media materials described below. German B2 per the Immatrikulationssatzung, deferrable to the third-semester re-registration deadline. The legally binding text is the Immatrikulationssatzung.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — explicitly, and computer science is named. The official page opens with: 'Ob in Architektur, Design, Musik, Medien, Informatik, Pädagogik oder Wissenschaft: hier verbindest du dein bisheriges Fachgebiet mit auditiven Perspektiven' ('Whether in architecture, design, music, media, COMPUTER SCIENCE, education or science: here you connect your existing field with auditory perspectives'), and lists 'Einstieg aus vielen Bereichen und Disziplinen möglich'. A software-engineering BSc is squarely in scope, and the assessment is of the idea, not of musicianship: 'Wir bewerten das Potenzial deiner Idee.'
programs.portfolioSpec: EXACT, confirmed verbatim, and note the delivery mechanism. In the portal, where a 'Link für die erste Phase' is requested, you literally enter 'USB-Stick' and then POST a USB stick containing: (1) the exposé of the project idea — 'Kurzes (Selfie-)Vorstellungsvideo zum Vorhaben (max. 2 Minuten)', a written account of 'max. 3 Seiten', and any early media sketches; (2) 'Eine Auswahl deiner bisherigen Arbeiten (max. 7)' — up to SEVEN previous works showing the full breadth of his output, each described in 'max. 1/2 Seite pro Arbeit', stating the year of creation, the idea/concept behind it, how it was realised, and the team involved if any. Separately uploaded via the portal's upload button: motivation letter, certificates, Zulassungsantrag, payment confirmation.
programs.auditionSpec: No on-site entrance examination — 'Es gibt keine Aufnahmeprüfung in Präsenz.' Shortlisted applicants get 'ein kurzes Gespräch per Videochat (ca. 15 Minuten)'. Note: separately, applicants without a German Abitur may face a Begabtenprüfung (a two-hour handwritten essay in German plus a 10–15 minute oral exam in German) — that route is described for applicants lacking a higher-education entrance qualification, so it should not apply to a completed BSc, but confirm.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 March (the school's standing application window for the winter semester is 01.03.–01.04.; for the summer semester 01.10.–01.11., but this programme has a winter start only).
programs.deadline: 1 March to 1 April, a standing annual window for the winter-semester intake — confirmed both on the programme page ('Vom 1. März bis 1. April reichst du deine Bewerbung über das Bewerbungsportal ein') and on the school's general Bewerbung page ('01.03. bis 01.04. für das Wintersemester'). The programme itself launches in October 2026; for an October 2027 start the window should be 1 March – 1 April 2027 — confirm when the portal opens (today is July 2026).
programs.tuitionIntl: SELF-PAY, now CONFIRMED — this is the biggest correction. The programme page's 'Keine Studiengebühren für EU-Bürger:innen bei Erstmaster' does not help him. Baden-Württemberg's LHGebG applies: 'Studiengebühr Internationale Studierende: 1.500 € pro Semester gem. § 3ff LHGebG für Studierende aus Ländern außerhalb der EU / des EWR ohne inländische Hochschulzulassungsberechtigung ... für alle Bachelor- und konsekutiven Master-Studiengänge'. Over four semesters that is €6,000, plus Verwaltungskostenbeitrag €80.00 and Studierendenwerksbeitrag €58.60 per semester (as of May 2026) — about €6,554 total. Exemptions exist under §§5–7 LHGebG (e.g. permanent domestic residence, spouses/children of EU/EEA nationals) and a waiver 'aufgrund besonderer Begabung gemäß § 6 Abs. 4 LHGebG' is possible on application; waiver applications are due 21 January / 21 June for the following semester.
programs.fundingLevel: None realistically (non-EU fee of €1,500/semester confirmed; no institutional support)
programs.scholarship: None from the institution — stated plainly on the school's own page for international applicants: 'Die Trossinger Hochschule kann keine finanzielle Unterstützung leisten', with only small Förderverein grants (e.g. competition travel) on application. It adds that German partial scholarships from the ministry or DAAD 'können erst nach einigen Semestern erfolgreichen Studierens beantragt werden' and go to very few students. A special-talent tuition waiver under § 6 Abs. 4 LHGebG is the one real lever. DAAD study scholarships normally require full-time enrolment, which a 50% part-time master does not satisfy — treat DAAD as unavailable here unless DAAD confirms otherwise.
programs.stipend: None. No stipend exists for this programme, and the school states it cannot provide financial support.
programs.facilities: Not published for this programme. The school has a Tonstudio and a 'Digital Concert Space', and links a Modulhandbuch and Studienverlaufsplan, but no studio, console or immersive-room inventory is given on the programme page — UNVERIFIED. With max 10 on-site days per semester, physical facility access would in any case be limited.
programs.fitNotes: The entry process is the friendliest anywhere in this batch — computer science named as a welcome background, no on-site exam, a 15-minute video interview, up to seven free-form works, and a German requirement he can defer to his second year. But almost everything after entry works against him. The school itself says 'This is not music production' and 'Stop producing. Start designing' — the deliverable is audio UX and design research, not tracks. It is 50% part-time and only 60 ECTS, which is a serious problem for a Tunisian national: German study visas and residence permits are premised on full-time study, so the part-time structure puts the whole immigration basis in doubt and should be checked with the German embassy before anything else. As a non-EU student he pays €1,500 per semester (about €6,554 all-in over two years) with no institutional funding and DAAD effectively off the table. And Trossingen is a village in rural Baden-Württemberg, roughly the opposite of a DJ's environment. Pursue only if he genuinely wants to become a sound designer for interfaces, installations and spatial experiences — and only after the visa question is answered.
programs.verificationNotes: Programme page scraped in full: M.A., 4 semesters, 50% part-time, 60 ECTS / 15 per semester, winter start, max 10 on-site days, up to 10 places, the 01.03.–01.04. window, the exact portfolio spec (2-minute selfie video, max 3 pages, max 7 works at max half a page each, delivered on a posted USB stick), 'Es gibt keine Aufnahmeprüfung in Präsenz', the ~15-minute video interview, and the explicit 'This is not music production' / 'Stop producing. Start designing.' framing — all CONFIRMED verbatim. The naming of 'Informatik' among welcome backgrounds is CONFIRMED, upgrading acceptsNonMusic to an explicit Yes. The school's Studiengebühren page RESOLVED the previously unverified non-EU fee: €1,500 per semester under §3ff LHGebG for non-EU/EEA students in all bachelor and consecutive master programmes, plus €80 admin and €58.60 Studierendenwerk per semester (as of May 2026), with §6(4) special-talent waiver possible and waiver deadlines of 21 January / 21 June. The international-applicants page confirmed the German B2 requirement AND that for this class of programme the certificate is only due before re-registration into the third semester, and confirmed 'Die Trossinger Hochschule kann keine finanzielle Unterstützung leisten'. NOT confirmed: studio/facility inventory; whether a 50% part-time master supports a German student visa (needs an embassy answer); whether DAAD would fund part-time study.

programs.program: Creative Production (Music) MA
programs.university: Catalyst – Institute for Creative Arts and Technology, Berlin (degree validated by Plymouth Marjon University, UK)
programs.institutionType: Private specialist creative-arts institute, not a German state Hochschule. Its own FAQ describes it as a registered training centre regulated under German law whose degrees are 'validated by our accrediting partner Plymouth Marjon University in the United Kingdom', with MA graduates receiving 'British degrees and certificates with an equivalent status recognised in Germany and the EU'. The earlier description 'state-accredited HEI' overstates this — correct it.
programs.degree: MA (Master of Arts), awarded by Plymouth Marjon University (UK)
programs.durationEcts: 1 year full-time or 2 years part-time. Credit total (UK credits or ECTS) is NOT published on the course page or fees page — it sits in the downloadable course guide/syllabus. UNVERIFIED.
programs.language: English throughout — 'taught entirely in English'. No German required.
programs.focus: Sonic Arts / practice-led artistic research, spanning music production, electronic and electroacoustic music, spatial and immersive audio, creative coding, sound art
programs.whatYouStudy: Five modules forming one arc: Imagine (detailed research proposal, research contract and work plan agreed with a supervisor), Contextualise (critical review of existing concepts, literature, practices and methods in the field), Investigate (survey then depth), Present (creation, public presentation and documentation of outward-facing work), Synthesise (a substantial original work or body of works). Three concurrent year-long workshops: Creative Sound Practices — weekly sessions moving 'between modular synthesis, spatial sound, creative coding, field recording, improvisation and sound installation', with the explicit aim being 'not technical mastery but the development of a personal methodology'; Contexts of Listening (musicology, sound studies, philosophy, critical theory — Oliveros, Schaeffer, Attali, Fisher, Butler, Derrida and others); and Supervision (one-to-one plus group critique). Guest artists have included Nicolas Collins, Bob Ostertag and Kaffe Matthews. The page is emphatic and repeats the warning twice: 'This is not a studio engineering degree, a vocational production course or a genre-based music programme. It is postgraduate artistic research' and 'This programme is not suited to those seeking vocational production training, DAW certification or a genre-based music course.' Encouragingly for him, past students have come 'from various backgrounds, including songwriting, house, techno, folk, jazz ... experimental and electroacoustic music'.
programs.entryRequirements: 'Bachelor's degree in a relevant discipline, with an Honours grade (e.g. 2:1 in the UK university system) or be in the final year of studies for one.' Non-standard entry exists: applicants lacking the minimum education requirement 'may be assessed on the strength of a professional CV and portfolio, which must demonstrate a solid background in artistic practice and research'. English at 'IELTS 6 (referred to as B2 in Germany and other EU countries)', evidenced either by an official certificate or by taking Catalyst's own online assessment — which is a real advantage given he has not sat IELTS. Submission is via an online portal: transcripts, portfolio with work samples, professional references, and a project proposal.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — likely yes, but not stated as such. The requirement is a bachelor's 'in a relevant discipline' at Honours level, and students are said to come 'from a wide range of backgrounds'. Software engineering is arguably relevant to creative coding and spatial audio, and the non-standard route offers a fallback, but the page does not name computer science and selection turns on the project proposal and portfolio. Ask Admissions directly whether an SE BSc satisfies 'relevant discipline'; the FAQ invites exactly that conversation.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not quantified anywhere public — UNVERIFIED as to number and duration. Confirmed components: a portfolio with work samples; a detailed project proposal framed as practice-led artistic research (the school runs free online prep workshops on artistic and practice-based research specifically to help applicants shape it, and offers to send a recent graduate's final project portfolio as a reference on request); a sample of research/academic writing; academic transcripts; professional references; and personal/educational documentation. The proposal, not the music, is the decisive artefact.
programs.auditionSpec: None — confirmed: there is no interview or audition requirement; the assessment is a digital submission reviewed by admissions. A voluntary call with the Admissions team is offered and, given the 'relevant discipline' question, he should take it.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling, with a priority deadline that carries a €1,000 tuition discount for early enrolment.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Published for the 2026 intake (start September 2026): priority deadline 28 February 2026 (early-enrolment bonus); visa-required applicants 30 April 2026; EU/visa-exempt 5 June 2026; late applications until 28 August 2026 'subject to availability'. For a September 2027 start expect the same pattern — priority around late February 2027 and a visa-required deadline around 30 April 2027 — but the 2027 dates are not yet published. As a Tunisian national he is bound by the EARLIER visa-required deadline, not the general one.
programs.tuitionIntl: SELF-PAY FALLBACK, confirmed, and the same for everyone: 'Our fees are the same for all students, no matter where you come from, and stay consistent for every year of your studies.' Full-time €6,028 per semester (two instalments per year) or €11,693 per year paid annually (3% discount). Part-time €3,678 per semester or €7,134 per year. Plus a non-refundable enrolment fee of €895 per study year, which includes visa support. So roughly €12,588 for the full-time year, or about €16,000 over two years part-time. Monthly and extended payment plans exist.
programs.fundingLevel: None (self-pay). BAföG and German/EU national schemes are referenced on the site but are not open to a first-time non-EU international student, and because the degree is awarded by a UK university rather than a German Hochschule, DAAD study scholarships for study in Germany would not apply either.
programs.scholarship: No means- or merit-based scholarship for a non-EU applicant was found. Only price reductions: €1,000 early-application/priority tuition discount, 3% discount for annual payment, a further discount for paying in full, and €500 off total tuition for combining a summer short course with a degree within two years.
programs.facilities: Located in the Funkhaus, the former GDR broadcasting complex. Confirmed from the site: multiple studios, extensive modular-synthesis equipment, spatial-sound tools, creative-coding resources and a bookable gear library; past MA projects have used 'the internationally unique Monom system based at the Funkhaus' for 4D multichannel composition. The programme is embedded in Berlin's experimental scene, engaging each year with Atonal, CTM, Floating University and MANIFEST:IO, running a public two-day MA Symposium and the student-run Etikett Radio (with partnerships including Refuge Worldwide). The 'Ableton Certified Training centre' claim was not seen on the pages checked — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: The best environment on this list for a would-be electronic producer and the only one with no language barrier: Berlin, the Funkhaus, English-taught, no audition, one year, and an English test he can sit through the school itself rather than booking IELTS. Two hard caveats. It costs about €12,588 for the full-time year with no funding he can access — label it the self-pay fallback and nothing else. And the school states twice, unprompted, that this is postgraduate artistic research and explicitly not vocational production training or a genre-based course; the admissions decision hinges on a practice-led research proposal, which is a genuinely unfamiliar genre of writing for a software-engineering graduate and the thing he would need months of preparation for (their free prep workshops exist for exactly this reason). Judged purely as a career move, the Berlin network, the Funkhaus studios, the symposium and the radio station may be worth more to a DJ career than any credential in this batch — but he would be buying access, not being funded into it.
programs.verificationNotes: Course page scraped in full and the Admissions FAQ and Course fees pages fetched. CONFIRMED: exact programme name, 1 year full-time / 2 years part-time, taught entirely in English, the five modules and three workshops with their content, the repeated 'not a studio engineering degree / not vocational production training' framing, the Honours-degree entry requirement with the professional-CV non-standard route, IELTS 6 (with Catalyst's own online assessment as an accepted alternative), NO interview or audition, the fee schedule (€6,028/semester or €11,693/year full-time; €3,678/semester or €7,134/year part-time; €895 enrolment fee per study year including visa support), fee parity for international students, the €1,000 priority and €500 combination discounts, validation by Plymouth Marjon University, and the Funkhaus facilities including the Monom system. CORRECTED: institutionType — Catalyst is a registered training centre under German law whose degrees are UK-validated, not a German state-accredited HEI. NOT confirmed: credit total (ECTS/UK credits); portfolio quantity and duration; the Ableton Certified Training claim; any 2027 deadline (2026 dates are the latest published, hence the PRIOR CYCLE label).

programs.program: Masterstudium Computermusik und Klangkunst (MA Computer Music and Sound Art)
programs.university: Kunstuniversität Graz (KUG) — Institute of Electronic Music and Acoustics (IEM)
programs.institutionType: Public university of music and performing arts (art university)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics + Sonic Arts + Immersive/Spatial Audio (computer music)
programs.language: German is the programme language. CORRECTION: KUG's official language table (Nachweis der Deutschkenntnisse, version 13.07.2026) requires German A2 already at application/admission and German B2 before the 3rd semester for the Masterstudium Computermusik und Klangkunst. The admission interview itself may be held in German OR English ("in deutscher oder englischer Sprache").
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (confirmed on the programme page)
programs.whatYouStudy: Computer-music composition; performance and interpretation of electronic works; conception and development of new electronic instruments; and music informatics, plus history, theory and aesthetics of computer music and (master level) methods of artistic-scientific research. IEM is one of Europe's leading centres for Ambisonics/spatial-audio research and maintains a widely used open-source plug-in suite and multichannel performance spaces.
programs.entryRequirements: Completed bachelor's degree; upload of the Bachelordiplom/-urkunde plus official transcripts. Admission is only possible after the study dean establishes equivalence of the prior study: "Erst nach Feststellung der Gleichwertigkeit des Vorstudiums durch den Studiendekan ... kann eine Zulassung zum Studium erfolgen." German A2 at application, B2 before semester 3. NOT CONFIRMED this round: the claim that the admission colloquium can prescribe up to 20 ECTS of bachelor catch-up courses — that comes from the curriculum PDF, which was not re-read; treat as UNVERIFIED.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED: "zwei aussagekräftige Beispiele deiner künstlerischen Arbeit" — two meaningful examples of your own artistic work in computer music and sound art, approx. 5 minutes each ("jeweils ca. 5 Minuten"), uploaded as compressed audio/video (mp3, h264) or online links, max approx. 150 MB total, submitted before the registration deadline. Multichannel material to be reduced to stereo.
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED: no live/on-site audition and no instrument required. "Das mündliche Prüfungsgespräch findet über Zoom statt" — an oral examination interview by Zoom, in German or English, covering the submitted works, artistic motivation and intended focus.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 March (annual registration opening)
programs.deadline: Registration 1 March – 1 May. The KUG page currently displays the Zoom interview as "xx. Juni 2027" — i.e. it is already showing the cycle that leads to a September/October 2027 start, but the exact interview DAY is still a placeholder. So: registration window is published (1 March – 1 May 2027), interview date PRIOR CYCLE / NOT YET PUBLISHED - confirm exact day when KUG fills in the placeholder.
programs.tuitionIntl: CONFIRMED on KUG's fee page: Studienbeitrag €363.36 per semester standard, €726.72 per semester for third-country nationals (a Tunisian citizen is a third-country national), plus ÖH-Beitrag €26.20 per semester. Total ≈ €752.92/semester.
programs.scholarship: None found for this profile. CONFIRMED: KUG's automatic tuition-fee waiver covers only Albania, Armenia, Belarus, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Türkiye and Ukraine — Tunisia is NOT on that list. A full exemption also exists for students from 29 least-developed countries; Tunisia is not one. So he pays the full €726.72.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (low public fee only; no stipend)
programs.stipend: UNVERIFIED — no stipend attached to admission
programs.facilities: IEM: multichannel/Ambisonics production and performance spaces, electronic-instrument development, strong music-informatics research profile, internationally recognised spatial-audio tooling. Detailed room/console inventory not published on the pages read (UNVERIFIED in detail).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — no formal field restriction, but equivalence is discretionary. The public page requires only a bachelor's degree plus the study dean's equivalence finding; no wording anywhere excludes a non-music bachelor, and none guarantees acceptance either. A software-engineering BSc would be judged almost entirely on the two 5-minute works. Realistic only if those works are genuinely strong electronic/computer-music pieces.
programs.fitNotes: Still the best European home for serious electronic/computer music and spatial audio, and the admission mechanics are unusually light: two 5-minute works plus a Zoom interview that can be taken in English, no live instrument audition, low public fee. Two real obstacles, one newly confirmed: (1) German A2 is required AT APPLICATION and B2 before semester 3 — this was previously understated; (2) the aesthetic centre of gravity is experimental/art computer music, not club-oriented DJ/producer craft. Worth noting: KUG separately runs a SOUND DESIGN programme whose official language is English (C1 English required, B2 at application, per the same language table) — a possible better-language-fit alternative at the same institution that this batch did not cover.
programs.verificationNotes: Official programme page re-fetched and confirmed: 4 semesters/120 ECTS, portfolio of two ~5-minute works (~150 MB), Zoom oral exam in German or English, registration 1 March – 1 May, interview shown as "xx. Juni 2027", equivalence assessed by the Studiendekan. Fees confirmed on KUG's official Studien- und Studierendenbeitrag page (€726.72 third-country + €26.20 ÖH) together with the exact country list for the fee waiver, which excludes Tunisia. programs.whatYouStudy: Managing complex audio productions end to end — artistic-technical planning, creative realisation, completion — with a large elective share to build an individual artistic profile inside one of three specialisations: Musikproduktion Klassik, Musikproduktion Popularmusik, or Filmton. Sound reinforcement and sound design can be added as further emphases. A master project is central.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED and stricter than a generic 'relevant degree'. The MA page requires "ein abgeschlossenes fachlich in Frage kommendes Bachelor- oder Diplomstudium" and names the mdw BA Tonmeister_in as the intended route. The official admission information sheet is explicit about what must be uploaded: "Nachweis über ein abgeschlossenes Studium (Bachelor o. Diplom) in einem facheinschlägigen Studium Tonmeister_in". Also required: German B2; a tabular CV covering musical background and technical prior training; and "Nachweis der einwandfreien Hörfähigkeit" — a specialist medical certificate no older than two months including an audiogram confirming physiologically flawless hearing across 125–8,000 Hz.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official Informationen zur Zulassungsprüfung PDF. (a) Motivation video, max 3 minutes, answering a fixed question list for the chosen specialisation (waived only for mdw BA Tonmeister graduates). (b) Instrument/voice video — Popularmusik: 2 jazz/popular works with improvisation or ad libs, an own composition allowed, tempo and style should vary; for piano one piece may be improvisation using electronic instruments such as keyboards, synthesizers or DAWs ("z. B. Ableton live") with clearly recognisable playing craft and recognisably own sound design; band or play-alongs permitted; total video duration max 15 minutes. Filmton: this section is waived. (c) Piano video if piano is not the main instrument (Klassik and Popularmusik only). (d) PORTFOLIO — POPULARMUSIK: SIX popular-music productions in different styles, produced, recorded and mixed substantially by the applicant, at least three with vocals, at least two involving recording of acoustic instruments, all supplied as pure stereo audio (5.1/Atmos versions optional extras), each at least 2:30 and max 30 minutes in total, plus written documentation of 7,000–12,000 characters incl. spaces (approach, justification of microphone choice, photos of recording situations, meaningful DAW screenshots, challenges, critical reflection). KLASSIK: three music-recording projects, two pure stereo audio productions with different ensembles plus one free project (audio or video, stereo/5.1/Atmos, stereo version always supplied), total 20–40 minutes, plus the same 7,000–12,000-character documentation. FILMTON: three film-sound projects from production sound, sound design and mixing, two with more complex sound design or mixing and at least one in 5.1, plus documentation of the same length. Technical: one work per file; .wav (5.1 as separate labelled wavs), ADM BWF for Atmos; .mp4/.mov video, max Full HD (no 4K), max 8 GB per file; documentation as PDF; instrument videos unedited, fixed camera, hands/face/torso visible, max 1 GB per file.

programs.program: MultiMediaArt (Master), department AUDIO
programs.university: Fachhochschule Salzburg (FH Salzburg / Salzburg University of Applied Sciences)

programs.institutionType: University of applied sciences (publicly co-funded Fachhochschule)
programs.focus: Music Production + Sound Design + Film/Game Sound + Immersive Audio
programs.language: CONFIRMED English (whole programme). Proof of English at CEFR level B2 is an explicit entry requirement.
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, full-time
programs.whatYouStudy: You choose ONE of four departments — Audio, Film, Communication Design or Producing — and build advanced skills in conceiving, designing, implementing and managing cross-media creative projects. The Audio department covers music production and recording, composition, sound synthesis and sound design, mix and mastering, interactive audio, soundtracks and audio post-production, and sound and performance, with cross-department collaboration on film soundtracks, game audio and multimedia installations.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED from the official Master-Admission info sheet (WS 2026/27 edition), three conditions: (1) a university degree or equivalent from a recognised post-secondary institution in Austria or abroad; (2) proof of a minimum number of ECTS in three core subject areas — 35 ECTS Creative-artistic design practice (graphic design, media design, film, TV, audio, music, game design), 10 ECTS Basic sciences (media theory, cultural theory, art theory, media informatics, media technology, media sociology, media history, communication and media studies, media psychology, aesthetics), 5 ECTS Economics and working methods in the field of media (project management, media economics, entrepreneurship, business administration, marketing, media law); (3) mastery of English at least level B2. Non-Austrian documents must be notarised/legalised where no international agreement applies, and certified translations of the degree certificate and transcripts must be uploaded.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official Master info sheet: "Portfolio: If you want to apply for Audio, Film or Communication Design, upload your portfolio in the application portal under 'Upload application project' as a ZIP file (which should contain a PDF). Present at least three of your best creative works from the last few years. Describe in your portfolio the role you played in the projects shown." Only the Producing department substitutes a letter of motivation. Also required: bachelor's degree certificate (may be submitted by 31 October at the latest), proof of English B2, passport copy, CV in English, the choice-of-department form (p.11 of the info sheet), the proof-of-academic-level form (p.9) and transcripts incl. ECTS key. All third-party material and any soundtrack used must be credited; undeclared external material or copied ideas cause exclusion from the admission procedure. NOTE: a separate FH Salzburg PDF titled "MultiMediaArt PORTFOLIO REQUIREMENTS" describes an Audio portfolio as a link to soundcloud/bandcamp/youtube plus CV, credit list and software/hardware list — that document uses the BACHELOR major names (computeranimation, audio, communicationdesign, film) and should not be relied on for the master. The master info sheet is the governing document.
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED: no performance audition. The procedure has exactly two mandatory phases — online application with document upload, then "Personal interview or, if travel to Salzburg is not possible, via video conference via MS Teams". The interview lasts about 15 minutes, is conducted by the department head and departmental lecturers, and covers motivation, previous projects and professional experience, plus any master-project ideas; you may show further creative work (audio snippets, music streaming, screenshots). Invitations go out about two weeks after the application deadline, interviews about one week later. Failure to attend the interview means exclusion.

programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED from the official course-contents and master-class pages. Core: economy, law, management and scientific work, plus TV, video and audio production, storytelling, video/audio/studio technology, media coding, digital imaging, information visualisation, 360-degree video, AR and VR. You then choose one of three master classes — Animation & Visual Effects, 3D Audio & Sound Design, or Film & TV. The Audio master class runs four independently designed, developed, planned, implemented and evaluated projects across four semesters: semester 1 Design Thinking, project on sound design in animation; semester 2 Prototyping & Implementation, project on Sonic Interaction; semester 3 Evaluation & Testing, project on 3D Audio & Virtual Realities; semester 4 a group project. In-depth courses: Audio System Design; Film & Location Sound & Post Production; Film & Game Sound Design; Prototyping & Implementation; Coaching & Consulting. Software focus: Pro Tools Ultimate with Dolby Atmos Production Suite, Nuendo, Reaper, Ableton Live, Max4Live, Max8, Pure Data, Unity 3D with Wwise, Python, IRCAM SPAT5, IEM Plugin Suite, Sparta VST, Zylia Studio Pro, EASE 4, Tsugi GameSynth, iZotope RX. Students can 'buy' skills they lack (e.g. programming, graphic design) from students in other master classes, paying in ECTS credits. Regular field trips to Tonmeistertagung (VDT), next_generation (ZKM), klingt gut! (HAW Hamburg), ICSA and AES Conventions.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED on USTP's general admission page: for a master degree programme, either completion of a relevant bachelor at a university of applied sciences, or completion of an equivalent programme at an accredited Austrian or foreign post-secondary institution with at least 180 ECTS and a duration of at least six semesters. Where equivalence is only partly established, the Academic Director may tie recognition to examinations taken during the master programme. Plus German B2 for all non-native speakers. Third-country applicants must upload their residence permit during the online application.
programs.portfolioSpec: Portfolio required; the specification is deliberately open. Official FAQ, verbatim: "For your application, you can submit a variety of projects that demonstrate the manifold facets of your work. These could be projects of your bachelor programme, projects from your professional work, or even private projects that match your chosen masterclass. Be creative and opt for projects that showcase your skills, interests, and your aptitude for the study programme of your choice." No fixed number, duration or format is published — UNVERIFIED at that level.
programs.auditionSpec: No musical audition. A standard FH admission procedure with scheduled admission dates: for the 2026/27 cycle the admission date for the master classes "3D Audio & Sound Design" and "Animation & Visual Effects" was a fixed date (a separate 15/06/2026 date applied to "Film & TV"), "and thereafter by appointment". Whether the admission appointment is on-site or remote is not stated for this programme — UNVERIFIED.
programs.applicationOpens: CONFIRMED forward-looking: "Applications for the winter semester 2027/28 will be possible from autumn 2026." That is exactly his intake.
programs.deadline: CONFIRMED status as of today: "The application deadline for the winter semester 2026/27 has expired. An application is currently not possible. Applications for the winter semester 2027/28 will be possible from autumn 2026." PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Third-country applicants at USTP face an earlier cut-off than the general one (for comparison, in the WS 2026/27 cycle the general master window ran from autumn to late spring while third-country nationals had to apply by late February) — he must check the third-country deadline specifically as soon as the 2027/28 window opens in autumn 2026.
programs.tuitionIntl: CORRECTED and confirmed on USTP's official costs page. Standard tuition €363.36 per semester, BUT: "third-country nationals are charged a tuition fee of EUR 1,500.00 plus the ÖH fee" (ÖH €26.20 per semester). A Tunisian citizen on a student residence permit pays €1,500 + €26.20 per semester, i.e. roughly €6,100 over four semesters. Additional master costs: €100 copy costs and €20 Campus Card fee. USTP also "collect[s] a deposit of EUR 200 from students from third countries". The €363.36 rate applies only to holders of other permits (Permanent Residence – EU, Family Member, Red-White-Red Card, etc.). The previously suspected €4,385/semester figure indeed belongs to a different continuing-education programme and does not apply.
programs.scholarship: CONFIRMED: none available to him. USTP's tuition-fee-waiver scheme for third-country nationals with higher tuition (best 20% of each semester receive a refund of the increased fee) applies ONLY to Creative Computing, Cyber Security and Resilience, Digital Innovation and Research, Citizen-Centered Digital Health and Social Care, and Gamified Reality Applications (GRACE) — Digital Media Production is explicitly not on that list. What DMP does have is small project grants: "Each semester, selected project teams of the degree programmes Media Technology, Digital Design, Digital Media Production, and Interactive Technologies are awarded grants" — departmental financial aid and equipment for student projects, not tuition relief. Ukrainian nationals get a fee waiver; Tunisians do not.
programs.fundingLevel: None for tuition (€1,500/semester third-country rate, no applicable waiver). Project grants only, which do not offset tuition.
programs.stipend: None found — CONFIRMED that the relevant third-country tuition-waiver scheme excludes this programme.
programs.facilities: CONFIRMED on the official master-class page: four audio studios for practical exercises and software training with 24 state-of-the-art iMac workstations and high-quality Focusrite interfaces; Studio A with Dolby Atmos surround sound; Austria's first Audiokinetic Wwise Certified School; an active AES Student Section at USTP; a student-run portfolio site; a USTP student won a 3D Audio competition in November 2025. Wide software licence base as listed above.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes in principle — CONFIRMED there is no music-degree requirement anywhere. This is an applied-sciences media/technology master; the requirement is a relevant bachelor of at least 180 ECTS and six semesters, with the Academic Director able to prescribe supplementary examinations where equivalence is only partial. A software-engineering BSc is a plausible fit for the technical side (programming, signal processing, real-time systems). The blocking condition is language and money, not musical background.
programs.fitNotes: On subject matter this is arguably the best technical fit in the whole batch for a software engineer who wants immersive-audio craft — Atmos, Ambisonics, Wwise/Unity game audio, Max/Pure Data, four self-run projects, four studios, AES links, and a dual degree with HAW Hamburg. But verification turned two soft caveats into hard blocks: (1) German B2 is required for admission because the degree programme is German-taught, and he has no German at all; (2) as a Tunisian third-country national he would pay €1,500 per semester (~€6,100 total) plus a €200 deposit, with the university's own third-country tuition-waiver scheme explicitly not covering this programme. The one genuinely good piece of news is timing: the 2027/28 application window — his intake — opens in autumn 2026. If he were ever to spend two years reaching German B2 and could self-fund, this would jump to an A; as of today it is C.
programs.verificationNotes: The institution's site is now reachable — the old fhstp.ac.at URLs 301-redirect and WebFetch kept returning 503, so the pages were retrieved directly over HTTPS from the new ustp.at domain. The sourceUrl has been corrected from the dead fhstp.ac.at path to the live USTP programme page. Confirmed on official pages: degree Diplom-Ingenieur (Dipl.-Ing.) — the earlier MA guess was wrong; Language of Instruction German; 4 semesters full-time block teaching; 20 places/year starting calendar week 37; the three master classes; the audio master class content, semester structure, software list, four audio studios, 24 iMac workstations, Studio A with Dolby Atmos, Wwise Certified School, AES Student Section; the open portfolio FAQ wording; the master entry requirement of 180 ECTS / six semesters; the German B2 requirement for all non-native speakers with DMP absent from the English-taught exemption list; tuition €363.36 standard and EUR 1,500.00 for third-country nationals plus €26.20 ÖH, €200 third-country deposit, €100 copy costs and €20 Campus Card for masters; the third-country tuition-waiver scheme and its five eligible programmes (DMP not among them); the DMP project grants; and the current deadline status with WS 2027/28 applications opening autumn 2026. Still unverified: total ECTS (120 is portal-sourced only), the exact 2027/28 third-country deadline, and whether the admission appointment is on-site or remote.

programs.focus: Music Production + Film/Game Sound + Sound Design
programs.language: German OR English. Official Language Requirements page: 'Master of Arts in Music — B2 German or English at the admission examination, or no later than the end of the 1st semester.'
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (stated on programme page)
programs.whatYouStudy: Programme page: specialisation 'in the different fields of music in media: film, theatre, advertising, audio branding, sound design and computer games', focused on 'applied production and scientific research into the interrelationships between music, communication, today's media and society'. programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED. No official page requires a MUSIC bachelor. Programme page states only 'Prerequisite for admission: Passed entrance examination'. Language B2 German or English.
programs.portfolioSpec: VERIFIED from the official PDF 'MA-Steps-of-the-admission-procedure-EN'. Upload: passport copy; certificates enabling enrolment in Master studies; CV; motivation letter (optional but recommended); an EXPOSÉ of the planned Master project (detailed spec in Annex 1 — cover page, field classification, state of research, methods, hypotheses, outline, timeline, bibliography); proof of the EUR 50 application fee; and recordings/scores. Artistic presentation = 'At least three performance pieces of free choice', audio and/or audio-visual material or scores (scores accepted for Media Music). programs.applicationOpens: Rolling — 'Audition dates: By arrangement'; online audition procedure open year-round via the registration form.

programs.tuitionIntl: MAJOR CORRECTION — the previously reported ~EUR 4,050–4,560/semester is WRONG. Official Studiengebühren page (DE and EN, raw HTML confirmed), heading 'pro Semester': Master of Arts in Music — EU citizens EUR 6,528; NON-EU citizens EUR 11,018 PER SEMESTER. Over 4 semesters that is approx. EUR 44,072. Plus a one-off enrolment fee of EUR 350 and a EUR 50 audition application fee. ÖH fee EUR 26.20 is included. programs.scholarship: Official 'Grants & Scholarships' page lists: JAM Grant (25%) and GRAND JAM Grant (50%) tuition reductions, awarded per semester to applicants with complete active enrolment (deadlines 31 Oct / 14 Mar); Ö1 Jazz Scholarship; Planet Festival Scholarship; Falco Scholarship; an External Merit Scholarship of EUR 750–1,500 one-off that explicitly includes 'third-country nationals'; and a Lower Austria foundation restricted to Austrian citizens. programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED at the level of studio inventory — no official page read itemises studios, consoles or immersive rooms. Luksch, Christof Unterberger, Yu-Chun Huang, Michael Klimas); 'Media Music at JAM MUSIC LAB is powered by Wien Holding'.

Not itemised anywhere official: studio infrastructure.

programs.program: Masterstudium Elektrotechnik-Toningenieur (Electrical Engineering and Audio Engineering) — inter-university with TU Graz
programs.university: Kunstuniversität Graz (KUG) jointly with Technische Universität Graz
programs.institutionType: Public art university + public technical university (joint programme)
programs.focus: Recording/Engineering (audio engineering fused with musical training)
programs.language: German. Proof of C1/CEFR required; alternatively, applicants who present proof of A2 at application may sit a supplementary German examination (Ergänzungsprüfung aus Deutsch) before beginning regular studies.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (Studienkennzahl UV 066 413)
programs.whatYouStudy: Official text: an interdisciplinary synthesis of technology and music, science and art. 'Based on a well-founded scientific and music-theoretical foundation, followed by specialisation with a choice among electrical/information-technology, music-practical and audio-technical areas.' Courses are held at Institute 17 — Electronic Music and Acoustics (IEM). Chairs: Robert Höldrich (recording and reproduction technology, electronic music), Alois Sontacchi (acoustics and audio engineering), Franz Zotter (acoustics and audio engineering). Graduates are aimed at the audio industry, acoustics and multimedia.
programs.entryRequirements: KUG/TU Graz BSc Elektrotechnik-Toningenieur graduates qualify automatically. External applicants must hold 'ein gleichwertiges und zur Zulassung berechtigendes Studium' (an equivalent degree conferring admission eligibility); equivalence is assessed by the Dean of Studies, and 'je nach Vorbildung und zur Erlangung der vollen Gleichwertigkeit' up to 30 ECTS of courses and exams from the bachelor programme may be prescribed. All externals must pass the admission examination. German C1, or A2 at application plus the supplementary German exam. Documents: bachelor diploma and final certificate, transcript of records, all with official German or English translations and possibly diplomatic legalisation, via KUGonline.
programs.portfolioSpec: NONE — there is no artistic portfolio and no recording dossier. Submission is purely academic (diploma, degree certificate, transcript, certified translations). A pre-check Infoblatt and Excel worksheet are offered so applicants can self-assess equivalence before applying.
programs.auditionSpec: No artistic audition. A written admission examination at IEM in three parts: (1) Seashore hearing test over headphones, approx. 40 minutes — paired-comparison thresholds for frequency, intensity and tone duration, timbre discrimination, tone and rhythm memory (sample tests with solutions are published on Moodle); (2) second written aural test, approx. 20 minutes — melodic and rhythmic dictation, recognition of modes, time signatures, triads and instruments, plus spotting errors in a printed score; (3) written music-theory test, approx. 15 minutes — interval and scale construction, rhythm. Confirmed on the page: 'Die Zulassungsprüfung für das Wintersemester 2027/28 findet online statt' — the WS 2027/28 admission exam is ONLINE. Results normally 2 days later via KUGonline.
programs.applicationOpens: Registration via KUGonline; opening date not published on the page. Overview of KUG admission-exam dates for the winter semester is linked from the page.
programs.deadline: 3 June, with the next admission test given as 'xx. Juni 2027'. This is already the WS 2027/28 cycle, but the exact test DAY is an unfilled placeholder on the official page — treat 3 June 2027 as the working application deadline and confirm the exam day once KUG fills it in.
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 752.92 per semester total for third-country nationals: Studienbeitrag EUR 726.72 plus ÖH-Beitrag EUR 26.20 (confirmed on the KUG fee-waiver page).
programs.scholarship: None applicable. KUG's Studienbeitrag waiver under the Ost-/Südosteuropaschwerpunkt applies only to Albania, Armenia, Belarus, Bosnia-Herzegovina, Georgia, Kosovo, Moldova, Montenegro, North Macedonia, Serbia, Türkiye and Ukraine — Tunisia is NOT on the list, so he pays the full EUR 752.92 per semester.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial — low public fee only (approx. EUR 3,012 tuition across four semesters). No scholarship identified.
programs.stipend: UNVERIFIED — no stipend found for this profile. Austrian OeAD scholarships were not checked against this programme.
programs.facilities: Institute 17 IEM (Electronic Music and Acoustics) at KUG hosts the teaching, with chairs in recording/reproduction technology and in acoustics and audio engineering; TU Graz supplies the electrical-engineering side. IEM's specific studio and Ambisonics inventory is not itemised on this page — UNVERIFIED at that level of detail.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, by design — the clearest technical-entry route in Austria. Official wording: 'Externe Studienwerber*innen, die kein Bachelorstudium der Studienrichtung Elektrotechnik-Toningenieur an der KUG/TU Graz absolviert haben, müssen über ein gleichwertiges und zur Zulassung berechtigendes Studium verfügen', with 'bis zu 30 ECTS aus dem Bachelorstudium Elektrotechnik–Toningenieur' potentially prescribed. A software-engineering BSc is a plausible base, but the Dean of Studies rules on equivalence and an SE degree is not an electrical-engineering degree — the 30-ECTS top-up is likely.
programs.fitNotes: The only affordable, portfolio-free route in this slice, and the online WS 2027/28 admission exam removes the travel barrier entirely. Two hard obstacles: German at C1 (or A2 plus a supplementary German exam that must be passed before regular studies begin), and the musical-aptitude battery — Seashore test, melodic/rhythmic dictation and music theory — which needs roughly a year of deliberate ear training. Also be honest about the content: this is an engineering degree in audio, not a DJ/producer degree, and the equivalence ruling on a software-engineering BSc is a genuine unknown.
programs.verificationNotes: Programme page read in full via raw HTML (German version; the English URL 404s). Confirmed: 4 semesters/120 ECTS, DI degree, German C1 or A2-plus-supplementary-exam, external-applicant equivalence rule with up to 30 ECTS top-up, the three-part admission exam, the online format for WS 2027/28, and the 3 June deadline with an unfilled 'xx. Juni 2027' exam date. Fees and the country list for the fee waiver confirmed on KUG's own waiver page (EUR 726.72 + EUR 26.20 = EUR 752.92; Tunisia excluded). Not verified: application-opening date, IEM studio inventory, any Austrian scholarship for this profile.

programs.language: CAUTION — two official statements. The programme fact box says 'Hauptunterrichtssprache: Deutsch' (main teaching language German). The registration page says 'Die Unterrichtssprache ist Deutsch oder Englisch' and the motivation letter may be in German or English. Non-native speakers must prove competence via mother tongue, a secondary-school subject pass (grade 4 minimum), a recognised certificate normally under 5 years old, or a degree taught in that language. Assume working German will be needed in practice.
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED: 4 semesters (Regelstudienzeit); Studienumfang Major / MA = 90 / 120 Credits. Autumn-semester start.
programs.whatYouStudy: Official text: work in the fast-developing field of sound for film, podcast, theatre, computer games, interactive media and products, requiring broad knowledge, technical skills and high artistic-creative competence — sound generation and manipulation plus linear and interactive sound dramaturgy, with programming knowledge from basic to advanced depending on the linear or interactive track. Delivery is mentorship and individual sessions, class teaching on technique/aesthetics/craft, and a large share of self-directed project work.
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree or equivalent from a recognised and accredited university (Rahmenordnung ZHdK, RO §19–24; StO MA Composition and Theory §4 ff.). Exception clause, quoted: 'In Ausnahmefällen kann die ZHdK Personen ohne Bachelorabschluss oder gleichwertigen Abschluss einer anerkannten und akkreditierten Hochschule zulassen.' Use of AI in the application is permitted but must be declared.
programs.portfolioSpec: VERIFIED and MORE DEMANDING than previously recorded. (1) Motivation letter, max 2 A4 pages, German or English — schooling, musical education, musical activities, knowledge of music software, leisure activities, plus why ZHdK Sound Design and your professional plans. (2) NEW, previously missed: a Bewerbungsvideo of 3–5 minutes, max 1 GB, mp4, presenting yourself in your own creative working environment. (3) Dossier of 3–4 of your own works, max 1.95 GB, totalling approx. 10 minutes — scores/texts/images as pdf, audio as mp3, video as mp4 — plus a commentary on each work (concept, significance, creation process) collected in ONE pdf of max 2 A4 pages named 'Kommentare.pdf'. Optional 'Links.pdf'. Everything zipped, filenames must carry your name and contain no special characters or umlauts. (4) NEW, previously missed: an AUDIOGRAM, not older than 2 months, issued by a doctor. (5) For candidates without a BA in Music: a video of your own artistic-musical performance, max 15 min / 1.95 GB, .mov or .mp4, fixed camera perspective, hands and face visible, movements complete and without cuts, phone/camera/laptop acceptable, stereo mic desirable, HD 720p–1080p, files named Nachname_Vorname_Komponist_Werk.
programs.auditionSpec: ON-SITE aptitude examination in Zurich, in three blocks. Practical: a Sound Design task, 90 minutes preparation and 20 minutes presentation and discussion. Oral: analysis of a short film scene, game level or sound scene, 60 minutes preparation and 10 minutes presentation and discussion; plus a 10-minute colloquium on one of the submitted works. Musical aptitude exam: 30 minutes of oral theory tasks — memory exercise, reproducing rhythms and melodies, recognising, naming and writing intervals and chords, a harmonic task, and a short improvisation.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE — online application opened 6 January 2026. The live page now reads: 'Das Zulassungsverfahren für den Studienbeginn im Herbst dieses Jahres ist abgeschlossen. Informationen zum nächsten Zulassungsverfahren werden Mitte November hier veröffentlicht.' Expect the 2027 cycle to open early January 2027, with dates published mid-November 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Published 2026 cycle: online application 6 January – 2 March 2026; minor selection 10–30 March; notification early April; aptitude exam 13–14 April 2026; results mid-May; studies begin 14 September 2026. The programme fact box lists a standing 'Anmeldeschluss 1. März'. For a September 2027 start expect roughly early January – 1/2 March 2027, with an on-site exam in April 2027.
programs.tuitionIntl: CORRECTED figures. Official fact box and ZHdK tuition page: CHF 720 per semester for CH students, CHF 1,220 per semester for non-CH — i.e. CHF 720 base plus a CHF 500 per-semester surcharge for students who move to Switzerland to study. Plus ASVZ university sport CHF 35 and an optional student-union fee CHF 32. Application: CHF 100 registration fee; a further CHF 200 examination fee if invited to the second stage. (Earlier CHF 750/1,250 figures were slightly out of date.)
programs.scholarship: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarships — ART category, for an initial Master's in an artistic field at a Swiss institution, CHF 2,450/month, maximum age 35. SBFI confirms: 'This scholarship is available to students from a limited number of countries only' and 'Information on application deadlines and scholarship available by country of origin will be published here in August 2026.' Applications open 20 August 2026; decisions by end of May. TUNISIA'S ELIGIBILITY FOR THE ART CATEGORY REMAINS UNVERIFIED — check the country list when SBFI publishes it in August 2026, or write to sgs@sbfi.admin.ch. Separately, ZHdK runs an Exzellenzstipendium for incoming master's students, but 'Eine Initiativbewerbung ohne Nomination der ZHdK ist nicht möglich' — nomination-only, you cannot apply for it.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial confirmed (CHF 1,220/semester, approx. CHF 4,880 tuition over four semesters); potentially Full if the Swiss Excellence ART scholarship turns out to be open to Tunisia — UNVERIFIED until August 2026.
programs.stipend: Swiss Government Excellence Scholarship: CHF 2,450 per month, max age 35. Whether tuition or housing is additionally covered is not stated on the SBFI page — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: Toni-Areal campus, Zurich. The programme page emphasises being networked with students from numerous artistic disciplines and access to state-of-the-art infrastructure, but does NOT itemise ICST or the Immersive Arts Space — those associations are plausible ZHdK-wide but were not confirmed on the pages read. Treat detailed facility claims as UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES, with a written extra hurdle. A bachelor from any recognised and accredited university qualifies you to apply, and ZHdK may even admit people without a bachelor 'in Ausnahmefällen'. Applicants without a BA in Music must additionally submit the uncut, fixed-camera artistic-musical performance video of max 15 minutes. The 30-minute musical aptitude exam on site applies to everyone.
programs.fitNotes: The strongest dedicated sound-design master in this slice: the fee is modest by Swiss standards, non-music graduates are explicitly accommodated in the regulations, and the practical sound-design task suits a programmer. Three real obstacles: he must produce a 15-minute uncut artistic-musical performance video (he currently has no performing act), he must pass a 30-minute oral music-theory and ear test, and the exam is ON SITE in Zurich in April — budget flights and a visa appointment. Add the audiogram and the 3–5 minute studio self-presentation video to his prep list. Main teaching language is listed as German, so start German alongside the ear training.
programs.verificationNotes: Registration page read in full via raw HTML, plus the programme fact box and the ZHdK tuition-fees page. Corrections made: duration/ECTS now confirmed (4 semesters, 90/120 credits, previously UNVERIFIED); fees corrected to CHF 720 + CHF 500 = CHF 1,220 per semester (not 750/1,250); two application items previously missed are now recorded (a 3–5 minute application video, and a doctor-issued audiogram under 2 months old); main teaching language is listed as German in the fact box even though the registration page allows German or English. The 2026 dates are confirmed as the CLOSED prior cycle — the live page states next-cycle information appears mid-November. ICST / Immersive Arts Space links were NOT confirmed on the pages read.

programs.whatYouStudy: Recording and production craft at Tonmeister level, mapped directly by the admission syllabus: expert operation of DAW and periphery, clear understanding of music-production processes, targeted microphone use, editing and mixing, sound aesthetics, recording management; mastery of analogue and digital signal-processing systems (desks, recorders, signal transmitters), digital audio synchronisation, transmission and storage quality factors, EQ/dynamics/reverb; and the underlying technical subjects — electrical engineering (circuit analysis, filters, transistor and op-amp circuits, microphones and loudspeakers), digital audio technology (sampling, A/D and D/A, interfaces, data compression, FFT, z-transform, digital filters), acoustics (room acoustics, absorption, measurement, ray tracing, eigenmodes) and mathematics (trigonometric and exponential functions, Fourier transform, complex numbers, differential and integral calculus).
