programs.program: DNSEP Design mention Design sonore (années 4 et 5)
programs.university: École supérieure d'art et de design TALM — site du Mans (TALM-Le Mans), in partnership with IRCAM, ENSCI-Les Ateliers and Le Mans Université / LAUM
programs.degree: DNSEP (Diplôme National Supérieur d'Expression Plastique) conférant le grade de master
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (années 4 and 5, semesters 7-10). Entry requires 180 ECTS for semester 7 or 180+60 for semester 9. Total programme ECTS not stated on the official pages — UNVERIFIED (French DNSEP 2e cycle = 120 ECTS).
programs.focus: Sound Design (industrial, object, environmental, multimodal, UX) + Sonic Arts + some Immersive/Spatial Audio
programs.institutionType: Public école supérieure d'art et de design (Ministère de la Culture), partnered with a research institute (IRCAM), a design school (ENSCI) and a university acoustics lab (LAUM/CNRS)
programs.language: French. CONFIRMED: 'Les candidat·s étranger·ères non-francophones doivent maîtriser suffisamment la langue française pour lire et dialoguer. Ils et elles doivent également justifier au minimum du niveau B2 au TCF … ou au DELF.' A compulsory English module ('Anglais, le langage comme matière, matériau et matériel') sits in UE3.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED (livret de formation). Semesters 7 and 9 modules: 'Création sonore appliquée', 'Workshop applicatif', 'Production, diffusion et perception du son, appliquées au design sonore', 'Informatique sonore et technique son', 'Workshop arduino', 'Méthodologie créative en design sonore', 'Atelier Radio', 'Éléments scientifiques', 'Concepts de design et cognition auditive appliqués au design sonore', 'Histoire et théorie du sonore', 'Ateliers de recherche et création (ARC)', 'Anthropocène : usage et mésusage du monde', histoire des arts, pratique professionnelle, pré-mémoire then mémoire. Semester 8 is an international exchange or a company placement. Semester 10 = mémoire and plastic-work defence before a jury of professionals. The year opens with a two-week 'workshop applicatif' answering a real brief from an industrial or institutional partner, in mixed teams with ENSCI design students — past clients include Décathlon, SETRAM / Le Mans Métropole (tram sonification), Groupe PSA (gestural and sound interfaces), SNCF Direction Innovation, Maison de la Radio / Radio France, RATP, GHT Psychiatrie Sainte-Anne. Students run radio on the school station and produce work for Le Mans Sonore, the city's international sound biennial (4th edition in 2026). NEW AND CONFIRMED: 'En 5ᵉ année, TALM offre à ses étudiant·es la possibilité d'effectuer leur master en alternance' — a paid apprenticeship route in the final year.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED from the live admissions page, which SUPERSEDES the older brochure. 'Cette commission est destinée : aux candidat·es déjà inscrit·es dans une autre école d'art agréée par le ministère de la Culture ; aux candidat·es ou diplômé·es d'un autre cursus artistique français ou étranger.' Credits: 'Les candidat·es doivent justifier de 180 crédits (intégration en semestre 7) ou 180 crédits + 60 crédits (intégration au semestre 9)'; non-EU diplomas 'feront l'objet d'un contrôle de leur comparabilité avec les diplômes français'. Language: minimum B2 TCF or DELF plus certified translations of diplomas. Fee: 'frais de gestion de dossiers … 55 euros', payable per site (a separate €55 for each site applied to). The 2022 brochure adds the accepted-diploma list: 'diplômé.e d'une filière artistique ou d'électroacoustique des universités (ou … inscrit.e en licence au moment du concours) ; d'une école d'art ou de design équivalent au niveau licence (DNA ou équivalents étrangers) ; d'une école d'enseignement musical spécialisé équivalent au niveau licence (DNSPM ou équivalents étrangers), d'un DEM de composition ou électroacoustique … à condition de posséder en plus une licence scientifique ou en sciences humaines.' Selection criteria: 'La motivation, l'ouverture d'esprit, la faculté d'adaptation à des contextes spécifiques, le potentiel à travailler en équipe'. About ten places: 'accessible à une dizaine de jeunes diplômé.e.s'.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW CONFIRMED (was previously recorded as unverified). 'Pièces constitutives du dossier de candidature : 1 – Dossier administratif … 2 – Dossier personnel : Curriculum vitae détaillant les acquis de formation sonore, acoustique design, pratique artistique, projets personnels ; Une lettre de motivation argumentée sur la conception du design sonore, les domaines d'intérêt ; Catalogue de réalisations artistiques, dessins, vidéos, musiques, photos, peinture, sculpture, etc. ; Catalogue de réalisation sonore – 1 ou plusieurs extraits pour un total de 5 minutes maximum. Pour chaque extrait il est nécessaire de définir par écrit l'objectif artistique ou de design, la nature originelle du document et le format du fichier ; Un projet d'échange international ou de stage qui a lieu au deuxième semestre ; Un projet de mémoire.' The downloadable dossier de candidature for the chosen mention is the authoritative version each year — request/download it from esad-talm.fr in January.
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED, and CORRECTED: the interview is REMOTE, not on site at Le Mans. Three steps. 1st: submit the completed dossier by the deadline to the mailbox indicated. 2nd: 'Présélection — Evaluation des dossiers de candidature par un jury d'enseignant·es.' 3rd: 'en distanciel … Le ou la candidat·e présente devant un jury son dossier personnel. Lors de l'entretien, les membres de la commission évaluent le dossier artistique du ou de la candidat·e et apprécient l'effective capacité de celui-ci ou de celle-ci à intégrer le domaine choisi.' Held 'via la plateforme Teams. Il ne sera pas nécessaire d'installer de logiciel, mais une caméra est obligatoire.' No written test, no on-site travel — a significant practical advantage.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO / CHECK — probably not eligible on his current profile. The live admissions page restricts the commission to candidates already enrolled in a Ministry-approved art school, or holders/graduates of 'un autre cursus artistique français ou étranger'. A software-engineering BSc is neither. In the brochure's diploma list a scientific licence appears only as an ADDITIONAL condition bolted onto the DEM route ('à condition de posséder en plus une licence scientifique ou en sciences humaines'), never as a standalone qualification. His 180 ECTS satisfy the credit rule, and the school does say the DNSEP 'sadresse à tout type de créat.eurs.rices sonores … dont la pratique sonore et musicale peut s'adapter', so there is discretion — but he must get written confirmation from contact-lemans@talm.fr / olivier.houix@talm.fr before investing.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Pattern published by the school: 'Les dossiers d'inscription à la commission sont mis en ligne chaque année sur notre site internet mi-janvier. La présélection puis l'entretien avec le jury se déroulent entre début avril et mi-mai selon les années.' Expect mid-January 2027 for the Sept-2027 intake.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 cycle (confirmed on the live admissions page): 'Date limite de candidature 2026 : le 22 mars'; presélection follows; interviews '1er, 2 ou 3 avril 2026 – en distanciel'. A supplementary September commission exists but for 2026 it covered only the Design computationnel mention (deadline 14 August 2026), not Design sonore. No 2027 dates published as of July 2026.
programs.tuitionIntl: CONFIRMED (official TALM 'Les droits d'inscription 2026-2027' page, délibération n°693-2024 of 19 Feb 2024): 'pour les élèves originaires de pays hors Union Européenne (hors mobilité) : 1 500 €' per year (vs €1,000 for EU students in 2e/3e cycle). 'Les élèves boursiers ou boursières sont exonéré·es de frais d'inscription.'
programs.fundingLevel: Partial — modest non-EU tuition (€1,500/yr) and full exemption for CROUS bursary holders, but no entry stipend. The year-5 alternance (apprenticeship) route is a genuine paid-study option worth investigating.
programs.scholarship: None found reserved for non-EU degree-seeking candidates. The school runs a 'Les bourses d'étude' page and exempts CROUS bursary holders from tuition entirely, but CROUS eligibility for a newly arrived Tunisian national is UNVERIFIED. Best lead beyond that is the 5th-year alternance contract, plus Campus France Tunisie / French Embassy funding.
programs.stipend: None at entry. UNVERIFIED what a year-5 alternance contract pays.
programs.facilities: CONFIRMED: 'Studio son, équipé d'une écoute en 5.1'; multitrack digital recorders, an ambisonic microphone, an octophonic diffusion system, assorted microphones, audio interfaces, amplifiers and loudspeakers; MIDI controllers and a radio studio; plus full art-school workshops (métallerie, sérigraphie, menuiserie, impression 3D, robotique, découpe laser, volume, photo, video, gravure, peinture, mécatronique) and a computer park with ProTools, Premiere Pro, the Adobe suite, Rhino and 3DsMax. Partners: IRCAM (Labo STMS, équipe Perception et Design Sonores — Nicolas Misdariis, Patrick Susini), ENSCI-Les Ateliers Paris (Roland Cahen, head of the sound studio), and Le Mans Université's LAUM (CNRS, Christophe Ayrault). Teaching team: Olivier Houix (IRCAM researcher, doctor in acoustics, coordinator), Rodolphe Alexis, Fabien Bourdier, Ludovic Germain (ENSCI graduate, founder of the LAPS sound-design agency). The school states it is 'le seul établissement à assurer sur le plan international une formation supérieure diplômante et qualifiante dans le secteur d'activité du design sonore'. Host of the Le Mans Sonore biennial.
programs.fitNotes: Exceptional industry exposure — live briefs from SNCF, RATP, PSA, Radio France, Décathlon — and the IRCAM / ENSCI / LAUM triangle has no European equivalent. Cost is manageable at €1,500/yr non-EU, admission is remote (no travel), the portfolio spec is now known, and the 5th year can be done as a paid alternance. But two things count against it for him. Discipline: this is FUNCTIONAL sound design — product, transport, museum, UX signage, radio — explicitly positioned AGAINST specialised music tracks ('Contrairement aux formations proposant des objectifs très spécialisés (design musical, son à l'image, jeux vidéos…)'), so it does not serve a DJ/producer goal. Eligibility: the commission is written for candidates coming from an art, design or electroacoustic cursus, and a software-engineering BSc is not one. Only pursue after written confirmation from the school, and only if he has by then built a real sound/art portfolio.
programs.verificationNotes: CORRECTED sourceUrl — the previously supplied PDF (presentation_detaillee_du_dnsep_design_sonore… ) is a brochure versioned 'v.17-01-22' (January 2022) and its admission section is now out of date; the live TALM admissions page 'Les commissions Design — Entrée en 4e et 5e années' is authoritative and is used instead. programs.program: Master Arts, Lettres et Civilisations — mention/parcours "Création musicale et arts sonores" (CMAS), now a parcours of the new Master "Musiques, Créations, Technologies" (MCT)
programs.university: Université Gustave Eiffel, UFR Lettres, Arts, Création, Technologies (LACT), with INA GRM
programs.city: Champs-sur-Marne / Marne-la-Vallée (Paris region); specialisation teaching at INA sup campus, Bry-sur-Marne
programs.degree: Master (bac+5), mention Arts, Lettres et Civilisations — national French state master
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters. INA campus page states 137 days of instruction, approx. 240 contact hours. ECTS not published on any page read — UNVERIFIED (a French national master is legally 120 ECTS).
programs.focus: Electroacoustic composition / Sonic Arts / Electronic Music (research-creation), practice-based
programs.institutionType: Public university, historically in partnership with INA GRM (Groupe de Recherches Musicales)
programs.language: French (an English module sits in the professionalisation unit). No English-taught route.
programs.whatYouStudy: MAJOR STRUCTURAL CHANGE CONFIRMED. The standalone CMAS diploma is being wound down and its content absorbed into Université Gustave Eiffel's new Master "Musiques, Créations, Technologies" (MCT), which the official MCT page describes as organised around four parcours: "Musiques et musicologies", "Musiques numériques et musicologie computationnelle", "Production et Performance", and "Création musicale et arts sonores". MCT aims "to train specialists in the fields of contemporary music and musical technologies, from musicology research to the development of digital tools for musical creation", with project-based pedagogy. The first four teaching units run on the Champs-sur-Marne campus; the specialisation teaching is held at INA sup, Bry-sur-Marne. Legacy CMAS structure: five teaching units per semester — general cultural approaches; composition; research-creation and professionalisation (compulsory internship + English); and a creation-techniques specialisation delivered by INA GRM; plus one option from aesthetics/musicology, computer music or digital arts.
programs.entryRequirements: Admission on dossier. Official wording (MCT page): a bac+3 level diploma — "une licence de musique ou artistique, un diplôme de conservatoire ou d'école d'art équivalent au niveau L3, ou autres masters connexes (180 crédits obtenus après le secondaire)" — with "pratique musicale ou sonore indispensable". No age limit. Cohort is very small: the INA page states max 10, the university/SFA listing states 12 places. CRITICAL PROCEDURAL CORRECTION: the pages say "apply via monmaster.gouv.fr", but Campus France Tunisie states explicitly that "les candidats de nationalité tunisienne ou d'une autre nationalité étrangère résidents en Tunisie … ne sont pas concernés par cette nouvelle plateforme de candidature" — he must use the Campus France "Études en France" procedure instead. Contact: master.musique@univ-eiffel.fr / Corinne Renoux, 01 49 32 90 11; INA side ndebade@ina.fr.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio spec published for CMAS itself — UNVERIFIED. However the sibling MIM parcours at the same university (same UFR, same admissions team) publishes a dossier spec that is almost certainly the shared model: transcripts, a motivation letter, a brief CV, and a research or research-creation project setting out context, subject, research question, preliminary bibliography and studied corpus, with the note that "a maximum of 3 personal works can supplement the file". So: a written research-creation project is the primary document and personal sound works are a capped supplement (max 3), NOT the core of the application. Confirm in writing with master.musique@univ-eiffel.fr.
programs.auditionSpec: None published. Selection is on dossier. No audition, no on-site test, no interview found on any official page read. UNVERIFIED whether an interview is used in practice.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO as published, and this is reconfirmed on the new MCT page: the accepted qualification is "une licence de musique ou artistique, un diplôme de conservatoire ou d'école d'art équivalent au niveau L3", plus "pratique musicale ou sonore indispensable". A BSc in Software Engineering is not on the list and does not qualify by equivalence. With 10-12 places against that wording, this is a formal eligibility blocker rather than a soft preference.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For HIM the governing calendar is Campus France "Études en France", not Mon Master: the 2025/2026 campaign opened 01/10/2025. Expect the Sept-2027 campaign to open around 1 October 2026 — i.e. roughly two months from now. (For reference, the domestic Mon Master 2026 calendar was: catalogue 2 Feb 2026, applications 17 Feb - 16 Mar 2026, results 3-16 June 2026.)
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Campus France Tunisie closed Master 1/2 applications on 15/01/2026 for the September 2026 intake; expect approximately 15 January 2027 for September 2027. No programme-specific deadline is published.
programs.tuitionIntl: The INA page states "243 € annually for initial university training" — that is the French/EU national master rate, NOT the non-EU rate. CORRECTED: under décret n° 2026-385 (in force 21 May 2026) the differentiated non-EU master rate is €3,941/yr. Université Gustave Eiffel states it is "renewing the partial exemption from the differentiated enrolment fees for newly arrived international students from outside the European Union … so that the amount due is aligned with the tuition fees applicable to European students" — but that decision is for 2026/2027 only, and the decree caps discretionary exemptions at 30% of a university's non-EU headcount in 2026-2027, falling to 25% in 2027-2028 and 20% thereafter. So €243 is plausible but NOT guaranteed for a September 2027 entry.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (potentially very low fee if the UGE exemption is renewed and he is inside the 30%/25% quota; no stipend)
programs.scholarship: None programme-specific. External only: France Excellence Eiffel (institution-nominated, so the university must put him forward), Bourse du Gouvernement Français via Campus France Tunisie. Note that holding a French government scholarship also triggers automatic exemption from differentiated fees.
programs.facilities: The distinguishing asset was INA GRM — the historic Groupe de Recherches Musicales, birthplace of musique concrète and developer of GRM Tools — delivering the creation-techniques specialisation at the INA campus in Bry-sur-Marne. VERIFIED CAVEAT, now stronger than previously recorded: the INA campus page states that from the 2026 intake INA campus will no longer offer this diploma, and explicitly redirects prospective candidates to Université Gustave Eiffel's new Master "Musiques, Créations, Technologies". The MCT page still lists INA GRM among its partners (alongside IRCAM, CDMC, École des Beaux-Arts de Bourges, regional conservatoires and concert halls, and international links to the UK, USA and Canada), so the partnership appears to survive in some form, but INA campus is out of the recruitment. Studio and equipment inventory not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Artistically prestigious and nominally cheap, but three hard problems for him, two of which are now confirmed rather than suspected. (1) Eligibility: the required degree is a music or arts licence with "pratique musicale ou sonore indispensable" — his software-engineering BSc does not qualify, and with 10-12 places there is no incentive for the jury to stretch. (2) The diploma has been restructured: INA campus stops recruiting from 2026 and points applicants to the new MCT master, so the thing described in the original record no longer exists in that form. (3) It is French-only and the dossier centres on a written research-creation project, not a producer's demo reel — the opposite of what a DJ/producer profile is built to show. Do not build a 2027 plan around this.
programs.verificationNotes: CONFIRMED from the official INA campus page (https://campus.ina.fr/formation/son/production-musicale/master-creation-musicale-et-arts-sonores): programme exists at bac+5, partner Université Gustave Eiffel, 2 years / 4 semesters / ~240h / 137 days, €243 per year for initial training, entry = bac+3 in music or arts or conservatory/art-school equivalent with mandatory musical or sound practice, no age limit, application via monmaster.gouv.fr, contact ndebade@ina.fr — AND the explicit notice that from autumn 2026 INA campus will no longer offer this diploma, redirecting candidates to Université Gustave Eiffel's new Master "Musiques, Créations, Technologies". CONFIRMED from Campus France Tunisie (tunisie.campusfrance.org) that Tunisian residents are excluded from Mon Master and must use "Études en France", campaign 01/10/2025-15/01/2026 for the 2026 intake. CONFIRMED from the Ministry that the Mon Master 2026 domestic calendar ran 17 Feb - 16 Mar 2026. Two application tracks: the computer-science profile applies to M2 Informatique (SAR track) and needs a master-level CS/mathematics degree or an engineering degree with a computing specialty; the acoustics profile applies to M2 Mécanique (Acoustique track) and needs a master-level physics/acoustics background or an engineering degree in physics/acoustics/signal processing. programs.fitNotes: Of everything in this batch this is the closest to 'become a producer' in the commercial-pop sense, and the entry evidence is exactly the kind he can build: three of his own recent productions. Second, 'reasonable command of a harmonic instrument (piano/guitar)' is a stated requirement he currently cannot meet. Third — newly confirmed — the audition includes a timed one-hour mix-and-rework of supplied audio and MIDI files presented live, which is a fair test for a producer but one he must train for. Everything financial and procedural needs a direct email to asc@codarts.nl because the site blocks automated reading: deadline, fee and whether non-EU candidates may audition remotely are all unknown.
programs.verificationNotes: The programme EXISTS at master level — the official admission-requirements URL is live and indexed, and the official Codarts Master of Music study guide 2025-2026 PDF (https://www.codarts.nl/fileadmin/user_upload/documenten/studiegidsen/2025-2026/study_guide_codarts_ma_music_2025-2026.pdf) was downloaded and read directly, confirming the two-year structure, 30 EC/yr main subject, 10 EC/yr Artistic Research, the Free Space portfolio, English-language teaching, the mandatory on-site Introduction Day and the personal budget. The admission page itself sits behind Cloudflare bot protection and could NOT be fetched by WebFetch or curl; its content was recovered only through search-engine indexing of the official URL, so treat the quoted admission wording as high-confidence but second-hand. CORRECTIONS MADE: the 'private SoundCloud / three tracks / no Splice vocals' portfolio spec could not be confirmed at master level and is downgraded to UNVERIFIED; the audition is confirmed to include a one-hour on-site production and mixing assignment, previously listed as UNVERIFIED. Deadline and non-EU tuition remain UNVERIFIED.

programs.program: Master of Music – specialisations Pop and Creator Performer
programs.university: Fontys Academy of Music and Performing Arts (Fontys Hogeschool voor de Kunsten)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years full-time (confirmed). ECTS: UNVERIFIED — Fontys does not state a credit total on the programme page.
programs.language: English (confirmed)
programs.institutionType: University of applied sciences / academy of music
programs.focus: Performer and creator development across Classical, Jazz, Music Theatre, Pop and Creator Performer. NO named music-production, studio-engineering or sound-design track exists — the framing is performer/creator, not producer.
programs.whatYouStudy: Five specialisations confirmed: Classical, Jazz, Music Theatre, Pop, Creator Performer. The distinctive mechanism is a personal budget: students receive funds to buy in teaching and can engage teachers globally, including outside Fontys, which in practice lets a producer assemble mentors Fontys does not employ. Individual lessons, ensemble coaching, research guidance and electives tailored to personal goals. Campus Zwijsenplein in Tilburg houses multiple art programmes and is pitched as experimental and collaborative. Module-level curriculum: not published.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFLICTING OFFICIAL WORDING — must be resolved before he invests effort. The main Fontys programme page states applicants need 'a relevant bachelor's degree' plus 'a minimum level of proficiency in the English language'. A separate Fontys Master of Music application page is indexed as stating 'Prerequisite for admission is a Bachelor of Music degree or equivalent.' Assessed submissions confirmed on both: a Personal Development Plan setting out professional goals for the two study years, and a single A4 research-project proposal of 500–1,000 words focused on your artistic practice as performer and/or creator. Entrance assessment mandatory.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK – UNRESOLVED, and riskier than the input data suggested. One official Fontys page says 'a relevant bachelor's degree'; another official Fontys page is indexed as saying 'Prerequisite for admission is a Bachelor of Music degree or equivalent', which would exclude him outright. Fontys nowhere addresses a non-music bachelor explicitly. This single question must be put in writing to Fontys admissions before anything else.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not published as a numbered audio/video portfolio. The assessed written submissions are the Personal Development Plan plus the single-A4 (500–1,000 word) artistic research proposal. Whether an audio/video work portfolio is additionally required for Pop / Creator Performer: UNVERIFIED — though candidates outside the region do submit a video audition (see auditionSpec).
programs.auditionSpec: Entrance assessment / audition is MANDATORY, and the exam commission evaluates the Personal Development Plan as part of it. NEW DETAIL confirmed on the Fontys application page: candidates living in the Netherlands, Belgium and western Germany are invited to a LIVE audition; candidates living elsewhere may UPLOAD A VIDEO AUDITION. As a Tunisian applicant he would fall in the video-audition group, which removes the travel barrier but not the performance requirement. Exact audition content for Pop / Creator Performer: UNVERIFIED.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Published dates, which the Fontys page ties to programmes commencing SEPTEMBER 2026: Pop 1 February; Jazz and Classical 9 April (non-EEA) / 1 June (EEA); Music Theatre 6 May. Enrolment closes 1 April (non-EEA) / 1 July (EEA). No Creator Performer date is listed separately — assume it follows the Pop date and confirm. For a September 2027 start expect roughly 1 February 2027, NOT yet published.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED officially – Fontys publishes no non-EU figure on the programme page and directs applicants to a tuition-fee calculator. An aggregator quotes €10,210/year for non-EU against €2,695 for EU; treat as unconfirmed. Fontys does state living costs of €900–1,100 per month.
programs.scholarship: NL Scholarship – Fontys University of Applied Sciences is a listed participating institution for 2026-2027.
programs.stipend: NL Scholarship: €5,000 one-off in the first year (national scheme rate). Separately, Fontys gives Master of Music students a two-year personal budget spendable on tailored tuition including teachers outside Fontys — CONFIRMED to exist on the official page but WITH NO AMOUNT PUBLISHED there; an aggregator quotes €3,000–€4,000 per year, unconfirmed.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — Fontys publishes no studio or equipment inventory for this programme. The genuinely unusual asset is the personal study budget, which can be spent on external teachers worldwide, useful for someone whose ideal mentors are working producers rather than academics.
programs.fitNotes: A fallback at best, and after verification weaker than the input data implied. There is no named production, sound-design or studio-engineering track anywhere in the five specialisations; the framing is performer/creator throughout. The personal budget is a real and unusual advantage for a self-taught producer who wants to buy mentoring from industry names, and the video-audition route for candidates outside NL/BE/western Germany is helpful. But there is a live conflict in Fontys's own published entry requirements — one page says 'a relevant bachelor's degree', another says 'a Bachelor of Music degree or equivalent' — and if the latter governs he is simply not eligible. Fee, ECTS, portfolio spec and current deadlines are all unconfirmed. Do not invest effort here until Fontys answers the non-music-bachelor question in writing.
programs.verificationNotes: Official Fontys programme page fetched (plus the fontys.edu mirror, which 302-redirects back to fontys.nl) and confirmed: Master of Music, Tilburg, 2 years full-time, English, five specialisations including Pop and Creator Performer, 'a relevant bachelor's degree' plus English proficiency, Personal Development Plan and 500–1,000-word A4 research proposal, mandatory entrance assessment, personal budget, deadlines Pop 1 February / Jazz and Classical 9 April non-EEA and 1 June EEA / Music Theatre 6 May, enrolment closing 1 April non-EEA and 1 July EEA, September 2026 start (hence prior cycle), living costs €900–1,100/month. NEW FINDING: video audition available for candidates outside NL/BE/western Germany. UNRESOLVED CONFLICT: a second official Fontys application page (fontys.edu/Bachelors-Masters/Masters/Master-of-Music/Apply-1.htm) is indexed as requiring 'a Bachelor of Music degree or equivalent', contradicting 'a relevant bachelor's degree'; that page returned 404 on direct fetch after redirect, so the conflict could not be settled. NOT CONFIRMED: ECTS total, non-EU tuition, personal-budget amount, any audio/video portfolio spec, and any 2027 dates.

programs.program: Master of Music (Arnhem) — single English-taught MMus; from 2026/2027 the Arnhem Jazz & Pop and Music Theatre masters merge into it. No dedicated production or sound-design specialism is published.
programs.university: ArtEZ University of the Arts – Academy of Music / Conservatorium Arnhem
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (confirmed on the programme page: '2 years', '120 ECTS')
programs.language: English (page header: 'English • Arnhem')
programs.institutionType: University of the arts (hogeschool)
programs.focus: Open artistic practice / individual route. NEW AND MATERIAL: from academic year 2026/2027 the Arnhem music master's programmes (Jazz & Pop and Music Theatre) merge into this English-taught Master of Music, so a popular-music/jazz strand now feeds into it — but Music Production, Sound Design and Electronic Music are still NOT published as named specialisms.
programs.whatYouStudy: Two-year flexible programme to 'deepen your artistic identity and develop your own creative practice'. Three components: an individual study route with substantial freedom to design your own path, plus a two-part shared programme of practical and theoretical lessons, research and masterclasses taught by professionals from different fields, with students selecting their own masterclass teachers. Confirmed on re-check: the page still publishes NO module list, no studio modules and no named specialisations — 'The page does not specify particular specialisations or routes'. Whether a producer can negotiate real studio teaching inside the individual route remains UNVERIFIED and must be settled by email to conservatorium.arnhem@artez.nl.
programs.entryRequirements: NOW VERIFIED on the dedicated admission-requirements page: 'You have completed a bachelor's programme.' and 'You may also apply with a diploma in another field. The admissions committee will then assess the relevance of your previous education and professional experience.' Also required: 'You received a positive result on your entrance examination (you have been admitted)' and you must 'be able to understand, speak, read, and write English at a high enough level to follow your classes.' English: the Arnhem MoM admission page states no numeric score, but ArtEZ confirms 'Language requirements apply to all ArtEZ master courses' — the merged Jazz & Pop master required IELTS 5.5, and the sister Master of Music in Zwolle requires 'A minimum IELTS score of 6, or an equivalent English-language certificate'. Plan on IELTS 6. Language-certificate delivery deadline for non-EU/EEA passport holders: 31 May.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly. Quoted from the ArtEZ Master of Music Arnhem admission-requirements page: 'You may also apply with a diploma in another field. The admissions committee will then assess the relevance of your previous education and professional experience.' The Zwolle sister programme is blunter: 'A completed bachelor's degree, preferably in music. If your bachelor's degree is in another field, the admissions committee may ask you to take additional bachelor's courses within the master's programme.' This is a genuine correction — the earlier assessment recorded this as UNVERIFIED. A software-engineering BSc is admissible in principle; the entrance exam, not the diploma, is the gate.
programs.portfolioSpec: Still only partly published. Portfolio must 'reflect the learning objectives that you indicated in your motivation letter'. Audio/video uploaded via YouTube, Vimeo or SoundCloud; scores as Finale, Sibelius or PDF uploaded directly to the application form. Number of works, durations and any producer-specific brief: UNVERIFIED — not published on any ArtEZ page reachable. Portfolio must be submitted by the application deadline (1 February for non-EEA).
programs.auditionSpec: LIVE entrance exam required (step 4 of the application process). Non-EEA applicants are scheduled into the FIRST round only: 'If you do not hold an EU/EEA passport, your entrance exam will be scheduled in April, due to you needing to meet visa application deadlines.' The later May/June round is explicitly restricted to NL & EU/EEA candidates. Format for a producer candidate: UNVERIFIED. Requires travel to Arnhem (no published remote option).
programs.applicationOpens: Application via Studielink; NL Scholarship and ArtEZ Scholarship applications open 1 February each year, after admission. Studielink opening date for the 2027 intake: UNVERIFIED.
programs.deadline: 2027 DATES ARE PUBLISHED (unusually — most peers are not). The Arnhem music master admission pages list: non-EEA application + portfolio deadline 1 February 2027; entrance exams 30 March – 1 April 2027; additional exams 31 May – 11 June 2027 (NL & EU/EEA only); NL & EU/EEA deadline 15 April 2027. CAUTION: the main Master of Music Arnhem landing page still shows the 2026 cycle (exams 30 March – 1 April 2026, apply before 1 February 2026; enrolment 31 May non-EU/EEA, 31 August EU/EEA) — PRIOR CYCLE on that page. Reconfirm the 1 February 2027 date directly before relying on it.
programs.tuitionIntl: NOW VERIFIED: institutional (non-EEA) fee €13,030 for students 'planning to start in the 2026-2027' academic year; statutory fee (EU/EEA and qualifying residents) €2,694 for 2026-2027. The 2025 non-EEA rate was €12,580, so budget c. €13,000–13,600/yr for a 2027 start. This corrects the previous UNVERIFIED entry. Additional compulsory costs: travel and accommodation for residential periods and a compulsory period abroad.
programs.scholarship: TWO stackable schemes, both confirmed. (1) NL Scholarship — ArtEZ is a participating institution; open to non-EU/EEA nationals who have passed the entrance exam, been accepted to a full-time ArtEZ bachelor's or master's course, and enrolled through Studielink. (2) ArtEZ Scholarship — covers 50% of the institutional tuition fee for the ENTIRE degree duration, for non-EU/EEA first-year students who have never studied in the Netherlands before, with demonstrated financial need.
programs.stipend: NL Scholarship: €5,000, paid once in the first year — explicitly 'not a full-tuition scholarship'. ArtEZ Scholarship: 50% of the institutional tuition fee (i.e. roughly €6,500/yr against a €13,030 fee), for the full duration of the degree, adjusting annually with tuition. Both open 1 February after admission; ArtEZ Scholarship documents due 1 May. ArtEZ states 'we have only a few scholarships to award' for both. Best realistic case: c. €6,500 waiver + €5,000 in year one, leaving roughly €6,500/yr net tuition plus living costs.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — ArtEZ publishes no studio, console or immersive-audio inventory for the Arnhem Master of Music on any page reachable. Given the 2026/2027 merger of Jazz & Pop into this master, popular-music teaching staff and rooms are present, but nothing specific to production or Atmos is documented.
programs.fitNotes: Upgraded on verification. Two facts change the picture: ArtEZ now states in writing that a diploma in another field is acceptable, and the Jazz & Pop master has merged into this degree, so the programme is no longer purely classical/conceptual. Funding is also better than first recorded — the ArtEZ Scholarship's 50% institutional-fee waiver runs for the whole degree, and stacks with the €5,000 NL Scholarship. The obstacles are real but ordinary: €13,030/yr list price, IELTS c. 6 required, a live entrance exam in Arnhem in April with no remote option, and — the core problem — no published production or sound-design curriculum, so he would be betting on negotiating an individual route. Email conservatorium.arnhem@artez.nl before investing in this application.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed on official ArtEZ pages: programme exists at master level, Arnhem, English, 2 years / 120 ECTS; non-music diploma explicitly accepted (admission-requirements page); institutional fee €13,030 and statutory €2,694 for 2026-2027 (tuition-fees page); NL Scholarship €5,000 one-off and ArtEZ Scholarship 50% of institutional fee for the full degree (both scholarship pages); non-EEA entrance exam scheduled in April with a 1 February portfolio deadline; 2027 exam and deadline dates published on the Arnhem music master admission pages. NOT confirmed: portfolio number of works and durations, entrance-exam content for a production candidate, any module list, any studio inventory, and whether a production route can be built inside the individual route. Note the internal inconsistency between the 2026 dates on the landing page and the 2027 dates on the admission pages.

programs.program: Master of Music – Music Production (Master in de muziek, afstudeerrichting muziekproductie); English-language master track available
programs.university: KASK & Conservatorium, School of Arts Gent (HOGENT and Howest)
programs.degree: Master of Music (2nd cycle, Master in de muziek)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (60 per year), on top of a 3-year bachelor — 3+2 path. Confirmed on the programme page.
programs.language: English-language master track alongside the Dutch one. Confirmed: 'There are no differences in curricula, competencies, learning outcomes or organization between the English-language programmes and their Dutch-language counterparts', and the school states dozens of foreign students enter the English masters each year.
programs.institutionType: Conservatory / school of arts within a university of applied sciences (HOGENT/Howest)
programs.focus: Music Production (primary); Recording/Engineering; songwriting and composition for production
programs.whatYouStudy: Module list confirmed exactly. Year 1 (60 ECTS): Producing & artistic research 31 ECTS; Projects master 1, 3 ECTS; Masterseminaries 8 ECTS; Thesis 1, 3 ECTS; Professional skills 3 ECTS; Minor/Specialisation/Electives 12 ECTS. Year 2 (60 ECTS): Master project Producing 33 ECTS; Projects master 2, 3 ECTS; Thesis 2, 6 ECTS; Arts in Practice 6 ECTS; Minor/Specialisation/Electives 12 ECTS. So 64 of 120 credits sit in producing and the producing capstone. Departmental philosophy: 'creativity, musicality (both performance and songwriting/composition) and technique', working in professionally equipped studios. Industry bridge via external mentors, internships and 'Arts in Practice'.
programs.entryRequirements: Degree route, quoted: 'a bachelor in performing music (for the master in classical music or jazz/pop), or a bachelor in composing music (for the master in music production, composition or music theory).' Language, quoted: 'You can study all our master's programs in Dutch or English. There are no formal level requirements for English in the master programs, but the Vantage B2 level is strongly recommended' — NO IELTS/TOEFL required for admission. IMPORTANT CAVEAT DISCOVERED ON VERIFICATION: this only removes the test from the ADMISSION path. The Master Mind scholarship separately requires, for Schools of Arts, IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 90 / B2 certification AND a GPA of 3.5 out of 4.0 — so if he wants Master Mind money he must test after all.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — bridging is the realistic route. Two published statements apply. On other artistic disciplines: holders of 'an academic bachelor's degree in another artistic discipline may have to take a preparatory program before they are admitted to the master's programs.' On mismatched degrees generally: 'If you wish to begin a master's program, but do not have the appropriate underlying bachelor's degree, you may, in some cases, follow a bridging program. In such cases, it is best to contact your study program supervisor.' Software engineering is neither performing nor composing music nor an artistic discipline, so a bridging (schakel) programme is the probable path, not direct master entry. Critically, funding is NOT lost by bridging: 'Scholarships can be awarded to students in a bridging program, preparation program and master program.'
programs.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED. The widely-quoted 'four songs' specification is the BACHELOR admission-test spec, not the master's. The bachelor test asks for four songs or compositions (three to five submitted initially plus one theme test piece), each 'composed (individually or in collaboration) and/or recorded, mixed, produced, and/or performed as a musician and/or arranged by the candidate', with 'a maximum of one non-original work, such as a cover, adaptation, or remix'. For the MASTER, what is actually published is: a digital portfolio plus a master proposal, judged by the orientation committee; 'You must upload links to an online portfolio or upload a PDF portfolio. We do not accept portfolios in physical format (usb, dvd, paper...)'; plus a motivation letter of max 1 page. Number of works for the master: UNVERIFIED — confirm with paul.lamont@hogent.be. Assessment criteria are published: creations 'in which you yourself have played an important, supporting, creative role', above-average musical talent, diversity in productions and collaborations, and originality and authenticity.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage, dossier-first — the gentlest admission format in this slice. Orientation test (oriënteringsproef) organised several times per academic year; 'Based on your portfolio and master proposal, the orientation committee will decide whether or not to invite you for an intake interview or audition.' Applicants are notified of the committee's decision by email. So stage 1 requires no travel; an on-site intake interview or audition follows only if shortlisted.
programs.applicationOpens: Registration for each orientation-test session via HOGENT web registration, ahead of the session date.
programs.deadline: Published session for music production: orientation test, August session, 24.08.26 — this is the CURRENT cycle, for September 2026 entry. For a SEPTEMBER 2027 start: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Expect sessions spread across the 2026-27 academic year plus a late-August 2027 session. Registration deadlines per session are not published on the master pages. Master Mind 2027-2028 call: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (the 2026-2027 call launched January 2026 with institution deadlines between 1 February and 1 April 2026).
programs.tuitionIntl: VERIFIED on the KASK financial page for 2026-2027: non-EEA increased tuition = fixed administrative amount €916.20 + €131.40 per credit, giving €8,800.20 for a standard 60-credit year. Applies to students of non-EEA nationality in drama, visual arts, audiovisual arts and music. Advanced master and postgraduate programmes cost more; the master in music production is charged at the standard rate above.
programs.scholarship: (1) KASK & Conservatorium's own non-EEA scholarship system for drama, visual arts, audiovisual arts and music — the institution 'will implement a scholarship system for non-EEA students' with awards that 'equal the amount of the increased tuition for non EEA-students', and 'Scholarships can be awarded to students in a bridging program, preparation program and master program'. (2) Government of Flanders Master Mind Scholarship — HOGENT is a participating institution, and 'All nationalities, except for Russian, can apply', so Tunisia is eligible.
programs.fundingLevel: Full (potentially) — the KASK non-EEA scholarship is explicitly sized to the increased tuition, and Master Mind adds a living grant on top
programs.stipend: KASK non-EEA scholarship: equals the increased non-EEA tuition, i.e. an effective waiver of up to c. €8,800/yr; crucially available to bridging and preparatory students too. Number of awards, selection criteria and deadline: UNVERIFIED — the linked scholarship PDF could not be text-extracted; contact paul.lamont@hogent.be or studiegeld@hogent.be. Master Mind: €10,225 per academic year PLUS a tuition-fee waiver (institution may charge only €136.50 for 2026-2027); 2 years for a 120-ECTS master. VERIFIED ELIGIBILITY HURDLE for Master Mind at Schools of Arts: IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 90 / B2 certificate, and GPA 3.5/4.0 from the most recent degree. Master Mind cannot be combined with Erasmus+/Erasmus Mundus, BAEF or Fulbright.
programs.facilities: Professionally equipped studios with extensive equipment collections; the music-production department has run since 1999 and is presented as a unique combination in Flanders of technique, musicality and creativity. External mentors and internships connect students to the working music industry. Specific console, monitoring and Atmos/immersive inventory: UNVERIFIED — not published. Alumni work as songwriters, performers, producers and composers.
programs.fitNotes: Still the strongest overall bet in this slice, and verification strengthened rather than weakened it: 64 of 120 credits are literally producing and a producing capstone; stage-one admission is dossier-only so his portfolio does the work before any travel; the non-EEA fee of €8,800.20 is confirmed and the school's own scholarship is confirmed to be sized to erase it, including for bridging students. Two honest caveats sharpened by this check. First, the master formally expects a bachelor in composing music, so September 2027 should be planned as entry into a bridging or preparatory year, not the master itself. Second, the much-cited 'no English test' advantage is real for admission but does NOT extend to Master Mind funding, which demands IELTS 6.5 and a 3.5/4.0 GPA — so if Master Mind is the funding plan, he must sit IELTS anyway. The KASK internal scholarship, which has no published language test, is therefore the more realistic money.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed on official KASK/School of Arts Gent pages: programme exists at master level in Ghent, 120 ECTS over two years with the exact module breakdown above; English-language master track with the quoted parity statement; degree requirement quoted verbatim; no formal English requirement with Vantage B2 recommended; bridging and preparatory routes quoted; portfolio must be digital with physical formats refused, plus max 1-page motivation letter; two-stage orientation test with dossier first; non-EEA fee €916.20 + €131.40/credit = €8,800.20 for 2026-2027; non-EEA scholarship equal to the increased tuition and available to bridging/preparatory/master students. CORRECTED: the 'four works' portfolio figure belongs to the BACHELOR admission test, not the master. NEWLY VERIFIED CAVEAT: Master Mind at Schools of Arts requires IELTS 6.5/TOEFL 90/B2 and GPA 3.5/4.0. NOT confirmed: master portfolio work count, scholarship award numbers and deadlines (PDF unreadable), studio inventory, 2027 orientation-test dates.

programs.program: Master of Arts in Audiovisual Arts – Sound Design (Master in de Audiovisuele Kunsten, afstudeerrichting Sound Design)
programs.university: RITCS – Royal Institute for Theatre, Cinema and Sound (Erasmushogeschool Brussel)
programs.degree: MA in Audiovisual Arts, specialisation Sound Design
programs.durationEcts: Academic bachelor 180 ECTS + 1 master year — 3+1 structure. The master year is not given an explicit ECTS figure on any RITCS page reachable; 60 ECTS is the Flemish standard and the Erasmushogeschool fee tables are built on a 60-credit year, but the programme page itself does not state it. Treat 60 ECTS as strongly indicated, not published.
programs.language: Dutch only. Confirmed verbatim on the English-language page: 'All classes are in Dutch.' The Dutch page confirms the programme language as Nederlands. There is no English track.
programs.institutionType: Film school / school of arts within Erasmushogeschool Brussel (associated with Vrije Universiteit Brussel)
programs.focus: Film & Game Sound; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering (film-oriented)
programs.whatYouStudy: Confirmed. The bachelor builds recording, editing and mixing for documentary and fiction, dialogue editing and film mixing 'using state-of-the-art tools and infrastructure'. The master year, quoted: 'In het masterjaar benader je sound design vanuit foley-creatie en doe je ervaring op met surround sound' — foley creation and surround sound, with music recording playing a more prominent role, development of a personal sound signature, and 'a final project that you learn to defend before a jury from the professional field'. Sound Design is one of eight specialisations (Animatiefilm, Cinematografie, Editing, Productie, Radio, Regie, Schrijven, Sound design), so sound students cut and mix classmates' films.
programs.entryRequirements: Artistic entrance test (toelatingsproef) required, in three parts. Degree requirement and any language certification: UNVERIFIED on the pages reachable; an academic bachelor in audiovisual arts is the normal route given the 3+1 structure. The decisive practical requirement is Dutch, since all teaching and the week-long assessment are in Dutch.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: UNVERIFIED — RITCS publishes no statement about applicants from non-arts backgrounds. In practice this is moot: the Dutch-only instruction and the Dutch-language workshop week are the binding barriers, not the discipline of the bachelor.
programs.portfolioSpec: A DOSSIER is one of three components of the artistic admission test. Note the precise wording is 'een dossier', not a portfolio per se. Number of works, formats, durations and what the dossier must contain: UNVERIFIED — not published. Published selection criteria are qualitative: creativity, curiosity, artistic feeling, cultural background, motivation and enthusiasm, assessed by a jury of teachers and makers.
programs.auditionSpec: Confirmed verbatim: 'The admission test consists of three parts: a dossier, an intake or selection interview and a workshop week' (Dutch: 'een dossier, een intake- of selectiegesprek en een werkweek'). The WORKSHOP WEEK is a week-long on-site assessment in Brussels, conducted in Dutch — the most demanding admission format in this slice by a wide margin.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — not published on any RITCS page reachable.
programs.deadline: UNVERIFIED — no application deadline or toelatingsproef date is published for the master. Flemish schools of arts typically run entrance tests in spring and late summer, but nothing specific to 2027 is published. Contact RITCS directly. Master Mind 2027-2028 call: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.tuitionIntl: NOW VERIFIED and it is the decisive number. RITCS states for 2026-2027: 'As student met een niet-EER-nationaliteit betaal je een verhoogd inschrijvingsgeld. Voor 60 studiepunten bedraagt dit € 17.501,40' — €17,501.40 for a 60-credit year for non-EEA students. By comparison an EEA non-scholarship student pays €1,181.40 for the same 60 credits. This corrects the previous UNVERIFIED entry and makes RITCS roughly twice the price of ArtEZ and double KASK.
programs.scholarship: Government of Flanders Master Mind Scholarship is the only route found. Eligibility is institution-wide rather than programme-specific: 'Applications will be accepted from all Flemish universities, Schools of Arts and the Antwerp Maritime Academy', and 'All nationalities, except for Russian, can apply', so RITCS as a Flemish School of Arts is in principle a valid host and Tunisia is an eligible nationality. RITCS's own participation and deadline are still not individually listed. No RITCS-internal non-EEA scholarship was found, in contrast to KASK.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial at best (Master Mind only, and unconfirmed at institution level)
programs.stipend: Master Mind, if awarded: €10,225 per academic year plus a tuition-fee waiver capping the institution's charge at €136.50 for 2026-2027; duration one academic year for a 60-ECTS master. Requirements for Schools of Arts: IELTS 6.5 / TOEFL 90 / B2 certification and GPA 3.5/4.0. Note the mismatch — the scholarship's language test is in ENGLISH, while the programme is taught entirely in DUTCH, so passing the Master Mind language bar does not make him able to follow the course. Without Master Mind the full €17,501.40 is self-pay.
programs.facilities: 'State-of-the-art tools and infrastructure' for sound recording, dialogue editing and film mixing; foley creation and surround sound facilities in the master year. Embedded in a working film school with eight specialisations, so sound students work on real fiction and documentary productions with classmates. Specific studio, console and immersive-format inventory: UNVERIFIED. RITCS is one of Belgium's two leading film schools.
programs.fitNotes: Verification confirmed the diagnosis and added a second blocker. The programme is genuinely excellent for film sound — foley, surround, a defended final project inside a real film school — but 'All classes are in Dutch', which he does not speak, and admission requires a week-long on-site workshop in Brussels conducted in Dutch. The newly verified fee of €17,501.40 per year for non-EEA students is the highest in this slice by a large margin, and unlike KASK there is no institutional scholarship sized to offset it; the only funding is Master Mind, whose 3.5/4.0 GPA and IELTS 6.5 bars are demanding and whose English test is irrelevant to a Dutch-taught degree. Effectively blocked for September 2027. Worth knowing about only if he commits to Dutch over several years.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed on official RITCS and Erasmushogeschool pages: the Sound Design specialisation exists within the academic bachelor/master Audiovisual Arts at RITCS in Brussels; 'All classes are in Dutch'; master-year content (foley, surround, music recording, jury-defended final project) quoted; three-part admission test (dossier, intake/selection interview, workshop week) quoted in both languages; Sound Design is one of eight specialisations; non-EEA tuition €17,501.40 for 60 credits in 2026-2027 quoted verbatim from the RITCS studiegelden page; Master Mind accepts applications from all Flemish Schools of Arts and all nationalities except Russian. programs.program: Master en Musique – Musiques appliquées et interactives (Applied and Interactive Music)

programs.durationEcts: Master following a bachelier, within the domain's Bachelier / Master / Master à finalité spécialisée structure. programs.language: French
programs.institutionType: Conservatoire / école supérieure des arts (public, Wallonia-Brussels Federation)
programs.focus: Music Production; Sound Design; Film/Game Sound; Electronic Music — composition for image, live arts and new technologies
programs.whatYouStudy: Confirmed and sharpened. Quoted: 'Le programme de Bachelier et de Master s'adresse aux musicien·ne·s désireux de développer une approche créative' — so a Master exists. The curriculum 'combine l'apprentissage des fondamentaux (écriture, orchestration, production sonore) et la réalisation de projets concrets', i.e. writing, orchestration and SOUND PRODUCTION alongside concrete project work, with collaborations, masterclasses, festival visits and individualised guidance on a final artistic project. ARTS² presents the section as unique in Belgium, focused on composition for image, performing arts and new technologies. Graduates work as composers for cinema, theatre, video games, advertising and interactive media, in sound design and sound creation, or in music education. Detailed course list and studio inventory: still UNVERIFIED (PDF grids not parsed).
programs.entryRequirements: Admission is subject to an épreuve d'admission. First complete the online registration form at artsaucarre.horizon.wbe.be, supplying diplomas, CV, experience, artistic background and transcripts of prior higher education; each domain then reviews submissions and schedules candidates for exams. Documents required for non-first-year entry, confirmed: ID/passport copy both sides (passport for non-EU), passport photo, secondary-education certificate or equivalent, evidence of prior artistic training with supporting documentation, records of previous NON-ARTISTIC higher education with justification, documentation covering activities from the past five years, and a debt-clearance letter if previously enrolled in Wallonia-Brussels. Full enrolment requires submitting administrative documents, paying tuition and signing the PAE (annual study plan).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — no bar found, and the dossier form explicitly anticipates it. ARTS² publishes no statement excluding non-music bachelors, and the required-documents list expressly asks for 'records of previous non-artistic higher education with justification', which shows candidates arriving from non-artistic degrees are a contemplated case. The real gate is the jury's épreuve d'admission. SEPARATE AND IMPORTANT: for the WBI grant specifically, ARTS² states the bachelor must be 'relevant and directly related to the Master's programme applied for' — so a software-engineering BSc may satisfy the school's admission jury while still weakening the scholarship application. Ask the section at info@artsaucarre.be.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — each domain and option sets its own exam requirements and the Musiques appliquées page publishes none. Must be requested from the section (info@artsaucarre.be). What IS required in the dossier: documentation of prior artistic training and of activities over the past five years. For a candidate with no music degree, that five-year activity record is where his self-produced work must be evidenced.
programs.auditionSpec: LIVE admission exam on site in Mons. Confirmed verbatim: 'Des épreuves d'admission sont organisées chaque année en mai et en septembre' — sessions every year in May and September, so the schedule is recurring rather than cycle-specific. Registration for the exam is via the online form; candidates are then scheduled by the domain. Exam content for this section: UNVERIFIED. April open days are recommended for meeting the teaching team.
programs.applicationOpens: Online registration form at artsaucarre.horizon.wbe.be, completed before sitting the admission exam. For the MASTER IN – WBI grant, the application goes to the institution (service.erasmus@artsaucarre.be), on a separate and much earlier timetable.
programs.deadline: Admission exams recur each May and September, so the May 2027 and September 2027 sessions are the relevant ones for a September 2027 start — this is a standing schedule, not a stale date. Tuition payment milestones published for 2026-27: €50 minimum deposit by 15 September 2026, balance plus the non-EU supplement by 15 January 2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm equivalent 2027-28 dates. CRITICAL EARLY DEADLINE: the MASTER IN – WBI grant application had to reach the institution by 31 March 2026 for 2026-2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect roughly 31 March 2027 for a September 2027 start, i.e. he must apply for the money BEFORE the May admission exam.
programs.tuitionIntl: €1,194 annual registration fee + mandatory supplementary contribution of €4,175 for non-EU students = c. €5,369/year for 2026-2027 (amounts indicative, pending final adoption by the Wallonia-Brussels Federation Parliament). The €4,175 supplement is waived for nationals of UN Least Developed Countries, holders of Wallonia-Brussels Federation secondary diplomas, and Wallonia-Brussels International scholarship holders. Tunisia is NOT an LDC, so he pays it unless he wins a WBI scholarship — in which case his cost falls to €1,194.
programs.scholarship: MAJOR FINDING ON VERIFICATION: the MASTER IN – WBI Grant. ARTS² is a confirmed host institution on the official Study in Belgium list, with 'All programmes available at ARTS²' eligible under regular admission conditions; institutional contact service.erasmus@artsaucarre.be. Decisively, TUNISIA IS ONE OF THE PRIORITY COUNTRIES for this grant (priority list: Brazil, Canada, Chile, Colombia, South Korea, Japan, Lebanon, Morocco, Mexico, United Kingdom, Switzerland, Taiwan, TUNISIA, USA). Holding a WBI scholarship also waives the €4,175 non-EU supplement. This was recorded as UNVERIFIED before and is the single most decision-relevant correction in this batch.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial by default; effectively Full if the MASTER IN – WBI grant is won (€10,020/yr living grant + €4,175 supplement waived, leaving €1,194 tuition)
programs.stipend: MASTER IN – WBI Grant: €10,020 per year, paid in 12 monthly instalments into a euro bank account. WBI also covers health insurance (mutual subrogation), repatriation and personal liability cover, and grants exemption from the Immigration Office administrative fee. NOT covered: visa fees and travel, which the candidate must advance; travel insurance. WBI states plainly that the grant 'does not cover the full costs of one academic year; therefore, the laureate must supplement these funds with personal resources.' Incompatible with other WBI or ARES support. Eligibility: a recognised foreign bachelor obtained no more than five years before the programme starts (he qualifies, graduating 2026), admission to the target master, and — per ARTS² — a bachelor 'relevant and directly related to the Master's programme applied for'. Deadline 31 March (2026 date for the 2026-27 cycle).
programs.facilities: Teaching team of practising composers: Thomas Foguenne, Yves Gourmeur and Fabian Fiorini, assisted by Sarah Triquet and Simon Vanneste, with further instructors covering sound design, recording techniques, mixing and interactive technologies — all confirmed on the section page. Presented as the only training of its kind in Belgium. Studio, console and equipment inventory: UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Upgraded to the top tier on verification, alongside KASK, and for a different reason: the money. Three things now line up. It is taught in FRENCH, which he speaks fluently, so no IELTS/TOEFL is on the critical path at all — a cleaner advantage than KASK's, where Master Mind reintroduces an English test. Base cost is c. €5,369/yr, half the Dutch conservatoires. And ARTS² is a confirmed host for the MASTER IN – WBI grant, for which Tunisia is an explicit priority country, worth €10,020/yr plus insurance plus a waiver of the €4,175 supplement — a near-full package. The content is genuinely applied: écriture, orchestration and production sonore, composing and sound design for film, games, theatre, advertising and interactive media. Two caveats remain honest. Everything about the admission exam and portfolio is unpublished and must be extracted by email. And the WBI condition that the bachelor be 'relevant and directly related' to the master is a real risk for a software-engineering graduate — he should build the argument that software engineering is directly relevant to INTERACTIVE music and game audio, which for this specific section is a defensible case. Act early: the WBI deadline (c. 31 March) falls before the May admission exam.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed on official ARTS² and Study in Belgium pages: the Musiques appliquées et interactives section exists with both Bachelier and Master, in French, at Mons; curriculum framing and the five named composition staff quoted; admission exams held every year in May and September, quoted; the full non-first-year dossier document list, including the requirement to document previous non-artistic higher education; tuition €1,194 + €4,175 non-EU supplement for 2026-2027 with the three exemption categories; payment milestones 15 September 2026 and 15 January 2027. The technical course spine — techniques de prise de son, techniques de synthèse, informatique musicale, spatialisation — is genuinely transferable craft, and his software background would be an asset in informatique musicale. Cost is c. €5,369/yr, or c. €1,194 plus a €10,020 living grant if the WBI grant lands, and there is no English-test barrier. But acousmatic music on fixed media is art music for concert diffusion, not club music: this would give him a serious sonic-craft education while pointing away from DJing and commercial production. Also, the WBI requirement that the bachelor be 'directly related' to the master is harder to argue here than for the interactive-music section. Choose the Mons Musiques appliquées section over this one unless he genuinely wants to compose art music.

programs.program: Master en Son — three separate 60-credit sound masters: Son Studio, Son Sono, and Cinéma Son (the first two presented on the faculty page under 'Master Radio-Télévision-Multimédia Son')
programs.university: IAD – Institut des Arts de Diffusion
programs.degree: Master (2nd cycle) in sound for audiovisual media
programs.durationEcts: 60 crédits each — confirmed verbatim on the IAD sound faculty page — following a 180-ECTS professional bachelor in sound. A 3+1 structure.
programs.language: French
programs.institutionType: Film school / école supérieure des arts (Wallonia-Brussels Federation)
programs.focus: Recording/Engineering (studio); Live sound reinforcement; Film & Game Sound; Sound Design
programs.whatYouStudy: IAD's sound training covers the full sound-engineer profession: studio and live recording, mixing, editing, mastering, event sound reinforcement (sonorisation) and sound design, training 'sound engineers who master sound recording tools and techniques in radio, television and multimedia, as well as editors and sound mixers who master editing and sound mixing tools'. The master combines artistic and technical coursework with workshops, an in-depth internship more advanced than at bachelor level, a final work evaluated by a jury of industry professionals, and a written thesis. Students collaborate with IAD's multimedia, theatre and directing programmes on real productions. The three orientations split the field: Son Studio is closest to music recording and mixing, Son Sono covers live sound, Cinéma Son covers film sound.
programs.entryRequirements: Confirmed verbatim, and it is the most degree-agnostic wording in this whole slice: 'La plupart des masters 60 ou 120 organisés à l'IAD sont ouverts aux étudiants titulaires d'un bachelier' — most 60- or 120-credit masters at IAD are open to holders of a bachelor's degree. The only stated exception is the teaching master (Section 5), which requires an existing master. Application is by email to admissions-masters@iad-arts.be with: identity photo, CV, motivation letter, secondary-education diploma, the relevant degree, ID copy, birth certificate, prior academic records, and the portfolio. Candidates selected on file and works are then auditioned by a jury.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes on paper — the strongest published position in this slice. IAD's wording is degree-agnostic ('La plupart des masters 60 ou 120 organisés à l'IAD sont ouverts aux étudiants titulaires d'un bachelier') and imposes no requirement for a music, sound or arts bachelor. The real gate is the portfolio, which must prove technical and artistic ability in the chosen orientation, and the assumed technical baseline is that of IAD's own 180-ECTS sound bachelor.
programs.portfolioSpec: Confirmed verbatim: 'un book de travaux aboutis qui prouvent vos aptitudes techniques et artistiques' — a portfolio of COMPLETED works proving technical and artistic aptitude, specific to the chosen orientation. Submitted alongside identity photo, CV, motivation letter, diplomas, ID and birth certificate. Number of works, durations and formats: UNVERIFIED — not published.
programs.auditionSpec: Two-stage with a mandatory IN-PERSON jury at Louvain-la-Neuve. Candidates are first selected on the basis of their file and works; those shortlisted are then auditioned by a jury. For the 2026-2027 intake the admission commissions ran in person from 24 August to 11 September 2026, with dates communicated individually by email. Requires travel to Belgium at the very end of the summer.
programs.applicationOpens: 4 May for the 2026-2027 intake (applications by email to admissions-masters@iad-arts.be). Application deposit for first-year masters is free.
programs.deadline: Applications 4 May – 14 August 2026; in-person admission juries 24 August – 11 September 2026 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For a September 2027 start expect roughly 4 May – 14 August 2027 with juries late August to mid-September 2027. Non-EU supplementary contribution must be paid by 31 January.
programs.tuitionIntl: NOW VERIFIED, correcting the previous entry. IAD publishes for 2026-2027: standard minerval €1,194 per academic year (covering student card, basic technical and artistic materials, software licences and IT services), plus a mandatory €4,175 annual supplementary contribution for non-EU students = c. €5,369/year. Payment: minimum €50 deposit by 31 October, balance by 31 January; the non-EU contribution is due by 31 January. IAD notes these 2026-2027 amounts are provisional pending final parliamentary approval by the Wallonia-Brussels Federation.
programs.scholarship: None found that he can realistically use — and this is a correction in the negative direction. The €4,175 supplement is waived for several categories IAD lists explicitly: 'ressortissants d'un pays membre de la liste LDC (ONU, pays les moins avancés)', long-term residents of Belgium, recognised refugees or holders of subsidiary protection, holders of a Wallonie-Bruxelles International scholarship, and students with qualifying EU-citizen parents. Tunisia is not an LDC, so only the WBI route applies. CRITICAL: IAD does NOT appear on the official list of MASTER IN – WBI grant host institutions (which does include ARTS², La Cambre, INSAS and other arts schools), so the main WBI master's scholarship is not available here. No IAD-internal scholarship for non-EU students was found.
programs.fundingLevel: None found — treat as SELF-PAY FALLBACK
programs.stipend: No stipend identified. The only financial relief available in principle is the €4,175 waiver for WBI scholarship holders, but the flagship MASTER IN – WBI grant cannot be used at IAD because IAD is not a listed host institution. Budget the full c. €5,369/year plus living costs in Louvain-la-Neuve as self-pay, plus travel to Belgium for the in-person jury.
programs.facilities: IAD is a full film and broadcast school teaching cinema, television, radio, theatre, 2D/3D animation, VFX and web, with three distinct 60-credit sound masters (studio, live sound, film sound) — an unusually granular offer for sound specifically. Master students undertake an advanced internship and defend a final work before a professional jury, and work across the school's multimedia, theatre and directing programmes. Specific studio, console and immersive inventory: UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Confirmed as a serious, very practical French-language route into professional audio, with the most welcoming admission wording anywhere in this slice — most IAD masters are open to any bachelor's holder, so his software-engineering BSc is not automatically disqualifying, and Son Studio is the orientation closest to music recording and mixing. Cost is now confirmed at a modest c. €5,369/yr and there is no English-test barrier. But verification made the funding picture worse rather than better: IAD is absent from the MASTER IN – WBI host-institution list, so the €10,020 grant that makes ARTS² so attractive simply cannot be used here, and no IAD-internal scholarship exists. That makes IAD a self-pay option. Add the in-person jury in Louvain-la-Neuve in late August/early September and a 60-credit master built on top of IAD's own three-year sound bachelor — meaning the assumed technical baseline is high and his portfolio must genuinely prove it — and this ranks below both ARTS² Musiques appliquées and KASK for him. Strong programme, weak funding fit.

Confirmed on official IAD pages: three sound masters exist (Son Studio, Son Sono, Cinéma Son), 60 crédits each, in French at Louvain-la-Neuve; the degree-agnostic admission wording quoted verbatim; the required-documents list and the portfolio wording 'un book de travaux aboutis qui prouvent vos aptitudes techniques et artistiques'; the two-stage file-then-in-person-jury process; application window 4 May – 14 August 2026 with juries 24 August – 11 September 2026; minerval €1,194 plus €4,175 non-EU supplement for 2026-2027 with payment deadlines and the full exemption list. programs.program: Master of Music (cand. musicae), Music Creation
programs.university: Rhythmic Music Conservatory (Rytmisk Musikkonservatorium, RMC)
programs.institutionType: Conservatory (state conservatoire under the Danish Ministry of Culture)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS. Confirmed on page: "The programme lasts two years (120 ECTS), is a full-time study programme with compulsory attendance".
programs.language: Danish-dominant. RMC's admission page states applications are accepted in "Danish, Norwegian, Swedish and English" and that "The entrance exam is usually held in Danish but can be conducted in English if you do not speak Danish." RMC publishes NO statement that the degree itself is delivered in English (unlike RDAM, which does). Full-degree English delivery remains UNVERIFIED and should be assumed to be Danish unless RMC confirms otherwise in writing.
programs.focus: Music Production / Electronic Music - composition, arrangement and production across all genres
programs.whatYouStudy: Two-year artistic master built on your own creative practice: Artistic Development Practice, Music Creation (composition, arrangement, instrumentation, lyrics, technology), Entrepreneurship, an External Module carried out with a music/cultural-industry partner, electives, and a concluding Master's Project presented publicly. RMC has recording studios and technology labs for electronic music and multimedia. VERY small intake: RMC's own 2025 admission statistics show 659 applicants for 97 places across nine programmes, with Composition (the Danish-language name covering this creation track) taking 8 places from 191 applicants - roughly a 4% admit rate. The detailed ECTS split per module (30/10/10/30/10/30) was NOT restated on the page fetched and should be treated as unconfirmed.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed Bachelor's degree in music from RMC, another Danish music conservatory, or a foreign music conservatory; or expected completion by 1 July of the entry year. Discretionary clause, quoted exactly: "Based on a specific assessment, the conservatory may recognise other artistically based Bachelor's degrees in music as qualifying." NOTE the corrected wording - it says other artistically based bachelor's degrees IN MUSIC, which is narrower than a general artistic-degree clause. Application fee DKK 600 per programme, non-refundable after the deadline. No IELTS/TOEFL requirement is published by RMC.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO, effectively. The published requirement is a bachelor's in music, and the only flexibility is "other artistically based Bachelor's degrees IN MUSIC" - a BSc Software Engineering is neither artistic nor in music. On the verified wording there is no route in for his degree. He would have to obtain a written pre-assessment from RMC before spending the DKK 600 fee, and the realistic answer is no.
programs.portfolioSpec: Round 1, digital: "2-3 music examples that you have composed, arranged and produced yourself", MP3 format, 10 minutes total maximum. Optional sheet music / scores / graphic notation / lyrics as PDF "if included in your work". Hard rule quoted exactly: "A minimum of one-third of the music submitted in your portfolio must be composed for and performed by others." Co-writes are prohibited. (The often-quoted line that RMC "also accepts applicants who work exclusively on computers" was NOT re-confirmed on the page fetched in July 2026 - treat it as unverified and ask RMC directly, because it is the single sentence that would make this programme viable for a laptop producer.)
programs.auditionSpec: LIVE, IN PERSON at RMC in Copenhagen. Round 2 lasts 25 minutes: a 10-minute presentation of your work (live, recording or a combination), a 5-minute presentation of artistic context, and a 10-minute interview. Explicit rule: "The works presented must not be identical to the material you uploaded to your first-round portfolio" - so a second body of work is required. Travel to Denmark at his own cost.
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 10,000 per study year for the Master programme, non-EU/EEA. (Bachelor is EUR 11,000.) Free for Danish, EU/EEA and Swiss citizens. Confirmed on rmc.dk/en/tuition.
programs.scholarship: None found. programs.language: English - CONFIRMED. RDAM's language-requirements page states: "All programmes, except the Music Teacher Programme, are available in English." programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO. The published prerequisite is a Tonmeister bachelor from RDAM, an equivalent from a Danish academy, or an equivalent Tonmeister BMus from abroad. This is the best-fitting curriculum in the slice and the hardest gate in it.

Each of the examples must be at least 7 minutes." Non-EU/EEA applicants must ADDITIONALLY submit a production plan containing "a simple time schedule, a list of the equipment/software used and a list of the participants and their roles". The certified audiogram is a Bachelor-level requirement, not master.
programs.auditionSpec: Principal-study examination, approximately 30 minutes including voting, built around a 20-minute discussion of the submitted works plus questions on your technical and musical standpoint, with an optional 5-minute conversation about motivation and career. Non-EU/EEA applicants audition ONLINE (no travel needed) and may face "an extra interview focusing on the musical entrance examination, including piano, ear training/solfege and theory". EU/EEA applicants audition in person. Graded on the Danish 7-point scale by two internal examiners.
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 11,100 per academic year for the Tonmeister/Sound Engineer MASTER, non-EU/EEA - confirmed on the 2026-2027 fee table. Paid in two instalments: 1 June (new students; 15 June for continuing) and 1 September. For context the master fee table spans EUR 11,000 (Organ) to EUR 14,900 (Voice). Free for EU/EEA citizens.

programs.verificationNotes: CONFIRMED on dkdm.dk/en/entrance-examinations-tonmeister: the two-production portfolio (one rhythmic, one classical, each at least 7 minutes), the extra production plan for non-EU/EEA applicants with its three required contents, the ~30-minute audition with 20-minute work discussion, online auditioning for non-EU/EEA applicants with a possible extra piano/ear-training/theory interview, and grading on the Danish 7-point scale by two internal examiners.
