Useful now for one reason: its 1 December 2026 deadline is real and published, so it is worth an email to admission@dkdm.dk to get a written ruling on whether any bridging route exists.

programs.program: MSc in Medialogy - specialisation in Sound and Music Computing

Confirmed SMC-track modules: Immersive Sonic Experiences (15 ECTS), Sonic Interaction Design (5 ECTS), Sound and Music Perception and Cognition (5 ECTS, also available as a general-track first-semester elective). AAU's problem-based learning means every semester is built around a group project. NOTE: the module names previously reported (New Interfaces for Musical Expression, Embodied Interaction, Sound and Music Signal Analysis, Physical Models for Sound Synthesis) belong to the OLD standalone SMC engineering curriculum, not the current Medialogy specialisation - do not rely on them. Admission WITHOUT direct access is listed for BSc Medialogy (Aalborg), Electronic Engineering, and Electronic Systems Engineering, provided the applicant has competencies in at least two of: Programming (min 10 ECTS), Technical knowledge of media technologies (min 10 ECTS), Interaction Design / User Experience Design methods (min 10 ECTS). Everyone else falls under: "Applicants with other backgrounds will be assessed individually by the Study Board of Media Technology." AAU's public summary phrases the baseline as "a Bachelor's in Medialogy or the like". English proficiency documentation required, equivalent to Danish B-level (roughly IELTS 6.5 - confirm the exact threshold with AAU). Non-EU applicants also pay an application fee.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES on the music question - no music degree, no music theory, no audition and no portfolio are required anywhere in this programme. But the earlier claim that "Datalogi (computer science)" and "Software" are named qualifying bachelors is NOT supported by the current curriculum, which names only Medialogy, Electronic Engineering and Electronic Systems Engineering. A BSc Software Engineering therefore enters through the discretionary route: "Applicants with other backgrounds will be assessed individually by the Study Board of Media Technology." His case is strong on the substance - he will comfortably clear the Programming (min 10 ECTS) competency and can likely argue media technologies and/or UX design from his coursework - but it is an individual assessment, not an entitlement. He should email mediatek-studvejlcph@create.aau.dk with his transcript in autumn 2026 for a pre-assessment.
programs.portfolioSpec: None. No portfolio of works is requested anywhere on the admission pages - admission runs on transcripts, the ECTS competency check and English documentation.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition, no live test, no on-site component.

PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date.
programs.verificationNotes: CONFIRMED on en.aau.dk/education/master/medialogy-cph: the programme exists at master level in Copenhagen, English-taught, 2 years / 120 ECTS, and the Sound and Music Computing specialisation chosen after semester 1. CONFIRMED on the official 2025 curriculum (studieordninger.aau.dk/2025/53/5887): the full four-semester structure, the SMC modules Immersive Sonic Experiences / Sonic Interaction Design / Sound and Music Perception and Cognition, and the CORRECTED qualifying-bachelor list with the 10-ECTS competency thresholds. CONFIRMED on students.aau.dk: the standalone SMC engineering MSc is "closed for admission from 2024" and replaced by this specialisation. CONFIRMED on en.aau.dk/education/apply/master/finance-and-fees: DKK 57,850 per semester / DKK 115,700 per year for technical programmes, the corrected 14-day payment deadline for new students, the refund tiers, ~15 scholarships per year, the tuition waiver plus DKK 11,225/month 2026 stipend, and automatic consideration with no separate application. CONFIRMED on en.aau.dk/education/apply/master/how-and-when-to-apply: portal opens medio December, non-EU deadline 15 January 23:59 CET with answers by 10 April, EU deadline 1 March with answers by 10 June. NOT CONFIRMED: any intake year on the deadline pages; the exact English test score threshold; the application fee amount; the previously reported industry-destination list (Bang & Olufsen, IO Interactive etc.), which did not appear in the fetched text.
programs.fitNotes: Still by far the best real option for him in the Nordics, but downgraded from A after verification. What holds up: English-taught, no audition, no portfolio, no music degree needed, and a genuine fully-funded path (tuition waiver plus about EUR 1,500/month) with automatic consideration and no extra application. What changed: his BSc Software Engineering is NOT on the published qualifying list - only Medialogy, Electronic Engineering and Electronic Systems Engineering are - so he enters via individual assessment by the Study Board of Media Technology. He should get that pre-assessment in writing before December 2026. The second honest caveat is unchanged: this is sound and music COMPUTING - immersive audio, sonic interaction design, perception and cognition, project-based engineering work - not DJing, not mixing records, not A&R. It makes him an audio developer or technical sound designer who produces on the side. Use it as the funded backbone of his plan, with craft learned independently; if the scholarship does not land, EUR 15,490/yr is a hard self-pay number.

programs.auditionSpec: Test 2 - a conversation with the jury, held ONLINE via Zoom, approximately 30 minutes, based on your portfolio material, covering a deeper presentation of the portfolio, your intended degree project, and questions about the programme. programs.tuitionIntl: SEK 264,000 per academic year for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens - confirmed on KMH's fees page ("The tuition fee is currently 264 000 SEK/academic year"). Application fee SEK 900, paid via universityadmissions.se. EU/EEA and Swiss citizens pay neither.
programs.scholarship: CONFIRMED and now detailed: KMH awards approximately THREE tuition-fee scholarships per academic year, each covering the full programme tuition cost for one student. Process: eligible students are INVITED to apply after the second selection notification (typically released mid-May) and must submit by around 1 June, providing a one-page CV and a motivational letter. programs.program: Master Radio Télévision Multimédia – spécialité Son
programs.university: INSAS – Institut National Supérieur des Arts du Spectacle et des Techniques de Diffusion
programs.degree: Master de type long (2nd cycle), 60 crédits
programs.durationEcts: 1 year / 60 credits — CONFIRMED. The official 2025-26 curriculum annexe is headed "Radio Télévision Multimedia - Son / Master de Type long - 60 crédits" and contains a single teaching block, "Bloc M1 60 crédits".
programs.language: French — CONFIRMED. Every teaching unit in the official curriculum annexe states "Langue d'enseignement et d'évaluation: Français". The admissions FAQ adds: "La quasi-totalité des cursus est dispensée en langue française (tant les cours artistiques, techniques et généraux)." Notably: "Il n'y a pas de test de langue" — no IELTS/TOEFL/DELF certificate is required, only "une bonne connaissance de la langue française".
programs.institutionType: Film / performing-arts school — public national higher institute of the Wallonia-Brussels Federation
programs.focus: Film & Game Sound; Recording/Engineering; Sound Design for radio, TV and multimedia; some Immersive Audio (5.1) and Sonic Arts
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED from the official curriculum annexe (Annexe-1_25-26_Master-RTM-Son.pdf). The year is dominated by a 30-credit artistic final project (TAFE, 55% of the weighting) split across three domains: "Prise de son à finalité audiovisuelle sur les productions de TFE de l'INSAS ou environnement sonore de productions théâtrales"; "Post-production sur des productions de l'INSAS"; and "Réalisation radiophonique et/ou prise de son musicale". The full list of teaching units is: Pratique artistique de la prise et du traitement (30 cr); Créations sonores; Conception et analyse de mixage 5.1; Création sonore en spectacle vivant; Conception du son cinéma; Projection et cinéma numérique; Étude de cas; Esthétique musicale; Droit d'auteur; Droit et communication des institutions culturelles; Droit social; Stage et Travail écrit de fin d'études (TEFE). Internships are compulsory and must be spread across cinema (shoot or post), live broadcast radio/TV, and non-image sound (music, theatre, live performance). Assessment is largely by external artistic jury (JAE). The programme is explicitly "la prolongation naturelle du cycle de Bachelier" — it assumes three prior years of INSAS-level sound training.
programs.entryRequirements: "Un diplôme de niveau bachelier (ou équivalent reconnu – 180 ECTS)", strong French, and success in the admission tests, subject to capacity. The admissions FAQ is far more restrictive than the public page: "En Master; Le candidat dispose d'un bachelier ou d'une licence DANS LE CURSUS VISÉ. Sa formation ne peut pas être exclusivement théorique. Le candidat doit avoir les prérequis équivalents à ceux obtenus au bout de trois années de bachelier à l'INSAS." Candidates with no diploma may build a VAE dossier ("Valorisation des Acquis de l'Expérience, professionnelle et personnelle sur 5 années en lien avec le cursus visé").
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — this is the decisive correction to the earlier draft. INSAS's own admissions FAQ states: "nous attirons votre attention, que les candidatures au parcours académique trop théoriques seront éconduites et ces candidats seront invités à candidater en première année de bachelier. Sauf pour les masters orphelins (TTC/CIN ecriture, prod, RTM RRTV, Danse)." The five "masters orphelins" that DO accept an unrelated, theoretical bachelor are named exactly: Cinéma–Écriture (120), Cinéma–Gestion de Production (120), RTM–Réalisation Radio Télévision (60), TTC–Gestion de Production (60), TTC–Écriture (120). RTM–SON IS NOT ON THAT LIST. For Son, the rule is the strict one: a bachelor in the field, not exclusively theoretical, with prerequisites equal to three years of INSAS bachelor. A BSc in Software Engineering with no sound training is precisely the profile the FAQ says will be "éconduites" and redirected to bachelor year 1. The "et/ou personal/professional experience" wording on the public page is real but is operationalised as the 5-year VAE route, which he cannot meet.
programs.portfolioSpec: Partly verified. Selection is in two phases; phase 1 is a dossier review resting "essentiellement sur l'analyse du dossier artistique du candidat et des acquis d'apprentissage de son parcours académique et personnel antérieur". The sister RTM specialty publishes the file constraint "1 PDF file of 20 MB maximum" for the artistic dossier (portfolio, scenarios, photographic work or internet links); the Son-specific list of required works, durations and formats is NOT published — the "Dossier artistique et épreuves d'admissions" detail page is behind the applicant portal. Contact admissions.ccm@insas.be.
programs.auditionSpec: On-site in Brussels, mandatory, and substantial. Two-phase process: dossier review (phase 1), then admission tests (phase 2) whose format is set by each cursus's jury. For the technical sections the FAQ confirms scientific tests: "les épreuves scientifiques sont principalement une manière de mieux connaître les profils des candidat·e·s" for "section Image/Réalisation/Son/Montage/Scripte", and warns these cursus contain maths, electricity and optics courses. A €50 fee is payable to sit phase 2. The "~600 candidates per year" figure in the earlier draft could NOT be confirmed on any INSAS page and should be dropped.
programs.applicationOpens: 9 March 2026 for the 2026-2027 intake — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (expect early March 2027 for September 2027 entry)
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Verified 2026-2027 calendar: complete administrative + artistic dossier in the applicant portal between 9 March 2026 and 5 May 2026 before 12:00; phase 1 results mid-June 2026; €50 test fee payable by 1 July 2026; admission tests 17 August – 11 September 2026; final results by 11 September 2026; enrolment by 31 October 2026. Expect the same shape for 2027, i.e. dossier due early May 2027 and on-site tests in Brussels in late August 2027.
programs.tuitionIntl: €5,369 for 2026-2027 — VERIFIED on the INSAS fees page. Standard minerval €1,194 (reduced to €835 / €374 / €0 on means-tested conditions) PLUS a supplementary contribution of €4,175/year for non-EU non-assimilated students. Payment: €50 deposit by 31 October 2026, balance €4,125 by 1 February 2027. Exemptions from the €4,175 supplement include UN Least Developed Countries (Tunisia does NOT qualify) and, importantly, holders of a Wallonie-Bruxelles International scholarship. By far the cheapest of the three programmes in this slice.
programs.scholarship: Bourse Master IN – Wallonie-Bruxelles International (WBI). Tunisia is explicitly named a priority partner country. INSAS's own fees page lists WBI scholarship holders among those exempt from the €4,175 non-EU supplement, so the two stack. Conditions: bachelor obtained no more than five years before the start of the programme (he qualifies, graduating 2026); must not already be studying in Belgium; a school of arts is an eligible host. Deadline 31 March 2026 for 2026-2027 — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect 31 March 2027 for the September 2027 intake.
programs.stipend: WBI Master IN: €10,000 per academic year, renewable on condition, plus full insurance cover (health, repatriation, civil liability). Against a €5,369 tuition bill for a 60-credit year, an award would cover fees and leave a genuine living allowance — effectively full funding. Timing caveat: the WBI dossier is due 31 March, while INSAS phase-1 results only land mid-June and final admission in September, so the scholarship application must be filed before admission is known.
programs.facilities: Belgium's national film and performing-arts school; the Son master works on INSAS's own graduation films, theatre productions and radio output, with 5.1 mixing and digital cinema projection taught as dedicated units. Detailed studio/console/Atmos inventory: UNVERIFIED — not published. The "more extensive scientific programme and in-depth musicology" characterisation in the earlier draft is partially supported: the curriculum does carry an "Esthétique musicale" unit and the FAQ confirms maths/electricity/optics content, but the specific claim about critical-listening musicology courses could not be located.
programs.fitNotes: Cheap, French-language (his strongest academic language, with no language test required), and genuinely fundable through WBI — everything about the money and the language works for him. It is the admission rule that blocks it: RTM–Son is not one of INSAS's five "masters orphelins", so an exclusively theoretical, unrelated bachelor is stated policy grounds for refusal and redirection to bachelor year 1. Content is also film/radio/theatre sound with only one strand of "prise de son musicale" — it serves a sound-engineer career, not a DJ/producer one. CONCRETE ALTERNATIVE worth raising with him: the sister 60-credit Master RTM – Réalisation Radio Télévision IS an orphan master, and INSAS explicitly says for those "Les études qu'iel aura suivi peuvent être plus théoriques et pas forcément en lien avec l'option désirée" — that is the door at INSAS that is actually open to him, though it is radio/TV directing rather than sound.

programs.degree: Master in de Kunsten / Master of Music (2nd cycle)

programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED on the official page. Music and Technology is described as "essentially an instrumental course" with a technical component (physics of sound, digital studio, programming, HCI, modular synthesis, sound design) and an artistic component resting on "the triangle performance – composition (creation) – digital lutherie". Underlying subject areas: Computer Music; Creative Programming (Max and Ableton Live); Sound Theory & Digital Education (frequency, amplitude, oscillators, microphone handling, recording, live mixing); Modular Synthesis & Sound Design; Sound Installation; Electro Acoustic Multimedia Ensemble. Three master specialisations confirmed: Live Electronics ("focuses on using electronics as the main instrument. You refine your skills as a creator but remain fundamentally a performer of your own work and/or (historical) repertoire"); Computer Music Composition (music creation and sound installation); Hybrid Performance (acoustic instrument plus electronics, requires a prior BA3 instrument diploma). programs.program: Master Live Electronics (Master Muziek, afstudeerrichting Jazz — Live Electronics)
programs.university: Koninklijk Conservatorium Antwerpen (AP School of Arts, AP Hogeschool)
programs.degree: Master in de Muziek / Master of Music — Jazz, Live Electronics
programs.durationEcts: 2 years — CONFIRMED ("Na je bacheloropleiding van drie jaar zet je jouw opleiding verder in de tweejarige master"). ECTS total NOT published; a two-year Flemish master is conventionally 120 ECTS but AP does not state it, so treat 120 as inference, not fact. This matters for the fee calculation below.
programs.language: No formal language requirement — CONFIRMED and a genuine advantage. AP states: "In 2026-2027 there are no official language requirements for the bachelor, master and postgraduate programmes Music" / "Voor de master- en postgraduaatsopleidingen Muziek zijn er geen officiële taalvoorwaarden." B2 Dutch is recommended, not required: "students are advised a B2 Dutch proficiency level for an effective day-to-day communication and high quality written assignments." (By contrast the educational master in Music requires mandatory B2 Dutch.) He would need no IELTS/TOEFL to enrol — though see the scholarship note, where IELTS 6.5 IS required.
programs.institutionType: Conservatoire within a university of applied sciences and arts (AP Hogeschool)
programs.focus: Live Electronics / Performance; Electronic Music Production; Immersive Audio (8-speaker system); algorithmic and live-coded music
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED on the official page. Live electronic performance and improvisation using live-coding environments (Sonic Pi, TidalCycles, Strudel, Vortex); modular synthesis on a vintage Roland System 100M plus modern eurorack; custom instrument building with Axoloti, Raspberry Pi, Arduino and Max; artificial intelligence for generating music in both audio and MIDI; performance at algoraves and jam sessions through an immersive eight-speaker system for spatial composition; both open-source and commercial DAWs. "Everything revolves around your artistic ambitions" — a personalised trajectory rather than a fixed syllabus. Teaching staff: Dago Sondervan, Lennart Heyndels, Inne Eysermans.
programs.entryRequirements: Verified verbatim from the official registration page: "een diploma academische bachelor Muziek, afstudeerrichting Jazz of Jazz/lichte muziek geeft toegang tot de masteropleiding Muziek, afstudeerrichting Jazz" — Live Electronics sits inside the Jazz afstudeerrichting. A foreign diploma goes to the admissions committee: "De toelatingscommissie kan een kandidaat-student toelaten die een buitenlands diploma of getuigschrift heeft behaald ... voor zover de toelatingscommissie het behaalde diploma en het specifieke opleidingsprofiel van de student van voldoende niveau acht" — request to toelating@ap.be, uiterlijk 1 oktober. An artistic entrance exam (toelatingsproef) is required on top of the diploma condition; a voorbereidingsprogramma may be imposed.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO in practice — corrected from the earlier draft's 'Check'. The registration page is much stricter than the marketing page's "open to all music students with an undergraduate degree": direct access requires an academic bachelor in MUSIC with a Jazz or Jazz/lichte muziek specialisation. The foreign-diploma clause is not a general-purpose escape hatch — the committee must judge "het behaalde diploma EN het specifieke opleidingsprofiel van de student" to be of sufficient level for this programme, which a Software Engineering BSc with no music training will not satisfy. The realistic published path for him is a voorbereidingsprogramma (preparatory year) before the master, and he should ask toelating@ap.be directly about it, well before the 1 October deadline.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED for Live Electronics specifically. AP publishes no portfolio specification (number of works, durations, formats) for this specialisation. Related data point: for Jazz, AP allows audition via media uploaded to an "online platform (YouTube, Vimeo, soundcloud, etc.)", and for Composition it requires recordings plus scores. Ask the jazz department.
programs.auditionSpec: An artistieke toelatingsproef is compulsory for all master applicants: "All master applicants must pass an orientation-based artistic test", with content varying by specialisation. Administrative fee €30 per separate School-of-Arts enrolment, never refunded.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — AP does not publish an opening date for the artistic entrance-exam registration.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Two dates are published and they are different things: the foreign-diploma admission request to toelating@ap.be is due "uiterlijk 1 oktober"; and 1 May is cited as the application deadline covering the full academic year / both semesters. Neither is given as a 2027-specific date. Confirm both directly with the jazz department and toelating@ap.be before relying on them.
programs.tuitionIntl: €25,065 per year for a 60-credit year — NEWLY VERIFIED and the single biggest correction here. AP publishes for 2026-2027: non-EEA "tuition fee fixed part: 2.500,00 euro + 375,00 euro / ECTS + 65 euro course related fee" (confirmed independently in AP's official Reglement Studiegelden 2026-27: "Studiegeld buitenlandse studenten — Diploma- en creditcontracten 2500 375"). At 60 credits that is 2,500 + 22,500 + 65 = €25,065; across a two-year 120-credit master, roughly €50,130 total. For comparison, an EEA student pays €305.40 + €14.60/ECTS + €65, i.e. about €1,246 a year. Non-EEA students lost Flemish basic financing from 2026-2027, which is what produced this.
programs.scholarship: Government of Flanders Master Mind. AP University of Applied Sciences and Arts IS a confirmed participating host institution, with a deadline of 1 March 2026 for the 2026-2027 call — PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; expect roughly 1 March 2027 for a September 2027 start, which fits his timeline if he starts early. Three hard obstacles: (a) GPA of 3.5/4.0 on his BSc; (b) IELTS overall band minimum 6.5 for schools of arts, certificate no older than 3 years — he has not sat it; (c) the master must be ENGLISH-TAUGHT, and AP's music master has no official language requirements at all rather than being an English-taught programme, so eligibility must be confirmed with AP's international office before counting on it. programs.fitNotes: Structurally the best-designed option in this batch for him and the only one that is not effectively blocked. English-taught; NO audition and NO required portfolio, which removes the single barrier that closes every other programme here; a 60-ECTS creative thesis means he would spend a full year actually making work; and the Csound audio-programming on-ramp rewards exactly the skills a software-engineering graduate already has. The individual-assessment clause is a real, published door rather than wishful reading. Two caveats keep it off an A. First, the 80-ECTS music-technology prerequisite means admission is discretionary, so he must win the assessment on evidence — build a portfolio and a documented body of production work even though none is formally requested. Second, NOK 198,800 per year with an explicit no-scholarship policy makes this the most expensive unfunded option here in total outlay, and he must also prove funding for the study permit, which directly contradicts his preference for funded study. Concrete next steps: sit IELTS or TOEFL well before the deadline (it must be under two years old), and email the MMUST coordinator in autumn 2026 with a portfolio asking how the individual assessment treats an engineering BSc. Also note this is music technology and creative audio, not DJing — it builds the producer half of his ambition, not the performer half.

programs.fitNotes: On facilities and intellectual content this is arguably the strongest technology-forward composition environment in the batch — instrument design, sound installation, creative programming and electroacoustic composition at Norway's leading music academy, with the option of a semester abroad. If he had a music background this would be an A. He does not, and the rubric puts it at C for two published reasons that compound: the specialisation requires 80 credits in performing or electronic music that he lacks, and the entrance exam is 50% AUDITION with a hard pass threshold, which he cannot currently clear and may not even be able to sit remotely. Add a flat no-scholarship policy against his funding preference. That said, this is the one C in the batch worth actively contesting rather than abandoning — the 'or equivalent' clause plus a genuinely strong body of electronic-music work is the most plausible argument available anywhere in this slice. Highest-value action: email Per Elias Drabløs (per.e.drablos@uia.no) in autumn 2026 with a portfolio, asking directly (a) whether an engineering BSc plus documented electronic-music practice can satisfy the 80-credit rule, and (b) whether the audition can be submitted as a recording from Tunisia. Both answers are needed before he spends anything on this.

programs.program: Master's Programme in Music Technology — study profiles: Recording Arts / Film and Game Music Producer / Creative Electronic Music Practices
programs.university: Sibelius Academy, University of the Arts Helsinki (Uniarts Helsinki)
programs.institutionType: Conservatory / national university of the arts
programs.durationEcts: CORRECTED: 150 ECTS over a normative 2.5 years — NOT 120 ECTS. Finnish music master's degrees are 150 credits, which also means a longer fee-paying period than a standard 120-ECTS master.
programs.language: Finnish, Swedish and English, with English holding a particularly strong position within the Music Technology programme — CONFIRMED. The presence of Finnish and Swedish as official languages of tuition is what makes the fee-exemption route below theoretically possible.
programs.focus: Recording/Engineering + Film & Game Sound + Electronic Music Production (choose one of three profiles at application)
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED. You select ONE of three study profiles when applying: Recording Arts (training advanced music producers and sound engineers in popular and classical music production); Film and Game Music Producer (composing and producing music for visual media); or Creative Electronic Music Practices (electroacoustic music, live electronics and sonic arts). Studies are built individually around a Final Project — applicants submit both a FINAL PROJECT PLAN and a preliminary STUDY PLAN of up to 150 ECTS with the application, so the curriculum is negotiated around the artistic goal. The department also shares teaching with Aalto University's Media Lab. Detailed course lists: UNVERIFIED — the admissions guide is reissued each cycle.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED eligibility routes: a bachelor's degree in music; a university-of-applied-sciences music degree; a foreign qualification giving eligibility for corresponding higher-education studies in the awarding country; or 'a lower university degree in another field AND, additionally, higher education studies in music'. Explicit clause: 'A higher education degree in the field of technology or media is also applicable if you also have a sufficient amount of music studies.' Sufficient proficiency in Finnish, Swedish or English required. Non-EU applicants pay a EUR 100 application fee.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: THE CLOSEST TO A YES ANYWHERE IN THIS BATCH, with one firm condition. A BSc Software Engineering is explicitly contemplated as a base degree under both the 'lower university degree in another field' route and the technology/media clause — but ONLY when combined with documented higher-education music studies. Bare, the BSc is not eligible; paired with, say, open-university music courses or a music-technology certificate, it is. That is a concrete and achievable action item, and it is the single most useful thing he could learn from this batch even though the programme itself is unavailable to him.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED, and unusually precise. ADVANCE ASSIGNMENTS = 40% of the total evaluation. (1) Portfolio and presentation: MAXIMUM 10 MINUTES IN TOTAL combined, containing a MAXIMUM OF THREE WORKS, at least one of which must be a sound or audiovisual recording; formats MP3 for audio, or MP4 with H.264 video and AAC audio codecs. (2) Project description form as PDF detailing each portfolio work. (3) Motivation letter, maximum 2 A4 pages. (4) CV as PDF covering education, training and artistic work. (5) Final project plan, maximum 2 A4 pages. (6) Preliminary study plan of maximum 150 ECTS.
programs.auditionSpec: CONFIRMED. ENTRANCE EXAMINATION = 60% of the total evaluation, held REMOTELY via remote connection (prior cycle: 31 March – 1 April 2026) — so no travel required, a genuine advantage. Two components: an INSTRUMENT OR VOICE AUDITION of 7 to 10 minutes, worth 40% of the entrance-exam score; and an INTERVIEW of up to 25 minutes, worth 60% of the entrance-exam score, covering the portfolio, the performance, background and project feasibility. The instrument/voice audition is a real hurdle for a non-instrumentalist and applies even to Music Technology applicants as published.
programs.tuitionIntl: CONFIRMED on Uniarts' official tuition-fee page: 'The amount of the tuition fee at Uniarts Helsinki is 28,000 euros per academic year at both the bachelor's and master's stage of studies starting from 1 August 2026', for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens studying in English. Because the degree runs 2.5 years / 150 ECTS, total exposure is on the order of EUR 70,000, not EUR 56,000. Plus a EUR 100 application fee. Comfortably the most expensive option in the batch.
programs.scholarship: CONFIRMED none from the university: 'The university does not have a scholarship programme related to the full-cost tuition fee', and Uniarts grants no scholarships for living expenses. ONE CONFIRMED WORKAROUND: Finnish- and Swedish-taught study is fee-exempt, and the official policy states that if 'a student's language of studies changes to Finnish or Swedish, they will no longer have to pay annual tuition fees', with already-paid future-term fees refunded. This is real and directly relevant because Music Technology's languages of tuition include Finnish and Swedish — but it would require functional Finnish or Swedish, neither of which he has. Whether the national Finland Scholarship applies at Uniarts: UNVERIFIED.
programs.fundingLevel: None from the institution — self-pay only, unless the Finnish/Swedish language-of-study exemption could ever be used.
programs.stipend: None — Uniarts explicitly grants no scholarships for living expenses.
programs.applicationOpens: Prior cycle opened 7 January 2026 at 08:00 EET. See the deadline field — there is no 2027 opening.
programs.deadline: BLOCKING SCHEDULE ISSUE — CONFIRMED, AND THIS REVERSES THE EARLIER ASSESSMENT. The official programme page states plainly: 'No admission in 2027. Next possible time to apply will be announced later.' The Department of Music Technology admits every other year, alternating between intake for the 5.5-year bachelor+master studies and intake for the 2.5-year master's studies. The prior cycle (application 7–21 Jan 2026, attachments 28 Jan, remote entrance exams 31 Mar – 1 Apr, results 10 Apr, place confirmed by 9 Jul 2026) served the 2026 intake. There is therefore NO September 2027 intake for this programme, and no future date is yet published. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date; monitor the programme page for the announcement.
programs.verificationNotes: SOURCE URL CORRECTED to the official programme page; the previous link was the cycle-specific application guide (https://www.uniarts.fi/en/guides/apply-to-the-masters-programme-in-music-technology/), which remains the source for the portfolio and entrance-exam detail but carries NO forward-looking information — it documents spring 2026 only. TWO MATERIAL CORRECTIONS to the earlier record. (1) DURATION/ECTS: the degree is 150 ECTS over 2.5 years, not 120 ECTS — this raises total tuition exposure to roughly EUR 70,000. (2) INTAKE TIMING: the earlier note that 'the next application period is in 2027' and that the guide updates in Oct–Nov 2026 is WRONG and inverted. The official programme page states 'No admission in 2027. Next possible time to apply will be announced later.' CONFIRMED: three study profiles, MMus degree, trilingual instruction with English prominent, the full eligibility wording including the technology/media clause, the complete advance-assignment portfolio spec (max 3 works, max 10 minutes total, MP3/MP4 H.264+AAC), the 40/60 split between advance assignments and entrance exam, the remote entrance exam with its 7–10 minute instrument audition (40%) and up-to-25-minute interview (60%), EUR 28,000/year from August 2026, the no-scholarship statement, and the Finnish/Swedish language-of-study fee exemption. NOT CONFIRMED: detailed course lists, whether the Finland Scholarship applies, and any future application date.
programs.fitNotes: This was the most promising entry in the batch on content and it has to be downgraded to C on verification. The Creative Electronic Music Practices profile at a top-tier conservatory, with remote entrance exams requiring no travel and an eligibility clause that explicitly names technology degrees, is close to ideal on paper. But the official programme page says 'No admission in 2027' — the department alternates intakes and the September 2027 target simply does not exist, with no replacement date published. That alone blocks it. Behind that sit three further problems: EUR 28,000 per year across a 2.5-year, 150-ECTS degree is roughly EUR 70,000 total with a written no-scholarship policy; the only fee escape requires switching to Finnish or Swedish instruction, which he cannot do; and the entrance exam includes a 7–10 minute instrument or voice audition worth 40% of the exam, which is hard for a DAW-based producer. Still, this programme teaches him the most useful lesson in the batch: its eligibility route — a technology bachelor PLUS documented higher-education music studies — is the template he should be building toward generally. Recommended actions regardless: start accumulating credit-bearing music coursework now, monitor the programme page for the next intake announcement, and email siba.admissions@uniarts.fi about how the instrument audition is applied to Music Technology applicants and whether the Finland Scholarship is available.

programs.program: Sound in New Media, Master of Arts (Art and Design) — a major within the Master's Programme in Art and Media
programs.university: Aalto University, School of Arts, Design and Architecture (Department of Art and Media / Aalto Media Lab)
programs.institutionType: Public university (art, design, technology and business)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, full-time / 120 ECTS
programs.language: English. "The language of instruction is English. Students can write their Master's Thesis in English, Finnish or Swedish."
programs.focus: Sound Design / Sonic Arts / Immersive Audio, sound and music computing, game audio, sonic interaction design
programs.whatYouStudy: CORRECTED SCOPE (quoted from the official page). Aim: "to explore, discover and comprehend the emerging digital technology and its aural impact in society; to find and exploit the possibilities it opens to acoustic communication, sonic interaction and new interfaces for musical expression". Named areas: "sound and music computing, sound art and auditory culture, sonic interaction design, artificial intelligence applied to sound design and music, game audio and acoustic branding". Tools and skills explicitly listed: "creative coding, physical computing, digital fabrication, sonic interaction design, extended reality, generative composition methods and other emerging technologies" — note how directly a software-engineering BSc maps onto creative coding and physical computing. Teaching is "project-oriented, combining practice with theory, hands-on with minds-on", with "intensive workshops" and "tutored studio work". Every student writes a Personal Study Plan (PSP); year 1 is programme/major core, year 2 is electives, minors and the thesis. Research anchor: the Sound and Physical Interaction research group (SOPI). CONFIRMED CROSS-REGISTRATION: "Majority of our students take courses from the Sibelius Academy Department of Music Technology, and these studies can be included to the MA degree." Closest internal partners: Aalto Department of Signal Processing and Acoustics and the Master's Programme in Information Networks.
programs.entryRequirements: Programme page eligibility line: "Relevant Bachelor's degree". Aalto general eligibility: a bachelor's degree equivalent to 180 ECTS / three years full-time, giving eligibility for master's study in the awarding country, from an institution recognised in its national education system. He may apply before graduating provided the degree is awarded by the equivalent of 31 July 2027 (2026-cycle wording: 31 July 2026). ENGLISH TEST IS REQUIRED — Tunisia is NOT on Aalto's exemption list, so he must sit one of: IELTS Academic overall 6.5 with Writing 6.0; TOEFL iBT (tests from 21 Jan 2026 onward) total 4.5 with all four subtests 4.0, or, for pre-21-Jan-2026 tests, total 92 with Writing 22; PTE Academic overall 68 with Writing 61; Cambridge C1 Advanced grade A/B/C; Cambridge C2 Proficiency grade A/B/C or Level C1. Scores are valid two years from the test date and must be uploaded by the document deadline (2026 cycle: 9 January 2026, 15:00 UTC+2). APPLICATION FEE: EUR 100 for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens. One application form; a maximum of TWO study options may be ranked on it.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — and unusually explicitly so for this applicant. The only stated degree condition is "Relevant Bachelor's degree"; there is no music-degree, music-theory or conservatory requirement anywhere on the page. Decisively, the published evaluation criteria for Artistic and/or design practice state: "Demonstrations of artistic and/or design work related to sound, e.g. artistic or commercial projects, publications, performance/exhibition documentations or other works of art and/or design in the audible domain. Proven musical competence of any kind (e.g. violin playing, DJ'ing etc) is a plus." DJing is named, in Aalto's own words, as a positive. The programme also states it "brings together a multicultural group of students with very versatile skills and backgrounds", and the toolset it teaches (creative coding, physical computing, generative composition) presupposes technical entrants. Selection is portfolio-, motivation- and interview-driven. Aalto does not publish an enumerated list of "relevant" fields — that single point remains unverified; confirm with arts-admissions@aalto.fi.
programs.portfolioSpec: EXACT published spec: "The portfolio is presented and discussed during the application interview. The form and format of the portfolio is free; however, the portfolio should be online so that it can be accessed via Internet with a common web browser (Google Chrome, Mozilla Firefox or Safari). The access to the portfolio might be password protected on the responsibility of the applicant. The portfolio may consist of individual art/design works, documentation of exhibitions and/or performances etc. The portfolio must showcase the applicant's previous academic, professional and/or scientific activity in a diverse and comprehensive manner. The applicant should be able to present the portfolio in 10 minutes." Maximum file size 1.0 GB; file named Portfolio-lastname-firstname.pdf; document language English. NOTE THE ODD HYBRID: Aalto asks for an online, browser-accessible portfolio AND names a PDF file — in practice submit a PDF that carries links out to hosted audio/video. NO fixed number of works, no per-track duration and no audio format are specified. Also required: motivation letter, max 4,000 characters, single PDF, English, explaining "why they wish to apply to the degree programme in question, what their particular areas of interest in this field are, and what their objectives and hopes are regarding the studies at the School of Arts, Design and Architecture"; and a CV (single PDF, English) with personal data, education, work experience, exhibitions, publications, awards and grants, study trips and positions of trust. "Lack of this application document will adversely affect the evaluation of the application."
programs.auditionSpec: NO live audition and NO on-site test. Two-phase selection, both remote-capable. Phase I scores Suitability/Motivation letter plus Other areas of competence (CV); "the scoring and/or ranking of the first phase doesn't affect the final, 2nd phase scoring." Only the highest-ranked are invited onward, with at least 7 days' notice. Phase II: "applicants complete one or more assignments within the given time. The assignment(s) can be written or audible and is (are) based on the provided material and/or given topic. The assignment(s) is (are) submitted in electronic form as text file(s) with possible supporting graphs and images and/or as audio file(s)." Plus "a 30-minute interview" (Aalto states interviews "may be conducted remotely"), in which the portfolio is presented and discussed. Important caution published by the programme: "the application process aims at a balanced group of different kinds of students... even exceptional skills and talent in one field don't automatically guarantee that the applicant would be selected. Furthermore, the more there are applicants with a similar profile, the harder the competition is."
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 20,000 per academic year for non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens (Art and Architecture fee band, for study rights beginning on or after 1 August 2025). CONFIRMED on both the programme page ("For non-EU/EEA citizens, €20000/y (Master's studies)") and Aalto's Scholarships and Tuition Fees page. Two-year exposure EUR 40,000. EU/EEA/Swiss citizens pay nothing. Separate non-refundable application fee of EUR 100 for non-EU/EEA applicants. Aalto advises budgeting "at least 800 euros per month" for living costs in the capital region.
programs.scholarship: Aalto University Excellence Scholarship. NAME AND TERMS CORRECTED: the old 50%/100% split no longer applies to study rights starting on or after 1 August 2025 — "Aalto University Excellence Scholarships are awarded as tuition fee waivers, covering the full tuition fee." Granted for the target time of the degree (two years / four terms for a master's), conditional on progressing per the approved personal study plan. Open only to fee-liable non-EU/EEA/Swiss citizens, so a Tunisian national is eligible. No separate application: "you can apply for the scholarship when you apply to Aalto University. The scholarship application is part of the application form for admission." Awarded "on a competitive basis to the highest-achieving applicants based on the programme's evaluation criteria." Material caveat, quoted: "There is a very limited number of scholarships available, and programmes may also decide not to grant any scholarships."
programs.fundingLevel: Full — but competitive and not guaranteed (100% tuition-fee waiver; a programme may award none in a given year)
programs.stipend: Tuition-fee waiver only. Explicitly: "Aalto University Excellence Scholarships do not cover living costs. Students need to cover all living expenses and other study related costs from their own financial resources." No living allowance, no housing. Budget from own funds at roughly EUR 800+/month.
programs.applicationOpens: 7 December 2026 — CONFIRMED as published, not inferred
programs.deadline: 5 January 2027 for studies beginning autumn 2027. CONFIRMED AND CURRENT — Aalto has already published it: "The application period for studies beginning in autumn 2027 will run from 7 December 2026 to 5 January 2027." This is his target intake and the date is real, not a prior-cycle date. Two riders: (a) Aalto adds "Admission instructions for the next round will be published on our website in autumn 2026 and may be subject to change"; (b) the document-upload deadline for the 2027 round is not yet published — in the 2026 cycle it fell one week after close (9 January 2026, 15:00 UTC+2), so plan for roughly 12 January 2027 and treat it as hard: "The deadline is the same for all applicants and cannot be extended. Please note that incomplete applications will be rejected." programs.verificationNotes: Official programme page fetched in full (page footer shows Updated: 2.7.2026), plus Aalto's Apply to master's programmes page, Scholarships and Tuition Fees page, the post-1-August-2025 scholarships page and the master's language-requirements page. CORRECTIONS MADE TO THE INPUT RECORD: (1) The parent programme is the Master's Programme in ART AND MEDIA, not "New Media" — Sound in New Media is one of its majors alongside New Media, Photography, Visual Communication Design, Game Design and Development, Visual Cultures Curating and Contemporary Art, and Visual Arts Education. (2) The scholarship is the Aalto University Excellence Scholarship and now covers the FULL tuition fee, not "either 50% or 100%". (3) The deadline is NOT a prior-cycle date — 7 Dec 2026 to 5 Jan 2027 is published for autumn 2027. (4) An EUR 100 application fee for non-EU applicants was missing. (5) English test scores and the fact that Tunisia carries no exemption were missing; exact thresholds now recorded. (6) The programme description was skewed toward "concept design to live performance" wording that does not appear on the current page; replaced with the page's actual language. (7) The Sibelius Academy cross-registration claim is CONFIRMED on the official page. (8) Campus is Otaniemi, Espoo. programs.fitNotes: The strongest Nordic option on the list by a wide margin, and the only one where the official evaluation criteria literally say "Proven musical competence of any kind (e.g. violin playing, DJ'ing etc) is a plus". No music degree, no instrument audition, no on-site test, no theory exam — a remote 30-minute interview plus a written-or-audio assignment. His software-engineering BSc is an asset rather than a liability here: the major teaches creative coding, physical computing and generative composition, and it sits next to Signal Processing and Acoustics. He can also pull Sibelius Academy Music Technology courses into the degree, which is the practical bridge from sound design toward music production. TWO REAL CAVEATS, which is why this is B and not A. First, money: EUR 20,000 per year, EUR 40,000 over the degree, with the only route to affordability being a competitive Excellence Scholarship that the programme is free to award to nobody — his admission and his funding stand or fall on the same application. Second, content drift: this is sound design, sonic interaction and sound art for media, installation and games, not club-music production or record mixing; the DJ/producer ambition is served obliquely. Practical plan: sit IELTS by spring 2027 at the latest (target 7.0 to leave headroom over the 6.5/6.0 floor), spend the next twelve months building a portfolio that pairs finished electronic tracks and DJ work with at least one technical/interactive sound project that shows the coding side, and note he can rank TWO study options on one form — pair this with a second Aalto or Finnish option rather than wasting the slot.

programs.program: Music Composition MA/M.Mus
programs.university: Iceland University of the Arts / Iceland Academy of the Arts (Listaháskóli Íslands, LHÍ), Department of Music
programs.institutionType: Art school / self-owned university of the arts
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS — NOW CONFIRMED on the official programme page (previously logged as UNVERIFIED)
programs.language: English — NOW CONFIRMED: "Program information is provided in English, as the language of MA program in composition is English" and "The Master Program of Composition is an international program conducted in English."
programs.focus: Art-music composition (contemporary classical), with an electronic-composition and sound-art application stream and a sound-technology course in the core
programs.whatYouStudy: "The international MA program in composition enables the student to develop his/her artistic and theoretical activity in a stimulating creative and critical environment, with access to the staff's wide professional experience and theoretical knowledge and supported by an inspiring learning community." Structure, per the official page: one-to-one private lessons with a composition tutor plus collective composition classes; "the subject of composition is by far the largest item in the syllabus, generating almost half the credits in the first three terms"; first two terms also carry "a course in sound technology, either electronic or instrumental, a course on artistic research, a course on music analysis and an introduction to some recent issues [in] music composition", plus electives. Weekly seminars analyse notable compositions and discuss students' research. The school "collaborates with professional musicians who give workshops where students' works are heard and discussed". Master's project options: (a) 20-credit composition + 10-credit paper, (b) 10-credit composition + 20-credit paper, or (c) a 26-credit practical project + a 4-credit reflection. CONFIRMED on the official page (previously flagged as aggregator-sourced): "Students are offered the opportunity to have their final project performed by the Caput Ensemble at a graduation concert." No PhD in music yet, though one is in development.
programs.entryRequirements: NOW PUBLISHED AND CONFIRMED (previously logged as UNVERIFIED). General: "a bachelor's degree or equivalent university education that supports the applicant's ability to meet the [demands] of the MA Program", with certified academic transcripts. Programme-specific: "Applicants will have completed a BA degree in composition or the related fields of music theory or the arts. Non musical academic degrees are not excluded, especially on graduate and doctoral levels. Applicants who do not have a BA degree in composition can be recommended to the program provided they demonstrate a comparable knowledge, experience and technical ability in the field of musical composition." Language: "Students must be proficient in spoken and written English in the academic context. In case the admission committee has doubts regarding the applicant's competence, he/she may be required to submit evidence of English proficiency" — so no blanket IELTS/TOEFL requirement, but a test can be demanded. Documents: certified degree certificate(s) and transcript(s) (PDF); ONE reference, max one page, submitted directly by the referee via an emailed link (waived for former LHÍ students); letter of motivation in English (PDF); CV in English (PDF); portfolio. Non-refundable application fee ISK 5,000, payable per application; the application is not valid until both submitted and paid.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: TECHNICALLY YES, PRACTICALLY DEMANDING. Quoted: "Non musical academic degrees are not excluded, especially on graduate and doctoral levels." But the same paragraph sets the real bar: an applicant without a BA in composition must "demonstrate a comparable knowledge, experience and technical ability in the field of musical composition" — i.e. the door is open only if the portfolio performs at conservatory-graduate level. With no music degree, no conservatory training and no professional audio experience, he would be asked to evidence exactly what he does not yet have. The sibling MMus in New Audiences and Innovative Practice (NAIP), described on the department page as suitable for musicians from diverse backgrounds with "innovative and interdisciplinary approaches to creating and communicating music", is the more permissive door — but it carries the identical Department of Music tuition, which is the real blocker.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW PUBLISHED AND CONFIRMED (previously UNVERIFIED). Item 5, "Portfolio of works (PDF/URL)", compulsory: "Portfolio of 5 scores with or without audio files are required for applications in instrumental composition. Applicants in electronic composition and sound art must submit 5 works. Applicants for interdisciplinary studies (composing for film, theater etc.) must submit 5 original works." So his route would be the electronic-composition/sound-art stream: FIVE works, no notation obligation on that stream. No per-work duration, no audio format and no total runtime cap are specified. Submitted as PDF or URL.
programs.auditionSpec: NO live audition and no on-site entrance test published. "An admission committee assesses applications on the grounds of assessment of the subject material, the applicant's motivation and aim with the study at the Iceland University of the Arts and the interview(s) with the applicant." Interview(s) form part of selection; the mode is not stated, so confirm whether they are held remotely. Additional risk on the official page: "If the number of applicants meeting the admission requirements for the study program falls below the minimum threshold, the program will not be offered for the upcoming academic year."
programs.tuitionIntl: BLOCKING FINDING — the amount is now published and it is very large. From LHÍ's tuition-fee page, for the academic year 2026-2027, non-EEA students pay per academic year: Department of Music ISK 5,500,000 (also Performing Arts and Film ISK 5,500,000; Architecture, Fine Art, Design and Arts Education ISK 4,500,000). ISK 5,500,000 is roughly EUR 37,000-38,000 per year at mid-2026 rates, i.e. on the order of EUR 75,000 for the two-year MA — indicative conversion, verify at the time. LHÍ states the fees "reflect the actual cost of the studies and the amount may change between academic years", are charged in ISK by bank transfer, are non-refundable, and "must be paid in full before enrolment or continuation of studies can be confirmed. Failure to pay on time or in full may result in the loss of the study place." The ISK 100,000 annual registration fee does NOT rescue him: it applies to "students with citizenship within the EEA, the Faroe Islands, Greenland and Switzerland as well as all students regardless of nationality who started studying at LHÍ in the fall of 2025 or earlier." Only two exemptions exist, neither of which he meets: holding an Icelandic permanent residence permit (or one that can lead to it), or studying at LHÍ via an international university cooperation project, cooperation programme or university network. Separate application fee ISK 5,000, non-refundable, per application, not deducted from any other fee.
programs.scholarship: None — and this is now an explicit institutional statement, not an absence of evidence. LHÍ's tuition-fee page: "IUA does not provide any scholarships for [tuition] fees or living expenses."
programs.stipend: None. Beyond tuition, LHÍ tells non-EEA students to budget for "study materials, equipment, and supplies", insurance, and living expenses in Iceland — one of the most expensive countries in Europe.
