STILL UNVERIFIED: whether the interview can be conducted remotely; whether non-EEA students also owe the ISK 100,000 registration fee on top of tuition; whether the ISK 5,500,000 figure will be revised for 2027-2028 (LHÍ warns it "may change between academic years"); and the full admission detail for the sibling NAIP MMus.
programs.fitNotes: DOWNGRADED TO C — this is now a confirmed financial dead end, not merely an unverified one. LHÍ has published the number the earlier record could not find: from autumn 2026 a non-EEA student in the Department of Music pays ISK 5,500,000 per academic year, roughly EUR 37,000-38,000, about EUR 75,000 across the MA, with tuition due in full before enrolment can be confirmed, no refunds, and the institution stating flat out that it offers no scholarships for tuition or living costs — in Iceland, one of Europe's most expensive countries. The only two exemptions are Icelandic residency and inbound exchange/network mobility; neither is available to him as a direct-entry Tunisian applicant. Set the money aside and the fit is still weak: it is a contemporary art-music composition MA built around private composition tutorials, score-based work and a Caput Ensemble graduation concert, with electronics as one course and one application stream. The published entry rule is honest about the bar — a non-composition bachelor is "not excluded" but must "demonstrate a comparable knowledge, experience and technical ability in the field of musical composition", which is precisely the evidence he cannot produce this cycle. There is one genuine positive to bank: the electronic-composition and sound-art portfolio route asks for five works with no notation requirement, which is a spec he could realistically meet in a year — the same five-work package would serve the Aalto portfolio. Recommendation: do not apply. If Iceland matters for non-academic reasons, email lhi@lhi.is and registration@lhi.is to check whether the NAIP MMus route or any Erasmus/network mobility arrangement could bring him in under the cooperation-programme exemption, since that is the only published mechanism that removes the fee.

programs.program: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound
programs.university: Consortium: IADT Dún Laoghaire (IE) · Universidade Lusófona (PT) · Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre / LMTA (LT)
programs.city: Dublin (Dún Laoghaire, sem 1) → Lisbon (sem 2) → Vilnius (sem 3) → sem 4 thesis at IADT, Lusófona or LMTA (student selects host)
programs.focus: Sound Design · Film/Game Sound · Immersive Audio · Music Production · Electronic Music · Sonic Arts
programs.degree: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master — joint diploma supplement 'MA in Sound (ReSound)' PLUS multiple degrees: IADT 'Master of Arts in Sound', Lusófona 'Master's in Sound Production Technology', LMTA 'Master of Arts in Film'
programs.institutionType: Consortium within the FilmEU European University alliance: art-and-technology institute (IADT, hosts Ireland's National Film School), private university film school (Lusófona), state academy of music and theatre (LMTA)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS — CONFIRMED by summing the published module table (30 ECTS per semester; sem 4 = 30 ECTS Thesis). Programme runs early September to early June of year 2.
programs.language: English (all instruction)
programs.whatYouStudy: Curriculum built on three pillars (Societal, Skills, Creative). Sem 1 IADT: Acoustics & Psychoacoustics (5), Audio and Music Production (10 — studio procedure, microphone technique, signal flow, critical listening), Synthesis and Sampling (5 — analogue/digital synthesis rebuilt in open-source environments), Interactive Systems (5), Sound Psychology (5). Sem 2 Lusófona: Film Sound Theory (5), Interdisciplinary Project Incubation (5), Sound Ecosystems (5), Sound/Music Interface (5 — music fundamentals bridged to electroacoustic music, soundscape composition, field recording, digital synthesis), Film Audio: Post-production Tools (10 — Pro Tools, includes Avid 101 and 110 certification). Sem 3 LMTA: Sound and the Environment (5), Film Sound: Integrative Methods and Practice (10), Sound Concepts (5), Sound Design and Immersion (5 — immersive mixing), Thesis Preparation (5). Sem 4: practice-based Thesis (30).
programs.facilities: CONFIRMED per campus. IADT: National Film School, two Dolby Atmos mix suites, a 5.1 surround mixing suite, Foley recording stage, vocal booth, immersive media production facility (VR/AR), two radio studios. Lusófona: general-purpose recording studio, 5.1 Dolby Surround post room, 7.1.4 Dolby Atmos post auditorium, Sonic Arts Lab (audio+video+microcontrollers), Apple/MIDI-equipped labs, large equipment loan warehouse. LMTA: spatial sound sphere, two recording studios, video/audio editing workstations, 99-seat cinema hall, dedicated sound mixing and mastering cinema hall, two film studios.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree in sound, music, film or media studies (minimum EQF Level 6 or equivalent; NARIC Ireland used to check equivalence). Other fields considered with relevant prior experience. Also required: passport copy, headshot, stamped degree documents + transcripts (certified English translation if needed), CV of professional qualifications and experience, TWO letters of recommendation (at least one academic, addressed to 'board members of ReSound'), letter of motivation (max 1000 characters, explicitly 'do not use AI / Large Language Models'), a 500-character description of a proposed final thesis project, portfolio, English proof. English: IELTS 6.0 with no component below 6.0, or TOEFL iBT 79 / Duolingo 110 / Cambridge B2 / LanguageCert ESOL, taken within the last two years; OR a full EQF Level 4+ qualification of at least one academic year taught through English. Final-year undergraduates may apply (conditional offer). No age limit and no time limit on when the bachelor was obtained.
programs.portfolioSpec: "Portfolio of previous sound/media related work. Please include a short reflective paragraph on each piece explicitly stating your role in the work. Please supply no more than 3 examples. You can supply a single hyperlink to a portfolio website or a compilation audio or video file. The team can realistically listen/watch 10-15 minutes of material per application, so please select the best work." FAQ adds: works can be "audio recordings or audio related outputs... video related outputs and there could be songs, music, soundtracks, arts and Electro acoustic music performance"; "Focus on contrast rather than have three of the same sort of style"; and explicitly "If I do not already have a suitable portfolio of work can I create one specifically for this programme? Yes. Absolutely."
programs.auditionSpec: No live audition and no on-site test. There IS an online interview stage: "Applicants with the highest scores resulting from the application package, which includes the Portfolio, will be called for an online Interview." FAQ: "Interviews are scheduled to take place online (over Microsoft Teams) during March", with at least one week's notice. English skills are judged partly from the interview. Offers expected no later than end of April.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — the strongest wording in this batch. "ReSound is open to both European and non-European students who hold a bachelor's degree in sound, music, film, or media studies. Applicants with degrees in other fields may also be considered if they possess relevant prior experience in areas such as sound, music, film, or media studies." FAQ: "I have not formally studied sound. Is prior experience in sound a requirement for admission? It is not a requirement to have formally studied sound specifically." CORRECTION to the draft: the current published eligibility text does NOT name "computational science" as an accepted field — the accepted list is sound, music, film, media studies, plus the other-fields-with-relevant-experience clause. A software-engineering BSc therefore goes through the discretionary clause and needs demonstrable sound/music practice, which his DJ/producer work can supply.
programs.tuitionIntl: €15,000 total for the whole 4-semester programme for non-scholarship holders, paid €7,500 before semester 1 and €7,500 before semester 3. Identical for EU and non-EU. Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders pay nothing. Fee covers all classes, insurance, enrolment at each partner, examinations and the final diploma; it does NOT cover travel, visas, accommodation or living costs. Living costs estimated at €600–1,000 per month.
programs.scholarship: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master Scholarship, "awarded on the basis of excellence" — open to any nationality including Tunisian; eligibility is holding a first higher-education degree or recognised equivalent, and not already having held an EMJM/Erasmus Mundus scholarship. "A maximum of 24 places are offered at ReSound each year. An Erasmus Mundus scholarship will be available only to a percentage of those places." CORRECTION: the site says "only to a percentage", not "a significant percentage".
programs.fundingLevel: Full (for Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders) / self-pay fallback €15,000 total
programs.stipend: €1,400 per month. Scholarship holders "pay no tuition fees and receive a scholarship of 1,400 EUR per month. These Erasmus+ scholarships contribute to travel, visa and a living allowance." Note: the scholarship does not begin until the student has arrived in Dublin and registered — he must fund his own travel to Ireland. Additional Erasmus Mundus special-needs funding exists for documented long-term impairments.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE — the 2026 round opened 20 October 2025. For a September 2027 start expect the call around October 2026; not yet published as of July 2026. Confirm on resound-ma.eu.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. FAQ (still live): the 2026 application period "will close at 17:00 (Western European Time) on the 20th January 2026"; the application page now reads "Applications for ReSound 2026 have now closed." (The draft's claim of an extension to 27 January 2026 could NOT be confirmed anywhere on the site.) No 2027 call published as of July 2026.
programs.fitNotes: Still the best fit in this batch and one of the best in Europe for him: English-taught, non-music bachelors admissible via the explicit other-fields clause, a small portfolio (3 pieces, 10–15 minutes) that can be his own tracks, no live audition (only an online Teams interview), a full Erasmus Mundus scholarship with €1,400/month, and hands-on production content from semester 1 (studio production, synthesis, Pro Tools certification, Atmos immersive mixing). Main obstacles: only 24 places worldwide and only a percentage funded; the centre of gravity is sound design / film / immersive rather than club music, so his three portfolio pieces should be contrasting (at least one designed or narrative piece, not three dance tracks); and he must sit IELTS/TOEFL and secure two references, one academic.
programs.verificationNotes: Full official site read directly (application, curriculum, the-masters and FAQ pages, raw HTML). Confirmed: 120 ECTS by module table, city rotation, degree structure, English test thresholds, exact portfolio wording, online-interview-only selection, €15,000 self-pay in two instalments, 24 places/year, €1,400/month EMJM stipend, prior-cycle dates. Corrected three draft errors: (1) 'computational science' is not in the published eligibility list; (2) there IS an online interview stage, not selection on written application alone; (3) the published 2026 deadline is 20 January 2026, not an extension to 27 January. Not verified: 2027 call dates (not published), and the exact split of scholarships versus self-payers.

programs.program: Composition and Music Technology (MA) — Electroacoustic Composition specialisation
programs.university: Estonian Academy of Music and Theatre (EAMT / EMTA)
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics · Electroacoustic Composition · Sonic Arts
programs.institutionType: Public national academy of music and theatre (conservatory)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS. EAMT states curricula are established on "the assumption that the standard volume is 30 ECTS per semester and 60 ECTS per academic year", and DreamApply gives 2 years — so 120 ECTS, though the figure is not printed on the programme page itself.
programs.language: English — CONFIRMED. The programme is listed on DreamApply (the platform EAMT uses "for the curricula in English") as [MA] Composition and Music Technology, taught in English. Tuition fees "apply to all international students whose language of tuition is English"; full-time study in Estonian is free.
programs.whatYouStudy: One curriculum with four fields: classical composition, electroacoustic composition, audiovisual composition, recording arts. Electroacoustic and audiovisual studies "combine musical, artistic and technical creativity", with the Academy's sound and multimedia studios and editing rooms "offering a learning environment under the guidance of acknowledged professionals". Creative mentorship model — students are not tied to a single professor. The curriculum collaborates with national and international art and music institutions and students take part in international festivals and workshops each year, including the annual COMMUTE Festival. Note EAMT's curricula page warns: "Applying for admission to a Master's curriculum in another field may require completing prerequisite subjects during Bachelor studies" — directly relevant to a software-engineering entrant.
programs.facilities: Sound and multimedia studios plus editing rooms in the purpose-built Tatari 13 building in central Tallinn; "state-of-the-art equipment" (wording used mainly of the recording arts track). Guest composers associated with the department include Arvo Pärt and Kaija Saariaho. Specific console/room inventory UNVERIFIED — no equipment list is published.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree (the MA admission page states no subject restriction). Documents: electronic application via DreamApply, photo, passport/ID copy, evidence of completing the previous educational level with grades or diploma supplement, proof of English proficiency. Application fee €75, normally by bank transfer. During the interview the panel "can test a candidate's knowledge in a narrower field of specialization as well as his or her general cultural knowledge. You will also be tested whether or not your English or Estonian language skills are sufficient." No numeric IELTS/TOEFL threshold is published on the admission pages.
programs.portfolioSpec: Three requirements, verbatim: (1) "The applicant must present his electroacoustic compositions in a recording or live performance (a total of approximately 15 minutes)." (2) "Participate in an oral examination where the Board may assess the candidate's knowledge of their area of specialization and their understanding of related cultural issues (colloquium)." (3) "Submit a portfolio of their original works." Scores are required only for the classical Composition track, not this one. Assessment criteria: artistic mindset and originality of creative ideas; logic of development and expressiveness of the works; technical refinement and appropriate technical choices; fulfilment of length and genre requirements; understanding of cultural and specialty-specific issues. Graded 0–10.
programs.auditionSpec: Entrance examination = presentation of the ~15 minutes of electroacoustic work (recording OR live performance) + an oral colloquium. Graded 0–10. Format: "EAMT prefers to audition you in person, but those foreign applicants, to whom traveling is not possible, are encouraged to submit an original video recording... candidates can only pass the entrance audition by video recording if the examination panel has no doubts about authenticity of the recording, the quality of the recording is sufficient for evaluation and the candidate's performance meets the highest standards, clearly exceeding the admission threshold." So remote is possible but held to a higher bar. Auditions/interviews last approximately 20–30 minutes.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — no music-degree requirement is published, and the MA admission page states no subject restriction at all. But the curricula page cautions that "Applying for admission to a Master's curriculum in another field may require completing prerequisite subjects during Bachelor studies", and the whole entrance exam is judged as composition. Contact katrin.puur@eamt.ee (study programme registrar) or admissions@eamt.ee before applying.
programs.tuitionIntl: Non-EU: €7,700/year for full- and part-time BA and MA studies, academic year 2026/2027, per EAMT Senate Regulation of 29 October 2025. EU/EEA and Ukrainian students: €1,750/year full-time. Only Cultural Management (€6,000 non-EU) and CPPM (€14,000 non-EU) are excepted — this curriculum is not.
programs.scholarship: "A limited number of scholarships are available for international students. Auditions for the scholarships usually take place at the end of September." No named scheme, no amount, no eligibility list published; the dedicated study-grants page carries nothing for non-EU degree students and notes that need-based special allowance "cannot any more be applied for by students who study in Estonia on the basis of TRP for studies (students from outside EU)", pointing instead to studyinestonia.ee. No Tunisia-specific scholarship found.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial / UNVERIFIED — nothing quantified is published for a non-EU applicant
programs.stipend: UNVERIFIED — no stipend published for master's students (only doctoral students are stated to receive a monthly stipend)
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE — DreamApply opened 1 February 2026 for English-taught curricula (2026/27 entry). Expect roughly February 2027 for a September 2027 start; not published as of July 2026. (As of July 2026 EAMT is running an additional admission round for a small number of 2026/27 places.)
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The 2026/27 admission period ran 1 February – 3 July 2026 via DreamApply. No 2027/28 dates published as of July 2026.
programs.fitNotes: English-taught, in an active Northern European electronic-music scene, €7,700/year non-EU (moderate for a conservatory), €75 application fee, real studio access, and a portfolio spec a self-taught producer can actually meet — roughly 15 minutes of electroacoustic work presented as recordings, with no scores required for this track. Main obstacles: it is judged as composition, so club tracks alone will read poorly against criteria like 'logic of development'; the colloquium tests cultural and specialist knowledge; remote examination is allowed only where travel is impossible and is held to a higher bar; and there is no quantified funding for a Tunisian, so realistically this is €7,700/year self-pay plus living costs.
programs.verificationNotes: Admission page fetched and read in full (raw HTML), plus the EAMT tuition-fees regulation page, the admission-dates/general-info page, the curricula page and the DreamApply listing. Confirmed verbatim: the exact electroacoustic portfolio wording, the colloquium wording, the five assessment criteria, the 0–10 scale, €7,700/year non-EU for 2026/27, €75 application fee, in-person-preferred/video-possible audition policy, English-taught status, 2026/27 dates. MAJOR CORRECTION: there is NO listening test on music eras in this MA entrance examination — the draft imported that from EAMT's separate BACHELOR-level Sound Engineering and Music Production admission page. The MA exam is portfolio presentation plus colloquium only. Not verified: exact ECTS printed for this curriculum, any English test score threshold, scholarship names/values/eligibility, and whether a non-music bachelor triggers prerequisite subjects.

programs.program: Composition and Music Technology (MA) — Recording Arts specialisation
programs.university: Estonian Academy of Music and Theatre (EAMT / EMTA)
programs.focus: Recording / Engineering · Music Production (classical-recording emphasis)
programs.institutionType: Public national academy of music and theatre (conservatory)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (EAMT standard volume: 30 ECTS per semester, 60 per academic year). Figure not printed on the programme page.
programs.language: English (same curriculum as the electroacoustic track; listed on DreamApply as an English-taught MA)
programs.whatYouStudy: "Recording Arts offers the possibility to learn in collaboration with the main national actors in the field: Estonian Public Broadcasting and the Estonian National Symphony Orchestra, and is the only place to study classical music recording in Estonia" — with pop and jazz recording alongside, using "state-of-the-art equipment". Sits inside the wider Composition and Music Technology curriculum, so the electroacoustic/audiovisual studios and the COMMUTE Festival are in the same department. Note: EAMT's separate Sound Engineering and Music Production curriculum (studio and live recording, songwriting, Ableton / Logic Pro / Pro Tools) is BACHELOR level only; this MA is the master-level continuation within the department.
programs.facilities: Academy sound and multimedia studios and editing rooms at Tatari 13, Tallinn; Estonian Public Broadcasting and Estonian National Symphony Orchestra partnerships for classical and location recording. Detailed equipment inventory UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree (no subject restriction published); DreamApply application with photo, ID copy, prior-degree certificate with grades or diploma supplement, proof of English proficiency; €75 application fee. The panel tests specialist knowledge, general cultural knowledge and language sufficiency during the interview. No numeric English test threshold published.
programs.portfolioSpec: Verbatim: the candidate must "present 10 minutes of his/her own recorded music accompanied with an explanation detailing the contents of the recording. The portfolio should contain the following: A recording of acoustic music; An overdub recording." Plus "Submit a list of works in the field of sound engineering and composition." Plus "Be able to converse on a variety of topics reflecting professional competence and knowledge of culture and society (colloquium)." Evaluated on: "Sound quality reflective of AES/EBU standards; Originality; Technique; Musicality; Knowledge of musical styles; Creative personality; General knowledge of music and culture." Graded 0–10, "with 5 being the minimum passing grade".
programs.auditionSpec: Entrance examination = presentation and defence of the 10 minutes of recordings + colloquium on professional competence and cultural knowledge. Graded 0–10, minimum pass 5. In-person in Tallinn preferred; video substitute permitted only where travel is impossible and only if authenticity and quality are beyond doubt and the performance "clearly exceed[s] the admission threshold".
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — the degree subject is not restricted on the page, but the real gate is the portfolio: an acoustic recording plus an overdub recording judged against AES/EBU sound-quality standards, and a list of prior sound-engineering and composition works. A software-engineering BSc is not excluded, but a candidate with no recording credits has nothing to put on that list.
programs.tuitionIntl: Non-EU: €7,700/year for 2026/2027 (EAMT Senate Regulation, 29 October 2025). EU/EEA and Ukrainian: €1,750/year full-time.
programs.scholarship: "A limited number of scholarships are available for international students. Auditions for the scholarships usually take place at the end of September." No named scheme, amount or nationality list published; need-based allowance is explicitly unavailable to students on a study residence permit from outside the EU. No Tunisia-eligible scheme found.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE — 1 February 2026 via DreamApply for 2026/27; expect roughly February 2027 for a September 2027 start.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026/27 admission period 1 February – 3 July 2026.
programs.fitNotes: The most craft-oriented, console-facing English-taught option in Estonia, with genuine location and classical recording work alongside a national broadcaster and symphony orchestra, at a moderate €7,700/year. But it is the weakest fit in this batch for HIS stated goal: it is a classical-recording engineering track, not electronic music production or DJing, and the entrance portfolio demands an acoustic recording and an overdub recording judged against AES/EBU standards plus a list of existing sound-engineering credits — none of which he has. Building that by early 2027 would mean pivoting his practice away from club music toward acoustic tracking. Treat as a fallback only if he decides he wants to be an engineer rather than a producer.
programs.verificationNotes: Same official admission page read in full (raw HTML), plus the tuition regulation and general admission info. Confirmed verbatim: the 10-minute recording requirement, the mandatory acoustic + overdub content, the required list of sound-engineering and composition works, the colloquium, all seven evaluation criteria including AES/EBU sound quality, the 0–10 scale with 5 as pass, €7,700/year non-EU, €75 fee, video-audition policy, 2026/27 dates. CORRECTION: as with the electroacoustic track, there is no music-history listening test in the MA entrance examination — that requirement belongs to the BA Sound Engineering and Music Production admission. Not verified: printed ECTS, English test threshold, scholarship value/eligibility.

programs.program: CoPeCo — Contemporary Performance and Composition (MA)
programs.university: Estonian Academy of Music and Theatre (coordinating) with Royal College of Music Stockholm (KMH), CNSMD Lyon, Hochschule für Musik und Theater Hamburg
programs.city: Tallinn (sem 1, Sep–Jan) → Stockholm (sem 2, Jan–Jun) → Lyon (sem 3, Sep–Feb) → Hamburg (sem 4, Apr–Sep)
programs.focus: Live Electronics / Performance · Electronic Music · Electroacoustic Composition
programs.degree: Joint MA (Master of Arts), 120 ECTS. KMH states graduates receive "an artistic master's degree from your home institution, along with a certificate signed by the vice-chancellors of the participating institutions" — so a home-institution degree plus a consortium certificate, not a single joint diploma.
programs.institutionType: Four public conservatories / academies of music
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (30 ECTS per semester) — confirmed independently by HfMT Hamburg and KMH Stockholm
programs.language: English; "Proof of English language skills (B1): IELTS, TOEFL or equivalent"
programs.whatYouStudy: Two-year joint programme for musicians — composer, performer or both — built around experimental practice and one large-scale individual artistic project. Curriculum includes live audio and video processing and the Max multimedia programming environment, alongside creation, production, performance and the relationship between musicians and society. Mandatory rotation through the four institutions, one semester each. Both HfMT and KMH stress that the Proposal for the Master's Degree Project (Independent Project) is the single most important element of the application, and should relate to CoPeCo's key features: collaborative work, cross-disciplinary interaction, new technologies, improvisation and arts management.
programs.facilities: Studios of four major European conservatories, including KMH Stockholm and CNSMD Lyon (a leading European centre for live electronics). Detailed equipment lists UNVERIFIED — no consortium facilities page exists since copeco.net went offline.
programs.entryRequirements: HfMT Hamburg: "at least a Bachelors degree in music or equivalent", or being in the final year of an undergraduate degree; bachelor of at least 180 ECTS with diploma supplement; transcripts; proof of English at B1 (IELTS, TOEFL or equivalent). KMH Stockholm states it more strictly: "a Degree of Bachelor of Fine Arts in Music (180 credits)". A degree-project proposal is required and is the most heavily weighted element.
programs.portfolioSpec: Composers: a portfolio of scores and/or recordings (where scores are not applicable) containing at least THREE contrasting original compositions, total duration at least 15 minutes. Performers: at least TWO contrasting performance excerpts, total at least 15 minutes. Composer/performers: at least one original composition, a recording of at least one performance excerpt and another work of your choice, total at least 15 minutes. Plus the Master's Degree Project proposal.
programs.auditionSpec: Yes — a jury audition, but held ONLINE. HfMT: auditions are conducted "online around middle/end of February" and include performance presentation, testing of improvisation, and interviews. KMH describes two entrance tests with multiple components, with selection based on entrance-examination results within selection groups. No on-site travel required at the audition stage.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No / effectively blocked. HfMT requires "at least a Bachelors degree in music or equivalent"; KMH is harder still, requiring "a Degree of Bachelor of Fine Arts in Music (180 credits)". Neither institution publishes any wording admitting non-music degrees, and there is no 'other fields considered' clause anywhere. A software-engineering BSc would have to be argued as 'equivalent', with an improvisation test and a four-conservatory jury on the other side.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED for CoPeCo specifically. No CoPeCo page at any of the four institutions publishes a fee. Context: EAMT's Senate regulation sets €7,700/year for non-EU students on English-taught BA/MA curricula, excepting only Cultural Management and CPPM — CoPeCo is not excepted, so €7,700/year is the likely EAMT-side rate; KMH charges tuition to non-EU/EEA students under Swedish rules; how fees are handled across four countries is not published. Must be confirmed with hanneleen.pihlak@eamt.ee.
programs.scholarship: UNVERIFIED. CoPeCo originated as an Erasmus Mundus / LLP Erasmus Curriculum Development project; no page read confirms an EMJM scholarship is attached to the 2027 intake. The central copeco.net site is confirmed dead — "The CoPeCo website is no longer active" — and redirects to the four institutions, none of which publish funding. Nothing Tunisia-specific found.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 December 2026 — CONFIRMED for the next (2027) intake. HfMT Hamburg publishes "Next applications are expected to be open from: December 1, 2026"; KMH independently states the application period is "1 December – 15 January (every other year)" and that there were no admissions for autumn 2026. EAMT's own admission notice confirms CoPeCo had no 2026 intake. This is the correct cycle for a September 2027 start.
programs.deadline: 31 January 2027 (HfMT Hamburg: "Applications must be submitted by January 31st, 2027"). Note KMH publishes 15 January as its own closing date via universityadmissions.se, so the two institutions differ — work to the earlier date and confirm with EAMT/HfMT. This is the only programme in this batch with next-cycle dates already published.
programs.fitNotes: Exceptional content for live electronics and Max/MSP performance practice across four countries, English-taught with only a B1 language bar, online audition, and its 2027 window is already announced. But it is the hardest artistic gate in this batch: a music bachelor is required in writing (KMH specifies a BFA in Music, 180 credits), the portfolio wants at least 15 minutes of contrasting original composition, and the audition tests improvisation before a conservatory jury. Fees and funding are entirely unpublished. Realistic only as a long-shot stretch application, and only if he has a genuinely compositional body of work by January 2027.
programs.verificationNotes: sourceUrl CHANGED from the EAMT CoPeCo page (which publishes almost nothing — only the city rotation and a contact) to the HfMT Hamburg CoPeCo page, which carries the actual admission specification. Cross-checked against KMH Stockholm and the EAMT page, and copeco.net was fetched and confirmed dead. Confirmed: 120 ECTS / 30 per semester, the four-city rotation with month ranges, B1 English, the exact portfolio requirements for all three applicant categories, the online February audition including improvisation testing, the degree-project proposal as the most heavily weighted element, the 1 Dec 2026 opening and 31 Jan 2027 deadline, the biennial cycle with no 2026 intake, and the 'bachelor in music' requirement in two independent wordings. NOT verified: tuition for CoPeCo, any scholarship or Erasmus Mundus funding for the 2027 intake, per-campus facilities, and whether the KMH 15 January or HfMT 31 January date governs.

programs.program: Composition (MA) — Digital Technologies (Electronic Music) specialisation
programs.university: Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre (LMTA)
programs.focus: Electronic Music · Electroacoustic/Digital Composition
programs.degree: MA (Master of Arts, second cycle). National code 6211PX001, main study field Music.
programs.institutionType: Public national academy of music and theatre (conservatory-level university)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (30 ECTS per semester) — confirmed on the programme list and in the official curriculum PDF. Admission is ANNUAL for Composition (unlike Dance Art and Film Art, which are biennial).
programs.language: Lithuanian or English — the curriculum documents are marked LT/EN and the programme list states "Language of instruction: Lithuanian or English". One of the few LMTA master's tracks genuinely available in English.
programs.whatYouStudy: Official curriculum (MA-KOMP-Skaitmenines-technologijos, 120 ECTS): Composition 10 ECTS in each of semesters 1–3 (30 total); Processes of Digital Sound 5 ECTS × 3; Programming and Synthesis 5 ECTS × 3; Cognitive Psychology of Music 5 (sem 1); an optional management-field subject 5 (sem 1); Basics of Research Paper 5 (sem 2); free optional subjects 5 (sem 2) + 5 (sem 3); Research Paper 5 (sem 3); Final Research Paper 5 (sem 4); Master's Composition Project 25 ECTS (sem 4, defended). LMTA states graduates work as "freelance composers, arrangers, music producers, or sound designers" in concert and recording production, film, theatre, media and the creative industries. LMTA is also the Vilnius host of the ReSound Erasmus Mundus master, so staff and studios overlap.
programs.facilities: Per the ReSound consortium page, LMTA's facilities include a spatial sound sphere, two recording studios, video and audio editing workstations, a 99-seat cinema hall, a specialised cinema hall for sound mixing and mastering, and two film studios. LMTA is Lithuania's national performing-arts university, founded 1933, roughly 1,000 students across three cycles.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's diploma + supplement (certified English or Lithuanian translation if needed), an academic recognition decision from LMTA, passport/ID copy, admission fee receipt, and English at minimum B1 evidenced by TOEFL, IELTS, Cambridge English, LanguageCert or Duolingo. CRITICAL, from the official entrance-examination requirements document (updated 28 November 2025): "Admission to the second-cycle studies in Composition study programme specialisation of Digital Technologies is open for individuals who have completed the first-cycle (Bachelor's) studies in the field of music. If the applicant has completed the first cycle studies in a field different than music, during the admission interview, they must provide documents (a professional portfolio) proving at least one year's professional experience." Admission score out of 10 = entrance examination (creating music) weighted 0.6 + admission interview weighted 0.2 + bachelor GPA from the diploma supplement weighted 0.2. Non-EU/EEA applicants cannot use the LAMA BPO system directly and must first contact priemimas@lmta.lt.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW VERIFIED (was UNVERIFIED in the draft). Entrance examination "creating music": "The applicant has to submit recordings and scores of one musical piece for a chamber ensemble and several pieces of chamber music. During the examination, the chamber music works submitted for the examination may be performed by a performer(s). A PDF file (name_surname_piece_name.pdf) containing active links to the piece(s) and its scores must be sent by e-mail kompozicija.ma@lmta.lt not later than 10 days before the beginning of the entrance examination. The letter must include the sender's name, LAMA BPO registration number, contacts, study programme, specialization." Separately, non-music-bachelor applicants must bring a professional portfolio documenting at least one year's professional experience to the interview.
programs.auditionSpec: Two mandatory components: (1) the entrance examination "creating music" — submitted scores and recordings, which may be performed live by musicians during the examination — weighted 0.6; (2) a motivational/admission interview on the chosen study programme, assessing knowledge and abilities in the field, desire to develop professionally and expectations, plus discussion of creative-study projects, Final Master's Thesis topics and the professional portfolio where applicable, weighted 0.2. LMTA states entrance examinations are "organised at the Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre or remotely where this is indicated", and video recordings may be permitted "if there is a justified reason"; whether remote is available for this track is UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Conditionally — and the condition blocks him. Published wording: admission "is open for individuals who have completed the first-cycle (Bachelor's) studies in the field of music", and a non-music bachelor requires "documents (a professional portfolio) proving at least one year's professional experience". He has a software-engineering BSc and no professional audio experience, so he fails this test unless he spends the year to September 2027 accumulating documented professional work. This is a hard correction to the draft, which recorded the requirement as unaddressed.
programs.tuitionIntl: €5,312 per SEMESTER for non-EU students — the per-semester reading is now confirmed: LMTA's official 2025 master's price list gives Composition (Kompozicija, 6211PX001) at €10,425 for one year of study, roughly double the semester figure. So expect approximately €10,600 per year at the current €5,312 rate — the highest fee in this batch. The asterisk reads: "Non-EU citizens and all students who do not receive state-funded support for studies must pay a yearly tuition fee fixed by the Academy's Senate. Depending on the year of entry, prices may change." The 2025 price list also notes the autumn semester fee may be reduced by rector's order — 50% for entrants to music-field studies — worth asking about explicitly.
programs.scholarship: None available to a Tunisian. LMTA advertises "70 grants in total" restricted to citizens of a named list: Armenia, Azerbaijan, China, Georgia, Indonesia, Israel, Japan, Kazakhstan, Moldova, New Zealand, Philippines, South Korea, Ukraine, USA, Uzbekistan, Vietnam, plus foreign citizens of Lithuanian descent. Tunisia is not on that list. No other LMTA scholarship open to Tunisians found.
programs.fundingLevel: None found (for a Tunisian national) — self-pay fallback
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE — for 2026 entry the main round closed 13 March 2026 with the entrance examination on 17 March 2026 at LMTA Building II, Vilnius; the admission process opened 1 June 2026 with invitations in early July 2026; an additional round opened 20 July 2026. Expect a comparable pattern for 2027; not published as of July 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 main round: 13 March 2026, 11:00. 2026 additional round: applications due no later than 24 hours before the relevant entrance examination; examinations 17–19 August 2026; results within 48 hours; invitations to study announced 21 August 2026 by 15:00.
programs.fitNotes: On paper attractive — English-taught electronic-music composition at a national academy, only a B1 English requirement (the lowest language bar he will find in Europe), annual intake, and 120 ECTS with substantial hands-on content (Composition 30 ECTS, Processes of Digital Sound 15, Programming and Synthesis 15) plus a 25-ECTS Master's Composition Project. In practice it is now the clearest 'blocked' case in this batch: the entrance examination requires recordings AND SCORES of a chamber-ensemble piece plus several chamber-music works — notated acoustic composition, not electronic production — and a non-music bachelor must additionally document at least one year's professional experience. Add roughly €10,600/year with no scholarship route open to Tunisians. Downgraded from the draft's optimistic reading.
programs.verificationNotes: Verified against the LMTA master's programme list, the master application page, the official curriculum PDF (MA-KOMP-Skaitmenines-technologijos-2024-LT-EN) and — decisively — the official entrance-examination requirements PDF for this specialisation, in BOTH its 2025 and 2026 versions (Composition_Digital_Tech_MA_ENG_2026.pdf, approved 7 December 2023, updated 28 November 2025), which the draft had marked UNVERIFIED. Also verified the 2025 master's price list (Kainos_www_2025_MA.pdf), resolving the per-semester versus per-year ambiguity, and the grant-eligible country list excluding Tunisia. TWO MAJOR CORRECTIONS: (1) the portfolio/entrance-exam spec is chamber-ensemble scores and recordings, not an unspecified creative submission; (2) a non-music bachelor is admissible ONLY with documented professional experience of at least one year. Not verified: whether the entrance examination for this specific track may be taken remotely, and the 2027 calendar.

programs.program: Film Art (MA) — Sound Design specialisation
programs.university: Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre (LMTA)
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound · Sound Design
programs.degree: MA (Master of Arts, second cycle). National code 6211PX003, main study field Film.
programs.institutionType: Public national academy of music and theatre; film faculty
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (30 ECTS per semester). CRITICAL: "Admission takes place every two years. The next intake will be in 2026." — so the intake after 2026 is 2028, NOT September 2027.
programs.language: LITHUANIAN ONLY — "Full-time studies are conducted in Lithuanian only. A C1-level Lithuanian language certificate is required."
programs.whatYouStudy: Verified from the official curriculum PDF (MA-KMEN-Garso-dizainas, 120 ECTS): Research in Cinema: Methods and Creative Strategies 5 (sem 1); Master's Project 10 + 10 + 15 (sems 1–3); Film Theory 5 (sem 1); Philosophy of Film 5 (sem 3); Research of Sound Context 5 (sem 1); Sound Design 5 + 5 (sems 1–2); Composing for Theatre and Cinema 5 (sem 2); Theories of Culture 5 (sem 1); Basics of Research Paper 5 (sem 2); Existential Psychology 5 (sem 3); optional subjects 5 (sem 3); Final Master's Project 30 ECTS (sem 4, defended). LMTA describes Film Art as preparing professionals to create innovative film projects and conduct artistic research, applying knowledge in directing, producing, cinematography and sound design.
programs.facilities: LMTA film faculty: two film studios, a 99-seat cinema hall, a specialised cinema hall for sound mixing and mastering, two recording studios, a spatial sound sphere, and video/audio editing workstations (per the ReSound consortium description of LMTA facilities).
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's diploma + supplement with certified translation, an LMTA academic recognition decision, passport/ID copy, admission fee, and a C1-level Lithuanian language certificate. Non-EU/EEA applicants must contact priemimas@lmta.lt before applying (they cannot use LAMA BPO directly).
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — no English-language entrance-examination requirements document for the Film Art / Sound Design specialisation could be located (the equivalents exist for Composition and Music Performance but not for this track, most likely because it recruits only in Lithuanian and only every second year). Contact admission@lmta.lt or priemimas@lmta.lt.
programs.auditionSpec: Entrance examination at LMTA in Vilnius; LMTA states examinations are held on site "or remotely where this is indicated", and video recordings may be allowed "if there is a justified reason". Format and content for this specialisation UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Moot. Two prior conditions block the application before the degree subject is even considered: the C1 Lithuanian certificate, and the biennial intake cycle whose next opening after 2026 falls in 2028.
programs.tuitionIntl: €3,558 per semester (approximately €7,100 per year), per the LMTA master's programme list. The footnote states non-EU citizens and all students without state funding "must pay a yearly tuition fee fixed by the Academy's Senate" and that prices may change with the year of entry.
programs.scholarship: None available to a Tunisian. LMTA's 70 grants are restricted to the same 16-country list (Armenia, Azerbaijan, China, Georgia, Indonesia, Israel, Japan, Kazakhstan, Moldova, New Zealand, Philippines, South Korea, Ukraine, USA, Uzbekistan, Vietnam) plus foreign citizens of Lithuanian descent. Tunisia is excluded.
programs.applicationOpens: NOT APPLICABLE for September 2027. The last intake opened in 2026 (main round deadline 13 March 2026; additional round from 20 July 2026, examinations 17–19 August 2026). On the published two-year cycle the next Film Art intake is 2028.
programs.deadline: No September 2027 deadline exists — the programme does not admit in 2027. For reference, the 2026 cycle closed with the additional round in August 2026 (invitations 21 August 2026).
programs.fitNotes: Retained only for completeness as the region's dedicated master-level film-sound track; the curriculum itself is solid (Sound Design 10 ECTS, Composing for Theatre and Cinema, a 35-ECTS Master's Project stream and a 30-ECTS Final Master's Project). It is NOT viable for him and should be treated as closed: taught exclusively in Lithuanian with a C1 certificate required, admitting only every second year with the last intake in 2026 and the next expected in 2028, no funding open to Tunisians, and €3,558 per semester. If he wants LMTA film sound in English, the route is ReSound, whose third semester is taught at LMTA in Vilnius.
programs.verificationNotes: Verified against the LMTA master's programme list (raw HTML read directly, confirming the Lithuanian-only statement, the C1 requirement, the €3,558 per-semester fee and the exact sentence "Admission takes place every two years. The next intake will be in 2026."), the official curriculum PDF (MA-KMEN-Garso-dizainas-2024-LT-EN) for the module and ECTS breakdown, the master application page for documents, dates and the grant-country list, and the ReSound consortium page for LMTA facilities. NEW FINDING not in the draft: the biennial intake means there is no September 2027 entry at all — a second, independent blocker on top of the C1 Lithuanian requirement. Not verified: the portfolio/entrance-examination specification for the Sound Design specialisation, which is not published in English.

programs.program: Music and Stage Art (Professional Master, Mūzika un skatuves māksla) — Skaņu režija / Sound Engineering specialisation
programs.university: Jāzeps Vītols Latvian Academy of Music (JVLMA)
programs.focus: Recording / Engineering · Music Production
programs.institutionType: Public national academy of music (conservatory)
programs.durationEcts: UNVERIFIED — neither duration nor ECTS is published on any English-language JVLMA page read. The Latvian professional master's norm is 1.5–2 years / 90–120 ECTS, but JVLMA does not state it publicly.
programs.language: Latvian (still UNVERIFIED but strongly indicated). JVLMA publishes no English-taught master's track; the admission regulations and the master's admission-content documents are Latvian-language PDFs, and the international provisions sit in a Latvian annex.
programs.whatYouStudy: The Sound Engineering department (created 2011) teaches "acoustics, audio technology operating principles, sound recording, working with audio computer programmes and other music disciplines," with "much of the study programme focus[ing] on the balance of theory and practice." Students record at the Academy's own facilities and gain practical experience at the deciBels contemporary-music festival and on orchestral concert recordings. NOTE: this description is published on the department page, which is written primarily around the professional BACHELOR programme; JVLMA does not publish a separate master-level curriculum description.
programs.facilities: JVLMA recording studios; students record and produce concerts at the deciBels contemporary music festival and orchestral concerts. Lecturers are described as "practising sound industry professionals — sound directors and sound recording producers." Console/room/Atmos specifics remain UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED: admission to the professional master's programme "Mūzika un skatuves māksla," sub-programme Mūzika, specialisation Skaņu režija, requires a professional bachelor's degree IN MUSIC ("profesionālais bakalaura grāds mūzikā") together with the level-6 professional qualification, plus knowledge and skills in the specialisation acquired during professional bachelor studies or through professional experience. No English-language test requirement is published because the programme is not offered in English.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — no portfolio specification is published on any English page. Provisions for international applicants are in Annex I, pp. 13–15 of the Latvian-language admission regulations PDF; the master's admission content is a separate downloadable Latvian document not rendered as web text.
programs.auditionSpec: ON-SITE, and physical presence in Riga is required. CONFIRMED wording from the admissions page: "Registration of applicants (submission of documents) for studies shall take place on 25th and 26th June 2026 from 10:00 to 16:00, and on 27th June 2026 from 10:00 to 14:00, at the Jāzeps Vītols Latvian Academy of Music in person." A specialised colloquium in Sound Engineering is the priority entrance examination (per the admission regulations); its exact format could not be re-read in the current cycle's Latvian PDF.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No. The published requirement is a professional bachelor's degree in music ("profesionālais bakalaura grāds mūzikā") plus a level-6 professional qualification. A Tunisian BSc in Software Engineering does not satisfy this on its face, and no alternative entry route (portfolio equivalence, bridging year) is published.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — JVLMA publishes no tuition table in English and no fee for non-EU students could be located.
programs.scholarship: None found. No named scholarship open to a Tunisian applicant is published by JVLMA; the international section covers only Erasmus+, Nordplus Music and masterclasses (i.e. exchange, not degree funding).
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For 2026 entry, in-person document registration ran 25–27 June 2026. Expect a comparable late-June 2027 window, but JVLMA had published nothing for 2027 as of July 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (25–27 June 2026 for 2026/2027 entry).
programs.verificationNotes: CONFIRMED: (a) the Professional Master programme "Music and performing arts" exists and the field-of-study-arts page explicitly lists "specialization Sound Engineering" within it — so the programme is real and at master level; (b) the entry requirement of a professional bachelor's degree in music for the Skaņu režija master specialisation; (c) in-person document registration in Riga on 25–27 June 2026, quoted verbatim from the admissions page. SOURCE URL CORRECTED: the originally supplied URL (jvlma.lv/en/studies/studies/sound-engineering) describes the BACHELOR programme — it states graduates receive "a Professional Bachelor's degree in Music" plus "the sixth level professional qualification" — so it was the wrong page for a master's entry; replaced with the field-of-study page that actually lists the master. NOT CONFIRMED: duration, ECTS, language of instruction, tuition for non-EU students, portfolio specification, and the exact colloquium format — none of these are published in English, and the governing documents are Latvian-language PDFs behind download links. Nothing found contradicts the original assessment; if anything the degree barrier is now firmer.
programs.fitNotes: Genuine studio training at a national academy, but structurally closed to him: entry demands a professional bachelor's degree in MUSIC with a level-6 qualification, instruction is almost certainly Latvian, and document submission requires him to be physically in Riga in late June. Keep it on the list only as a documented exclusion.

programs.program: New Media and Audiovisual Art (MA) — "Sound Art and Electronic Music" specialisation (joint programme with RISEBA, in cooperation with RIXC and MPLab)
programs.university: RTU Liepāja Academy, Riga Technical University (formerly Liepāja University — LiepU merged into RTU on 1 March 2024) with RISEBA University of Applied Sciences
programs.city: Liepāja and Riga (studies split between both cities)
programs.focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based) · Electronic Music · Immersive Audio
programs.degree: Academic Master's degree (MA), second cycle, EQF/LQF level 7
programs.durationEcts: 2 years full-time / 120 credit points. Note a discrepancy: the RTU programme registry entry (code HMJ) states 120 CP, while one third-party listing states 132 ECTS — confirm the current figure with RTU before relying on it.
programs.institutionType: Public technical university (RTU, arts faculty via its Liepāja Academy) jointly with a private university of applied sciences (RISEBA), in cooperation with the independent RIXC New Media Culture Centre
programs.language: English. CONFIRMED via the RTU programme registry, which records the programme as full-time, 2 years, taught in English; the local Latvian-language intake also exists. Because the LiepU→RTU merger reorganised the arts offer, confirm in writing that the English cohort is actually running for the September 2027 intake.
programs.whatYouStudy: Multidisciplinary, practice-led and research-based work across acoustic art, digital and networked media, art-and-science, interactive technologies, video and photographic media, VR/AR and 360° video. Four specialisation tracks: "Sound Art and Electronic Music" and "Digital Art and Immersive Media" are run by RTU Liepāja Academy; "Audiovisual Media Art" and "Multimedia Stage Art" are run by RISEBA in Riga. Sound-specific teaching sits in Liepāja and is built around the MPLab, the iWeek media-arts week and the "Skaņas dienas" (Sound Days) sound-art festival. Classes are scheduled Thursday and Friday evenings (18:00–21:00) and Saturdays (10:00–15:00), which is designed to be combinable with work.
programs.facilities: MPLab (Art Research Laboratory) in Liepāja, one of the Baltic region's established media-art labs; the RIXC festival and network in Riga; the Sound Days sound-art festival as a production platform. Specific studio hardware, consoles and immersive-audio rooms remain UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED and materially better than previously recorded: the programme's own published description states it is for "anyone interested in this program, including those that have already obtained a bachelor's or master's degree in OTHER FIELDS." A bachelor's degree is required. RTU's international admission adds: bachelor's certificate with transcript in the original language plus certified English translation, and English at B2 or above evidenced by a recognised certificate or a Medium of Instruction letter. Registration fee €30 for the first choice (+€10 per further option) on the Latvian-track application; RTU's international application fee is listed at €150 — confirm which applies to a non-EU applicant. From 1 January 2026 RTU international applicants must additionally show proof of living funds of €9,400 per year for the residence permit.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED: a master's thesis proposal of up to ONE A4 page, plus an artistic portfolio of UP TO 5 WORKS, each with photo documentation of the artwork, a description and, where relevant, a link to video or a website. For collaborative works the applicant must "indicate precisely your individual contribution."
programs.auditionSpec: Online entrance interview via MS Teams — no on-site test. CONFIRMED wording: applicants "will have to present your master's thesis application and portfolio, answer the questions of the admission commission." For the 2026 intake the interview was held on 10 August. This remains one of the few genuinely remote-friendly admission processes in the slice.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — this is a correction to the earlier assessment. The programme page explicitly welcomes "those that have already obtained a bachelor's or master's degree in other fields." The earlier concern that entry was restricted to "Humanitarian, Social, Art or Educational sciences" reflected an older LiepU field list; the current published wording imposes no such restriction. Still worth a one-line written confirmation to RTU Liepāja Academy given the merger, but it is no longer the main risk.
programs.tuitionIntl: €3,100 per year for self-funded study, as published on the programme's own page alongside "5 state-budget places, 5 personal-expense places." One aggregator quotes ≈USD 2,992/year (consistent). CAUTION: post-merger RTU lists graduate tuition in the €2,670–4,190 range generally, and one aggregator quotes €11,000/year for this programme — that outlier is almost certainly wrong, but the non-EU rate specifically was NOT confirmed on an RTU page (rtu.lv returns 403 to automated fetching). Treat €3,100/year as the published figure and confirm the non-EU rate in writing.
programs.scholarship: State-funded (budget) places exist — 5 per intake — but eligibility for a non-EU/Tunisian applicant is UNVERIFIED and Latvian budget places are normally reserved for EU/EEA nationals. No named international scholarship found.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial / UNVERIFIED (the low published fee functions as de facto partial funding; true budget-place access for a Tunisian is unconfirmed)
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For 2026 entry, LiepU/RTU applications ran to 7 August with a supplementary round 26 July – 20 August 2026; RISEBA accepted applications into early September. RTU's international portal (apply.rtu.lv) opens separately and earlier for autumn intakes.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 2026 entry: 7 August application deadline, online interview 10 August, supplementary round to 20 August 2026. One aggregator lists 1 February 2027 for a September 2027 intake — UNVERIFIED, do not rely on it; the international RTU deadline is likely to be considerably earlier than the local August one.
programs.verificationNotes: MAJOR STRUCTURAL CORRECTION: Liepāja University no longer exists as an independent institution — it merged into Riga Technical University on 1 March 2024 and now operates as RTU Liepāja Academy. liepu.lv redirects to rtu.lv/lv/liepaja. The university field has been corrected accordingly; any application must go through RTU. CONFIRMED from the programme's own page: €3,100/year self-funded, 5 budget + 5 fee-paying places, portfolio of up to 5 works with documentation, one-A4 thesis proposal, online MS Teams interview, the four specialisation tracks and which partner runs each, and — importantly — that the programme is open to holders of bachelor's or master's degrees in OTHER FIELDS. CONFIRMED from the RTU programme registry (code HMJ): academic master, 2 years, 120 CP, English, Liepāja Academy, accredited 4 Oct 2023 – 5 Oct 2029. NOT CONFIRMED: the non-EU tuition rate specifically (rtu.lv blocks automated fetching with HTTP 403), whether the English cohort runs in 2027, the English-test threshold (the programme page previously cited IELTS 5.5; RTU's international rule is B2, and one aggregator claims IELTS 6.5–7.5 — three inconsistent figures, so treat as unresolved), and 2027 deadlines. SEPARATE FINDING WORTH FLAGGING: RISEBA's own page at the same slug now presents a rebranded RISEBA-only master, "Audiovisual and Immersive Technology Arts" (120 ECTS, English or Latvian evening study, €4,100/yr EU / €4,700/yr non-EU, portfolio of 3–5 works). Its entry rules explicitly admit "a bachelor's degree in social sciences, engineering, computer science, or related fields" provided the applicant adds either 12+ months of professional creative work experience or 12+ ECTS of humanities/arts coursework. That is a second, separately-documented Riga route with an engineering-friendly entry clause, and it suggests the joint LiepU+RISEBA structure may be being unbundled — verify the joint programme's current status with both institutions.
programs.fitNotes: Still the best value-for-money creative option in the Baltics, and now materially stronger for him: €3,100/year published fee, portfolio of only 5 works, an online interview rather than an on-site audition, a real sound-art/electronic-music track with a festival attached, and published entry wording that explicitly welcomes bachelor's holders from other fields — so his software-engineering BSc is no longer the blocker it appeared to be. Remaining caveats keep it at B rather than A: the LiepU→RTU merger means the joint structure and the English cohort both need written confirmation, the non-EU tuition rate is unconfirmed and RTU now requires proof of €9,400/year in living funds, and the training is sonic art and research rather than commercial DJ/producer craft.

programs.program: Reżyseria dźwięku (Sound Engineering / Sound Direction), studia II stopnia — specialisations: reżyseria muzyczna, reżyseria dźwięku w filmie i telewizji, reżyseria dźwięku w multimediach
programs.university: Uniwersytet Muzyczny Fryderyka Chopina (Chopin University of Music, UMFC), Faculty of Sound Engineering
programs.focus: Recording / Engineering · Music Production · Film/Game Sound · Immersive Audio
programs.institutionType: Public university of music (conservatory), supervised by the Minister of Culture and National Heritage
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters — CONFIRMED verbatim: "Stopień drugi – magisterski – trwa 2 lata (4 semestry)." Total ECTS is not stated on the faculty pages; the Polish second-cycle statutory norm is 120 ECTS but UMFC does not publish the figure.
programs.language: Polish for the sound-engineering track. UMFC's recruitment page confirms the university "znacznie poszerza ofertę edukacyjną o studia prowadzone w języku wykładowym angielskim na specjalnościach cieszących się największym zainteresowaniem wśród studentów zagranicznych," but the specialisations concerned are not enumerated on the page and reżyseria dźwięku is NOT identified as one of them. Assume Polish until the faculty informator says otherwise.
programs.whatYouStudy: Three master-level specialisations, CONFIRMED verbatim: "Kandydaci mają do wyboru jedną z trzech specjalności: reżyserię muzyczną, reżyserię dźwięku w filmie i telewizji oraz reżyserię dźwięku w multimediach." (1) Music sound direction — studio and live recording of classical and popular music; (2) sound for film and television — building a film's sound layer and audio post-production; (3) sound in multimedia — interactive sound design, particularly for video games and audiovisual forms.
programs.facilities: The Faculty runs multiple recording studios with professional equipment for student productions. Founded in 1954, it is one of the oldest sound-direction training centres in the world and the only faculty of its kind in Poland. Console and Atmos/immersive-room specifics remain UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: A first-cycle (bachelor's) diploma, plus passing the entrance tests and completing the qualification procedure. Registration is exclusively through the IRK system at irk.chopin.edu.pl — CONFIRMED verbatim: "Rejestracja w systemie IRK jest obowiązkowa i będzie dostępna poprzez stronę irk.chopin.edu.pl od dnia 1 maja 2026 r." Recruitment fee 150 PLN. A separate procedure and deadline schedule for cudzoziemcy (foreigners) is published as a dedicated PDF on the recruitment page.
programs.portfolioSpec: No conventional creative portfolio is required for entry — selection is by examination. Where audio-video recordings are submitted as part of an application, UMFC requires the candidate to be shown "in full without close-ups, without image movement, and without editing within a single piece," with clear audio and proper lighting.
programs.auditionSpec: ON-SITE and multi-stage, plus a compulsory hearing test. CONFIRMED: "W przypadku kierunku Reżyseria Dźwięku kandydaci muszą przed sprawdzianami wykonać audiometryczne badanie słuchu w Katedrze Akustyki Muzycznej i Multimediów UMFC" — i.e. every sound-engineering candidate must sit a free audiometric hearing examination at the Department of Musical Acoustics and Multimedia in Warsaw BEFORE the entrance tests (~40 min, room 413). The tests themselves comprise a written/practical examination in ear training with elements of harmony, acoustics, and knowledge of music-recording production and film sound, followed by a qualification interview (ear-training test up to 25 points, interview score ×2, maximum 75 points). The exact 2026/27 scoring table sits inside the recruitment guide PDF, which is image-compressed and could not be re-read as text.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — probably yes on paper. The published requirement is only a first-cycle diploma, with no subject restriction, and the matura expectations for this field point at mathematics (basic level) and mathematics or physics (extended level) rather than music. So a software-engineering BSc is formally admissible. The real filter is the ear-training and harmony examination, which presumes solfège-level musicianship he does not yet have.

programs.program: Inżynieria Akustyczna (Acoustic Engineering), studia II stopnia — specjalność "Inżynieria dźwięku w mediach i kulturze" (Sound Engineering in Media and Culture)
programs.university: AGH University of Krakow (Akademia Górniczo-Hutnicza im. Stanisława Staszica), Faculty of Mechanical Engineering and Robotics
programs.focus: Recording / Engineering · Immersive / Spatial Audio · Sound for media (technical route)
programs.institutionType: Public technical university, supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED from the AGH recruitment page: winter recruitment 3 semesters (entry requirement INŻYNIER); summer recruitment 4 semesters (entry requirement LICENCJAT). The 90 ECTS figure for the 3-semester track is consistent with AGH's programme documents but is not stated on the recruitment page itself.
programs.language: Polish. CONFIRMED indirectly and importantly: AGH requires foreign applicants to "confirm knowledge of the language of instruction at a minimum level of B-2" — so a Polish-taught acoustic-engineering master requires certified B2 Polish. No English-taught version of inżynieria akustyczna was found; contact wkr-imir@agh.edu.pl to confirm.
programs.whatYouStudy: Two master specialisations: "Drgania i hałas w technice i środowisku" (Vibrations and Noise in Technology and Environment) and the relevant one, "Inżynieria dźwięku w mediach i kulturze" (Sound Engineering in Media and Culture). Graduates are trained as sound-system designers, sound engineers in media, and audio programmers in IT companies, and are explicitly prepared for supporting cultural and artistic institutions and participating in art-creation processes. This is the technical/engineering route into professional audio, not an artistic one.
programs.facilities: Laboratories of the AGH Department of Mechanics and Vibroacoustics. Recording-studio and Atmos/immersive facilities remain UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED AND MORE DEMANDING THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. Prior degree: LICENCJAT for the summer round (4 semesters, includes a compensatory semester), INŻYNIER for the winter round (3 semesters) — a Tunisian BSc in Software Engineering would most plausibly map to the inżynier route, subject to AGH's recognition assessment. There IS an entrance examination: AGH computes a recruitment index WR = wE·E + wS·S, where E is the entrance-exam score on a 0–100 scale ("scores below 30 disqualify candidates"), S is the standardised first-cycle GPA, and the weights sum to 10; the programme page shows both weights at 5, i.e. exam and GPA count equally. Maximum index 1000 points ("Maksymalna wartość wskaźnika rekrutacji wynosi 1000 pkt"). Foreign applicants must additionally document language of instruction at B2. Recruitment fee: the programme page shows 100 PLN; AGH's general 2026/2027 schedule lists 85 PLN where the AGH mathematics exam is not taken and 100 PLN where it is.
programs.portfolioSpec: None — this is a technical programme and admission turns on the entrance-exam score plus first-cycle GPA, not on creative work. CONFIRMED: no portfolio appears anywhere in the qualification formula.
programs.auditionSpec: None — no audition, no creative test, no audiometry. But note this is NOT the same as "no examination": a written qualification exam scored 0–100 is part of the recruitment index, with a disqualifying floor of 30 points. Its subject content for inżynieria akustyczna could not be confirmed and should be requested from wkr-imir@agh.edu.pl.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, by design — it is an engineering degree and a software-engineering bachelor is a natural feeder. This remains the one programme in the slice where his degree is an asset rather than an obstacle. The qualifying constraints are the entrance exam and B2 Polish, not his subject.
programs.tuitionIntl: CORRECTED — the "0 PLN" is misleading for him. The programme page does show a semester fee of 0 PLN, but that reflects the standard full-time Polish-track rate for those entitled to free study. AGH's International Students Office publishes separate fees for foreigners: roughly €1,000–2,750 per semester for full-time study depending on programme and level, with engineering programmes in the €1,250–2,750 band. Exemption from tuition is available on defined grounds, including a NAWA decision (which is how Banach delivers free study), and notably also for holders of a C1 Polish-language certificate on full-time Polish-taught programmes. Exact 2026/2027 amounts are in Attachment No. 3 to Rector's Regulation No. 39/2026.
programs.scholarship: Banach NAWA Programme — genuinely available here, and for a better reason than previously stated. CONFIRMED from the Banach 2026 call (Announcement No. 16/2026 of 13 April 2026): Tunisia is an eligible country and sits in Group 3 (with Angola, Jordan, Kenya, Lebanon, Palestine, Rwanda, Senegal, Tanzania). CORRECTION: the call imposes NO field-of-study restriction on any group — the earlier claim that Group 3 is limited to engineering, agricultural and natural sciences does not appear in the current call. What the call DOES restrict is the institution: it funds studies "conducted at universities supervised by the Minister of Science and Higher Education that have concluded a framework agreement with NAWA." AGH is such a university, which is precisely why Banach works here and fails at every Polish music academy in this slice. Other eligibility conditions he meets or must watch: no prior master's degree; no previous NAWA second-cycle scholarship; first-cycle degree obtained no earlier than 2024 (he graduates 2026, so fine); and documented B2 in the language of instruction (B2 Polish for the Polish track, or B1 Polish if he takes the funded one-year preparatory course first).
programs.stipend: Banach NAWA: PLN 2,500 per month, paid for up to 12 months per academic year (max 5 months in the winter semester, 7 in the summer); exemption from education fees at public universities; and a one-off lump sum for international travel paid together with the first monthly scholarship. A one-year NAWA Polish preparatory course, also on scholarship terms, can precede Polish-taught studies.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. AGH runs summer and winter recruitment rounds; the general 2026 admission window ran from 1 June to 11 September 2026, and 2027 dates were not published as of July 2026. The Banach NAWA 2026 call opened 13 April 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date for both. IMPORTANT TIMING POINT: the Banach 2026 call funds studies starting in the winter semester 2026/27, so for a September 2027 start he needs the Banach 2027 call, expected around April–May 2027 — which lines up well with his target intake.
programs.verificationNotes: CONFIRMED on the official AGH recruitment page: both master specialisations including "Inżynieria dźwięku w mediach i kulturze"; 3-semester winter track requiring an inżynier degree and 4-semester summer track requiring a licencjat; 0 PLN listed semester fee; 100 PLN recruitment fee; and qualification by exam result and academic record at equal weight. CONFIRMED on the AGH general recruitment-conditions page: the WR = wE·E + wS·S formula, the 0–100 exam scale with a disqualifying floor of 30, and the 1000-point maximum. CONFIRMED on AGH's international office pages: B2 in the language of instruction for foreign applicants, per-semester tuition for foreigners in the €1,000–2,750 range with engineering at €1,250–2,750, the exemption grounds including a NAWA decision and a C1 Polish certificate, and the 2026/2027 fee schedule reference (Attachment 3 to Rector's Regulation 39/2026). CONFIRMED from the primary Banach 2026 call PDF, read in full: Tunisia's eligibility and Group 3 placement, the absence of any field-of-study restriction, the Ministry-of-Science-and-Higher-Education institutional limitation, PLN 2,500/month, fee exemption at public universities, the travel lump sum, the 8 May 2026 15:00 deadline with a 300-application quota per group, the 2024-or-later first-degree rule, and the B1/B2 language thresholds. TWO SUBSTANTIVE CORRECTIONS to the previous entry: (1) tuition is NOT free for a non-EU self-funded applicant — the 0 PLN figure does not apply to him absent an exemption; (2) there IS an entrance examination, so the previous 'no audition or portfolio' framing understated the barrier, even though no CREATIVE test exists. One item still open: whether AGH holds a current framework agreement with NAWA (a Banach precondition) could not be confirmed from the sources read, and should be checked with AGH's International Students Office.
programs.fitNotes: Still the only credible fully-funded, degree-compatible route found in Poland: his software-engineering BSc fits the entry requirement, there is no creative audition or portfolio, and Banach NAWA is genuinely reachable here — Tunisia is eligible, there is no subject restriction, and AGH is the right kind of institution, unlike every music academy in this slice. Downgraded from an unqualified recommendation to B because verification exposed two real hurdles the earlier note missed: he must pass a written entrance exam with a disqualifying floor, and he must certify B2 Polish (or take the funded NAWA preparatory year first, which pushes the start to 2028). And the deeper caveat stands — this trains a competent audio engineer or audio programmer, not a producer or DJ. Best treated as the funded pragmatic option with music production pursued alongside.
