programs.program: Akustyka (Acoustics), studia II stopnia — specjalność "Dźwięk i multimedia" (Sound and Multimedia)
programs.university: Adam Mickiewicz University in Poznań (UAM), Faculty of Physics and Astronomy / Katedra Akustyki (Department of Acoustics, formerly Institute of Acoustics)
programs.focus: Recording / Engineering · Immersive Audio · Film/Game Sound — delivered inside a scientific-acoustics degree, not a music degree
programs.institutionType: Public research university
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters, full-time ("Poziom studiów: drugiego stopnia", "forma studiów: stacjonarne", "czas trwania: 2 lata"). Total ECTS is NOT stated on the recruitment or faculty pages read; the Polish statutory norm for a 2-year second-cycle degree is 120 ECTS, but this specific figure remains UNVERIFIED (the UAM syllabus server, sylabus.amu.edu.pl, returned HTTP 503 on repeated attempts).
programs.language: Polish only ("Język prowadzenia studiów: polski"). CONFIRMED on both the Polish and English recruitment pages: "All foreign applicants must provide documentation of Polish language proficiency at B2 level." Per UAM's admissions Q&A, since 1 August 2025 non-EU citizens must supply one of the documents listed in the Ministerial Ordinance of 30 July 2025 — the online Polish placement test route is available to EU citizens only, so he cannot test into it during recruitment. The qualification interview is also conducted in Polish.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED and considerably better than previously recorded. Semester 1 is common acoustics foundations; from semester 2 students follow one of three specialisations — Akustyka audiologiczna (audiological/hearing-aid acoustics), Akustyka stosowana (applied/noise and environmental acoustics), or Dźwięk i multimedia (sound and multimedia). The Faculty of Physics page names actual modules on the Sound and Multimedia track: "Studio Recording", "Sound in Films and Games" and "Immersive and Spatial Sound", plus shared modules "Artificial Intelligence in Physical Signal Processing" and "Project Management". So there IS genuine hands-on studio, game/film-audio and spatial-audio content. What there is NOT: composition, DJing, electronic music performance, beat-making, arrangement or artist development. The framing is engineering and physics of sound; career destinations listed are recording studios, hearing-aid fitting, environmental-protection agencies, research labs and IT.
programs.facilities: CONFIRMED to exist, detail partly from secondary industry press rather than the official page. The Department of Acoustics runs Poland's Reżyseria dźwięku (Sound Direction) bachelor, launched 1999/2000, and teaches it in two dedicated recording studios; an anechoic chamber and recording studio complex was opened in April 2002 and described at the time as the most modern in Poland. Official faculty page states "well-equipped research and teaching laboratories" with modern instrumentation and international partnerships with universities in the UK, Sweden, Norway and Japan. No published console/monitoring/Atmos inventory — immersive audio is taught as a module, but whether a certified Dolby Atmos room exists is UNVERIFIED. No music-industry or label links published; this is an academic physics department, not an industry school.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED verbatim on the English recruitment page: selection is "for graduates of first- or second-cycle studies within the area of exact sciences, technology or natural sciences". Qualification = GPA from prior higher studies (max 5 points) + "interview concerning acoustics - signal analysis, psychoacoustics and physical acoustics" (max 5 points); 10 points maximum. Non-EU applicants additionally: documented Polish at B2, apostille or consular legalisation of the foreign diploma, sworn translation, and confirmation of eligibility to apply for second-cycle studies in Poland. Recruitment fee 100 PLN. Limit: 15 places. NOTE A DISCREPANCY worth raising with the department: the Faculty of Physics programme page states applicants should hold a bachelor's "preferably in Acoustics or Sound Direction" and that the interview tests first-cycle acoustics knowledge — so while a software-engineering BSc is formally admissible, he would be competing against UAM's own Reżyseria dźwięku and Akustyka graduates for 15 seats, on their syllabus.
programs.portfolioSpec: None. CONFIRMED — no portfolio, demo reel, or creative submission of any kind appears in the admission criteria. Admission is GPA + oral technical interview only.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition and no performance test. There IS a compulsory oral qualification interview ("rozmowa kwalifikacyjna") on signal analysis, psychoacoustics and physical acoustics, worth half the admission score, conducted in Polish. For the 2026/27 cycle it is scheduled for 17 September 2026 with results 18 September 2026; candidates are given their exact slot via their account in the UAM online admission system. Whether foreign candidates may sit it remotely is NOT published — UNVERIFIED, and must be asked directly (ia@amu.edu.pl / +48 61 829 51 24), since travelling to Poznań for a 5-point interview before holding a visa is a real practical obstacle.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, formally. The published entry rule is a degree "within the area of exact sciences, technology or natural sciences" — a BSc in Software Engineering sits squarely inside that, and no music background is required or expected. The real filter is not the diploma but the interview: it examines first-cycle acoustics content (signal analysis, psychoacoustics, physical acoustics) that his curriculum only partly overlaps (DSP yes; psychoacoustics and physical acoustics no), and it is examined in Polish.
programs.tuitionIntl: VERIFIED and CORRECTED — previously recorded as UNVERIFIED. UAM's official fees page for international candidates gives 4,000 PLN per semester for foreigners on full-time Polish-language studies in 2026/2027, i.e. approx. 8,000 PLN / roughly EUR 1,850 per year (the 15,400 PLN/semester figure applies to medical programmes only). Plus a one-off 100 PLN recruitment fee. Notably, the published exemption list includes holders of a C1 Polish certificate from the State Certification Commission — so a candidate who reached C1 Polish would study tuition-free even without a scholarship. By European standards this is a genuinely low-cost option.
programs.scholarship: Banach NAWA (Prof. Stefan Banach Programme). VERIFIED against the official 2026 call (NAWA announcement no. 16/2026 of 13 April 2026): Tunisia is explicitly named as an eligible country and is listed in Group 3. IMPORTANT CORRECTION to the previous record: the 2026 call contains NO field-of-study restriction by country group — the groups only govern application quotas (the call closes at 300 applications per group for Groups 1-3). So the earlier worry about whether Acoustics counts as an eligible Banach field is moot; any second-cycle field at an eligible Polish public university qualifies. Hard eligibility conditions he meets: not a Polish citizen; first-cycle degree obtained in a Programme country (Tunisia) no earlier than 2024; no prior master's degree; no prior NAWA second-cycle scholarship. Selection is 0-110 points: 0-70 for first-cycle GPA (minimum 50 required, i.e. roughly a 71%+ average), 0-30 for a 1-3 minute recorded self-presentation video justifying the field choice, 0-10 for an optional Polish diplomatic-mission recommendation. Also potentially relevant: the C1-Polish tuition exemption above, and general UAM/Polish-government scholarship routes — not separately verified.
programs.fundingLevel: Full if Banach NAWA is won (stipend + tuition exemption + travel); otherwise Partial-by-default, since the self-pay cost is only about 8,000 PLN/year and drops to zero with a C1 Polish certificate.
programs.stipend: Banach NAWA, per the official 2026 call: PLN 2,500 per month, paid up to 12 months per academic year (max 5 months in the winter semester, 7 in the summer), running from the first month of classes and also during the NAWA preparatory year; plus exemption from tuition at public universities; plus a one-off lump sum for international travel to Poland, paid together with the first monthly instalment. CORRECTION: the travel lump sum's AMOUNT is not stated in the call text (it is cross-referenced to the NAWA Act); the previously recorded "PLN 2,500 travel allowance" appears to be a misreading of the PLN 2,500 monthly scholarship it is bundled with — treat the travel figure as UNVERIFIED.
programs.applicationOpens: UAM: 1 June for the 2026/27 cycle. For his SEPTEMBER 2027 target the 2027/28 dates are not yet published — expect a comparable early-June 2027 opening, but confirm. Banach NAWA: the 2026 call opened 13 April 2026 and closed 8 May 2026; a Banach 2027 call, if repeated on the same pattern, would open around spring 2027 — NOT the Oct 2026-Feb 2027 window assumed elsewhere in this shortlist, so the NAWA calendar must be tracked separately from the university calendar.

Banach NAWA 2026: deadline 8 May 2026, 15:00 Warsaw (or earlier if 300 Group-3 applications arrive first), results by 31 July 2026 — this deadline has ALREADY PASSED and applied only to studies starting October 2026. programs.verificationNotes: CONFIRMED on official UAM pages (rekrutacja.amu.edu.pl Polish and English catalogue entries, fizyka.amu.edu.pl programme page, amu.edu.pl fees and admissions Q&A) and the official NAWA 2026 call PDF: the programme exists at second-cycle level in Poznań; 2 years full-time; Polish-language; three specialisations with Dźwięk i multimedia among them; module names Studio Recording / Sound in Films and Games / Immersive and Spatial Sound; entry open to exact-sciences, technical and natural-sciences graduates; GPA + acoustics interview scoring; no portfolio; 15 places; 100 PLN recruitment fee; mandatory B2 Polish for foreign applicants; non-EU tuition 4,000 PLN per semester with a C1-Polish exemption; Tunisia's Banach Group-3 eligibility, the PLN 2,500/month stipend, the tuition exemption, the preparatory-year path and the full scoring rubric. NEWLY CORRECTED: tuition was previously UNVERIFIED and is now confirmed and cheap; the claimed Banach field-of-study restriction does not exist in the 2026 call; the PLN 2,500 travel allowance figure is not supported by the call text; the source URL was upgraded to the official English catalogue page. STILL UNVERIFIED: total ECTS (syllabus server returned 503 repeatedly); whether the qualification interview can be sat remotely by an overseas candidate; the specific studio/console/Atmos inventory available to master's students on the Sound and Multimedia track; whether UAM holds a current NAWA framework agreement (Attachment 2 of the call, not retrieved — it is a ministry-supervised public university so this is very likely but should be checked); and all 2027/28 dates. Rated Partial rather than Verified because of the ECTS gap, the interview-mode question, and the unresolved discrepancy between the recruitment page's open eligibility wording and the faculty page's "preferably in Acoustics or Sound Direction" preference.
programs.fitNotes: Downgraded from the earlier optimistic read. What is genuinely good: his BSc is formally accepted, there is no portfolio and no audition, the tuition is among the cheapest on the whole shortlist (about EUR 1,850/year, zero with C1 Polish), Tunisia is confirmed Banach-eligible with no field restriction, and the Dźwięk i multimedia track really does teach studio recording, game/film sound and immersive audio. What blocks it: (1) B2 Polish is mandatory for non-EU applicants and cannot be waived or tested-around — he has no Polish at all, and the online test route is EU-only; (2) the Banach workaround, a funded preparatory Polish year, needs only B1 at application but pushes the actual degree start to October 2028, missing his September 2027 target by a full year, and the direct path would require B2 Polish from zero inside ~14 months; (3) half the admission score is an acoustics interview, in Polish, on psychoacoustics and physical acoustics he has never studied, for 15 places, against UAM's own sound-engineering graduates; (4) even on success, this is a physics degree that trains recording and acoustics engineers — it will not make him a DJ or a producer, and there is no artist-development, composition or industry-network dimension. Best treated as a cheap, funded long-game fallback if he is willing to commit to learning Polish, not as a route to the September 2027 intake.

programs.program: Zvuková tvorba (Sound Design) — navazující magisterský studijní program (N0211A310015)
programs.university: Akademie múzických umění v Praze — FAMU (Film and TV School)
programs.institutionType: Public film school / academy of performing arts
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive Audio
programs.language: Czech. The official specific-conditions document for 2026/27 is issued in Czech and the programme record is Czech-language; FAMU's fee-paying English-taught MFA offer does not include Sound Design. (FAMU's English admissions page returned 404 on fetch — the English-language tuition figure could NOT be confirmed and is withdrawn.)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (standard Czech navazující magisterský). Exact internal credit split not restated in the 2026/27 specific-conditions PDF.
programs.whatYouStudy: Quoted premise from the official 2026/27 conditions: the master's programme 'vychází z premisy filmového zvuku jako komplexního fenoménu' — it proceeds from film sound as a complex phenomenon. Broad knowledge of the technical means and procedures of sound production and post-production is treated as a necessary but NOT sufficient condition of the profession; emphasis is on conceptual thinking and on active argumentative/discursive ability. Every practical exercise is coupled with a defence (obhajoba) in which the student reflects on the poetics, style and context of the work submitted. Students run the sound on FAMU student films end-to-end and graduate as sound designers / sound supervisors / re-recording mixers.
programs.entryRequirements: Completed bachelor's degree. Official wording: the programme is 'přístupné absolventům a absolventkám bakalářského studia studijního programu Zvuková tvorba FAMU, případně též absolventům a absolventkám jiného vysokoškolského studijního programu' (open to graduates of FAMU's own BA in Sound Design, or possibly also to graduates of another higher-education programme). Applicants from outside FAMU must ADDITIONALLY attach: a CV with address, e-mail and phone; proof of having passed the state bachelor examination; and a school-certified list of ALL courses of the completed programme with grades. Czech-language study, so Czech at B2/C1 is the practical gate. CORRECTION: medical fitness is explicitly NOT required — 'Zdravotní způsobilost: Pro přijetí do tohoto oboru se nevyžaduje.'
programs.portfolioSpec: Round 1, documents only, uploaded via prihlaska.amu.cz by the works deadline (1 Sept in the 2026/27 cycle): (1) a LIST of all own sound works made during bachelor's study (audiovisual/multimedia works, music recordings, radio and theatre sound design), each with title, genre classification, director's first and last name, plus production, running time and year — ordered by date of creation, and INCLUDING unfinished works in progress; (2) TWO audiovisual works on whose sound component the applicant participated significantly, with detailed written explications of both, plus the applicant's own theoretical work in the field (this item is waived only for KZT FAMU graduates who passed their state exam in 2025/26 — i.e. it is aimed squarely at external applicants); (3) a written Project for master's study at FAMU: intended specialisation, expected outcomes, which courses he would take in FAMU's elective programme or at other universities, and any interest in a foreign internship. FILE SPEC (newly confirmed): filenames 'ČÍSLO ÚKOLU - NÁZEV ÚKOLU - PŘÍJMENÍ JMÉNO' without diacritics; audio in WAV; video preferably MP4/MOV, H.264, max 10 Mbit/s; written documents in PDF with a header giving field, name and address. A signed declaration of authorship is mandatory, and it now ALSO requires declaring any use of generative AI (research / language check / narrative consultation / other / none).
programs.auditionSpec: Round 2 is an IN-PERSON oral examination in Prague. CORRECTION — this is more than an interview: the candidate must demonstrate theoretical knowledge of the artistic and technical problems of the field at the level of a FAMU Sound Design BA graduate, AND must prove musical erudition through one of several chosen forms — 'hrou na hudební nástroj (melodický, rytmický, elektronický), zpěvem, nebo jinou vhodně zvolenou formou živého vystoupení' (playing a musical instrument — melodic, rhythmic or ELECTRONIC — singing, or another suitably chosen form of live performance). He must then also sit a pitch-memory test and a rhythmic dictation. The submitted Project and the list of works form the basis of the interview. Scoring: candidates who reach Round 2 need 40 of 60 points overall, and must also reach the minimum in each sub-examination.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — formally yes, practically hard. Official wording permits graduates of 'jiného vysokoškolského studijního programu' (another higher-education programme), so a software-engineering BSc is not excluded, and the extra CV/transcript requirement shows external applicants are anticipated. But Round 2 tests knowledge at the level of FAMU's own BA graduates, and the two-finished-AV-works portfolio is the real filter. Note one small positive: an ELECTRONIC instrument is explicitly accepted for the musicality demonstration.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Verified from the official 2026/27 specific-conditions PDF: application open 1 June – 13 August 2026; last date to send the application 13 August 2026; last date to submit the mandatory works 1 September 2026; Round 1 (without candidates present) 14 September 2026; Round 2 (in person) 17 September 2026; enrolment 24 September 2026 at Smetanovo nábřeží 2, Prague. For a September 2027 start expect an analogous June–September 2027 window — unusually late, which gives him an extra preparation year.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. 1 June (2026 cycle opened 1 June 2026 via prihlaska.amu.cz). AMU application fee 990 CZK, card payment; the works upload folder is only unlocked after the application is closed and the fee paid.
programs.tuitionIntl: 0 CZK for study in Czech at a Czech public university — nationality is irrelevant under Czech law; only study in a foreign language is charged. The previously listed CZK 550,000/year figure for FAMU's English MFAs could NOT be reconfirmed (page 404) and should not be relied on; it is irrelevant anyway, since Sound Design has no English track.
programs.scholarship: No dedicated scholarship found for Tunisians. CORRECTION to the eligible-country list: the Czech Government Scholarships (Developing Countries) 2026/27 list is Bosnia & Herzegovina, Georgia, Ukraine, Belarus (democratic forces), Ethiopia, Nigeria, Rwanda, Zambia, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, Guatemala and Jordan — broader than previously recorded, but Tunisia is still NOT on it. The 2027/28 list is expected to be published around late July / early August 2026 with a late-September 2026 deadline, so it is worth re-checking within weeks. programs.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free if studying in Czech; living costs self-funded)
programs.stipend: Tuition waiver by law for Czech-taught study. No stipend identified. UNVERIFIED whether AMU internal scholarships reach non-EU first-year master's students.
programs.facilities: FAMU Department of Sound (Katedra zvukové tvorby), Smetanovo nábřeží 2, Prague 1 — mixing and post-production rooms integrated with the school's film production pipeline, with audio-recording teaching partly delivered by HAMU's Sound Studio. Dolby Atmos certification of FAMU rooms: UNVERIFIED. Alumni of the school include Miloš Forman, Věra Chytilová, Jiří Menzel, Emir Kusturica, Agnieszka Holland.
programs.fitNotes: Prestigious and genuinely hands-on, but it is a FILM sound school — nothing here trains him as a DJ or club/electronic producer. Three compounding obstacles, one worse than previously recorded: Czech at B2/C1; a portfolio of two FINISHED audiovisual works with his own sound design plus a theoretical paper, which he does not have; and a live musicality test (instrument, voice or live performance) plus pitch-memory and rhythmic dictation. Only 6 places. Realistic as a 2028+ target at the earliest, after building a film/game sound reel.
programs.verificationNotes: Programme confirmed to exist at master level. The department page (https://kzt.famu.cz/prijimaci-rizeni/) confirmed the two-round structure and the wording 'Přihlásit se může kdokoliv s vystudovaným bakalářským studiem'. programs.program: Zvuková tvorba a hudební režie — specializace Zvuková tvorba (Sound Design / recording engineering), navazující magisterské studium
programs.university: Akademie múzických umění v Praze — HAMU (Music and Dance Faculty)
programs.institutionType: Public conservatory / academy of music (music faculty of AMU)
programs.focus: Recording/Engineering; Music Production; Electronic Music/Live Electronics; Immersive Audio
programs.language: Czech. Confirmed against HAMU's own list of English-taught options (Composition, String Instruments, Jazz Music, Dance Pedagogy and Choreology) — Zvuková tvorba a hudební režie is NOT among them.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years; ECTS total UNVERIFIED — not published on the department or programme pages (standard Czech follow-up master = 120 ECTS).
programs.whatYouStudy: Confirmed on the programme page: artistic-technical work with sound at the level of autonomous sound creation — recording production for classical music and jazz, realisation of electroacoustic music, sound and music post-production, live sound reinforcement, concert recording, online streaming, film scoring sessions and theatre sound. Graduates are described as artist-technicians able to work independently and creatively with sound in professional settings.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree. A CURRENT AUDIOGRAM with an ENT (ORL) specialist's statement is a mandatory attachment — confirmed, and confirmed to be eliminating: a hearing disorder results in rejection BEFORE Round 1. Testing can be arranged at HAMU's own Sound Studio. The application must be submitted electronically with required attachments sent by post or delivered in person by the stated deadline. Czech-language study; Czech at B2/C1 needed in practice.
programs.portfolioSpec: 'Prezentace vlastních zvukových nahrávek' — presentation of the candidate's own sound recordings, presented and defended in Round 2. CONFIRMED that the department publishes NO number of works, no maximum duration and no file format on either the admissions page or the programme page. UNVERIFIED beyond 'presentation of own recordings'; the exact spec must be requested from the Katedra zvukové tvorby a hudební režie.
programs.auditionSpec: Yes — two IN-PERSON rounds in Prague, both confirmed. Round 1 (electronic/aural test): 'Sluchový test zaměřený na základní analýzu zvukového signálu a stereofonního obrazu' (hearing test on basic analysis of the sound signal and the stereophonic image), plus melodic and rhythmic pattern work and detection of sound faults, plus a written knowledge test in acoustics, electronics and sound equipment. HARD GATE: minimum 20 of 25 points, below which the admission process ends. Round 2 (talent examination): practical mix of speech + music + sound effects on an ANALOGUE console (~2 min); mix of electronic music for artistic effect on a DIGITAL console (max ~2 min); an instrument proficiency test (piano preferred); presentation of own recordings; and 'ústní pohovor s důrazem na vizi vlastního profesního rozvoje' (oral interview stressing the candidate's vision of his own professional development). Final admission requires 20+ points and falling within the quota.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, conditionally — quote CONFIRMED verbatim on the programme page: 'Studenti přicházející z jiných bakalářských oborů, splní-li minimální technicko-umělecké požadavky přijímacího řízení do magisterského studia' (students coming from other bachelor's fields, provided they meet the minimum technical-artistic requirements of the master's admission procedure). The diploma is therefore not the barrier; the audiogram, the 20/25 aural/acoustics gate and the console and piano tests are.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. CORRECTION — this was previously recorded as UNVERIFIED but is now confirmed at faculty level for 2026/27: applications 15 March – 15 April 2026; entrance examinations 8–19 June 2026 (individual departments fine-tune dates by candidate numbers, changes reserved). For a September 2027 start expect roughly 15 March – 15 April 2027 with exams in June 2027.

programs.tuitionIntl: 0 CZK for Czech-taught study at a Czech public university, any nationality. Confirmed by the faculty's separation of Czech-taught from fee-paying foreign-language programmes, none of which is this one.
programs.scholarship: None found specific to Tunisians. Czech Government Scholarships (Developing Countries) 2026/27 covered Bosnia & Herzegovina, Georgia, Ukraine, Belarus (democratic forces), Ethiopia, Nigeria, Rwanda, Zambia, Cambodia, Sri Lanka, Guatemala and Jordan — Tunisia excluded; 2027/28 list due around late July/early August 2026. AMU internal accommodation/social/merit scholarships exist; non-EU eligibility UNVERIFIED.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free in Czech; living costs self-funded)
programs.facilities: HAMU's own Zvukové studio (Sound Studio), Malostranské náměstí 258/13, Prague 1 — analogue and digital mixing consoles (both are used in the entrance exam itself, which confirms they exist), recording studio for classical and jazz sessions, and the facility that also delivers audio-recording teaching to FAMU. Audiograms for applicants can be arranged there. Department runs bachelor, master and doctoral levels.
programs.fitNotes: The closest thing in Prague to a Tonmeister/recording-engineering master, and its electroacoustic and post-production strands do touch electronic music. But the entrance exam is brutal for a self-taught producer: a medical audiogram that can eliminate him before Round 1, an aural and acoustics test with a 20/25 pass bar, a live analogue-console mix, a digital-console electronic-music mix and a piano test. Czech is required. Not realistic for September 2027 without a year of Czech plus serious classical-recording, acoustics and keyboard preparation. The one genuinely encouraging element is the confirmed written openness to applicants from other bachelor fields.
programs.verificationNotes: Programme confirmed at master level in Prague, Czech-taught. Department admissions page confirmed the audiogram requirement (including that a hearing disorder ends the process before Round 1), the full two-round exam content, the 990 CZK fee and the 20/25 and 20-point thresholds. The programme page (…/studijni-programy/…zvukova-tvorba-162/) supplied the verbatim quote confirming that graduates of other bachelor fields may enrol. Faculty admissions page CORRECTED the previously-UNVERIFIED deadline to 15 March – 15 April 2026 with exams 8–19 June 2026, and confirmed the programme is not among HAMU's English-taught offer. Still UNVERIFIED: total ECTS, the exact portfolio specification (number/duration/format of recordings), and AMU internal scholarship eligibility for non-EU students.

programs.program: Zvuková tvorba a hudební režie — specializace Hudební režie (Music Direction / classical record production), navazující magisterské studium
programs.university: Akademie múzických umění v Praze — HAMU
programs.institutionType: Public academy of music
programs.focus: Recording/Engineering; Music Production (classical record production)
programs.language: Czech. Not among HAMU's English-taught programmes.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years; ECTS UNVERIFIED (not published on the programme page).
programs.whatYouStudy: Confirmed on the programme page: training an 'umělecky rozvinutý, muzikálně erudovaný' (artistically developed, musically erudite) music producer specialising in serious/classical music across all stylistic periods and genres. Content covers critical analysis of sound recordings, leading and directing recording sessions with soloists and complex ensembles, post-production (editing and mixing), and collaboration with performing musicians and the recording team. Graduates independently manage recording projects end-to-end.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree plus very high musical literacy — score reading, transposition, orchestration knowledge, aural dictation and piano are all examined. Audiogram with ENT statement required, as for the sister specialisation. Czech-language study.
programs.portfolioSpec: Presentation of the candidate's own sound recordings in Round 2. CONFIRMED that the exact number, duration and format are NOT published — UNVERIFIED; request from the department.
programs.auditionSpec: Yes — IN-PERSON, two rounds, both confirmed. Round 1 (written/practical test) has a practical part — ear-training dictation, listening comprehension of reproduced music and critical judgement of recordings, including 'analýza harmonických intervalů a souzvuků' (analysis of harmonic intervals and chords) and identification of musical styles and recording characteristics — and a theoretical part covering score orientation, instrumental transpositions and 'přepis partitury do obvyklých klíčů' (transcription of a score into the usual clefs), plus a piano assessment consisting of a prepared piece and sight-reading from a vocal score excerpt. Minimum 20 points to advance. Round 2: practical music direction in the sound studio, presentation of own sound recordings, and an oral interview on the vision of artistic development in music direction.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: No in practice — CONFIRMED. There is no formal bar on the prior degree stated, but Round 1 examines harmonic-interval analysis, score transposition into standard clefs, orchestration, aural dictation and prepared-plus-sight-read piano. A software-engineering BSc holder with no conservatory training cannot clear that. Treat as effectively closed.

programs.fitNotes: Listed for completeness as the region's classical record-production master. programs.program: Zvukový design a multimediální technologie (Sound Design and Multimedia Technologies) — navazující magisterské studium
programs.university: Masarykova univerzita (Masaryk University), Faculty of Arts — Department of Musicology, jointly delivered with FEKT VUT Brno
programs.institutionType: Public university (Faculty of Arts), taught jointly with the Brno University of Technology electrical-engineering faculty and industry practitioners
programs.focus: Sound Design; Music Production; Recording/Engineering; Immersive Audio
programs.language: Czech — confirmed on the official programme page.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years, confirmed. Offered in BOTH prezenční (full-time) and kombinovaná (part-time/blended) form — confirmed. Total ECTS is not stated on the programme page; 120 ECTS is the Czech standard for a two-year follow-up master but is here an inference, not a quoted figure.
programs.whatYouStudy: Four strands, matching the four components of the oral entrance exam: (1) technical foundations of sound creation — mathematics, physics, acoustics, studio technology; (2) production foundations / sound design proper; (3) sound production and programming — recording-studio work, audio software, autonomous sound production in the digital environment, live music production sound; (4) theory, aesthetics and history of sound creation. Practical skills training runs across all four semesters and taught by practitioners alongside MUNI musicologists and BUT engineers. A mandatory external internship is part of the degree (stated in the programme description; its credit weight is UNVERIFIED).
programs.entryRequirements: Any bachelor's degree. Quote CONFIRMED on the official page: the programme is intended for 'absolventům bakalářského studia – bez omezení' (bachelor's graduates — without restriction). NEWLY FOUND: graduates of certain specified related bachelor's/master's programmes are EXEMPT from the professional/technical part of the entrance exam — a Tunisian software-engineering BSc will not qualify for that exemption, so he must sit the full oral exam. Czech-language study, so Czech at B2/C1 is the practical requirement.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED — no conventional portfolio of finished works is demanded. The second exam component is a CREATIVE PROJECT PROPOSAL of maximum 2 pages setting out motivation and the intended creative/specialisation direction. IMPORTANT NEWLY-CONFIRMED DETAIL: the project must be uploaded to the e-application by 1 JUNE — i.e. a month AFTER the 30 April application deadline, a separate second deadline that is easy to miss.
programs.auditionSpec: No live artistic audition. On-site ORAL entrance examination in Brno in two components: (a) professional and artistic competence — oral examination on the technical foundations of sound creation, production prerequisites, sound production and programming, and the theory/aesthetics/history of sound work, max 40 points; (b) the creative project and study motivation, max 60 points. Pass mark 50 of 100. Confirmed. Faculty of Arts entrance exams for autumn entry ran 1–30 June in the 2026 cycle.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly, and this remains the standout finding of the slice. Official wording: 'Program je určen absolventům bakalářského studia – bez omezení' ('the programme is intended for bachelor's graduates — without restriction'). This is the only programme in the Czech/Slovak/Hungarian slice that states openness to any bachelor field in writing, so a software-engineering BSc is formally unproblematic. Caveat now confirmed: no exam exemption for him, so he sits the full oral technical/theoretical examination.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Confirmed for the 2026 cycle: applications 1 January – 30 April 2026 for autumn-semester entry; creative project uploaded by 1 June 2026; Faculty of Arts entrance exams 1–30 June 2026; remote enrolment 20–22 July 2026. But this cuts both ways: a Tunisian SOFTWARE-engineering BSc must be checked against the required electronics and signal-processing coursework, and he would sit an entrance exam in analogue low-frequency technology, electroacoustics and acoustics — material a pure software curriculum does not usually cover. Confirm eligibility and exam scope with FEKT before committing.

programs.program: Master of Music in Music Production, Technology, and Innovation (MPTI)

programs.focus: Music Production; Electronic Music; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering (incl. Dolby Atmos); Interactive/Immersive Audio; DJing
programs.durationEcts: 1 year / 3 consecutive semesters (fall, spring, summer). CONFIRMED on the official cost page: 32–33 US credits minimum, 37–38 maximum with the optional internship, at USD 1,615 per credit. ECTS equivalence is NOT published — remains UNVERIFIED.
programs.language: English (the campus operates in English; the page does not state it explicitly, but the whole admissions apparatus — TOEFL/IELTS thresholds, English-language exemption rule — confirms it in practice)
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED on the official programme page. Four modules: (1) CORE — six required courses in audio engineering, studio production, music video, interactive media, electronic production and career preparation; (2) ELECTIVE — minimum 4 credits from named tracks: DJing ("DJing and Turntablism", "Controller-Enhanced Performance"), Mixing/Audio Engineering (stereo mixing, Dolby Atmos, mastering, live sound), Sound Design ("Professional and Creative Music Sound Design", analog synthesis), Video Production, Interactive Media (Max/MSP, physical computing, multimedia installation); (3) FINAL PROJECT — three seminars (Past, Present, Future) plus a culminating experience proposal, development and faculty-committee defence, described as "a technology-aided composition, a large-scale recording project, and/or live performances" involving interactivity, multi-channel audio or custom digital instruments; (4) optional ensembles that do not count toward the degree. Software: Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools, Adobe Premiere.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree required. English (non-native speakers), CONFIRMED on the How to Apply page — note MPTI sits in the HIGHER band, not the Contemporary Performance band: Duolingo 130, TOEFL iBT 100 (for exams before 21 Jan 2026) or the new TOEFL scale score of 5 (exams from 21 Jan 2026), IELTS Academic 7.5, Cambridge CAE or higher. Also: statement of purpose 400–500 words; résumé; ONE letter of recommendation from a professional you have worked with (not a peer); course-by-course credential evaluation with GPA conversion from an approved agency (SpanTran or ECE) since his degree is from outside the US/Canada; USD 150 non-refundable application fee.
programs.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED AND EXPANDED — the official How to Apply page specifies MORE than three tracks. MPTI requires: (a) THREE recorded musical projects, with a description of your role in each, AND (b) a 3-MINUTE VIDEO describing potential thesis projects. Everything must be "organized in one PDF document with all links properly embedded and sections clearly labeled." The general Berklee guidance adds: "choose three exceptional performances, recordings, or compositions that demonstrate your musical skills at their best." The thesis video is a material extra requirement that was missing from the prior record.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition for MPTI. The entrance-requirements page keeps "Auditions" and "Interviews" as separate sections and no audition is specified under MPTI; auditions attach to the Contemporary Performance Production concentration. Shortlisted applicants may be interviewed.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, conditionally — wording CONFIRMED verbatim on the official entrance-requirements page: applicants should hold "a bachelor's degree in music while demonstrating technological proficiency," but "Bachelor's degrees in other disciplines will be considered, provided the student demonstrates a high degree of musicianship." A software-engineering BSc is admissible; the phrase "high degree of musicianship" means the three tracks plus the thesis video have to carry the entire case.
programs.tuitionIntl: CONFIRMED on the official 2026/27 graduate cost page: tuition USD 50,430 + comprehensive fee USD 1,600 = USD 52,030 direct cost for the one-year degree, plus USD 150 application fee, a USD 2,500 non-refundable tuition deposit (credited to the first payment), a required software bundle of USD 200–850, and student health insurance at variable cost. Indirect estimates published by Berklee: housing USD 10,000–12,000, laptop USD 3,000, books USD 300–800, transport USD 300–600, personal USD 1,000. Realistic all-in one-year figure: roughly USD 67,000–70,000. By far the most expensive option in this slice.
programs.scholarship: CORRECTED. The €125,000 figure previously recorded is NOT a general international pot — it belongs to the CACSA / Palau de les Arts "Valencian Students Scholarships Program", restricted to students of the Valencian Community, deadline 1 April. He is not eligible for it. Berklee separately states it offers over USD 1.5 million in merit- and need-based scholarships to graduate students on the Valencia campus. Awards actually open to him, confirmed on the graduate scholarships page: BERKLEE GENERAL SCHOLARSHIP — "all master's degree applicants" eligible, varying amounts, multiple awards (this is his main route); BERKLEE VALENCIA DIVERSITY SCHOLARSHIP — up to 50% of tuition, for demonstrated leadership supporting underrepresented communities; BERKLEE GLOBAL PARTNERS SCHOLARSHIP — USD 18,000, but only for students/alumni/faculty of a Berklee Global Partners school, which he is not. Also CORRECTED: the Berklee Outstanding Women Scholarship (up to 70% of tuition) is real and does cover MPTI, but it is a women's award and irrelevant to him — the prior record cited it as his headline option. The Berklee Groove Scholarship (up to 90%) is restricted to Contemporary Performance instrumentalists. No Tunisia or North Africa award exists.
programs.stipend: Tuition discount only — no stipend, no housing, no travel. Scholarship deadlines CONFIRMED and are LATER than the application deadlines: 15 November (Early Action), 1 February (Regular Action), 10 March (Extended Action).
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — Berklee does not publish a portal opening date. The deadline structure is a fixed annual calendar, so the portal is normally open from late summer; for a September 2027 start expect it to open around August–September 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date (the published calendar carries no academic year, so the dates below are the standing annual pattern, not confirmed 2027 dates). CONFIRMED on the official deadlines page: Early Action — apply 1 Nov, scholarship 15 Nov, decisions 15 Dec; Regular Action — apply 15 Jan, scholarship 1 Feb, decisions 15 Mar; Extended Action — apply 10 Mar, scholarship 10 Mar, decisions 20 Apr. Mapped to a September 2027 intake that is 1 Nov 2026 / 15 Jan 2027 / 10 Mar 2027. programs.facilities: CONFIRMED in general terms on the programme page: "state-of-the-art recording studios, equipment, and facilities" plus industry-standard software (Ableton Live, Max, Pro Tools, Adobe Premiere) and hardware, on the Palau de les Arts campus. Dedicated DJ-lab claims are implied by the DJing/Turntablism and Controller-Enhanced Performance courses but the specific room inventory is UNVERIFIED. programs.program: ReSound — Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts in Sound Design for Media Arts
programs.university: Consortium: IADT Dún Laoghaire (Dublin, coordinating school), Universidade Lusófona (Lisbon), Lithuanian Academy of Music and Theatre (Vilnius)
programs.city: Dublin (semester 1) → Lisbon (semester 2) → Vilnius (semester 3) → thesis placement (semester 4, located by research need)
programs.degree: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master of Arts (EMJM), NFQ Level 9, 120 ECTS
programs.institutionType: Joint consortium of a state art-and-technology institute, a private university and a state music academy, all within the FilmEU European University alliance
programs.focus: Sound Design; Film/Screen Sound; Sonic Arts (practice-based); Game/Interactive Audio; Sound Production and Technologies
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, with compulsory mobility across three countries
programs.language: English (confirmed — all documents must be submitted in English and English-language certification is required of non-native speakers)
programs.whatYouStudy: Mobility path CONFIRMED on the IADT course page: Semester 1 at IADT Dún Laoghaire, Dublin — screen and media-arts sound; Semester 2 at Universidade Lusófona, Lisbon — sound production and technologies, sharing the Pro Tools / Max-MSP / Arduino infrastructure of Lusófona's own Produção e Tecnologias do Som master; Semester 3 at LMTA Vilnius — music and theatre technology; Semester 4 a thesis/practice placement located according to your research needs and supervisor fit. The consortium markets it as studying "across Northern, Western, and Southern Europe." A semester-by-semester module list with ECTS is NOT published on either the consortium site or the IADT page — request the current study plan from the consortium before applying.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED. A bachelor's degree in "sound, music, film, media studies, computational science or related disciplines" (the fuller IADT wording); applicants from other fields "may be considered if they demonstrate relevant prior experience in areas such as sound, music, film, or media studies." English certification dated within TWO YEARS of application: IELTS 6.0 with no component below 6.0, TOEFL iBT 79, Duolingo 110, Cambridge B2, or LanguageCert ESOL — waived if you hold a full EQF Level 4+ qualification of at least one academic year taught in English. Top-scoring applicants proceed to an online interview on a date set by the selection committee.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED and precise. No more than THREE examples of previous sound or media work, each with a short reflective paragraph explaining your role. Submit either as a SINGLE hyperlink to a portfolio website or as ONE compiled audio or video file. The selection team states it can realistically review 10–15 minutes of material per application, so keep the total inside that. All documents in English.
programs.auditionSpec: None. Online interview only, for shortlisted (top-scoring) applicants, at a date set by the selection committee.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — the most favourable wording in the entire slice for his background. IADT's published entry requirement names "computational science" as an accepted bachelor field, listed alongside sound, music, film and media studies. A software-engineering BSc is squarely inside the named intake, not an exception to it. The portfolio then has to show he can actually work with sound.
programs.tuitionIntl: CONFIRMED: €15,000 total for the two years, paid as €7,500 before semester 1 and €7,500 before semester 3, for self-funded students. Erasmus Mundus scholarship holders pay NOTHING — the fee is waived in full.
programs.scholarship: Erasmus Mundus Joint Master scholarship, open to non-EU nationals including Tunisians and awarded on merit through the same single application. CONFIRMED: maximum 24 places on the programme per intake, with "a significant percentage" of successful candidates receiving the scholarship. No separate scholarship application is needed.
programs.stipend: CONFIRMED in outline on the consortium site: full tuition waiver plus €1,400 per month, described as covering travel, visa and living costs. The consortium estimates actual living expenses at €600–1,000/month across the three cities, so the allowance leaves real headroom. The prior record's additional itemisation (a separate €2,000–3,000/year travel allowance, €1,000 installation allowance, health insurance) reflects standard EMJM contribution categories but was NOT itemised separately on the pages read — treat the €1,400/month plus tuition waiver as the confirmed floor and reconfirm the breakdown against the 2027 call, since EMJM rates are fixed per call.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The 2026 intake opened 20 October 2025. The site currently states only "Applications for ReSound 2026 have closed" and gives no 2027 information. Expect the next call to open around mid-to-late October 2026 — start checking resound-ma.eu weekly from early October 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The 2026 intake closed 27 January 2026 (extended from an original 20 January). Nothing is published for 2027. For a September 2027 start expect a deadline in the second half of January 2027. This is the single most important date in the whole slice and the one to build the year around. Caveat worth knowing: the 2026 round was advertised as the SECOND edition of this EMJM, and EMJM projects are funded for a fixed number of intakes — confirm with the consortium that a 2027 intake with scholarships is actually running before betting the plan on it.
programs.facilities: FilmEU European University alliance infrastructure across the three schools. IADT is one of Ireland's principal screen-media institutes; LMTA is Lithuania's national music and theatre academy; Lusófona operates the Lisbon sound labs on a Pro Tools / Max-MSP / Arduino toolchain. Specific studio inventory, named staff and alumni are UNVERIFIED — nothing itemised on the pages read.
programs.fitNotes: By a wide margin the best funding-to-fit ratio available to a Tunisian applicant in this slice, and the only genuinely fully funded option: no tuition, €1,400/month, taught in English at an IELTS 6.0 bar he can realistically hit (versus Berklee's 7.5), assessed on a three-piece portfolio rather than an audition, and it names computational science as an accepted feeder degree. Two honest caveats. First, competition — a maximum of 24 places worldwide, so this cannot be his only application. Second, and more important for his stated goal, the subject is sound design for MEDIA ARTS: screen sound, sonic arts, theatre and game audio. It will make him an excellent sound designer with strong production technique and a European network, but it will not on its own train him as a club/dance-music producer or DJ the way Berklee's elective tracks would. Apply for it as the funded anchor; treat the DJ/producer craft as something he builds alongside it.
programs.verificationNotes: CONFIRMED on resound-ma.eu/application: closure of the 2026 intake, entry requirements, the full English-language score list and the two-year currency rule, the exact portfolio spec (max 3 examples, reflective paragraphs, single link or one compiled file, 10–15 minutes reviewable), the online interview for top-scoring applicants, maximum 24 places, €15,000 total fee paid in two €7,500 instalments, the Erasmus Mundus tuition waiver plus €1,400/month, and the €600–1,000/month living estimate. programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED — no portfolio specification is published on any UC course page. programs.program: Mestrado em Produção e Tecnologias do Som (Master in Sound Production and Technologies)

programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, in-person (presencial), pós-laboral — evening classes starting at 18:00 on weekdays.
programs.language: Portuguese (all unit titles, course page and application materials are Portuguese; no English-taught route is offered). Documents in Spanish, French or English are accepted at application stage, but the teaching is not.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED in outline. Four semesters on a common core. Year 1 builds foundations in acoustics, sound capture, synthesis and sonic composition, mixing and studio practice, signal processing, virtual auditory environments and the relationship between sound and image. Year 2 covers research methodology and a dissertation/thesis project (30 ECTS). Principal software taught: Avid Pro Tools, Max/MSP and Arduino. Published career outcomes: sound director, audio technician, music producer, recording and mastering engineer, sound designer across the creative industries. A unit-by-unit plan with ECTS was not extractable from the course page — request it.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED. Holders of a licenciatura or legal equivalent; holders of a foreign first-cycle degree from a Bologna-process country; holders of a recognised equivalent foreign degree; or candidates whose "currículo escolar, científico ou profissional" is recognised by the institution as demonstrating capacity for master's study. Selection weighting published on the course page: 25% prior qualification + 75% interview and portfolio; for candidates without a degree, 100% interview. For international applicants the university additionally requires (confirmed on its international admissions page): passport copy; diploma or completion certificate; academic transcript; CV (DeGóis, FCT-SIG or similar format); a LETTER OF MOTIVATION; and certificates of any other relevant higher-education coursework. Diplomas must be authenticated by the Portuguese Consulate in Tunisia or apostilled under the Hague Convention, and translated by a sworn translator if not in Portuguese, Spanish, French or English — his French-language documents are acceptable without translation, which saves time and money.
programs.portfolioSpec: Portfolio required and decisive — it and the interview together carry 75% of the admission score. The number of works, duration and format are NOT published. A further inconsistency to resolve: the university's international-applicant document list names a portfolio requirement only for Cinema Studies and Animation Arts, not for this master, while the course page weights a portfolio at 75%. Request the current regulamento/edital de candidatura in writing and get the portfolio scope confirmed by email before building it.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. An admission interview is required and is heavily weighted (part of the 75% block, and 100% of the score for candidates admitted on professional CV rather than a degree). Held in Portuguese in all likelihood — confirm.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, but less explicitly than the other Portuguese options. The course page describes the target intake as "licenciados nas áreas da musicologia e tecnologias do som, realização e produção audiovisual" plus professionals with substantial audiovisual and media-production experience — engineering and computer science are NOT named. The general admission rule does accept any licenciatura, so a software-engineering BSc is formally admissible, but he would enter outside the stated target group and the 75%-weighted portfolio and interview would have to do all the work.
programs.tuitionIntl: PARTIALLY CONFIRMED and internally inconsistent as published (2025/26 figures on the course page): a monthly propina of €365.40 for a 30-ECTS enrolment, a stated rate of €12.18 per ECTS, and a €450 fee. €365.40 is exactly 30 × €12.18, which reads as a monthly charge scaled to credits enrolled — implying roughly €7,300 over two years at 30 ECTS/semester across 10 monthly instalments a year, but potentially double that if the monthly amount scales to a 60-ECTS annual load. Treat the total as UNVERIFIED and insist on a written payment plan (plano de pagamentos) before committing. No separate international rate was published.
programs.scholarship: None found for this standalone master; the university's international admissions page carries no tuition or scholarship information at all and directs enquiries to info.cul@ulusofona.pt. Important strategic note: Lusófona is the LISBON PARTNER in the fully funded ReSound Erasmus Mundus master listed separately in this slice — same building, same Pro Tools / Max-MSP / Arduino infrastructure, but with a full scholarship and English-language teaching. That is the route to try first.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED. Lusófona has restructured its application calendar by application type and no dated master's calendar was retrievable (the calendar page renders its dates behind interactive filters). The previously recorded 18 July opening could not be confirmed on any official page.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date, and now UNVERIFIED. The previously recorded 2026/27 window of 18 July – 1 September 2026 could NOT be confirmed against any official Lusófona page in this check. What is confirmed is that Lusófona runs programme-specific calendars rather than one university-wide window — for comparison, its DIGISOC European master ran applications 22 Dec 2025 – 27 Feb 2026 with a non-EU document deadline of 15 May 2026. For a September 2027 start, ask the university directly for the Produção e Tecnologias do Som calendar and, critically, for the NON-EU DOCUMENT DEADLINE, which at Lusófona falls months before the EU one and is the date that actually binds him.
programs.facilities: Recording studios and digital labs on the Lisbon campus with a Pro Tools / Max-MSP / Arduino toolchain; free parking for postgraduate students attending evening sessions. Shares infrastructure with the ReSound EMJM consortium and the FilmEU alliance. Course coordinator: Prof. Dr. João Marques Carrilho. Studio inventory beyond the software toolchain is UNVERIFIED.
programs.fitNotes: Genuinely a production-and-engineering master rather than a theory course — recording, mastering, mixing and studio practice are the substance, and a portfolio worth 75% of the decision suits an applicant whose evidence is tracks rather than transcripts. The evening timetable would leave his days free. But the obstacles are real and stack up: teaching is entirely in Portuguese, which he does not have; there is no visible funding of any kind; the tuition figures published are contradictory; his degree field is outside the stated target intake; and the application calendar could not even be verified. The sensible use of this programme is as a labelled self-pay fallback in the same city and the same building as ReSound — apply for the Erasmus Mundus scholarship first and keep this in reserve.
