A CPLP reduction exists but Tunisia is not a CPLP country and does not benefit. 2026/27 values are fixed by the P.PORTO General Council and made public by 31 July. Expect a public-polytechnic figure well below the private options, but obtain it in writing.
programs.scholarship: None found. No scholarship scheme for non-EU master's students surfaced on ESMAE or P.PORTO pages read.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. CONFIRMED: for 2026/27, applications to Artes e Tecnologias do Som opened 5 January 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. CONFIRMED on the official ESMAE 2026/27 admissions notice: Artes e Tecnologias do Som had an EXTENDED phase-1 window of 5 January – 11 April 2026, with tests/interviews on 7–8 May 2026. (The music performance and composition masters had a shorter window, 5–23 January, with tests 2–11 February — Sound Arts deliberately gets the longer runway.) A second phase also runs in some years for courses with places left; in 2024/25 the second phase ran 5–26 August with 7 remaining places in this specific master, which indicates a small cohort and that late entry is sometimes possible. For a September 2027 start expect an equivalent January–April 2027 window with interviews in early May 2027.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED in detail. ESMAE is the principal public performing-arts conservatory in northern Portugal, with concert halls and studio infrastructure in central Porto, and the optional catalogue (Áudio 3D, Performance e Tecnologia, Eletroacústica Aplicada) implies spatial-audio and live-electronics rooms. No facility inventory is published on the pages read. Confirm studio access directly — for a production-focused candidate this is decisive.
programs.fitNotes: Artistically the most serious sound-arts master in northern Portugal, cheap by European standards, and it does contain a real Produção Musical option plus creative coding inside an otherwise art-led curriculum. But it is the weakest fit in the slice for what he actually wants. The framing is authorial, research-led sound art aimed at musicians and sonic artists, not commercial music production; admission requires a defensible project or dissertation proposal on top of the portfolio; nothing confirms that a pure software-engineering BSc is eligible; teaching is almost certainly Portuguese; tuition, funding, ECTS and language are all unpublished; and there is a fixed interview/test date in Porto whose remote feasibility is unknown. Too many unresolved blockers to treat as a target. If it interests him, the low-cost first step is a short email to coordinator Bruno Pereira asking two questions: is a computer-science/engineering licenciatura eligible, and can the interview be done online from abroad.
programs.verificationNotes: CONFIRMED on esmae.ipp.pt/cursos/mestrados/mestrado-artes-tecnologias-som: programme name, master's degree, diurno regime, the mandatory-core-plus-options structure, the full optional catalogue including Produção Musical and Programação Criativa, the target audience of musicians and sonic artists developing authorial work, CNAEF 213, Despacho n.º 10666/2018, and the coordinator's name. CONFIRMED on the /acesso sub-page: the interdisciplinary target-audience wording naming acoustics; the three mandatory submissions (portfolio, project/dissertation proposal, updated CV); jury evaluation followed by interview; and the pointer to the edital on the P.PORTO DOMUS portal. CONFIRMED on the official 2026/27 admissions notice: application window 5 January – 11 April 2026 and tests/interviews 7–8 May 2026 for this specific course, distinct from the shorter music-programme window. Also confirmed from the archived second-phase notice: a second August phase exists and this master had only 7 remaining places in the 2024/25 second phase. NOT CONFIRMED: total ECTS and duration (plano-de-estudos and estrutura-curricular URLs both 404); language of instruction; formal list of eligible bachelor degrees; exact portfolio specification; total number of places; whether interviews can be held remotely; tuition for national or international students (P.PORTO publishes amounts only inside deliberation PDFs and per-school international values); and any scholarship. The 2025/26 edital PDF is published at esmae.ipp.pt/download-docs/edital_mestrados_2025-2026 but is not machine-readable through this tooling — it should be downloaded and read manually, as it contains the eligibility rule and portfolio spec that decide whether this programme is open to him at all.

programs.program: Multimediální tvorba — navazující magisterské studium (Multimedia Creation, follow-up master)
programs.university: Janáčkova akademie múzických umění v Brně (JAMU), Hudební fakulta — Katedra kompozice a multimediální tvorby
programs.institutionType: Public academy of performing arts (music faculty)
programs.focus: Sonic Arts; Electronic Music/Live Electronics; Sound Design (multimedia/installation-led)
programs.language: Czech only ("Jazyk výuky: Česky"). No English track found.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years (BcA. 4 + MgA. 2). ECTS not published on the programme or admissions pages — UNVERIFIED (Czech follow-up master's standard is 120).
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED on the official page: works using "multiple, meaningfully and irreplaceably complementary media within a single work" — performance, interactive installation, video art, opera, experimental documentary, computer games. Contemporary composition, electronic music, multimedia design and collaborative creative work, using electroacoustic studios, multichannel audio, modular synthesis and field-recording gear. Teaching shared across JAMU's Music and Theatre faculties, BUT's Faculty of Fine Arts and Masaryk University. Final state exam (official): public presentation and defence of the final artistic work plus written documentation, a diploma thesis of at least 40 pages, and exams in Multimedia Composition and Contemporary Trends and Theory of Composition.
programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED AND NOW VERIFIED — this is stricter than previously recorded. Official master's admission page states verbatim: "Podmínkou přijetí je ukončené vysokoškolské vzdělání, dosažené alespoň v bakalářském stupni studia oboru Multimediální tvorba nebo příbuzného uměleckého oboru" (admission conditional on a completed bachelor's in Multimedia Creation OR A RELATED ARTISTIC FIELD). Plus, from the 2026/27 decree, a HARD Czech-language barrier: "cizí státní příslušníci (s výjimkou uchazečů ze Slovenské republiky), musí předložit vysvědčení o vykonání požadované zkoušky z českého jazyka dle stanovených podmínek (B1 SERR)" — foreign nationals must produce a Czech B1 CEFR certificate (in the 2026/27 cycle by 14 June 2026), plus officially translated bachelor documents and, for a foreign diploma, a nostrification decision. JAMU runs its own Czech verification exam (3,000 CZK) focused on music/culture vocabulary; accredited B1 CEFR certificates are also accepted. Mandatory attachments: proof of bachelor completion, structured CV.
programs.portfolioSpec: PARTIALLY CORRECTED. At MASTER level the official page requires only "portfolio dosavadních uměleckých a jiných odborných aktivit" (portfolio of previous artistic and other professional activities) with NO published number, duration or format. IMPORTANT: the widely-quoted "minimum 20 / maximum 40 items" spec is the BACHELOR-level requirement (bachelor page: "Předložení portfolia domácích prací v celkovém počtu minimálně 20 nebo maximálně 40 položek", worth 10%) — do not apply it to the MgA. The master's application must ALSO include, in writing: a concept for the master's project, and a proposed diploma-thesis topic with basic theses.
programs.auditionSpec: On-site, single-round, in Brno. Talent exam = 90% of the score, conducted as an oral interview (ústní pohovor) assessing prior study results and the bachelor graduation project, the portfolio, the written master's project concept, the written thesis-topic proposal, knowledge of current developments in the field, and language readiness. Foreign-language written test = 10%, a lexico-grammatical test at B2+ CEFR including specialist music terminology. CRUCIAL EXTRA: "V případě uchazeče, který absolvoval bakalářské studium v jiném (byť příbuzném) oboru, se úroveň jeho znalostí prověří praktickou zkouškou" — an applicant from a different field sits an additional practical exam in three parts: (a) a thematic task, a multimedia-work project on a set theme; (b) a practical task on the visual component; (c) a free task in any media with a compulsory musical component. 2026/27 exam date was 16 June 2026 (KKMT). Only 2 places.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check, leaning NO. The published condition is a bachelor "in Multimedia Creation or a related ARTISTIC field" — a software-engineering BSc is not an artistic field, so acceptance is at the committee's discretion. There IS an explicit route: applicants from another field are tested by the three-part practical exam above. Combined with the Czech B1 certificate requirement, this is a genuine barrier, not a formality. The department's talent advisory service (booking address for Multimediální tvorba is fajnor@jamu.cz; department head doc. Dan Dlouhý, dlouhy@jamu.cz) is the correct first contact.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Verified 2026/27 decree: applications open January and close 10 May 2026; talent exam 16 June 2026; Czech B1 certificate due 14 June 2026; single round. For September 2027 entry expect roughly a 10 May 2027 deadline with a mid-June 2027 exam — not yet published as of July 2026.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. In the 2026/27 cycle the E-PŘIHLÁŠKA opened in January 2026 at is.jamu.cz. Expect January 2027 for the 2027/28 cycle.
programs.tuitionIntl: 0 CZK. Czech-taught study at a Czech public university is tuition-free for all nationalities. Application fee 990 CZK per specialisation (verified in the 2026/27 decree). JAMU's own Czech language verification exam costs 3,000 CZK. Nostrification of the foreign diploma may carry a separate fee.
programs.scholarship: None found for Tunisians. JAMU publishes no international entrance scholarship for this programme.
programs.stipend: None. Tuition waiver by default only. Admission does not create any entitlement to a place in a JAMU hall of residence (stated in the decree).
programs.facilities: VERIFIED on the department/programme pages: two electroacoustic music studios, a professional recording studio, a fully equipped theatre and chamber hall, interactive technologies, multichannel audio systems, a large stock of professional software and hardware, a MODULAR SYNTHESISER, and an equipped loan pool of microphones, field recorders, video cameras and sensors. Documented collaboration with the National Theatre Brno and the Institute of Sonology (The Hague). Department led by doc. Mgr. Ing. MgA. Dan Dlouhý, Ph.D.; staff include prof. Ivo Medek, doc. Jaroslav Šťastný, MgA. Jiří Suchánek.
programs.fitNotes: Superb kit for electronic music and genuinely experimental, but three verified obstacles now stack against him: a Czech B1 certificate is mandatory for foreign nationals with a hard deadline weeks before the exam; the entry condition names an artistic bachelor; and only 2 places exist. The added three-part practical exam for other-field applicants is a fair route but assumes visual and multimedia authorship, not DJ/production. Also note the direction is installation and sound art, not club releases.
programs.verificationNotes: Programme confirmed to exist at MgA level in Brno, Czech-taught, 2 years. Verified against four official sources: the programme database page; the master's admission-requirements page (https://hf.jamu.cz/studijni-obor/multimedialni-tvorba-3-prijimaci-rizeni/) for entry conditions and exam weights; the bachelor page (https://hf.jamu.cz/studijni-obor/multimedialni-tvorba-2-prijimaci-rizeni/) which is where the 20–40 item portfolio spec actually lives; and the official decree PDF "Vyhláška – magisterské navazující studium pro akademický rok 2026-2027" (https://is.jamu.cz/do/jamu/doc/5451/smer_pr_hf/Vyhlaska_nav.MgA.26-27_JVS.pdf) for the deadline, exam date, 990 CZK fee, 2 places and the Czech B1 requirement. CORRECTIONS MADE: (1) prior record said portfolio spec was entirely UNVERIFIED — the master's spec is in fact published, it simply carries no item count, and the 20–40 figure belongs to the bachelor; (2) prior record said acceptsNonMusic was 'not stated' — it IS stated, requiring a related artistic field, with a defined extra practical exam for other-field entrants; (3) prior record gave no Czech-language condition — a B1 CEFR certificate is mandatory and is the single biggest blocker; (4) deadline and exam dates now sourced. STILL UNVERIFIED: ECTS total; whether the Czech B1 requirement is ever waived.

programs.program: Kompozice — specializace Kompozice elektroakustické hudby (Electroacoustic Music Composition)
programs.university: Janáčkova akademie múzických umění v Brně (JAMU), Hudební fakulta — Katedra kompozice a multimediální tvorby
programs.degree: MgA. — five-year one-tier master (pětileté magisterské studium)
programs.institutionType: Public academy of performing arts
programs.focus: Electroacoustic Composition; Electronic Music/Live Electronics; Sound Design
programs.language: Czech only ("Jazyk výuky: Česky"). No English track.
programs.durationEcts: 5 years as a one-tier master ("Doba studia: 5 let"). Bachelor holders from other institutions may enter directly into year 4 after differential exams, making it effectively 2 years. ECTS UNVERIFIED.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED verbatim on the official page: compositional craft plus close collaboration with multimedia creators, conductors, choirmasters, opera directors and audio engineers, teaching students "moderně uvažovat o hudební tvorbě" (to think about music-making in a modern way). Practical work covers conversion of visual, haptic and other parameters into sound, realisation of graphic scores, microtonal tuning research, interactive electronic systems, multichannel reproduction and compositional use of field recordings. Students collaborate with the National Theatre Brno and internationally with the Institute of Sonology, The Hague, and may use their own recording studios.
programs.entryRequirements: Standard route is entry at year 1 from secondary school — the 2026/27 five-year decree lists a maturita (secondary leaving certificate) as a mandatory attachment, not a bachelor's degree. Separate route CONFIRMED verbatim on the programme page: "Pokud se o studium zajímají i absolventi bakalářských studijních programů z jiných škol, mohou se přihlásit k přijímacím zkouškám, absolvovat rozdílové zkoušky a po jejich úspěšném složení následně postoupit rovnou do čtvrtého ročníku JAMU" (bachelor graduates from other schools may sit the entrance exams, take differential exams, and on passing proceed straight to JAMU's fourth year). HARD BARRIER, verified in the decree: foreign nationals (Slovaks excepted) must submit a Czech B1 CEFR certificate — in the 2026/27 cycle by 22 January 2026 — plus officially translated school certificates. Structured CV required.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW VERIFIED AND MUCH MORE FAVOURABLE THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. Official requirements page states: "Predložit nahrávky několika odlišných skladeb, vytvořených za použití různých metod tvorby zvuku" — submit RECORDINGS of several different pieces created using various methods of sound creation. This part alone is 50% of the total score. No sheet music, no score submission, and no fixed number, duration or file format is published. The remaining weights are published: 30% for knowledge of different ways of creating electronic sound, work with a DAW, use of various music-making programs, or building open-source software or hardware instruments; 10% for the ability to play some electroacoustic instrument at least at a basic level; 10% for a written test of general cultural knowledge, plus an interview probing interest in the field.
programs.auditionSpec: On-site, single-round, in Brno. Components as weighted above (recordings 50%, electronic-sound/DAW knowledge 30%, basic electroacoustic instrument 10%, written general-knowledge test 10%, plus interview). The general page also notes candidates "budou prokazovat své znalosti hudebně teoretických disciplín a instrumentace" (will demonstrate knowledge of music-theory disciplines and instrumentation), which is not separately weighted. 2026/27 exam date 26 January 2026; scoring 0–25 points, minimum 20 to be proposed for admission; 2 places. Bachelor-holder entrants additionally sit rozdílové (differential) exams.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — no field restriction is published, and the exam content is unusually favourable. The programme page's wording covers "absolventi bakalářských studijních programů z jiných škol" (graduates of bachelor programmes from OTHER SCHOOLS), which is about the institution, not the field, and nothing bars a non-music bachelor. Crucially, 80% of the exam score rests on submitted recordings plus DAW and electronic-sound-creation knowledge — exactly a self-taught producer's strengths — with no classical harmony, counterpoint or score-reading test. The real blocker is Czech B1, not musical pedigree. Confirm the year-4 entry route and the differential-exam content with doc. Dan Dlouhý, dlouhy@jamu.cz.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Verified 2026/27 decree: application deadline 30 November 2025 (much earlier than the follow-up master's), entrance exam 26 January 2026, Czech B1 certificate due 22 January 2026, admissions board 13 February 2026. For September 2027 entry expect roughly 30 November 2026 with a late-January 2027 exam — meaning the application window may open only months from now. No substitute exam date is offered except on documented acute illness.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. E-PŘIHLÁŠKA at is.jamu.cz; the 2026/27 decree was issued 1 June 2025 for a 30 November 2025 close, so expect the 2027/28 decree around mid-2026 — check hf.jamu.cz/prijimaci-rizeni/vyhlasky-prijimaciho-rizeni/ now.
programs.tuitionIntl: 0 CZK. Czech-taught study at a Czech public university is free for all nationalities. Application fee 990 CZK per specialisation, non-refundable. JAMU Czech language verification exam 3,000 CZK.
programs.scholarship: None found for Tunisians.
programs.stipend: None. Tuition waiver only. The decree states accommodation in halls is not possible during the entrance exams and admission creates no entitlement to a hall place.
programs.facilities: VERIFIED verbatim: "dvě špičkově vybavená studia pro tvorbu elektroakustické hudby" (two top-equipped electroacoustic music studios), a fully equipped theatre, a chamber hall, interactive technologies, multichannel audio systems, a large stock of professional software and hardware, a professional recording studio, a MODULAR SYNTHESISER, and an equipment loan pool with microphones, field recorders, video cameras and sensors. Collaboration with the National Theatre Brno and the Institute of Sonology, The Hague.
programs.fitNotes: MAJOR REASSESSMENT: the entrance exam is by far the most producer-friendly in this entire slice — 50% recordings of your own varied work, 30% DAW and electronic-sound-creation knowledge, only 10% for basic playing of an electroacoustic instrument. There is no classical composition test, no fugue, no score reading. Someone self-taught who makes tracks and understands synthesis could actually compete here. What blocks it is Czech: a B1 certificate is mandatory, due in the 2026/27 cycle by 22 January, i.e. before the exam. Add a very early (end-November) deadline, only 2 places, a 5-year one-tier structure whose standard entry expects a maturita, and the need to pass differential exams to jump to year 4. If he were willing to commit hard to Czech, this would be the best craft match in the region; as things stand for September 2027 it is effectively blocked by language.
programs.verificationNotes: Programme confirmed to exist, MgA., 5 years, Czech, Brno. Verified against: the specialisation page (sourceUrl); the programme database page https://hf.jamu.cz/database/study/kompozice-elektroakusticke-hudby-285/ for duration, language, staff and facilities; the official entrance-requirements page https://hf.jamu.cz/studijni-obor/kompozice-elektroakusticke-hudby-2-prijimaci-rizeni/ for the exact 50/30/10/10 weighting; and the decree PDF "Vyhláška – pětileté magisterské studium pro akademický rok 2026-2027" (https://is.jamu.cz/do/jamu/doc/5451/smer_pr_hf/Vyhlaska_dl.mag.2026_27.pdf) for the 30 Nov 2025 deadline, 26 Jan 2026 exam, 990 CZK fee, 2 places, 0–25 point scale with a 20-point threshold, maturita requirement and the Czech B1 deadline of 22 Jan 2026. CORRECTIONS MADE: (1) prior record called the portfolio spec UNVERIFIED and guessed at 'compositions/recordings plus scores' — the real spec is published, is recordings-only, and carries an explicit 50% weight; (2) prior record warned 'a composition entrance exam will assume real compositional and music-theory ability, so a software-engineering BSc is a stretch' — this is WRONG for this specialisation, whose exam is weighted overwhelmingly toward DAW skill and submitted recordings; (3) the decisive obstacle is the Czech B1 certificate, which the prior record did not mention at all; (4) deadline is end-November, not unknown, and is much earlier than the follow-up master's; (5) the decree's standard entry requires a maturita, confirming this is a one-tier programme entered from secondary school. STILL UNVERIFIED: ECTS; the content and scheduling of the rozdílové zkoušky for the year-4 route; whether any number/duration of submitted recordings is expected.

programs.program: Strihová a zvuková skladba — študijný plán Zvuková skladba (Sound Composition), magisterské štúdium
programs.university: Vysoká škola múzických umení v Bratislave (VŠMU), Filmová a televízna fakulta (FTF) — Ateliér zvukovej skladby
programs.institutionType: Public film and television faculty of a national academy of performing arts
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Immersive Audio; Recording/Engineering
programs.language: Slovak only. Verified verbatim: "Štúdium sa uskutočňuje iba v slovenskom jazyku."
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semestre / 120 ECTS, full-time (denná forma). CONFIRMED on the official programme page.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED named courses on the official page: Mixáž a mastering (Mixing and Mastering); Zvuková tvorba – Audiovizuálna tvorba; Teória filmového zvuku (Film Sound Theory); Hudobná réžia (Music Direction); Zvuková syntéza (Sound Synthesis); plus music recording theory and practice and sound design theory. Master level explicitly targets film sound in surround, Dolby Surround 7.1 and Dolby Atmos, and film music. Official aim (portalvs description): to develop independent creative thinking and the ability to be a full partner in a film or TV crew across preparation, shooting and post-production; the graduate as a "zvukový majster" adapts sound expressive means to a dramaturgical intent, and is also equipped for radio production, classical-music recording, live recording and sound reinforcement, and work in music recording studios.
programs.entryRequirements: Formal condition is simply a completed bachelor's degree ("Základnou podmienkou prijatia na magisterské štúdium je úspešné ukončenie bakalárskeho štúdia", §56 of the Higher Education Act), with conditional admission possible if the degree is awarded by enrolment day. LANGUAGE CONDITION NOW VERIFIED and lower than expected: "Minimálne kritérium na prijatie zahraničného uchádzača na študijný program uskutočňovaný v slovenskom jazyku, je znalosť slovenského jazyka na úrovni A2 doložená certifikátom" — a Slovak A2 certificate, not B1 or B2. Foreign applicants must also supply a recognition statement (uznávacia doložka) and officially certified, translated copies of prior qualifications. Note the framing caveat: "Magisterské štúdium študijného programu STRIHOVÁ A ZVUKOVÁ SKLADBA nadväzuje na bakalársky študijný program s rovnakým názvom" (the MA follows on from the bachelor programme of the same name). Application via ePrihláška; fee €40 electronic / €60 paper. Approximately 5 places.
programs.portfolioSpec: Still UNVERIFIED at the level of exact specification — no number of works, duration or format is published. What IS now confirmed: home works must be submitted, and there is a hard upload deadline separate from the application deadline — "Domáce práce k prijímaciemu konaniu je potrebné nahrať podľa zaslaných inštrukcií najneskôr do 12. 6. 2026. Práce zaslané po termíne nebudú akceptované a uchádzač nebude pripustený k prijímaciemu konaniu" (works uploaded after the deadline are not accepted and the applicant is excluded). Instructions are sent individually after the application. Request the prospekt / požiadavky na prijímacie skúšky from the FTF study department (study coordinator Jana Mihoková, jana.mihokova@vsmu.sk, +421 2 2100 6511 ext. 511).
programs.auditionSpec: On-site entrance examination in Bratislava. Form confirmed on portalvs as: talentová, písomná, ústna, testy (talent, written, oral, tests). Single published exam date — 23 June 2026 in the prior cycle, with home works due 12 June 2026. No remote or online option is published for FTF; the Music and Dance Faculty of the same university runs a different process with an online interview for internationals, but that is a separate faculty and does not apply here. Worth asking the study department directly whether any remote accommodation exists.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check, leaning cautiously positive. The published basic condition is only "successful completion of bachelor's study" with NO named field — better than any other programme in this slice. The soft caveat is the statement that the MA "follows on from the bachelor programme of the same name", and the ateliér trains sound masters and sound engineers, so a strong practical portfolio would have to carry the case. No statement anywhere bars a non-music or non-film bachelor. Ask the coordinator directly.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Prior cycles: application by 9 April 2025 (2025/26) and 8 April 2026 (2026/27); home works upload by 12 June 2026; entrance exam 23 June 2026. For September 2027 entry expect roughly early April 2027, a mid-June 2027 works deadline and a late-June 2027 exam. Nothing for 2027/28 is published as of July 2026.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Via ePrihláška on the FTF VŠMU site; opening date not published. Fee €40 electronic, €60 paper.
programs.tuitionIntl: €0 per year for full-time study in Slovak within the standard length of study — CONFIRMED: "Ročné školné — Štandardná dĺžka štúdia: bezplatne", and VŠMU states that study in Slovak-language programmes is free, with foreign students treated on the same terms as Slovak ones. Fees apply only in defined cases: exceeding the standard length or parallel study costs €2,150/year at master's level in the arts field for 2025/26 (CORRECTED — the prior record's €1,650 is the BACHELOR-level rate). Programmes delivered in a foreign language cost €4,500/year regardless of nationality, but that does not apply to this Slovak-taught programme.
programs.scholarship: None found that this programme is eligible for. CRITICAL CORRECTION: the Slovak Ministry's "Scholarships for talented students from all over the world" (scholarships.portalvs.sk) is NOT available here. It is restricted to selected study programmes falling under the Smart Specialisation Strategy SK RIS3 2021+, and VŠMU does not appear anywhere in the official "List of selected smart specialization study programmes SK RIS 3 2021+" (checked directly — zero occurrences of VŠMU, Múzických, zvuk or skladba in the list). The scheme also requires an SAT score of at least 1100 or SCIO tests at the 63rd percentile, and pays €500/month up to €15,000 over two master's years — not the €1,025/month or €10,000 previously recorded, which conflated it with the separate National Scholarship Programme (NSP), a short-term mobility scheme for students already enrolled abroad, not a full-degree award.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial (tuition-free only). NOT full — no stipend scheme is available to him for this programme.
programs.stipend: None available. Tuition waiver by default. The €500/month national talent scholarship is closed to VŠMU programmes (not on the SK RIS3 list). The NSP is a mobility grant for stays of 1–10 months, not full degree study. Living costs in Bratislava would be entirely self-funded.
programs.facilities: Founded 1999. Described on the official page as one of Slovakia's most modern audio complexes and holding DOLBY ATMOS MUSIC STUDIO certification: five sound mixing suites, a cinema hall, professional microphones and field-recording equipment, working from stereo through multichannel for cinema and streaming. A development project upgrades one mixing suite to Dolby Atmos 12.1 and the cinema to Dolby Atmos 39.2. Head: Mgr. art. Tobiáš Potočný, ArtD.; staff include prof. Peter Mojžiš, doc. Dušan Kozák, doc. Marek Piaček. Facilities claims come from the ateliér's own page and were not independently corroborated.
programs.fitNotes: Still the best facilities-per-euro in the slice — Dolby Atmos Music certified, five mixing suites, 120 ECTS, and genuinely €0 tuition for a Tunisian. programs.program: Music Composition MA — Electroacoustic Composition specialisation
programs.university: Liszt Ferenc Zeneművészeti Egyetem (Liszt Academy of Music), Composition Department
programs.institutionType: Public conservatory / national academy of music
programs.focus: Electroacoustic Composition; Electronic Music/Live Electronics; Sonic Arts
programs.language: English — the Stipendium Hungaricum course record confirms "Study language: English". But the Academy's own page carries a conditional: "in case of non-instrumental majors, tuition is only offered in English if there are a minimum of 3 international students admitted in a given year to the same major." This remains the key structural risk for an English-track applicant.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years — CONFIRMED as "4 semesters (120 ECTS)" on the Stipendium Hungaricum course record. (Prior record listed ECTS as unverified; now verified.)
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED programme description: one-to-one lessons with a composition teacher developing one's own compositions and analysing 20th- and 21st-century pieces; performance of orchestral and vocal final diploma pieces; composition-related special courses freely chosen by interest; master courses from visiting professors and artists; and explicitly "Possibility to deepen studies in the field of electronic music." Applicants admitted to Classical Composition who have not studied electronic music before may have to complete two semesters of 'The basics of electronic composition'. Note: no specialisation named "Elektronikus zenei médiaművészet" or "EZMM" appears on the official MA admission page — the three published tracks are Classical, Electroacoustic and Applied Composition.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor diploma or higher. CONFIRMED verbatim: "Applicants must submit a preliminary credit recognition request directly to the Liszt Academy to determine whether the applicant's BA diploma can be accepted to apply for the programme, unless they have finished their BA studies at the Liszt Academy in the same field. Deadline: 31 March." Acceptable BA diplomas are defined in Annex 8 of the Academic Regulations for Students. An official Hungarian translation of the BA diploma is required by 31 March, made from the original document (not a copy); English translations are accepted during the application window only. Language certificate: TOEFL iBT min. 60, IELTS Academic min. 5.0, or Cambridge min. 154 — no other certificates accepted. A motivation letter is required. Applications route through the Stipendium Hungaricum portal or, for self-financed study, separately by 31 March.
programs.portfolioSpec: MAJOR CORRECTION — this is far less classical than previously recorded. For the ELECTROACOUSTIC COMPOSITION specialisation, verbatim: "Presentation of a fixed electroacoustic music piece and another piece applying live electronics with an acoustic instrument", and "The pieces submitted together must not exceed 25-30 minutes." Style exercises for electroacoustic are: "1 short etude in the style of any significant 20th-century musique concrète composer" and "1 short etude in the style of significant 20th-century synthesis technique composer". THERE IS NO BACH FUGUE AND NO CLASSICAL SONATA REQUIREMENT for this specialisation — the fugue, the Viennese Classical sonata movement and the 20th-century etude apply ONLY to Classical and Applied Composition. Separately, the Stipendium Hungaricum course record states generically that applicants "are to upload sheet music of three of their own compositions (and recordings if possible)" and are first pre-screened on that portfolio — reconcile this generic wording with the specialisation-specific spec directly with the Academy.
programs.auditionSpec: In person in Budapest, per the Academy's Stipendium Hungaricum page, verbatim: "All applicants are required to appear at the entrance examinations in person in Budapest, Hungary. The live entrance examinations cannot be substituted in any way", and on the SH course record: "Live streaming, video streaming, DVDs, CDs, or any other recordings are not accepted as a substitute." Exams take place late June / early July; candidates who clear the portfolio pre-screening are told their date during May. Components FOR ELECTROACOUSTIC specifically: formal analysis, written and oral, of a 20th-century instrumental work and an electroacoustic work; orchestration assessed as "MIDI sequencer orchestrating a chamber music piece for MIDI instruments or sampler" (not symphony-orchestra orchestration, which is the Classical track); score reading replaced by "Analysis of a contemporary graphic music notation"; a mandatory written test on the basics of electronic music (history from Varèse through Stockhausen, Xenakis, Chowning; sound parameters; waveform/spectrum/sonogram; sound types; tunings; sampling rate, Nyquist, bit depth; additive, subtractive, FM and granular synthesis); an oral practical computer task — mounting in ProTools or another DAW, algorithmic music in MAX/MSP or Pd, or sound synthesis in MAX/MSP, CSound, Pd or SuperCollider; and a personal interview on artistic beliefs, goals and general musical literacy. NOTE A CONTRADICTION: the admission-requirements page carries the heading "For applicants for the online entrance examination:", implying an online route exists, while the SH pages insist on in-person only. Resolve with international.office@lisztacademy.hu.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — no longer a flat 'no', but genuinely uncertain and gated. Nothing formally bars a non-music BA, and the electroacoustic exam does NOT test classical composition craft. The binding gate is the mandatory preliminary credit recognition request, which decides "whether the applicant's BA diploma can be accepted to apply for the programme" against Annex 8 of the Academic Regulations — a software-engineering BSc may simply fail that check, and it is decided before the exam. The exam itself still assumes he can produce two credible electroacoustic works including one with live electronics and an acoustic instrument, write two style etudes, analyse 20th-century scores and graphic notation, and pass an electronic-music theory test. This is buildable in a year of hard work in a way a Bach fugue is not. Submit the credit recognition request early and treat its outcome as the go/no-go.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Verified prior cycle (2026/27): Stipendium Hungaricum application deadline 15 January 2026; preliminary credit recognition request for MA due 31 March 2026; language certificates and Hungarian diploma translations due 31 March 2026; entrance examinations late June / early July 2026. Self-financed applicants apply separately, also by 31 March. For September 2027 entry expect a mid-January 2027 SH deadline with a 31 March 2027 credit-recognition deadline. Nothing for 2027/28 is published as of July 2026; the SH course page currently reads "Not available for applying at the moment".
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The Stipendium Hungaricum call typically opens in November for a mid-January close; the 2027/28 call should appear on stipendiumhungaricum.hu around November 2026.
programs.tuitionIntl: NOW VERIFIED: 950,000 HUF per semester for master's training, all programmes including Composition (roughly €2,400/semester, about €4,800/year). International students may pay in EUR at the Hungarian National Bank rate on the first day of classes. The annual fee covers two semesters and may be paid annually or per semester. Fully covered if admitted through Stipendium Hungaricum. (Prior record listed this as UNVERIFIED.)
programs.scholarship: STIPENDIUM HUNGARICUM — TUNISIA CONFIRMED ELIGIBLE. Tunisia appears by name in the territory list on the official SH course record for [MA] Music Composition at the Liszt Ferenc Academy of Music. The programme is in the SH catalogue as a full-degree, English-taught MA. Note the Academy's own SH page phrasing that the scholarship is available for "BA, MA and postgraduate Piano Soloist studies" — MA Music Composition is listed in the SH catalogue, so this reads as covering MA generally.
programs.stipend: Stipendium Hungaricum covers full tuition, a monthly stipend, a housing/accommodation contribution and medical insurance. Exact 2027/28 monthly amounts UNVERIFIED — read the official Call for Applications when published on stipendiumhungaricum.hu.
programs.facilities: Composition Department of Hungary's national music academy, with one-to-one composition teaching, visiting master courses, and performance of orchestral and vocal diploma pieces. The electronic-music strand is evidenced by the mandatory practical exam task requiring ProTools/DAW, MAX/MSP, Pd, CSound or SuperCollider work, implying computer-music studio provision. Exact studio and equipment inventory UNVERIFIED — no equipment list is published on the pages read. Institutional prestige is very high.
programs.fitNotes: SUBSTANTIALLY UPGRADED on verification. This is the only fully-funded, English-taught, Tunisia-eligible route in the slice, and the electroacoustic entrance exam turns out to be about electroacoustic craft, not classical conservatory training — no fugue, no sonata, no orchestral score reading, and the orchestration test is MIDI sequencing. The real work he would have to do is genuine and specific: produce a fixed-media piece plus a piece for acoustic instrument with live electronics inside 25–30 minutes, write two style etudes in musique concrète and synthesis idioms, learn 20th-century analysis and graphic notation, and pass an electronic-music theory test. Two hard gates remain: the preliminary credit recognition decision on a software-engineering BSc, and a mandatory in-person exam in Budapest. IELTS 5.0 is a low bar he can clear easily. Also be clear this is art-music composition, not dancefloor production.
programs.verificationNotes: Programme confirmed to exist as an MA in Budapest, English-taught via Stipendium Hungaricum, 4 semesters / 120 ECTS, with an Electroacoustic Composition specialisation. Verified against: the official MA Composition admission-requirements page (sourceUrl), read in full for the per-specialisation breakdown; the Stipendium Hungaricum course record https://apply.stipendiumhungaricum.hu/courses/course/654-ma-music-composition for language, ECTS, Tunisia's presence in the eligible territory list, the credit-recognition rule, language certificate thresholds and the in-person requirement; the Academy's SH 2026/27 news page for deadlines and the in-person statement; and the Academy tuition-fees page for the 950,000 HUF/semester master's rate. STILL UNVERIFIED: 2027/28 SH stipend amounts; the studio/equipment inventory; whether the English track will actually run (the 3-international-student rule); the contents of Annex 8.

programs.whatYouStudy: Sound art as a primary medium — installation, multimedia performance, sound experiments and interdisciplinary forms at the intersection of music, visual art and media art. Continues the topics of the faculty's Electronic Music Media Art BA. With 48 of roughly 120 credits in studio and creative project work, it is genuinely hands-on rather than theoretical.
programs.entryRequirements: A BA or higher university qualification, held by applicants with "komplex számítógépes művészeti (különösen zenei) ismeretekkel" (complex computer-based artistic, especially musical, knowledge) whose interests point at the creative and research areas of sound art. Instruction is in Hungarian, so a Hungarian-language capability is implicit. No published international-applicant procedure, no published language-certificate requirement, and no dedicated international contact on the programme pages.
programs.portfolioSpec: UNVERIFIED as to exact specification — confirmed that no number of works, duration or file format is published. What IS published verbatim: the portfolio is "eddigi alkotói és szakmai munkát bemutató, elektronikus dokumentáció" (electronic documentation presenting prior creative and professional work), submitted with a work plan comprising "a képzés idejére tervezett szakmai munka ismertetése, témakör szerinti és időbeli bontásban" (description of planned professional work over the programme, broken down by topic and timeline), a bibliography and work list, and "várható művészeti és tudományos publikációk ismertetése" (description of expected artistic and scientific publications). programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — the wording is genuinely favourable. The requirement is a BA "or higher university qualification" plus "complex computer-based artistic (especially musical) knowledge", not a music degree, and the exam is a portfolio, a work plan and an on-site multimedia task with no fugue, no score reading and no theory paper. A computer-science graduate with a demonstrable computer-music practice arguably fits the stated profile better than most applicants. Confirm with the institute — but note this favourable door opens onto a Hungarian-language programme.

programs.program: Máster de formación permanente en Producción de Música y Sonido para Experiencias del Entretenimiento (marketed as "Máster en Música y Sonido para Experiencias del Entretenimiento")

En caso de no disponer de un título de grado oficial, al finalizar el máster se obtendrá un certificado." programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED full module list from the official plan de estudios: Notación musical (Finale); Guion interactivo y musical; Técnicas de grabación (professional studio recording); Logic Pro (recording, advanced editing, mixing, synthesis, virtual orchestration, MIDI); Unity & Unreal (integral audio solutions for game projects); Música en el cine; Audio inmersivo (physics of spatial sound + a creative immersive recording/production project); Pro Tools; Diseño sonoro (dialogue, ambience, FX and music through production, recording, editing, mixing, export and implementation into a real video game); Middleware (FMOD and Wwise, based on the official courses); Luthería digital (designing and building digital musical instruments); Mezcla y masterización (mixing and mastering, broadcast standards, hands-on mastering); Historia de la música interactiva; Ableton (sound physics, digital audio, MIDI, production techniques, synthesis — the club/electronic-facing module); Proyecto (compose an original string-quartet work, optionally with electronics, premiered by professional performers); Propiedad intelectual (music industry, self-releasing, publishing and licensing); TFM; Prácticas (compulsory industry internship). programs.entryRequirements: No prior-study requirement, but a mandatory admission interview. Para pedir la entrevista, hay que escribir un correo electrónico a [master email]." And: "Si no se tiene un título de grado oficial, al terminar se obtendrá un certificado." programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio specification is published anywhere on the official page — CONFIRMED absent, not merely unfound. programs.fitNotes: On content this is the single best craft match found for him: Ableton, Logic and Pro Tools taught as full modules, a dedicated mixing-and-mastering module, studio recording, immersive audio, an in-house record label, a compulsory internship, and "DJ" printed on the official careers list — all reachable with no music degree and no audition, just an interview, at a UB-badged school that explicitly names developers as a target profile. Two obstacles decide it, and neither is small: the entire programme is taught in Spanish, which he does not speak (though he has ~14 months and fluent French to build on), and the price is undisclosed with zero master-level funding — the ENTI scholarship scheme is undergraduate-only. Treat it as a high-priority early enquiry: email for the price and the interview now, and start Spanish immediately if the number is survivable.
programs.verificationNotes: Official ENTI programme page retrieved and read in full (WebFetch was blocked by a 503 bot filter; the page was obtained directly and parsed). CONFIRMED verbatim: programme exists and runs; título propio de máster from the Universitat de Barcelona; 60 ECTS; 1 year; presencial with an afternoon timetable; 30 places; "Idioma de les clases: Castellano"; "Inicio: octubre del 2026"; the no-minimum-prior-study rule; the mandatory interview with the academic director; the certificate-instead-of-title consequence of lacking a degree; developers named in the recommended profiles; the complete 18-module curriculum; DJ listed among career outcomes; price available only on request. Campus address and studio/VR/mocap facilities confirmed from ENTI's own Campus Diagonal page. Scholarship exclusion confirmed from ENTI's own Becas page. NOT CONFIRMED: the tuition figure (withheld by the institution itself), any application deadline, whether the admission interview can be done remotely, and any 2027-28 intake details. CORRECTIONS to the prior record: the awarded title is "Producción de Música y Sonido para Experiencias del Entretenimiento" (fuller than the marketing name); the advertised start is October 2026, not an unspecified October; scholarships are now a confirmed negative rather than UNVERIFIED; facilities are now verified (professional music studio, VR/mocap, per-student workstations, ENTI Records) rather than 'implied'; and the Spanish-only language of instruction should be treated as a blocking-level caveat rather than an unknown.

programs.program: Màster en Art Sonor (Master in Sound Art)
programs.university: Universitat de Barcelona — Facultat de Belles Arts, Departament d'Arts Visuals i Disseny / Laboratori d'Art Sonor
programs.city: Barcelona (Faculty of Fine Arts, C/ Pau Gargallo 4, 08028 Barcelona). An online modality is also offered.
programs.degree: Màster propi (UB own title) — 90 ECTS, awarded only on completion of two 30-ECTS postgraduate certificates plus a 30-ECTS final master's project. Applicants without a bachelor's degree can only obtain a "diploma de extensión universitaria" instead. Not an official (oficial) Spanish master's.
programs.institutionType: Public university — fine arts faculty (own-title / continuing-education programme, so fees are commercial rather than public per-credit rates)
programs.focus: Sonic Arts (practice-based); Sound Design (spatial/architectural); experimental and electroacoustic music; field recording and soundscape
programs.durationEcts: CORRECTED: 90 ECTS, not 70 — and it runs over TWO academic years, not one. Verified wording: "The Master degree in Sound Art is 90 ECTS credits and is structured into two specialization courses: Sound Creation Postgraduate (30 ECTS) and Sound Design Postgraduate (30 ECTS) plus a Master's Final Project (30 ECTS). To present the Final Project it is mandatory to have approved the two postgraduates (60 credits)." Also verified: "with a duration of two specific academic years... Completion of the two specific degrees and the Final Project must begin and end within the two established academic years", and the Final Project is taken in the first semester of the year FOLLOWING the two postgraduate blocks. Per the official academic calendar, Sound Design runs from after 12 October to early February and Sound Creation from after 10 February to late June; classes are Tuesday, Wednesday and Thursday mornings (10:00-14:00). Note: the Structure page states the reverse semester order to the Calendar page — an internal inconsistency on the official site worth querying.
programs.language: CORRECTED: English. The official English Introduction page states plainly: "Language — Classes are usually held in English." The prior assumption of Spanish/Catalan-only was wrong; the site itself is published in Catalan, Spanish and English. This removes what looked like the main barrier for him.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED full subject list. Postgraduate in Sound Creation: Materials and Tools (30 ECTS) — Audio formats, editors and mixers (2 ECTS, Lina Bautista); Deep Listening and Soundscape Recording (6 ECTS, Mikel R. Nieto); Ethics and aesthetics of sound art; Musical generation elements; Phonetics; Psychoacoustics and experimental music; Radio Creation; Sculpture and sound object. Postgraduate in Sound Design: Projection and Space (30 ECTS) — Architectural acoustics; Artistic orientation seminars; Social and political implications of sound art; Sound Installation; Spatial Metaphors of Sound; Technical orientation seminar; Time and space in experimental music. Final Master's Project (30 ECTS) — an artistic-production or theoretical-research project supervised by a master's tutor with technical support from the UB Sound Art Laboratory, aimed at public presentation at a venue such as Arts Santa Mònica or Hangar. Verified methodology: "a practical work system based on direct experimentation with sounds, spaces and materials". CORRECTION: there is no "audio post-production" subject; the nearest equivalent is the 2-ECTS "Audio formats, editors and mixers". Nothing in the syllabus covers music production, DAW-based composition, mixing/mastering for release, or electronic dance music.
programs.entryRequirements: CORRECTED — a bachelor's degree IS required, contrary to the previous UNVERIFIED note, and engineering is explicitly named as qualifying. Verified wording: "Los solicitantes del máster deberán poseer el título de grado, licenciatura, INGENIERÍA, arquitectura o titulación correspondiente (español o extranjero) que dé acceso al posgrado o máster... En el caso de no tener un grado o licenciatura, no será posible acceder a la maestría en arte sonoro. En su lugar, siempre será posible acceder a un diploma de extensión universitaria." Pre-registration documents: ID/passport copy; copy of the degree certificate; "Breve currículum vitae, incluyendo formación y actividad profesional en el campo del arte sonoro, si existe"; and "Carta de motivación de no más de 3.000 caracteres (espacios incluidos), explicando las razones por las cuales se quiere cursar el postgrado o máster y la línea de investigación o producción artística que se espera poder desarrollar." Selection: "La selección de los alumnos será realizada por los profesores del máster, en base a la carta de motivación, el expediente académico del grado o los posgrados o másteres previamente estudiados, el currículo artístico y la experiencia profesional." Admitted applicants receive a letter from the director roughly 15 days after full submission; only accepted applicants may enrol. Enrolment additionally requires the original or certified copy of the degree certificate and the full academic transcript, two passport photos and form P4, delivered IN PERSON at the Faculty of Fine Arts postgraduate office — a logistical problem for an applicant abroad, so ask about remote submission. No language certificate (IELTS/TOEFL) is mentioned anywhere in the requirements.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio of works is required — now CONFIRMED as a negative rather than an unknown. The only creative submission is (a) a short CV including any training and professional activity in the field of sound art, expressly caveated "si existe" (i.e. it is acceptable to have none), and (b) a motivation letter of no more than 3,000 characters including spaces, setting out why he wants the programme and the line of research or artistic production he intends to develop. That letter is the primary selection instrument. Submission by email to marti.ruiz@ub.edu or jmberenguer@ub.edu, stating whether he is applying to one postgraduate block or the full master.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition, no on-site test and no interview is published at any stage. Selection is a paper review by the master's teaching staff of the motivation letter, academic transcript, artistic CV and professional experience.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes for eligibility, but he is off-profile for content. "Ingeniería" is named among the degrees that give access, so his software-engineering BSc formally qualifies him for the full master's title. However the stated audience is different: "The master's degree is preferably aimed at graduates and professionals in the fields of plastic arts, architecture and music. Due to its content, this postgraduate course may be of interest to graduates and professionals in art history, pedagogy, psychology and philosophy." Software engineering is not on that list, and selection weighs "el currículo artístico y la experiencia profesional", which he does not yet have. Eligible on paper; competitive only with a persuasive motivation letter framing a sound-art research line.
programs.tuitionIntl: CORRECTED from UNVERIFIED to a confirmed figure: EUR 2,000 per component plus university fees, for each of the three components (Sound Creation postgraduate, Sound Design postgraduate, Final Master's Project) = EUR 6,000 total, plus university fees of "around 70 euros" per year. No separate international rate is published, so the same price applies to a Tunisian student. Only one component is paid per enrolment period; payment is due within one week of receiving the payment sheet and cannot be split.
programs.scholarship: None found — now a confirmed negative. The official Scholarships page states: "The Master's Degree does not have scholarships or other types of student grants." It only signposts external searches (general UB grant pages, AECID, Universia, Becas.com, Servibeca). AECID is the one avenue theoretically open to a Tunisian national, but nothing is ring-fenced for this programme. Self-pay should be assumed.
programs.applicationOpens: Pre-registration is open all year round ("La preinscripción para el máster se puede realizar durante todo el año"). CORRECTED enrolment windows — the official Enrollment page gives them as approximate recurring periods, not fixed 1-30 dates: "From mid-September to the end of October" (to enrol in the Sound Design postgraduate or the Final Master's Project) and "From mid-January to the end of February" (to enrol in the Sound Creation postgraduate or the Final Master's Project).
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No 2027-28 dates are published. What IS verified and recurring: pre-registration open year-round; enrolment mid-September to end of October, and mid-January to end of February; teaching starts after 12 October (Sound Design) and after 10 February (Sound Creation). For an October 2027 entry he would pre-register during 2026-27 and enrol in the mid-Sept-to-end-Oct 2027 window — but because admission requires an acceptance letter issued roughly 15 days after documents are complete, he should submit pre-registration months earlier. Confirm the 2027-28 calendar with the coordinators when published.
programs.facilities: Faculty of Fine Arts, C/ Pau Gargallo 4, 08028 Barcelona. Verified resources: the UB Laboratori d'Art Sonor with technical staff supporting final projects; the Faculty's sculpture workshops (open Tuesday to Friday, all day); image and audio editing studios in the classrooms. Practical sessions, conferences, sound installations and concerts take place at Arts Santa Mònica and at Hangar (Barcelona's contemporary art production centre), and strong final projects are shown publicly at such venues. Established faculty and guest lecturers include José Manuel Berenguer, Martí Ruiz, Pedro Alcalde, Lina Bautista, Carmen Pardo, Barbara Held, Agustí Fernández, Eduard Escoffet, Mikel R. Nieto, Anna Bofill Leví and Luz María Sánchez. No music-production control room, console or Atmos/immersive mixing suite is advertised.
programs.fitNotes: Verification improved the access picture and worsened the content picture. Good news: it is taught in English, his engineering degree explicitly qualifies him, there is no audition and no portfolio — just a 3,000-character motivation letter and a CV — pre-registration is open all year, the total cost is a modest EUR 6,000, and either 30-ECTS block can be taken standalone as a low-risk trial (there is also a fully online mode). Bad news: this is art-world sound practice — sound installation, soundscape and deep listening, radio art, architectural acoustics, psychoacoustics, sound sculpture — with no music production, no DAW-based composition, no mixing or mastering for release and nothing club-facing. It also costs two academic years and awards a título propio, and confirmed to have zero scholarships. It would make him a sound artist, not a DJ/producer. Keep it as a fallback or as a cheap English-language route into Barcelona's scene, not as the main plan.
programs.verificationNotes: Six official pages of the programme's own UB site were retrieved and read: Introduction, Structure, Subjects, Academic Calendar, Preregistration, Enrollment, Fees and payment, and Scholarships. CONFIRMED verbatim: 90 ECTS across three 30-ECTS components; two academic years; classes usually in English; bachelor's degree required with "ingeniería" explicitly listed as qualifying; the exact pre-registration document set (ID, degree copy, short CV, 3,000-character motivation letter); selection by staff review with an admission letter ~15 days later; no audition; EUR 2,000 per component plus ~EUR 70 university fees; "The Master's Degree does not have scholarships or other types of student grants"; year-round pre-registration with mid-Sept-to-Oct and mid-Jan-to-Feb enrolment windows; the complete 15-subject syllabus; the Sound Art Laboratory, sculpture workshops, and Arts Santa Mònica / Hangar links; and the existence of an online modality. FIVE CORRECTIONS to the prior record: (1) the master is 90 ECTS with a 30-ECTS final project, NOT 70 ECTS with a 10-ECTS project; (2) it spans two academic years, not one; (3) instruction is in English, not Spanish/Catalan; (4) a prior bachelor's degree is mandatory (previously logged as unpublished), and engineering explicitly qualifies; (5) tuition is published at EUR 6,000 total, not unpublished. Also corrected: "audio post-production" is not a subject on the syllabus, and the enrolment windows are approximate mid-month-to-month-end periods rather than fixed 1-30 October / 1-28 February dates. NOT CONFIRMED: any 2027-28 calendar; whether the in-person enrolment document handover at Pau Gargallo can be done remotely from Tunisia; whether the online modality is priced identically; and the internal contradiction between the Structure page and the Academic Calendar page over which block runs in which semester. The prior sourceUrl (site root) has been replaced with the official English Introduction page, which carries the language and audience statements.

programs.program: Mestrado em Multimédia — Especialização em Música Interativa e Design de Som (Master in Multimedia — Interactive Music and Sound Design)
programs.university: Universidade do Porto — Faculdade de Engenharia (FEUP), interdisciplinary programme taught by staff from five U.Porto faculties
programs.degree: Mestrado (2nd-cycle master). SIGARRA lists the certificate as "Master in Multimedia - Interactive Music and Sound Design (120 ECTS credits)"; a shorter "Specialization in Multimedia - Interactive Music and Sound Design (72 ECTS)" certificate also exists.
programs.institutionType: Public university (engineering faculty leading a five-faculty interdisciplinary programme)
programs.focus: Sound Design; Film/Game Sound; Immersive/Interactive Audio; Electronic Music (interactive musical systems)
programs.durationEcts: VERIFIED: 2 years / 120 ECTS. Academic year September–June/July, daytime regime. Semesters 1 and 2 have five 3-hour courses each; semester 3 has two electives running alongside the (annual) dissertation; semester 4 is entirely dissertation, submitted in June and defended in July. Classes fall on Tuesday, Thursday and Friday in slots starting 9:30, 14:00 and 17:00.
programs.language: CONFLICTING OFFICIAL SOURCES — must be resolved before applying. The programme's own official microsite (fe.up.pt/estudar/mm) states "LANGUAGE: ENGLISH". The FEUP course-catalogue page (fe.up.pt/estudar/cursos/mestrado-multimedia) states "Em Português e parcialmente em Inglês" (Portuguese, partly in English). Email mmult@fe.up.pt and ask which language the Interactive Music and Sound Design units are actually taught in.
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED specialisation description: "Provides skills to develop advanced work in the area of interactive musical systems, including design, creation, and operation of these systems in various application contexts, including (but not limited to) games, interactive installations, and other applications. Develops the ability to develop advanced work in the area of sound design for film or other audio-visual solutions, as well as digital games." One of four specialisations (Culture and Arts; Education; Interactive Music and Sound Design; Interactive Technologies and Digital Games). Specialisation coordinator VERIFIED: Prof. Gilberto Bernardes (FEUP). Programme director: Jorge Manuel Gomes Barbosa; assistant director: Maria Teresa Andrade. The full unit-by-unit list per specialisation sits on the microsite's specialisations pages but was not itemised here — request the plano de estudos from mmult@fe.up.pt.
programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED (SIGARRA): "Holders of Degree or equivalent (national or foreign), or holders of academic, scientific or professional curriculum recognized by the scientific committee as attesting the capacity to attend this program." Ranking is by curricular analysis plus an interview "if necessary", weighted: final degree mark or relevant academic/scientific/professional curriculum 30%; professional experience 20%; PROJECT PROPOSAL 50%. Mandatory documents: ID/passport; graduation certificate; transcript listing all courses with ECTS; CV; motivation letter (PDF, max 1 page); dissertation/research-topic proposal (max 5 pages); portfolio. Recommendation letters and photo are optional. Foreign qualifications must be in Portuguese, English, French or Spanish and signed/certified by the issuing institution, or authenticated and consularised, or carry a Hague Apostille — his French-language Tunisian paperwork is directly acceptable. Application fee €55 (PayPal accepted for applicants without a Portuguese bank account). No language certificate appears on the published documentation list.
programs.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED — a portfolio IS mandatory, and so is a project proposal. Published wording: "Portfolio (mandatory) — Portfolio of projects and works developed in academic, personal, and professional settings, related to the area." No number of works, duration, or file format is specified. Separately mandatory: "Dissertation/research topic proposal ... presented succinctly (max. 5 pages) including the motivation, a set of goals, and a brief description of how the student intends to develop it and which are the major skills already acquired and to be developed during the master programme" — this proposal is 50% of the admission score, the single heaviest criterion.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition, no on-site test. Selection is curricular analysis plus "an interview (if necessary)" — remote interview is normal for international applicants.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — VERIFIED. Entry is open to "Holders of Degree or equivalent (national or foreign)" with no subject restriction, and the programme explicitly targets "students and professionals from multiple areas of knowledge", listing Communication Technology and Sound Technology and Music among its feeder areas. It is run out of the engineering faculty's informatics department and its sibling specialisation is Interactive Technologies and Digital Games. A BSc Software Engineering is a natural feeder. The competitive risk is not the degree subject — it is the mandatory portfolio and the 50%-weighted project proposal.
programs.tuitionIntl: VERIFIED from the official FEUP 2026/2027 tuition table: Master in Multimedia, students covered by INTERNATIONAL STUDENT STATUS (a Tunisian national's default), full-time = €4,700.00 per year → approx. €9,400 over two years. National/non-international-status band = €1,500.00/year. CPLP international band = €2,600.00/year, but Tunisia is not a CPLP member so this does not apply. Part-time international bands also published (€1,645 / €3,290 / €3,760 / €2,350 by ECTS load).
programs.scholarship: None found. Crucially, U.Porto's SASUP social scholarships are open to Portuguese and EU nationals, stateless persons and nationals of countries with reciprocity protocols — but expressly EXCLUDE students holding International Student Status, which is the status a Tunisian applicant would hold. No entry scholarship for non-EU master's students was found on any official U.Porto/FEUP page.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For 2026/2027, phase 1 opened 9 February 2026. Expect a comparable early-February 2027 opening for a September 2027 start; the 2027/2028 calendar is not yet published.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Verified 2026/2027 calendar (three phases): 1st phase 9 Feb – 5 Mar 2026 (final results 17 Apr, enrolment 21–30 Apr); 2nd phase 6 Mar – 21 May 2026 (final results 16 Jul, enrolment 21 Jul – 3 Aug); 3rd phase 22 Jul – 13 Aug 2026 (final results 18 Sep, enrolment 21–25 Sep). CORRECTED place counts: 60 places in total for the Master in Multimedia across all four specialisations, split 10 (1st phase) / 30 (2nd) / 20 (3rd) — not 20 per phase. FEUP explicitly warns visa-needing international students to check each phase's result-posting and enrolment dates; for a Tunisian applicant phase 1 or 2 is effectively mandatory.
programs.facilities: Five-faculty interdisciplinary teaching base at U.Porto (engineering plus fine arts, sciences, letters, economics). The sound/music side is coordinated by Gilberto Bernardes, a recognised figure in music information retrieval and interactive music at FEUP/INESC TEC. Student group NCGM runs game jams, LAN parties and the Game Dev Meet Porto. Studio and console inventory is UNVERIFIED — no equipment list is published on the programme pages.
programs.fitNotes: The most CS-native route into sound in this batch, and the cheapest verified non-EU price here (€4,700/yr). It will take a software-engineering BSc without argument. Two real obstacles: the language of instruction is stated inconsistently on two official FEUP pages and must be clarified — if it is genuinely part-Portuguese that is a live problem for him; and admission is 50% weighted on a five-page dissertation project proposal plus a mandatory portfolio, neither of which he has today. It is where a programmer becomes a technical sound designer, not where you learn to mix a club track.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed on official sources: the programme exists at master level, 120 ECTS over 2 years (SIGARRA certificates list), the Interactive Music and Sound Design specialisation and its official description, the specialisation coordinator, the entry rule ("Holders of Degree or equivalent"), the 30/20/50 ranking weights, the mandatory portfolio + max-5-page project proposal + max-1-page motivation letter document list, the €55 application fee, the absence of any audition, the 2026/2027 three-phase calendar and the 60/10/30/20 place split, and the official 2026/2027 tuition table showing €4,700/yr for international-student status. Also confirmed that SASUP scholarships exclude International Student Status holders. NOT resolved: the direct contradiction between the FEUP catalogue page ("Português e parcialmente em Inglês") and the programme microsite ("LANGUAGE: ENGLISH"); the unit-level curriculum; studio/equipment inventory; and any 2027/2028 dates (none exist yet). The originally supplied sourceUrl (fe.up.pt/estudar/cursos/mestrado-multimedia/) is a valid but thin FEUP page — replaced with the SIGARRA course record, which carries the admission rules and ECTS.

programs.program: Màster Universitari en Tecnologies del So i de la Música / Master in Sound and Music Computing (SMC)
programs.university: Universitat Pompeu Fabra (UPF) — Department of Engineering, linked to the Music Technology Group
programs.institutionType: Public university
programs.focus: Computational and immersive audio; Electronic Music technology; sound synthesis, signal processing, music information retrieval and music AI — research/engineering-led, not studio production
programs.durationEcts: VERIFIED: 60 ECTS — 40 credits of compulsory and optional subjects plus a 20-credit master's thesis (the official Catalan register breaks this into 25 mandatory + 15 optional + 20 thesis). Face-to-face, full-time, one year by default; an official PART-TIME route spreads the 60 ECTS over two years. Depending on prior education you may be required to take up to 15 (full-time) or up to 50 (part-time) complementary undergraduate credits, extending the master to two years. Three trimesters: Sept–Dec, Jan–Mar, Apr–Jun; classes start around 21 September; thesis defended orally in the first week of July, final document due end of August. 25 places.
programs.language: English (verified on the official Overview page). All complementary undergraduate courses are also taught in English.
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED: the whole sound-communication chain — creation and generation of sound, transmission, perception. Grounding in "the most advanced technologies for the analysis, synthesis, transformation, and production of sound and music" plus the technologies and processes supporting sound and musical creation. Draws on music (composition, performance, musicology), physics/acoustics, engineering (signal processing, AI, human-computer interaction, electronics) and psychology (psychoacoustics). The programme explicitly "focuses on the more technical aspects of this field". Research focus mirrors the MTG: audio signal processing, music information retrieval, musical interfaces, computational musicology. Coordinator: Xavier Serra. Workload is openly stated as roughly 50 hours/week; mornings are deliberately kept free for study and NOT to make the master compatible with parallel work.
programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED on UPF's official admission-requirements page under this exact master: official bachelor's or master's degree from the EHEA or an equivalent foreign degree giving access to postgraduate study in the issuing country — and, verbatim, "S'accepten titulacions de qualsevol àmbit acadèmic" (degrees from ANY academic field are accepted); academic transcript with grade average; CV in English; motivation letter in English of 400–600 words; at least ONE academic recommendation letter (requested through the online application, institutional email addresses only — no gmail/yahoo/hotmail); accredited English at B2 level; passport/ID. "Complementàriament ... la comissió de selecció pot concertar una entrevista amb el candidat" — the committee may additionally arrange an interview. The SMC FAQ adds that the most important criterion is "excellence in the academic CV as related to the topics of the master", then the motivation letter, and that "if you do not have a Computer Science degree, you should be able to demonstrate an equivalent background" in maths, programming, signal processing and/or machine learning. Documents not in Catalan, Spanish, English, French, Italian or Portuguese need a sworn translation — his French-language documents are directly acceptable.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED: no portfolio required. Admission is CV + transcript + 400–600-word motivation letter + one academic reference + English B2 + passport, with a possible interview. The FAQ notes that if he has no formal music education, "the motivation letter is a good place to explain your non-formal musical training" — so his music case is made in prose, not in a submitted body of work.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition and no on-site test. The only possible live element is a discretionary selection-committee interview, normally by video for international candidates.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, unambiguously — the strongest verified "yes" in this batch. UPF's official requirements page states "S'accepten titulacions de qualsevol àmbit acadèmic" (degrees from any academic field are accepted), and the programme's own FAQ says "The ideal candidate has an undergraduate degree in Computer Science." His BSc Software Engineering is literally the preferred profile. No music degree is required at any point.
programs.tuitionIntl: VERIFIED on UPF's official page under this master: "Estudiants UE: 1.302 € / Estudiants no UE: 5.749,8 €". A Tunisian national pays €5,749.80 for the 60 ECTS. A separate non-refundable pre-registration fee applies (reported around €30 by third parties; not confirmed officially).
programs.scholarship: None found for a non-EU Tunisian. The SMC scholarships page simply redirects to UPF's general master's grants list, on which every item is a Spanish/Catalan state or regional grant with residency conditions (AGAUR general grant, EQUITAT, Basque Government, UPF community hardship aid), a Santander programme tied to enrolment at a Spanish university, or nationality-restricted — Fundación Carolina, the most visible option, is for IBERO-AMERICAN graduates only and therefore excludes Tunisia. What the MTG does offer, after enrolment, is paid research assistantships on specific projects plus partner-company internships (see the SMC internships page) — a partial offset, not entry funding.
programs.stipend: None at entry. Post-enrolment MTG research assistantships and partner-company internships exist; amounts are not published.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For 2026–2027 the application opened 14 November 2025. Expect an equivalent mid-November 2026 opening for the 2027–2028 (September 2027) intake; not yet published.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Verified 2026–2027 rounds: 14 January / 4 March / 27 April / 5 June 2026. UPF's own advice, quoted: "International candidates are encouraged to apply in the first and second application periods to allow admitted candidates enough time to address visa issues and get their documents legalized." For a September 2027 start he should plan a January–March 2027 submission once the 2027–2028 dates appear. Only complete applications validated by the administrator are considered.
programs.facilities: UPF's Music Technology Group is among Europe's most cited sound-and-music research groups (origin of Freesound and the Essentia audio-analysis library). Verified graduate destinations are R&D roles or PhDs: BMAT, Native Instruments, Sony CSL, Dolby, Pandora, Telefónica, Google, Apple, Adobe, Spotify; PhDs at IRCAM, QMUL, Amsterdam, Utrecht, NYU, City London, Stanford. Located in the Tànger building, Poblenou campus. A recording-studio/production-facility inventory is UNVERIFIED — none is published, consistent with an engineering department rather than a studio school.
programs.fitNotes: The best academic fit in this batch for his existing skill set and the easiest to get into on paper: any-field degrees accepted, CS explicitly the ideal profile, English, no portfolio, no audition, Barcelona. It is also the worst fit for the stated goal — its own FAQ says graduates go to R&D jobs or PhDs. Two points in his favour: the B2 English requirement can be met without IELTS/TOEFL by taking UPF's own non-accrediting level test and attaching the receipt, and a part-time route exists. Two against: €5,749.80 with no non-EU funding, and a self-declared ~50 hour/week load UPF says is incompatible with parallel work. Take it only if he enters the industry through the technology door.
programs.verificationNotes: The original sourceUrl was a gencat aggregator record and upf.edu returns HTTP 403 to ordinary fetching — the pages were retrieved via a headless-browser scrape, so everything here is from UPF's own pages, not third parties. Confirmed: official master level, English, Barcelona/Poblenou, 60 ECTS (40 taught + 20 thesis), 25 places, face-to-face, part-time option, trimester calendar and thesis timeline, coordinator Xavier Serra, the exact admission document list, the verbatim "any academic field accepted" clause, the 400–600-word motivation letter, the one-academic-reference rule, B2 English with the UPF level-test alternative, the possible committee interview, and the exact fees €1,302 EU / €5,749.80 non-EU. Confirmed the 2026–2027 opening (14 Nov 2025) and all four round deadlines from the MTG announcement. CORRECTED two prior claims: the entry expectation is NOT "a major in engineering or architecture" (aggregator text), and only ONE recommendation letter is required. NOT verified: the pre-registration fee amount and any studio/production facility inventory. No 2027–2028 dates exist yet.

programs.program: Màster propi en Composició Musical amb Tecnologies / Master's Degree in Composition with Technologies
programs.university: ESMUC — Escola Superior de Música de Catalunya
programs.degree: Màster propi (the school's own title, not an official state master), 60 ECTS
programs.institutionType: Public higher music school / conservatory
programs.focus: Electroacoustic and mixed composition; Live Electronics; interactive systems and live coding — composition-led, not commercial production
