programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED. Semester 1 (Producción de música electrónica): sound theory, music theory (chord construction, programming bass lines), cabling and connections, MIDI protocol, audio processing (dynamics processors, FX handling, EQ), hardware and software synthesisers, samplers, vocal recording and processing, mixing techniques, and two sequencers in depth — Ableton Live and Logic Pro X. Assessment: one exam plus four practical projects (MIDI-station integration exercise, a mix, a remix, a free original track). Semester 2 (Producción de música electrónica avanzada): advanced mixing and production, hardware and modular synthesis (Moog Sub 37, Prophet 12, Doepfer), sound design, advanced harmony, building a LIVE PERFORMANCE, mastering in the box, interactive installations and Max for Live, plus the industry block — how the industry works, managing an artist career, digital marketing for artists, copyright, contracts, press dossier and promotion channels, with guest producers from electrónica and urbana. Final deliverable: a complete, professionally mastered production. Named hardware/software partners: Native Instruments, Apple, Logic, Ableton, Universal Audio, Moog, Dave Smith, Doepfer, Elektron, Roland, Akai.
programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED (international tab): to obtain the Máster de Formación Permanente (25 ECTS) from UDIMA you must hold "un título universitario oficial de Grado, Licenciatura, Ingeniería Superior o Técnica, Arquitectura Superior o Técnica, Diplomatura o equivalente"; without one you receive the Máster Profesional from UDIMA provided you demonstrate at least 2 years of professional experience. Minimum age 18 for international students (16 on the national tab). Process: complete the admissions questionnaire and attend an access appointment/interview with an educational advisor, in person or by Zoom/Skype. Non-EU nationals must obtain a student stay authorisation or visa. International admissions also require the admission form, enrolment agreement, educational offer, passport photo, proof of the pre-registration transfer and a copy of the visa if applicable — all sent together; documents sent separately are not accepted.

programs.degree: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello (2nd-cycle diploma, EQF 7 — master-equivalent)

programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED module-by-module from the official DCSL34 accreditation PDF. YEAR 1 (60 CFA): Storia della musica elettroacustica 6; Ritmica della musica contemporanea 6; Esecuzione e interpretazione della musica elettroacustica — Ambienti esecutivi e di controllo per il live electronics 6; Composizione musicale elettroacustica 18 (INDIVIDUAL lesson); Informatica musicale 6; Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e della registrazione audio 2; Analisi compositiva 6; Acustica degli spazi musicali 4; Lingua straniera comunitaria 6. YEAR 2 (60 CFA): Storia della musica elettroacustica 6; Esecuzione e interpretazione — Ambienti esecutivi multimodali e interattivi 6; Composizione musicale informatica 18 (INDIVIDUAL); Informatica musicale 6; Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e della registrazione audio 2; Acustica degli strumenti musicali 4; a scelta dello studente 6; Prova finale (COME/02, composizione musicale elettroacustica) 12. THE DECISIVE DETAIL, newly verified from the published syllabus of Prof. Mario Salvucci (Informatica musicale COME/05): BIENNIO YEAR 1 = programming in Max MSP + java/javascript/nodejs; gen~/genexpr/C++ implementation of synthesis algorithms; adaptive filters; deterministic chaos, self-similar structures, strange attractors, flocking; MACHINE LEARNING — Markov chains, generative grammars, genetic algorithms, neural networks, GAN/StyleGAN/VAE, Stable Diffusion and GPT; ML libraries in Max (ml5js, MediaPipe, Magenta, Essentia); TensorFlow. BIENNIO YEAR 2 = introduction to C++ (control structures, functions, classes, pointers, dynamic memory) and to JUCE, culminating in implementing a full subtractive synthesizer AS A PLUGIN (MIDI in/sound out, oscillators, envelopes, polyphony and voice handling, modulation, filtering, GUI, host parameter communication); sound design of dynamic systems (artificial, natural, idiophone, mechanical, organic sources); Jitter, matrix/tensor operations, real-time video-audio interaction, OpenGL pipeline and SHADER PROGRAMMING, glitch/pixel-sort/databending algorithms, raytracing/raymarching; physical modelling (mass-spring, string, bowed instrument, waveguides). The composition syllabus (Prof. Silvia Lanzalone, COME/02) biennio year 1 covers composing the soundscape and acoustic ecology, intermedia Sound Art, SOUND INSTALLATION projects, multimedia/intermedia interaction with image and dance, electronic lutherie and sound design for augmented instruments (sensors, feedback systems, embedded systems); year 2 covers generative music, open forms, ecosystems and non-deterministic processes. Each year you deliver an original composition project supervised by the teacher.
programs.entryRequirements: Diploma accademico di primo livello, OR a university degree (laurea) or equivalent recognised foreign qualification, plus passing the entrance exam. Non-EU visa applicants pre-enrol through Universitaly (the conservatory's own admission notice points explicitly to www.universitaly.it for entry, residence, enrolment and credential recognition). Registration is on Esse3 Cineca (https://consrm.esse3.cineca.it/) and the conservatory warns NOT to use SPID or CIE when registering. programs.fitNotes: The strongest single find in this batch. Two things now verified change the picture completely: (1) the admission bar for a non-music graduate is just TWO original works plus an interview — the lowest documented bar of the six; (2) the biennio informatics syllabus is, in substance, an audio-software-engineering degree — he would spend year 2 writing C++ and building a polyphonic synthesizer plugin in JUCE, and year 1 doing ML for music in Max/TensorFlow. His BSc is a direct, compounding asset, not a handicap. The composition side is also more craft-oriented than assumed: sound design, DAW editing and montage, installations, augmented instruments, generative music. THE OBSTACLE IS ITALIAN — instruction is in Italian, the exam is on-site in Rome, and non-EU entry runs through Universitaly. Also note the aesthetic: this is art electronic music and sound art, not club or dancefloor production; it will make him a formidable sound designer and audio programmer, not a house producer. Realistic path: start Italian now (roughly 12 months to a usable level before the spring 2027 exam), and build two strong original audiovisual/electronic works.

A Software Engineering BSc is arguably coherent with 'Musica elettronica e tecnologie del suono', but this is an institutional judgement, not an entitlement, and should be confirmed in writing before applying. The good news: it is genuinely English-taught, it is real (3 semesters / 90 ECTS / MQF 7), the total non-EU fee of EUR 10,800 is modest by MFA standards, 'the auditory' is named in the official rationale, and a non-arts bachelor is not formally barred. The bad news is structural: 80 of the 90 ECTS are a single self-directed Project and Dissertation, so the degree mentors an existing practice rather than teaching him one. He wants to be taught mixing, production and sound design — this programme teaches none of that, and there is no audio module in the published structure. Admission also requires a 'substantial portfolio' plus, for him specifically, an interviewing board convened precisely because his first degree is not in Creative Arts/Media. Add an untaken IELTS and no funding. It remains the only plausible master-level practice-based option in Malta — UM's Master of Music provision is classical/academic and MCAST's sound provision is undergraduate — but 'only option in the country' is not a reason to apply. If he is curious, the university itself mandates contacting da.maks@um.edu.mt before applying; ask there whether sound practice is actually supervised and who would supervise it.
programs.verificationNotes: The sourceUrl was WRONG and has been FIXED. The previous URL (lowercase, 2025-6) redirected to UM's generic course-finder and rendered no course data, which is why the earlier entry was almost entirely UNVERIFIED. The uppercase 2026-7 code renders fully. CONFIRMED on that official page: Master of Fine Arts in Digital Arts exists at MQF Level 7; 3 semesters; 90 ECTS; full-time by research with a part-time option; study units DGA5011 (5 ECTS), DGA5017 (5 ECTS), DGA5908 Project and Dissertation (80 ECTS); non-EU tuition EUR 10,800 total (Year 1 EUR 10,800, Year 2 NIL); entry requires Second Class (Honours) in Creative Arts/Media or related field plus a substantial portfolio, or relevant professional qualifications/experience approved by Senate with possible preparatory coursework; the mandatory interviewing board for non-Creative-Arts first degrees (direct quote captured); mandatory pre-application consultation with the Department; the course rationale naming 'the visual, the auditory and the media arts'. COULD NOT CONFIRM: any application deadline or intake date (course page gives none; um.edu.mt/apply gave no dates; um.edu.mt/scholarships returned 404); EU tuition; any scholarship open to a Tunisian; department facilities, studios or staff specialisms; the exact portfolio specification. The Department of Digital Arts landing page carries contact details only. Web search budget was exhausted during this verification, so no supplementary sources could be consulted.

programs.program: Biennio Accademico di II livello in Music Production — ministerial course code DCSL34 Musica Elettronica (indirizzo Music Production); award: Diploma Accademico di II livello in Music Production
programs.university: Saint Louis College of Music
programs.city: Rome (via Baccina 47 main site; also via Urbana, via Boschetto, via Cimarra; a Milan operational site exists)
programs.institutionType: Private AFAM higher music-education institution authorised by the Italian MUR. Footer states it is "La prima Istituzione di Alta Formazione Artistica Musicale in Italia autorizzata dal Ministero dell'Università e della Ricerca al rilascio di diplomi accademici di I e II livello, equivalenti a laurea magistrale specialistica". Legal entity: Saint Louis Music Center srl.
programs.degree: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello (master-equivalent, MUR-recognised)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 CFA — NOW VERIFIED from the official Piano di studi PDF (Year 1 = 60 CFA: Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e registrazione 1 (6) + Analisi compositiva (8) + Composizione musicale elettroacustica I (22) + Storia delle tecnologie elettroacustiche (8) + Tecniche compositive pop rock I (10) + Materie elettive (6); Year 2 = 60 CFA: Ripresa e registrazione II (6) + Forme, sistemi e linguaggi musicali (8) + Composizione musicale elettroacustica II (22) + Diritto d'autore e royalties (5) + Tecniche compositive pop rock II (10) + Tesi e prova finale (9)). Teaching is fortnightly, concentrated in two consecutive days, approx. 300 contact hours per year.
programs.language: Course page states "Lingua: Italiano e Inglese". The official international-students page goes further: "Tutti i Corsi al Saint Louis sono offerti in lingua inglese o in lingua italiana, in base alla preferenza dello studente" — Italian is explicitly NOT a prerequisite, A2 is recommended, and a weekly Italian course is included in the ordinary fees. His French/English/Arabic profile is workable here.
programs.focus: Music Production — the closest thing in this slice to a producer's degree. Note the formal home department is Musica Elettronica e Nuove Tecnologie, so the study plan is weighted toward electroacoustic composition alongside the production craft.
programs.whatYouStudy: Verified against BOTH the course page and the official Piano di studi PDF, and they differ in emphasis — read the PDF, not the marketing copy. Marketing prose: managing a music-production project through every phase, from creative idea to arrangement with real and virtual instruments, recording, mixing and mastering. The actual credit-weighted plan is: COMPOSIZIONE MUSICALE ELETTROACUSTICA I and II — 22 CFA each, by far the largest component; TECNOLOGIE E TECNICHE DELLA RIPRESA E DELLA REGISTRAZIONE 1 and II (6 CFA each) — the Music Producer specialisation strand, in which "ciascuno specializzando produrra' sotto la guida del docente due brani", taking two tracks from songwriting and pre-production (key, bpm, groove, feel, style) through arrangement with real and virtual instruments, rehearsals, recording and overdubbing in both a home and a commercial studio, microphone choice and placement, monitoring, executive production, mix and mastering, for himself and for third parties; TECNICHE COMPOSITIVE POP ROCK I and II (10 CFA each); ANALISI COMPOSITIVA (8) and FORME, SISTEMI E LINGUAGGI MUSICALI (8); STORIA DELLE TECNOLOGIE ELETTROACUSTICHE (8); DIRITTO D'AUTORE E ROYALTIES (5) covering copyright, royalties, licence, publishing, production and performance contracts; 6 CFA of free electives usable across any department; 9 CFA thesis and final work. The bienni are "costruiti intorno alle inclinazioni artistiche di ciascuno studente", with original productions and third-party commissioned work running through the degree.
programs.entryRequirements: TWO different statements exist and the international one is the one that governs his case. Course page: "Diploma accademico triennale di primo livello già conseguito o da conseguirsi entro la sessione di Febbraio (iscrizione con riserva)". Official international-students page: "Accademici di II Livello: possono richiedere l'ammissione Cittadini UE o NON-UE in possesso del Diploma di Triennio universitario o accademico (o equivalente), ottenuto in Italia o nel proprio Paese di provenienza. È inoltre necessario dimostrare di avere un minimo di 15 anni di scolarizzazione." Degree must be submitted as a scanned original plus certified translation plus DOV (Dichiarazione di Valore) from the Italian embassy/consulate, or alternatively a CIMEA Diplome certificate. Attendance minimum 80% of classes; a part-time route exists. Erasmus+ mobility up to 12 months within the biennio. Non-EU applicants must ALSO run the parallel Universitaly pre-enrolment through the Italian diplomatic mission in Tunisia, which normally closes in July with no extensions; Saint Louis advises starting it no later than January/February.
programs.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED — the prior record's "3 pieces in a group of at least a trio" brief does NOT apply to him. That wording belongs to the performer accordions (Jazz, Composizione Jazz, Pop). The accordion that actually covers this course — "SONGWRITING + FILM TV SCORING + MUSICA APPLICATA + LIVE ELECTRONICS + MUSIC PRODUCTION + MIX E MASTERING" — omits the videoclip step entirely. And the official international-students page gives the applicable brief verbatim: "Composizione/Musica Elettronica/Musica Applicata: Prepara un link contenente il Portfolio (video, audio, spartiti) dei tuoi lavori più indicativi e recenti." So: a single link to a portfolio of his most representative and recent works (video, audio, scores). No number of works, no duration, no format prescribed.
programs.auditionSpec: NO performance audition. The official Piano di studi publishes the exact test: "PROVA DI AMMISSIONE — 1) colloquio individuale; 2) test a risposte multiple su argomenti di tecnologia musicale: fondamenti di audio digitale, sintesi sonora, protocollo MIDI; 3) clausura di 5 ore in cui gli allievi dovranno produrre un brano in due versioni diverse senza vincoli stilistici, a partire da una traccia vocale che verrà fornita loro." That third element is a supervised FIVE-HOUR production test: build a track in two different versions, any style, from a supplied vocal. CRUCIAL for him: the international-students page states that for international candidates the admission tests "potranno essere sostenute online tra Gennaio e Giugno, in date da concordare individualmente" — online, individually scheduled, January to June; only if he chooses to sit them in person is there a single June session. Numero chiuso: maximum 20 students per academic year, from Saint Louis's own first-level courses or selected by audition among external candidates.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — RESOLVED, and this is the biggest correction to the prior record. The official international-students page states that admission to II livello is open to EU or NON-EU citizens holding a "Diploma di Triennio universitario o accademico (o equivalente)" obtained in Italy or in their home country, with a minimum of 15 years of schooling. A university bachelor is therefore explicitly acceptable — no Italian first-level music diploma is required of an international applicant. What he must supply is the DOV or CIMEA certificate. Residual risk: "Gli studenti la cui preparazione in entrata NON sia RITENUTA IDONEA all'ingresso diretto ai Corsi di livello Accademico, potranno accedere ai Corsi di livello pre-accademico" — if the commission judges his musical preparation inadequate he can be routed to a pre-accademico year instead.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — genuinely not published. The site publishes no tuition schedule for academic courses anywhere (no fee page exists in the sitemap). Confirmed and published: registration fee €240–290 depending on the month of enrolment, plus a €250 down payment deducted from the annual fee; the admission process itself is free but the registration fee is non-refundable. The commonly cited "~€2,800/year" figure is NOT on the official site — do not rely on it. Request a written preventivo from the Segreteria Didattica. Fees are ISEE-linked for scholarship purposes, which matters below.
programs.scholarship: Saint Louis borse di studio (partial exonerations), Borse di collaborazione, LAZIODISCO regional right-to-study grants, Banca Sella student financing. NOT applicable to him: the Giorgia Mileto award, which is restricted to instrument and voice courses in the Jazz and Popular Music departments and is decided by a live audition in a Rome club.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial — self-pay baseline with income-and-merit-based reductions and a possible regional grant. No full-ride route found.
programs.stipend: No stipend. Saint Louis's own scholarships are partial exonerations worth €500–2,500 per year of full-time study, conditional on BOTH an ISEE below €22,000 AND, for students who did not come through Saint Louis's pre-accademici, an admission-test average of at least 26/30 (penalty of 1 point per outstanding subject). Applications run 2–31 July each year. Borse di collaborazione are worth €1,095 each for up to 150 hours of work per year. LAZIODISCO is compatible and can be held simultaneously. PRACTICAL WARNING: the ISEE threshold requires an ISEE parificato, which a Tunisian family must obtain through an Italian CAF — build time for this.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 January for international applicants ("Le domande di ammissione ai corsi accademici, che devono essere inviate complete dei link per la pre-selezione, vengono accettate ogni anno a partire dal 1° gennaio"). The generic Italian course page instead says 3 February. Both are standing annual rules rather than a dated cycle, but confirm the 2027 edition.
programs.deadline: 30 April (standing annual rule: "dal 3 febbraio al 30 aprile" on the course page; "a partire dal 1° gennaio, entro e non oltre il 30 APRILE" on the international page). Late applications considered only against remaining places. In-person admission tests in June and September; online tests for internationals January–June. PRIOR CYCLE — these are published standing dates, not a 2027-specific calendar; confirm the 2027/28 edition, and note the separate Universitaly pre-enrolment deadline of roughly July 2027 set by the Italian ministry.
programs.facilities: Rome campus across four sites plus a Milan site. Resident bands and permanent ensembles gigging in Rome clubs year-round, plus a large formation doing theatre concerts and record productions with international guests — recent named guests include Aaron Parks, Gegè Telesforo, Greg Hutchinson, Roberto Gatto, Vince Mendoza, Paolo Fresu, Fabrizio Bosso, Gianluca Petrella, Javier Girotto. Note the "Synth Louis" ensemble, an experimental group dedicated to electronic music, synthesisers and electronic instruments, open to electronic musicians. Erasmus+ partner since 2012 with up to 12 months of mobility per cycle. A dedicated International Office with a named Head of International Admissions (Marzia Bagli) and a per-department tutor for Musica Elettronica e Applicata (Sergio Bachelet). UNVERIFIED: studio, console and immersive-room inventory.
programs.fitNotes: Re-rated upward after verification. Three things the prior record got wrong in his favour: his BSc is explicitly accepted for a non-EU applicant, his portfolio is simply a link to his own audio/video works rather than a live-trio video, and the admission tests can be taken online from Tunis between January and June. Courses can be delivered in English. What remains genuinely hard: (1) tuition is not published anywhere, so this is an unpriced fee-paying route until he gets a written quote; (2) the scholarship route runs through ISEE, which is awkward from Tunisia; (3) the admission test includes a five-hour supervised production task — building a track in two versions from a supplied vocal — which he cannot pass on theory alone and must train for over the coming year; (4) the credit-weighted study plan is dominated by electroacoustic composition (44 of 120 CFA), so this is less of a pure record-production degree than the landing page implies. Still the strongest craft-and-production match in this slice.
programs.verificationNotes: The live site is behind a SiteGround proof-of-work bot challenge; the challenge was solved programmatically and the genuine live pages were read in full (not archived copies). Confirmed directly on saintlouis.eu: course exists at II livello, Rome, 2 years, fortnightly two-day blocks, ~300 h/year, "Lingua: Italiano e Inglese", numero chiuso of 20, entry-title wording, application window 3 Feb–30 Apr, admission tests in June and September over two consecutive days, 80% attendance, part-time route, Erasmus+. Additionally verified from the official Piano di studi PDF (linked from the course page): ministerial code DCSL34 Musica Elettronica indirizzo Music Production, the full 120-CFA subject list, and the exact three-part admission test including the five-hour production clausura. Additionally verified from https://saintlouis.eu/studenti-internazionali/ : non-EU entry title (university triennio + 15 years schooling), DOV/CIMEA requirement, the Composizione/Musica Elettronica portfolio brief, online admission tests January–June for internationals, 1 January–30 April window, €240–290 registration + €250 deposit, Universitaly pre-enrolment, Italian not a prerequisite. Additionally verified from https://saintlouis.eu/borse-di-studio/ : scholarship values, ISEE and merit criteria, 2–31 July window, LAZIODISCO compatibility, collaboration grants. COULD NOT VERIFY: annual tuition (no fee page exists on the site or in its sitemap); the CFA total for the second year's thesis line was read from the PDF and is included above; 2027-cycle dates are not yet published.

programs.program: Biennio Accademico di II livello in Sound Design & Post Production — ministerial course code DCSL61 Tecnico del Suono (indirizzo Sound Design & Post Production); award: Diploma Accademico di II livello in Sound Design
programs.university: Saint Louis College of Music
programs.institutionType: Private AFAM higher music-education institution authorised by the Italian MUR to award first- and second-level academic diplomas equivalent to an Italian laurea magistrale specialistica
programs.degree: Diploma Accademico di Secondo Livello in Sound Design (MUR-recognised)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years; fortnightly teaching in two consecutive days, approx. 300 contact hours per year. Year 1 = 60 CFA VERIFIED from the official Piano di studi (Storia del Sound Design e della post produzione audio I 6 + Sound Design I 20 + Audio Interattivo non Lineare Wwise I 8 + Tecnologie e tecniche del Restauro I 8 + Tecnologie e tecniche della ripresa e della registrazione audio I 12 + Materie elettive 6). Year 2 lists Restauro II 6 + Sound Design II 20 + Campionamento e post produzione Audio 8 + Wwise II 8 + Ripresa e registrazione II 12 + Materie elettive 3 = 57 CFA in the readable extract; the thesis/final-work line did not render, so the 120 CFA total is inferred rather than fully read.
programs.language: "Lingua: Italiano e Inglese" on the course page; the international-students page confirms all Saint Louis courses are delivered in English or Italian according to student preference, Italian is not an entry prerequisite, A2 is recommended, and a weekly Italian course is included in the fees.
programs.focus: Sound Design; Film, TV series, gaming, animation, media and advertising post-production; interactive game audio; audio restoration and forensic audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Verified against the course page and the official Piano di studi. SOUND DESIGN I–II (20 CFA each, the largest block): creating, recording and manipulating sound effects — ambiences, specials, Foley, organic and artificial effects — plus the Pro Tools post-production workflow (session setup, AAF/OMF interchange, working to picture, video export, timecode and frame-rate sync), the aesthetics of sound design (analysing a film's sound requirements, sound design in trailers, the relationship between effects and music in modern cinematic language) and hardware technique (microphones, portable recorders). AUDIO INTERATTIVO NON LINEARE WWISE I–II (8 CFA each): non-linear game audio through Audiokinetic Wwise, covering the full 101 syllabus plus advanced material — navigating the Wwise environment, building an implementation to spec, events, spatialisation, non-linear mixing and integration into the game engine. CAMPIONAMENTO E POST PRODUZIONE AUDIO (8): sampling and building custom sound libraries — instruments, modulators, envelopes, mapping, digital sound management. TECNOLOGIE E TECNICHE DEL RESTAURO I–II (8 + 6): audio restoration and remastering, from digitising historic material to recovery and treatment in specialised labs. TECNOLOGIE E TECNICHE DELLA RIPRESA E DELLA REGISTRAZIONE AUDIO I–II (12 each). STORIA DEL SOUND DESIGN E DELLA POST PRODUZIONE AUDIO. Original projects with Saint Louis's Composizione and Musica Applicata alle Immagini departments and with RUFA (Rome University of Fine Arts) and Vigamus.
programs.entryRequirements: Course page: "Diploma accademico triennale di primo livello già conseguito o da conseguirsi entro la sessione di Febbraio (iscrizione con riserva)". Governing rule for him, from the official international-students page: EU or NON-EU citizens holding a "Diploma di Triennio universitario o accademico (o equivalente)" plus a minimum of 15 years of schooling, evidenced by scanned original degree + certified translation + DOV from the Italian embassy, or a CIMEA Diplome certificate. 80% minimum attendance; part-time route available; Erasmus+ up to 12 months. Non-EU applicants must also complete Universitaly pre-enrolment through the Italian mission in Tunisia, normally closing in July.
programs.portfolioSpec: NONE — RESOLVED, and this reverses the prior record's UNVERIFIED. The official international-students page states plainly: "Per il Corso di Tecnico del Suono non è prevista pre-selezione ma un colloquio attitudinale." This course IS Tecnico del Suono (DCSL61). There is no pre-selection stage and no portfolio to submit — only an aptitude interview. The ensemble-video wording elsewhere on the page belongs to the Jazz/Pop/Songwriting/Classical performer tracks and does not apply.
programs.auditionSpec: NO audition and no practical production test. The official Piano di studi publishes the exact test: "PROVA DI AMMISSIONE — 1) Colloquio attitudinale; 2) Test scritto a risposte multiple incentrato sui seguenti argomenti: Fondamenti di audio digitale, Pro Tools, Riprese microfoniche, Protocollo MIDI." That is the whole thing: an aptitude interview plus a written multiple-choice test on digital audio fundamentals, Pro Tools, microphone technique and MIDI. For international candidates these tests can be sat ONLINE between January and June on individually agreed dates; an in-person route exists as a single June session. Numero chiuso: maximum 20 students per academic year.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES for a non-EU applicant — the international-students page accepts a university triennio (or equivalent) with 15 years of schooling, with no requirement for an Italian first-level music diploma. This is also the most natural of the two Saint Louis routes for an engineer: the feeder programmes are the first-level diplomas in Tecnico del Suono and Musica Elettronica, the entrance test is a technical multiple-choice paper rather than a musical performance, and the Wwise/game-engine strand rewards a software background directly. Residual risk unchanged: a candidate judged unprepared can be routed to a pre-accademico year.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED — no tuition schedule is published on saintlouis.eu for academic courses. Published and confirmed: registration fee €240–290 depending on month of enrolment, plus a €250 down payment credited against the annual fee; the admission process is otherwise free and the registration fee is non-refundable. Request a written preventivo from the Segreteria Didattica.
programs.scholarship: Saint Louis borse di studio (partial exonerations of €500–2,500 per year), Borse di collaborazione (€1,095 for up to 150 hours per year), LAZIODISCO regional grants (compatible and holdable simultaneously), Banca Sella student financing. The Giorgia Mileto award does not apply — it is restricted to Jazz and Popular Music instrument and voice courses.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial — self-pay baseline with income-and-merit-based reduction plus a possible regional grant.
programs.stipend: No stipend. Saint Louis exonerations require BOTH an ISEE below €22,000 AND an admission-test average of at least 26/30 for candidates not coming from its own pre-accademici; applications 2–31 July. The ISEE requirement means obtaining an ISEE parificato through an Italian CAF, which takes lead time from Tunisia.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 January for international applicants; 3 February per the generic Italian course page. Published as standing annual rules — confirm the 2027 edition.
programs.deadline: 30 April (standing annual window). Later applications considered only against remaining places. Admission tests in June and September in person; online January–June for internationals. PRIOR CYCLE — standing dates, not a published 2027 calendar; confirm, and factor in the separate ministry-set Universitaly pre-enrolment deadline of roughly July 2027.
programs.facilities: Pro Tools-based post-production teaching, Audiokinetic Wwise for interactive game audio, dedicated audio-restoration labs handling digitisation of historic material, cross-departmental projects with Composizione and Musica Applicata alle Immagini, and partnerships with RUFA and Vigamus. Erasmus+ network since 2012 with up to 12 months of mobility. Dedicated international tutor for Tecnico del Suono (Davide Prestanicola). Rome campus across four sites plus Milan. UNVERIFIED: console, studio and immersive-room inventory.
programs.fitNotes: After verification this is the single most ATTAINABLE programme in the slice for him: no portfolio at all, no audition, no performance requirement, an admission test that is an interview plus a multiple-choice paper on digital audio, Pro Tools, mic technique and MIDI — all sittable online from Tunis — and a non-EU entry rule that explicitly accepts his university bachelor. The Wwise and game-engine strand converts his software-engineering background into an immediate advantage. Two honest caveats. First, this is post-production for picture and games, not electronic music production — it will make him employable as a sound designer and give him a paying craft, but it will not by itself make him a producer or a DJ; the sister Music Production biennio is the better fit for the stated goal, and this one is the better fit for the bank balance. Second, tuition is unpublished and the scholarship route runs through ISEE, so treat it as an unpriced fee-paying route until the Segreteria gives him a written quote. Best used as the low-risk Italian application alongside a craft-focused first choice.

programs.program: Master of Science in Music and Acoustic Engineering (Music Engineering / MMI track)
programs.university: Politecnico di Milano
programs.city: Milan (Leonardo campus). The official programme page lists Campus as "Milano Leonardo" AND "Cremona" — Cremona hosts the Acoustic Engineering track.
programs.institutionType: Public technical university
programs.durationEcts: 2 years — VERIFIED on the programme page ("Duration: 2 Years", "Level: Master of Science", "Language: English"). The credit total is NOT stated on the programme page; it directs you to the Study Plan and the Programme Educational Regulations. 120 CFU is the standard for an Italian laurea magistrale but is not published on the page read, so treat the exact figure as unconfirmed.
programs.language: English — VERIFIED on the official page factsheet. Note a separate obligation: Politecnico requires ALL students to prove Italian language proficiency at B2 IN ORDER TO GRADUATE, explicitly flagged as "NOT an entry requirement"; a free Italian course and an exit test are provided.
programs.focus: Immersive/spatial audio, recording and audio engineering, music technologies and multimedia systems — the technical route, not the artistic one
programs.whatYouStudy: From the official page: "advanced education in the fields of sound and acoustic engineering, adopting an interdisciplinary approach that integrates competences in information engineering, acoustics, signal processing, computer engineering, and music technologies". It covers theoretical and applied acoustics, digital audio and sound signal processing, with focus on sound modelling, analysis and synthesis, audio acquisition and reproduction systems, music technologies and multimedia systems, plus design of hardware and software systems for audio, musical and acoustic applications, and perceptual evaluation and sound-quality assessment. Delivery combines theoretical courses, laboratory activities and project-based work. CAVEAT: the specific course list previously recorded (Advanced Coding Tools, Computer Music, Multimedia Signal Processing, Sound Analysis Synthesis and Processing, Electronics and Electroacoustics, Fundamentals of Acoustics, Creative Programming and Computing, Music Production Technologies, Capstone, 20-credit thesis) is NOT reproduced on the programme page, which points to the Study Plan document instead — plausible but not re-verified in this pass.
programs.entryRequirements: Verified verbatim from the official page. For a non-Italian degree: "Admission ... is open to students holding a Bachelor's or Master's degree awarded by a non-Italian higher education institution, provided that the qualification is recognised as equivalent in level, nature, and academic content to an Italian degree. Applicants must demonstrate an adequate background in information and industrial engineering disciplines, particularly in computer engineering, electronics, telecommunications, mathematics, and physics. Admission is subject to the evaluation of curricular requirements and personal preparation by the relevant Admission Committee." From the central admissions pages, additional hard requirements: the bachelor must give access to EQF Level 7; must "contain subjects closely related to the MSc programme you are applying to"; must be issued by an institution in the official education system of the country (franchising degrees are refused); "Applicants who have a Bachelor of Science in a different field or have attended a vocational school, cannot apply directly for a Master of Science"; an English language certificate is required of ALL applicants (or a university-certified statement that the bachelor was taught in English); country-specific minimum GPA rules apply to a listed set of countries; and Politecnico may at any stage demand a Declaration of Value or a CIMEA Statement of Comparability — without one at enrolment the student cannot register even after a positive evaluation. Maximum two programmes per application, one application per semester.
programs.portfolioSpec: None. No portfolio of creative work is required for this programme. Admission is on transcript, curricular background and English certification. Note that the merit-scholarship call does mention "the portfolio when requested" among assessment inputs — that clause applies to design/architecture programmes, not to this one.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition, no on-site test, no interview — a document-based competitive selection.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, emphatically — a non-music engineering bachelor is not merely accepted, it is required. The page names "computer engineering, electronics, telecommunications, mathematics, and physics" as the wanted background. His BSc in Software Engineering is the target profile; a conservatory graduate would be the one who struggles. The real gate is not the subject but the paperwork: his SMU MedTech degree must be shown to sit in Tunisia's official education system (not a franchise arrangement), give EQF Level 7 access, and be backed by a DOV or CIMEA comparability statement.
programs.tuitionIntl: VERIFIED for AY 2025/26 from the official tuition page: the annual all-inclusive contribution is €3,726.00, plus the regional diritto-allo-studio tax of €140.00, stamp duty €16.00 and insurance €11.04 — roughly €3,893 per year at the full rate. programs.program: ΔΠΜΣ «Τέχνες και Τεχνολογίες του Ήχου» / Interdepartmental MA in Sonic Arts and Audio Technologies, with two specialisations: Ηλεκτροακουστική Καλλιτεχνική Δημιουργία (Sonic Arts) and Εφαρμοσμένη Ηχητική Παραγωγή (Audio Technologies)
programs.university: Ionian University — jointly run by the Department of Music Studies and the Department of Audio and Visual Arts, School of Music and Audiovisual Arts
programs.institutionType: Public university
programs.durationEcts: 3 semesters / 90 ECTS — VERIFIED from the official curriculum table (Semester A: 5 modules × 6 ECTS = 30; Semester B: research project 12 ECTS + 3 modules × 6 = 30; Semester C: thesis 30; "Σύνολο Πιστωτικών Μονάδων: 90 ECTS"). Part-time study is expressly not available: "Το ΔΠΜΣ «Τέχνες και Τεχνολογίες του Ήχου» δεν παρέχει δυνατότητα μερικής φοίτησης."
programs.language: Greek, with some parts in English — VERIFIED verbatim: "Η γλώσσα διδασκαλίας είναι η ελληνική, με κάποια μέρη της διδασκαλίας να πραγματοποιούνται και στην αγγλική." The thesis may be written in English. There is no English-taught track.
programs.focus: Sonic Arts / electroacoustic music and live electronics (Specialisation A); Audio Technologies / applied sound production, recording and sound design for film, games, performing arts, virtual environments and the record industry (Specialisation B)
programs.whatYouStudy: Verified from the official curriculum and regulation. Semester A, both specialisations: Ήχος και Τέχνη / Sound and Art (6 ECTS) and Μουσική Πληροφορική / Music Informatics (6) — the latter teaching code-based representation of musical structures, Music Information Retrieval, SuperCollider, ChucK, Python, TensorFlow and LilyPond, plus hands-on additive, subtractive, FM, non-linear waveshaping, spectral, convolution, physical-modelling, granular and stochastic synthesis. Specialisation A adds Σύνθεση Ηλεκτροακουστικής Μουσικής (6) and Ηχητικός Σχεδιασμός / Sound Design (6); Specialisation B adds Τεχνική και Τεχνολογία της Ηχογράφησης / Recording Technique and Technology (6) and Ακουστική – Ψηφιακός Ήχος (6). Semester B: a compulsory 12-ECTS individual research project producing a complete creative work, plus Ραδιοφωνική Ηχητική Τέχνη, Διαδραστικά Ηχητικά Περιβάλλοντα, Σχεδιασμός Λογισμικού Ηχητικής Επεξεργασίας (audio-software design), ΜΟΥΣΙΚΗ ΠΑΡΑΓΩΓΗ / Music Production (6), Ηχητική Επένδυση and Ακουστικός Σχεδιασμός Χώρων. Semester C: 30-ECTS thesis. Article 7 and the curriculum page both guarantee that applied creative work "αντιστοιχούν κατ' ελάχιστον στο 50% του συνολικού διδακτικού έργου" — at least half of all teaching work is practical creation, not theory. Seminars named include MAX/MSP, PureData and SuperCollider, video-game sound design, radio art, acoustic ecology, new interfaces for musical expression, and rights management.
programs.entryRequirements: Holders of a first-cycle degree from a Greek HEI or an equivalent foreign institution under Article 34 of Law 4485/2017, in a field related to (a) sound and music art and science, (b) SOUND TECHNOLOGY — explicitly including Μουσικής Τεχνολογίας & Ακουστικής, Φυσικής, ΠΛΗΡΟΦΟΡΙΚΗΣ (Informatics), Ηλεκτρονικής, Ηλεκτρολογίας, Τεχνολογίας Ήχου and engineering diploma-holders from Polytechnic or Architecture schools, or (c) applied fields such as cultural management, cultural technology and communication, cinema and mass media. Graduates of other fields may enter only if they can demonstrate substantial research and/or artistic activity in the field. Required documents: application form stating the chosen specialisation; ID copy; two photographs; degree certificates — and for foreign degrees, "συνοδευόμενους από βεβαίωση αναγνώρισης ισοτιμίας από τον Δ.Ο.Α.Τ.Α.Π.", i.e. a formal DOATAP equivalence recognition, which is a slow and non-trivial process for a Tunisian degree; a certificate of at least good knowledge of English; full CV; statement of purpose; and AT LEAST TWO recommendation letters. Submission in the last published cycle was BY POST to the secretariat in Corfu.
programs.portfolioSpec: Recommended but not mandatory. The official document list places "φάκελος καλλιτεχνικών έργων" (artistic portfolio) alongside work experience, scientific publications and documented technological development work under the optional heading "Λοιπά στοιχεία (εφόσον υπάρχουν) που να τεκμηριώνουν την υποψηφιότητα". No number of works, duration or format is prescribed. But it is decisive in practice: Article 11 of the regulation sets a 100-point scale of formal qualifications 30, scientific/artistic qualifications 30, written examinations where held 15, and statement of purpose plus interview 25 — so 30 of 100 points hang on demonstrable artistic or research output, and a further sub-rule gives up to 10 points for certified professional experience at 2 points per year, which he does not have.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. Candidates whose files are complete and meet the criteria are called for interview before the evaluation committees, held "είτε με φυσική παρουσία στην έδρα του ΔΠΜΣ (Κέρκυρα), είτε διαδικτυακά" — in person in Corfu OR online. The interview is worth 25 of 100 points. A written examination may be set (15 points) but is conditional, not automatic.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, explicitly. Πληροφορικής (Informatics), Ηλεκτρονικής, Ηλεκτρολογίας, Φυσικής and Polytechnic-school engineering diplomas are all on the named eligible list, so a software-engineering BSc is squarely eligible without invoking the escape clause. The practical gate is not the discipline but DOATAP equivalence recognition of the Tunisian degree.
programs.tuitionIntl: €2,700 total for the whole programme — VERIFIED from both the official call and Article 18 of the regulation. Payable in one sum or in five instalments: €500 on enrolment, €400 before the first-semester exam period, €400 within two weeks of the second semester starting, €500 before the second-semester exam period, €900 within two weeks of the third semester starting. Non-refundable if studies are interrupted. This figure is from the 2022-23 edition — Greek postgraduate fee law has changed since, so confirm for 2027.
programs.scholarship: Article 18 fee waivers: "Ποσοστό έως 30% κατά μέγιστο των εισακτέων μεταπτυχιακών φοιτητών απαλλάσσονται από την καταβολή του συνόλου των τελών φοίτησης" — up to 30% of admitted students are fully exempt from all tuition under Article 35 of Law 4485/2017. Additionally, in semesters 1 and 2 the best-performing student of the cohort can be granted a waiver of the following semester's fees (worth €900), conditional on having passed every module of the reference semester.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial to Full on tuition — a full fee waiver is genuinely available to up to 30% of the intake; no living stipend exists.
programs.stipend: None. Fee waiver only, and it carries a service obligation: waiver holders and scholarship recipients "έχουν την υποχρέωση να προσφέρουν υπηρεσίες υποστήριξης προς τα δύο Τμήματα" — laboratory, tutorial or other support work for the two departments. He would self-fund living costs in Corfu.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The most recent call published on the official site opened 1 July 2022 for the 2022-23 year. No newer call is posted and the announcements page is empty.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date: 18 September 2022 for the 2022-23 intake, by postal submission, date-stamped by the programme secretariat. For a September 2027 start a summer 2027 call would be expected — but see the continuation warning below before planning around it.
programs.facilities: Corfu — the Music Studies secretariat is at the Palaio Frourio (Old Fortress), the Audio and Visual Arts department at Tsirigoti Square in the old town. Annual festival and artistic summer school immediately after the spring semester, at which student creative work is formally presented. Places strictly capped at 15 per specialisation. UNVERIFIED: studio, console and immersive-room inventory.
programs.fitNotes: On paper still the best-designed curriculum in the slice for his profile — an Informatics/engineering bachelor is named as eligible, there is no audition, the portfolio is formally optional, the interview can be done online from Tunis, tuition is only €2,700 with a real 30% chance of a full waiver, at least half of all teaching is guaranteed to be applied creative work, and Specialisation B literally contains a Music Production module. Semester A, three compulsory modules: Τεχνολογία και Τέχνη (Technology and Art), Ψηφιακή Αφήγηση (Digital Narrative), ΗΧΗΤΙΚΗ ΤΕΧΝΗ (Sound Art); plus two electives from five: Digital Illustration and Motion Graphics, Semiotic Analysis of New Media, Creative Web Technologies, Digital Poetics, Organic Open-Source Programming. DELIVERY MODEL, newly verified and significant: 10% of teaching hours in person, 90% at a distance via a synchronous tele-education platform.
programs.entryRequirements: Holders of a first-cycle degree from a Greek HEI or an equivalent foreign institution under Article 34 of Law 4485/2017 — BUT with a decisive restriction, quoted from the 2026-27 call: "Βάσει της ανωτέρω ιδιαίτερης στοχοθεσίας του ΠΜΣ, το πτυχίο των υποψηφίων που θα γίνονται δεκτοί στο ΠΜΣ θα πρέπει να έχει σχέση πρωτίστως με τις παραδοσιακές μορφές τέχνης" — the candidate's degree must relate primarily to TRADITIONAL ART FORMS. The three eligible categories are (a) Arts, Design and Architecture (Fine or Applied Arts, Cinema, Graphic Arts, Photography, Industrial Design, Architecture), (b) Music Science and Art (Music Studies), (c) applied art and audiovisual technology and communication (Cultural Environment Management and New Technologies, Cultural Technology and Communication, Mass Media). Required documents: online application; ID copy; recent photograph; degree certificates (with a place-of-study certificate for foreign awards and a DOATAP national-register check — no formal act of academic equivalence is needed if the institution is on the DOATAP National Register of Recognised Foreign HEIs); a foreign-language certificate; full CV; Statement of Purpose; AT LEAST TWO recommendation letters; the mandatory portfolio; and any further supporting evidence.
programs.portfolioSpec: MANDATORY — this corrects the prior record's UNVERIFIED. Item 9 of the 2026-27 call's document list reads: "Υποχρεωτικό φάκελος που να τεκμηριώνουν την υποψηφιότητα όπως, εργασιακή εμπειρία, φάκελος καλλιτεχνικών έργων (Σχέδιο, Ζωγραφική, Φωτογραφία, Μουσική, Βίντεο, Πολυμεσικό Έργο, Animation, Κόμικ, Οπτικοακουστικές Εγκαταστάσεις, και οποιοδήποτε άλλο δημιουργικό έργο)." A portfolio of artistic works — drawing, painting, photography, MUSIC, video, multimedia work, animation, comics, audiovisual installations or any other creative work — is compulsory. No number, duration or format is prescribed. For a candidate entering via the exception clause the portfolio is doubly load-bearing, since it is the evidence of the pre-existing artistic activity the clause requires.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. Candidates meeting the criteria may be called for interview if the evaluation committee deems it necessary, within one month of the application deadline, and "Οι συνεντεύξεις θα πραγματοποιηθούν διαδικτυακά" — the interviews are held ONLINE. programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO as a matter of ordinary eligibility — this reverses the prior record's "Likely yes". programs.durationEcts: 3 semesters full-time or 6 semesters part-time / 90 ECTS — VERIFIED from the current call. Semester 1: Digital Audio Processing 7.5, Audio Application Programming 7.5, General Acoustics 7.5, Sound Synthesis 7.5 = 30 ECTS. Semester 2: Special Topics in Acoustics 7.5, Applied Machine Learning for Sound and Music 7.5, Sound and Movement 7.5, Optoacoustics 7.5 = 30 ECTS. Semester 3: thesis 30 ECTS. Part-time students take the eight courses across four semesters with up to a year for the thesis. Attendance is compulsory and in person, with a maximum of three absences per course: "Το Π.Μ.Σ. υλοποιείται με τη διά ζώσης εκπαιδευτική διαδικασία. Η παρακολούθηση όλων των μαθημάτων είναι υποχρεωτική."
programs.language: NOT STATED in the official call or on the programme pages — genuinely unresolved. What is verifiable cuts both ways: the courses are listed and timetabled in Greek and taught by Greek faculty in Rethymno, which points to Greek delivery; but the ONLY language certificate the call demands is "Πιστοποιητικό γνώσης της Αγγλικής γλώσσας επιπέδου τουλάχιστον Β2" — an English certificate at B2 or above — and no Greek-language requirement appears anywhere. He must email the department to establish the actual language of delivery before applying. This is the single decisive unknown.
programs.focus: Recording and audio engineering, sound synthesis and sound design, digital audio processing, machine learning for sound and music, acoustics and optoacoustics, motion-based interaction
programs.whatYouStudy: Verified from the official call and the department pages. The programme "explores sound in its multiple dimensions: as a wave, as a signal, and as a carrier of information", combining applied knowledge with current research in digital audio processing, sound synthesis, acoustics and audiovisual technologies, artificial intelligence, and motion tracking for musical applications. The eight compulsory courses: DIGITAL AUDIO PROCESSING — PCM, sampling-rate conversion, spectral analysis, digital filters, noise minimisation, audio coding and decoding; AUDIO APPLICATION PROGRAMMING — building audio and music applications for capture, recording, spectral analysis and signal extraction in Python or C with specialised APIs; GENERAL ACOUSTICS; SOUND SYNTHESIS — advanced synthesis and modulation techniques, computer implementation and their application to contemporary music creation; SPECIAL TOPICS IN ACOUSTICS — musical, structural and psycho-acoustics, electroacoustics, computational acoustics; APPLIED MACHINE LEARNING FOR SOUND AND MUSIC — inferring music content information and sound-scene and event detection for intelligent applications; SOUND AND MOVEMENT — embodied music cognition, multimodality in audio interaction, correlating audio and motion data, and building interactive sound systems in which motion drives sound; OPTOACOUSTICS — optical detection of sound, light-generated sound sources, micro- and nano-acoustics. The thesis may be carried out in one of the collaborating laboratories in Greece or abroad. Weekly timetable for the current year runs Monday and Wednesday afternoons and evenings, 14:15–22:00.
programs.entryRequirements: NOW VERIFIED from the 2026-27 call, and better for him than previously recorded. Admitted, after selection, are graduates of: Faculties of Natural Sciences; POLYTECHNIC (ENGINEERING) SCHOOLS; TEI Engineering; Sound Technology and Musical Instruments T.E. and Traditional and Folk Music T.E.; Music Studies (and Ethnomusicology), Audio and Visual Arts, Journalism and Media; and Cultural Technology and Communication. "Επιπλέον στο ΠΜΣ γίνονται δεκτοί απόφοιτοι τμημάτων που είναι αντίστοιχα των παραπάνω και ανήκουν σε ομοταγή ιδρύματα της αλλοδαπής" — graduates of corresponding departments at equivalent foreign institutions are also admitted, and "Για άλλες περιπτώσεις υποψηφίων και για τη συνάφεια των ειδικοτήτων θα αποφασίζει κατά περίπτωση η Συνέλευση του Τμήματος". Required documents: two-sided copy of ID or PASSPORT; CV; degree copy and other qualifications, or a completion certificate; full undergraduate transcript; an English language certificate at level B2 or above; copies of publications and/or evidence of professional experience if any; TWO recommendation letters (or a statement of the reasons if they cannot be supplied, e.g. time constraints); and a short report of no more than one typed page on his scientific and professional interests with a clear statement of why he wants to take the programme.
programs.portfolioSpec: None. No portfolio is required or mentioned anywhere in the official call. The only creative/professional evidence sought is optional: copies of scientific publications and/or proof of professional experience "εφόσον υπάρχουν" — if they exist.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition and no written entrance examination. "Η διαδικασία επιλογής υποψηφίων περιλαμβάνει, μεταξύ άλλων, και προσωπική συνέντευξη, η οποία μπορεί, αν συντρέχουν λόγοι, να γίνει εξ' αποστάσεως" — the selection process includes a personal interview which may, where warranted, be held remotely. Evaluation takes place after the application deadline on a date depending on the number of candidates. Maximum intake 15 students per year.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, and this is now confirmed rather than inferred. Graduates of Polytechnic (engineering) schools and Faculties of Natural Sciences head the eligible list, and corresponding foreign departments are expressly included. A Tunisian BSc in Software Engineering from an engineering school is a natural fit for that category, with the Department Assembly ruling case by case on the relatedness of the specialisation. No special pleading and no music background needed.
programs.tuitionIntl: FREE — VERIFIED in the official call: "δεν απαιτείται η καταβολή τέλους φοίτησης", and on the programme page: "Το πρόγραμμα λειτουργεί χωρίς τέλη φοίτησης και οι φοιτούντες έχουν την υπόσταση υπότροφου κι επομένως αναμένεται να προσφέρουν έργο στην υποβοήθηση των εκπαιδευτικών αναγκών του Τμήματος" — no tuition fee at all; students hold the status of scholarship holders and are expected to contribute work supporting the department's teaching. This is the only tuition-free programme in the slice.
programs.scholarship: Not applicable to tuition, which is already zero and where every student holds nominal scholar status. No living-cost scholarship is published. Separately available through HMU student welfare: a meal card giving free meals in the university restaurant, and low-cost places in university halls, subject to published criteria.
programs.fundingLevel: Full on tuition (no fees at all); no maintenance stipend
programs.stipend: None. The programme charges nothing but pays nothing. He would self-fund living costs in Rethymno, which are among the lowest in this slice, with the free-meals card and subsidised halls materially reducing them if he qualifies.
programs.applicationOpens: 27 April for the current cycle. The 2026-27 call opened 27 April 2026. For a SEPTEMBER 2027 start expect the equivalent call to open around late April 2027.

For his SEPTEMBER 2027 target: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date, but the pattern is a late-April opening with an early-September close, so expect roughly late April to 7 September 2027.
programs.facilities: Department of Music Technology and Acoustics, operating since September 1999, within the School of Music and Optoacoustic Technologies established in Rethymno in 2019 — described as the only academic programme in Greece dedicated to sound and music technologies combined with the science of acoustics. Named teaching staff include Assoc. Prof. Chrysoula Alexandraki (programme director, Digital Audio Processing), Assoc. Prof. Maximos Kaliakatsos-Papakostas (Audio Application Programming, also department chair), Asst. Prof. Nikos Stefanakis (General Acoustics), Nikolas Valsamakis (Sound Synthesis) and Asst. Prof. Panagiota-Styliani Paschalidou. The thesis may be done in a collaborating laboratory in Greece or abroad. A doctoral programme covers the same fields. HMU student welfare provides a free-meals card and a student residence. UNVERIFIED: studio and console inventory.
programs.fitNotes: The strongest pure-funding case in the slice, and verification improved it on several fronts the prior record had marked as unknown: engineering graduates head the eligible-degree list, there is no portfolio and no audition, the interview can be held remotely, two recommendation letters and a one-page statement are the only written work required, and the sole language certificate demanded is ENGLISH at B2 — Greek is never mentioned as a requirement. Tuition is zero, Rethymno is cheap, and subsidised meals and housing exist. His software background maps directly onto Audio Application Programming, Applied Machine Learning for Sound and Music, and Sound and Movement. Three real obstacles. FIRST, the language of instruction is not published and the courses are timetabled in Greek — he must email the department (chrisoula@hmu.gr, maximoskp@hmu.gr, or the secretariat at ngoniota@hmu.gr) and get a straight answer before committing. SECOND, applications are submitted through morpheus.hmu.gr using TaxisNet credentials, which are Greek tax-authority login codes a Tunisian applicant does not have — he must ask the secretariat for the alternative route for foreign applicants, and should do so early. THIRD, only 15 places, attendance is compulsory and in person with a maximum of three absences per course, and the content is DSP, acoustics and machine learning rather than production or DJing — this would make him an audio engineer or audio-software specialist, not a producer. Worth pursuing as the free, funded, engineering-friendly option, but the language and TaxisNet questions must be settled first.
programs.verificationNotes: SOURCE URL UPDATED to the Greek programme page, which carries the live call; the English page at https://mta.hmu.gr/en/postgraduate/msc-in-sound-and-music-technologies/ is also official and was cross-read. Verified from the official 2026-27 call PDF (PROSKLISI_PMS_2026_27.pdf, published April 2026 and linked from the programme page): programme title in Greek and English, base in Rethymno, 3 semesters full-time / 6 part-time, maximum 15 students per year, no tuition fee, the complete eligible-degree list including Polytechnic schools and the foreign-equivalence clause, the 27 April – 7 September 2026 application window, online submission via morpheus.hmu.gr with TaxisNet, the personal interview that may be held remotely, the complete eight-item document list including the English B2 certificate and two recommendation letters, the 90 ECTS award and the full course-by-course credit table. Additionally verified from the department pages: the scholar-status/service expectation, compulsory in-person attendance with a maximum of three absences per course, the current weekly timetable, the coordinating committee membership, and the governing regulations (ΦΕΚ 6895/τΒ/08-12-2023 and ΦΕΚ 1154/τΒ/19-02-2024). NOT VERIFIED AND DECISIVE: the language of instruction is stated nowhere in the call or on the pages read — the only certificate required is English B2 and Greek is never mentioned, but the courses are timetabled in Greek, so this must be confirmed directly. Also unverified: whether a non-Greek applicant can complete the morpheus/TaxisNet application, the recognition route for a Tunisian degree, and the studio inventory. The department's HTML page states the deadline as "7 Σεπτεμβρίου 2027" while the call PDF for the same 2026-27 year says 2026 — treated above as a typo on the web page.

programs.program: Music (M.A.) — Sonic Arts concentration area (1st Education, thesis master)
programs.university: Istanbul Technical University (İTÜ) — Dr. Erol Üçer Center for Advanced Studies in Music (MIAM)
programs.institutionType: Public technical university; specialist music research centre and graduate school within it
programs.degree: M.A. in Music, thesis track (1st Education). A non-thesis '2nd Education' variant exists and awards a Term Project instead of a thesis.
programs.focus: Electronic Music / Live Electronics; Sonic Arts; Immersive Audio; Sound Design; some Music Production
programs.language: English. Confirmed verbatim on the 1st Education Masters page: 'The educational language of the program is %100 English.'
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters normal, 6 maximum, counted from the first course registration (excluding the scientific-preparation/preparatory semester). 36 credits required for graduation = 12 courses x 3 credits, of which at least 6 must be compulsory. ECTS equivalent is NOT published on any MIAM page — UNVERIFIED.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED curriculum. Optional 0-credit preparatory semester (the on-ramp for non-music entrants) includes Studio Practices, Introduction to Music Theory, Ear Training and Sight Singing, Preparatory Studies in Sonic Arts, Research Methodology. Compulsory pool relevant to him: Music Technology, Multitrack Recording and Mixing, History of Electronic Music, Audio Programming, Critical Listening, plus one course each from Music Theory, Music History and Ethnomusicology groups. Sonic Arts core per the concentration page: 'aspects of electronic music composition, history, audio programming, and multimedia design', electives include Mixed Electroacoustic Composition and Sound Studies. Stated areas of interest: 'electroacoustic music, mixed media composition, sound art installation concept and design, live laptop performance, interactive improvisation with computers and live performers, and multimedia composition.' Graduation requirement, verbatim: 'The final project or thesis for the Master's program is a portfolio of sound compositions of not less than 30 minutes, or sound art project of comparable scale. In addition students must submit a research paper of publishable quality.'
programs.portfolioSpec: CORRECTED — the prior-cycle text on file is obsolete. Current spec is the İTÜ MİAM 2026-2027 Fall Term Entrance Exam Handbook (published 13 May 2026), Sonic Arts section, verbatim: 'Applicants should submit a representative portfolio of creative work. The portfolio can include any of the following: electroacoustic or acousmatic compositions; sound installations; sound design; live performance(s); any other sound-based works using physical, digital, or electronic media; examples of creative audio coding / programming. You can include non-sonic elements if these are an important part of your creative practice (e.g. video, architectural drawings, text), but overall the portfolio must demonstrate a clear interest in sound/music. Please provide audio or audiovisual documentation as appropriate. You may also share examples of writing related to sound or music that you have produced (journal articles, reviews, curatorial statements etc.), though this is not required.' NO minimum number of works, NO duration, NO format prescribed. Delivery method has ALSO changed: no longer e-mail. Now: compress everything into a single .zip or .rar, upload to Google Drive / Dropbox / OneDrive only ('Please do not use any other service, such as Wetransfer or Rapidshare, since such services delete the files'), create an open sharing link, and submit it through the web form at http://tiny.cc/MiamApplication26-27Fall. Files must be named so 'the exam jury members will be able to understand its contents from the file name'. Portfolio contacts: Dr. Reuben de Lautour (lautour@itu.edu.tr) or Dr. Sair Sinan Kestelli (kestelli@itu.edu.tr). Portfolio submission does NOT replace registration at sis.itu.edu.tr — candidates who skip SIS registration 'will not be permitted to participate in the İTÜ MİAM Entrance Exams, even if a portfolio has been submitted by them.'
programs.auditionSpec: Yes, but MATERIALLY EASIER FOR HIM THAN PREVIOUSLY RECORDED. 2026-2027 handbook, verbatim: 'For Turkish candidates, entrance exams and interviews will be conducted in person at İTÜ Maçka Campus, specifically in the Maçka Artillery (Maçka Silahhane Binası), old building of School of Foreign Languages. International candidates have the option to do an online interview via Zoom as well.' Structure (2026 cycle): (1) written General Music Knowledge and Music Theory Exams, 10:00-13:00; (2) Field exam 14:00-16:00 — Sonic Arts is explicitly named as one of only three master's field exams (SED, Sonic Arts, Composition); (3) interviews over three days. NOTE: the Zoom concession is worded for the INTERVIEW only; the handbook does not say the written and field exams can be sat remotely. Confirm with miam@itu.edu.tr whether an overseas candidate must travel to Istanbul for the written papers. No instrumental audition for Sonic Arts (that is the Performance concentration only).
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED verbatim on the 1st Education Masters page: 'GPA: Not required.' 'ALES/GMAT/GRE: Talep edilmemektedir' (not requested). 'Concentration area requirements: There are no department / concentration area requirements.' Additional documents: 'Two letters of recommendations must be submitted by the candidate to verify their motivation and determination' and 'Candidates must prepare a portfolio relevant to their application area.' Online pre-registration at www.sis.itu.edu.tr, selecting the 'Müzik/Music' programme (NOT 'Müzik Teorisi ve Kompozisyon', which belongs to the Turkish Music State Conservatory). IMPORTANT CORRECTION ON ENGLISH: İTÜ does NOT accept IELTS. Accepted tests and minimum scores for master's entry are İTÜ Proficiency 65/100, TOEFL iBT 78/120, PTE Academic 62/90 (rising to 67/90 from 2026-2027 fall), YDS/e-YDS/YÖKDİL 65/100, OTE Advanced 111/140, e-Tep 50. Scores valid 2 years (YDS variants 5 years). Further constraint: 'TOEFL iBT and PTE Academic exam results must be taken from the exam centers in state universities.' He must plan for TOEFL iBT (at a qualifying centre) or the İTÜ Proficiency exam — booking IELTS would be wasted money.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — now confirmed, not merely 'leaning favourable'. The 1st Education Masters page states in the Application Conditions section: 'Concentration area requirements: There are no department / concentration area requirements.' Combined with 'GPA: Not required' and no ALES/GRE, entry is decided on portfolio + exams + interview + two references. The 0-credit preparatory semester (Introduction to Music Theory, Ear Training and Sight Singing, Preparatory Studies in Sonic Arts, Studio Practices) is the institution's published mechanism for entrants without prior music training. The 2026-2027 Sonic Arts portfolio spec explicitly invites 'examples of creative audio coding / programming', which directly rewards a software-engineering background. The one thing NOT waived for non-music applicants is the written General Music Knowledge and Music Theory exam.
programs.deadline: CURRENT CYCLE (Sept 2026 entry) — ALREADY CLOSED, and NOT his target. From the 2026-2027 Fall handbook: portfolio submission deadline 26 June 2026; SIS online registration deadline 26 June 2026; General Music Knowledge and Music Theory exams 1 July 2026 10:00-13:00; field exams 1 July 2026 14:00-16:00; interviews 1-2-3 July 2026 (schedule announced on the MIAM site 1 July 2026). For a SEPTEMBER 2027 start he needs the 2027-2028 Fall handbook — NOT YET PUBLISHED. Expect an equivalent late-June 2027 portfolio deadline with exams in the first days of July 2027. A separate spring-semester round also exists (the 2025-2026 Spring handbook was published 17 January 2026).
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR/CURRENT CYCLE pattern — the autumn handbook is posted on the MIAM news page in May (2026-2027 handbook: 13 May 2026; 2024-2025: 23 May 2024). The spring handbook appears in late January (2025-2026 Spring: 17 January 2026). The 2027-2028 announcement is not yet published; watch https://miam.itu.edu.tr/en/news from about May 2027.
programs.scholarship: Türkiye Bursları (Türkiye Scholarships, YTB). CONFIRMED on turkiyeburslari.gov.tr: a government scholarship open to non-Turkish nationals, covering Associate, Bachelor's, Master's, PhD and Research levels, with 'Music and Musicology', 'Fine Arts (Painting, Sculpture, Lithography)', 'Design', 'Photography' and 'Cinematography' among the listed eligible fields, and 2026 applications announced as open. NOT CONFIRMED in this pass: the specific 'Arts Scholarship Programme' sub-track, the claim that İTÜ is one of only three participating universities, and the claim that music technology is explicitly listed at master's level — the YTB site is JavaScript-driven and those detail pages did not render. Treat the Arts sub-programme as plausible but unverified; check tbbs.turkiyeburslari.gov.tr directly. Structural caveat: YTB places the scholar at a university rather than the scholar choosing freely, and a YTB award would still not exempt him from the MIAM entrance exam.
programs.fundingLevel: Full if Türkiye Bursları is awarded (unverified sub-track); otherwise genuinely low-cost — see tuition.
programs.stipend: PARTIAL. turkiyeburslari.gov.tr confirms the package covers a monthly stipend, tuition, accommodation, health insurance, a flight ticket and a Turkish language course. The specific figure of 6,500 TL/month at master's level and the age-under-30 / 75%-average criteria could NOT be verified on the official site in this pass — UNVERIFIED.
programs.tuitionIntl: NOW VERIFIED and far cheaper than previously estimated. İTÜ Registrar's published fee schedule: international graduate ('Institute') students who entered in 2024-2025 and 2025-2026 pay 33,300 TL for the academic year (those from 2023-2024 and earlier pay 23,500 TL). Turkish citizens at graduate level pay 1,115 TL/year. Paid in two equal instalments, first at registration, second at the start of the second semester. The earlier third-party estimate of USD 2,000-5,000/year was WRONG — 33,300 TL is roughly USD 800-1,000. The 2026-2027 figure will be set annually by the Council of Higher Education; expect an inflation-linked rise.
programs.facilities: CONFIRMED. Sonic Arts Lab, verbatim: 'the main teaching and research space for students and faculty in the Sonic Arts program. The laboratory houses a 8 channel sound diffusion system that can be configured for a range of purposes including high order ambisonics, spatial composition, loudspeaker orchestras, or multichannel sound installations. The laboratory also includes a workstation with advanced sound processing software as well as a variety of microphones and field recording equipment.' Also listed on the Facilities menu: Recording Studio, Immersive Lab, Percussion Lab, Sound Gallery, Concert & Seminar Halls, Library. Located on the İTÜ Maçka campus, Beşiktaş, central Istanbul. Resident contemporary ensemble Hezarfen performs student work. Sonic Arts faculty contacts: Dr. Reuben de Lautour, Dr. Sair Sinan Kestelli.
programs.fitNotes: Strongest fit in this slice and the one to build the next twelve months around. Fully English-taught, roughly USD 1,000/year tuition even without a scholarship, in a major electronic-music city, with a published 'no department / concentration area requirements' entry rule and a preparatory semester designed for people like him. The 2026-2027 portfolio wording is close to written for his profile: his own electronic tracks plus any Max/SuperCollider/Pure Data patches count as 'examples of creative audio coding / programming'. The obstacles are real but all solvable in a year: the compulsory written General Music Knowledge and Music Theory exam (start theory study now), TOEFL iBT 78 at a qualifying state-university test centre (do NOT book IELTS), two academic references, and probable travel to Istanbul for the written papers even though the interview can be on Zoom. Direction-of-travel caveat: Sonic Arts is electroacoustic/sound-art rather than club/dance production — it will make him a far better sound designer and a more technically literate producer, but it is not a DJ course.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed against https://miam.itu.edu.tr/en/academic-program/1st-education-masters (duration, 36 credits, 100% English, GPA/ALES not required, no concentration-area requirement, full curriculum), https://miam.itu.edu.tr/en/academic-program/concentration-areas (Sonic Arts overview, curriculum, 30-minute final portfolio), https://miam.itu.edu.tr/en/about-us/facilities/sonic-arts-lab (equipment), the İTÜ MİAM 2026-2027 Fall Term Entrance Exam Handbook PDF (portfolio spec, delivery method, full exam calendar, in-person rule and the Zoom option for international candidates), https://www.sis.itu.edu.tr/EN/student/tuition-fee/ (33,300 TL international graduate fee) and https://www.sis.itu.edu.tr/EN/regulations/valid-english-tests-and-minimum-scores.php (English tests — IELTS absent). Corrected from the prior record: the portfolio specification (rewritten and much broader), the delivery mechanism (web form + cloud link, not e-mail; WeTransfer now banned), the audition rule (online Zoom interview available to international candidates), the acceptsNonMusic status (now explicitly confirmed, not 'CHECK'), the tuition figure, and the English-test requirement (IELTS not accepted). Source URL updated from the near-empty /admission page to the substantive 1st Education Masters page.

programs.degree: M.A. in Music, thesis track (1st Education); non-thesis 2nd Education variant also available (Term Project instead of thesis)

programs.language: English ('The educational language of the program is %100 English')
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters normal, 6 maximum (excluding the preparatory semester); 36 credits = 12 courses x 3 credits, at least 6 compulsory. ECTS equivalent not published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED from the concentration-areas page. Verbatim: 'The core of the MIAM SED program consists of the following four courses: Studio Practices, Multitrack Recording and Mixing, Advanced Mixing and Mastering. However, the students are encouraged to expand their sonic knowledge by taking courses of their interest, such as Computer Music, Audio Programming and Classical Production.' Also verbatim: 'The opportunity for the students to work as both assistants and in some cases primary engineers at MIAM's recording studios during their studies is one of the most invaluable aspects of the program. These recording and mixing experiences compel the students to prepare different recording setups, mixes and masters for various genres and ensembles.' The concentration 'seeks to address the technical, commercial, and musical aspects of the discipline in equal measure' and requires students to take courses from every other concentration area as well. Compulsory-pool courses shared with all MIAM masters include Music Technology, Multitrack Recording and Mixing, Critical Listening, History of Electronic Music, Audio Programming, Music Business and Management.
programs.portfolioSpec: UPDATED to the 2026-2027 Fall handbook. Sound Engineering and Design, verbatim: 'Three mixes of recordings made by the candidate are required. Each mix must include at least one track from an acoustic source, recorded with a microphone.' / 'Demos must not contain any material recorded by others, downloaded online, or generated with AI tools.' / '1 page description of the mixes sent.' Example information required in that page: 'When was the recording done? Where was the recording done? What equipment was used? What software was used? Credits.' / 'Photos from recording sessions, as well as other supporting material, are also welcome.' NEW vs the prior cycle: the explicit prohibition on borrowed, downloaded or AI-generated material. Written General Music Knowledge and Music Theory exams (1 July 2026, 10:00-13:00), then a Sound Engineering and Design field exam (14:00-16:00 — SED is explicitly one of the three master's field exams), then an individual interview across 1-3 July. Handbook rule: in person at İTÜ Maçka Campus for Turkish candidates; 'International candidates have the option to do an online interview via Zoom as well' — the Zoom option is stated for the interview only, not the written or field exams. The secondary claim from the prior record that applicants demonstrate microphone recordings during the interview is NOT in the official handbook — treat as UNVERIFIED.
programs.entryRequirements: Same as Sonic Arts and confirmed verbatim: 'GPA: Not required', 'ALES/GMAT/GRE: Talep edilmemektedir', 'There are no department / concentration area requirements', two letters of recommendation, a portfolio relevant to the application area, and online pre-registration at www.sis.itu.edu.tr under 'Müzik/Music'. English proficiency: IELTS is NOT accepted by İTÜ. Master's minimums are İTÜ Proficiency 65/100, TOEFL iBT 78/120, PTE Academic 62/90 (67/90 from 2026-2027 fall), YDS/e-YDS/YÖKDİL 65/100, OTE Advanced 111/140, e-Tep 50; TOEFL iBT and PTE must be sat at exam centres in state universities.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES on paper — 'There are no department / concentration area requirements', no GPA and no ALES/GRE, and a 0-credit preparatory semester (including Studio Practices) exists for entrants without music training. The practical filter is not the degree but the portfolio: three of the candidate's OWN multitrack mixes, each containing at least one microphone-recorded acoustic track, with no borrowed, downloaded or AI-generated material. A self-taught in-the-box electronic producer cannot satisfy that from his existing catalogue; he must go and record real acoustic sources. The written General Music Knowledge and Music Theory exam is also not waived.

programs.program: Звуков дизайн (Sound Design) — MA. NOTE: the programme previously recorded here, 'Аудиопродукция и мастеринг' (Audio Production and Mastering), NO LONGER EXISTS and has been replaced.

programs.focus: Sound Design; Film / Game / Theatre Sound; Recording and Post-production; some Music Production and spatial audio
