programs.durationEcts: 2 semesters ('Срок на обучение: 2 семестъра'), full-time, fee-paying ('редовна (платено обучение)'). ECTS total not published — UNVERIFIED. NOTE this is 2 semesters, not the 3 semesters recorded for the withdrawn Audio Production and Mastering programme.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED verbatim from the official page. programs.portfolioSpec: An independently developed PROJECT presented at the admission interview, verbatim: 'събеседване по представен проект, самостоятелно разработен от кандидатите и представен на стандартен носител в електронен формат' (an interview on a presented project, independently developed by the candidate and submitted on a standard digital medium in electronic format). CORRECTION: the earlier, more permissive wording naming 'композиция, ремикс, рекламен спот' (composition, REMIX, advertising spot) belonged to the now-withdrawn Audio Production and Mastering page and is NO LONGER PUBLISHED. programs.program: Тонрежисура (Sound Engineering / Tonmeister) — master's programme
programs.university: New Bulgarian University (Нов български университет, NBU) — Master's Faculty, Department of Music
programs.institutionType: Private accredited university
programs.focus: Recording / Engineering; Electronic Music; Music Production; Mastering; Film & TV Sound
programs.language: Bulgarian
programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED in the 2026/2027 electronic catalogue. Two semesters for holders of a bachelor's in music and dance arts. Credit structure: 4 lecture courses (12 credits), 2 individual practical courses (6 credits), 5 training courses in semester 1 (15 credits), and 6 extracurricular study forms in semester 2 (30 credits) = 63 credits. FOR HIM: 'тези които са се обучавали в друга област се изготвя индивидуална програма на обучение което трае минимум 3 семестъра, като първият е подготвителен' — graduates of other fields get an individualised curriculum of a MINIMUM of 3 semesters, the first being preparatory.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED verbatim: 'Програмата предлага специализирано музикално обучение в областите: тонрежисура, звукови технологии, софтуерни решения в музикалното студио, електронен звук, звуков монтаж, аудиодизайн на звук, синтез на звук, мастеринг, звук в киното и телевизията, компютърно моделиране на звуковата картина' (sound direction, audio technologies, software solutions in the music studio, electronic sound, audio editing, sound design, sound synthesis, mastering, sound in cinema and television, computer modelling of the sound picture). Described as 'практически насочена с възможност за обмен с Европейски образователни институции' (practice-oriented with exchange opportunities at European institutions). The programme has internship and placement agreements with Bulgarian institutions and Erasmus+ agreements with over 20 European universities in Austria, the UK, Greece, Spain, Italy, Poland, Finland, France, Croatia, Switzerland and Türkiye. Graduation is by defence of a master's thesis, a diploma project, or a state examination after the required credits are earned.
programs.portfolioSpec: NO FORMAL PORTFOLIO, and the prior record overstated this. The admission tab lists only two specialised-exam components: 'Есе на тема: Защо избрах да се обучавам в Магистърска програма „Тонрежисура" в НБУ' (an essay on the theme: Why I chose to study in the MA programme Tonrezhisura at NBU) and 'Интервю на кандидата с Комисията по прием' (an interview with the admissions commission). CORRECTION: the earlier claim that candidates 'may also present compositions or developed audio projects to the commission' is NOT on the official admission page and could not be confirmed — treat as UNVERIFIED. Bringing production work anyway is obviously sensible, but it is not a published requirement or entitlement.
programs.auditionSpec: No performance audition. The specialised exam is the written essay plus an interview with the admissions commission. Whether the essay and interview can be conducted remotely for an overseas candidate is UNVERIFIED. The general ТОП aptitude test is a separate matter — foreign citizens and applicants who already hold a higher-education degree are exempt, so he would be exempt on both grounds (this general rule is stated in NBU's admission framework rather than on the programme page; treat the exemption as PARTIAL until confirmed with the Master's Faculty).
programs.entryRequirements: Verbatim: 'Кандидатите трябва да имат завършено ниво „бакалавър"' — candidates must hold a completed bachelor's level. Nothing else is specified on the admission tab: no grade minimum, no ALES-equivalent, no language certificate mentioned. Since all teaching is in Bulgarian, a Bulgarian-language qualification will in practice be required — the specific requirement is not published on the programme page and is UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — explicitly, and this remains the clearest published accommodation of a non-music bachelor in the whole slice. Verbatim from the 2026/2027 admission tab: 'Тези, което са завършили бакалавър в областта на музикалните и танцови изкуства се обучават 2 семестър, а тези които са се обучавали в друга област се изготвя индивидуална програма на обучение което трае минимум 3 семестъра, като първият е подготвителен.' (Those who completed a bachelor's in music and dance arts study 2 semesters; for those who studied in another field an individualised curriculum is drawn up lasting a minimum of 3 semesters, the first of which is preparatory.) A software-engineering BSc falls squarely into 'друга област' and triggers the 3-semester preparatory route.
programs.deadline: CURRENT CYCLE, not his. NBU's master's autumn intake for 2026/2027 runs 26 May 2026 to 9 October 2026, with ranking rounds through the summer. For a SEPTEMBER 2027 start he needs the 2027/2028 admission calendar, which is NOT YET PUBLISHED — expect an equivalent May-to-October 2027 window with July and August ranking rounds.
programs.applicationOpens: CURRENT CYCLE: 26 May 2026 for 2026/2027 autumn entry. 2027/2028 opening date unpublished; expect late May 2027.
programs.scholarship: None found for this programme or for external international applicants. NBU's published reductions are internal only — family discounts, 50% for students with disabilities, 50% for full orphans, and 25% off the first semester for NBU's own bachelor graduates. None applies to a Tunisian applicant arriving from outside.
programs.tuitionIntl: VERIFIED for 2026/2027, and no separate foreign-student rate is published. Two-semester master's programmes: 1,800-2,000 EUR (3,520.49-3,911.66 BGN) per semester. Three-semester master's programmes: 1,600-1,800 EUR (3,129.33-3,520.49 BGN) per semester. On the 3-semester non-music track that he would be placed on, total tuition is approximately 4,800-5,400 EUR. NBU states 'Семестриалната такса остава непроменена за целия период на обучение' — the semester fee stays unchanged for the whole period of uninterrupted study.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — no studio inventory is published on the electronic-catalogue pages. Programme director: гл. ас. д-р Ана Линчева, alincheva@nbu.bg, +359 2 8110 505, office 504A, building 1. Secretary: Алие Байрактар, abayraktar@nbu.bg. Master's Faculty office: building 1, office 122, +359 2 8110 133 / 8110 142.
programs.fitNotes: Still the best structural fit for his exact profile anywhere in this slice: NBU has already written a rule for people arriving from non-music degrees, complete with a preparatory first semester, and the content list (electronic sound, sound synthesis, mastering, studio software, sound in film and TV) maps directly onto what he wants to do. The admission bar is also the softest anywhere — an essay and an interview, no theory exam, no audition, no portfolio requirement. But two blockers are decisive for a September 2027 start: everything is taught in Bulgarian, a language he has no basis in and for which NBU offers no funded preparatory route, and it is a private university charging roughly 4,800-5,400 EUR with zero funding identified. Reclassify to B only if he is genuinely willing to spend a year on Bulgarian and can self-fund.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed against the NBU electronic catalogue for 2026/2027 — the generalinfo tab (programme scope, 63-credit structure, two-semester baseline, practice orientation, Erasmus+ partners, graduation route) and the admission tab (bachelor requirement, the verbatim non-music 3-semester preparatory rule, the essay theme, the interview, and the director's contact details), both at ecatalog.nbu.bg with P_ID=3311. programs.program: Arta sunetului de film (Film Sound Art) — master
programs.university: UNATC 'I.L. Caragiale' — National University of Theatre and Cinematography, Faculty of Film
programs.institutionType: Public national arts university (film and theatre school)
programs.degree: Master (2nd cycle), full-time (IF), domain Cinematografie și media
programs.focus: Film & Game Sound; Sound Design; Foley; Multichannel / immersive mixing
programs.language: Romanian. Confirmed: Arta sunetului de film is NOT among UNATC's English-taught Film Faculty masters, which per the 2026-2027 fee schedule are Design for New Media, Visual Effects, Audiovisual Preservation and Programming, Interactive Technologies for Performing and Media Arts, and Art of Game Design.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 credits — confirmed on the official admission page.
programs.whatYouStudy: Year 1: Sound Design; Sound Capture and Editing; Foley Art; Research and Creative Cinematography Workshop; Internship and Practice. Year 2: Advanced Sound Design; Film Sound Production/Post-production; Multichannel Mixing; Research and Creative Cinematography Workshop; Internship and Practice; Dissertation. Master's students concentrate on recording and processing sound for film, games and virtual reality, working on real fiction, documentary and animation productions in collaboration with the directing, cinematography and editing departments. The admission page names the DAWs in scope: ProTools, Nuendo, Reaper, Adobe Audition, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED verbatim. The dossier must contain a CV in EuroPass format and 'un portofoliu ce va conține lucrări artistice cu design sonor realizat de către candidat' (a portfolio containing artistic works with sound design created by the candidate), which may include digital copies of films or relevant sound-design projects. In addition the candidate must bring to the oral exam the DAW PROJECT FILE for one portfolio work of their own choosing, in ProTools, Nuendo, Reaper, Adobe Audition, Premiere Pro or DaVinci Resolve. No minimum or maximum number of works and no duration requirement is published. Portfolios are uploaded electronically through the 2BitsEDU / Edubits candidate platform after registration.
programs.auditionSpec: On-site, one evaluation stage in two parts. Proba 1 (written): film-culture exam based on a set bibliography, plus technical knowledge of sound design. Proba 2 (oral/colloquium): presentation and discussion of one self-selected portfolio work, with a live DAW project demonstration. Each part scored 1-10; tiebreaker is Proba 2 then Proba 1. Minimum passing grade 6.0/10. No live musical performance.
programs.entryRequirements: Completion of 'o specializare cu 180 credite sau 240 credite' — a study programme worth 180 or 240 credits, with NO field of study specified. A three-year Tunisian licence in software engineering (180 ECTS) satisfies this. HARD CONSTRAINT FOR HIM: UNATC's own admission pages state that foreign citizens must complete 'anul pregătitor de limba română' — the Romanian language preparatory year — BEFORE sitting the admission exams. Exemptions apply only to candidates who present Romanian educational credentials, prove at least four consecutive years of study in Romanian, or hold a minimum B1 certificate from an accredited Romanian institution or cultural organisation. Registration is exclusively via the 2BitsEDU online platform. Places: 3 state-funded (buget) + 3 tuition-based (taxă) for the 2026 cycle.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES — unambiguously. Published eligibility is purely credit-based: 'absolvit o specializare cu 180 credite sau 240 credite', with no discipline named. There is no music-degree requirement, no theory exam, and no audition. The written exam tests film culture and sound-design technical knowledge, both of which are learnable from a bibliography. This is the most open eligibility rule in the slice.
programs.deadline: CURRENT CYCLE (September 2026 entry) — NOT his target, and currently OPEN. 2026 cycle: registration 4 August - 9 September 2026; file verification 10-11 September 2026; exam period 15-20 September 2026. The 2027 calendar is NOT YET PUBLISHED — expect the same August-to-September 2027 pattern. Note a separate, earlier May-to-July pre-registration window applies to the English-taught masters (for 2026: 1 May - 1 July 2026), which does not cover this programme.
programs.applicationOpens: CURRENT CYCLE: 4 August 2026. 2027 window unpublished; expect early August 2027.
programs.scholarship: Romanian Government scholarships administered through the Ministry of Foreign Affairs (MAE), open specifically to non-EU citizens — Tunisia qualifies. Applications are made through scholarships.studyinromania.gov.ro. Eligibility confirmed on that portal: 'good results in education, respectively an average of the study years, for the last graduated school, of at least 7 (seven)' or an equivalent 'Good'. Excluded categories include persons of Romanian origin, those seeking protection in Romania, stateless persons, diplomatic staff, international-organisation employees, and existing state scholarship holders.
programs.fundingLevel: Full if the Romanian Government / MAE scholarship is awarded; plus 3 domestic tuition-free 'buget' places at programme level (competitive and normally taken by Romanian candidates).
programs.stipend: PARTIAL, and the prior record over-promised. Confirmed on studyinromania.gov.ro: the scholarship covers tuition, and provides free preparatory Romanian language instruction for those lacking proficiency (exemptions for prior Romanian-language education or a certified B1). Master's-level study is 'only in Romanian'. IMPORTANT CORRECTION: the portal states the scholarship does NOT cover 'personal expenses and international transport', and that accommodation in university dormitories remains the student's responsibility. The exact monthly stipend figure in lei for master's level could not be retrieved — UNVERIFIED. Do not assume airfare or free housing.
programs.tuitionIntl: NOW VERIFIED for the taxă place. UNATC Senate Decision 290/2026, annexed fee schedule 'TAXE DE STUDII – CICLUL II – STUDII UNIVERSITARE DE MASTERAT, studenți înmatriculați în anul I începând cu anul univ. 2026-2027': Arta sunetului de film = 13,750 lei per year (roughly 2,750 EUR). By comparison the same schedule prices Producție de film and Conținut și producție TV at 10,000 lei and Scenaristică and Filmologie at 6,875 lei. The schedule contains NO separate euro-denominated rate for foreign citizens — a distinct non-EU 'own funds' fee may be set by ministerial order and is UNVERIFIED. Contact secretariat@unatc.ro or study@unatc.ro.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED in detail — no equipment inventory is published. The curriculum implies a Foley stage and multichannel mixing rooms, and the department confirms students work on live fiction, documentary and animation productions alongside the directing, cinematography and editing departments, building professional portfolios. 13 specialised teaching staff. The admission page's named DAW list (ProTools, Nuendo, Reaper, Adobe Audition, Premiere Pro, DaVinci Resolve) indicates the toolchain in use.
programs.fitNotes: The most open door in the slice on paper — eligibility is purely 180 or 240 credits with no subject restriction, there is no music-theory exam and no audition, and the oral exam rewards demonstrable DAW craft over conservatory training. A government scholarship route exists that covers tuition and a free Romanian language year. Two things keep it off the top spot. First, timing: as a non-EU citizen he must complete the Romanian preparatory year BEFORE he can sit the admission exams, so a September 2027 target realistically means starting the prep year in 2027 and entering the master in 2028 — unless he obtains a B1 Romanian certificate independently. Second, direction: this is film, game and VR sound with Foley and picture-locked mixing, not club music production or DJing. It would make him an excellent sound designer with a bankable post-production skill, but it does not advance the DJ half of his ambition, and he currently has no sound-design-to-picture work to put in the portfolio.

programs.program: Музичка продукција (Muzička produkcija / Music Production) — master academic studies (MAS), interdisciplinary studies
programs.university: Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad (Akademija umetnosti, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu)
programs.institutionType: Public art academy within a public university
programs.degree: Master academic studies; professional title 'Мастер музички продуцент' (Master music producer). Administratively classed under Интердисциплинарне студије (interdisciplinary studies), attached to the Drama Arts department block in the admission competition.
programs.focus: Music Production; Electronic Music; Film and Media music production
programs.language: Serbian. Foreign applicants must submit 'доказ о познавању српског језика' — proof of knowledge of the Serbian language — as part of the application file.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year / 60 ECTS (2023 accreditation), consistent with the competition's requirement of a completed 240-ECTS undergraduate degree for entry.
programs.whatYouStudy: Core: Музичка продукција (Music Production, 2+2); Звук и музика на филму (Sound and Music in Film, 2+1); Савремене тенденције у музичкој продукцији 1 and 2 (Contemporary Trends in Music Production); Музика-догађај-публика (Music-Event-Audience); Мастер рад - истраживање (master thesis research) and Мастер рад (master thesis). Electives totalling 12 ECTS from: Драматургија савременог филма; Методе у музичком образовању у дигиталном окружењу; Историја електроакустичке музике (History of Electroacoustic Music); Историја популарне музике (History of Popular Music); Продукција музике за нове медије (Production of Music for New Media); Музика у медијима (Music in Media). Curriculum published under 'Nastavni plan i program studijskog programa – Akreditacija 2023'.
programs.portfolioSpec: NO PORTFOLIO IS REQUIRED AT APPLICATION. The 2026/2027 competition text lists the documents to be submitted for all programmes — application form, undergraduate diploma, transcript of passed exams, ID, CV, and proof of payment of the entrance-exam fee — and then names portfolio requirements for only two programmes: 'Мастер професор у области уметности' (portfolio and motivation letter) and 'Мултимедијална режија' (portfolio and links to previous work). Muzička produkcija is not among them. Everything is submitted electronically by e-mail, one message per candidate, total attachments not exceeding 12 MB, with the study programme and module named in the subject line, to aunsprijemni.muzicki@uns.ac.rs. The content of the entrance exam itself is 'прописан Правилником Академије уметности о критеријумима и поступку избора кандидата' and the separate Informatori documents, neither of which is reproduced in the competition text — the exam content remains UNVERIFIED.
programs.auditionSpec: An entrance examination (пријемни испит) is compulsory and is held on site in Novi Sad between 7 and 13 October 2026 for the first round (23-28 October 2026 for the second). 'Пријемни испит представља јединствену целину' — the entrance exam constitutes a single unified whole. Its specific content for Muzička produkcija is set by the Academy's Pravilnik and the Informatori and is NOT published in the competition text — UNVERIFIED. Exam fee 12,000 RSD; enrolment cost for successful candidates 5,500 RSD.
programs.entryRequirements: NOW VERIFIED AND RESTRICTIVE. 2026/2027 competition text, verbatim: 'Студијски програм – Музичка продукција: завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању из уметничке области Музичка продукција, или сродан студијски програм (240 ЕСПБ)' — completed four-year undergraduate academic studies IN THE ARTISTIC FIELD OF MUSIC PRODUCTION, or a closely related study programme, worth 240 ECTS. Foreign nationals: 'Страни држављанин се може уписати на студијске програме мастер академских студија под истим условима као и домаћи држављанин' (same conditions as domestic candidates), but must additionally submit a formal recognition decision for the foreign undergraduate diploma, proof of health insurance, and proof of knowledge of Serbian.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — this is now confirmed as a hard block, reversing the prior 'UNVERIFIED'. The 2026/2027 competition requires a four-year (240 ECTS) undergraduate degree specifically 'из уметничке области Музичка продукција, или сродан студијски програм' — from the artistic field of Music Production, or a closely related programme. A BSc in Software Engineering is neither an artistic-field degree nor a programme related to Music Production, and a three-year Tunisian licence would additionally fall short of the 240 ECTS bar. Note that the Academy applies this kind of field restriction selectively and explicitly (for example Музичка педагогија lists six named acceptable undergraduate degrees plus differential exams), so the naming of a required field here is deliberate, not boilerplate.
programs.deadline: CURRENT CYCLE (October 2026 entry) — this is an OCTOBER intake, not September. 2026/2027 first round: electronic application 5 October 2026; entrance exam 7-13 October 2026; preliminary ranking list 15 October 2026; final list 20 October 2026; enrolment 20 October 2026. Second round: application 21 October 2026; exam 23-28 October 2026; preliminary list 30 October 2026; final list and enrolment 3 November 2026. For a 2027 start the equivalent competition will be published around June 2027 — NOT YET PUBLISHED.
programs.applicationOpens: The annual competition text is published in June (the 2026/2027 text was posted in June 2026); applications themselves open in early October. 2027/2028 dates unpublished.
programs.scholarship: None found. The programme carries 2 budget-financed (буџет) and 8 self-financing places, and budget places at Serbian public institutions go overwhelmingly to domestic candidates. No Tunisia-specific or general international award was identified.
programs.fundingLevel: None found for an international candidate; 2 domestic budget places exist at programme level.
programs.tuitionIntl: NOW VERIFIED. 2026/2027 competition text: tuition for foreign nationals ('Школарина за странце') is 1,800 EUR for the year across all master programmes at the Academy, including Музичка продукција. Domestic self-financing students pay 125,000 RSD. Additional costs: 12,000 RSD entrance-exam fee and 5,500 RSD enrolment fee. Doctoral level, for reference, is 2,400 EUR for foreigners.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED — no studio inventory published. The Academy has run a Sound Recording and Sound Design programme since 2003 within its audiovisual media provision and also runs a four-year undergraduate Music Production and Sound Design degree, so studio infrastructure clearly exists. Contact: Служба за студије и студентска питања, +381 21 422-177 ext. 2 / +381 21 422-176 ext. 2, aofarts@uns.ac.rs; music-department admissions e-mail aunsprijemni.muzicki@uns.ac.rs.
programs.fitNotes: The curriculum remains the closest match in the slice to what he actually wants — a one-year master literally called Music Production, with electives in the history of electroacoustic music, the history of popular music, and music production for new media — and at 1,800 EUR for the year it is cheap. But verification has closed the door rather than opened it. The 2026/2027 competition requires a four-year 240-ECTS undergraduate degree in the artistic field of Music Production or a closely related programme; a Tunisian software-engineering BSc does not qualify on either the field test or, if it is a three-year licence, the credit test. Add proof of Serbian-language competence as a documentary requirement for foreign applicants, an on-site October entrance exam of unpublished content, and no funding route, and there is no realistic path here for September 2027. Not worth an e-mail enquiry beyond a single question confirming whether the Academy would ever treat an engineering degree as 'сродан' — the wording makes that unlikely.
programs.verificationNotes: Confirmed against the official 2026/2027 competition text 'Tekst-Konkursa-Master-Doktorske-2026.pdf', published June 2026 and linked from https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/prijemni-muzicki-mas/. That document confirms the programme exists and is recruiting (2 budget + 8 self-financing = 10 places, listed under Интердисциплинарне студије), the verbatim field-and-credit entry restriction, the 1,800 EUR foreign-student tuition and 125,000 RSD domestic self-financing fee, the 12,000 RSD exam fee and 5,500 RSD enrolment fee, the full October 2026 two-round calendar, the electronic application procedure and document list, and the additional requirements for foreign nationals including proof of Serbian. Programme existence and curriculum cross-checked at https://akademija.uns.ac.rs/programi/ (Akreditacija 2023). Corrections to the prior record: entry requirements are published and restrictive, not unverified; acceptsNonMusic is NO, not unknown; tuition for foreigners is a confirmed 1,800 EUR; the intake is October, not September-October generally; quotas are 2+8, not unknown; and no portfolio is required at application. Remaining UNVERIFIED: the content of the entrance exam itself (set by the Academy's Pravilnik and Informatori, not reproduced in the competition text) and studio facilities. Source URL updated from the generic programme index to the music-department master admissions page that hosts the competition text.

programs.program: Müzik Teknolojisi Yüksek Lisans / Master of Science in Music Technology (MSc), thesis track
programs.university: Dokuz Eylül Üniversitesi (Dokuz Eylül University) — Güzel Sanatlar Enstitüsü / Graduate School of Fine Arts
programs.city: İzmir (Buca — DEÜ Tınaztepe Campus, Adatepe Mah. Doğuş Cad. No:209, 35390)
programs.institutionType: Public university (state university graduate school of fine arts)
programs.degree: Yüksek Lisans / 'Second Cycle (Master's) Degree with Thesis'; award: 'Master of Science in Music Technology (MSc)'
programs.focus: Recording/Engineering and academic music technology — acoustics, acoustic design, studio recording technique, electro-acoustics, media analysis. Research/thesis degree, NOT a music-production or DJ craft degree.
programs.language: Turkish — CONFIRMED (previously UNVERIFIED). The official DEU course catalogue lists 'Language of Instruction: Turkish' for every single course in the curriculum, including the thesis and seminar. The 2026-2027 entrance announcement adds: 'KESİN KAYIT ESNASINDA GEREKLİ OLAN EVRAKLARIN HEPSİ TÜRKÇE OLMAK ZORUNDADIR' (all documents required at final registration must be in Turkish).
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS / 4 semesters — CONFIRMED (previously UNVERIFIED). Catalogue: '2 years (120 ECTS), 4 Semesters, 16-18 weeks per semester'. Structure: at least 7 courses, 1 seminar, 1 specialisation course and thesis, minimum 21 local credits.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED from the official DEU course catalogue. Required: Methods of Scientific Research and Publication Ethics (GSE 5011, 5 ECTS); Guided Writing in Music Technology I (MZT 5011, 6 ECTS) and II (MZT 5028, 4 ECTS); Seminar (MZT 5096, 3 ECTS); Field of Study (MZT 5800, 6 ECTS); Thesis (MZT 5900, 54 ECTS). Electives, all in two-semester pairs: Media Analysis I/II, Studio Recording Techniques I/II, Acoustic Design I/II, CAD and Electro-acoustic Applications I/II. Note the shape: the thesis alone is 54 of 120 ECTS (45%), and there is no course in composition, arrangement, electronic-music production, DAW work, DJing or live electronics. Graduate profile is stated as 'sound recording, audio post production, arrangement, broadcast sound... and also work in the academic fields'.
programs.portfolioSpec: No portfolio is required or published. Entrance examination is 'Interview 100%' — an oral interview held at the Music Technology Studio covering 'Acoustics, Noise, Recording / Mixing / Mastering Technologies, Sound Systems'. Final ranking = Scientific Examination 50% + cumulative undergraduate GPA 50%. NEW FINDING not in the input: the DEU course catalogue additionally lists 'Acceptable score on ALES (Academic Personnel and Graduate Education Entrance Exam) or Equivalent GRE, GMAT score' plus 'Acceptable score on Language Proficiency Tests'. ALES is a Turkish-language national exam. The catalogue states an ALES waiver exists for 'second cycle graduate programs offered by the Conservatory and the departments of Fine Arts Faculty, where students are admitted only by the Artistic Aptitude Test' — it is NOT clearly established that Music Technology at the Graduate School of Fine Arts falls under that waiver, so ALES must be treated as a live requirement until the institute confirms otherwise.
programs.auditionSpec: Yes — mandatory on-site oral/technical interview in İzmir at the Music Technology Studio, weighting 100% of the entrance examination. Confirmed date for the current cycle: Müzik Teknolojisi master's entrance exam 25 August 2026 at 10:00. No remote option is published. There is no performance audition, but there is a technical viva conducted in Turkish.
programs.entryRequirements: Institute programme page: admission targets 'candidates who have earned their bachelor's degree in the field of music technology'; prerequisite is a bachelor's degree in music technology from a four-year undergraduate programme. Course catalogue wording is marginally softer: 'First Cycle Degree in the same or in related disciplines', plus transcript, ALES/GRE/GMAT and language proficiency scores. DECISIVE NEW FINDING from the official 2026-2027 entrance announcement: 'ÖĞRENCİ KAYNAĞINDA ESAS OLAN, BELİRLENEN KAYNAĞIN DİPLOMA VEYA GEÇİCİ MEZUNİYET BELGESİ AYNEN YAZMASIDIR' — the designated source field must appear VERBATIM on the diploma or provisional graduation certificate — and 'ÖĞRENCİ KAYNAĞINA UYGUN OLMAYAN, YA DA EKSİK / YANLIŞ GİRİŞ YAPMIŞ OLAN ADAYLAR SINAVLARA ALINMAYACAKTIR' (candidates not matching the student source will not be admitted to the examinations at all). Eligibility lists are published before the exam; ineligible candidates are screened out.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — and this is now confirmed as a hard, mechanically enforced block, not a soft preference. The published öğrenci kaynağı is a music-technology bachelor's degree; the 2026-2027 announcement states the designated source must be written verbatim on the diploma and that non-matching candidates are barred from sitting the exam. A BSc in Software Engineering fails on field, and a three-year BSc also fails the four-year requirement. The programme profile reinforces it: 'Masters in Music Technology program is primarily intended for students who hold a bachelor's degree in Music Technology'. The only conceivable route is a prior music-technology bachelor or a formal equivalence ruling from the Graduate School Executive Committee — neither is published as available.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. For SEPTEMBER 2027 entry nothing is published. Fully confirmed current cycle (2026-2027 fall, i.e. September 2026 entry, announcement published 06-07-2026): pre-registration opens 10 August 2026 10:00 and closes 14 August 2026 17:00; eligibility lists 19 August 2026 17:00; entrance exams 24-28 August 2026 (Music Technology 25 August 2026 10:00); results 31 August 2026 17:00; final registration 1-2 September 2026, reserves 3 September 2026. IMPORTANT PLANNING CORRECTION: this is a mid-August application window, NOT the October-February window assumed for European calls. Expect the 2027-2028 call around July 2027 with an August 2027 deadline.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Current cycle opened 10 August 2026 via ogrbasvuru.deu.edu.tr; foreign nationals (yabancı uyruklu) apply through a separate portal at debis.deu.edu.tr/OgrenciIsleri/Ogrenci/yabanciogrensbasvuru/. Expect an equivalent early-August opening for the 2027-2028 cycle, announced roughly one month earlier.
programs.scholarship: None found. No scholarship, waiver, stipend or assistantship is advertised on the Graduate School of Fine Arts pages for this programme. The input's speculation about Türkiye Bursları could not be checked (web-search budget exhausted) and remains UNVERIFIED — but it is moot, since Türkiye Bursları placement still requires the host programme's own eligibility rules to be met, and those exclude him.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED. No fee schedule is published on the Graduate School of Fine Arts site (gse.deu.edu.tr/en/tuition-fees/ returns 404) or on the DEU international office site (international.deu.edu.tr/en/tuition-fees/ returns 404). As a Turkish state university, fees for non-EU internationals are set annually by Council of Ministers decision and are typically low, but no figure could be confirmed from an official page.
programs.facilities: CORRECTED DOWNWARD — the input overstated this substantially. The official course catalogue states plainly: 'There are 2 academic members in the department. A recording studio and electronics lab is also available for practical purposes.' The institute page separately names a 'Music Technology Studio' used for teaching and for the entrance interview. Programme history per the catalogue: the Music Technology MASTER was founded in 2009, after the Music Technology BACHELOR was founded in 2008 — this contradicts the input's claims of a 2007 bachelor department and a 1991 'tonmeister' lineage, neither of which appears on the official pages verified here. Programme manager: Prof. Dr. Cihan Işıkhan; department head Prof. Dr. Feridun Öziş. No Atmos/immersive room, no console inventory and no industry-partnership claim is published.
programs.fitNotes: Keep on the list only as a documented NEGATIVE. Four independent blockers, each sufficient on its own: (1) the music-technology bachelor is enforced verbatim against the diploma, and non-matching candidates are refused entry to the exam; (2) 100% of the entrance mark is an on-site technical interview in İzmir, conducted in Turkish; (3) the entire curriculum is Turkish and all registration documents must be Turkish; (4) probable ALES requirement, a Turkish-language national exam. Separately, even if he were eligible the content is wrong for him: 54 of 120 ECTS is a research thesis, with acoustics and studio-engineering theory and zero production, electronic-music or DJ craft. Do not apply. Do not spend enquiry effort here either.
programs.verificationNotes: CONFIRMED from official sources: programme exists at master level and is currently live (2026-2027 fall intake announced 06-07-2026); degree title and thesis track; 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS; Turkish as sole language of instruction across all listed courses; full curriculum with course codes and ECTS; admission prerequisite of a music-technology bachelor; 'Interview 100%' at the Music Technology Studio covering acoustics, noise, recording/mixing/mastering and sound systems; final weighting 50% exam + 50% undergraduate GPA; quota 8 (+1 international student); full current-cycle application and exam calendar; the öğrenci kaynağı verbatim-diploma rule and the exclusion of non-matching candidates from the exam; Turkish-only registration documents; facilities (recording studio + electronics lab, 2 academic staff); programme founding dates 2009 (MSc) / 2008 (BSc). NOT CONFIRMED: non-EU tuition (both candidate fee pages 404); any scholarship or stipend; whether the ALES waiver extends to this programme. DISCREPANCY: the programme page states quota '8 (+1 International Student)' while the institute's English Quotas page — which is stale, headed '2020-2021 ACADEMIC YEAR' — lists Music Technology as 8 with no foreign-student allocation at all; treat the international place as uncertain and re-check when the 2027 quota table is issued. CORRECTIONS TO INPUT: language, duration and ECTS moved from UNVERIFIED to confirmed; facilities and institutional history downgraded (no 1991 tonmeister lineage or 2007 bachelor on any official page read); ALES requirement added; verbatim-diploma exclusion rule added; the August (not autumn/winter) application window added. programs.program: Аудиовизуален дизайн / Audiovisual Design — MA, in the specialty 'Музикални медийни технологии и тонрежисура' (Musical Media Technologies and Sound Direction)
programs.university: Софийски университет 'Св. Климент Охридски' / Sofia University 'St. Kliment Ohridski' — Факултет по науки за образованието и изкуствата (ФНОИ / Faculty of Educational Sciences and Arts), Department of Music and Multimedia Technologies
programs.institutionType: Public university
programs.degree: ОКС 'магистър' (MA, second cycle); professional qualification awarded: 'Multimedia Designer'
programs.focus: Sound Design; audiovisual/multimedia post-production; mastering; video editing and VFX. Post-production oriented rather than music-production oriented.
programs.language: Bulgarian for the main programme — CONFIRMED. IMPORTANT CORRECTION/UPGRADE: a separate English-taught variant genuinely exists and is confirmed — 'MA Programme Audiovisual Design (in English)', listed under the same specialty, same 2-semester length, same director (Assoc. Prof. Dr. Silvana Karagyozova). However it carries EXACTLY the same bachelor-field restriction, so the English option does not unlock it for him.
programs.durationEcts: 2 semesters (one academic year), full-time ('редовна форма'), fee-paying ('платено обучение') — CONFIRMED. Total ECTS is not published on either the Bulgarian or the English programme page; remains UNVERIFIED.
programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED. Theoretical grounding in digital audio and audiovisual technologies combined with specialised practical and elective courses: sound engineering/tonrezhisura, sound design, video editing, post-production and mastering, 2D compositing and visual effects. Graduates qualify as 'Multimedia Designer' and are placed as video editors in electronic media and as audiovisual specialists/editors for broadcast and online platforms. There is no composition, DAW-based music production, DJ practice or live-electronics content published.
programs.portfolioSpec: One independently developed, already-realised media project, presented and discussed at the admission interview, submitted in electronic format on a standard digital storage medium. CONFIRMED that no number of works, no duration limit, no file-format specification and no genre requirement is published on either the Bulgarian or the English page.
programs.auditionSpec: No live audition, no performance test and no written music-theory exam. Admission is by interview only, built around the presented realised media project. Whether the interview may be held remotely is not published — assume on-site in Sofia unless the department confirms otherwise.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor's degree with a diploma grade not lower than 'добър' (Good), from one of two qualifying professional fields ONLY, plus the interview on the presented media project. Verbatim eligibility wording used across this specialty: 'завършили бакалавърска степен от професионални направления 1.3 Педагогика на обучението по музика и 8.3 Музикално и танцово изкуство'.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: NO — confirmed independently on BOTH the Bulgarian page and the English-language page. Eligibility is closed to professional fields 1.3 Pedagogy of Music Education and 8.3 Music and Dance Arts. A Software Engineering BSc sits in a different professional field entirely and does not qualify. There is no published bridging, equivalence or 'for graduates of other specialties' variant of this programme — notable because the same faculty DOES publish explicit 'за завършили други специалности' (for graduates of other specialties) variants of several of its pedagogy and logopedics masters, and deliberately does not do so here.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Nothing is published for a September 2027 intake. Confirmed pattern: ФНОИ runs an annual 'Кандидатмагистърска кампания'; the campaign for academic year 2026-2027 was announced on 17.07.2026 and explicitly includes the 'Музикални медийни технологии и тонрежисура' specialty, but the announcement page as published lists only the programme set, with no dates. Historically a mid-to-late-summer campaign for a winter-semester (autumn) start. Expect the 2027-2028 call around July 2027.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Announced annually in mid-July for the coming academic year (the 2026-2027 campaign was posted 17 July 2026). Exact opening date not published on the pages verified.
programs.scholarship: None found. No scholarship, waiver or stipend attached to this programme is published, and the programme is explicitly designated fee-paying ('платено обучение'), which in the Bulgarian system means it is outside the state-subsidised places that carry stipend eligibility.
programs.fundingLevel: None found — programme is fee-paying by design
programs.tuitionIntl: Partially resolved. The official ФНОИ semester fee table for 2024-2025 lists 'Аудиовизуален дизайн — 1400 лв' per semester, i.e. approximately BGN 2,800 (~EUR 1,430) for the full two-semester programme. CAVEAT: that table is the standard domestic/EU schedule. Sofia University sets a separate, higher fee for non-EU foreign nationals under a national tariff, and that non-EU figure could NOT be located on any official page — treat the non-EU cost as UNVERIFIED and expect it to be materially higher than BGN 1,400 per semester.
programs.facilities: Partially verified. Run by the Катедра 'Музика и мултимедийни технологии', which maintains a dedicated block-2 facility (the faculty publishes a virtual walkthrough of it). No studio, console, monitoring or immersive-audio inventory is published; no industry partnerships, notable alumni or named staff beyond the director are listed. Programme director: Assoc. Prof. Dr. Silvana Karagyozova, skkaraguoz@uni-sofia.bg — CONFIRMED on both the Bulgarian and English pages.
programs.fitNotes: Keep as a documented NEGATIVE, and note that the input's proposed workaround is wrong. The subject matter (sound design, post-production, mastering) is genuinely appealing and the fee is low by European standards, but entry is formally closed to anyone outside professional fields 1.3 and 8.3, on both the Bulgarian and the English-taught versions. CRITICAL CORRECTION TO THE INPUT: there is NO programme called 'Audio Production and Mastering' (Аудиопродуциране и мастеринг) at this faculty — it does not exist. The specialty contains exactly four entries: Аудиовизуален дизайн, MA Audiovisual Design (in English), Аудиовизуална реставрация (Audiovisual Restoration) and Звуков дизайн (Sound Design). I verified Звуков дизайн directly and it imposes the IDENTICAL 1.3/8.3 restriction, so the advice to 'apply to the sibling programme instead' must be struck — the whole specialty is closed to him. The only remaining action, and a low-probability one, is a direct email to Assoc. Prof. Karagyozova asking whether a software-engineering bachelor plus a strong media project can be admitted by exception. Do not build the application plan around this faculty.

programs.program: Sveučilišni diplomski studij Montaža — usmjerenje Oblikovanje zvuka (MA Editing — Sound Design specialization)
programs.university: Academy of Dramatic Art (Akademija dramske umjetnosti, ADU), University of Zagreb
programs.institutionType: Public film/theatre academy within a public university
programs.degree: Sveučilišni diplomski studij (MA); title magistar/magistra montaže (mag. art. montaže)
programs.focus: Film & Game Sound; Sound Design; theatre, radio and performing-arts sound
programs.language: Croatian. Verbatim: 'Prijamni ispiti, kao i nastava na ADU održavaju se na hrvatskom jeziku pa se tako od svih kandidata očekuje poznavanje hrvatskog jezika u govoru i pismu.' ADU requires no certificate, but 'Povjerenstva Prijamnih ispita imaju pravo eliminirati kandidata iz natječajnog postupka ako ocjene da kandidat ne poznaje hrvatski jezik u mjeri koja je potrebna za uspješno studiranje.'
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 4 semesters / 120 ECTS (standard Croatian diplomski following a 180-ECTS prijediplomski). The ECTS total is not restated on the programme description page itself.
programs.whatYouStudy: Sound-design module within the Montaža master, described on the official programme page as training sound designers for film, television and multimedia. Practical, production-based: sound-design students realise the sound for ADU's own directing, cinematography and editing productions plus radio and stage work. Teaching staff are working sound recordists, sound editors, music editors, re-recording mixers and sound designers. ADU claims 'devedeset posto završenih studenata našlo je posao u struci' (90% of graduates work in the field).
programs.portfolioSpec: VERIFIED VERBATIM from ADU's official 'Specifični elementi i tijek Prijamnog ispita za diplomski studij Montaže - usmjerenje: OBLIKOVANJE ZVUKA'. Stage (A) submission: (1) životopis (CV); (2) motivacijsko pismo, 'do 2 kartice teksta' (up to 2 standard pages, ~3,600 characters); (3) 'audiovizualni rad za koji je pristupnik osmislio zvučnu sliku ili sudjelovao u njezinu stvaranju' — an audiovisual work whose sound picture the candidate conceived or helped create; (4) 'pisana analiza priloženog audiovizualnog rada s obrazloženjem koncepta zvučne slike te navedenim podrijetlom šumova, glazbe, zvučnih efekata i računalnih programa koji su korišteni u postprodukciji zvuka'. Verbatim eliminatory rule: 'Preduvjet za ulazak u provjere Prijamnog ispita je od strane Povjerenstva pozitivno ocijenjen pristupni audiovizualni rad kandidata.' The older DVD-in-3-copies format note is NOT in the current document — submission format now goes through the online Prijavnica.
programs.auditionSpec: YES — on-site, three-part, in Croatian, out of 100 points with an 80/100 pass threshold. Verbatim: '1. klauzurni rad (do 20 bodova) 2. izlaganje koncepta zvučne slike za zadani predložak (do 30 bodova) 3. razgovor s povjerenstvom (do 50 bodova)'; 'Bodovni prag prešli su pristupnici koji su ostvarili 80% ili više od ukupnog broja bodova.' The commission assesses 'znanje iz povijesti filma, povijesti filmske glazbe, povijesti glazbe te raspoznavanje glazbenih oblika, stilova i žanrova', assuming 'dobro poznavanje klasičnih djela svjetske i hrvatske kinematografije'. Recommended reading: Filmska enciklopedija (LZMK); Peterlić, Osnove teorije filma; Sonnenschein, Sound Design; Weis & Belton, Film Sound. ADU's own Montaža BA graduates who have passed all main artistic subjects are exempted from part 2 and auto-awarded its 30 points — an external candidate is not.
programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED verbatim from ADU's 'Glavne odredbe u postupcima Natječaja za upis u I. godinu sveučilišnih DIPLOMSKIH (MA) studija ADU': for Montaža the required prior level is 'trogodišnji sveučilišni ili stručni prijediplomski studij, 180 ECTS b.' — a three-year university OR professional undergraduate degree of 180 ECTS, with no field specified. Croatian-language competence expected in speech and writing (see language field). NEW FINDING: the commission may assign catch-up subjects, and 'Ako je skupna vrijednost zadanog programa iznosi 16 i više ECTS bodova, student mora upisati razlikovnu studijsku godinu' — 16+ ECTS of prescribed catch-up triggers a full paid bridging year before year 1.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES on paper — VERIFIED. The prerequisite table names only '180 ECTS' with no subject restriction, so a software-engineering BSc formally qualifies. Direct admission (izravni upis) is reserved for ADU's own Montaža BA students, so an external applicant simply sits the full entrance exam. The genuine filters are (a) the exam's assumed film/film-music/music-history knowledge, (b) Croatian, and (c) the possible razlikovna godina.
programs.deadline: 2026/27 CYCLE (Sept 2026 entry), NOT 2027 — confirm 2027 dates. VERIFIED from ADU's official 'MA - termini prijamnih ispita 26-27' document: Montaža application and submission of works '1.9. - 4.9.2026.'; Oblikovanje zvuka entrance exam '14.9.2026.' at ADU, Trg RH 5 (Soba 016 09:00–11:00, Soba 104 11:00–15:00). For a September 2027 start, expect an equivalent early-September 2027 window; also check whether an earlier foreign-national window (as ADU has run for Snimanje) applies to Montaža.
programs.applicationOpens: 2026/27 cycle opened 1 September 2026. 2027/28 dates not yet published (today is July 2026).
programs.scholarship: None found for non-EU applicants at ADU or University of Zagreb level.
programs.fundingLevel: Partial for EU/Croatian students only (first year of a first study at this level is fully exempt); non-EU pay prescribed tuition — UNVERIFIED amount
programs.tuitionIntl: VERIFIED for EU/Croatian: '1.278,00 €' per year, 'vrijednost jednog ECTS boda iznosi 21,30 €', payable in two instalments (start of winter and summer semesters), with the first year of a first study at this level fully exempt. For NON-EU, verbatim: 'Strani studenti koji ne dolaze iz zemalja članica EU, ili nisu uključeni u posebne sporazume, plaćaju školarinu koja je propisana' and 'participiraju u troškovima studija prema odlukama nadređenih tijela (Ministarstvo znanosti i obrazovanja, Sveučilište u Zagrebu)'. The actual non-EU figure is NOT published — request it from referada@adu.hr.
programs.facilities: No studio inventory published. The programme is production-based across ADU's three buildings (Trg Republike Hrvatske 5 and 8, Frankopanska 22): students do the sound for ADU's directing, cinematography and editing productions plus radio and stage work.
programs.fitNotes: Formally open to him — his degree level satisfies the stated 180-ECTS condition — and the entrance procedure is exceptionally well documented, which is rare. But three things block him now: everything (exam and teaching) is in Croatian and the commission can eliminate on language alone; the submission requires an audiovisual work whose sound picture he designed, which he does not have; and the interview tests film-history and music-history knowledge, not club production. The quota is max. 1 foreign student on the module. Realistic only after a year of building a picture-based sound portfolio plus serious Croatian.

programs.program: Master akademske studije Dramske i audiovizuelne umetnosti — modul Snimanje i dizajn zvuka (Sound Recording and Design)
programs.university: Faculty of Dramatic Arts (Fakultet dramskih umetnosti, FDU), University of Arts in Belgrade
programs.institutionType: Public film/drama faculty within the University of Arts
programs.focus: Recording / Engineering; Film & Game Sound; Sound Design; radio and theatre sound
programs.language: Serbian
programs.durationEcts: 1 academic year / 2 semesters / 60 ECTS — now CONFIRMED on the official MA programme page (previously inferred). Entry requires a prior degree of at least 240 ECTS.
programs.whatYouStudy: Core: 'Sound Recording and Design for FTV 7 and 8' — 'students perfect their knowledge in the field of sound recording and post-production for the most complex film and television structures'; and 'Sound Recording and Design for Theater and Radio 7 and 8', covering 'highly esthetic forms of radio creativity such as musique concrète' and complex stage sound design. Plus specialised courses in Classical Music Recording, Popular Music Recording and Sound Design in Multimedia, and elective theoretical/artistic courses. The programme emphasises developing a personal artistic voice and creative application of new sound technologies as a foundation for doctoral work. Full curriculum PDF: fdu.bg.ac.rs/uploads/attachment/strana/65/MAS_Snimanje_i_dizajn_zvuka.pdf
programs.portfolioSpec: VERIFIED. 'Portfolio — pregled do tri reprezentativna samostalna autorska rada u minimalnom ukupnom trajanju od 10 minuta' — up to THREE representative independent authored works, MINIMUM 10 MINUTES total, drawn from film sound design, television/streaming audio, radio production, live-event sound design, CREATIVE MUSIC PRODUCTION, or video-game / interactive audio design. Each project needs PDF documentation stating the candidate's role, an artistic explanation, technical equipment used, photos, and hyperlinks to the work on YouTube/Vimeo/SoundCloud. Technical formats: video H.264 MP4/MKV at 1920x1080; audio PCM WAV 44.1–192 kHz, 24-bit. Also required, all verified: application form; certified copy of the undergraduate diploma/uverenje with average grade; motivation letter 'maksimalne dužine dve stranice u A4 formatu sa proredom 1.5 i veličinom slova 12, latiničnim ili ćiriličnim pismom'; 'Biografiju sa navedenim profesionalnim radovima'; proof of the 8,000 RSD fee (žiro račun 840-32934845-84, poziv na broj 03); and 'Uverenje o zdravstvenom stanju čula sluha sa audiogramom izdatim od zvanične specijalizovane lekarske ustanove ili ordinacije, ne starijim od 3 (tri) meseca' — a hearing certificate WITH AUDIOGRAM, under 3 months old.
programs.auditionSpec: YES — on-site, in Serbian, three parts, and NEWLY CONFIRMED to include an ELIMINATORY test: (1) 'Provere muzikalnosti i znanja iz akustike i audio-tehnike (eliminacioni deo)' — musicality plus acoustics and audio-engineering knowledge, eliminatory; (2) realisation and defence of a practical work produced during the exam; (3) defence of the submitted portfolio work plus an interview on artistic potential. Scoring out of 100: prior undergraduate success (GPA × 3) up to 30 points; exam up to 70, broken down as musicality/acoustics 5, portfolio work 10, practical work 15, interview/creative potential 40. Budget-financed admission requires ≥80 points; self-financed ≥60.
programs.entryRequirements: Completed undergraduate academic studies of AT LEAST 240 ECTS, or graduate studies under pre-Bologna regulations. Serbian-language instruction and examination. Application fee 8,000 RSD.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CONFLICTING OFFICIAL WORDING — the real answer is 'the degree LENGTH blocks him, not the subject.' The 2026/27 konkurs and the MA programme page state only '240 ECTS', naming no field. But the department page still carries: 'A precondition for enrolling M.A. Studies are previously completed undergraduate artistic academic studies.' So: subject-wise the konkurs is field-neutral; length-wise a 3-year/180-ECTS Tunisian licence fails outright. Get the faculty's written position on both points before doing anything else.
programs.deadline: 2026/27 CYCLE, NOT 2027 — confirm new date. VERIFIED: candidate registration 7 and 8 October 2026, 09:00–14:00 at the Faculty Secretariat; entrance exam Monday–Tuesday 12 and 13 October 2026 at 09:00 in classroom KS1. Expect an equivalent early-October 2027 window for a 2027/28 start — note this is an OCTOBER intake, not September.
programs.applicationOpens: 2026/27 cycle: 7 October 2026. 2027/28 dates not yet published.
programs.scholarship: None found for foreign nationals. Budget-financed (tuition-free) places exist but require ≥80/100 and in practice go to domestic candidates.
programs.fundingLevel: None found for a non-EU foreign applicant
programs.tuitionIntl: VERIFIED for 2026/27, Snimanje i dizajn zvuka: 440,000 RSD for Serbian citizens; 550,000 RSD for foreign students from neighbouring countries; 660,000 RSD for other foreign students (≈€5,600). Application fee 8,000 RSD.
programs.facilities: No studio inventory published. The faculty references a 'Theater and Radio Studio' and a 'Film and television studio' but gives no equipment detail. Strong regional reputation as the main Serbian film-sound school; 8 of the department's 11 teachers are its own graduates working in the industry.
programs.fitNotes: The portfolio spec is unusually generous — 'creative music production' and 'video game / interactive audio design' are explicitly acceptable domains, so his own tracks could legitimately count toward the 10-minute minimum. But four things stand against him: the 240-ECTS floor (a 3-year Tunisian licence fails), Serbian-language teaching and examination, a newly confirmed ELIMINATORY musicality-plus-acoustics test he would sit cold, and a mandatory audiogram. Roughly €5,600/year with no funding route for a foreigner. Confirm eligibility by e-mail before investing effort; if refused, Novi Sad is the fallback.
programs.verificationNotes: Re-verified against the official 2026/27 master konkurs page (fdu.bg.ac.rs/sr-lat/upis/master-studije), the MA programme page (fdu.bg.ac.rs/en/studies/m-a-studies/sound-recording-and-design, confirming 1 year / 60 ECTS and the 240-ECTS condition), and the department page (fdu.bg.ac.rs/en/departments/department-of-sound-recording-and-design, which is where the 'artistic academic studies' sentence lives). CORRECTIONS vs. prior report: (a) the konkurs itself imposes NO artistic-field restriction — only 240 ECTS — so the prior 'PROBABLY NOT, fails on two counts' overstated the subject barrier while understating the length barrier; (b) the entrance exam contains an eliminatory musicality/acoustics/audio-technique component that the prior report omitted entirely; (c) 60 ECTS is now confirmed, not inferred. Audiogram, motivation-letter format, portfolio spec, tuition tiers and October dates all confirmed verbatim.

programs.program: Master akademske studije Audiovizuelni mediji — modul Dizajn zvuka (Sound Design)
programs.university: Academy of Arts, University of Novi Sad (Akademija umetnosti, Univerzitet u Novom Sadu)
programs.institutionType: Public art academy within a public university
programs.degree: Master akademske studije; professional title 'Мастер аудиовизуелни уметник' (Master audiovisual artist)
programs.focus: Sound Design; Film & Game Sound; Immersive / interactive audio
programs.language: Serbian. Foreign applicants must supply 'доказ о познавању српског језика' (proof of Serbian-language knowledge) as part of the application.
programs.durationEcts: 1 year / 60 ECTS — confirmed on the official curriculum sheet (mas-dizajn-zvuka.pdf): 'Дужина трајања студија: 1 година; Обим студија изражен у ЕСПБ бодовима: 60'.
programs.whatYouStudy: VERIFIED from the official curriculum sheet. Core: Супервизија звука (Sound Supervision, 2+4 weekly hours — by far the heaviest course); Драматургија савременог филма; Режија - анализа и синтеза; Авангардни филм; Завршни рад and Завршни рад - истраживање. Electives, choose 12 ECTS: Аудиовизуелна артикулација; Звук у филмској уметности; Постпродукција филмске слике; Светлосна артикулација у визуелним медијима; Продукција музике за нове медије (Production of Music for New Media); Филмска и телевизијска продукција; Имерзивне игре (Immersive Games); Видео арт. Note the sibling MAS Музичка продукција (also 1 year / 60 ECTS) is far closer to club/electronic production — its courses include Музичка продукција, Звук и музика на филму, Савремене тенденције у музичкој продукцији 1 and 2, Историја електроакустичке музике and Историја популарне музике — but its entry is restricted to a four-year degree in the artistic field Музичка продукција or a cognate programme, so it is closed to him.
programs.portfolioSpec: STILL UNPUBLISHED. The 2026 konkurs states only: 'Програм пријемних испита прописан је Правилником Академије уметности о критеријумима и поступку избора кандидата за упис на мастер академске студије и Информаторима о програмским садржајима пријемних испита'. The Academy publishes Informator PDFs for Pozorišni oblici, Dizajn video igara, Kreiranje serija and Muzička produkcija — but NOT for Dizajn zvuka. Request the Informator for Dizajn zvuka directly from aofarts@uns.ac.rs.
programs.auditionSpec: An entrance exam (пријемни испит) is compulsory and on-site — 'У прву годину мастер академских студија може се уписати лице које положи пријемни испит' — held 07–13 October 2026 (first round) or 23–28 October 2026 (second round). Its content for Dizajn zvuka is not published. Scoring context from the konkurs: a threshold of at least 36 of a possible 70 exam points is applied.
programs.entryRequirements: VERIFIED verbatim: 'Модул Дизајн звука: завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању' — completed FOUR-YEAR undergraduate academic studies, i.e. the general 240-ECTS floor, with NO artistic-field restriction. Foreign nationals: 'Страни држављанин се може уписати на студијске програме мастер академских студија под истим условима као и домаћи држављанин', submitting additionally (1) решење о извршеном признавању стране дипломе (formal recognition of the foreign degree), (2) доказ о здравственом осигурању, (3) доказ о познавању српског језика. Places for Dizajn zvuka 2026/27: 4 budget + 1 self-financing = 5 total.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: YES on subject — this is the key correction. The 2026 konkurs restricts the sibling modules by field (Дизајн светла requires the artistic field Дизајн светла 'или неки сродан студијски програм'; Анимација и визуелни ефекти likewise; Мултимедијална режија requires Режија) but for Дизајн звука it requires ONLY 'завршене основне академске студије у четворогодишњем трајању'. No artistic or musical field is named. The binding constraint is therefore LENGTH (four-year / 240 ECTS), not subject — a 3-year Tunisian licence would fail, a 4-year or 5-year engineering degree would satisfy it.

programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering
programs.whatYouStudy: 120 ECTS covering film sound as a complete craft: effects recording, audio drama, music in narrative, on-set sound recording and post-production sound design, plus joint departmental film studies and a thesis. Teaching is 'learning by doing' in small groups on ELO's own productions. CONFIRMED on the official page: 120 ECTS and the MA structure. programs.entryRequirements: A relevant Bachelor's degree. The official page adds the key sentence: 'Applicants without a previous degree or with a degree from another field are taken into account.' English proficiency evidence required (IELTS/TOEFL or equivalent) — he has NOT taken a test yet and must book one well before the December application window.

programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED verbatim on the official page: a MAXIMUM OF THREE work samples, with a COMBINED viewing time of 30 MINUTES OR LESS, supplied as downloadable/streaming links (Vimeo, YouTube or equivalent). Phase I is a document and portfolio review (portfolio, prior studies, motivation letter, work experience) with no attendance required. Phase II is an interview for shortlisted candidates; some applicants are given 1-2 assignments to submit before the interview. Interview invitations are sent a MINIMUM OF 7 DAYS in advance. (Correction to prior draft: the page specifies 7 days' notice, not 'about a week of preparation time'.)

programs.program: Sound Design for Film and Television (MFA)
programs.university: National Film and Television School (NFTS)
programs.durationEcts: 2 years full-time, in person at the main campus. ECTS not published (UK MFA).
programs.institutionType: Film school (independent postgraduate national film school; CILECT/GEECT member)
programs.language: English
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound; Sound Design; Recording/Engineering; Immersive Audio
programs.whatYouStudy: Craft-first and entirely project-based: dialogue editing, atmospheres, Foley, ADR, designed effects, post-production technology and storytelling through sound. Students move from foundational workshops onto NFTS graduation films across fiction, documentary, animation, games and TV, working with NFTS directors, editors, composers and producers on real productions. Confirmed facilities used daily: Apple workstations running Pro Tools with industry plugins, PSI LCR/5.1 monitoring and Avid S1 mix controllers; Dolby-approved dubbing theatres with Avid S6 and S4 consoles and JBL monitoring; a Dolby Atmos dubbing theatre in the original Anvil recording studio; and a dedicated music recording studio used for live music and Foley.
programs.entryRequirements: No fixed qualification list, and a degree is NOT mandatory. Official wording: 'While many applicants will have a degree from a British or overseas university, we will consider applicants who do not have a degree if they have an impressive portfolio, a creative track record or an alternative qualification.' International applicants must additionally satisfy UK student-visa and English-language requirements — he has NOT yet taken IELTS, so this must be booked well ahead.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes. The course explicitly seeks 'a group of students with diverse and varied backgrounds' and states 'There is no "typical" student or perfect candidate.' No music, sound or film degree is required. CORRECTION to prior draft: the phrase 'background may be in the arts or other media' could NOT be located on the current page — use the two confirmed quotes above instead.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED: two items, both submitted as VIMEO LINKS. (1) A custom sound-design exercise — you download a video file supplied with the application form and return your complete sound design for it. (2) One further piece — preferably a short film you worked on (MAXIMUM 10 MINUTES), or an audio-only work.
programs.auditionSpec: Interview for shortlisted applicants, followed by a FIVE-DAY selection workshop held in person at the Beaconsfield campus, carrying a £150 workshop fee. A £500 non-refundable deposit is payable on confirming a place. Physical attendance in the UK is unavoidable — budget for a visa and travel on top of tuition.

programs.institutionType: Public university of the arts incorporating the former Dramatiska Institutet film school (GEECT member)

Research-preparatory as well as practice-based — expect a heavier artistic-research component than at NFTS or Filmakademie. The admission portfolio asks for an 'artistic research question', which confirms how central that framing is.
programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED from the Swedish page: general eligibility for advanced-level (avancerad nivå) study; a relevant bachelor's degree in film/media or equivalent, including at least 15 ECTS plus a thesis/degree project in a related field from a film-and-media bachelor programme; Swedish 1, 2 and 3 and English 6; AND a passed artistic assessment of the submitted work samples. A BSc in Software Engineering does not satisfy that on paper. The reell kompetens clause is a real route and is not subject-blind in his favour — it would require him to evidence equivalent film-sound competence he does not yet have. Separately, Svenska 1, 2 och 3 is a formal eligibility requirement he cannot meet.
programs.portfolioSpec: EXACT, from the official Swedish programme page (submitted via the Varbi system): TWO clips of 4–5 MINUTES EACH in which you carried INDEPENDENT ARTISTIC RESPONSIBILITY for the sound design — maximum 150 MB per file, accepted formats mov, mp4, avi, mp3, wav, m4a, aiff; a MOTIVATION LETTER of maximum 4,000 characters; a CV; an ARTISTIC RESEARCH QUESTION of maximum 4,000 characters; a PROCESS DESCRIPTION of maximum 4,000 characters; and a SIGNED VERIFICATION STATEMENT from a collaborator on the submitted project confirming your role. This replaces the previous 'UNVERIFIED' entry.
programs.auditionSpec: The published selection instrument is the artistic assessment of the work samples above ("godkänd konstnärlig prövning"). No separate live audition or on-site test is published on either the Swedish or English page — an interview stage for shortlisted candidates is common at SKH but is NOT published for this programme, so treat it as unconfirmed rather than absent.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 December 2026 — CONFIRMED as the next cycle's opening on the Swedish page.
programs.deadline: 15 January 2027, for a START IN AUTUMN 2027. This is a genuinely current, published date and matches his target intake exactly. The programme runs on a BIENNIAL cycle (the present cohort was admitted for autumn 2025 and runs to June 2027), so autumn 2027 is a real intake — but if he misses it the next is autumn 2029. Non-EU/EEA applicants also pay a non-refundable SEK 900 application fee via universityadmissions.se.

programs.entryRequirements: CONFIRMED from MA_GlavneOdredbe and the MA application-method document: a completed three-year undergraduate degree worth 180 ECTS (or a certificate showing no more than 30 ECTS still outstanding); admission is by competitive entrance exam (prijamni ispit) unless the applicant qualifies for direct admission (izravni upis), which is reserved for graduates of ADU's own corresponding BA programmes (Gluma, Dramaturgija, Snimanje, Montaža). Applicants holding a foreign degree must FIRST obtain a "Rješenje o akademskom priznavanju inozemnih visokoškolskih kvalifikacija" (academic recognition decision) from the University of Zagreb before applying — an extra multi-week step for a Tunisian diploma. Application requires the form, diploma + diploma supplement, ID scan, CV, programme-specific portfolio, OIB (Croatian tax number) confirmation for foreign nationals, and proof of a EUR 65 exam fee (IBAN HR4223900011100013453). Materials go to the department email with referada@adu.hr in copy; an exam code is emailed back within 24 h.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: CHECK — formally possible, practically penalised. The general provisions set only "a completed three-year undergraduate degree with 180 ECTS" as the baseline for the Montaža/Oblikovanje zvuka group (university OR professional bachelor accepted; only Theatre Directing, Acting and Dramaturgy demand a university-level degree). But the same document states that students without the corresponding undergraduate credential may be assigned 15+ ECTS of prerequisite (razlikovni) courses, potentially a FULL REMEDIAL YEAR before starting graduate coursework. In addition, applicants who completed all core editing and sound courses of ADU's own BA are automatically credited the 30-point presentation component of the entrance exam — an outside applicant must earn those points in competition. No wording anywhere accepts or addresses an engineering/computer-science background specifically.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED (MA_PRIJAMNI_MONT_OBZV). Candidates must submit: (1) a curriculum vitae; (2) a motivational letter, "motivacijsko pismo (do 2 kartice teksta)" — up to two standard pages; (3) an AUDIOVISUAL WORK on which the applicant created or co-created the sound design; (4) a WRITTEN ANALYSIS of that work explaining the sound concept, including the sources of the sounds, the music and effects used, and the software used. No number-of-works or duration limit is stated beyond this.
programs.auditionSpec: YES — a live, on-site, three-part entrance exam in Zagreb, conducted in Croatian, with photo ID required. Components: (a) an in-class practical assignment, up to 20 points; (b) presentation of a sound concept for a given template/clip, up to 30 points (automatically credited to graduates of ADU's own BA editing/sound courses); (c) an interview with the committee, up to 50 points. Total 100. The pass mark is high: "80 ili više bodova" (80 or more points) are required to pass. The interview tests knowledge of film history, film-music history, general music history, and recognition of musical forms and genres.

M2 Game Audio Technologies (middleware Wwise and FMOD, game engines Unity and Unreal, recording, sound design technique, mixing, profiling). M3 Research and Critical Reflection (5,000-word report). M4 Interactive Audio (vehicle sounds for racing games, advanced loop editing, personal style). M5 3D Audio Environments (3D world implementation, dynamic mixing, VR/AR audio). M6 one elective from FMOD / Unreal & Blueprint / Musical Sound Design / Audio Post-Production / Career Development for Sound Designers — page warns electives are "provisional", "subject to change" and need minimum enrolment. The Wwise/FMOD/Unity/Unreal stack is where his software-engineering background converts directly into an advantage. Against it: zero funding for a non-UK student, £13,500 self-pay and rising after the 2026 fee freeze lapses, and — most important for HIS actual goal — it is online-only. programs.focus: Music Production + Sound Design + Electronic Music + Composition, with an explicit games and interactive-installation strand
programs.institutionType: Conservatory / university of the arts (publicly funded Dutch hogeschool)
programs.language: Page lists the programme as "Engels|Nederlands". CLARIFICATION CONFIRMED: lessons are taught in English, but roughly two-thirds of students are Dutch, so the day-to-day social and studio language will often be Dutch. His Arabic/French/English profile covers the teaching language; the informal environment is the risk.
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED. The page publishes no non-EEA figure and routes applicants to HKU's "Collegegeldwizard" fee calculator; HKU's tuition page could not be retrieved (404 on the URLs tried). The page distinguishes a statutory rate (wettelijk collegegeld, EEA only) from an institutional rate (instellingstarief) that applies to non-EEA students and is typically several times higher. Get a written quote before committing. The page also notes a laptop or computer is a required additional cost.
programs.scholarship: Holland Scholarship — named on the page as available to talented international candidates. This is a Dutch Ministry of Education scheme co-funded by institutions and is restricted to non-EEA students, so a Tunisian national is in scope. It is competitive and awarded independently of when in the round he applies.
programs.stipend: UNVERIFIED. The Holland Scholarship is normally a one-off first-year contribution (commonly around €5,000) rather than a full waiver, and carries no monthly stipend or housing. The amount is not stated on the HKU page — confirm with HKU. Against a likely non-EEA institutional fee, this would leave a large gap.
programs.entryRequirements: A completed bachelor "in een relevante richting" (in a relevant field), or equivalent foreign qualifications plus professional experience. Application dossier: portfolio, motivation letter, study plan and CV. Two-round selection: portfolio/dossier review, then an interview. English or Dutch language-test requirements are NOT stated on the page — UNVERIFIED.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — possible in principle, demanding in practice. Verbatim: "The academy can make an exception for candidates without a Bachelor of Music, but only in case of exceptional talent and a steady track record." So a BSc Software Engineering is not a formal bar, but he would be admitted on demonstrated musical output rather than on the degree. "A steady track record" is the operative phrase and it is precisely what he does not yet have — no releases, no professional credits, no performance history.
programs.portfolioSpec: A portfolio is required alongside a motivation letter, study plan and CV. The programme deliberately de-emphasises equipment: what is assessed is the creative musical work achieved with whatever technology the candidate has access to, together with documented, explainable creative and technical decision-making. No minimum number of works, duration or file format is published. Practical reading: quantity of gear will not help him; a small body of finished, self-directed work he can justify decision-by-decision will.
programs.auditionSpec: CORRECTION — this was previously unverified and is now confirmed. There is no conservatory-style live performance audition, but selection is a TWO-ROUND process: portfolio and dossier review, followed by an ONLINE INTERVIEW assessing motivation and the submitted materials. The online format is a genuine advantage — no travel to the Netherlands is required to be assessed.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 October 2026 (registration opens 1 October for the 2027-2028 intake). This is the single most actionable, forward-looking date in the slice and it lines up exactly with his September 2027 target. Recheck the page in September 2026 to confirm the year label before relying on it.
programs.deadline: Four upload deadlines are published for the 2027-2028 round: 24 November, 12 January, 16 February and 13 April. Treat the exact days as provisional until the 1 October 2026 opening goes live — these repeat the prior cycle's pattern almost exactly, so confirm rather than assume. Strategy: aim for the FIRST round (late November 2026), because Dutch art-school places and scholarship budgets deplete across successive rounds.
programs.whatYouStudy: One master with four non-binding strands the student combines: Music Technology; Music Production (live, recorded, media, games, interactive installations); Sound Design (film, theatre, games); and Composition. Because the strands are non-binding he can weight the degree toward electronic/club production while taking the games and interactive-installation work where his coding is an asset. A detailed module-by-module list is NOT published — UNVERIFIED.
programs.facilities: UNVERIFIED on the programme page — no studios, consoles or immersive rooms are described. Contextual note (not from this page): HKU's School of Music and Technology also runs bachelor programmes in Audio Design, Music Design for Games and Interaction, Composition and Music Production, and Composition Electronic Music, so the master sits on a deep music-technology faculty — but the specific infrastructure must be confirmed at an open day or by email.
programs.fitNotes: On paper the closest match in this slice to what he actually wants — a Master of Music covering music production, electronic composition, sound design AND games, at a Dutch conservatory, in a country with a serious electronic-music industry, assessed by portfolio plus an ONLINE interview, with applications opening 1 October 2026 precisely on his timeline. Two hard obstacles. First, entry without a Bachelor of Music requires "exceptional talent and a steady track record", which is a higher bar than any other entry here and one he cannot meet today — the next twelve months would have to produce real, released, defensible work. Second, non-EEA tuition is unpublished and likely high, with the Holland Scholarship covering only a fraction. Verdict: worth preparing for hard, but he should not treat it as a safe bet.

programs.auditionSpec: None. No live audition, no on-site test, and no interview is mentioned in the admissions documentation. Assessment is transcript + personal statement + portfolio links, all submitted remotely.
programs.applicationOpens: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. Glasgow normally opens taught-master applications around October for the following September, but the 2027-entry opening is not published — recheck from October 2026.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. The page currently shows 24 August 2026 for both International & EU and Home applicants — that is the September 2026 entry deadline, NOT his.
