programs.whatYouStudy: Semester 1 core: Sound Shaping and Design; Creative Sound Recording; Thinking Through Sound and Media. Semester 2 core: Audiovisual Composition; Creative Sound & Media Performance. One optional course from a College-wide list including Sonic Arts: Sound for Narrative Film, Music Cities, Popular Music History and others. It is the only entry that explicitly names "computing" as an accepted bachelor, needs no audition or interview, asks for only two or three portfolio pieces, gives verified access to real studios including an ambisonic room, sits in a strong UK music city, and has a full-tuition-waiver route in principle. Three caveats keep it out of the top rating. The African Excellence Award's eligibility for Tunisia is unconfirmed and everything financial hinges on it — without a waiver the cost is £26,460 plus Glasgow living costs. He must sit IELTS and clear 6.5 with no band below 6.0. And the curriculum rewards his creative and immersive-audio development rather than his programming — there is no middleware teaching at all, and nothing that directly serves a DJ career.

programs.institutionType: Public university, internationally recognised as the leading UK games university
programs.language: English
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED. The page confirms that separate Scottish, rest-of-UK and international rates exist but routes to a fees page that could not be retrieved (404 on the URLs tried).

programs.entryRequirements: "Upper Second Class Honours degree (or equivalent) at undergraduate level in an appropriate discipline and/or a Master's degree." The degree must include an independent research component evidenced on the transcript — a dissertation, project or thesis. English is notably demanding for a research degree: IELTS Academic 7.0 overall with a minimum of 6.5 in every component (alternatives: TOEFL iBT 95 with 21 per component; PTE Academic 67 with 61 per component; CAE/CPE 185 with 176 per component). Application requires transcripts, references and a research proposal of roughly 6-8 pages including references, covering title, abstract, introduction/background, hypotheses/objectives, methodology, dissemination pathways, ethical considerations, conclusions, references, resource requirements and personal background.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes in principle — the requirement is "an appropriate discipline" with an evidenced independent research component, and the department's research strengths are explicitly technical (synthesis, game-engine audio integration, VR/AR). A software-engineering BSc with a final-year project would satisfy the letter of the requirement. BUT this is academic for him: see the blocker below.
programs.portfolioSpec: No creative portfolio is required at all. The decisive submission is a RESEARCH PROPOSAL of approximately 6-8 pages including references, with the full section structure listed under entry requirements. This is a fundamentally different application from every other entry in this slice — it rewards research design and academic writing, not finished tracks or sound-design reels.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition and no on-site test. No interview is explicitly mentioned on the page, though research admissions normally involve supervisor contact.
programs.applicationOpens: Rolling — three entry points per year (February, June and October) rather than a single annual round.
programs.deadline: Standing deadlines by entry point, PRIOR CYCLE - confirm they still apply for 2027: February entry 15 December (30 November for visa applicants); June entry 30 April (31 March for visa applicants); October entry 31 August (31 July for visa applicants). Note the visa-applicant deadline is the one that binds him, and it is always the earlier of the pair.
programs.whatYouStudy: Supervised independent research, practical or theoretical, into sound and music for interactive media — games, immersive experiences and installations. Confirmed departmental strengths: "synthesis, integration of dynamic audio within game engines and technologies, and exploration of sound design within virtual and augmented reality". There is no taught module list; the shape of the degree is whatever his own research proposal defines. No specific middleware (Wwise, FMOD) is named on the page.
programs.facilities: Confirmed: the Emergent Technology Centre with an adjacent recording studio, specialist audio labs, recording equipment and professional software access.
programs.fitNotes: BLOCKED for him as published. Abertay is the obvious name in UK game audio and its technical research strengths map almost perfectly onto a programmer's skills — but the page carries an explicit and decisive restriction: "we are not accepting international applications to Masters by Research/MPhil due to the number of CAS available to support international students." As a Tunisian national he therefore cannot apply to the MSc by Research or the MPhil at all. Only the PhD route remains open, and that is a three-to-four-year research commitment that is the wrong instrument entirely for someone who wants hands-on production craft and a DJ career. Layered on top: IELTS 7.0 with 6.5 in every band is a high bar he has not attempted, the application is a research proposal rather than music, and no funding open to him was found. Worth monitoring in case the CAS restriction lifts for 2027, but he should not build any part of his plan around it.

programs.durationEcts: CONFIRMED: "One full academic year" = three semesters (fall, spring, summer). Credits confirmed on the programme page: minimum "32 or 33 with internship", maximum "37 or 38 with internship" US credits. ECTS equivalence is NOT published — UNVERIFIED. programs.language: English (instruction and all application materials; the CV must be "in English"). Not stated as a bullet on the programme page but confirmed by the English-proficiency requirements and by materials being required in English.
programs.tuitionIntl: CONFIRMED for 2026/27 on valencia.berklee.edu/tuition-fees-payment/tuition-and-related-costs-for-graduate-programs: Tuition USD 50,430; Comprehensive Fee USD 1,600; MPTI software bundle USD 800; application fee USD 150 (waived for Berklee alumni); non-refundable tuition deposit USD 2,500. Mandatory Berklee Student Health Insurance Plan (cost not on this page) unless comparable coverage proven. Estimated indirect costs: housing USD 10,000–12,000; laptop USD 3,000 (may be waived); books USD 300–800; local transport USD 300–600; personal USD 1,000. Direct charges therefore ≈ USD 52,980 before living costs.
programs.scholarship: CONFIRMED on valencia.berklee.edu/scholarships-financial-aid/scholarships-for-graduate-programs. No nationality restriction is stated on any of these, so a Tunisian is eligible: (1) Berklee General Scholarship — eligibility "All master's degree applicants", "Amount varies, multiple awards", automatic via the scholarship application. (2) Berklee Valencia Diversity Scholarship — "Up to 50 percent of the tuition", up to four awardees per academic year, requires a separate submission (video max 3 minutes OR 500-word essay) to scholarshipsvalencia@berklee.edu. (3) Berklee Outstanding Women Scholarship with Mentorship (MPTI-specific) — "up to 70 percent of tuition fees, plus mentorship sessions", one recipient, but restricted to women. Not applicable to a male applicant. Also exist but NOT applicable to him: Berklee Alumni Scholarship (USD 18,000, alumni only), Global Partners Scholarship (USD 18,000, partner-school students only), CACSA–Palau de les Arts (Valencian students only). Total of all Berklee awards cannot exceed 90 percent of tuition. Scholarship deadlines: 15 November (early), 1 February (regular).
programs.fundingLevel: Partial. Realistic best case for him is the General Scholarship plus the Diversity Scholarship, capped in aggregate at 90% of tuition. No stipend, no living support, and the 90% cap is a ceiling, not an expectation.
programs.stipend: Tuition reduction only. No stipend, no housing, no living allowance. Scholarships cannot be applied to the USD 2,500 deposit, the comprehensive fee, the software bundle or insurance.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree. Entrance-requirements page: "Applicants should possess a bachelor's degree in music while demonstrating technological proficiency, musical excellence in performance and/or composition, leadership, motivation, intellectual curiosity, and promise of great achievement in their area of study." Ideal candidate: "Excellent musicality; Facility with technology; Success in both artistic and academic settings; A strong work ethic, including prior accomplishment; and The motivation to make massive progress in one year." ENGLISH (CONFIRMED, and this is the HIGH tier that applies to MPTI — Contemporary Performance is the only programme on the lower tier): IELTS Academic 7.5; TOEFL iBT 100 (tests before 21 Jan 2026) or the new TOEFL score of 5; Duolingo 130; Cambridge CAE or higher. Waived if the bachelor's was completed at an English-speaking university — a Tunisian BSc will NOT trigger this waiver. Other required items (CONFIRMED): online application + USD 150 fee; statement of purpose "between 400 and 500 words"; résumé/CV in English; ONE letter of recommendation from a professor or supervisor who can speak to musical strengths; official transcripts. Non-US/Canada degrees require a course-by-course credential evaluation with GPA conversion via an approved agency (SpanTran, ECE) — the site warns this "takes several weeks".
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, conditionally — CONFIRMED in substance. The official entrance-requirements page states the expectation is a bachelor's degree in music, and that non-music bachelor's degrees are acceptable where the applicant demonstrates substantial musical competency. CAUTION: the exact sentence "Bachelor's degrees in other disciplines will be considered, provided the student demonstrates a high degree of musicianship" could not be reproduced verbatim from the page as rendered, so treat the wording as paraphrased-confirmed rather than a verified quote. Practical effect for him: an SMU MedTech software-engineering BSc is admissible on paper, but the entire burden of proof shifts to the portfolio and the interview — and the IELTS 7.5 bar applies in full.
programs.portfolioSpec: CONFIRMED on the How to Apply page, MPTI-specific: (a) a self-produced video, MAXIMUM 3 MINUTES, describing THREE projects you are passionate about and would like to develop as your Culminating Experience (thesis) — must be projects not already completed; (b) THREE recorded musical projects (audio or video files of your work), each with a short description of your role; (c) corresponding scores are OPTIONAL. FORMAT RULES: all programme-specific materials organised in ONE PDF with links properly embedded and sections clearly labelled; links must be public or unlisted; "We will not download materials" — no WeTransfer, Dropbox, Google Drive or similar.
programs.auditionSpec: NO AUDITION — CONFIRMED verbatim on the Auditions page: "Selected contemporary performance applicants will be required to complete both an audition and interview." All other master's applicants who advance do an INTERVIEW ONLY. Interviews are conducted ONLINE, scheduled in Central European Time, and are by invitation only after the Graduate Board of Admissions reviews the complete file. Timing: Early Action mid-November to early December; Regular Action end of January to early March. Interview covers preparedness, career goals, why Berklee, and contribution to the community, plus programme-specific technical questions.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED — no portal opening date is published on any page read. Working back from the 1 November Early Action deadline, expect the September-2027 cycle to open around late summer / early autumn 2026.

programs.whatYouStudy: CONFIRMED module structure. CORE: Audio Engineering; Studio Music Production; Music Video Production; Interactive Media; Electronic Music Production and Performance; Career Preparation; Proficiencies. FINAL PROJECT MODULE: three seminars (Past, Present, Future) plus Culminating Experience Project courses. ELECTIVE MODULE: 4 credits chosen from audio engineering, production, theory/songwriting, DJing, video production, interactive media and electronic music. OPTIONAL: ensembles, private instruction, research, internship (adds ~5 credits). The year culminates in a self-defined Culminating Experience project — and the application video is literally you pitching three candidate CE projects, so the portfolio and the degree are continuous.
programs.fitNotes: Content-wise this is the strongest match in the private/specialist bracket for someone who wants to be a producer and electronic artist: electronic music production AND performance is a core course, DJing is an available elective, and the whole year is hands-on studio and technology work in English in a European city, finished in twelve months. Two hard obstacles. (1) MONEY: ~USD 53,000 in direct charges plus USD 12,000–17,000 living; scholarships are capped in aggregate at 90% of TUITION only, there is no stipend, and the MPTI-specific 70% Outstanding Women award is closed to him. Even a strong award leaves a large five-figure bill. (2) ENGLISH: IELTS Academic 7.5 (or TOEFL 100) is a genuinely demanding bar for someone at working-level English who has not sat the test — this is the single most likely reason his application fails. Act now: book IELTS preparation immediately, and start the SpanTran/ECE course-by-course evaluation of the SMU MedTech BSc months before the deadline because Berklee warns it takes weeks.

NOT CONFIRMED on the SAE page: duration, credits, entry requirements, English requirement, portfolio, audition/interview, fees, scholarships, start date or deadlines — the page carries none of these and links to ICMP for full details. programs.program: Medialogy (Copenhagen) — MSc, with specialisation in Sound and Music Computing (CORRECTION: NOT closed — it survives as a specialisation, not a standalone degree)
programs.university: Aalborg University (AAU), Copenhagen campus
programs.degree: MSc (cand.scient. in Medialogy). Sound and Music Computing is an officially published specialisation chosen after the 1st semester — the diploma is Medialogy, the specialisation is the track.
programs.durationEcts: 2 years / 120 ECTS (4 semesters). Confirmed on the official page: "Specialiseringen i Sound and Music Computing på Aalborg Universitet består af fire semestre (120 ECTS-point)".
programs.focus: Sound Design + Immersive Audio + Electronic/interactive audio (sonic interaction design, spatial audio for VR/AR, machine learning for sound). This is the CS-to-audio bridge — engineering and interaction-design framing, not music-conservatory craft.
programs.institutionType: Public university (problem-based learning / group project model)
programs.language: English. Confirmed: the Medialogy Copenhagen page lists "Engelsk" as Sprog, and the specialisation page states "2-årig specialisering / Engelsk". (The AAU website itself is Danish; teaching is English.)
programs.tuitionIntl: 57,850 DKK / EUR 7,745 PER SEMESTER for non-EU/EEA students, listed explicitly as "Medialogy (Copenhagen)" in the official 2026 tuition table. That is roughly EUR 30,980 / 231,400 DKK for the full 2-year degree. Plus a non-refundable application fee of EUR 150 (1,150 DKK) for non-EU/EEA applicants, which covers up to 3 AAU applications and is refunded if he enrols.
programs.fundingLevel: Full (competitive, scarce) or None. There is no partial tier.
programs.scholarship: Danish Government Scholarships administered by AAU. Official wording: "Each September intake, Aalborg University grants a limited number of scholarships to individually selected applicants from non-EU/EEA countries based on strategic considerations and academic qualifications... All non-EU applicants are automatically considered when applying to a master's programme. Therefore, it is not possible to apply for a scholarship separately." A Tunisian national is eligible. BUT: "approximately 15 each year" for the ENTIRE university, and AAU explicitly warns "We do not advise you to rely solely on receiving a scholarship".
programs.stipend: A scholarship = full tuition-fee waiver PLUS a monthly living stipend. 2026 rate: 11,225 DKK / EUR 1,503 per month, paid for four semesters. Possibly taxable. Decision communicated by early July at the latest; if he has already paid tuition it is refunded.
programs.entryRequirements: Bachelor's degree. Three bachelors are pre-approved as directly qualifying: BSc Medialogy (Aalborg or Copenhagen) and BSc Engineering (Electronic Engineering / Electronic Systems Engineering) at AAU. Everyone else is individually assessed against explicit ECTS thresholds: "Minimum 10 ECTS i Programming", "Minimum 10 ECTS i technical knowledge behind media technologies", "Minimum 10 ECTS i methods within Interaction Design/User Experience Design". CRITICAL WARNING, quoted: "Bemærk, at det ikke er muligt at supplere fag for at opfylde adgangskravene" — it is NOT possible to take top-up courses to meet the entry requirements. Also: no pre-assessment is offered ("Der foretages ikke forhåndsvurderinger"). English at Danish B-level required, evidenced by upper-secondary certificate or an accepted English test. The programme is capacity-capped (adgangsbegrænset): Medialogy Copenhagen offered 33 places in 2025, and qualified applicants are ranked by (1) bachelor grades, (2) a max 1-page English statement of relevance/motivation and knowledge of the programme — where he may indicate he wants the Sound and Music Computing specialisation, and (3) documented relevant activity such as work experience in IT, media production, programming, sound or film.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — emphatically. This is an engineering/media-technology master and no music qualification is asked for anywhere. The risk runs the other way: his BSc Software Engineering will clear the 10 ECTS Programming bar easily, but he must be able to point to 10 ECTS of media-technology content AND 10 ECTS of Interaction Design / UX methods in his SMU MedTech transcript, and he cannot make up a shortfall afterwards. He should map his transcript against those three lines before anything else.
programs.portfolioSpec: No creative portfolio required. The only written submission is the ranking-criterion statement: an English text of maximum 1 page covering relevance to his future career goals, his reasons for applying, and his knowledge of the programme — plus documentation of relevant activities/work experience. Uploads: bachelor diploma and full transcript (or transcript to date if not yet graduated), and English B-level documentation.
programs.auditionSpec: None. No audition, no interview, no on-site test. Selection is entirely on documents and grade ranking.
programs.applicationOpens: The application portal (Ansøgningsportalen) opens "medio december" — mid-December — for the following September intake. For a September 2027 start that means roughly mid-December 2026. This is a published standing rule, not a one-off date.
programs.deadline: 1 March at 23:59 for a September start — published as a standing annual rule on AAU's official 'Ansøgning og frister' page ("Du skal søge senest den 1. marts kl. 23.59, hvis du vil optages til september"), with decisions by 10 June at the latest and any leftover places advertised mid-June on a first-come-first-served basis. So for September 2027: apply by 1 March 2027. Re-confirm in late 2026, but this is a stable rule rather than a lapsed cycle date. He may apply to a maximum of 3 AAU masters per intake.
programs.whatYouStudy: Semester 1: project 'Adaptive Media Systems' plus 'Machine Learning for Media Experiences', choosing two electives from Sound and Music Perception and Cognition (recommended for this specialisation), Real-Time Computer Graphics, Mobile and Wearable Computing, Narratives in Interactive Systems. Semester 2: project 'Immersive Sonic Experiences' plus the course 'Sonic Interaction Design', with two electives from Multi-Sensory Interaction and Media Cognition, Signal Processing for Interactive Systems, Embodied Interaction, Spatial User Interfaces, Game Research and Development. Semester 3: a company internship, DADIU Game Production (the Danish national game-production programme), a regular project, or a semester abroad. Semester 4: thesis only. Everything is problem-based group project work. Honest framing for him: this is audio ENGINEERING and interaction design — spatial audio, VR/AR sound, AI for sound, new interfaces for musical expression — not beat-making, mixing records or DJ craft.
programs.facilities: The Multi-sensory Experience Lab is attached to the programme and is named on the official page in a student testimonial as offering "ekstraordinære faciliteter" for spatial audio in VR. Named employer/industry pipeline on the official page: Bang & Olufsen, T-Rex Engineering, IO Interactive, Carl Martin, Dicentia. Semester 3 can be spent inside DADIU, the Danish national game-production consortium.
programs.fitNotes: The previous entry's claim that this programme is dead is WRONG and must be corrected before he sees it. The old standalone smc.aau.dk / 'Sound and Music Computing' master URL does redirect into AAU's 'programmes without admission' area, which is what caused the false negative — but the content has moved: it is now a live 2-year, 120-ECTS, English-taught specialisation inside the MSc Medialogy at the Copenhagen campus, and it is open for application. This remains the single most natural destination in this whole slice for a computer-science graduate who wants to work in sound. Two real obstacles: (1) the hard ECTS gate — 10 ECTS each of programming, media technology and interaction design/UX, with no possibility of topping up, and no pre-assessment, so he is guessing until he submits; (2) money — EUR 7,745 per semester, about EUR 31,000 all in, with the only escape being one of roughly 15 government scholarships awarded across the whole university, which do at least pay tuition in full plus about EUR 1,500 a month. It will not, on its own, make him a DJ or a record producer; it will make him someone who can build audio technology and design interactive sound.
programs.verificationNotes: sourceUrl CORRECTED. Verified directly on the live official AAU pages: the specialisation page (curriculum, 120 ECTS, English, entry ECTS thresholds, ranking criteria, 33 places), the parent Medialogy Copenhagen page (Copenhagen, English, 2 years, September start), AAU's official master admission-and-deadlines page (1 March deadline, portal opens mid-December, decision by 10 June), and AAU's official English 'Finance and fees' page (Medialogy Copenhagen listed at 57,850 DKK / EUR 7,745 per semester for 2026; EUR 150 application fee; Danish Government Scholarship terms and the 11,225 DKK monthly stipend rate). Not verified: whether the 33-place cap is unchanged for 2027, and whether his specific SMU MedTech transcript satisfies the media-technology and interaction-design ECTS lines — AAU refuses pre-assessment, so this can only be resolved by applying or by emailing the study board.

programs.program: MA Music Composition and Sound for Film and Games
programs.university: University of Hertfordshire, School of Creative Arts
programs.city: Hatfield, Hertfordshire (College Lane Campus, ~30 min by train from London)
programs.durationEcts: 1 year full time (or 2 years part time). 180 UK credits total = approx. 90 ECTS: two taught semesters of 120 credits plus a third semester for the 60-credit major project. Institution code H36.
programs.focus: Film/Game Sound + Music Production + Sound Design. Covers linear (film) and non-linear (game) audio, hybrid scoring, middleware integration, and studio production.
programs.institutionType: Public university
programs.language: English
programs.tuitionIntl: GBP 17,950 for the 2026/2027 academic year, full time — the official page lists the identical figure for 'EU Students' and 'International Students' (part time: GBP 1,495 per 15 credits). UK rate for comparison is GBP 10,320. 2027/28 fees are not yet published and the page warns fees may rise.
programs.scholarship: University of Hertfordshire international scholarships and discounts, described on the official international pages as "up to GBP 4,000 towards study fees". Open to overseas applicants, so a Tunisian national is eligible in principle. No named Tunisia-specific award and no fully funded route found. An international applicant requiring a CAS must also pay a tuition deposit as a condition of the offer.
programs.stipend: None. Fee discount only — no living costs, no housing.
programs.entryRequirements: Quoted verbatim from the official page: "A good honours degree (1st, 2:1 or 2:2) in Music, Music Technology, Music Performance, or a related discipline (or an equivalent international qualification)" OR "A minimum of five years' professional industry experience, assessed at the discretion of the Admissions Team or Programme Tutor." Then, and this is the line that matters most for him: "All applicants are expected to demonstrate a solid prior knowledge of standard music studio equipment and its functions, along with practical experience using a range of common audio software platforms." The page confirms "Applications open to international and EU students: Yes". No IELTS/TOEFL score is quoted on the course page itself — he must confirm the English requirement with the international admissions team (he has not sat a test yet).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Check — genuinely ambiguous, and he must ask before investing. The named degrees are Music, Music Technology and Music Performance "or a related discipline"; BSc Software Engineering is not obviously within that family. There is no explicit statement that non-music bachelors are accepted, and there is no explicit exclusion either. The harder gate is the separate sentence requiring demonstrated prior knowledge of studio equipment and common audio software — that applies to ALL applicants regardless of degree, so he cannot route around it. Practical advice: email the Programme Leader, Bruce Aisher (b.aisher@herts.ac.uk, named on the official page), with his situation and a link to his work, before applying.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOT published. The official course page specifies no portfolio, showreel or work-sample requirement — the entry-requirements block lists only the degree/experience condition and the studio-knowledge expectation. Do not assume there is none: for a composition-titled MA, admissions will very likely ask for evidence of creative work, and the studio-knowledge clause effectively demands it. He must obtain the exact brief from the programme team. Application is direct to the university, not via UCAS: international applicants use the herts.ac.uk international application portal; the portal asks for the standard transcript/qualification documents.
programs.auditionSpec: None published. No audition, no on-site test and no interview is mentioned anywhere on the official course page. Assessment on the course itself is 100% coursework ("All assessment is coursework-based").
programs.applicationOpens: ALREADY OPEN for the 2027 intake — this is the standout practical fact. The official page's 'How to apply' table lists a 2027 instance: start 22/09/2027, end 30/09/2028, UH Hatfield Campus, with live 'Apply online' links for both full time and part time. The 2026 instance (22/09/2026) is also still listed.
programs.deadline: No fixed closing date is published. UK postgraduate taught admission here is rolling — applications are considered until the cohort fills. For a September 2027 start he should apply in autumn 2026 to early 2027, well ahead of the UK student-visa (CAS) and deposit timeline. Because no deadline is published at all, nothing here is a lapsed prior-cycle date.
programs.whatYouStudy: Five compulsory Level 7 modules, all named on the official page: 'Soundtrack in Interactive Games' (30 credits — composition and production of music and sound in non-linear environments, plus integration and automation of audio layers using industry-standard game audio tools and middleware); 'Soundtrack in Narrative Film' (30 credits — film and narrative theory, then composition and production across music, sound design and foley, diegetic and non-diegetic); 'Sound Design for Visual Media' (30 credits — sound-design principles plus the studio techniques and technologies of current sound production); 'Industry, Innovation and Enterprise' (30 credits — research methods, business, legislation and professional practice in the music and sound industries); and the 'Major Project in Music and Sound for Film and Games' (60 credits — a substantial self-directed creative or technical work suitable for showing to employers). The stated deliverable is a professional showreel. Teaching is interactive lectures, workshops, one-to-one tutorials and practical work, with cross-course collaboration alongside the animation, games and film students.
programs.facilities: Detailed on the official page: recording studios, dubbing suites, mix and mastering studios, performance spaces, critical listening spaces, high-spec computing labs, and a free-to-borrow kit loan store, based in the Film, Music and Media Building on College Lane Campus. Microphone stock named: Soundfield, Neumann, AKG, Coles, Shure, Audio-Technica, Beyerdynamic. Software named: Logic, Pro Tools and Ableton Live, with iZotope, Native Instruments, East West and Universal Audio plug-ins — Ableton Live in particular is directly relevant to his electronic-music ambition. Staff named: Rob Wright (Head of Music); Bruce Aisher (Postgraduate Music Programme Leader — a working producer, remixer and sound designer credited on 100+ commercial releases including a US Billboard Club Chart No.1, and on products by Apple, BandLab, Splice and Native Instruments); Dr James Stonehouse (adaptive non-linear game soundtracks, middleware, commentary audio designer for the Olympic Broadcast Service); Tess Tyler (screen composer, LEGO, Asgard's Wrath 2); Dr Kyriacos Michael (songwriting, immersive music). Industry links via the Music Academic Partnership. Graduate destinations listed: Splash Damage, Splice, Sweet Justice Sound, Videoheads, Zimmer Audio. School named Best Creative School in the UK by The Rookies, 2025.
programs.fitNotes: Content-wise this is by far the best match in this batch: real studios, Ableton and Logic, a producer as programme leader, game-audio middleware, and a showreel as the output — it teaches the craft he actually wants. Two caveats keep it out of A. First, money: GBP 17,950 tuition against a maximum GBP 4,000 discount, plus a CAS deposit and Hatfield living costs, so realistically GBP 30,000+ out of pocket with no fully funded route — that is the opposite of his stated preference. Second, the entry wording asks for a music-family degree or five years of industry experience, and expects everyone to already know their way around a studio and a DAW; he has neither a music degree nor pro experience, so his admission depends on convincing the programme tutor with self-taught production work. Concrete plan if he wants it: spend the next twelve months building a real body of Ableton production and sound-design work, then email Bruce Aisher directly for a read on his eligibility before spending anything.
programs.verificationNotes: Read in full from the live official course page (the earlier 403 was Cloudflare bot protection; the page was retrieved successfully with a browser-grade fetch). Confirmed at first hand: title, MA award, 1-year full-time / 2-year part-time structure, Hatfield location, institution code H36, the full entry-requirements text, all five modules with credit weightings, the facilities and software list, the named staff, the 2026/27 fee table including the GBP 17,950 international rate, 'Applications open to international and EU students: Yes', and the live 2027 apply-online instance (22/09/2027-30/09/2028). Scholarship figure (up to GBP 4,000) verified on the University's official international scholarships-and-fees page. NOT verified: the IELTS/TOEFL score required (not stated on the course page), whether a portfolio or showreel is requested at application, and 2027/28 tuition (not yet published — the page states fees may be higher in future years).

programs.program: M.A. Game Development and Research (VERIFIED NEGATIVE for audio — no sound or music teaching in the curriculum)
programs.university: TH Köln (Cologne University of Applied Sciences) — Cologne Game Lab
programs.degree: MA (Master of Arts), accredited by the German Accreditation Council and awarded by TH Köln. Formally a 'further education' / continuing-education master (Weiterbildungsmaster), which is why it charges tuition where most German public masters do not.
programs.durationEcts: 4 semesters (2 years) / 120 ECTS. Official wording: "Graduates complete the MA 'Game Development and Research' with 120 ECTS." Timetabled to be combinable with a part-time job — required attendance is Mondays all day plus Wednesday evenings.
programs.focus: Game development and games research: project work, game design theory, visual design, media and game studies, professionalization. NO audio, sound-design, music or middleware content in the published module structure.
programs.institutionType: University of applied sciences (public) — Cologne Game Lab is TH Köln's dedicated games institute
programs.language: English. Official wording on the M.A. Overview page: "Language of instruction: English". Only B2 English is required and a formal certificate is OPTIONAL.
programs.tuitionIntl: EUR 2,500 per semester for NON-EU citizens (EUR 1,500 for EU citizens) = EUR 10,000 over the four semesters, PLUS a general semester fee of about EUR 265-300 per semester (about EUR 1,240 total) which includes a public-transport pass covering Cologne, Bonn and Düsseldorf. CORRECTION to the prior entry: this is NOT a fee-free German public master — it is a continuing-education master and it does charge tuition to everyone. CGL's own cost worksheet for a non-EU student over the whole programme: EUR 200 + EUR 1,240 semester fees + EUR 10,000 tuition + EUR 22,416 living costs, and the EUR 22,416 must be proved to the Immigration Office to obtain the residence permit.
programs.scholarship: No programme scholarship. The official FAQ only signposts external routes: TH Köln's scholarship advice service (stipendienberatung@th-koeln.de), daad.de/scholarships for international students, and applicaid.org. DAAD is a genuinely separate application track with its own much earlier deadlines and would need its own research.
programs.entryRequirements: Three hard conditions, quoted from the official application page: (1) "The successful completion of a university degree with the degree 'Bachelor of Arts' or 'Bachelor of Sciences' or with an equivalent or higher degree... in any field." (2) "Proof of at least 12 months of professional experience relevant to the course of study, completed AFTER earning the first university degree... should be accumulated by the start of the program. It can, however, be acquired cumulatively... gained within the last five years prior to the application." (3) A portfolio documenting creative and scholarly achievements, plus English at minimum B2. International applicants must ALSO have their degree validated by uni-assist in parallel, by the same deadline, with certified copies and certified translations if the documents are not in English or German. He can pre-check whether SMU MedTech is recognised at anabin.kmk.org (needs status H+).
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes, without qualification — "a university degree... in any field", and the FAQ adds "The MA Game Development and Research program welcomes applicants from all professional backgrounds." A software-engineering degree is an asset here, not a problem. The real gate is not the degree but the 12 months of post-bachelor professional experience in a games/media-relevant field: he graduates in 2026 with none, so for a September 2027 start he would need roughly a year of relevant work between graduation and enrolment (employment, self-employment, project work, internships and research-assistant posts all count, and can be accumulated in pieces).
programs.portfolioSpec: Now fully documented. The portfolio is free-form work samples, explicitly NOT required to be game work: "These do not need to be works in game design, since we do not require that applicants have previous experience in that field." Submit as a PDF, a Dropbox/Google Drive link or an online portfolio; analogue work must be scanned or photographed. CGL's own list of acceptable content includes, under 'Samples of other Audiovisual Artwork': "Audio Work: If you have sound design or music composition skills, present examples" — so his production work would count. Alongside the portfolio, every MA GDR applicant must complete the annual application TASK, which consists of a project idea, an application video of maximum 10 minutes, and three short written assignments; the exact brief is published only when the portal opens on 1 March. Other uploads: CV, portrait photo, scanned certificates and degree, proof of the 12 months' experience (contracts or dated project documents), and optionally an English certificate.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. The formal selection is an "artistic-scientific aptitude test" made up of the submitted documents and application tasks. An interview is only sometimes used: "In some cases, the committee may invite applicants to an individual online-interview (approximately 10 minutes)... The interview is an additional method to evaluate an applicant's language skills." It is ONLINE, short, and about English proficiency, not performance. CORRECTION to the prior entry: the '11 and 13 June' interview dates came from a one-off news post about an extended cycle, not from the standing admission process.
programs.applicationOpens: 1 March each year — "The application tasks are always published on March 1st", which is also when the application portal opens. For a September 2027 start, expect 1 March 2027.
programs.deadline: 31 March at 23:59 CEST — published as a standing annual rule: "The application deadline is always March 31, at 23:59 CEST", with the uni-assist submission deadline also 31 March, and successful applicants notified in June to start in September. PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date only for the extension: the news page that was originally cited as the source announced a one-off extension to 24 April with interviews on 11 and 13 June; that is not the standing rule and must not be planned around. Practical timing for September 2027: begin uni-assist paperwork by roughly January 2027 (evaluation takes up to four weeks or longer at peak), watch for the tasks on 1 March 2027, submit by 31 March 2027.
programs.whatYouStudy: Confirmed module structure, four semesters. Semester 1 'Equalization & Exchange' — levelling projects 'Playing with Theater', 'Playing with Cinema', 'Playing with Video Games', plus Media and Game Studies 101, Visual Design 101, Game Design Theory 101. Semester 2 'Critical Play & Adaptation' — projects on Board Games, Serious Games and Non-Linear Adaptation, plus the 102-level theory courses. Semester 3 'Professionalization & Experimentation' — the commercial games market, financing, self-publishing versus publishers, pitch and marketing strategy, plus a larger experimental third-semester project and the 103-level theory courses. Semester 4 — Master's Project: thesis with a theoretical and a practical part, plus a colloquium. Only 20 students per year. THE DECISIVE FINDING: there is no audio, sound-design, music, Wwise/FMOD or middleware module anywhere in the published structure. The programme describes itself as research into "non-linear audio-visuality", which reads as audio-related but in practice means audiovisual media as a whole; the taught strands are game design, visual design, media and game studies, programming and professionalization. Graduate profiles listed by CGL: Game Designer, Game Artist, Game Programmer, Interactive Designer, Concept Author, Stage Director, Project Manager — no audio role.
programs.facilities: Not itemised on the official pages. Confirmed instead: a dedicated games institute with its own building in Cologne, six named professors (Bartholdy, Freyermuth, Guardiola, Hoffmann, Klemke, Limpach) plus industry guest lecturers, a cohort of only 20, the Clash of Realities international games conference hosted in-house, and an incubator strand (The Game Starter Foundry, Broken Paternoster Games). No studio, console or audio facility is claimed.
programs.fitNotes: Verified as existing, well-run and genuinely open to a software engineer — and verified as the wrong programme for him. It is English-taught, accepts any bachelor, accepts an audio portfolio, needs no audition, needs no IELTS, and costs a manageable EUR 10,000 plus fees. But it does not teach sound. If his goal shifts to games programming or games research it is a strong option; for becoming a producer, DJ or sound designer it teaches him nothing he needs. Secondary blocker even then: 12 months of post-degree professional experience in a media-relevant field, which he will not have until roughly late 2027 at the earliest. Recommend excluding from the audio shortlist.
programs.verificationNotes: sourceUrl CORRECTED — the URL previously cited was a news/announcement post about a deadline extension, which is why almost every field came back UNVERIFIED. The real programme pages were located and read in full: Overview (120 ECTS, 4 semesters, English, EUR 1,500/2,500 per semester, ~EUR 300 semester fee, 20 students, late-September start), Application Process (the three entry conditions verbatim, the application steps, the 1 March / 31 March timeline, the document list, the uni-assist requirement), Modules (the full four-semester structure — confirming the absence of any audio module), and FAQs (120 ECTS accreditation statement, the non-EU tuition comparison table, the portfolio guidance including audio work samples, how to evidence the 12 months' experience, the total cost worksheet, and the scholarship signposts). Everything above is first-hand from those official pages. Not verified: whether specific software-engineering employment would be accepted as 'relevant' professional experience — that is a committee judgement and worth an email to CGL's office before he counts on it.

programs.institutionType: University of applied sciences (public)
programs.language: English
programs.tuitionIntl: UNVERIFIED for non-EU. The official page publishes only the statutory rate: "For academic year 2026-2027 the statutory tuition fee for master's programmes is EUR 2,694. programs.fundingLevel: UNVERIFIED (statutory EU rate is low; the non-EU institutional rate is unpublished)

The Holland Scholarship is a general Dutch national scheme for non-EEA students, worth checking independently — not confirmed for this programme.
programs.entryRequirements: A bachelor's degree in a relevant game-development field — IT, programming, art, animation, design or production. "Pre-existing knowledge in the field you wish to explore is required", and applicants must already have the skills to build the test environments their research needs ("To support your thesis, you can, for example, create a test environment, but you must already have the skills to do so"). He has not sat any of these yet. Intake is capped at 28 students across the three disciplines.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Yes — it REQUIRES a technical or design background rather than a musical one. "IT" and "programming" are named accepted fields, so a BSc Software Engineering is a direct fit. This is the one programme in the batch where his degree is an outright advantage. It simply does not teach audio.
programs.portfolioSpec: Not a creative portfolio. The selection artefact is a programme-specific ASSIGNMENT set by BUas and issued inside 'My Online Application' — and the official application-procedure page links the template as 'Template-Literature-Review.pdf', so it is an academic literature review, not a reel of work. Alongside it: CV, motivation letter, passport copy, bachelor diploma and transcript (or current transcript if not yet graduated), and certified translations if documents are not in English, Dutch, French or German. Application starts in Studielink, then continues in My Online Application. Industry reviewers are involved in assessing the intake assignment.
programs.auditionSpec: No audition. After the assignment passes, applicants are invited to an intake INTERVIEW held online via Microsoft Teams, with the admission decision communicated within five working days.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED - confirm. Only the closing arrangement is published.
programs.deadline: "Application is open until 15 August, but we strongly recommend applying before 1 July to avoid delays due to the summer holidays." This reads as a standing annual rule rather than a lapsed date, so for a September 2027 start expect a 15 August 2027 close and apply by June 2027. First, this trains screen composers and game-audio designers, not DJs or club producers; it is a career hedge toward where the paid work is, not a route to an artist career. Second, and more concretely, the Composition, Arrangement & Orchestration module assumes classical and jazz stylistic literacy and arranging for strings, brass and woodwind — a substantial barrier for a self-taught software engineer with no conservatoire training, and the module is compulsory. The 50% Berlin scholarship that exists for this exact course is closed to him because it is BIMM-alumni-only. Only worth taking if he decides he genuinely wants sound design or game audio as a profession.

programs.fitNotes: STILL NOT A MASTER'S — but the correct verdict is now sharper than "unaccredited marketing". It is a real, NCFE-accredited, Home-Office-overseen, Level 5 vocational qualification, and Abbey Road Institute London genuinely holds a Student Visa sponsorship licence: "Abbey Road Institute London holds a Student Visa sponsorship licence. This means that we are now able to accept a limited number of international students who require a Student visa to study on the UK." So a Tunisian national CAN legally come and study here, unlike the Amsterdam campus. The problem is value, not legitimacy. He would pay £23,950 in full up front, with no work rights, to earn a Level 5 award — one level BELOW the BSc he already holds, and worth nothing towards a master's, a Level 7 recognition in Europe, or doctoral progression. The teaching and the Abbey Road access are probably excellent, and the portfolio bar ("we do not expect to receive high-quality productions") is realistically within reach for him. But as a step after a completed bachelor's, paying nearly £24k to move DOWN the qualification framework is hard to justify, especially with zero funding. If he wants the Abbey Road name cheaply, the 4-day Song Production Masterclass (10-13 Oct 2026, one day at Abbey Road Studios, three at Angel Studios, with Sylvia Massy) is the sane version of this.

programs.entryRequirements: NOW VERIFIED, under the heading "Zugangsvoraussetzungen": (1) "Berufsqualifizierender Hochschulabschluss" — a professionally qualifying higher-education degree, (2) "mindestens 180 ECTS", (3) "Künstlerische Eignung" — artistic aptitude, assessed via a test (see auditionSpec). And, listed FIRST under Zugangsvoraussetzungen: "Teilnehmende aus der EU (deutschsprachig)" — participants from the EU, German-speaking. His BSc would satisfy (1) and (2); the EU-residency and German-language conditions are what stop him.
programs.acceptsNonMusic: Formally YES on the academic side — the requirement is only a "berufsqualifizierender Hochschulabschluss" with at least 180 ECTS, with no subject restriction, and the project fields are deliberately broad ("Musik, Film, Video-, Installations- und Medienkunst, Sound-Art, bildende Kunst, Fotografie, Game-Art"). Admission is portfolio- and project-led, not subject-led, so a software-engineering BSc is not itself a barrier. He would, however, have to pass the artistic aptitude test on the strength of a proposed master project and prior creative work — which he does not yet have.
programs.portfolioSpec: NOW VERIFIED in substance, and it is unusual: there is no conventional Mappe. The application is a WRITTEN PROJECT PROPOSAL. Verbatim: "Ablauf des künstlerische Eignungstests: Der/Die Bewerber/in bewirbt sich mit einer schriftlich verfassten Idee für ein künstlerisches Masterprojekt. Daraufhin findet auf Basis der Projektidee ein Kolloquium statt, um den/die Bewerber/in, dessen bisherige Werke/Tätigkeiten und das Projekt besser kennenzulernen." Existing works may be shown at the colloquium but are not the formal submission.
programs.auditionSpec: YES — an artistic aptitude examination in the form of a colloquium before a joint panel. Verbatim: "Wie ist die künstlerische Eignungsprüfung aufgebaut? Hierbei handelt es sich um ein Kolloquium, in dem du deine Projektidee einer Prüfungskommission, bestehend aus Mitgliedern des SAE Instituts und der Folkwang UdK, vorstellst. Natürlich kannst du in diesem Kolloquium auch bestehende künstlerische Arbeiten von dir vorstellen, um der Kommission einen Einblick in dein bisheriges Schaffen zu geben." This is a defence of a project idea in German before an academic panel — not a performance audition, but a substantial hurdle.
programs.applicationOpens: UNVERIFIED. SAE publishes generic "Bewerbung & Zulassung", "Kosten & Zahlungspläne" and "Internationale Bewerber·innen" pages but no dated application window for this programme.
programs.deadline: PRIOR CYCLE - confirm new date. No application deadline is published. The only published date is the intake month: "Starttermin: Oktober" (Bochum, annually). For an October 2027 start, expect a first-half-of-2027 deadline, but nothing is currently published.
programs.facilities: Genuine institutional depth, now confirmed: "Der Master of Arts in Professional Media Creation wird in Kooperation mit der Folkwang Universität der Künste angeboten, einer der zentralen künstlerischen Ausbildungsstätten für Musik, Theater, Tanz, Gestaltung und Wissenschaft in Deutschland", with the cooperation running "seit 2010". Elective modules may be taken at SAE OR at Folkwang, which opens access to Folkwang's ICEM — "Das Institut für Computermusik und elektronische Medien (ICEM) der Folkwang Universität der Künste beschäftigt sich mit allen Aspekten medialer Zeitkünste wie Computermusik, Video und Interaktion" — a serious computer-music and electronic-media institute. Delivered at SAE's Bochum campus. Specific studio inventory still UNVERIFIED.
programs.whatYouStudy: A two-year, supervised, self-directed artistic master project, developed across three project modules (artistic practice and reflection, project planning and goal-setting, narration, project marketing, project and event management), 30 ECTS of electives taken at SAE or Folkwang (one week of SAE electives = 1 ECTS, documented in a logbook), and a 30-ECTS final thesis consisting of the realised project plus its public release. "Alle Inhalte dieses Masterstudiengangs führen zur öffentlichen Aufführung des Abschlussprojekts." Sound art and music are legitimate project fields, but this is an interdisciplinary media-art master's, not a music-production or mixing course.
programs.fitNotes: RULED OUT ON TWO CONFIRMED GROUNDS, one of which is new and harder than language. (1) ELIGIBILITY: the programme's own Zugangsvoraussetzungen block restricts it to "Teilnehmende aus der EU (deutschsprachig)" — EU participants. That is a nationality/residency restriction, not merely a language note, and a Tunisian national is outside it. (2) LANGUAGE: delivery and the admission colloquium are in German, which he does not speak; reaching the required level by autumn 2027 is not realistic from a standing start. (3) A third practical problem even if the first two vanished: compulsory modules run as weekend blocks explicitly so students can hold down a job, which is a weak basis for a German student visa. Add that the content is self-directed media art culminating in a public performance, not the hands-on production, mixing and sound-design craft he wants. The attraction — a genuinely state-recognised German MA at only ~€12,000 all-in with 120 ECTS — is real but not available to him. If he still wants Germany, look for English-taught, non-EU-open master's at public Hochschulen instead; SAE's other master's (Professional Practice, University of Hertfordshire, online) carries the same "EU (deutschsprachig)" restriction and is no help.
